Patrologia Latina · Vol. 113 ·

LIBER PSALMORUM

One book of the Glossa ordinaria — the whole gloss, book by book.

PL 113, coll. 841–1080  ·  Latin from the Migne printing  ·  New English translation  ·  column numbers follow the original plates, not the Garnier reprint

Anselm of Laon and his school

Anselmus Laudunensis et schola

twelfth century

The masters of the cathedral school of Laon, gathered around Anselm (c. 1050–1117), to whom the making of the Glossa ordinaria on the Bible is traditionally credited. The gloss is a school's work rather than one man's: it draws its comment from the Fathers — Rabanus, Isidore, Bede, Jerome, Gregory — and names them as it goes, and it grew by accretion over generations. Migne prints it under the name of Walafrid Strabo, an ascription now known to be mistaken.

PROLOGUS BEATI HIERONYMI IN LIBRUM PSALMORUM.

( Vide Operum ejus tom. VIII. )

THE PROLOGUE OF BLESSED JEROME ON THE BOOK OF PSALMS.

( Vide Operum ejus tom. VIII. )

PROTHEMATA IN PSALTERIUM.

841A(AUG.) Liber iste intitulatur apud Hebraeos Liber hymnorum, hac ratione, quia hymnus est ubi habentur verba et laus cum cantico, quod in psalmis invenitur. Intitulatur etiam, secundum quosdam, liber Soliloquiorum: quod ideo videtur fieri, quia illud quod aliquis secum rimatur, et a nullo discit, nisi a veritate sibi interius praesidente, soliloquium dicitur, verbi gratia, quemadmodum beatus Augustinus secum de natura animae, et de natura Dei investigavit, eodem modo potest dici Propheta secum investigasse de incarnatione Filii Dei, et de reparatione humani generis. Rex David et propheta, cum prospere regnaret, volens cultum Dei magnificare, cum arcam a Philisthaeis redditam, longo tempore 841Bpost incertis sedibus vagantem, tandem in Jerusalem reduceret, nudus cum cithara praecedebat (II Reg. VI): sed et quatuor millia virorum elegerat, qui, non solum voce, sed etiam instrumentis musicis, psalmos canerent: quibus praeposuit quatuor, Asaph, Idithun, Eman, Ethan, vel filios Core, qui a patris scelere vel sacrilegio degenerantes quem ignis consumpserat (Num. XVI), in cultu Dei devotissimi perstiterunt.

(HIERON.) Psalterium est quoddam musicum instrumentum in modum Δ litterae compositum: et ab eo musico instrumento (per quod modulatum fuit praesens opus) nomen sibi sumpsit. Psalterium apud Hebraeos vocatur nebel (נבל), apud Graecos, ψαλτήριον, apud Latinos vero organum. Multi dicunt David 841Cnon fecisse omnes psalmos, eo quod quidam ex ipsis intitulantur in persona aliorum. Sed, ut dicit beatus Hieronymus, non sunt audiendi in hoc. Nam David composuit omnes psalmos: modo etiam apposuit, in quo multos auxiliatores habuit, quibus praefecit quatuor, videlicet Eman, Ethan, Asaph et Idithun. Divino consilio hoc fuit factum, ut psalmi intitularentur in personis aliorum, vel propter interpretationem nominum tantum, vel propter negotium, vel propter utrumque. Propter interpretationem nominum tantum, ut in persona Idithun; propter negotium, ut in persona Aggaei et Zachariae; propter utrumque, ut in persona Salomonis; Idithun, Asaph, filii Core et caeteri hujusmodi, non fuerunt auctores psalmorum, sed praepositi artificibus qui psalmos 841Dpersonabant tribus modis: vel humana voce, vel musicis instrumentis, vel communiter utroque modo. Et hoc dupliciter, vel post vocem instrumento, vel post instrumentum voce: unde nomina illorum ut 842Ahonorem de ministerio sumerent, titulis inseruntur maxime pro significatione rerum. Psalmus vero est instrumenti sonus, canticum humanae vocis cantus in laudem Dei; psalmi canticum, cum post instrumentum vox, psalmus cantici, cum post vocem instrumentum.

(CASS.) Solet quaeri cur prae aliis Scripturis psalmi in Ecclesia legantur? Quod ideo est quia antiquitus apud Hebraeos mos iste in templo Dei erat. Vel, quia psalmi plus mysteriorum quam caeterae Scripturae continent, et breviter multa dicunt, in quibus omnis lex et prophetae et Evangelium constat.

(CASS.) Prophetia est inspiratio vel revelatio divina, quae eventus rerum vel per facta, vel per dicta immobili 842Bveritate pronuntiat, unde prophetia visio, propheta videns. Multis autem modis haec gratia data est: vel per operationes hominum, ut fuit arca Noe et sacrificium Abrahae, et transitus maris Rubri; vel per nativitates, ut Esau et Jacob, qui futura significabant; vel per loquentes angelos, sicut locuti sunt Abrahae, Lot et aliis; vel per visiones, sicut Isaiae et Ezechieli, et caeteris; vel per somnia, sicut Salomoni, Joseph et Danieli; vel per nubem et vocem de coelo, ut Moysi; vel adhuc aliis modis. David autem nullo horum, sed coelesti aspiratione intus edoctus, Spiritu in eo loquente, completus est, ut in I Reg.: « Directus est Spiritus Domini in David (I Reg. XVI). » Et Dominus: « Si David in spiritu vocat eum Dominum, quomodo 842Cfilius ejus est? » (Matth. XXII.) Spiritus autem sanctus sic datus est prophetis, ut aliquando pro peccatis recederet et placatus rediret; et sicut Petrus ait: « Non voluntate humana allata est aliquando prophetia, sed, Spiritu sancto inspirati, locuti sunt sancti homines Dei (II Pet. I). » Non sunt autem illi a munere prophetiae alieni, quibus data est facultas intelligendi vel interpretandi Scripturas.

(HIERON.) Multa genera sunt christorum: patriarchae dicti sunt christi, ut: « Nolite tangere christos meos (Psal. CIV); » in Parabolis, dicuntur christi omnes qui de Aegypto egressi sunt. Chrisma in Exodo fit, unde sacerdotes uncti; est aliud unguentum, quo reges inunguntur; sed hoc duobus modis, quia si David est et Salomon, id est, forti manu et 842Dpacificus, ungitur cornu; si Jehu et Azahel, lenticula, quod est vas fictile. Sed et Cyrus, rex Persarum et Medorum, qui Israel relaxavit, christus est, secundum illud: « Haec dicit Dominus christo meo 843ACyro (Isa. XLV), » quod non sinunt sequentia de Salvatore accipi, ut quidam putant. Est unguentum propheticum, quo praecipitur Eliae ut ungat Elisaeum in prophetam (III Reg. XIX); super omnia est unguentum spirituale, quod dicitur oleum exsultationis, quo Christus unctus est prae participibus, qui habent chrisma baptismi. Quod si perdat quis, non desperet; quia de separando chrismate scribitur in Levitico (Lev. XIII), quod cum lepra alicujus fuerit mundata, mittat ei sacerdos oleum in manu sinistra, et caetera quae ibi dicuntur, et ipse vocetur christus Dei. Hoc autem restat quod idem homo frequenter ungitur, ne sit occasio ruinae negligenti. Sufficit enim leproso ut, post primum unguentum perditum, ungatur secundo; sed ille saepe ungitur qui semper 843Bproficit: et, de oleo leprosi, venit ad unguentum populi; inde ad sacerdotale; de quo ad chrisma pontificis; a pontifice ad regem; a rege ad patriarchas; a patriarchis ad Christum.

(CASS.) Sicut prophetia fit diversis modis, ita et diversis temporibus. Est igitur alia de praesenti, ut Elisabeth: « Unde mihi hoc, ut veniat mater Domini? etc. » (Luc. I.) De praeterito, ut Moyses: « In principio, creavit Deus coelum et terram (Gen. I). » De futuro, ut: « Ecce Virgo concipiet, etc. (Isa. VII). »

Item prophetia alia est secundum praescientiam Dei, quam necesse est omnibus modis impleri, ut: « Ecce Virgo concipiet, etc. » Alia secundum comminationem, ut: « Quadraginta dies, et Ninive subvertetur (Jonae III). »

843CNotandum igitur quod propheta aliquando loquitur indiscrete de futuris quasi de praesentibus; aliquando de praeteritis, aliquando etiam proprie de futuris: quod ideo fit, quoniam omnia dictante Spiritu sancto dicit, cui sunt omnia nota, sive praeterita, sive futura, tanquam praesentia.

(REMIG.) Liber iste ex centum quinquaginta psalmis, non sine altioris mysterii ratione, consistit. Hic enim numerus mysteriis celeberrimus. Constat enim ex octogenario et septuagenario, quibus ex octonario et septenario principium et significatio est. Octonarius enim octavam resurrectionem significat: quia cum sex sint aetates viventium, septima morientium, octava resurgentium erit. Per septenarium vero, hujus vitae tempus significatur, quod septem dierum 843Drepetitione agitur. Recte ergo tali psalmorum numero liber iste compositus est, quia sic in hujus vitae septenario operari ac vivere nos docet, ut in octava resurrectionis stolam gloriae consequamur. Vel ideo quia per octonarium Novum Testamentum significatur: octoadi enim patres Novi Testamenti deserviunt, observantes diem octavam resurrectionis Christi, id est, Dominicam, octavas sanctorum, exspectantes octavam resurrectionis mortuorum. Per septenarium vero Vetus Testamentum, quia hebdomadi, id est septenario, patres Veteris Testamenti servierunt, observantes septimum diem, septimam septimanam, septimum annum et quinquagesimum, qui septenis annorum hebdomadibus texitur, id est 844Ajubilaeum: unde Salomon: « Da partes septem, necnon et octo (Eccl. XI). » Bene igitur hoc numero psalmorum liber iste editus est, cujus partes utriusque Testamenti doctrinam et mandata continent.

(AUG.) Item per tres quinquagenas triplex fit psalmorum distinctio, propter tres status Christianae religionis significandos: primus poenitentiae, in qua et prima psalmorum quinquagena terminatur, scilicet: « Miserere mei Deus; » secundus justitiae, in qua et secunda quinquagena: « Misericordiam et judicium cantabo tibi; » tertius status vitae aeternae, in cujus laudem tertia quinquagena finitur, scilicet: « Omnis spiritus laudet Dominum. »

(ID.) Unus est liber Psalmorum, non quinque, ut in Actibus apostolorum legitur: « Sicut scriptum 844Best in libro Psalmorum » (Act. I). Hieronymus tamen dicit quinque libros, id est, quinque distinctiones quae fiunt per « fiat, fiat. »

Ordo psalmorum ab ordine historiae discordat, quia ante peccavit David cum uxore Uriae, et de poenitentia cecinit: « Miserere mei, Deus, » quam filius ejus eum persequeretur et cecinerit: « Domine, quid multiplicati; » sed ab Esdra propheta instinctu divino ita ordinari creduntur.

Materia est integer Christus, sponsus et sponsa. Intentio, homines in Adam deformatos Christo novo homini conformare. Modus tractandi: Quandoque agit de Christo, secundum quod caput est, aliquando secundum corpus, aliquando secundum utrumque. Secundum quod caput, tripliciter: quia vel secundum 844Cdivinitatem, ut: « Tecum principium, etc.; » aliquando secundum humanitatem, ut: « Ego dormivi, etc., » aliquando per transsumptionem, ut quando utitur voce membrorum, sicut ibi: « Longe a salute mea, etc. » Item de Ecclesia tribus modis: aliquando secundum perfectos, aliquando secundum imperfectos, aliquando secundum malos: qui sunt in Ecclesia corpore, non mente; numero, non merito; nomine, non numine.

PROTHEMATA ON THE PSALTER.

841A(AUG.) This book is entitled among the Hebrews the Book of Hymns, for this reason, that a hymn is where words and praise are held together with a song, which is found in the psalms. It is also entitled, according to some, the Book of Soliloquies: which seems to be so done for this reason, that what a man searches out with himself, and learns from none save from the truth presiding within him, is called a soliloquy, for example, in the manner in which blessed Augustine searched out with himself concerning the nature of the soul and concerning the nature of God, in the same way the Prophet may be said to have searched out with himself concerning the incarnation of the Son of God, and concerning the repairing of the human race. King David and prophet, when he was reigning prosperously, wishing to magnify the worship of God, when at last he was bringing back to Jerusalem the ark that had been given back by the Philistines and had for a long time 841Bafterward wandered in uncertain seats, went before it naked with the harp (II Reg. VI): but he had also chosen four thousand men who should sing psalms not only with the voice but also with musical instruments: over whom he set four, Asaph, Idithun, Eman, Ethan, or the sons of Core, who, falling away from the crime or sacrilege of their father, whom the fire had consumed (Num. XVI), stood on most devoted in the worship of God.

(HIERON.) The psaltery is a certain musical instrument put together in the shape of the letter Δ: and from that musical instrument (by which the present work was set to measure) it took its name to itself. The psaltery is called among the Hebrews nebel (נבל), among the Greeks ψαλτήριον, but among the Latins organum. Many say that David 841Cdid not make all the psalms, because certain of them are entitled in the person of others. But, as blessed Jerome says, they are not to be listened to in this. For David composed all the psalms: he moreover appended them, wherein he had many helpers, over whom he set four, namely Eman, Ethan, Asaph and Idithun. By divine counsel this was done, that the psalms should be entitled in the persons of others, either for the interpretation of the names only, or for the business in hand, or for both. For the interpretation of the names only, as in the person of Idithun; for the business, as in the person of Aggeus and Zacharias; for both, as in the person of Solomon; Idithun, Asaph, the sons of Core and the rest of this kind were not authors of the psalms, but were set over the craftsmen who sounded the psalms 841Din three ways: either by the human voice, or by musical instruments, or commonly in both ways. And this in two manners, either by the instrument after the voice, or by the voice after the instrument: whence their names, that they might take 842Ahonour from the ministry, are inserted in the titles, chiefly for the signifying of things. But a psalm is the sound of the instrument, a canticle the singing of the human voice in the praise of God; a canticle of a psalm, when the voice comes after the instrument, a psalm of a canticle, when the instrument comes after the voice.

(CASS.) It is commonly asked: why are the psalms read in the Church before other Scriptures? This is for the reason that of old among the Hebrews this custom obtained in the temple of God. Or, because the psalms contain more of mysteries than the other Scriptures, and say many things briefly, in which the whole law and the prophets and the Gospel consist.

(CASS.) Prophecy is a divine inspiration or revelation, which declares the outcomes of things, whether by deeds or by words, with unmoving 842Btruth, whence prophecy is a vision, the prophet one that sees. Now this grace has been given in many ways: either through the works of men, as were the ark of Noe and the sacrifice of Abraham, and the passage of the Red Sea; or through births, as of Esau and Jacob, who signified things to come; or through speaking angels, as they spoke to Abraham, to Lot and to others; or through visions, as to Isaias and Ezechiel, and the rest; or through dreams, as to Solomon, Joseph and Daniel; or through the cloud and the voice from heaven, as to Moses; or in yet other ways. David, however, by none of these, but taught inwardly by a heavenly breathing, with the Spirit speaking in him, was filled full, as in I Kings: « The Spirit of the Lord was directed into David (I Reg. XVI). » And the Lord: « If David in spirit calls him Lord, how is he 842Chis son? » (Matth. XXII.) But the Holy Spirit was so given to the prophets that at times he withdrew for their sins and returned appeased; and as Peter says: « Prophecy was not at any time brought by human will, but, inspired by the Holy Spirit, holy men of God spoke (II Pet. I). » Nor are those strangers to the gift of prophecy to whom is given the faculty of understanding or of interpreting the Scriptures.

(HIERON.) There are many kinds of anointed ones: the patriarchs were called anointed, as: « Touch ye not my anointed (Psal. CIV); » in the Parables, all who came out of Egypt are called anointed. The chrism is made in Exodus, whence the priests are anointed; there is another ointment, with which kings are anointed; but this in two manners, for if it is David and Solomon, that is, strong of hand and 842Dpeaceable, one is anointed with the horn; if Jehu and Azahel, with the cruse, which is an earthen vessel. But Cyrus also, king of the Persians and Medes, who released Israel, is an anointed one, according to that word: « Thus saith the Lord to my anointed 843ACyrus (Isa. XLV), » which the words that follow do not permit to be taken of the Saviour, as some suppose. There is a prophetic ointment, with which Elias is commanded to anoint Eliseus for a prophet (III Reg. XIX); above all is the spiritual ointment, which is called the oil of gladness, wherewith Christ was anointed above his fellows, who have the chrism of baptism. And if any man lose it, let him not despair; because concerning the separating chrism it is written in Leviticus (Lev. XIII), that when any man's leprosy has been cleansed, the priest shall put oil for him in his left hand, and the rest of the things that are said there, and let him himself be called the anointed of God. But this remains, that the same man is often anointed, lest there be occasion of ruin to the negligent. For it is enough for the leper that, after the first ointment has been lost, he be anointed a second time; but he is often anointed who is always 843Bgoing forward: and, from the oil of the leper, he comes to the ointment of the people; thence to the priestly; from that to the chrism of the bishop; from the bishop to the king; from the king to the patriarchs; from the patriarchs to Christ.

(CASS.) As prophecy comes about in diverse ways, so also at diverse times. There is therefore one concerning the present, as Elizabeth: « Whence is this to me, that the mother of the Lord should come? etc. » (Luc. I.) Concerning the past, as Moses: « In the beginning God created heaven and earth (Gen. I). » Concerning the future, as: « Behold a Virgin shall conceive, etc. (Isa. VII). »

Again, one prophecy is according to the foreknowledge of God, which must in all ways be fulfilled, as: « Behold a Virgin shall conceive, etc. » Another is according to threatening, as: « Forty days, and Ninive shall be overthrown (Jonae III). »

843CIt is therefore to be noted that the prophet sometimes speaks indiscriminately of things to come as of things present; sometimes of things past, sometimes also properly of things to come: which is done for this reason, that he says all things at the dictation of the Holy Spirit, to whom all things are known, whether past or future, as though present.

(REMIG.) This book consists of a hundred and fifty psalms, not without the reason of a deeper mystery. For this number is most renowned for mysteries. For it is made up of eighty and seventy, whose beginning and signification come from eight and seven. For the eightfold signifies the eighth, the resurrection: because, whereas there are six ages of the living, the seventh of the dying, the eighth will be of those that rise again. But by the sevenfold is signified the time of this life, which is carried on by the repetition of seven 843Ddays. Rightly therefore has this book been composed of such a number of psalms, because it thus teaches us so to work and to live in the sevenfold of this life that in the eighth of the resurrection we may obtain the robe of glory. Or else because by the eightfold the New Testament is signified: for the fathers of the New Testament serve the ogdoad, observing the eighth day of Christ's resurrection, that is, the Lord's day, the octaves of the saints, awaiting the eighth of the resurrection of the dead. But by the sevenfold the Old Testament, because the fathers of the Old Testament served the hebdomad, that is, the sevenfold, observing the seventh day, the seventh week, the seventh year and the fiftieth, which is woven of seven weeks of years, that is 844Athe jubilee: whence Solomon: « Give portions to seven, and also to eight (Eccl. XI). » Well therefore has this book been published with this number of psalms, whose parts contain the doctrine and the commandments of both Testaments.

(AUG.) Again, by three fifties a threefold division of the psalms is made, for the signifying of the three states of the Christian religion: the first of penitence, in which also the first fifty of the psalms is ended, namely: « Have mercy on me, O God; » the second of righteousness, in which also the second fifty: « Mercy and judgment I will sing to thee; » the third the state of eternal life, in whose praise the third fifty is finished, namely: « Let every spirit praise the Lord. »

(ID.) The Book of Psalms is one, not five, as is read in the Acts of the Apostles: « As it is written 844Bin the book of Psalms » (Act. I). Jerome nevertheless says five books, that is, five divisions which are made by « so be it, so be it. »

The order of the psalms disagrees with the order of the history, because David sinned with the wife of Urias, and sang of penitence: « Have mercy on me, O God, » before his son persecuted him and he sang: « Lord, why are they multiplied; » but they are believed to have been so ordered by Esdras the prophet at a divine prompting.

The matter is the whole Christ, bridegroom and bride. The intention, to conform to Christ the new man those men who were deformed in Adam. The manner of treating: sometimes he deals with Christ according to that which is the head, sometimes according to the body, sometimes according to both. According to that which is the head, in three ways: for either according 844Cto the divinity, as: « With thee is the beginning, etc.; » sometimes according to the humanity, as: « I have slept, etc., » sometimes by transumption, as when he uses the voice of the members, as there: « Far from my salvation, etc. » Again, of the Church in three ways: sometimes according to the perfect, sometimes according to the imperfect, sometimes according to the evil: who are in the Church in body, not in mind; in number, not in merit; in name, not in the divine power.

PSALMUS PRIMUS.

VERS. 1.-- « Beatus vir qui non abiit, etc. » (AUG., Enarr. in Psal., tom. III.) Ordo, abiit Adam cum a Deo recessit; stetit, cum delectatus est peccato; sedit, cum in superbia confirmatus redire non potuit, nisi per istum liberatus, qui nil horum habuit. 844DAbiit Adam cum persuasioni diaboli consensit; stetit, dum pomum comedit; sedit, dum se excusavit: « Mulier quam dedisti mihi me seduxit. » (Gen. III). Ad similitudinem exsulantium, qui dum sunt in via facilius revocantur, dum jam stant difficilius: demum difficillime, dum ibi magistri et domini effecti sunt. (REMI.) Peccatur cogitatione, actu et verbis docendo. (CASS.) Impius in Deum, peccator in se, pestilens in proximum. « In cathedra dans exemplum peccandi. » (CASS.) Thronus regum, tribunal judicum, cathedra proprie doctorum. (Ibid.) Quasi ita ait: Vos qui cecidistis per primum Adam, conformamini huic secundo: quia beatus primo contrarius

845AVERS. 2.-- « Sed in lege. » AUG. (CASS.) Hic ostenditur plenus omni bono in se. (AUG.) Non est laus perfecta fugere vituperanda, nisi sequantur laudanda. Quo ordine creverunt in primo, removentur a secundo.

« In lege. » (Ibid.) Qui est in lege secundum legem agit, qui sub lege secundum legem agitur: ille liber, iste servus. (Ibid. AMBR.) Aliud est lex quae scribitur servienti, aliud quae mente conspicitur ab eo qui non indiget litteris. « Voluntas. » (CASS.) Ut non sit taedium laboris, nec otiosa, sed meditabitur semper. Voluntas sensus est sub lege; rationis, in lege; divinitatis, supra legem.

VERS. 3.-- « Et erit. » (Ibid.) Hic ostenditur utilis nobis, dans fructum vitae, et folia, et obumbrans, 845B« Beatus vir. Sed in lege. Et erit. » Plena definitio beati viri. Haec omnia non omni beato viro, sed soli Christo, conveniunt. « Tanquam lignum. » (Ibid.) Secundum similitudinem ligni vitae quod est in paradiso, unde obediens homo comederet. « Lignum. » (Ibid.) In paradiso est lignum vitae, lignum ad vitam, et lignum scientiae boni et mali. « Aquarum. » (AUG.) Aquae Spiritus sanctus, secundum illud: « Qui crediderit in me, flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquae vivae (Joan. VII), » et est contra aestus vitiorum. (CASS.) Vel per aquam, sapientia Dei, qua reficitur interior homo, ut sitis aqua. (AUG.) Vel mortale genus, ut Job: « Aquae multae populi multi, » quia defluunt in mortem, ut aquae in mare. « Dabit. » (Ibid.) Dare pertinet ad rationalem sensum et ad offerentis voluntatem. 845C« Et folium. » (Ibid.) Sicut folia fructus tegunt, ita verba Domini promissiones suas custodiunt. « Et omnia. » (Ibid.) Quid per singula.

VERS. 4.-- « Non sic impii. » Hic de ultione iniquorum adversos terret, horum formido gratiora facit praemissa. « A facie terrae. » (AUG.) Stabilitatis aeternae, quia ut haec terra nutrit et continet hominem, ita illa interiorem.

VERS. 5.-- « Ideo non resurgent. » Quia projicit ventus, id est, ideo quia dati sunt in reprobum sensum: ideo non resurgunt prima resurrectione, ut se judicent in consilio, ut voluntates Dei suis praeferant. Vel in concilio, id est, in concordi multitudine justorum impii idololatrae, vel apostatae. Peccatores, falsi Christiani: vel ideo non resurgunt in futuro, 845Dut judicent, vel ut judicati in concilio, id est, in collegio justorum quiescant. « In judicio, etc. » In judicio quatuor erunt ordines: alii judicabunt et non judicabuntur, ut perfectissimi; alii nec judicabunt, nec judicabuntur, ut damnati infideles; alii judicabuntur et salvabuntur, ut mediocriter boni; alii judicabuntur et peribunt, ut fideles mali. « In concilio. » (AUG.) In aeterno bono, quod sequi consilium fuit sanctis. « Vel in concilio, » in judicio, ut cum eis judicent; quia judicium est, quando diversa peccata diversis poenis punientur; et ex hoc similitudine dicitur. « Resurgunt. » Quae resurrectiones: animae, a peccatis in praesenti; corporis, a morte in futuro, qua fiet impassibile et immortale.

846AVERS. 6.-- « Quoniam novit Dominus, etc., » Id est, non resurgunt hi in anima, quia Deus non approbat opera eorum, sed justorum tantum.

PSALM ONE.

VERS. 1.-- « Blessed is the man who hath not gone away, etc. » (AUG., Enarr. in Psal., tom. III.) The order, Adam went away when he withdrew from God; he stood, when he was delighted with sin; he sat, when, confirmed in pride, he could not return, save as set free by this man, who had none of these things. 844DAdam went away when he consented to the persuasion of the devil; he stood, while he ate the apple; he sat, while he excused himself: « The woman whom thou gavest me seduced me. » (Gen. III) [Vulg. Gn 3:12 Mulier, quam dedisti mihi sociam, dedit mihi de ligno, et comedi, "The woman, whom thou gavest me as a companion, gave me of the tree, and I did eat"; the printed me seduxit imports the seducing that the Vulgate assigns to the serpent at Gn 3:13.]. After the likeness of exiles, who, while they are on the road, are more easily called back, while they now stand, with more difficulty: at length with the greatest difficulty, when they have there been made masters and lords. (REMI.) There is sinning by thought, by act, and by words in teaching. (CASS.) The impious man is so against God, the sinner against himself, the pestilent man against his neighbour. « In the chair, giving an example of sinning. » (CASS.) The throne is of kings, the tribunal of judges, the chair properly of teachers. (Ibid.) It is as though he said: You who have fallen through the first Adam, be ye conformed to this second one: because the blessed man is the contrary of the first

845AVERS. 2.-- « But in the law. » AUG. (CASS.) Here he is shown full of every good in himself. (AUG.) It is not perfect praise to flee the things to be blamed, unless the things to be praised follow. In the order in which they grew in the first man, they are taken away in the second.

« In the law. » (Ibid.) He who is in the law acts according to the law, he who is under the law is acted upon according to the law: the one is free, the other a slave. (Ibid. AMBR.) One thing is the law which is written for him that serves, another that which is beheld with the mind by him who has no need of letters. « The will. » (CASS.) That there be no weariness of labour, nor idleness, but he shall meditate always. The will of sense is under the law; of reason, in the law; of divinity, above the law.

VERS. 3.-- « And he shall be. » (Ibid.) Here he is shown useful to us, giving the fruit of life, and leaves, and overshadowing us, 845B« Blessed is the man. But in the law. And he shall be. » The full definition of the blessed man. All these things belong not to every blessed man, but to Christ alone. « As a tree. » (Ibid.) After the likeness of the tree of life which is in paradise, whereof obedient man was to have eaten. « A tree. » (Ibid.) In paradise there is the tree of life, a tree unto life, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. « Of waters. » (AUG.) The waters are the Holy Spirit, according to that word: « He that shall have believed in me, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water (Joan. VII), » and it is against the heats of the vices. (CASS.) Or, by water, the wisdom of God, by which the inner man is restored, as thirst by water. (AUG.) Or the mortal race, as Job: « Many waters, many peoples, » because they flow down into death, as waters into the sea. « He shall give. » (Ibid.) To give pertains to the rational sense and to the will of the one offering. 845C« And the leaf. » (Ibid.) As the leaves cover the fruit, so the words of the Lord guard his promises. « And all things. » (Ibid.) Why go through them one by one.

VERS. 4.-- « Not so the impious. » Here by the vengeance upon the wicked he terrifies the adverse, the dread of these makes what has gone before more welcome. « From the face of the earth. » (AUG.) Of eternal stability, because as this earth nourishes and holds up a man, so that other earth holds up the inner man.

VERS. 5.-- « Therefore they shall not rise again. » Because the wind casteth them away, that is, therefore, because they have been given over to a reprobate sense: therefore they do not rise again in the first resurrection, that they may judge themselves in counsel, that they may set the wills of God before their own. Or in the council, that is, in the harmonious multitude of the just, the impious idolaters, or apostates. Sinners, false Christians: or else therefore they do not rise again in the time to come, 845Dthat they may judge, or that, being judged, they may rest in the council, that is, in the college of the just. « In judgment, etc. » In the judgment there will be four orders: some shall judge and shall not be judged, as the most perfect; some shall neither judge nor be judged, as the damned unbelievers; some shall be judged and shall be saved, as the moderately good; some shall be judged and shall perish, as the evil faithful. « In the council. » (AUG.) In the eternal good, to follow which was counsel to the saints. « Or in the council, » in the judgment, that they may judge together with them; for there is judgment when different sins are punished with different penalties; and it is said from this by likeness. « They rise again. » What resurrections these are: of the soul, from sins in the present; of the body, from death in the time to come, whereby it shall be made impassible and immortal.

846AVERS. 6.-- « For the Lord knoweth, etc., » That is, these do not rise again in the soul, because God does not approve their works, but those of the just only.

PSALMUS II.

« Psalmus. » Modulatio quae fit per tactum decem chordarum est bona operatio, quae fit per observantiam decem mandatorum. « David. » (CASS.) Manu fortis vel pulcher aspectu Christus est, qui aereas debellavit potestates, in quem et angeli prospicere desiderant.

VERS. 1.-- « Quare fremuerunt gentes, etc. » (CASS.) Iste psalmus est secundus in ordine, primus in titulo; unde in Actibus apostolorum dicitur primus. Primo increpat persequentes et minatur, 846Bpraedicit quasi propheta. « Inania. » (Ibid.) Detinere eum in morte; vel, ne mundus post eum abiret.

VERS. 2.-- « Reges. » (Ibid.) Prior qui infantes occidit Herodes, posterior qui Pilato consensit in morte Christi. Reges et principes. (Ibid.) Potuit etiam secundum Ambrosium de uno pluraliter dicere. Solus enim rex Herodes et princeps Pilatus in apostolorum Actibus adversus Christum conspirasse voce Petri produntur.

VERS. 3.-- « Dirumpamus. » (AMB.) Vel convenerunt, dicentes: Dirumpamus rationes eorum, Domini et Christi, vel Christi et discipulorum, quibus nos sibi astringere volunt. (AUG.) Et si aliter posset dici apertius illis convenit qui nolunt jugum Christi sibi imponi. « Vincula. » Promissiones vitae aeternae, 846Cet comminationes gehennae, per quae volunt nos sibi subjugare. « Projiciamus. » Destructis rationibus, dominium ipsius a nobis excutiamus. (Ibid.) Jugum, id est, legem: sed « qui habitat in coelis. »

VERS. 4.-- « Irridebit. » (Ibid.) Ut quando positis custodibus surrexit: « Subsannabit, » quando per mundum dispersi sunt. Irrisio Dei vis est praescientiae quam dat Deus sanctis, ut, videntes nomen Christi futurum in omnibus gentibus, illos inania meditatos intelligant.

VERS. 5.-- « Loquetur ad eos. » (Ibid.) Planius aperit cum dicit, conturbabit. Ira Dei est motus qui fit in anima quae legem Dei novit, cum videt eam a malo praeteriri per quem motum multa vindicantur: vel, ira Dei est obscuratio mentis transgressorum 846Dlegis.

VERS. 6.-- « Ego autem. » (CASS.) Secundo, inducit verba ejus de omnipotenti regno et inenarrabili generatione sua, ubi de divinitate et humanitate ejus discimus. « Rex. » (ID.) Sic et reges terrae ab eo constituti. « Praedicans super Sion, » sic et prophetae, « Filius, » sic et Israel, « Genui te. » Hoc soli Christo.

VERS. 7.-- « Dominus dixit. » Persona regnantis. « Filius meus. » (AUG.) Ideo do tibi gentes haereditatem potius quam alicui obedienti: quia Filius per naturam, et consubstantialis ineffabili genitura. « Hodie. » (Ibid.) Etsi possit accipi de die qua secundum hominem natus est, tamen hodie quia praesentiam 847Asignificat, de sempiterna generatione sapientiae Dei accipiatur.

VERS. 8.-- « Postula. » (AUG.) Ad susceptionem hominis pertinet: quae pro salute hominum facta, secundum quam interpellat pro nobis. « Haereditatem. » (CASS.) Haereditas ab hero, quod in ea potestate libera dominetur.

VERS. 9.-- « Reges eos. » (AUG.) Partim reges, partim franges, secundum illud: « Ecce hic positus est in ruinam et in resurrectionem multorum (Luc. II), » ut qui justus est, justificetur adhuc: et qui in sordibus est, sordescet adhuc (Apoc. XXII). » « Virga ferrea. » (CASS.) Potestas Christi, virga ferrea; peccator, vas figuli, quod et luteum et facile frangitur.

VERS. 10.-- « Et nunc, reges, intelligite. » Nunc, 847Bid est, per ea quae dicta sunt. (CAS.) Tertio pro his patefactis admonet omnes humiliter obedire, et suadet ab utili ne pereant, et ab honesto, quia beati qui confidunt in eo. In hoc post Christum quasi Apostolus loquitur.

(AUG.) Vel, me rege constituto, ne tristemini, reges terrae; expedit enim vobis ut sub illo sitis, a quo est intellectus, et eruditio, ut non temere dominemini, sed Domino omnium serviatis, et in beatitudine exsultetis.

VERS. 12.-- « Nequando irascatur. » (Ibid.) Dubitatio non secundum prophetam, sed secundum ipsos, qui cum dubitatione cogitant iram Dei. « De via justa, » id est, Christo sublati, vel de bona operatione.

847CVERS. 13.-- « Cum exarserit. » (CASS.) Modo non ardet cum castigat, ut pater, sed in futuro ardebit, quia nihil patientiae in futuro erit. « In brevi ira. » Quia non singula horum separatim, sed simul omnia discutit.

PSALM II.

« A psalm. » The modulation that is made by the touching of ten strings is the good work that is done by the keeping of the ten commandments. « David. » (CASS.) Strong of hand, or fair of aspect, is Christ, who warred down the powers of the air, upon whom the angels also desire to look.

VERS. 1.-- « Why have the nations raged, etc. » (CASS.) This psalm is the second in order, the first in title; whence in the Acts of the Apostles it is called the first. First he rebukes the persecutors and threatens them, 846Band foretells as a prophet. « Vain things. » (Ibid.) To hold him in death; or, that the world should not go away after him.

VERS. 2.-- « Kings. » (Ibid.) The former, who slew the infants, is Herod, the latter, he who consented with Pilate in the death of Christ. Kings and princes. (Ibid.) He could also, according to Ambrose, speak in the plural of one man. For only king Herod and prince Pilate are shown by the voice of Peter, in the Acts of the Apostles, to have conspired against Christ.

VERS. 3.-- « Let us break asunder. » (AMB.) Or they came together, saying: Let us break asunder their reasonings, that is, of the Lord and of his Christ, or of Christ and of the disciples, by which they wish to bind us to themselves. (AUG.) And although it might be said otherwise, it fits more openly those who are unwilling that the yoke of Christ be laid upon them. « Bonds. » The promises of eternal life, 846Cand the threatenings of hell, by which they wish to subjugate us to themselves. « Let us cast away. » Their reasonings being destroyed, let us shake off his dominion from us. (Ibid.) The yoke, that is, the law: but « he that dwelleth in the heavens. »

VERS. 4.-- « He shall laugh them to scorn. » (Ibid.) As when he rose again with the guards set: « He shall deride, » when they were scattered through the world. The derision of God is the force of the foreknowledge which God gives to his saints, that, seeing the name of Christ to be in all nations hereafter, they may understand that those men meditated vain things.

VERS. 5.-- « He shall speak to them. » (Ibid.) He opens it more plainly when he says, he shall trouble them. The anger of God is a motion that arises in a soul which knows the law of God, when it sees that law passed over by an evil man, through which motion many things are avenged: or, the anger of God is the darkening of the mind of the transgressors 846Dof the law.

VERS. 6.-- « But I. » (CASS.) Secondly, he brings in his words concerning his almighty kingdom and his unspeakable generation, where we learn of his divinity and his humanity. « King. » (ID.) So also are the kings of the earth appointed by him. « Preaching upon Sion, » so also are the prophets, « The Son, » so also is Israel, « I have begotten thee. » This to Christ alone.

VERS. 7.-- « The Lord hath said. » The person of him that reigns. « My Son. » (AUG.) Therefore do I give thee the nations for an inheritance rather than to any obedient servant: because thou art Son by nature, and consubstantial by an ineffable begetting. « This day. » (Ibid.) Although it might be taken of the day on which he was born according to man, yet, since "this day" signifies 847Aa presence, let it be taken of the everlasting generation of the wisdom of God.

VERS. 8.-- « Ask. » (AUG.) It pertains to the taking up of man: which was done for the salvation of men, and according to which he intercedes for us. « An inheritance. » (CASS.) Inheritance is from lord (herus), because in it he holds dominion with free power.

VERS. 9.-- « Thou shalt rule them. » (AUG.) Partly thou shalt rule, partly thou shalt break, according to that word: « Behold, this one here is set for the ruin and for the resurrection of many (Luc. II), » so that he who is just may be justified still: and he who is in filth shall be defiled still (Apoc. XXII). » « A rod of iron. » (CASS.) The power of Christ is the rod of iron; the sinner is the potter's vessel, which is both of clay and easily broken.

VERS. 10.-- « And now, ye kings, understand. » Now, 847Bthat is, by the things that have been said. (CAS.) Thirdly, on account of these things laid open, he admonishes all to obey humbly, and persuades them from the useful, that they perish not, and from the honourable, because blessed are they that trust in him. In this, after Christ, he speaks as it were an Apostle.

(AUG.) Or, now that I am appointed king, be not sorrowful, ye kings of the earth; for it is expedient for you to be under him, from whom come understanding and learning, that you may not rule rashly, but may serve the Lord of all, and may exult in blessedness.

VERS. 12.-- « Lest at any time he be angry. » (Ibid.) The doubt is not according to the prophet, but according to those men themselves, who think upon the anger of God with doubting. « From the just way, » that is, being taken away from Christ, or from good working.

847CVERS. 13.-- « When his wrath shall be kindled. » (CASS.) Now he does not burn when he chastises, as a father, but in the time to come he will burn, because there will be nothing of patience in the time to come. « In a short time his anger. » Because he examines not each of these things separately, but all of them together.

PSALMUS III.

VERS. 1.-- « Psalmus, » (AUG.) de passione et resurrectione Christi: Filius Judas a quo fugit, cum illo discedente cum caeteris in montem secessit; vel potius cum mentem ejus sapientia Dei deseruit, ut totus esset diaboli, quae desertio fuga propter celeritatem dicitur. Unde: « Quod facis, fac citius (Joan. XIII). » Cui Christus pacem exhibuit, ut et David filio iniquo, unde pax patris dicitur: Judas vero ut Absalon suspensus interiit. Proponit duas partes 847Doppositas. Vox Christi quasi admirantis, cum ad salvandum venit: « Domine, quid, etc. »

VERS. 2.-- « Domine, quid. » (CASS.) Primus psalmus de his qui breviter de passione et resurrectione facit, contra eos, et maxime paganos, qui gloriam majestatis non putant ad humilia posse descendere.

VERS. 3.-- « Multi dicunt, etc. » (AUG.) Vel hoc dicit unusquisque qui a vitiis et cupiditatibus impugnatur.

« Dicunt animae: Non est salus, etc. » Coacervatione vitiorum subrepit desperatio sanitatis, quasi vitiis insultantibus animae; vel etiam diabolis et angelis ejus, per suggestiones.

848AVERS. 4.-- « Susceptor meus es. » (CASS.) In Christo. Caput, Christum, vel mentem quae servit legi Dei. « Percussisti omnes. » Recte in praedestinatione dicitur de diabolo et angelis ejus. « Super populum. » Hoc est unumquemque nostrum. (ID.) Vel hoc loquitur Ecclesia et caput ejus, inter procellas persecutionum per totum orbem constituta. Multi dicunt, Christianum nomen, exstinguere cupientes, « Non est salus. » Aliter non sperarent delere Ecclesiam late pullulantem. « Susceptor. » Quia in Christo suscepta et cum eo exaltata. Caput ipsum qui primus ascendit in coelum.

VERS. 5.-- « Et exaudivit me de monte, etc. » Id est, Christo auditur oratio Ecclesiae, vel justitia.

VERS. 6.-- « Ego dormivi: » secundum illud: 848B« Exsurge a mortuis, et illuminabit tibi Christus (Ephes. V). » Nihil mirum Salvatorem haec dicere, quando multo majora pro animarum salute gessit, quo tempore a corpore abfuit, quae in epistola catholica apud sanctum Petrum recensentur: « Quando iis qui erant in carcere, spiritibus profectas praedicavit, qui increduli aliquando fuerant (I Petr. III). »

VERS. 7.-- « Non timebo millia, » quae nomen Christi conantur exstinguere.-- « Exsurge. » O caput Christe, in cujus resurrectione salus est.

VERS. 8.-- « Quoniam tu percussisti, etc. » Jam regnante Ecclesia, inimici confusione percussi sunt. « Dentes peccatorum, » verba, scilicet, maledica; vel principes in interitum fiunt. Ergo credite, homines, 848Cquod « Domini est salus, » et o Domine « benedictio tua sit super populum tuum. Voce mea. » Haec mihi merito, quia « voce mea. » Qui bonus est, et bona petit, voce sua clamat; aliena voce, id est, vitae suae non concordante. « Ego dormivi. » Finis rei, unde proponit non timendum. « Ego, » cum pondere; quasi: saeviunt illi, sed non dormirem, nisi vellem. Vel, dormivi consentiendo; soporatus, male operando; exsurrexi, peccata deserendo. « Quoniam. » (AUG.) Non retropendet, non praeterea salvum facit quia percussit: sed inde contriti sunt dentes, quia percussit; id est, maledica verba in irritum ducta sunt; vel, dentes, sunt qui quosdam de numero sanctorum praecidunt, et malis incorporant.

PSALM III.

VERS. 1.-- « A psalm, » (AUG.) concerning the passion and resurrection of Christ: the son is Judas, from whom he fled, when, at his departing, he withdrew with the rest into the mountain; or rather when the wisdom of God forsook his mind, so that he was wholly the devil's, which forsaking is called a flight because of its swiftness. Whence: « That which thou dost, do quickly (Joan. XIII). » To him Christ showed peace, as David also did to his wicked son, whence he is called the peace of the father: but Judas, like Absalom, perished by hanging. He sets forth two opposed 847Dparts. The voice of Christ, as it were wondering, when he came to save: « Lord, why, etc. »

VERS. 2.-- « Lord, why. » (CASS.) The first psalm of those which treat briefly of the passion and the resurrection, against those men, and chiefly the pagans, who do not think that the glory of majesty can descend to lowly things.

VERS. 3.-- « Many say, etc. » (AUG.) Or this each man says who is assailed by vices and desires.

« They say to my soul: There is no salvation, etc. » By the heaping up of vices there creeps in a despair of health, as though the vices were insulting the soul; or also by devils and his angels, through suggestions.

848AVERS. 4.-- « Thou art my upholder. » (CASS.) In Christ. The head, that is, Christ, or the mind which serves the law of God. « Thou hast struck all. » It is rightly said in the predestination concerning the devil and his angels. « Upon the people. » This is each one of us. (ID.) Or the Church and its head speaks this, set amid the storms of persecutions throughout the whole world. Many say, desiring to extinguish the Christian name, « There is no salvation. » Otherwise they would not hope to destroy the Church that was sprouting far and wide. « Upholder. » Because it was taken up in Christ and exalted with him. The head is he himself who first ascended into heaven.

VERS. 5.-- « And he hath heard me from the mount, etc. » That is, by Christ the prayer of the Church is heard, or its righteousness.

VERS. 6.-- « I have slept: » according to that word: 848B« Rise from the dead, and Christ shall enlighten thee (Ephes. V). » It is no wonder that the Saviour says these things, when he did far greater things for the salvation of souls at that time when he was absent from the body, which things are recounted in the catholic epistle under the name of Saint Peter: « When he preached, having gone forth, to those spirits who were in prison, who had at one time been unbelieving (I Petr. III). » [Vulg. 1 Pt 3:19 spiritibus veniens praedicavit, "coming, he preached to the spirits"; Migne prints profectas, an unconstruable feminine accusative for what the sense requires as profectus, "having gone forth."]

VERS. 7.-- « I will not fear thousands, » who try to extinguish the name of Christ.-- « Rise up. » O Christ our head, in whose resurrection is salvation.

VERS. 8.-- « For thou hast struck, etc. » Now that the Church reigns, the enemies have been struck with confusion. « The teeth of sinners, » that is, their cursing words; or the princes become teeth unto destruction. Therefore believe, O men, 848Cthat « salvation is the Lord's, » and, O Lord, « let thy blessing be upon thy people. With my voice. » These things are mine by desert, because « with my voice. » He who is good, and asks good things, cries with his own voice; with another's voice, that is, with one not according with his own life. « I have slept. » The end of the matter, whence he sets forth that there is nothing to fear. « I, » with weight; as though: they rage, but I would not sleep, unless I willed it. Or, I slept by consenting; I was made drowsy, by doing evil; I rose up, by forsaking sins. « For. » (AUG.) He does not weigh back, nor besides does he make safe because he has struck: but from thence the teeth were broken, because he struck; that is, the cursing words were brought to nothing; or, the teeth are those who cut off certain men from the number of the saints, and incorporate them among the evil.

PSALMUS IV.

  • 848D

VERS. 1.-- « In finem. » (AUG.) Finis duobus dicitur modis, quando aliquid deficit, vel quando perficitur. (Ibid.) Canticum laetitiam indicat. Psalmi sunt qui cantantur ad psalterium, quo in magno mysterio usus est Propheta. « Psalmus, » de moribus ad agendum, ut deserantur falsi dii et vana saeculi; « Cantici, » quia fit mentio de aeterna jucunditate.

VERS. 2.-- « Cum invocarem, etc. » (CASS.) Exemplo sui increpat infideles de falsis. « Dilatasti mihi. » (Ibid.) Ab angustiis tristitiae in latitudine gaudii duxisti. V. « Gaudemus in tribulationibus scientes quod tribulatio, etc. » (Rom. V.) Prius indicavit se auditum: jam quasi habens in corde 849ADeum, ei loquitur. « Miserere mei. » Misertus de justitia et dilatione. Item, miserere contra miserias hujus vitae. « Orationem meam. » De petendis bonis. Et cum ita de me, « Filii hominum, usquequo gravi corde? »

VERS. 3.-- « Diligitis vanitatem, etc. » (CASS.) Voto amplexamini, quaeritis labore vana idola, et mendacia, quae non Deus: vel terrena, quae non faciunt quod promittunt.

VERS. 4.-- « Et scitote, etc. » Proposito novo homine veterem jubet exuere. (AUG.) Nota, « Et » in initiis poni, ut dicta, cum visione quae in corde est conjungat, ita hic, ut: « Nolite diligere vana. Et scitote. » Sed diapsalma sic conjungi vetat. Diapsalma secundum Hieronymum semper, Hebraei 849BSela, id est, semper in confirmatione praecedentis partis. Sympsalma, id est, conjunctio psalmi. « Dominus exaudiet. » De requie ita, et vos: et ideo clamate, sic digni auditu.

VERS. 5.-- « Irascimini. » Si motus surgit animi qui non est in potestate, non ei consentiat ratio. (CASS.) Motus animi in potestate nostra non est, sed Dei gratia temperare possumus: quod ergo consuetudinis est, permittit; quod culpae, prohibet.

(HIER.) Hoc docet Apostolus: « Sol non occidat super iracundiam vestram (Ephes. IV), » ut peccatum sit omnino vel leviter irasci: justitia autem, iram celeri poenitudine mitigare. « In cordibus vestris. » (AUG.) De his quae tractatis in corde, quem novit Deus: id est, de consensu; et de his quae volvitis 849Cin cubili, id est delectatione carnis, in qua captiva versatur ratio, ut fera in cubili, « Compungimini, » per poenitentiam; vel cubilia sunt cogitationes ferocium. (CASS.) Venialis est ira quae non ducitur ad effectum. Diapsalma. « Sacrificate. » (CASS.) Deposito veteri homine, nos in sacrificium jubemur offerri, quia certi de bonis. (AUG.) « Sacrificium justitiae, » spiritus contribulatus, ut se puniens mactet Deo: vel, opera justa post poenitentiam quod notat diapsalma, ut de veteri vita transeatur ad novam, et sic sperate bona. Sed quia vix est qui diligat interiora bona, subdit:

VERS. 6.-- « Multi dicunt: Quis ostendit nobis bona? » Futura, scilicet de quibus dubitant et desperant. Ad quod respondens ostendit breviter quae 849Dbona sunt quaerenda.

VERS. 7.-- « Signatum est super nos lumen, etc. » (AUG.) Hoc lumen est totum, et verum hominis bonum, quo signatur, ut denarius imagine regis. « Lumen. » (AUG.) Lumen, id est, luminosus vultus, et illuminans nos, imago qua cognosceris. (CASS.) Vel: Crux nobis impressa est, in signum regis nostri, quae est lumen vultus: quia in talibus radiat Deus. Imago creationis, ratio; recreationis, gratia; similitudinis, tota Trinitas. « In corde. (AUG.) Non foris in vanis, sed intus ubi habitat Deus, quaerenda est laetitia.

VERS. 8.-- « A fructu. » (CAS.) Quia putant in his consummatum bonum. Haec tria tanquam usibus 850Ahumanis magis accommoda pro omnibus divitiis ponit.

VERS. 9.-- « In pace in idipsum. » (CASS.) Ego autem in pace mentis dormiam, hic oblitus mundi, et requiescam in futuro: quia jam in una spe, non in multiplicitate saeculi. « In pace dormiam et requiescam. » (AUG.) Ab omnibus saeculi cum mortale hoc induet immortalitatem: et hoc vere erit, quia jam est spes: et hoc est: « Quoniam tu, Domine, » et profecto erit quod speratur.

PSALM IV.

  • 848D

VERS. 1.-- « Unto the end. » (AUG.) The end is said in two ways, when something fails, or when it is completed. (Ibid.) A canticle indicates gladness. Psalms are those things which are sung to the psaltery, which the Prophet used in a great mystery. « A psalm, » concerning morals, for the doing of them, that the false gods and the vanities of the world may be forsaken; « Of a canticle, » because mention is made of the eternal delight.

VERS. 2.-- « When I called upon, etc. » (CASS.) By his own example he rebukes the unbelieving concerning false things. « Thou hast enlarged for me. » (Ibid.) From the straits of sadness thou hast led me into the breadth of joy. V. « We rejoice in tribulations, knowing that tribulation, etc. » (Rom. V.) [Vulg. Rm 5:3 gloriamur in tribulationibus, "we glory in tribulations."] He first showed that he had been heard: now, as though having God in his heart, 849Ahe speaks to him. « Have mercy on me. » He had mercy concerning righteousness and concerning the enlarging. Again, have mercy against the miseries of this life. « My prayer. » Concerning the good things that are to be asked for. And when it is thus concerning me, « Ye sons of men, how long will ye be heavy of heart? »

VERS. 3.-- « Ye love vanity, etc. » (CASS.) With your desire you embrace, with labour you seek vain idols, and lies, which are not God: or earthly things, which do not do what they promise.

VERS. 4.-- « And know ye, etc. » The new man being set forth, he bids them put off the old. (AUG.) Note that « And » is placed at beginnings, so that it may join the things said with the vision that is in the heart, so here, as: « Love not vain things. And know ye. » But the diapsalma forbids their being so joined. Diapsalma, according to Jerome, is always, the Hebrews, 849BSela, that is, always, in confirmation of the preceding part. Sympsalma, that is, the joining of a psalm. « The Lord will hear. » Concerning rest it is thus, and so with you: and therefore cry out, being thus worthy to be heard.

VERS. 5.-- « Be ye angry. » If a motion of the soul arises which is not in our power, let not reason consent to it. (CASS.) A motion of the soul is not in our power, but by the grace of God we are able to temper it: what therefore belongs to custom, he permits; what belongs to fault, he forbids.

(HIER.) This the Apostle teaches: « Let not the sun go down upon your anger (Ephes. IV), » so that it is altogether a sin to be angry even lightly: but it is righteousness to soften anger by a swift repentance. « In your hearts. » (AUG.) Concerning those things which you handle in the heart, which God knows: that is, concerning consent; and concerning those things which you turn over 849Cin the bed, that is, in the delight of the flesh, in which reason dwells captive, as a wild beast in its lair, « Be ye pricked, » through penance; or the beds are the thoughts of the fierce. (CASS.) Venial is the anger which is not carried through to effect. Diapsalma. « Sacrifice ye. » (CASS.) The old man being laid aside, we are bidden to be offered in sacrifice, because we are sure of good things. (AUG.) « The sacrifice of righteousness, » a contrite spirit, that, punishing itself, it may be slain to God: or, just works after penance, which the diapsalma marks, that from the old life there may be a passing over to the new, and so hope ye for good things. But because there is scarcely one who loves the inner goods, he adds:

VERS. 6.-- « Many say: Who showeth us good things? » Things to come, namely, of which they doubt and despair. Answering to which he shows briefly what 849Dgood things are to be sought.

VERS. 7.-- « The light is signed upon us, etc. » (AUG.) This light is the whole and the true good of man, wherewith he is signed, as a penny with the image of the king. « Light. » (AUG.) Light, that is, a shining countenance, and one that enlightens us, an image whereby thou art known. (CASS.) Or: the cross has been imprinted upon us, for a sign of our king, which is the light of the countenance: because in such men God shines out. The image of creation is reason; of re-creation, grace; of likeness, the whole Trinity. « In the heart. (AUG.) Not without in vain things, but within, where God dwells, is gladness to be sought.

VERS. 8.-- « From the fruit. » (CAS.) Because they think that in these things the good is consummated. These three, as being more suited to human 850Auses, he sets down for all riches.

VERS. 9.-- « In peace in the selfsame. » (CASS.) But I will sleep in the peace of the mind, here forgetful of the world, and I will rest in the time to come: because I am already in one hope, not in the manifoldness of the world. « In peace I will sleep and I will rest. » (AUG.) From all the things of the world, when this mortal shall put on immortality: and this will truly be, because it is already hope: and this is: « For thou, O Lord, » and assuredly that will be which is hoped for.

PSALMUS V.

VERS. 1.-- « Pro ea quae consequitur haereditatem. » Quia hic honoratur cui habenda haereditas affirmatur, a qua aemula excluditur. Ecclesia est, 850Bquae haereditatem, id est, vitam aeternam, ipsum Deum accipit, quae hic loquitur de haereditate, quam sibi petit, et asserit, aemulam dicens excludi. (BEDA.) Id est, pro Ecclesia, quae, Christo resurgente, bonorum spiritualium dona percepit, quae et ipsa nonnunquam Domini vocatur haereditas, cujus pretioso est sanguine comparata: unde dictum est: « Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes, haereditatem tuam. » Totus ergo psalmus a persona catholicae profertur Ecclesiae, quae prima sectione orationem suam poscit audiri, haereticos et schismaticos praedicans a Domini muneribus esse excludendos. Secunda sectione per intellectum Scripturarum divinarum recto tramite dirigi se ad illam felicem patriam deprecatur, perfidos inde asserens funditus 850Cfieri alienos. Ad postremum commemorans praemia beatorum, ut una praedicatione et malos praedicta poena converteret, et justos promissa praemia concitarent.

VERS. 2.-- « Verba mea. » (CASS.) Hic innuit propheta trinam orationem esse faciendam. Sunt enim tria principalia vitia in prosperis, tria in adversis: contra quae trinam debemus facere orationem. In prosperis, contra carnis concupiscentiam, contra concupiscentiam oculorum, contra superbiam vitae. In adversis, contra timorem mortis, periculi, utilitatis. (Ibid.) Trina oratio, verba, oris psalmodiam, clamorem, cordis affectum, ideo: « Exaudies. » Ecce ter de eodem. « Auribus. » Aures Dei sunt potentia, clementia. Potentia, qua potest: clementia, 850Dqua vult audire; nisi enim esset clementia, nullius preces exaudiret.

VERS. 3.-- « Voci. » Illa oratio vocem habet, quae est digna audiri. « Rex. » (AUG.) Proprie Filius, bene primo rex, quia per eum itur ad Patrem, unde subdit: Et « Deus meus: » et tamen non dicit intendite, sed intende, quia unus Deus.

VERS. 4.-- « Quoniam, etc. » (AUG.) Hucusque oratio ut audiatur, etc., usque ad et hoc mane mox ut tenebras deserit.

VERS. 5.-- « Mane astabo. » (CASS.) Vel, mane quando incipiet aeternitas, et tunc plene videbo quod non placet iniquitas: quia tunc non habitabit, « sed tolletur impius, ne videat gloriam Dei (Isa. 851AXXVI): » et tunc non permanebunt, etsi misericordiam ejus habuerint.

VERS. 6.-- « Neque permanebunt injusti. » Qui mala faciunt. Nam odisti qui operantur, non qui operati sunt.

VERS. 7.-- « Perdes omnes qui loquuntur mendacium. » (AUG.) Quia hoc est veritati contrarium. Veritas est de eo quod est. Mendacium non est substantia vel natura, sed de eo quod non est, et merito perditur, quod declinat ab eo quod est ad id quod non est. (Ibid.) Mentiri est loqui contra hoc quod animo sentitur. (Ibid.) Sunt mendacia quaedam pro salute, etc., usque ad non cogitavi furentem posse repetere.

VERS. 8.-- « Ego autem. » (AUG.) Tertio, dicit se 851Bfuturam domum Dei, et nunc proximare in timore ante consummationem, quae expellit timorem.

« Introibo. » (CASS.) Per hoc introibo, quia adorabo. (Ibid.) Petit contra ea quae aemula ingerit: unde ipsa peribit.

VERS. 9.-- « Domine, deduc. » (AUG.) Quarto, proficiens inter impedimenta orat juvari intus, ne linguis dolosis avertatur. « In justitia tua. » (CASS.) Quia poenitentes et supplices recipis. « In conspectu. » (AUG.) Ubi homo non videt, cui laudanti vel vituperanti non est credendum: quia non videt in conscientia, in qua iter ad Deum dirigitur. Ideo subdit: « Quoniam non est in ore eorum veritas. »

VERS. 10.-- « Quoniam non est, etc. » Non modo non est veritas in ore, sed sepulcrum: quia fetida 851Cpromunt ad corrumpendum, quibus si non proficiunt, dolose agunt, id est, non modo moliuntur, sed efficiunt.

VERS. 11, 12.-- « Judica illos Deus. Decidant a cogitationibus suis. » Non optat, sed quod futurum est praedicit. Decidit qui spe bona frustratur.

« Et laetentur. » (CASS.) Post retributiones malorum subdit praemia bonorum, ut sicut poena terret, praemia incitent.

VERS. 13.-- « Ut scuto. (CASS.) Uno verbo indicat beneficia Dei gratuita. Voluntas quae vocat, est defensio contra omnia, et corona, et clypeus. Capiti aptatus corona est, cordi defensio.

PSALM V.

VERS. 1.-- « For her that obtaineth the inheritance. » Because he is honoured here to whom the inheritance is affirmed to belong, from which the rival is shut out. It is the Church, 850Bwhich receives the inheritance, that is, eternal life, God himself, which here speaks of the inheritance which it asks for itself and asserts, saying that the rival is shut out. (BEDA.) That is, for the Church, which, at Christ's rising again, received the gifts of spiritual goods, which is itself also sometimes called the Lord's inheritance, purchased with his precious blood: whence it is said: « Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles, thy inheritance. » The whole psalm therefore is uttered in the person of the catholic Church, which in the first section asks that her prayer be heard, proclaiming that heretics and schismatics are to be shut out from the Lord's gifts. In the second section she prays that by the understanding of the divine Scriptures she may be directed by a straight path to that happy country, asserting that the faithless are thereby made utterly 850Cstrangers to it. At the last, calling to mind the rewards of the blessed, that by one preaching the punishment foretold might convert the wicked also, and the promised rewards rouse the just.

VERS. 2.-- « My words. » (CASS.) Here the prophet hints that a threefold prayer is to be made. For there are three principal vices in prosperity, three in adversity: against which we ought to make a threefold prayer. In prosperity, against the concupiscence of the flesh, against the concupiscence of the eyes, against the pride of life. In adversity, against the fear of death, of peril, of profit. (Ibid.) A threefold prayer: words, the psalmody of the mouth, a cry, the affection of the heart, therefore: « Thou shalt hear. » Behold, three times of the same thing. « With thine ears. » The ears of God are power, mercy. Power, whereby he can: mercy, 850Dwhereby he wills to hear; for unless there were mercy, he would hear no one's prayers.

VERS. 3.-- « To the voice. » That prayer has a voice which is worthy to be heard. « King. » (AUG.) Properly the Son, rightly first king, because through him one goes to the Father, whence he adds: And « my God: » and yet he does not say attend ye, but attend, because God is one.

VERS. 4.-- « For, etc. » (AUG.) Thus far the prayer, that it may be heard, etc., as far as and this in the morning, as soon as it forsakes the darkness.

VERS. 5.-- « In the morning I will stand. » (CASS.) Or, in the morning when eternity shall begin, and then I shall fully see that iniquity pleases not: because then it shall not dwell, « but the wicked shall be taken away, that he may not see the glory of God (Isa. 851AXXVI): » [Vulg. Is 26:10 et non videbit gloriam Domini, "and he shall not see the glory of the Lord"; the Vulgate has nothing answering to tolletur impius] and then they shall not remain, even though they have had his mercy.

VERS. 6.-- « Neither shall the unjust remain. » Who do evil things. For thou hast hated those who work them, not those who have worked them.

VERS. 7.-- « Thou wilt destroy all that speak a lie. » (AUG.) Because this is contrary to truth. Truth is of that which is. A lie is not a substance or a nature, but is of that which is not, and deservedly is that destroyed which turns aside from that which is to that which is not. (Ibid.) To lie is to speak against that which is felt in the mind. (Ibid.) There are certain lies told for safety's sake, etc., as far as I did not consider that one raving could demand it back.

VERS. 8.-- « But I. » (AUG.) Thirdly, he says that he 851Bwill be the house of God, and that now he draws near in fear, before that consummation which casts out fear.

« I will go in. » (CASS.) By this I shall go in, because I shall adore. (Ibid.) He asks against those things which the rival brings in: whence she herself shall perish.

VERS. 9.-- « Lord, lead me. » (AUG.) Fourthly, making progress amid hindrances, he prays to be helped within, lest he be turned aside by deceitful tongues. « In thy justice. » (CASS.) Because thou receivest the penitent and the suppliant. « In thy sight. » (AUG.) Where man does not see, who is not to be believed whether he praise or blame: because he does not see into the conscience, in which the way to God is directed. Therefore he adds: « For there is no truth in their mouth. »

VERS. 10.-- « For there is not, etc. » Not only is there no truth in the mouth, but a sepulchre: because they bring forth stinking things 851Cto corrupt, and if they do not prevail with them, they act deceitfully, that is, they do not only contrive, but accomplish.

VERS. 11, 12.-- « Judge them, O God. Let them fall from their thoughts. » He does not wish it, but foretells what shall be. He falls away who is disappointed of a good hope.

« And let them be glad. » (CASS.) After the retributions of the wicked he adds the rewards of the good, that as the punishment terrifies, so the rewards may incite.

VERS. 13.-- « As with a shield. (CASS.) In one word he indicates the free benefits of God. The will which calls is a defence against all things, and a crown, and a shield. Fitted to the head it is a crown, to the heart, a defence.

PSALMUS VI.

851DVERS. 1.-- « Octava » est adventus Domini, in qua peccator timet argui, et ideo poenitet. (AUG.) Octavam dicunt aliqui adventum Domini, etc., usque ad unde timens Ecclesia hic orat.

VERS. 2.-- « Domine, ne in furore. » (BASIL.) Confessio est deprecativa, quae apud Deum valet. Primo est exordium, in quo captat benevolentiam, per potestatem judicis, per infirmitatem suam, per consuetudinem parcendi: quia non vult a mortuis, sed a vivis rogari. « Arguas. » (AUG.) Argui gravius est quam accusari, unde damnatio timetur. Corripi mitius, id est, emendari vel erudiri. Arguuntur in judicio, qui sine fundamento. Emendantur, id est, purgantur, qui supra illud lignum, fenum, stipulam 852Aaedificaverunt. Dicit ergo hic: « Sana, » ne ibi sit opus, unde subdit: « Miserere. »

VERS. 3.-- « Infirmus » (AUG.) Reatu infirmatur anima, a quo sana, quia ossa, id est, mens conturbatur ad praesentiam, et anima, id est, sensualitas: ergo usquequo differs, quasi dicat: Quid restat quin sanes? « Usquequo. » (AUG.) Innuit se diu luctari cum vitiis. Non est autem crudelitas dilatio Dei, sed ut persuadeat animae, in quae mala se praecipitavit. Nondum enim tam perfecte orat, ut ei dicatur: « Adhuc te loquente dicam, ecce adsum (Isa. LXV). » Ut ex difficultate sanationis inde magis caveat sibi, et ut ostendatur quae poena sit non conversis, si tanta difficultas sit conversis, unde: « Si justus vix salvabitur, impius ubi apparebit? » (I Petr. IV.)

852BVERS. 5.-- « Convertere. » (CASS.) Qui aversus eras, vel a vindicta. « Eripe, » ab imminente morte. Vel eripe animam peccatis ligatam. « Salvum me fac, etc., » dando virtutes.

VERS. 6.-- « Quoniam non est. » (CASS.) Ideo hic festino dimitti, quia post mortem et in inferno non accipitur confessio. « In inferno. (AUG.) Confessus est dives, qui Lazarum vidit, etsi de profundo, cujus comparatione coactus est confiteri mala sua, usque adeo, ut et fratres roget ab his praemoneri: sed post judicium in profundioribus tenebris nullam lucem Dei videbunt, cui confiteantur. Vel, mortem dicit peccatum in quo immemor est Dei qui mandata ejus contemnit.

VERS. 7.-- « Laboravi. » (CASS.) Narrat aerumnas 852Cquibus poenitentes avertitur; gemit dum videt quid egit, et quae poena futura. « Lectum. » Conscientiam, quae quibusdam quies, quibusdam tormentum. Stratum, sensualitatem; fertilem faciam, quae erat arida. Vel, lectus delectatio corporis, in qua homo resolvitur. Stratus, cumulus peccatorum ut vestium, quo resoluto, imbre lacrymarum, nova messis virtutum crescat.

VERS. 8.-- « A furore. » (AUG.) Ab ira, vel Dei, quae in judicio, etc., usque ad ne quis desperet de gravitate peccatorum, subdit: « Discedite, etc. » (CASS.) Correptio, ut separetur ab illis, quorum collegio peccavit, et insistat mandatis Dei. « Inimicos, » (AUG.) id est, vitia, vel malos homines, qui vere sunt inimici ad Deum se convertentium, a quibus 852Dseparatur omnis bonus, non loco, sed animo. Quia vero non est inanis tantus labor poenitentiae, exauditum se significans, subdit: « Discedite. »

VERS. 9, 10.-- « Dominus. » Ter Dominus, quia Trinitatem affuisse precibus ostendit: Incepit a lacrymis, exauditus exsultat. « Exaudivit Dominus. » (CAS.) Dat exemplum fideliter orantes audiri.

VERS. 11.-- « Erubescant et conturbentur. » (CASS.) Quasi in conclusione, jam liber a peccatis, exsultans, pro inimicis, ut convertantur, orat, ut, sicut ipse, habeant veniam. (AUG.) « Erubescant. » Hoc non hic (ubi potius irrident eos qui omnia relinquunt, et infirmos erubescere faciunt), sed in judicio.

PSALM VI.

851DVERS. 1.-- « The octave » is the coming of the Lord, in which the sinner fears to be rebuked, and therefore repents. (AUG.) Some call the octave the coming of the Lord, etc., as far as whence the Church, fearing, here prays.

VERS. 2.-- « O Lord, not in thy fury. » (BASIL.) It is a deprecatory confession, which avails with God. First there is an exordium, in which he wins goodwill, by the power of the judge, by his own weakness, by the custom of sparing: because he wills to be entreated not by the dead, but by the living. « Rebuke. » (AUG.) To be rebuked is graver than to be accused, whence damnation is feared. To be chastised is milder, that is, to be amended or instructed. They are rebuked in the judgment, who are without a foundation. They are amended, that is, purged, who have built upon that foundation wood, hay, stubble. 852AHere therefore he says: « Heal, » lest there be work there, whence he adds: « Have mercy. »

VERS. 3.-- « Weak » (AUG.) The soul is made weak by guilt, from which do thou heal her, because the bones, that is, the mind, is troubled at his presence, and the soul, that is, sensuality: therefore how long dost thou put it off, as if he said: What remains but that thou shouldst heal? « How long. » (AUG.) He hints that he has long wrestled with vices. But God's delay is not cruelty, but is that he may convince the soul into what evils she has flung herself. For she does not yet pray so perfectly that it may be said to her: « While thou art yet speaking I will say, behold I am here (Isa. LXV). » [Vulg. Is 65:24 adhuc illis loquentibus, ego audiam, "while they are yet speaking, I will hear"] That out of the difficulty of the healing she may thereafter be the more on her guard, and that it may be shown what punishment there is for the unconverted, if there is so great a difficulty for the converted, whence: « If the just man shall scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly appear? » (I Petr. IV.)

852BVERS. 5.-- « Turn thee. » (CASS.) Thou who wast turned away, or, from vengeance. « Deliver, » from imminent death. Or, deliver the soul bound by sins. « Save me, etc., » by giving virtues.

VERS. 6.-- « For there is not. » (CASS.) Therefore I hasten to be released here, because after death and in hell confession is not received. « In hell. (AUG.) The rich man confessed who saw Lazarus, although out of the deep, and by comparison with him he was compelled to confess his own evils, even so far as to ask that his brothers also be forewarned by these: but after the judgment, in the deeper darkness, they shall see no light of God, to whom they might confess. Or, he calls death the sin in which he is unmindful of God who despises his commandments.

VERS. 7.-- « I have laboured. » (CASS.) He narrates the hardships 852Cby which penitents are turned away poenitentes avertitur; he groans while he sees what he has done, and what punishment is to come. « The bed. » The conscience, which to some is rest, to some torment. The couch, sensuality; I will make fertile what was dry. Or, the bed is the delight of the body, in which a man is dissolved. The couch, the heap of sins as of garments, which being loosed, by the shower of tears, a new harvest of virtues may grow.

VERS. 8.-- « From wrath. » (AUG.) From anger, either God's, which is in the judgment, etc., as far as lest any despair because of the grievousness of his sins, he adds: « Depart, etc. » (CASS.) A chastisement, that he may be separated from those in whose company he sinned, and may press on in the commandments of God. « Enemies, » (AUG.) that is, vices, or evil men, who are truly the enemies of those who turn themselves to God, from whom 852Devery good man is separated, not in place, but in mind. But because so great a labour of penitence is not vain, signifying that he has been heard, he adds: « Depart. »

VERS. 9, 10.-- « The Lord. » Thrice the Lord, because he shows that the Trinity was present to his prayers: he began with tears, being heard he exults. « The Lord hath heard. » (CAS.) He gives an example that those who pray faithfully are heard.

VERS. 11.-- « Let them be ashamed and be troubled. » (CASS.) As in conclusion, now free from sins, exulting, he prays for his enemies, that they may be converted, that, like himself, they may have pardon. (AUG.) « Let them be ashamed. » Not here (where rather they mock those who leave all things, and make the weak ashamed), but in the judgment.

PSALMUS VII.

  • 853A

VERS. 1.-- « In finem, psalmus. (AUG.) Chusi, qui transivit in partem Absalon, etc., usque ad non enim erat eis abscondendum, pro quibus gestum est. (AUG.) Potest hic psalmus in persona Christi intelligi; si qua humiliter dicta sunt, ad infirmitatem nostram referantur, quam gestavit. Primo petit ex omnibus tribulationibus liberari.

VERS. 2.-- « Domine Deus. » (CASS.) Iste est primus psalmus eorum, in quibus per actus David futura mysteria Domini significantur. Mysterium incarnationis, silentium fuit Judaeis; ut David a filio, ita Christus a populo, quem nutrierat, persecutionem sustinuit. « Libera. » (AUG.) Quasi, superato 853Bomni bello vitiorum, jam profecto nihil restat, nisi invidus diabolus.

VERS. 3.-- « Rapiat, etc. » « Redimat, etc. » (CASS.) Propria verba: Domini est liberare, leonis rapere. Ordo, prius persequentes ponit, inde leonem. Expiatus enim ab omnibus spiritualibus nequitiis a diabolo liberatur.

VERS. 4, 5.-- « Domine, si feci istud. » (Ibid.) Ad litteram de David, et Absalon. « Si feci istud, » id est, si hoc malum mihi per praeteritam culpam contigit. Vel si modo est iniquitas in manibus, id est, operibus meis. Vel, « si reddidi retribuentibus mihi mala, etc., » (quod dicitur aequitas apud homines), « merito » (etsi non videatur hominibus) « decidam ab inimicis meis inanis, » a fructu mansuetudinis.

853C(AUG.) « Si feci istud, » vel, universale peccatum, quod sine nomine dixit, quod est superbia, quae est radix omnium malorum. Vel, quod sequitur, « si est iniquitas, » quod de omni peccato accipitur. « Si reddidi. » (Ibid.) Id est, si te non sum imitatus in justo silentio, id est, patientia, quae pro me operatus es. « Decidam merito ab inimicis. » (Ibid.) Non jurejurando hoc sibi imprecatur, sed dicit quod contingit se vindicantibus: prophetat ergo, non jurat per exsecrationem; quod est gravissimum jurisjurandi genus. Inanis factus vana et superba laetitia, quod quasi vinci non potuit: Salomon, « Melior est qui vincit iram, quam qui cepit civitatem » (Prov. XVI).

853DVERS. 6.-- « Conculcet, etc. » (Ibid.) Anima peccatoris de quo, « Terra es, et in terram reverteris (Gen. III), » cibus serpentis est cui in maledictione dictum est, ( « Terram manducabis, » ) id est, diaboli, quia terra, id est, terrena est. Et ideo hic ait: « Conculcet in terra vitam meam, id est, in terram redactam sibi incorporet, et ibi sit despicabilis. « Gloriam meam. » (Ibid.) Quae debet esse in conscientia, ubi Deus videt; et solida in Domino, ut: « Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur (I Cor. I). » « Deducat in pulverem, » id est, in superbiam et jactantiam, ut scilicet velim gloriari apud homines. « In pulverem deducat. Pulvis quem projicit ventus. » (Ibid.) Superborum jactantia. Vult ergo ut 854Agloria sua sit solida intus, ubi Deus videt: est enim pulvis, si apud homines gloriatur; ecce quam cavenda superbia.

VERS. 7, 8.-- « Exsurge, Domine. » Petit ut gloria resurrectionis Christi subveniat. « In ira tua. » Perfectus enim iste non precatur hic adversus homines, sed adversus diabolum, ut possessionem ejus amittat, peccatores, scilicet et impios, qui sunt ejus possessio. Et quia ablatio hominis, quia poena est diabolo, dicitur ira Dei contra eum. Vel, precatur hic Christi resurrectionem, sicut in praecedenti, ejus incarnationem: ut « O Domine Deus meus, etc. » « In finibus. » Mundus, vel infernus, sunt fines diaboli.

« Et exsurge, Domine. » Superbus diabolus, quia 854Bper iniquitatem vincitur, subdit: Vel, « Exsurge, » id est, in toto orbe notus efficere, resurgendo. « In praecepto, » ut praeceptum humilitatis facias implere: et hoc inde sequitur, quia Synagoga de diversis populis, vel specialiter Judaeis, « circumdabit te, » amando, vel persequendo: « Propter hanc, » id est, amantem, « regredere, » id est, fac scire eos omnipotentiam tuam, qui descendisti ut te viderent; vel « propter hanc, » id est, persequentem, in qua locum non invenis, « regredere in altum, » id est, subtrahere his qui te persequuntur. « Synagoga. » (Ibid.) Congregatio populi, etc., usque ad Dominus judicat, de judicio regressi, id est, Christi. « Innocentiam. » (Ibid.) Quia non reddidi retribuentibus mihi. « Super me. » (Ibid.) Justitia et innocentia 854Csunt super me, quia non a me, sed a Deo.

VERS. 10.-- « Scrutans corda. » (Ibid.) Quid quisque cogitet. « Renes. » Quid quemque delectet; quia finis curae et cogitationis est delectatio, ad quam nititur pervenire. Opera nostra in dictis et in factis possunt videre homines: sed quo animo fiant, et quo pervenire cupiant, solus videt Deus; qui cum videt cor esse in coelo, et non delectari in carne, sed in Domino, id est, cum bonae sunt cogitationes, et earum fines dirigit justum, et non solum dirigit, sed adjuvat justum.

VERS. 11.-- « Justum adjutorium. » (Ibid.) Duo sunt officia medicinae, scilicet morbum sanare et sanitatem custodire. Secundum primum dixit in alio psalmo: « Infirmus sum, sana me, Domine. » Juxta 854Dalteram dicit hic perfectus, « justum adjutorium meum a Domino. » Et illa enim et ista medicina salvos facit: sed illa ex aegritudine transfert ad salutem, haec in ipsa salute conservat. Illa ad morbum evadendum, remedium; haec autem ne ad morbum recidat, remedium praestat. Illa sanamur infirmi, hac custodimur sani.

VERS. 12.-- « Deus judex. » (CASS.) Hic metu futuri judicii terret, et spem reversis promittit. « Nunquid irascitur. » (AUG.) Alia littera: « Nunquid adducit iram per singulos dies. » In Graeco significantius, « adducit iram: » quia non in ipso est ira qua punit, sed in angelis irae, per quos punit: qui non propter justitiam qua non gaudent, sed propter 855Amalitiam, poena humana delectantur: quos per singulos dies non congregat ad vindictam, sed per patientiam ad poenitentiam invitat.
