VERS. 13.-- « Gladium suum. » (AUG.) Alia littera: Frameam suam splendificavit. (CASS.) « Gladium suum, » manifestam vindictam exercebit, nec impar dictum est hoc, quia arcum suum tetendit, » minatur, ne putetur remissa patientia; « paravit, » ut mox missurus sagittam putetur. « Arcum suum. » (Ibid.) A simili. Sicut enim qui tetendit arcum minatur, ita per sacram Scripturam minatur malis, ne remissa putetur Dei patientia; et « paravit, » qui mox missurus sagittam putetur: sicut quis arcum parat, ut sagittam mittat. « Arcum suum tetendit, » (AUG.) temperando Vetus Testamentum 855Bper Novum Testamentum: « Paravit, » per explanationem. (Ibid.) Vel, « paravit. » Parat et disponit Deus, etc., usque ad sed ardentibus studio, sagittae.

VERS. 15.-- « Ecce. » Quasi, haec paravit Deus in Scripturis. (Ibid.) Unde videtur homini esse causa damnationis. Sed « ecce » quod non ex Deo, sed ex homine est, quia « lacum aperuit, etc. Concepit dolorem, » (Ibid.) id est, appetitu temporalium rerum. « Peperit, » effecit, emisit: et in emissa iniquitate est lacus, id est, praecipitium aliis. Unde subdit:

VERS. 16.-- « Lacum aperuit. » Et sic est comparabilis aperienti lacum: aperit enim concipiendo 855Cfraudem: effodit parturiendo, instando operi fraudis; incidit pariendo fraudem, scilicet, perpetrando.

VERS. 17.-- « Convertetur dolor, etc. » Caput, anima, vertex, ratio: cui dominantur peccata, et supersunt: et superdescendent cum in poenas detrudent.

VERS. 18.-- « Confitebor Domino. » (CASS.) Conclusio, quasi omnia in summam colligens, alacriter se dicit confiteri.

PSALM VII.

  • 853A

VERS. 1.-- « Unto the end, a psalm. (AUG.) Chusi, who went over to Absalom's party, etc., as far as for it was not to be hidden from those for whom it was done. (AUG.) This psalm can be understood in the person of Christ; if any things are said humbly, let them be referred to our weakness, which he bore. First he asks to be delivered out of all tribulations.

VERS. 2.-- « O Lord my God. » (CASS.) This is the first of those psalms in which by the acts of David the future mysteries of the Lord are signified. The mystery of the incarnation was a silence to the Jews; as David from his son, so Christ endured persecution from the people whom he had nourished. « Deliver. » (AUG.) As it were, when 853Bevery war of the vices has been overcome, now indeed nothing remains but the envious devil.

VERS. 3.-- « Lest he seize, etc. » « Who may redeem, etc. » (CASS.) Proper words: it belongs to the Lord to deliver, to the lion to seize. The order, first he sets the persecutors, then the lion. For when a man has been cleansed from all spiritual wickednesses he is delivered from the devil.

VERS. 4, 5.-- « O Lord, if I have done this. » (Ibid.) Literally, of David and Absalom. « If I have done this, » that is, if this evil has befallen me through a past fault. Or, if there be now iniquity in my hands, that is, in my works. Or, « if I have rendered evils to them that repaid me, etc., » (which is called equity among men), « deservedly » (even though it may not seem so to men) « let me fall away from my enemies empty, » from the fruit of meekness.

853C(AUG.) « If I have done this, » or, the universal sin, which he named without a name, which is pride, which is the root of all evils. Or, that which follows, « if there is iniquity, » which is taken of every sin. « If I have rendered. » (Ibid.) That is, if I have not imitated thee in a just silence, that is, in the patience which thou didst work for me. « Let me deservedly fall away from my enemies. » (Ibid.) He does not imprecate this on himself by an oath, but says what befalls those who avenge themselves: he prophesies therefore, he does not swear by an execration; which is the gravest kind of oath. Made empty by a vain and proud gladness, in that he could as it were not be overcome: Solomon, « Better is he that overcometh anger than he that taketh a city » (Prov. XVI). [Vulg. Prv 16:32 Melior est patiens viro forti, et qui dominatur animo suo expugnatore urbium, "Better is the patient man than the valiant, and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh cities"]

853DVERS. 6.-- « Let him tread down, etc. » (Ibid.) The soul of the sinner, of which, « Earth thou art, and into earth thou shalt return (Gen. III), » [Vulg. Gn 3:19 pulvis es et in pulverem reverteris, "dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return"] is the food of the serpent, to whom it was said in the malediction, ( « Earth shalt thou eat, » ) that is, of the devil, because it is earth, that is, earthly. And therefore he here says: « Let him tread down my life in the earth, that is, let him incorporate it into himself when it has been brought down to earth, and let it there be despicable. « My glory. » (Ibid.) Which ought to be in the conscience, where God sees; and solid in the Lord, as: « He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord (I Cor. I). » « Let him bring down into the dust, » that is, into pride and boasting, namely that I should wish to glory among men. « Let him bring down into the dust. The dust which the wind casteth forth. » (Ibid.) The boasting of the proud. He wishes therefore that 854Ahis glory be solid within, where God sees: for it is dust, if he glories among men; behold how greatly pride is to be shunned.

VERS. 7, 8.-- « Arise, O Lord. » He asks that the glory of Christ's resurrection may come to his aid. « In thy anger. » For this perfect man does not here pray against men, but against the devil, that he may lose his possession, namely sinners and the ungodly, who are his possession. And because the taking away of a man, because it is a punishment to the devil, is called the anger of God against him. Or, he prays here for Christ's resurrection, as in the preceding for his incarnation: as « O Lord my God, etc. » « In the borders. » The world, or hell, are the borders of the devil.

« And arise, O Lord. » The devil is proud, because 854Bhe is overcome by iniquity, he adds: Or, « Arise, » that is, be made known in the whole world, by rising again. « In the precept, » that thou mayest make the precept of humility to be fulfilled: and this follows thereupon, because the Synagogue, out of divers peoples, or specially of the Jews, « shall compass thee about, » by loving, or by persecuting: « For this, » that is, for her that loves, « return, » that is, make them know thy omnipotence, thou who didst descend that they might see thee; or « for this, » that is, for her that persecutes, in whom thou findest no place, « return on high, » that is, withdraw thyself from those who persecute thee. « Synagogue. » (Ibid.) The congregation of the people, etc., as far as the Lord judges, of the judgment of him that returned, that is, of Christ. « Innocence. » (Ibid.) Because I have not rendered to them that repaid me. « Upon me. » (Ibid.) Justice and innocence 854Care upon me, because not from me, but from God.

VERS. 10.-- « Searching the hearts. » (Ibid.) What each one thinks. « The reins. » What delights each one; because the end of care and of thought is delight, to which one strives to attain. Men can see our works in words and in deeds: but with what mind they are done, and whither they desire to attain, God alone sees; who, when he sees the heart to be in heaven, and not to be delighted in the flesh, but in the Lord, that is, when the thoughts are good, directs also their ends, the just man, and not only directs, but helps the just man.

VERS. 11.-- « A just help. » (Ibid.) There are two offices of medicine, namely to heal disease and to keep health. According to the first he said in another psalm: « I am weak, heal me, O Lord. » According to 854Dthe other this perfect man here says, « my just help is from the Lord. » For both that medicine and this make men whole: but that one carries a man over from sickness to health, this preserves him in health itself. That one is a remedy for escaping disease; this affords a remedy lest he fall back into disease. By that one we are healed when sick, by this we are kept when whole.

VERS. 12.-- « God the judge. » (CASS.) Here he terrifies by the fear of the judgment to come, and promises hope to those who return. « Is he angry. » (AUG.) Another reading: « Doth he bring anger every day. » In the Greek more significantly, « he bringeth anger: » because the anger with which he punishes is not in himself, but in the angels of anger, through whom he punishes: who are delighted with human punishment not for the sake of the justice in which they do not rejoice, but for the sake of 855Amalice: whom he does not gather every day for vengeance, but by patience invites to repentance.

VERS. 13.-- « His sword. » (AUG.) Another reading: He hath made bright his javelin. (CASS.) « His sword, » he will exercise manifest vengeance, nor is this said unequally, because he hath bent his bow, » he threatens, lest his patience be thought remiss; « he hath prepared, » that he may be thought about presently to send the arrow. « His bow. » (Ibid.) From a like case. For as he who has bent a bow threatens, so through sacred Scripture he threatens the wicked, lest the patience of God be thought remiss; and « he hath prepared, » who may be thought about presently to send an arrow: as one prepares a bow, that he may send an arrow. « He hath bent his bow, » (AUG.) by tempering the Old Testament 855Bthrough the New Testament: « He hath prepared, » by explanation. (Ibid.) Or, « he hath prepared. » God prepares and disposes, etc., as far as but for those burning with zeal, arrows.

VERS. 15.-- « Behold. » As it were, these things God hath prepared in the Scriptures. (Ibid.) Whence it seems to a man to be the cause of damnation. But « behold » that it is not from God, but from man, because « he hath opened a pit, etc. He hath conceived sorrow, » (Ibid.) that is, by the appetite of temporal things. « He hath brought forth, » he has effected, sent out: and in the iniquity sent out there is a pit, that is, a downfall for others. Whence he adds:

VERS. 16.-- « He hath opened a pit. » And so he is comparable to one opening a pit: for he opens by conceiving 855Cfraud: he digs out by travailing, by pressing on the work of fraud; he falls in by bringing forth fraud, namely, by perpetrating it.

VERS. 17.-- « His sorrow shall be turned, etc. » The head, the soul, the crown, the reason: over which sins have dominion, and remain over: and they shall come down upon it when they shall thrust it into punishments.

VERS. 18.-- « I will confess to the Lord. » (CASS.) The conclusion, as it were gathering all things into a sum, he says that he confesses cheerfully.

PSALMUS VIII.

VERS. 1.-- « In finem, pro torcularibus, etc. » Pro torcularibus, id est, Ecclesiis, etc., usque ad animae in requiem emanant.

855DVERS. 2.-- « Domine, Dominus noster, quam admirabile nomen! etc. » (CASS.) Primo laudes Dei, majestas ejus, et operatio excelsa describuntur. « In universa. » (Ibid.) Non ergo Judaei vel quilibet alii sibi vindicent quod omnium est, quod est intentio. « Super coelos. » (AUG.) Ad litteram, vel Scripturas: quia excedit eloquia omnium Scripturarum; vel, « super coelos. » Continuando cum sequentibus, id est, in Scripturas, quas inclinat infantibus, propter inimicos crucis: qui destruuntur, cum videntur, id est, intelliguntur Scripturae usque ad infantes ductae: et cum per eas usque ad robur nutriuntur, et sublimitatem intelligentiae eriguntur.

VERS. 3.-- « Ex ore infantium. » (Ibid.) Insipientium, quibus Apostolus lac dabat, quos signabant illi, 856Aqui Dominum laudabant, in quos hoc utitur Dominus testimonio. Ex his perfecit laudem, quia si soli perfecti essent in Ecclesia, non consuleretur humano generi; sicut nunc, cum et minimi nondum capaces cognitionis rerum spiritualium nutriuntur fide temporalis historiae. « Inimici, » sunt omnes, qui dispensationi per Crucifixum factae, contraria dicunt. « Defensores » videntur haeretici fidei, philosophi sapientiae, cum tamen et illi fidem, et hi sapientiam veram impugnent. « Lactentium, » (CASS.) non aetate, sed ut Petrus, « quasi modo geniti (I Petr. II), » qui nondum escam, sed lac sumere possunt; et est, non solum a perfectis, sed et ab insipientibus praedicaris. Vel, infantes et lactentes dicit apostolos, qui fuerunt homines simplices et indocti; unde: « Stulta mundi 856B« elegit Deus ut confundat fortia (I Cor. I). » Perfectior est laus. Vel, ex ore infantium et lactentium, id est, ex verbis puerorum Hebraeorum perfecisti laudem, quae videbatur pueriliter agi propter inimicos, ne videatur humana sapientia, sed divinitus data. « Inimicos tuos. » Paganos. « Inimicum. » Judaeum, qui inimicus est Dei, dum Patrem solum defendit: quia « qui non honorificat Filium, non honorificat « Patrem, » vel inimicus voto.

VERS. 4.-- « Quoniam videbo. » Prae Judaeo, spiritu. « Coelos tuos, » apostolos, videbo praesentialiter in posteris; hoc bene convenit primitivis. « Opera digitorum tuorum. » Quia cooperatione Trinitatis perfecti, quae significatur in tribus digitis hic, ut ibi: « Qui appendit tribus digitis molem terrae. » (Isa. XL.) Et per eos, 856C« Lunam et stellas quae tu fundasti. » Non illi.

VERS. 5.-- « Quid est homo. » (Ibid.) Secundo, naturam hominis olim vitiatam dicit in Christo super omnia exaltatam. Prius enim ostenderat omnipotentiam Deitatis. Per hominem, peccatores; per filium hominis, spirituales. (Ibid.) Homo, quilibet vilis, cujus memor Deus miserendo, Filius hominis, Christus homo: quoniam per eum tu visitas eum, cum Verbum caro factum est, in quo medicus venit ad infirmos. « Aut filius. » (AUG.) Disjunctio innuit distare inter hominem et filium hominis. Omnis filius hominis homo, sed non e converso ut Adam. Homo ergo omnis, qui portat imaginem terreni: Filius hominis, qui coelestis, et merito novus homo, 856Dfilius hominis: quia novus ex veteri quadam mutatione fit. (AUG.) Cur relictis altioribus haec ima dicit? Sed oves, etc., usque ad qui semine verbi Dei hominum corda fructificare faciunt.

VERS. 8.-- « Insuper et pecora. » Malos ergo Christo subjectos esse notat, quod minus videtur: hi enim carnales in latitudine campi, id est, in amplitudine voluptatum, non in montibus virtutum, habitantes. « Pecora campi. » (Ibid.) Qui in carne vivunt, ubi nihil arduum ascendunt: sed lata via, cui inhaerent, est quae ducit ad interitum: unde et Abel in campo occiditur.

VERS. 9.-- « Volucres, » superbi: de quibus, « Posuerunt in coelum os suum (Psal. LXXII). » Quorum caput dicit: « Ascendam in coelum et exaltabo 857Asolium meum, et ero similis Altissimo (Isa. XIV). « Pisces maris qui perambulant semitas maris, » curiosi. Haec tria, voluptas carnis, superbia, curiositas, includunt omnia vitia, quae sunt concupiscentia carnis, ambitio saeculi, id est superbia, concupiscentia oculorum, per oculos curiositas maxime praevalet.

PSALM VIII.

VERS. 1.-- « Unto the end, for the winepresses, etc. » For the winepresses, that is, for the Churches, etc., as far as souls flow out into rest.

855DVERS. 2.-- « O Lord, our Lord, how admirable is thy name! etc. » (CASS.) First the praises of God, his majesty, and his exalted working are described. « In the whole. » (Ibid.) Let not the Jews therefore, or any others, claim for themselves what belongs to all, which is the intent. « Above the heavens. » (AUG.) Literally, or the Scriptures: because it exceeds the utterances of all the Scriptures; or, « above the heavens. » Continuing with what follows, that is, into the Scriptures, which he bends down to babes, on account of the enemies of the cross: who are destroyed, when the Scriptures are seen, that is, understood, to be led down as far as babes: and when through them they are nourished unto strength, and are raised to the sublimity of understanding.

VERS. 3.-- « Out of the mouth of infants. » (Ibid.) Of the unwise, to whom the Apostle gave milk, whom those signified 856Awho praised the Lord, in whom the Lord uses this testimony. Out of these he hath perfected praise, because if only the perfect were in the Church, no counsel would be taken for the human race; as now, when even the least, not yet capable of the knowledge of spiritual things, are nourished by faith in the history of things temporal. « Enemies » are all who speak things contrary to the dispensation made through the Crucified. « Defenders » the heretics seem of the faith, the philosophers of wisdom, although yet the former impugn the faith, and the latter true wisdom. « Sucklings, » (CASS.) not in age, but as Peter has it, « as newborn babes (I Petr. II), » who cannot yet take food, but milk; and it is: thou art proclaimed not only by the perfect, but also by the unwise. Or, he calls infants and sucklings the apostles, who were simple and unlearned men; whence: « The foolish things of the world 856B« God hath chosen, that he may confound the strong (I Cor. I). » [Vulg. 1Cor 1:27 quae stulta sunt mundi elegit Deus, ut confundat sapientes, "the foolish things of the world God hath chosen, that he may confound the wise"; fortia answers to a second clause, infirma mundi elegit Deus] The praise is more perfect. Or, out of the mouth of infants and sucklings, that is, out of the words of the Hebrew children thou hast perfected praise, which seemed to be done childishly, on account of the enemies, that it might not seem to be human wisdom, but divinely given. « Thine enemies. » The pagans. « The enemy. » The Jew, who is an enemy of God, while he defends the Father alone: because « he that honoureth not the Son, honoureth not « the Father, » or an enemy in his will.

VERS. 4.-- « For I shall see. » Before the Jew, in spirit. « Thy heavens, » the apostles, I shall see present in their descendants; this well suits those of the first age. « The works of thy fingers. » Because they are perfected by the cooperation of the Trinity, which is signified here in the three fingers, as there: « Who weigheth the bulk of the earth with three fingers. » (Isa. XL.) And through them, 856C« The moon and the stars which thou hast founded. » Not they.

VERS. 5.-- « What is man. » (Ibid.) Secondly, he says that the nature of man, once corrupted, is exalted in Christ above all things. For before he had shown the omnipotence of the Godhead. By man, sinners; by the son of man, the spiritual. (Ibid.) Man, any vile person, of whom God is mindful in showing mercy, the Son of man, Christ as man: since through him thou visitest him, when the Word was made flesh, in which the physician came to the sick. « Or the son. » (AUG.) The disjunction hints that there is a distance between man and the son of man. Every son of man is man, but not conversely, as Adam. Every man therefore, who bears the image of the earthly: the Son of man, who is heavenly, and deservedly a new man, 856Dson of man: because the new is made out of the old by a certain change. (AUG.) Why, leaving the higher things, does he speak of these lowest ones? But the sheep, etc., as far as who by the seed of the word of God make the hearts of men to bear fruit.

VERS. 8.-- « Moreover the cattle also. » He notes therefore that the wicked also are subject to Christ, which seems less: for these carnal men dwell in the breadth of the plain, that is, in the amplitude of pleasures, not in the mountains of virtues. « The cattle of the field. » (Ibid.) Who live in the flesh, where they climb nothing steep: but the broad way, to which they cling, is that which leads to destruction: whence also Abel is slain in the field.

VERS. 9.-- « The birds, » the proud: of whom, « They have set their mouth against heaven (Psal. LXXII). » Whose head says: « I will ascend into heaven, and I will exalt 857Amy throne, and I will be like the Most High (Isa. XIV). « The fishes of the sea that walk through the paths of the sea, » the curious. These three, the pleasure of the flesh, pride, curiosity, include all vices, which are the concupiscence of the flesh, the ambition of the world, that is, pride, the concupiscence of the eyes, since through the eyes curiosity chiefly prevails.

PSALMUS IX.

VERS. 1.-- « In finem pro occultis filiis. » Nec additur cujus, per excellentiam est unigenitus Dei. « Occultis. » Quia alia ejus sunt manifesta, etc., usque ad et de poena, qua judicat purgando, convertendo, excaecando.

VERS. 2.-- « Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto « corde meo, etc. » Propheta laetus psallit, quia cultura 857Bdiaboli adventu Christi destruitur: et Christus regnat, judicat, adjuvat.

VERS. 4.-- « In convertendo inimicum meum, etc., » « peribunt, etc. » (AUG.) Quia dum diabolum convertisti retro, membra infirmantur, ut nil nocere possint, et non erunt, vel, destruentur ex toto ab impugnatione tua, cum dices, « Ite, maledicti (Matth. XXV), » vel, peribunt cum aufert Deus ab eis iniquitatem.

VERS. 5.-- « Fecisti judicium meum et causam « meam. » (Ibid.) Quia mihi servierunt ad utilitatem, quia « sedisti. » « Judicas. » (HIER.) Pater, ut Christus moriatur pro genere hominum. (AUG.) Vel, Christus in fine judicabit, cui Pater omne judicium dedit.

857CVERS. 6.-- « In saeculum et in saeculum. » (Ibid.) Saeculum est hoc praesens quod volvitur: saeculum saeculi aeternum, cujus illud imago est. Vel, determinatio est, ne hoc praesens acciperes.

VERS. 7.-- « Frameae. (CASS.) Virtus diaboli in fine saeculi destruetur. « Civitates. » Populi ejus. « Cum sonitu, » id est, clamore maximo, ut fit cum res prosperae gravi « fine » clauduntur. Sed e contra Dominus permanet. « Finem, (AUG.) » est gladius quem vibrabit in secundo adventu aperte judicans, et qui modo occulte, usque ad quem aliquid valent hostis frameae, sed tunc penitus deficient. « Eorum. » (CASS.) Pluraliter, cum supra inimici singulariter dixit, quia cum plures sunt daemones, quia tamen in 857Dmalitia similes sunt, quasi unum. « Cum sonitu. » (AUG.) Id est, et strepitus et tumultus impietatis periit: vel, cum impietas evertitur, strepitus fit, quia non venit ad summam pacem, nisi qui magno strepitu cum vitiis pugnavit. « Thronum suum. » (CASS.) Judiciariam potestatem, qui in humilitate judicatus est, in majestate judicabit.

VERS. 10.-- « Et factus. » Quantum est, eum qui judex est, esse refugium pauperi, qui nihil mundi cupit. « In opportunitatibus. » (AUG.) Non opportunius homo a saeculo avertitur, nisi his voluptatibus, labores et dolores misceantur.

VERS. 11.-- « Sperent. » (AUG.) Cum desinunt sperare in rebus saeculi. Aversos a saeculo, quaerentes ubi figant spem, excipit cognitio nominis. Nomen 858Ascitur, cum ille cujus est nomen, noscitur. Nomen est illi Dominus, quod novit, qui libenter ei servit, vel, qui est, et ideo nemo speret in transitoriis, nihil habentibus praeter, fuit, et erit. Nam quod in illis futurum est, cum venerit, fit statim praeteritum, exspectatur cum cupiditate, amittitur cum dolore, non tenetur cum certitudine. « Quoniam non reliquisti. » Fideles provocat ad laudem Propheta, respiciens beneficia praesentis temporis et futuri.

VERS. 12.-- « Sion. » (Ibid.) Speculatio, quae modo agitur, ut perveniamus ad pacis visionem, id est, de Sion in Jerusalem: quaelibet autem studiosa speculatio fit in errorem, nisi Dominus in ea habitet. « Studia. » (HIER.) Id est, mandata ejus quibus studendum est.

858BVERS. 13.-- « Quoniam requirens. » (Ibid.) Sed quasi dicant, qui missi sunt evangelizare, nemo credit nobis, et occidimur, respondit: non sine fructu, quia « requirens ultione sanguinem eorum, » in judicio, ubi gloria occiso, poena occisori erit: « recordatus est, etc » (Ibid.) non post oblivionem, sed post longum tempus, secundum affectum infirmorum, qui oblitum putant, quia non tam cito fit ut volunt: quibus etiam adde, imo non est oblitus ut putatis: et si dixi « recordatus, » hoc contra querentes, qui pro dilatione putant oblitum.

VERS. 14.-- « Miserere. » (CASS.) In sua persona dicit quod unusquisque petit. « Vide. » (Ibid.) Aspectus Dei, auxilium est, qui cum fit, et lux tenebras fugat: de superbia inimici aestimatur humilitas patientis, 858Cquia tantum hi humiliantur, quantum illi extolluntur.

VERS. 15.-- « Qui exaltas me de portis mortis, etc. » (AUG.) Id est ab omnibus cupiditatibus, quibus itur ad mortem: mors jam est ipsa laetitia in perfruendo cupitis; unde Apostolus: « Vidua, quae vivit « in deliciis, mortua est (I Tim. V). » « Portis filiae « Sion. » Sunt omnia optima studia, etc., usque ad quae nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit. (CASS.) Portae contra portas, quia hae mortis, illae vitae. « Sion. » (Ibid.) Omnes Ecclesias mundi generavit, quia ibi natus est Christus unde fides incoepit.

VERS. 16.-- « Exsultabo. » (AUG.) Hucusque clamor, inde dicit Ecclesia quae affligitur, exsultabo in Jesu. (CASS.) Spe enim salva est. « In laqueo. » (Ibid.) 858DLaqueus occultus, dolosa cogitatio: Pes, animae amor, qui, si pravus est, dicitur cupiditas, si rectus, charitas. Eo enim movetur anima quasi ad locum, quo se pervenisse per amorem laetatur. « In laqueo » ergo, id est, fraudulento consilio: pes, id est, amor qui per fraudem pervenit ad vanam laetitiam, comprehensus est, quia illa delectatio alligat eos, ut inde abrumpere amorem, et ad utilia vertere non audeant. Si enim conentur, dolor est deserere, quae delectant, et ille dolor non sinit abscedere.

VERS. 17.-- Cognoscetur. (CASS.) Vel de futuro judicio, etc., usque ad ut quidam falso putant.

VERS. 18.-- Convertantur peccatores. (AUG.) Hic est canticum diapsalmatis, quasi occulta laetitia separationis: 859Aquae hic fit non loco, sed affectu, intra bonos et malos. (CASS.) Peccatoribus cum Antichristo finem malorum praedicit; quasi hoc interim, sed tandem convertentur, ne in suis gaudeant. In infernum, ne alibi mittendos se putent.

VERS. 19.-- Patientia. (AUG.) Patienter, propter hoc praecipue memor erit Deus pauperum, scilicet propter patientiam.

VERS. 20.-- Exsurge. (AUG.) Precatur futurum judicium. (CASS.) Loquens de fine saeculi propheta, prospexit adventum Antichristi; unde quasi territus clamat: exsurge.

VERS. 21.-- Sciant. Id est, cruciati experiantur quod homines stulti fuerunt.

PSALM IX.

VERS. 1.-- « Unto the end, for the hidden sons. » [Vulg. Ps 9:1 pro occultis filii, "for the hidden things of the son", a genitive singular, which is what the gloss's cujus presupposes] Nor is it added whose, by excellence he is the only-begotten of God. « Hidden. » Because other things of his are manifest, etc., as far as and of the punishment by which he judges, in purging, in converting, in blinding.

VERS. 2.-- « I will confess to thee, O Lord, with my whole « heart, etc. » The prophet sings joyfully, because the worship 857Bof the devil is destroyed by the coming of Christ: and Christ reigns, judges, helps.

VERS. 4.-- « When my enemy is turned back, etc., » « they shall perish, etc. » (AUG.) Because when thou hast turned the devil backward, his members are weakened, so that they can do no hurt, and they shall not be, or, they shall be utterly destroyed by thy assault, when thou shalt say, « Go, ye cursed (Matth. XXV), » [Vulg. Mt 25:41 Discedite a me maledicti, "Depart from me, ye cursed"] or, they shall perish when God takes away iniquity from them.

VERS. 5.-- « Thou hast made my judgment and my « cause. » (Ibid.) Because they have served me to my profit, because « thou hast sat. » « Thou judgest. » (HIER.) The Father, that Christ might die for the race of men. (AUG.) Or, Christ shall judge at the end, to whom the Father hath given all judgment.

857CVERS. 6.-- « For ever and for ever. » (Ibid.) The age is this present one which rolls on: the age of the age is eternal, of which that one is the image. Or, it is a determination, lest thou shouldst take this present one.

VERS. 7.-- « The javelins. (CASS.) The power of the devil shall be destroyed at the end of the world. « Cities. » His peoples. « With a noise, » that is, with the greatest outcry, as happens when prosperous things are shut up with a heavy « end. » But on the contrary the Lord remaineth. « The end, (AUG.) » is the sword which he shall brandish at the second coming, judging openly, and which now judges secretly, up to which the javelins of the enemy avail somewhat, but then they shall wholly fail. « Of them. » (CASS.) In the plural, although above he said the enemy in the singular, because although the demons are many, yet because in 857Dmalice they are alike, they are as it were one.

« With a noise. » (AUG.) That is, both the din and the tumult of impiety hath perished: or, when impiety is overthrown, a din is made, because none comes to the highest peace but he who has fought with the vices with a great din. « His throne. » (CASS.) The judiciary power, he who was judged in humility shall judge in majesty.

VERS. 10.-- « And he is become. » How great a thing it is, that he who is judge should be a refuge to the poor man, who desires nothing of the world. « In opportunities. » (AUG.) Man is not more opportunely turned away from the world, unless to these pleasures labours and sorrows be mingled.

VERS. 11.-- « Let them hope. » (AUG.) When they cease to hope in the things of the world. Those turned away from the world, seeking where to fix their hope, the knowledge of the name receives. The name 858Ais known, when he whose the name is, is known. His name is Lord, which he knows who willingly serves him, or, who is, and therefore let no one hope in transitory things, which have nothing besides "it was" and "it will be." For what in them is to come, when it has come, straightway becomes past, it is awaited with desire, it is lost with sorrow, it is not held with certainty. « For thou hast not forsaken. » The prophet provokes the faithful to praise, looking upon the benefits of the present time and of the time to come.

VERS. 12.-- « Sion. » (Ibid.) Contemplation, which is practised now, that we may come to the vision of peace, that is, from Sion into Jerusalem: but any zealous contemplation falls into error, unless the Lord dwell in it. « Pursuits. » (HIER.) That is, his commandments, upon which zeal is to be spent.

858BVERS. 13.-- « For requiring. » (Ibid.) But as if they who are sent to evangelize should say, No one believes us, and we are slain, he answered: not without fruit, because « requiring in vengeance their blood, » [Vulg. Ps 9:13 quoniam requirens sanguinem eorum, without ultione] in the judgment, where there shall be glory to the slain, punishment to the slayer: « he hath remembered, etc » (Ibid.) not after forgetfulness, but after a long time, according to the feeling of the weak, who think him forgetful, because it is not done so quickly as they wish: to whom also add, nay, he is not forgetful, as you think: and if I have said « he hath remembered, » this is against the complainers, who because of the delay think him forgetful.

VERS. 14.-- « Have mercy. » (CASS.) In his own person he says what each one asks. « See. » (Ibid.) The look of God is help, and when it comes, the light also puts the darkness to flight: from the pride of the enemy is measured the humility of the sufferer, 858Cbecause these are humbled just so much as those are exalted.

VERS. 15.-- « Who liftest me up from the gates of death, etc. » (AUG.) That is, from all covetous desires, by which one goes to death: death now is that very gladness in the enjoying of things desired; whence the Apostle: « A widow that liveth « in delights is dead (I Tim. V). » [Vulg. 1Tim 5:6 Nam quae in deliciis est, vivens mortua est, "for she that is in delights is dead while she liveth"] « In the gates of the daughter « of Sion. » They are all the best pursuits, etc., as far as which neither eye hath seen, nor ear heard. (CASS.) Gates against gates, because these are of death, those of life. « Sion. » (Ibid.) She begat all the Churches of the world, because there Christ was born, whence faith began.

VERS. 16.-- « I will exult. » (AUG.) Thus far the cry, thereafter the Church which is afflicted says, I will exult in Jesus. (CASS.) For by hope she is saved. « In the snare. » (Ibid.) 858DA hidden snare is a deceitful thought: the foot is the soul's love, which, if it be crooked, is called covetousness, if right, charity. For by it the soul is moved as it were to a place, whither it rejoices to have come by love. « In the snare » therefore, that is, in a fraudulent counsel: the foot, that is, the love which through fraud comes to a vain gladness, is caught, because that delight binds them, so that they dare not break off their love from thence and turn it to useful things. For if they should try, it is grief to leave the things which delight, and that grief does not suffer them to depart.

VERS. 17.-- He shall be known. (CASS.) Or, of the judgment to come, etc., as far as as certain men falsely think.

VERS. 18.-- Let sinners be turned. (AUG.) Here is the canticle of the diapsalma, as it were the hidden gladness of the separation: 859Awhich is made here not by place, but by affection, between the good and the evil. (CASS.) To sinners with Antichrist he foretells the end of evils; as it were this meanwhile, but at last they shall be turned, lest they rejoice in their own things. Into hell, lest they think themselves to be sent elsewhere.

VERS. 19.-- Patience. (AUG.) Patiently, for this chiefly will God be mindful of the poor, namely because of their patience.

VERS. 20.-- Arise. (AUG.) He prays for the judgment to come. (CASS.) The prophet, speaking of the end of the world, foresaw the coming of Antichrist; whence as if terrified he cries: arise.

VERS. 21.-- Let them know. That is, being tormented let them find by experience that they were foolish men.

PSALMUS X.-- Secundum Hebraeos.

859BVERS. 1.-- Ut quid. (AUG.) Diapsalma, quia illi (Antichristo) licebit tanta facere, ut Deus putetur: subdit quasi vocem gementium et quaerentium de dilatione judicii.

(CASS., AUG.) Ut quid. Mala illius temporis pertractat, etc., usque ad sed opportune, ita scilicet, Dum superbit.

VERS. 2.-- Incenditur pauper, comprehenduntur in consiliis quibus cogitant. (AUG.) Mire providentia Dei de malis operatur, etc., usque ad sic damnantur mali, justi salvantur.

VERS. 3.-- Quoniam laudatur. Ideo superbit vel comprehenditur, quia laudatur a suis, impletione desideriorum sensualitatis suae.

(AUG.) Adulantium linguae alligant animas in peccatis: 859Cdelectat enim ea facere, in quibus non solum non metuitur reprehensor, sed etiam auditur laudator.

VERS. 4.-- Irae suae. (CASS.) Antichristi, quia omnia turbulenter et crudeliter faciet: vel, Dei, non quaeret Deum poenitendo; vel, Deus eum, ut hic ulciscatur, sed in futuro gravius puniturus.

VERS. 5.-- Inquinatae. (CASS.) Nequitiae causa est, quod Deum non habet ante oculos, et ideo viae ejus, id est, cogitationes et opera sordent.

In omni tempore. (AUG.) Suo, scilicet vitae suae, etc., usque ad et quia omnium inimicorum suorum dominabitur.

VERS. 6.-- Dixit, etc. Omnes gentes occupabo, sed non sine malo, id est, peccato, quod ei proprium 859Dest. Vel semper ero sine malo: hoc sibi promittit, cujus maledictione os plenum, etc.

Non movebor. (AUG.) Vel, putabit se malis artibus, et non aliter, venturum de mortali generatione in aeternam, quod et Simon magus putavit.

VERS. 7.-- Sub lingua. (CASS.) Id est, cogitationes ejus sunt de labore sanctorum et dolore corporeo, quod in martyribus patet. Vel, labor sanctorum et dolor, qui est in poenis corporis est sub lingua ejus, id est levior, lingua ejus, quae intus nocet: illa, scilicet poena extra.

Vel, sub lingua, quia verba plus timentur et nocebunt quam verbera, quibus praecipitatur et peribit anima.

860AVERS. 8.-- In occultis, etc. (AUG.), id est, ambiguis, ubi non facile videtur quid petendum, quid non.

VERS. 9.-- Oculi ejus in pauperem, etc. (Ibid.) Exponit insidias, oculi, quasi misericordia et affectu, vel, alios sic decipit, quod oculi crudeliter respiciunt in pauperes spiritu.

Leo in spelunca, etc. Quia in eo vis et dolus, etc., usque ad per haereticos et falsos fratres.

VERS. 10.-- Inclinabit. (CASS.) Cum nimia felicitate in otium remiserit animum, cadet repentino interitu: et Dominus spiritu oris ejus interficiet eum.

In finem. Negant videre Deum, etc., usque ad excitat Dominum, Exsurge, Domine.

VERS. 12.-- Exsurge, Domine Deus, et exaltetur 860Bmanus, ut obliviscaris, etc. (Ibid.) Precatur judicium, ut hic cito finiantur, quae tanta sunt, ut nemo velit tempus quo haec fiunt dilatari.

Exsurge. Quasi ex improviso, ut conterantur, dum tui tecum exaltati glorificantur.

VERS. 13.-- Propter quod irritavit impius Deum. (AUG.) Jam itaque et de judicio illo intelligens et exsultans, dicit, propter quid? id est, quid proficit tanta mala facere?

Dixit enim Deus in corde suo, etc. (Ibid.) Sensus iste pronuntiationem quaerit, etc., usque ad ne laborent, vel irascantur.

(AUG.) Christus Judam toleravit et ad praedicandum misit, et ei eucharistiam dedit ut ostenderet dona pervenire ad eos qui fidem accipiunt, qualis 860CJudas fuit.

VERS. 14.-- Vides enim quoniam tu laborem et dolorem. Id jam praeordinasti, ubi tradas eos in manu tua.

Orphano, etc. (AUG.) Cui moritur pater mundus, per quem carnaliter est genitus, ut dicat: Mihi mundus crucifixus est, et ego mundo.

VERS. 15.-- Contere brachium. Poenis terret, bonis demulcet.

Quaeretur. (AUG.) Quando adhuc necessarium sit ad purgandos nos, sicut supra dum superbit impius, etc.; sed quia non invenietur, id est, quia jam non est in quo sit locus peccato illius, plano ferro non est opus lima.

860DVERS. 16.-- Dominus regnabit in aeternum et in saeculum saeculi. Hoc regnum gratius erit pro concurrentibus malis, quod veniet destructo Antichristo, ab hoc regno peribitis gentes, sed pauperes habebunt, quia desiderium pauperum, etc.

VERS. 17.-- Praeparationem cordis. (CASS.) Vel, concupiscentiam, quod est ubi omnibus viribus animae aliquid ardentius petitur. Vel, hoc, quod in cordibus eorum ipse Deus praeparavit. Vel, quam statim volunt petere Deus audiat.

Auris, etc. (AUG.) Nominatis membris, quae in nobis visibilia et corporea sunt, in Deo potentias operationum intelligi oportet.

Judicare pupillo et humili, etc. Secundus adventus 861Amanifestus erit, etc., usque ad auctor malorum cum sua plebe damnabitur.

PSALM X.-- According to the Hebrews.

859BVERS. 1.-- Why. (AUG.) Diapsalma, because it will be permitted to him (to Antichrist) to do such great things that he may be thought God: he adds, as it were, the voice of those who groan and who ask concerning the deferring of judgment.

(CASS., AUG.) Why. He treats at length of the evils of that time, etc., as far as but opportunely, namely thus, While the wicked man is proud.

VERS. 2.-- The poor man is set on fire, they are caught in the counsels which they devise. (AUG.) Wondrously does the providence of God work out of evils, etc., as far as thus the evil are damned, the just are saved.

VERS. 3.-- For the sinner is praised. Therefore he is proud, or is caught, because he is praised by his own, by the fulfilling of the desires of his sensuality.

(AUG.) The tongues of flatterers bind souls fast in sins: 859Cfor it is a delight to do those things in which not only is no reprover feared, but a praiser is even heard.

VERS. 4.-- Of his wrath. (CASS.) Of Antichrist's, because he will do all things turbulently and cruelly; or, of God's: he will not seek God by repenting; or, God will not seek him out, that he should take vengeance here, but is about to punish him more heavily in the time to come.

VERS. 5.-- Defiled. (CASS.) The cause of his wickedness is that he does not hold God before his eyes, and therefore his ways, that is, his thoughts and his works, are foul.

At all times. (AUG.) His own, namely of his life, etc., as far as and because he shall have dominion over all his enemies.

VERS. 6.-- He hath said, etc. I will take possession of all nations, but not without evil, that is, without sin, which is proper 859Dto him. Or: I shall always be without evil; this he promises himself, whose mouth is full of cursing, etc.

I shall not be moved. (AUG.) Or, he will think that he will come by evil arts, and not otherwise, from a mortal generation into an eternal one, which Simon Magus also thought.

VERS. 7.-- Under the tongue. (CASS.) That is, his thoughts are of the labour of the saints and of bodily sorrow, which is plain in the martyrs. Or, the labour of the saints and the sorrow which lies in the punishments of the body is under his tongue, that is, it is the lighter; his tongue, which harms within: that other, namely, is the punishment without.

Or, under the tongue, because words are more feared and will do more harm than stripes, by which the soul is cast headlong and will perish.

860AVERS. 8.-- In secret places, etc. (AUG.), that is, in ambiguous ones, where it is not easily seen what is to be sought and what is not.

VERS. 9.-- His eyes are upon the poor man, etc. (Ibid.) He sets out the ambushes: the eyes, as though with mercy and affection; or, he so deceives others that his eyes look cruelly upon the poor in spirit.

A lion in his den, etc. Because in him is violence and guile, etc., as far as through heretics and false brethren.

VERS. 10.-- He shall bow himself down. (CASS.) When through excessive prosperity he has let his mind slacken into idleness, he shall fall by a sudden destruction: and the Lord shall slay him with the spirit of his mouth.

Unto the end. They deny that God sees, etc., as far as he rouses the Lord, Arise, O Lord.

VERS. 12.-- Arise, O Lord God, and let 860Bthy hand be exalted, that thou mayest forget, etc. [Vulg. Ps 9:33 exaltetur manus tua ; ne obliviscaris pauperum, "let thy hand be exalted: forget not the poor"] (Ibid.) He prays for judgment, that these things may be quickly ended here, things so great that no one would wish the time in which they happen to be prolonged.

Arise. As it were unlooked for, that they may be crushed, while thine own, exalted with thee, are glorified.

VERS. 13.-- Wherefore hath the wicked provoked God. [Vulg. Ps 9:34 Propter quid, the interrogative "for what reason"] (AUG.) And so now, both understanding and exulting concerning that judgment, he says, wherefore? that is, what does it profit to do such great evils?

For God hath said in his heart, etc. [Vulg. Ps 9:34 dixit enim in corde suo, with no Deus: the speaker there is the wicked man] (Ibid.) This sense calls for a delivery, etc., as far as lest they toil, or grow angry.

(AUG.) Christ bore with Judas and sent him to preach, and gave him the eucharist, that he might show that the gifts reach those who receive the faith, such as 860CJudas was.

VERS. 14.-- For thou seest that thou considerest labour and sorrow. This thou hast already foreordained, where thou deliverest them into thy hand.

To the fatherless, etc. (AUG.) To him for whom the world dies as a father, by which he was carnally begotten, so that he may say: The world is crucified to me, and I to the world.

VERS. 15.-- Break thou the arm. By punishments he terrifies, by good things he soothes.

It shall be sought. (AUG.) While it is still needful for our purging, as above, while the wicked man is proud, etc.; but because it shall not be found, that is, because there is now no one in whom there is room for his sin, smooth iron has no need of a file.

860DVERS. 16.-- The Lord shall reign for ever, and unto ages of ages. This kingdom will be the more welcome for the evils that run alongside it, in that it will come when Antichrist has been destroyed; from this kingdom ye shall perish, O nations, but the poor shall have it, because the desire of the poor, etc.

VERS. 17.-- The preparation of the heart. (CASS.) Or, concupiscence, which is where a thing is sought more ardently with all the powers of the soul. Or, this, which God himself has prepared in their hearts. Or, that God may hear as soon as they wish to ask.

The ear, etc. (AUG.) When members are named which in us are visible and bodily, in God powers of operation must be understood.

To judge for the fatherless and the humble, etc. The second coming 861Awill be manifest, etc., as far as the author of evils will be damned with his own people.

PSALMUS X.

VERS. 1.-- In finem. (AUG.) Psal. David prophetae docentis resistere haereticis.

VERS. 2.-- In Domino confido. (AUG.) De haereticis qui catholicos in suam volunt convertere pravitatem.

(Ibid.) In Domino confido. Quoad litteram potest legi de passione, et dicit, Christus secundum hominem, ut solet contra terrores Judaeorum, In Domino confido.

In Domino confido. Cum peccantes volunt sagittare rectos.

861BQuoniam ecce. (Ibid.) Hi sunt terrores comminantium nobis de peccatoribus, ut ad se quasi justos transeamus. Dicunt enim: Peccatores intenderunt arcum, Scripturas, unde venenatas sagittas mittant, quas in cordis occulto parant.

VERS. 3.-- In obscuro. (CASS.) In simplici sensu degentes, vel in suis ambiguis sententiis, non quod Scriptura ad hoc valeat, sed quia:

VERS. 4.-- Quoniam quae perfecisti. Convertit ab his sermonem ad Deum quasi: Cur dicunt transmigra? Cur de peccatoribus terretur, qui intendunt sagittare rectos? quia quae perfecisti destruxerunt in suis conventibus, ubi parvulos, qui erant lacte nutriendi, ex quorum ore laus perficitur, venenis necant.

861CJustus autem, quid fecit? (AUG.) Secundum utramque partem, etc., usque ad animae suae nocet, non justo, qui Deo credit.

VERS. 6.-- Dominus interrogat, etc. Justus autem. Minatur judicium, cujus timore deserant falsitates.

Interrogat. (Ibid.) Id est probat, quia boni de obscuris non fatigantur, sed exercentur de cognitione: non inflantur, sed confirmantur.

Quae perfecisti. Id est, perfecte edidisti, vel implendo praedicta. Destruxerunt, male exponendo.

(Ibid.) In obscuro. Vel obscura luna. Duae sunt opiniones lunae, etc., usque ad qui tunc dicit sancta sacramenta, cum per sanctos dentur.

VERS. 7.-- Pluet super. Quid malis reddat ostendit. --(AUG.) Pluit de nubibus, id est pseudoprophetis. 861DVel de bonis unde emanant laquei, cum male intelligitur: sed non nisi his qui peccatores sunt. Ignis. Primo igne cupiditatum vastantur: inde malorum operum fetore abjiciuntur a sanctis, inde merguntur aeternis poenis.

VERS. 8.-- Justitias. (Ibid.) Pluraliter, ut justos accipias, in quibus multae justitiae, cum una sit Dei.

Aequitatem vidit. Aequitas visa est in facie, id est, notitia ejus: facies enim est notitia ejus, id est, potentia qua dignis innotescet. Vel vidit, quia non se dat noscendum malis, sed bonis, quod est aequitas.

PSALM X.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end. (AUG.) A psalm of David the prophet, teaching men to resist heretics.

VERS. 2.-- In the Lord I put my trust. (AUG.) Of the heretics who wish to turn Catholics to their own depravity.

(Ibid.) In the Lord I put my trust. As to the letter it can be read of the passion; and Christ says, according to his manhood, as he is wont, against the terrors of the Jews, In the Lord I put my trust.

In the Lord I put my trust. When sinners wish to shoot at the upright.

861BFor behold. (Ibid.) These are the terrors of those who threaten us with sinners, that we may pass over to them as to just men. For they say: The sinners have bent their bow, the Scriptures, whence they may send poisoned arrows, which they prepare in the secret place of the heart.

VERS. 3.-- In the dark. (CASS.) Those who live in the simple sense, or in their own ambiguous opinions; not that Scripture avails for this, but because:

VERS. 4.-- For the things which thou hast perfected. He turns his speech away from these to God, as it were: Why do they say, Remove? Why is he terrified by sinners, who bend the bow to shoot at the upright? because the things which thou hast perfected they have destroyed in their assemblies, where they slay with poisons the little ones who were to be nourished with milk, out of whose mouth praise is perfected.

861CBut the just, what hath he done? (AUG.) According to either part, etc., as far as he harms his own soul, not the just man, who believes God.

VERS. 6.-- The Lord questioneth, etc. But the just. He threatens judgment, by fear of which they may forsake their falsehoods.

He questioneth. (Ibid.) That is, he proves; because the good are not wearied by obscure things, but are exercised in knowledge: they are not puffed up, but confirmed.

The things which thou hast perfected. That is, thou hast published them perfectly, or by fulfilling what was foretold. They have destroyed them by expounding them ill.

(Ibid.) In the dark. Or when the moon is dark. There are two opinions about the moon, etc., as far as he then calls the sacraments holy, when they are given through holy men.

VERS. 7.-- He shall rain upon. He shows what he renders to the wicked. --(AUG.) He rains from the clouds, that is, from false prophets. 861DOr from good things, whence snares flow out when they are ill understood: but not save upon those who are sinners. Fire. First they are laid waste by the fire of covetous desires: thence by the stench of evil works they are cast out from the saints, thence they are plunged in eternal punishments.

VERS. 8.-- Justices. (Ibid.) In the plural, that thou mayest take it of the just, in whom there are many justices, though God's is one.

He hath beheld equity. Equity was seen in his face, that is, in the knowledge of him: for his face is the knowledge of him, that is, the power by which he will become known to the worthy. Or he hath seen, because he does not give himself to be known to the evil, but to the good, which is equity.

PSALMUS XI.

VERS. 1.-- Pro octava. (CASS.) Pro octava, quia 862Ahic petit propheta iniquitatem mundi destrui, ut ad veritatem promissionis futurae perveniat.

(AUG.) Octava pro die judicii, sicut in sexto psalmo dictum est.

VERS. 2.-- Salvum me fac. Revocat autem a falsitatibus saeculi ad eloquia Dei, ubi salus, a perversitate saeculi petit salvari.

Quoniam defecit. (CASS.) Exponit quae timuit multa: congregans in unum, ut sit major vis.

Sanctus. (Ibid.) Deus, qui ubique praesens, quantum ad homines defecit, qui in eum non credunt.

VERS. 3.-- Proximum. (AUG.) Proximus omnis homo, cum nullo male agendum est: proximus primae nativitatis conditione est omnis homo; carnis cognatione, amici et cognati; misericordiae comparatione, 862Bbeneficus quilibet.

Corde, etc. Germinatio, duplex cor significat, in quo dolosus describitur, unde: Vir duplex animo inconstans est in omnibus viis suis. Boni habent unum cor et unam animam.

VERS. 4.-- Disperdat Dominus universa labia, etc. (CASS.) Id est, passim pereant, qui in una pravitate conveniunt.

Linguam magniloquam. (Ibid.) Id est, superbam: hi sunt hypocritae, habentes speciem in sermone ad decipiendos homines, et Deo non subditi. (REMIG.) Vel, philosophi.

VERS. 5.-- Qui dixerunt: linguam nostram. (CASS.) Jactant se de potestate labiorum, quasi non a Deo acceperint.

862CVERS. 6.-- Inopum et gemitum pauperum. AUG., (CASS.) Inopes, gentiles, qui nec legem, nec prophetas habuerunt; pauperes, Judaei. Nunc. Quod non in priori populo. Exsurgam. Apparebo in Filio. Ponam. Consolationem pauperum. Fiducialiter. Potenter, cui nil resistit.

VERS. 7.-- Eloquia Domini. (Ibid.) Contra mala saeculi Christus a Patre missus, cujus eloquia vera sunt, impiorum falsa. Casta. Contra hoc quod supra, vana locuti sunt.--Examinatum. Contra, labia dolosa in corde et corde locuti sunt.

Septuplum. (AUG.) Perfecte, etc. usque ad et quod perfectum est demonstrat.

VERS. 8.-- Tu, Domine. (CASS.) Utilitatem divinorum eloquiorum, ad Dominum se convertens, 862Dostendit.

VERS. 9. In circuitu. Conclusio de utraque parte. (AUG.) In circuitu, id est, cupiditate temporalium, quae septem diebus volvuntur, et non veniunt in octavum, id est, aeternum: unde ventilator est impiorum rex sapiens, et immittit illis rotam malorum (Prov. II), id est, ambitum volubilium.

Multiplicasti filios hominum. (Ibid.) Est et multiplicatio in temporalibus quae avertit ab unitate Dei: sed justi multiplicantur secundum altitudinem, quando eunt de virtute in virtutem.

PSALM XI.

VERS. 1.-- For the octave. (CASS.) For the octave, because 862Ahere the prophet asks that the iniquity of the world be destroyed, so that he may come through to the truth of the promise to come.

(AUG.) The octave stands for the day of judgment, as was said in the sixth psalm.

VERS. 2.-- Save me. And he calls men back from the falsehoods of the world to the words of God, where salvation is; he asks to be saved from the perversity of the world.

For there hath failed. (CASS.) He sets out the many things he feared, gathering them into one, that the force may be the greater.

The holy one. (Ibid.) God, who is everywhere present, has failed so far as concerns men, who do not believe in him.

VERS. 3.-- His neighbour. (AUG.) Every man is a neighbour, since with none is evil to be done: by the condition of the first birth every man is a neighbour; by kinship of the flesh, friends and kinsmen; by the reckoning of mercy, 862Bany man who does good.

With a heart, etc. Germination [Germinatio; read Geminatio, "the doubling"] signifies a double heart, in which the deceitful man is described; whence: A man double in mind is inconstant in all his ways. The good have one heart and one soul.

VERS. 4.-- May the Lord destroy all lips, etc. (CASS.) That is, let them perish on every side who come together in one depravity.

The tongue that speaketh great things. (Ibid.) That is, a proud one: these are hypocrites, having a show in speech to deceive men, and not subject to God. (REMIG.) Or, philosophers.

VERS. 5.-- Who have said: our tongue. (CASS.) They boast of the power of their lips, as though they had not received it from God.

862CVERS. 6.-- Of the needy and the groaning of the poor. AUG., (CASS.) The needy, the Gentiles, who had neither the law nor the prophets; the poor, the Jews. Now. Which was not so in the former people. I will arise. I shall appear in the Son. I will set. The consolation of the poor. With confidence. Powerfully, in that nothing resists him.

VERS. 7.-- The words of the Lord. (Ibid.) Against the evils of the world Christ was sent by the Father, whose words are true, those of the wicked false. Chaste. Against that which is above, they have spoken vain things.--Tried by fire. Against, with deceitful lips, in a heart and a heart have they spoken.

Sevenfold. (AUG.) Perfectly, etc. as far as and it shows what is perfect.

VERS. 8.-- Thou, O Lord. (CASS.) Turning himself to the Lord, he 862Dshows the usefulness of the divine words.

VERS. 9. Round about. A conclusion concerning either part. (AUG.) Round about, that is, in the desire of temporal things, which are rolled round in seven days and do not come to the eighth, that is, to the eternal: whence a wise king is the winnower of the wicked, and brings in upon them the wheel of evils (Prov. II), [Vulg. Prov 20:26 Dissipat impios rex sapiens, et incurvat super eos fornicem, "a wise king scattereth the wicked, and bendeth an arch over them"] that is, the circuit of things that roll.

Thou hast multiplied the children of men. (Ibid.) There is also a multiplication in temporal things which turns a man away from the unity of God: but the just are multiplied according to the height, when they go from virtue to virtue.

PSALMUS XII.

VERS. 1.-- In finem. (CASS.) Psalmus de charitate 863AChristi, etc., usque ad secundum illud: Cupio dissolvi et esse cum Christo. (Phil. I.)

VERS. 2.-- Quandiu. (CAS.) Magnus ardor sustinentis, etc., usque ad quia spes protrahitur.

Consilia. (AUG.) Consilio non est opus, etc., usque ad dolens precansque aeterna.

VERS. 3.-- Usquequo exaltabitur, etc. (CASS.) Dicit quia, ante adventum Christi, diabolus captivos tenebat homines. Vel super me, id est, meam crudelitatem, quia toto orbe colitur, et quia sic orbis interit, plorat.

VERS. 4.-- Respice. (Ibid.) Post conquestionem, oratio, ut illuminetur, ne cedat fraudibus inimici, qui in misericordia confidit. Respice. (AUG.) Mitte quem missurus es. Exaudi. (CASS.) Pro omnibus, pro quibus generaliter petit. Illumina. Si non corpore, 863Bvideamus vel mente. Obdormiam. Quando fidei lumine sepulto, carnali delectatione clauduntur. In morte. Id est, in peccato quod fit in Spiritum sanctum de quo Joannes: Est peccatum ad mortem, non pro eo dico ut quis oret.

VERS. 6.-- Exsultabunt. (AUG.) Non solum propter me illuminare, sed ne inimicus gaudeat. Speravi (CASS.) Et si festinat, tamen patiens est: quia et si differtur, firmus est in spe, et interius jam videns exsultat, quem carne videre desiderat: unde et sibi bona data dicit qui prius querebatur. Tribuit. Non tribuet: magna virtus fidei jam habet quod futurum est. Exsultabit cor. Si tantum desiderat, si sic famulatur venturo, quid faciendum suscepto?

PSALM XII.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end. (CASS.) A psalm concerning the charity 863Aof Christ, etc., as far as according to that word: I desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ. (Phil. I.)

VERS. 2.-- How long. (CAS.) Great is the ardour of him who endures, etc., as far as because hope is drawn out.

Counsels. (AUG.) There is no need of counsel, etc., as far as grieving and praying for eternal things.

VERS. 3.-- How long shall he be exalted, etc. (CASS.) He says that before the coming of Christ the devil held men captive. Or over me, that is, over my cruelty, because he is worshipped in the whole world; and because the world so perishes, he weeps.

VERS. 4.-- Look thou upon me. (Ibid.) After the complaint, a prayer, that he may be enlightened, lest he yield to the frauds of the enemy, he who trusts in mercy. Look thou upon me. (AUG.) Send him whom thou art to send. Hear me. (CASS.) For all, for whom he asks in general. Enlighten. If not in body, 863Blet us see at least in mind. That I sleep. When, the light of faith being buried, they are shut up in carnal delight. In death. That is, in the sin which is committed against the Holy Spirit, of which John says: There is a sin unto death, I do not say for it that any man should pray.

VERS. 6.-- They shall rejoice. (AUG.) Not only for enlightening me, but lest the enemy rejoice. I have hoped (CASS.) And though he makes haste, yet he is patient: because even if it is put off, he is firm in hope, and already seeing inwardly he exults over him whom he longs to see in the flesh: whence he who before complained says that good things have already been given him. He hath given. Not, he will give: the great power of faith already has what is to come. My heart shall rejoice. If he desires so much, if he so serves him who is to come, what must be done when he has been received?

PSALMUS XIII.

863CVERS. 1.-- Dixit insipiens. (CASS.) Increpatio Judaeorum, descripta eorum malitia. Primus psalmus de increpatione Judaeorum, etc., usque ad hic homo non est Deus.

VERS. 2.-- Dominus de coelo. (Ibid.) Sed inde inexcusabiles, quia Dominus prospexit, id est, de humana natura eminuit. (AUG.) De coelo, id est, per sanctas animas prospicit: nam per se nil eum latet. Vel, de coelo, per animas sanctas, quae sunt coelum et sedes Dei. Vel, Dominus Pater de coelo, id est, secreto divinae mentis. (CAS.) Vel de aequalitate Dei Patris. Si est intelligens. Vel vidit, si est intelligens, et invenit quod aliquis non intelligit: quia non requirit, sed declinat, nam: Omnes declinaverunt, etc.

VERS. 3.-- Sepulcrum. (Ibid.) Ita inutiles aliis 863Dfacti, quia guttur eorum est sepulcrum, etc. Sepulcrum. Dicuntur hi tres versus, qui sunt usque ad secundam divisionem, ibi, Nonne cognoscent, etc., non esse de Hebraeo, etc., usque ad eos non habet.

Contritio (AUG.) Ita inutiles sibi facti sunt, etc., usque ad et infelicitas in futuro.

(CASS) Via impiorum, etc., usque ad: Timor Dei ante oculos, etc.

VERS. 4.-- Nonne cognoscent. Minatur judicium impiis.

VERS. 5.-- Dominum non, etc. (AUG.) Non enim vere hunc invocant, qui Deo displicentia amant.--(CASS.) Inde augetur interitus, quia necesse est mala agere, cum superbi nolunt Deum invocare. Sicut 864Acautela est, opportune timere; ita ignavia, inepte trepidare, ut pro gente et loco, timore Dei abjecto.

VERS. 6.-- Consilium inopis. (CASS.) Invectio in Judaeos, etc., usque ad, id est, de Judaeis procedens, etc.

VERS. 7.-- Quis dabit ex Sion, etc. (CASS.) Postremo Judaeorum conversio praedicitur, quae fiet cum plenitudo gentium intraverit. Cum averterit. Pro Judaeis etiam hoc testimonium Isaiae ponit Apostolus: Veniet ex Sion qui avertit captivitatem, vel impietatem a Jacob.

PSALM XIII.

863CVERS. 1.-- The fool hath said. (CASS.) A rebuke of the Jews, their malice being described. The first psalm concerning the rebuke of the Jews, etc., as far as this man is not God.

VERS. 2.-- The Lord from heaven. (Ibid.) But from thence they are without excuse, because the Lord looked down, that is, he stood forth out of human nature. (AUG.) From heaven, that is, he looks down through holy souls: for by himself nothing lies hidden from him. Or, from heaven, through holy souls, which are the heaven and the seat of God. Or, the Lord the Father from heaven, that is, from the secret of the divine mind. (CAS.) Or, from the equality of God the Father. If there be one that understandeth. Or, he saw whether there be one that understandeth, and he found that not one understands: because he does not seek, but turns aside, for: All have gone aside, etc.

VERS. 3.-- A sepulchre. (Ibid.) Thus made useless to others, 863Dbecause their throat is a sepulchre, etc. A sepulchre. These three verses, which run as far as the second division, at Shall they not know, etc., are said not to be from the Hebrew, etc., as far as it does not have them.

Destruction (AUG.) Thus they have been made useless to themselves, etc., as far as and unhappiness in the time to come.

(CASS) The way of the wicked, etc., as far as: The fear of God before their eyes, etc.

VERS. 4.-- Shall they not know. He threatens judgment to the wicked.

VERS. 5.-- The Lord they have not called upon, etc. (AUG.) For they do not truly call upon him who love the things that displease God.--(CASS.) Thence destruction is increased, because they must needs do evil, since the proud will not call upon God. As 864Ait is caution to fear at the fitting time, so it is cowardice to tremble unfittingly, as for nation and place, the fear of God being cast away.

VERS. 6.-- The counsel of the needy. (CASS.) An invective against the Jews, etc., as far as, that is, proceeding from the Jews, etc.

VERS. 7.-- Who shall give out of Sion, etc. (CASS.) Last of all the conversion of the Jews is foretold, which will come to pass when the fulness of the Gentiles has come in. When he shall have turned away. For the Jews too the Apostle sets down this testimony of Isaiah: There shall come out of Sion he that turneth away the captivity, or the impiety, from Jacob.

PSALMUS XIV.

VERS. 1.-- Domine, quis? (CAS.) Psalmus iste proprie morum est institutorius, praesumptionis repressio: ubi 864Bagitur de unitate praesentis Ecclesiae et futura quiete. Primo interrogat propheta, quasi sacerdos ante faciem Domini stans, et responsa petit; volens scire quos Deus sua dignos judicet Ecclesia.

VERS. 2.-- Qui. (Ibid.) Responsio Domini, etc. usque ad ut Christus agnus sine fractura membrorum, qui proprie templum ingressus est, non ut expiaretur sicut caeteri, sed sine macula. Operatur justitiam. Ut dum vendentes et ementes ejecit de templo.

VERS. 3.-- Qui loquitur. Hic exsequitur plenius. Veritas est cum res ita est, ut dicitur: Hoc proprie Christus fecit. In corde, qui aliquando tacuit indignis fraudulenter quaerentibus. Non egit dolum. Dolus est in lingua, cum aliud dicitur, aliud est in pectore. Vel, non egit dolum, quia omnia quae audivit a Patre, 864Csine aliqua adjectione vel suppressione, nota fecit proximis, id est, discipulis; Judaeis, proximis secundum carnem. Nec fecit proximo malum. Sed pro eis oravit; non acceptum habuit opprobrium adversus proximos suos, sicut est patens per hoc quod Judam non mordaci increpatione lacerabat.

VERS. 4.-- Ad nihilum, etc. (AUG.) Haec est perfectio, ut nihil in homine valeat malignus, et ut hic sit in conspectu, id est, certe sciat, malignum non esse, nisi qui a Creatore ad creata convertitur. Malignus, id est, diabolus, despicitur; ut cum dixit: Vade retro, Satanas, etc. E contra, timentes Dominum glorificat. Juravit, quando apostolis certissima veritate promisit: Jam non dicam vos servos, sed amicos.

864DVERS. 5.-- Qui jurat proximo, etc. (Ibid.) Haec tria non sunt magna, etc., usque ad cum in superiori conclusione praeteritum posuerit, ad nihilum deductus est.

Pecuniam. Vel terrena est, quae penitus ad usuram dari prohibetur, quam Dominus Judae tradidit ad erogandum pauperibus, non ad usuram. Vel spiritualis, quae ad usuram dari jubetur, id est, praedicatio ad instruendos homines. Et munera super innocentem. Accipit quidem Christus munera, ut a magis, et quotidie pias oblationes; sed non contra innocentes, imo animam pro eis dedit. Qui facit haec, non movebitur. Ecce absoluta responsio interroganti: facit (dicit), ut ad actum nos invitet, non solum ad 865Acantandum haec. Qui facit haec, non movebitur. (CASS.) Conclusio. Similiter qui facit haec, requiescet in monte.

PSALM XIV.

VERS. 1.-- Lord, who? (CAS.) This psalm is properly an instructor in morals, a repressing of presumption: where 864Bit treats of the unity of the present Church and of the quiet to come. First the prophet asks, as a priest standing before the face of the Lord, and seeks answers; wishing to know whom God judges worthy of his Church.

VERS. 2.-- He that. (Ibid.) The answer of the Lord, etc. as far as as Christ the lamb, without breaking of members, who properly entered the temple, not that he might be expiated like the rest, but without stain. He worketh justice. As when he cast out of the temple those that sold and bought.

VERS. 3.-- He that speaketh. Here he follows it out more fully. Truth is when the thing is so as it is said: this Christ did properly. In his heart, who at times kept silence toward the unworthy who questioned him fraudulently. He hath not wrought deceit. Deceit is in the tongue, when one thing is said and another is in the breast. Or, he hath not wrought deceit, because all that he heard from the Father, 864Cwithout any addition or suppression, he made known to his neighbours, that is, to the disciples; to the Jews, his neighbours according to the flesh. Nor hath he done evil to his neighbour. But he prayed for them; he did not take up reproach against his neighbours, as is plain from this, that he did not tear Judas with a biting rebuke.

VERS. 4.-- To nothing, etc. (AUG.) This is perfection, that the malignant one avail nothing in a man, and that this be in his sight, that is, that he know for certain that no one is malignant save he who turns from the Creator to created things. The malignant one, that is, the devil, is despised; as when he said: Go back, Satan, etc. On the contrary, he glorifieth them that fear the Lord. He swore, when he promised the apostles with most certain truth: Now I will not call you servants, but friends.

864DVERS. 5.-- He that sweareth to his neighbour, etc. (Ibid.) These three things are not great, etc., as far as since in the conclusion above he set down a past tense, he is brought to nothing.

Money. Either it is earthly, which is utterly forbidden to be given out at usury, and which the Lord handed over to Judas to be paid out to the poor, not for usury. Or it is spiritual, which is commanded to be given out at usury, that is, preaching for the instructing of men. And gifts against the innocent. Christ does indeed receive gifts, as from the Magi, and daily devout offerings; but not against the innocent; rather he gave his soul for them. He that doeth these things shall not be moved. Behold the complete answer to the questioner: he does them (he says), that he may invite us to the act, not only to 865Athe singing of them. He that doeth these things shall not be moved. (CASS.) The conclusion. In like manner he that doeth these things shall rest on the mountain.

PSALMUS XV.

VERS. 1.-- Tituli inscriptio. (CASS.) Hic titulus de Evangelio, non de Veteri Testamento, sumitur. Quod titulus notavit, id est, victoria et regnum, convenit Christo, quod hic agitur.

VERS. 2.-- Conserva, etc. Psalmus secundus, qui breviter de passione et resurrectione tangit; primo, unam hominis naturam Christus ostendens, petit se servari, dicens omnia quae pertulit ad gloriam haereditatis suae perducta. (AUG.) Christus secundum hominem hic loquitur, de quo titulus regalis in passione eminuit: Jesus Nazarenus rex Judaeorum.--Bonorum 865Bmeorum, etc. (CASS.) Si Christi hominis bonis non eget Deus, sed ab ipso habet omnia, destruitur arrogantia hominum et haeresis Pelagianorum, qui putant aliquid bonis suis viribus fieri.

VERS. 3.-- Sanctis qui sunt in terra. (Ibid.) Exposuit jam Christus qualiter oravit, narrat nunc quae bona fecit illi Deus. (AUG.) Sanctis, etc., usque ad et potentia ut resurgerem.

Mirificavit. (CASS.) Quasi, haec dixi Domino: Dominus autem mirificavit, id est, fecit miras voluntates, hae sunt mirae dum eis obedientes, fiunt de terrenis coelestes.

VERS. 4.-- Multiplicatae. (Ibid.) Qua mirificavit, 865Cetc., usque ad quae in uno sono consonant, quibus voluntates ejus ostenduntur.

VERS. 5.-- Pars haereditatis. (AUG.) Eligant alii alia, etc., usque ad sed qui Deum eligunt partem. (CASS.) Vel, Dominus est pars, id est, portio et praemium, haereditatis meae, id est, sanctorum. Et pars calicis mei, id est, merces passionis. Haereditas enim ad gentes, calix ad passionem pertinet, qui bibitus dat resurrectionem. Sed nemo se putet haeredem nisi praeclarus.

VERS. 6.-- Funes, etc. (Ibid.) Quasi forte, in qua est divina electio, ut et sors cecidit super Matthiam, et quisque capit ad mensuram suam. In praeclaris. Id est, in sanctis.

VERS. 7.-- Benedicam Dominum. (Ibid.) Gratias 865Dagit Patri de intellectu, et passione, in qua eo favente vincit, et de resurrectione, et confessione, et haec sunt, per quae haereditas restituitur ut sit rex Judaeorum, ut titulus dicit. Intellectum, etc. (AUG.) Quo haec haereditas videri et possideri potest. Insuper, etc. Id est, super intellectum. Usque ad noctem, etc. Id est, mortem, erudivit me, inferior pars mea carnis assumptio, ut expelleret tenebras mortalitatis quas ille intellectus non habet, quia pro eis nec turbari nec deficere potuit. Renes. Ex quibus secundum carnem exivi, scilicet parentela: increpuerunt injuriis, tentatione et passione.

VERS. 8.-- Providebam Dominum. (Ibid.) Hinc trahe exemplum, quo peccata vitentur: qui enim 866ADeum semper acie mentis intuetur, non peccatis inclinatur.

PSALM XV.

VERS. 1.-- The inscription of a title. (CASS.) This title is taken from the Gospel, not from the Old Testament. What the title noted, that is, victory and kingdom, belongs to Christ, and that is what is treated of here.

VERS. 2.-- Preserve me, etc. The second psalm, which touches briefly on the passion and the resurrection; first, Christ, showing the one nature of man, asks to be preserved, saying that all that he endured has been brought through to the glory of his inheritance. (AUG.) Christ speaks here according to his manhood, of whom the royal title stood out in the passion: Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews.--Of my 865Bgoods, etc. (CASS.) If God has no need of the goods of Christ the man, but Christ the man has all things from him, the arrogance of men is overthrown, and the heresy of the Pelagians, who think that anything is done by their own good powers.

VERS. 3.-- To the saints who are in the land. (Ibid.) Christ has now set out how he prayed; he now tells what good things God did for him. (AUG.) To the saints, etc., as far as and power that I might rise again.

He hath made wonderful. (CASS.) As if to say, these things I said to the Lord: but the Lord made them wonderful, that is, he made my wills wonderful; and they are wonderful in that those who obey them become heavenly out of earthly.

VERS. 4.-- They are multiplied. (Ibid.) Whereby he made them wonderful, 865Cetc., as far as which sound together in one note, by which his wills are shown.

VERS. 5.-- The portion of my inheritance. (AUG.) Let others choose other things, etc., as far as but those who choose God as their portion. (CASS.) Or, the Lord is the portion, that is, the share and the reward, of my inheritance, that is, of the saints. And the portion of my cup, that is, the wage of the passion. For the inheritance belongs to the Gentiles, the cup to the passion, which when drunk gives resurrection. But let no one think himself an heir save he that is illustrious.

VERS. 6.-- The lines, etc. (Ibid.) As it were by lot, in which is the divine election, as the lot also fell upon Matthias, and each man takes according to his own measure. In goodly places. That is, among the saints.

VERS. 7.-- I will bless the Lord. (Ibid.) He gives 865Dthanks to the Father for understanding, and for the passion, in which by his favour he conquers, and for the resurrection, and for confession; and these are the things through which the inheritance is restored, so that he is king of the Jews, as the title says. Understanding, etc. (AUG.) Whereby this inheritance can be seen and possessed. Moreover, etc. That is, above understanding. Even till night, etc. That is, till death, he hath instructed me, that is, my lower part, the assumption of flesh, that he might drive out the darknesses of mortality which that understanding does not have, because for them it could neither be troubled nor fail. My reins. From whom according to the flesh I came forth, namely my kindred: they have chided me with injuries, with temptation and with passion.

VERS. 8.-- I set the Lord before me. (Ibid.) From this draw an example, whereby sins may be shunned: for he who 866Aalways beholds God with the keen edge of the mind is not bowed down by sins.

PSALMUS XVI.

VERS. 1.-- Oratio David. (CASS.) Oratio personae Domini convenit, adjuncta Ecclesia, quae ejus corpus est. Exaudi, Domine. (Ibid.) Iste psalmus veram naturam humanitatis facit attendere. Oratio Christi institutio est fidelium: sicut flendo Lazarum charitatem proximi habere nos docuit; persecutores fugit, ut inconsideratae temeritatis nobis auferret audaciam. Primo, petit secundum justitiam sibi retribui. Non in labiis dolosis. Ut qui inique damnatur; vel, ut qui dicit: Domine, Domine, et non facit opera. (AUG.) Vel, non in labiis dolosis de vultu tuo judicium meum prodeat, ut judicans non proferam 866Baliud quam intelligo.

VERS. 2.-- De vultu tuo. (CASS.) Id est, secundum ea quae in me cognoscis, qui nullum habeo peccatum. Judicium. Quo sui judicatus videatur prodisse. De vultu tuo, non de dispositione Judaeorum, quod factum patet in resurrectione. Vel, judicium, quo discernit omnia.

VERS. 3.-- Probasti. (CASS.) A similitudine fornacis, etc., usque ad tu scis me purum.

VERS. 4.-- Vias duras. (Ibid.) Scilicet opera hominum: quas scilicet merentur opera hominum. Vel quas debent imitari homines, quibus iter vitiorum leve est, virtutum difficile. Vel, non est inventa, ita ut non loquatur, id est, ut non jactanter haec dicam, vel, ut non peccem in lingua, quod est opus hominum. 866C(AUG.) Vel, vias duras latronis, etc., usque ad postquam perrexi vias duras et perfeci gressus.

VERS. 5.-- Perfice. (CASS.) Usque in finem: ante non est nisi inchoatio. Gressus, id est, humanas actiones, ut qui volunt imitari non moveantur a te, vel vestigia ab eis.

VERS. 6.-- Ego clamavi. (Ibid.) Secundo, precatur ut a Judaeorum insidiis ejus puritas liberetur. Ego etiam clamavi, quasi diceres, hoc non nisi justo convenit, qui confidenter orat, quia scit audiri.

VERS. 7.-- Mirifica. (AUG.) Mira, sunt quae nova sunt: haec sunt quae in carne cessit mirantibus Judaeis.

VERS. 8.-- Pupillam. Perexigua est, et tamen per eam acies luminis dirigitur, quo lux et tenebrae dijudicantur, 866Dsicut per humanitatem Christi divinitas discernens est inter bonos et malos.

VERS. 10.-- Adipem. (CASS.) A similitudine animalium, quae ex adipe inflantur, id est, superbiam retinuerunt, non macri, id est, non humiles, adipem, id est, carnalem sensum retinuerunt, vel sceleribus saginati veram intelligentiam perdiderunt, unde restat superba loqui. Os eorum locutum est superbiam. Non cor, quia saepe iniqui quod ore defendunt, corde damnant.

VERS. 12.-- Susceperunt me, etc. (Ibid.) Unde eis haec opportunitas? Respondeo susceperunt a Deo cujus dispositio est, vel, a traditore, vel, a judice acceperunt avide. Sicut leo paratus, etc. (AUG., CASS.) 867APrincipes comparandi leoni diabolo, quo auctore faciunt: Populus catulus leonis, id est, filius diaboli, habitans, permanens in insidiis, quia mos est malis vota tegere, ut latenter possint perficere.

VERS. 13.-- Exsurge, Domine. (CASS.) De retributionibus oratio. Praeveni, etc. (Ibid.) A similitudine currentis: nemo non prius in se quam in alium peccat. Supplanta eum: a similitudine luctantis, id est, inefficaces fac et dejice eos. Eripe animam meam ab impio. (AUG.) Resuscitando a morte ab impiis illata. Frameam. Anima mea est framea; quam manus, id est, virtus tua assumpsit, ut per eam regna iniquitatis debellet, et justos dividat ab impiis. Divide eos, etc., (CASS.) id est, Judaeos divisos, etc., usque ad miseria, quasi merito: quia, de absconditis. De absconditis 867Btuis. Id est, de immunditiis, etc., usque ad id est, ad satietatem usque malorum participes erunt. De absconditis. (AUG.) Non solum eis haec poena visibilis, sed de absconditis, id est, peccatis (quae a lumine veritatis tuae absconduntur) plena est memoria eorum, ut obliviscantur Deum.

PSALM XVI.

VERS. 1.-- The prayer of David. (CASS.) The prayer belongs to the person of the Lord, the Church being joined to him, which is his body. Hear, O Lord. (Ibid.) This psalm makes us attend to the true nature of his humanity. The prayer of Christ is an instruction of the faithful: as by weeping over Lazarus he taught us to have charity toward our neighbour; he fled his persecutors, that he might take from us the boldness of ill-considered rashness. First, he asks that it be rendered to him according to justice. Not in deceitful lips. As one who is unjustly condemned; or, as one who says: Lord, Lord, and does not do the works. (AUG.) Or, let my judgment come forth from thy countenance not in deceitful lips, so that in judging I may not put forth 866Banything other than I understand.

VERS. 2.-- From thy countenance. (CASS.) That is, according to those things which thou knowest in me, who have no sin. Judgment. Whereby he who was judged may be seen to have come forth as his own. From thy countenance, not from the disposition of the Jews, which deed is plain in the resurrection. Or, judgment, whereby he discerns all things.

VERS. 3.-- Thou hast proved. (CASS.) From the likeness of a furnace, etc., as far as thou knowest me to be pure.

VERS. 4.-- Hard ways. (Ibid.) Namely the works of men: which, namely, the works of men deserve. Or, which men ought to imitate, for whom the road of the vices is easy, that of the virtues hard. Or, it was not found, so that he should not speak, that is, that I may not say these things boastfully, or, that I may not sin with my tongue, which is the work of men. 866C(AUG.) Or, the hard ways of the thief, etc., as far as after I had gone along the hard ways and completed my steps.

VERS. 5.-- Perfect thou. (CASS.) Even to the end: before that there is nothing but a beginning. Steps, that is, human actions, so that they who wish to imitate may not be moved away from thee, nor their footsteps from them.

VERS. 6.-- I have cried. (Ibid.) Secondly, he prays that his purity be delivered from the ambushes of the Jews. I too have cried, as though thou shouldst say, this belongs to none but the just man, who prays with confidence, because he knows he is heard.

VERS. 7.-- Make wonderful. (AUG.) Wonderful are the things that are new: these are the things which he yielded in the flesh, the Jews marvelling.
