VERS. 8.-- The apple of the eye. It is very small, and yet through it the keen edge of sight is directed, whereby light and darkness are distinguished, 866Djust as through the humanity of Christ the godhead is what discerns between the good and the evil.

VERS. 10.-- Their fat. (CASS.) From the likeness of animals, which are puffed up from fat, that is, they have kept pride, not lean, that is, not humble; the fat, that is, they have kept the carnal understanding; or, fattened with crimes they have lost true understanding, whence it remains for them to speak proud things. Their mouth hath spoken pride. Not their heart, because often the wicked condemn in their heart what they defend with their mouth.

VERS. 12.-- They have taken me, etc. (Ibid.) Whence had they this opportunity? I answer: they took it from God, whose ordering it is; or, from the betrayer; or, they received it greedily from the judge. As a lion prepared, etc. (AUG., CASS.) 867AThe princes are to be compared to the lion, the devil, by whose authorship they act: the people is the young of a lion, that is, the son of the devil, dwelling, remaining in ambushes, because it is the way of evil men to cover their vows, that they may accomplish them secretly.

VERS. 13.-- Arise, O Lord. (CASS.) A prayer concerning retributions. Prevent, etc. (Ibid.) From the likeness of one running: there is no one who does not sin against himself before he sins against another. Supplant him: from the likeness of one wrestling, that is, make them ineffectual and cast them down. Deliver my soul from the wicked one. (AUG.) By raising it again from the death brought upon it by the wicked. The sword. My soul is the sword, which thy hand, that is, thy power, took up, that through it he might war down the kingdoms of iniquity and divide the just from the wicked. Divide them, etc., (CASS.) that is, the Jews divided, etc., as far as misery, as though deservedly: because, of the hidden things. Of the hidden things 867Bthat are thine. That is, of uncleannesses, etc., as far as that is, they shall be sharers of evils even to satiety. Of the hidden things. (AUG.) Not only is this punishment visible to them, but from hidden things, that is, from sins (which are hidden away from the light of thy truth), their memory is full, so that they forget God.

PSALMUS XVII.

VERS. 1.-- Diligam te, Domine, fortitudo mea, etc. (CASS.) Dicit hoc Christus, quod Ecclesia, id est, totus Christus.

(Ibid.) Primo, propheta summam colligens, de liberatione gratias agit.

VERS. 3.-- Refugium. (Ibid.) Quando erat opus consilio, David ad eum refugit et invenit. Liberator, ut si potens, captum ab hostibus liberet. Protector, 867C(AUG.) quia de me non praesumpsi, quasi cornu superbiae contra te erigens; sed te celsitudinem salutis inveni, quod ut invenirem suscepisti me.

VERS. 4.-- Laudans invocabo. (CASS.) Post omnia non elatus se jactat, sed omnia Deo tribuit: et ideo salvus; nam qui aliter facit, sibi relictus perit, etsi vicisse videbatur.

VERS. 5.-- Circumdederunt me. (Ibid.) In persona iustorum ante adventum Christi, etc., usque ad qui rapidis iniquitatibus conturbati sunt.

VERS. 6.-- Dolores inferni. Gentiles in inferno debito dolore torquendi. Praeoccupaverunt me laquei mortis, sequitur:

VERS. 8.-- Commota est. Ecce quomodo, etc., usque ad et hoc qui praeoccupavit mortalitas et possibilitas.

867DDe templo. (CASS.) Vel de coelo, vel de venturo Christi corpore.

Commota est. (AUG.) Ita clarificato Christo commoti sunt et contremuerunt peccatores. Fundamenta, etc. (CASS.) Praesumptiones superborum, id est, divitiae et hujusmodi quibus innitebantur: spes enim mundi abiit, quam odit Deus.

VERS. 10.-- Coelos. (Ibid.) Id est, praedicatores inclinavit a contemplativa ad ministerium, et ad ferendas molestias. Descendit, etc. Ipse passus in eis, et in quorumdam notitiam. Caligo: tenebrosi, qui etiam persequuntur, sub ejus potestate sunt; vel, qui simpliciter credunt, subjecti ei sunt.

868AVERS. 11.-- Et ascendit. Facit enim quosdam plenos scientia, in quibus supereminet, quorum celeritatem intellectus transcendit: tenebrosis autem latenter utitur: unde, Virga furoris mei Assur, ipse vero non cognovit, sed sui cognoscunt. Volavit super pennas vento. Ventos, quibus nihil est velocius, superat fama ejus, ut dum mox natus, magis per stellam nuntiatus est.

VERS. 12.-- Tenebras. (AUG.) Obscuritates sacramentorum, vel, in his tenebris, ubi videntes per fidem ambulamus, et non per speciem (Matth. II).

Non per coelos. (CASS.) Descendit et ascendit (II Cor. V), sed per nubes aethereas (quod in Hebraeo), id est, per prophetas in quibus obscura doctrina sit, sed per nubes quae (non aetheris, id est, Apostoli) 868Bpraefulgidae sunt in cognitione ejus, id est, vicinius contemplantes.

VERS. 13.-- Grando. (AUG.) Objurgationes, quae dura corda feriunt, sed si ignis charitatis resolvit, in miti animo fit aqua satians [ alias saliens]. Et carbones, quia illo igne tenebrosa corda accensa reviviscunt.

VERS. 14.-- Intonuit. (CASS.) Ad litteram, ut quando visum est tonitruum, Deo dicente: Clarificavi, et iterum clarificabo. Dedit vocem: ut non dixit: Hic est Filius meus dilectus in quo mihi complacui.

VERS. 15.-- Et misit. (Ibid.) Dominus intonuit, et Dominus misit: non enim transitus ad gentes semper erat certus neque rationabilis habitus.

VERS. 16.-- Et apparuerunt fontes. Christo veniente, 868Cpatuit quod obscuritas divini tegebat eloquii. Ab increpatione. Conversio ad Deum: quasi cum gratiarum actione, quia per praedicationem increpabat peccantes, et inspirabat ut timerent iram futuram.

Misit. (Ibid.) Hucusque de adventu Domini, hinc de temporibus Christianis. Misit Pater Christum. Accepit me. Ecclesiam sponsam. De aquis. (Ibid.) Baptismi. Vel misit Spiritum, qui est donum. De alto, quia aequalis Patri et Filio. Accepit, quasi fugativam. Assumpsit, in altitudinem virtutis et boni operis.

VERS. 18.-- De inimicis meis. (AUG.) Id est, vitiis, quae super omnes inimicos plus nocent. Et ab his qui, etc. Id est exterioribus inimicis hominibus, scilicet et daemonibus quod necesse est, quia confortati 868Dsecundum quid. Ecce praevenerunt, id est, praevaluerunt. Per hoc magis eripit, quia illi sunt confortati; cum enim affligitur Ecclesia, magis crescit.

VERS. 20.-- In latitudinem. (Ibid.) Per saevitiam malorum, crescit Ecclesia numero et merito. Salvum me fecit, quod ad fidem venit. Quoniam voluit me. (AUG.) Id est, gratis elegit.

VERS. 21.-- Et retribuet secundum justitiam bonae voluntatis. Et secundum puritatem manuum (Ibid.) opera, quae sunt post prima beneficia Dei, scilicet fidem et charitatem, quae gratuito sine praecedenti merito Deus praestat.

VERS. 22.-- Quia custodivi. (Ibid.) Vel ita continuando 869Acum praecedente versu, etc., usque ad et sicut coepi, ero immaculatus, unde in futuro retribuet.

VERS. 24.-- Cum eo, ei, adhaerens. Et observabo, ne iterum cadam. Ab iniquitate, quae est mors beati.

VERS. 25.-- Et retribuet. (CASS.) Dupliciter Deus retribuit: hic in praesenti, ut justus justificetur, et qui in sordibus est, sordescat adhuc, unde hic dicit: Cum sancto sanctus, etc., et in futuro praemium bonis, et poenam malis, unde ibi: Quoniam tu populum humilem, etc., quasi, ita hic: quia in futuro tu populum humilem salvum facies.

(AUG.) Et tribuet: jam non solum propter latitudinem fidei quae per dilectionem operatur, sed propter longanimitatem retribuet mihi. In conspectu: 869Bhoc justis convenit, ut sicut illi Deum semper contuentur, ita Deus eos jugiter respiciat.

VERS. 26.-- Cum sancto. (CASS.) Dixerat, retribui secundum justitiam, etc., usque ad quia tu, Domine, populum humilem salvum facies. Et oculos superborum humiliabis.

(AUG.) Est etiam occulta profunditas, qua intelligeris cum sancto sanctus, quia tu sanctificas.

Quoniam tu illuminas. Quod enuntiavit de electis et sanctificatis, orat nunc de aliis.

VERS. 29.-- Lucernam. (Ibid.) Fuerunt praedicatores, in quibus lux, id est, cognitio veritatis, qua illuminaverunt alios, unde: Habemus thesaurum istum in vasis fictilibus. Tenebras. (AUG.) eos, qui adhuc sunt in tenebris. Meas. Praedestinatione.

869CVERS. 30.-- In Deo meo. (CASS.) Deus enim meus, est via, qua itur ad coelum, impolluta. Vel, via qua venit in mundum sancta et immaculata Virgo. Et quidquid dixit Spiritu sancto examinatum est, id est, utile et honestum: ut sapiens, quidquid dicit, prius apud se dijudicat. Transgrediar. (Ibid.) Diruere non penitus potest homo, sed ope Dei transit murum obstaculum peccatorum.

VERS. 31.-- Deus meus. (Ibid.) Et continuando sequitur: Eripies me de contradictionibus populi. Caetera interponit ad commendationem. Eloquia. Igne examinationis probantur. Omnium. (Ibid.) Nullus excipitur, nisi qui sperare non vult.

VERS. 32.-- Quoniam quis. (Ibid.) Deus dico: quia quis est alius Deus, nisi qui et Dominus in rebus 869Dest? Et quia in Judaea notus, non dii gentium; haec contra paganos, qui multos sibi fingunt.

VERS. 33.-- Deus qui. (Ibid.) Adhuc praeter communia, commendat per specialia, quia tertio Christus de virtute et potentia sua commendatur. Praecinxit. (Ibid.) Id est, perarmavit. Vel a similitudine currentis. Vel, dignitatem notat et fortitudinem, quod ei convenit, qui potestate sua judicabit populum, vel mundum. Immaculatam, sine peccato. Cervus spinas et hiantia loca transilit, sic Christus spinas et foveas peccatorum: et sicut cervus alta, ita Christus super omnes creaturas conscendit.

VERS. 35.-- Qui docet: ab imminentibus insidiis cautum facio. Manus, opera vel voluntates. Ad praelium, 870Acontra diabolum. Ut arcum, etc., similitudine rei quae non est, id est, irremissibilem fortitudinem. Brachia. Christi prophetae, et apostoli, per quos operatur: qui arcus aereus, quia praedicando non mollescunt, sed, semper fortes, verba salutis jaculantur.

VERS. 36.-- Protectionem salutis. Non ut nihil patiar, quod tamen est ad profectum. Tribulatio est correctio, et doctrina, et dilatatio, et confirmatio.

VERS. 37.-- Dilatasti (AUG.) Ne impediant carnales angustiae, quia latam fecisti charitatem hilariter operantem, etiam de his quae sunt sub me, scilicet de mortalibus rebus et membris.

VERS. 38.-- Persequar. (CASS.) Arguendo, diversis afflictionibus fatigando.

VERS. 43.-- Et comminuam. (AUG.) Ecce eadem 870Boperatio Patris et Filii. Supra ait: Disperdidisti, Pater, et jam ait comminuam, id est, auferam virtutes, ut post cedant omni vento doctrinae.

VERS. 44.-- Eripies. (CASS.) De illis ira: Sed eripies me, depressio Judaeorum, et exaltatio gentium.

VERS. 46.-- Filii. Judaei quos enutrivi, facti alieni: Mentiti sunt mihi, ad honorem meum. Inveterati sunt et claudicaverunt a semitis suis, sequentes potius suas traditiones quam Dei.

VERS. 47.-- Vivit. (Ibid.) Quarto exsultans Ecclesia summatim munera Dei laudat. Vel vivit, quia vivificat. Benedictus, quia omnia benedicit. Et exaltetur Deus salutis. (AUG.) Non terreno more de Deo salutis meae sentiam, nec ipsam salutem terrenam, 870Csed in excelso de illo sperabo.

VERS. 48.-- Vindictas. (CASS.) Pia vindicta, dum rebellis subditur. Iracundis. Major gloria est a ferventibus malis liberare.

VERS. 51.-- Magnificans, salutes. Deus qui magnificat: Faciens, Deus qui facit.

PSALM XVII.

VERS. 1.-- I will love thee, O Lord, my strength, etc. (CASS.) Christ says this, and so the Church, that is, the whole Christ.

(Ibid.) First, the prophet, gathering up the sum, gives thanks for the deliverance.

VERS. 3.-- My refuge. (Ibid.) When there was need of counsel, David fled to him and found it. My deliverer, as one who, being powerful, sets free a man taken captive by his enemies. My protector, 867C(AUG.) because I have not presumed upon myself, as though raising a horn of pride against thee; but I have found thee the height of my salvation, and that I might find it thou hast taken me up.

VERS. 4.-- Praising I will call upon. (CASS.) After all things he does not boast of himself, puffed up, but ascribes all to God: and therefore he is safe; for he who does otherwise, left to himself, perishes, even though he seemed to have conquered.

VERS. 5.-- They have compassed me about. (Ibid.) In the person of the just before the coming of Christ, etc., as far as who have been troubled by rushing iniquities.

VERS. 6.-- The sorrows of hell. The Gentiles, to be tormented in hell with the sorrow they have deserved. The snares of death have prevented me, there follows:

VERS. 8.-- It was moved. Behold how, etc., as far as and this, which mortality and possibility forestalled.

867DOut of his temple. (CASS.) Either of heaven, or of the body of Christ that was to come.

It was moved. (AUG.) Thus, when Christ was glorified, sinners were moved and trembled. The foundations, etc. (CASS.) The presumptions of the proud, that is, riches and the like on which they leaned: for the hope of the world, which God hates, has passed away.

VERS. 10.-- The heavens. (Ibid.) That is, he bowed the preachers down from the contemplative life to ministry, and to the bearing of troubles. He came down, etc. He himself suffered in them, and came into the knowledge of certain men. Darkness: the dark, who even persecute, are under his power; or, those who believe simply are subject to him.

868AVERS. 11.-- And he ascended. For he makes certain men full of knowledge, in whom he stands out above, whose swiftness of understanding he transcends: but the dark he uses secretly: whence, Assur is the rod of my wrath, yet he himself hath not known it, but his own know. He flew upon the wings of the wind. [Vulg. Ps 17:11 volavit super pennas ventorum, "the wings of the winds", plural — the plural the gloss's own Ventos takes up] The winds, than which nothing is swifter, his fame outstrips, as when, newly born, he was rather announced by a star.

VERS. 12.-- Darkness. (AUG.) The obscurities of the sacraments; or, in these darknesses, where seeing we walk by faith, and not by sight (Matth. II).

Not through the heavens. (CASS.) He came down and ascended (II Cor. V), but through the ethereal clouds (which is in the Hebrew), that is, through the prophets in whom the teaching is obscure; but through the clouds which (not of the ether, that is, the Apostles) 868Bare exceedingly bright in the knowledge of him, that is, contemplating more nearly.

VERS. 13.-- Hail. (AUG.) Rebukes, which strike hard hearts; but if the fire of charity dissolves them, in a gentle soul it becomes water that satisfies [ alias saliens]. And coals, because by that fire dark hearts are kindled and come to life again.

VERS. 14.-- He thundered. (CASS.) To the letter, as when the thunder was seen, God saying: I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again. He gave his voice: in that he did not say: This is my beloved Son in whom I am well pleased.

VERS. 15.-- And he sent. (Ibid.) The Lord thundered, and the Lord sent: for the passing over to the Gentiles was not always held to be certain nor reasonable.

VERS. 16.-- And the fountains appeared. When Christ came, 868Cthere lay open what the obscurity of the divine word had covered. At thy rebuke. A turning to God: as it were with thanksgiving, because through preaching he rebuked sinners, and breathed into them that they should fear the wrath to come.

He sent. (Ibid.) Thus far concerning the coming of the Lord; from here on, concerning Christian times. He sent, the Father, Christ. He took me. The Church his bride. Out of the waters. (Ibid.) Of baptism. Or he sent the Spirit, who is the gift. From on high, because he is equal to the Father and to the Son. He took, as it were a runaway. He assumed, into the height of virtue and of good work.

VERS. 18.-- From my enemies. (AUG.) That is, from vices, which above all enemies do the more harm. And from them who, etc. That is, from outward enemies, men, and also demons, as must needs be, because they have been strengthened 868Din a certain respect. Behold, they have prevented, that is, they have prevailed. By this he delivers the more, because they have been strengthened; for when the Church is afflicted, it grows the more.

VERS. 20.-- Into a large place. (Ibid.) Through the savagery of the wicked, the Church grows in number and in merit. He hath saved me, in that it came to the faith. Because he would have me. (AUG.) That is, he chose freely.

VERS. 21.-- And he will reward according to the justice of a good will. And according to the cleanness of the hands (Ibid.) the works which come after the first benefits of God, namely faith and charity, which God bestows freely, without preceding merit.

VERS. 22.-- Because I have kept. (Ibid.) Or, joining it thus 869Awith the preceding verse, etc., as far as and as I have begun, I shall be unspotted, whence in time to come he will reward me.

VERS. 24.-- With him, cleaving to him. And I will keep myself, lest I fall again. From iniquity, which is the death of the blessed man.

VERS. 25.-- And he will reward. (CASS.) God rewards in two ways: here in the present, that the just may be justified, and he that is in filth may be filthy still, whence here he says: With the holy thou wilt be holy, etc.; and in time to come a reward for the good and a punishment for the evil, whence there: For thou wilt save the humble people, etc., as if to say, so here: because in time to come thou wilt save the humble people.

(AUG.) And he will give: now not only for the breadth of faith which works through love, but for long-suffering he will reward me. In the sight: 869Bthis belongs to the just, that as they always behold God, so God may continually look upon them.

VERS. 26.-- With the holy. (CASS.) He had said that it was rendered according to justice, etc., as far as because thou, O Lord, wilt save the humble people. And thou wilt bring down the eyes of the proud.

(AUG.) There is also a hidden depth, by which thou art understood to be holy with the holy, because it is thou that sanctifiest.

For thou dost light. What he declared concerning the elect and the sanctified, he now prays concerning others.

VERS. 29.-- My lamp. (Ibid.) There were preachers, in whom was light, that is, the knowledge of truth, by which they enlightened others; whence: We have this treasure in earthen vessels. Darkness. (AUG.) those who are still in darkness. Mine. By predestination.

869CVERS. 30.-- In my God. (CASS.) For my God is the way, undefiled, by which one goes to heaven. Or, the way by which the holy and immaculate Virgin came into the world. And whatever he said has been tried by the Holy Spirit, that is, it is useful and honourable: as a wise man first judges within himself whatever he says. I shall go over. (Ibid.) A man cannot utterly pull it down, but by the help of God he passes over the wall, the obstacle of sins.

VERS. 31.-- My God. (Ibid.) And, joining them, there follows: Thou wilt deliver me from the contradictions of the people. The rest he interposes by way of commendation. The words. They are proved by the fire of trial. Of all. (Ibid.) No one is excepted, save he who will not hope.

VERS. 32.-- For who. (Ibid.) I say God: for who is another God, save he who also 869Dis Lord over things? And because he is known in Judea, not the gods of the nations; these things are against the pagans, who fashion many for themselves.

VERS. 33.-- God who. (Ibid.) Still further, beyond what is common, he commends him by what is special, for thirdly Christ is commended for his virtue and his power. He hath girded. (Ibid.) That is, he has armed him thoroughly. Or, from the likeness of one running. Or, it marks dignity and strength, which belongs to him who by his own power will judge the people, or the world. Unspotted, without sin. The stag leaps over thorns and gaping places, so Christ over the thorns and pits of sins: and as the stag climbs the heights, so Christ ascends above all creatures.

VERS. 35.-- Who teacheth: I make him wary of the ambushes that threaten. Hands, works or wills. To battle, 870Aagainst the devil. As a bow, etc., by the likeness of a thing which does not exist, that is, unrelenting strength. Arms. The prophets of Christ, and the apostles, through whom he works: who are a brazen bow, because they do not grow soft by preaching, but, always strong, hurl forth the words of salvation.

VERS. 36.-- The protection of salvation. Not that I should suffer nothing, which nevertheless is for my profit. Tribulation is correction, and teaching, and enlargement, and confirmation.

VERS. 37.-- Thou hast enlarged (AUG.) Lest fleshly straits hinder, because thou hast made wide the charity that works cheerfully, even out of those things which are under me, namely out of mortal things and members.

VERS. 38.-- I will pursue. (CASS.) By reproving, by wearying them with divers afflictions.

VERS. 43.-- And I will break them small. (AUG.) Behold the same 870Boperation of the Father and of the Son. Above he says: Thou hast destroyed, O Father, and now he says, I will break them small, that is, I will take away their powers, so that afterwards they may yield to every wind of doctrine.

VERS. 44.-- Thou wilt deliver. (CASS.) Upon them, wrath: But thou wilt deliver me, the casting down of the Jews, and the exalting of the Gentiles.

VERS. 46.-- The children. The Jews whom I nourished, made strangers: They have lied to me, as to my honour. They have grown old and have halted from their paths, following their own traditions rather than God's.

VERS. 47.-- He liveth. (Ibid.) Fourthly, the Church exulting praises in sum the gifts of God. Or he liveth, because he gives life. Blessed, because he blesses all things. And let the God of salvation be exalted. (AUG.) I will not think of the God of my salvation after an earthly manner, nor of that salvation itself as earthly, 870Cbut on high I will hope in him.

VERS. 48.-- Revenges. (CASS.) The vengeance is dutiful, when the rebel is subdued. From the wrathful. It is a greater glory to deliver from raging evils.

VERS. 51.-- Magnifying, the salvations. God who magnifies: Doing, God who does.

PSALMUS XVIII.

VERS. 1.-- In finem. (CASS.) Psalmus de primo adventu, unde tyrannus cadit, homo absolvitur, hic propheta respicit in finem, id est, Christum, vel in ultima tempora.

VERS. 2.-- Coeli enarrant. (Ibid.) Primo, loquens de incarnatione, commendat praedicationem novae legis. (AUG.) Coeli, apostoli, de gloria Christi in qua 870DPatris aequalis. (CASS.) Vel coeli, qui stellam miserunt. Gloriam. (Ibid.): Quod Deus gratis peccata dimittat. Opera. (AUG.) Quae secundum hominem, etc., usque ad et ipsi eidem facti nox, tenebrosis scientiam quae de humanis. (CASS.) Et hoc tam mirifice, quod in omnibus linguis; et tam late, quod in omni parte ambitus terrae.

VERS. 3.-- Dies diei. (CASS.) Demonstrative agit. (AUG.) Dies diei. Spiritus spiritualibus profert plenitudinem sapientiae, etc., usque ad haec doctrina diebus et noctibus continuatur usque ad posteros.

VERS. 4.-- Loquelae. (CASS.) Publicae suasiones. Sermones. Communes narrationes. Quorum non. Planius diceret, in quibus non audiantur voces eorum, 871Avel, omnium sermonum audiantur voces eorum: illud idem facit per relativum.

(AUG.) Omnibus linguis primos loqui fecit spiritus, qui omnes gentes in unum erat congregaturus, unus homo tunc omnibus, sic modo unus Christus caput et corpus.

VERS. 6.-- In sole (CASS.) Quod alios fecisse laudat, ipse facit, praedicat incarnationem. Vel in sole, in manifesto mundi, vel in labore. Sol urit, lucet, et variat tempora. Tabernaculum suum. (AUG.) Quasi militare habitaculum, id est, dispensationem incarnationis suae, in qua venit expugnare errores mundi. Vel tabernaculum, Ecclesiam in manifesto, non in occulto, ut lateat. Sponsus. (CASS.) Toties prophetis promissus, magna similitudo sacramenti: ideo de 871Bvirgine natus, ut Ecclesiam sibi virginem copularet. De thalamo. (AUG.) Id est, virginali utero, ubi Deus humanae naturae, ut sponsus sponsae, copulatus est. Ecce humilis misericordia, sed fortis majestate. Gigas ad currendam. (CASS.) Imperturbabilis, irrevocabilis, humanam naturam potentia superans. A summo. Hic Trinitas ostenditur, etc., usque ad notat unitatem Trinitatis. Nec est qui se abscondat, etc. (AUG.) Verbum caro factum, non permisit ullum se excusare de umbra mortis: quia et ipsam penetravit calor verbi. Vel, calor est Spiritus, quem misit reversus, qui lex, testimonium, justitia, praeceptum, timor et judicia, quia haec agit.

VERS. 8.-- Lex Domini. (CAS.) Secundo, laudat praecepta Novi et Veteris Testamenti. (Ibid.) Lex per 871CMoysen data, omnia verba sua distinctione corrigens, et ad Christi gratiam mittens. Convertens. (AUG.) Libertate, ad se imitandum, non premens jugo servitutis. Anima. Voluntates, non modo manus, ut Vetus Testamentum. Testimonium. Quaecunquae testimonia dedit Israel plena sunt veritate, et humilibus sapientiam dederunt. Sapientium: de divinis.

VERS. 9.-- Justitiae Domini. (Ibid.) Omnes in illo recte, qui non docuit quod non fecit, ut imitantes gauderent in eis, qui libere cum charitate facerent, non serviliter cum timore. (CASS.) Justitiae, lex quae justificat; quidquid praecipit justum est.

VERS. 10.-- Timor Domini. (Ibid.) Timor saeculi non sanctus, quia non proficuus, et cum temporibus mutatur. Timor Domini sine omni perturbatione, 871Dquia est mista cum pavore dilectio, quia si timet judicem, scit misericordem. (AUG.) Timor, non ille poenalis pro terrenis quorum amore formidat anima, sed castus, quo quanto diligit, cavet offendere sponsum, et ideo non foras mittitur, sed permanet. Judicia. Judicia Dei non egent alterius auctoritate.

VERS. 11.-- Desiderabilia. (Ibid.) Vel, multum desiderabilia, vel multum aurum et lapis; vel multum pretiosum. Desiderabilia super aurum, etc., usque ad, cujus voluntatem suae praeponit, et dulciora sunt quam ipse sibi. Super aurum, id est, omne quod appetitur, pro divitiis, vel potentia, vel pro voluptate. Mel. Cibus Dei est mel; id est, solutus jam a saeculo; et favus, id est, quia adhuc circumplicatur, cui opus 872Aest pressura exprimentis manus Dei, ut eat in vitam.

VERS. 13.-- Delicta quis. (Ibid.) Tertio petit se a vitiis purgari, ut sit dignus Psalmista, qui haec referat sacramenta. Menti videnti suavis est veritas, dulcia judicia; non videnti quae suavitas? sed quare non videtur? propter delicta: nec mirum: Delicta enim quis intelligit? (CASS.) Delicta: omnia, quaedam enim nota sunt. Mea inquinant, aliena affligunt, et jam parce, repelle suasorem. Ab occultis. Omnia peccata duobus includit, etc., usque ad quo homo seductus est; et consentiendo fecit suum. (AUG.) Non est majus delictum quam apostatare a Deo, quod est initium superbiae: superbia vero est initium et causa omnis peccati.

PSALM XVIII.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end. (CASS.) A psalm of the first coming, whereby the tyrant falls and man is set free; here the prophet looks unto the end, that is, unto Christ, or unto the last times.

VERS. 2.-- The heavens shew forth. (Ibid.) First, speaking of the incarnation, he commends the preaching of the new law. (AUG.) The heavens, the apostles, concerning the glory of Christ in which 870Dhe is equal to the Father. (CASS.) Or the heavens, they who sent the star. The glory. (Ibid.): That God freely forgives sins. The works. (AUG.) Those which are according to man, etc., as far as and these same are made night to him, giving to the darkened the knowledge which is of things human. (CASS.) And this so wonderfully, that it is in all tongues; and so widely, that it is in every part of the compass of the earth.

VERS. 3.-- Day unto day. (CASS.) He treats of it by demonstration. (AUG.) Day unto day. The Spirit brings forth to spiritual men the fullness of wisdom, etc., as far as this teaching is continued by days and by nights down to those who come after.

VERS. 4.-- Speeches. (CASS.) Public persuadings. Words. Common narrations. Whose voices are not heard. He would say more plainly, in whom their voices are not heard, 871Aor, the voices of all their words are heard: he does the same thing by means of the relative.

(AUG.) The Spirit made the first men speak with all tongues, he who was to gather all nations into one; then one man was for all, so now one Christ, head and body.

VERS. 6.-- In the sun (CASS.) What he praises others for having done, he himself does: he preaches the incarnation. Or in the sun, in the open sight of the world, or in labour. The sun burns, and shines, and varies the seasons. His tabernacle. (AUG.) As it were a soldier's dwelling, that is, the dispensation of his incarnation, in which he came to storm the errors of the world. Or the tabernacle, the Church in the open, not in secret, so as to lie hid. A bridegroom. (CASS.) So often promised by the prophets, a great likeness of the sacrament: therefore born of 871Ba virgin, that he might join to himself the Church a virgin. Out of his bride-chamber. (AUG.) That is, the virginal womb, where God was joined to human nature as a bridegroom to a bride. Behold, humble in mercy, but strong in majesty. As a giant to run. (CASS.) Unshaken, not to be called back, overcoming human nature by his power. From the highest. Here the Trinity is shewn, etc., as far as it marks the unity of the Trinity. Neither is there any that can hide himself, etc. (AUG.) The Word made flesh permitted no man to excuse himself out of the shadow of death: because the heat of the Word pierced even that. Or, the heat is the Spirit, whom he sent when he had returned, who is law, testimony, justice, commandment, fear and judgments, because he does these things.

VERS. 8.-- The law of the Lord. (CAS.) Secondly, he praises the precepts of the New and the Old Testament. (Ibid.) The law given through 871CMoses, correcting all things by the distinction of its words, and sending them on to the grace of Christ. Converting. (AUG.) By liberty, unto the imitating of himself, not pressing down with the yoke of servitude. Souls. Wills, not merely hands, as the Old Testament did. The testimony. Whatsoever Quaecunquae testimonies he gave to Israel are full of truth, and have given wisdom to the humble. Wisdom: concerning things divine.

VERS. 9.-- The justices of the Lord. (Ibid.) All are right in him, who taught not what he did not do, so that they who imitate them might rejoice in them, seeing they would do them freely with charity, not slavishly with fear. (CASS.) Justices, the law which justifies; whatsoever it commands is just.

VERS. 10.-- The fear of the Lord. (Ibid.) The fear of the world is not holy, because it is not profitable, and it changes with the times. The fear of the Lord is without any perturbation, 871Dbecause it is a love mingled with dread, because if it fears the judge, it knows him merciful. (AUG.) Fear, not that penal fear for earthly things, for love of which the soul is afraid, but the chaste fear whereby, the more it loves, the more it is wary of offending the bridegroom, and therefore it is not cast out, but abides. Judgments. The judgments of God need not another's authority.

VERS. 11.-- Desirable things. (Ibid.) Or, much to be desired, or much gold and stone; or much that is precious. Desirable above gold, etc., as far as, whose will he sets before his own, and they are sweeter than he himself is to himself. Above gold, that is, everything that is sought after, whether for riches, or for power, or for pleasure. Honey. The food of God is honey; that is, one now loosed from the world; and the honeycomb, that is, because he is still wrapped about, for whom there is need 872Aof the pressure of God's hand squeezing him out, that he may go into life.

VERS. 13.-- Who understandeth sins. (Ibid.) Thirdly he asks to be purged of vices, that he may be a worthy psalmist, to report these sacraments. To a mind that sees, truth is sweet, and judgments sweet; to one that does not see, what sweetness is there? But why is it not seen? Because of sins: nor is it any wonder: For who understandeth sins? (CASS.) Sins: all of them, for certain of them are known. Mine defile, others' afflict, and now spare, drive back the persuader. From my secret ones. He includes all sins under two heads, etc., as far as whereby man was seduced; and by consenting he made it his own. (AUG.) There is no greater sin than to apostatize from God, which is the beginning of pride: but pride is the beginning and the cause of all sin.

PSALMUS XIX.

  • 872B

In finem. (CASS.) Figura operandi, quae ventura sunt Propheta canit.

(Ibid.) Propheta ex nimia charitate optat prospere evenire Ecclesiae, quae per Christum videbat ventura.

VERS. 2.-- Exaudiat: quae tempore tribulationis vult ei fieri. In die tribulationis, quo majori desiderio Deum precamur. Dei Jacob, ut sicut illi, ita tibi gratiam benedictionis det, et praeponat Judaeis.

VERS. 3.-- Mittat: pater. Auxilium, misso Filio.

VERS. 4.-- Memor. Agit quasi de sacerdote immolaturo et rege pugnaturo. Sacrificii. (Ibid.) Sacrificium 872CEcclesiae praevidebat, non pecudum, sed sanguinis et corporis Christi.

VERS. 5.-- Tribuat. Diapsalma, quae tempore gloriae optat et affirmat. Omne. (AUG.) Non solum quo animam posuisti pro vita plurimorum; sed et quo caecitas ex parte contigit in Israel, et sic omnis Israel salvus fieret.

VERS. 6.-- Laetabimur. (Ibid.) Ideo haec oratio, quia laetabimur et magnificabimur, ostendit se unum de Ecclesia tanto ante tempore.

VERS. 7.-- In potentatibus. (AUG.) Potentatus nostri sunt salus favoris ejus cum et de tribulatione dat auxilium, quia vana salus hominum, quae est sinistrae, unde et superbia nascitur. Salus dexterae. 872D(Ibid.), id est gratia spiritualis, etc., usque ad qui terrena dignitate praesumunt.

PSALM XIX.

  • 872B

Unto the end. (CASS.) A figure of the working; the Prophet sings the things that are to come.

(Ibid.) The Prophet out of exceeding charity wishes a prosperous issue for the Church, which he saw would come to pass through Christ.

VERS. 2.-- May he hear thee: the things which he wills to be done for her in the time of tribulation. In the day of tribulation, wherein we pray to God with the greater desire. Of the God of Jacob, that as to him, so to thee he may give the grace of blessing, and set thee before the Jews.

VERS. 3.-- May he send: the Father. Help, by sending the Son.

VERS. 4.-- Mindful. He treats as it were of a priest about to offer sacrifice and of a king about to fight. Of thy sacrifice. (Ibid.) He foresaw the sacrifice 872Cof the Church, not of cattle, but of the blood and the body of Christ.

VERS. 5.-- May he give. Diapsalma, the things which he wishes and affirms for the time of glory. All thy counsel. (AUG.) Not only in that thou hast laid down thy soul for the life of very many; but also in that blindness in part hath happened in Israel, and so all Israel should be saved.

VERS. 6.-- We shall rejoice. (Ibid.) Therefore this prayer, because we shall rejoice and shall be magnified; he shews himself to be one of the Church so long a time before.

VERS. 7.-- In powers. (AUG.) Our powers are the salvation of his favour, since he gives help even out of tribulation, because vain is the salvation of men, which is of the left hand, whence also pride is born. The salvation of his right hand. 872D(Ibid.), that is, spiritual grace, etc., as far as they who presume upon earthly dignity.

PSALMUS XX.

VERS. 1.-- In finem. Tertius psalmus de duabus naturis in Christo, coelestem regem describit, ut auditu credat mundus, quem visum contemnit Judaeus. Demonstrativam facit orationem in laudem Dei.

VERS. 2.-- Domine in virtute tua laetabitur. (CASS.) Summam proponit, scilicet, meritum et praemium.

VERS. 4.-- Quoniam praevenisti. (CASS.) Diapsalma; virtutes ejus et gloriam describit, etc., usque ad quasi capiti in coronam. Coronam. (Ibid.) Quia circumitus 873AApostolorum docentem ambiebat, vel totus mundi circulus, id est, Ecclesia generalis.

VERS. 6.-- In salutari tuo: gloriam et magnum decorem, etc. (CASS.) Verbo Patris, quae inde gloria. Gloriam de judicio, quia in Deitate judicabit. Decorem in majestate, quae tunc apparebit. Gloriam et magnum decorem, etc. Gloriosus, ut Petrus, cujus umbra infirmi sanabantur; et decor est super eum, praeter quem non est aliud fundamentum. Ideo super eum, quoniam dabis . . . . .

VERS. 7.-- In gaudio cum vultu tuo. Quoniam rex sperat in Domino, et in misericordia, etc. (ID.). Id est, de hoc quod sui gaudebunt cum tua praesentia, quando eris omnia in omnibus.

VERS. 9.-- Inveniatur manus tua, etc. (ID.) De 873Bpoenis inimicorum, ut supra de laudibus Christi.

VERS. 11.-- Fructum eorum de terra perdes, et semen eorum. Non erit eis fructus beatitudinis in terra viventium.

VERS. 13.-- Quoniam pones. (CASS.) Dicta de futura, etc., usque ad ut cum putarent occidere, salus fieret.

VERS. 14.-- Exaltare. (ID.) Conclusio.

PSALM XX.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end. The third psalm, of the two natures in Christ; it describes the heavenly king, that the world might believe by hearing him whom the Jew, having seen him, despises. He makes a demonstrative oration in praise of God.

VERS. 2.-- Lord, in thy strength shall he rejoice. (CASS.) He sets forth the sum, namely, the merit and the reward.

VERS. 4.-- For thou hast prevented him. (CASS.) Diapsalma; he describes his virtues and his glory, etc., as far as as it were for a crown to the head. A crown. (Ibid.) Because the circuit 873Aof the Apostles hemmed him about as he taught, or the whole circle of the world, that is, the general Church.

VERS. 6.-- In thy salvation: glory and great beauty, etc. (CASS.) By the Word of the Father, whence comes that glory. Glory as to the judgment, because he shall judge in his Godhead. Beauty in majesty, which shall then appear. Glory and great beauty, etc. Glorious, as Peter, by whose shadow the sick were healed; and beauty is upon him, beside whom there is no other foundation. Therefore upon him, because thou shalt give . . . . .

VERS. 7.-- In joy with thy countenance. For the king hopeth in the Lord, and in the mercy, etc. (ID.). That is, of this, that his own shall rejoice with thy presence, when thou shalt be all in all.

VERS. 9.-- Let thy hand be found, etc. (ID.) Of 873Bthe punishments of his enemies, as above of the praises of Christ.

VERS. 11.-- Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth, and their seed. There shall not be for them the fruit of blessedness in the land of the living.

VERS. 13.-- For thou shalt make. (CASS.) Things said of what is to come, etc., as far as that when they thought to kill, salvation might come to be.

VERS. 14.-- Be thou exalted. (ID.) The conclusion.

PSALMUS XXI.

VERS. 2.-- Deus, Deus. (CASS.) Praemittitur conquestio de derelictione, necnon et oratio, sicut in omnibus psalmis de passione. (AUG., CASS.) Deus, Deus: geminat ex affectu, vel Deus omnium per 873Ccreationis potentiam, meus proprie per cultum. (AUG.) Quando hoc in cruce dixerat, psalmum istum de se scriptum indicavit. Respice in me. (CASS.) Non est in Hebraeo, sed a septuaginta interpretibus additum. Quare me dereliquisti? (AUG.) Mirum hoc, cum et Deus esset cum eo; sed pro nobis, qui in eo corpus ejus. Longe a salute mea, id est, mei veteris hominis, quia longe a peccatoribus salus, et haec sunt verba non justitiae, sed delictorum. Vel, longe a salute sunt verba delictorum meorum, quae sunt tollenda.

VERS. 3.-- Clamabo. (AUG.) De nobis, corpore suo dicit, ut cum forte dicit: Transeat a me calix iste, id est, putatur timuisse mori; sed pro suis infirmis qui timent mori, haec dixit, sic et haec vox 873Dmembrorum est: Clamabo et non exaudies. Per diem, et non exaudies, et nocte et non ad insipientiam. (CASS.) Quia nullae in eo tenebrae, et tamen non auditur ad salutem corporalem.

VERS. 4.-- In sancto habitas. (AUG.) Et ita mirum, quia patres liberasti; ego autem sum vermis.

(CASS.) Tu habitas in sancto, quia Deus erat in Christo mundum sibi reconcilians. Laus Israel, (AUG.) id est, videntis te, non ejus qui se voluit abscondere a conspectu tuo.

VERS. 5.-- In te speraverunt patres nostri, speraverunt. (CASS.) Magnus decor, dum iterat speraverunt.

874AVERS. 7.-- Ego autem, etc. (AUG.) Hucusque Christus in persona veteris hominis, hic jam proprie in sua persona loquitur. Ego autem. Jam proprie Christus, sine semine natus sum, ut essem ultra homines in homine, in quo factus sum opprobrium, ut vel sic superbia hominis humilem imitetur. Vermis et non homo, opprobrium. (CASS.) Ita viliter conculcatus, etc., usque ad vermis, sine coitu natus, mortalis, humilis et vilis, silentio repens.

VERS. 9.-- Speravit in Domino, etc. (CASS.) Dicentes: Spera in Domino, etc. Ironia Judaeorum, ecce quasi historialis narratio, non prophetia, ne qua sit excusatio, ne qua ambiguitas.

VERS. 10.-- Ab uberibus. Non ex quo lactari 874Bcoepi, etc., usque ad sed fuisti Deus meus. De ventre.

VERS. 11.-- De ventre. (AUG.) Non solum matris, quae lex nascendi est omnibus; sed de tenebris Synagogae, in quibus infidelis est, nondum in luce Christi natus, qui in observationibus illis carnalibus sabbati et circumcisionis confidit.

VERS. 12.-- Ne discesseris a me, qui jam coepisti.

Tu extraxisti: non vir, ne dubitetur virginis partus, virtute Dei factum est. Spes mea ab uberibus: vera humanitas et magna perfectio; ab uberibus enim facit, quod vix maturus.

In te projectus sum, non in peccata hominis. Alii in Adam projiciuntur, ex quo rei. De ventre matris 874Cmeae, Deus meus. (CASS.) Nec conceptio sine Deo, nec in peccato, ut homo; unde Angelus: Spiritus sanctus superveniet in te.

VERS. 13.-- Circumdederunt. (ID.) Describitur passio, quam terminat oratio; ad convincendos Judaeos refert futura quasi praeterita.

VERS. 14.-- Aperuerunt. (ID.) Ut ferae volentes deglutire, os suum, non ad sapientiam reseratum. Sicut leo. (AUG.) Ut leo rapiens circumdederunt, ut rugiens os aperuerunt.

VERS. 15.-- Sicut aqua. Quando funditur aqua, etc., usque ad unde relicto eo fugerunt. (CASS.) Sicut aquae sacramentum ablutio peccatorum, etc., usque ad et solidata est. Tanquam cera. Bene legis mysteria 874Dcomparat cerae, etc., usque ad quoniam circumdederunt. In medio ventris mei. (AUG.) Venter infirmos in Ecclesia, vel memoriam Ecclesiae significat.

VERS. 16.-- Aruit tanquam testa virtus mea. (CASS.) Non ut fenum, sed ut testa quae igne fit firmior. Lingua mea. (AUG.) Servaverunt praecepta mea apud se hi per quos locuturus eram: et per eos in cognationem eorum, qui erant pulvis mortis, deductus sum.

VERS. 17.-- Foderunt. (ID.) Evangelica narratio. Etsi haec ad litteram, innuit fossio manuum, quod operibus ejus non crediderunt; pedum, quod Apostolos laceraverunt. (CASS.): foderunt. 875ATerra fossa fructum facit, sic fructum vitae dedit Christus vulneratus.

VERS. 18.-- Dinumeraverunt omnia ossa mea. (CASS.) Proprie describitur poena crucis. Sic ossa dinumeraverunt, id est, Apostolos; ne in majorem numerum crescerent, quaerebant exstinguere. Inspexerunt me. (ID.) Cum diligentia et delectatione, cum a re crudeli soleant oculi averti. Ecce quam obstinati, non casu aliquid factum, nec tot miraculis cor mollitum.

VERS. 19.-- Diviserunt sibi vestimenta mea, etc. (AUG.) Sacramenta ipsius potuerunt dividi per haereses, sed non tunica desuper, id est, a Deo data; haec est charitas vel unitas, quam nemo potest dividere. (CASS.) Sed forte et dono Dei quibusdam 875Bvenit, etc., usque ad ut ramus olivae a columba delatus ad arcam. (AUG.) Vel, per animam unicam caput et corpus, quod unum diversitates respuit.

VERS. 22.-- Unicornium, humilitatem meam, etc. (ID.) Judaei, terrena tantum petentes: vel, de cultu Dei singulariter se jactantes, vel singulariter superbientes, occiso etiam filio post servos.

VERS. 24.-- Qui timetis Dominum, laudate eum, etc. (CASS.) Timor humanus non laudem, sed vituperium parit.

VERS. 25.-- Timeat eum omne semen Israel, quoniam non sprevit, etc. Quos dixerit semen Jacob, aperit, subdens: Pauperis. (AUG.) Non ejus qui verbis delictorum clamat de vana vita, sed 875Cnon tumentis de pompis saeculi.

VERS. 26.-- Apud te laus mea in Ecclesia magna, etc. (ID.) Apud Deum laudem ponit, qui docet in homine non praesumi.

VERS. 27.-- Laudabunt Dominum qui requirunt eum: vivent. (ID.) Pauperes Deum divites se: ideo pauperes, quia Deum laudant ut eum quaerant, et ipse est divitiae pauperum. Corda eorum in saeculum saeculi reminiscentur et convertentur ad Dominum. (ID.) Quia ille cibus est cordis.

VERS. 30.-- Manducaverunt et adoraverunt. (ID.) Non prohibeat dispensator manducare, sed exactorem moneat timere. In conspectu ejus cadent. (CASS.) Ecclesia utrosque recipit, sed ipse videt et discernit.

875DVERS. 32.-- Annuntiabitur, etc. (ID.) An angelis qui preces hominum Deo offerunt, non pro instructione, sed pro ministerio.

(CASS.) Nota psalmos de passione in magna spe Christianorum terminari, ut sciatur ex passione salus esse.

PSALM XXI.

VERS. 2.-- God, my God. (CASS.) A complaint of being forsaken is set before, and prayer also, as in all the psalms of the passion. (AUG., CASS.) God, my God: he doubles it out of affection, or God of all through 873Cthe power of creation, mine properly through worship. (AUG.) When he had said this on the cross, he shewed that this psalm was written of himself. Look upon me. (CASS.) It is not in the Hebrew, but was added by the seventy interpreters. Why hast thou forsaken me? (AUG.) This is a wonder, since God also was with him; but it was for us, who in him are his body. Far from my salvation, that is, from that of my old man, because salvation is far from sinners, and these are the words not of justice, but of sins. Or, far from salvation are the words of my sins, which are to be taken away.

VERS. 3.-- I shall cry. (AUG.) He speaks of us, of his own body, as when perchance he says: Let this chalice pass from me, that is, he is thought to have feared to die; but he said these things for his own weak ones who fear to die, and so this also is the voice 873Dof the members: I shall cry and thou wilt not hear. By day, and thou wilt not hear, and by night, and not unto folly. [Vulg. Ps 21:3 cries "by day" once only, without the doubled "and thou wilt not hear," and closes with mihi] (CASS.) Because there are no shadows in him, and yet he is not heard unto bodily salvation.

VERS. 4.-- Thou dwellest in the holy place. (AUG.) And so it is a wonder, because thou hast delivered the fathers; but I am a worm.

(CASS.) Thou dwellest in the holy place, because God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself. The praise of Israel, (AUG.) that is, of him that sees thee, not of him who wished to hide himself from thy sight.

VERS. 5.-- In thee have our fathers hoped: they have hoped. (CASS.) It is a great beauty, while he repeats they have hoped.

874AVERS. 7.-- But I am, etc. (AUG.) Thus far Christ in the person of the old man; here now he speaks properly in his own person. But I am. Now properly Christ: I was born without seed, that I might be beyond men in man, in whom I was made a reproach, that at least so the pride of man might imitate the humble. A worm and no man, a reproach. (CASS.) So vilely trodden down, etc., as far as a worm, born without coupling, mortal, humble and vile, creeping in silence.

VERS. 9.-- He hoped in the Lord, etc. (CASS.) Saying: Hope thou in the Lord, etc. The irony of the Jews; behold, as it were a historical narration, not a prophecy, lest there be any excuse, lest there be any ambiguity.

VERS. 10.-- From the breasts. Not from the time when I began to be suckled, etc., as far as but thou hast been my God. From the womb.

VERS. 11.-- From the womb. (AUG.) Not only of a mother, which is the law of being born for all; but from the darkness of the Synagogue, in which he is unbelieving, 874Bnot yet born into the light of Christ, who trusts in those carnal observances of the sabbath and of circumcision.

VERS. 12.-- Depart not from me, thou who hast already begun.

Thou hast drawn me out: not a man; lest the virgin's childbearing be doubted, it was done by the power of God. My hope from the breasts: true humanity and great perfection; for from the breasts he does what one scarcely come of age can do.

In thee was I cast, not into the sins of man. Others are cast into Adam, whence they are guilty. From my mother's womb, 874Cmy God. (CASS.) Neither was the conception without God, nor in sin, as man's is; whence the Angel: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee.

VERS. 13.-- They have surrounded. (ID.) The passion is described, which prayer concludes; to convince the Jews he relates things to come as though they were past.

VERS. 14.-- They have opened. (ID.) As wild beasts wishing to swallow him down, their mouth, not unlocked unto wisdom. As a lion. (AUG.) As a lion seizing they surrounded him, as one roaring they opened their mouth.

VERS. 15.-- As water. When water is poured out, etc., as far as whence, leaving him, they fled. (CASS.) As water is the sacrament of the washing away of sins, etc., as far as and it was made solid. Like wax. Well does he compare the mysteries of the law 874Dto wax, etc., as far as for they have surrounded. In the midst of my belly. (AUG.) The belly signifies the weak in the Church, or the memory of the Church.

VERS. 16.-- My strength is dried up like a potsherd. (CASS.) Not as hay, but as a potsherd, which by fire is made the firmer. My tongue. (AUG.) They kept my precepts with them, through whom I was to speak: and through them I was brought down into the kindred of those who were the dust of death.

VERS. 17.-- They have dug. (ID.) The gospel narration. Although these things are so to the letter, the digging of the hands hints that they did not believe his works; of the feet, that they mangled the Apostles. (CASS.): they have dug. 875ADug earth bears fruit, so Christ wounded gave the fruit of life.

VERS. 18.-- They have numbered all my bones. (CASS.) The punishment of the cross is properly described. Thus they numbered the bones, that is, the Apostles; lest they should grow into a greater number, they sought to extinguish them. They have looked upon me. (ID.) With diligence and with delight, whereas the eyes are wont to be turned away from a cruel thing. Behold how obstinate they are: nothing was done by chance, nor was their heart softened by so many miracles.

VERS. 19.-- They parted my garments among them, etc. (AUG.) His own sacraments could be divided by heresies, but not the coat from above, that is, given by God; this is charity, or unity, which no man can divide. (CASS.) But perhaps it came to certain men even by the gift of God, 875Betc., as far as as the olive branch brought by the dove to the ark. (AUG.) Or, through the one soul the head and the body, which being one rejects diversities.

VERS. 22.-- From the unicorns, my lowness, etc. (ID.) The Jews, seeking earthly things only: or, boasting themselves singularly of the worship of God, or being singularly proud, the son also having been slain after the servants.

VERS. 24.-- Ye that fear the Lord, praise him, etc. (CASS.) Human fear brings forth not praise, but blame.

VERS. 25.-- Let all the seed of Israel fear him, because he hath not despised, etc. Whom he means by the seed of Jacob he opens, adding: Of the poor man. (AUG.) Not of him who cries out with the words of sins out of a vain life, but 875Cof him who is not swollen with the pomps of the world.

VERS. 26.-- With thee is my praise in a great church, etc. (ID.) He places his praise with God, who teaches that there be no presuming in man.

VERS. 27.-- They shall praise the Lord that seek him: they shall live. (ID.) The poor are rich in God: therefore poor, because they praise God that they may seek him, and he himself is the riches of the poor. Their hearts shall remember for ever and ever, and shall be converted to the Lord. (ID.) Because he is the food of the heart.

VERS. 30.-- They have eaten and have adored. (ID.) Let not the dispenser forbid to eat, but let him warn the exactor to fear. In his sight shall they fall. (CASS.) The Church receives both, but he himself sees and discerns.

875DVERS. 32.-- It shall be shewn, etc. (ID.) Or to the angels, who offer the prayers of men to God, not for instruction, but for ministry.

(CASS.) Note that the psalms of the passion end in the great hope of Christians, that it may be known that salvation is from the passion.

PSALMUS XXII.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus David. (CASS.) Propheta reditum populi de Babylone praedixit. Dominus regit me. Psalmus de misericordia, enumerans decem gratias, ut omnes sperent in misericordia Dei. (AUG.) Ecclesia loquitur de Christo.

VERS. 2.-- In loco pascuae. (CASS.) Prima gratia, locus pascuae, id est, sermo divinus, qui saginat meditantes. 876ASuper aquam. Secunda gratia, aqua refectionis.

VERS. 3.-- Animam meam. (ID.) Tertia gratia, etc., usque ad sed prius educavit super aquam refectionis, sed prius animam meam convertit. Deduxit. (ID.) Quarta, quod super charitatis praecepta duxit. Super semitas. (AUG.) Arctiora mandata et perfectiora consilia, quasi semitis pauci justi ambulant, sicut semitae arctiores sunt quam viae.

VERS. 4.-- Nam et si. (CASS.) Quinta, quod in umbra mortis non timet mala. Mecum es. (AUG.) In corde per fidem, ut post umbram mortis ego tecum sim. Virga tua. (CASS.) Sexta, correctio; vel virga districtio, quae convertit vitia. Baculus gubernatio, quae sustinet fideles.

876BVERS. 5.-- Parasti in conspectu. (CASS.) Septima, mensa Domini, beata convivatio, saturitas fidei, esca coelestis, de qua Apostolus: Qui manducat et bibit indigne, judicium sibi manducat et bibit. In conspectu meo mensam: etsi non impiorum. De hac dicitur: Seb isti ad mensam divitis, id est, Christi, scito et te similia debere praeparare, id est, pati sicut ipse. Impinguisti: octava, unctio capitis, scilicet Christi, quod nulla ariditate peccati exaruit, unde caetera laetantur membra, quia capite descendit unguentum in barbam barbam Aaron, et in oram vestimenti ejus. Et calix meus. Nona, calix, Christi sanguis, qui sic inebriat ut sobrios reddat. Meus, quia accipio. Vel, tuus, quia das. Mensa et calix, caro, sanguis, quanquam unum sint sacramentum, sub diversis 876Ctamen speciebus, quia utrumque sumitur, divisim hic ponuntur.

VERS. 6.-- Et misericordia. (CASS.) Decima, misericordia subsequens ad custodiam quae praecedit ad gratiam conferendam.

VERS. 7.-- Et ut inhabitem. (HIER.) Hoc omnibus superioribus jungitur. Quasi collocasti, educasti, deduxisti, etc., et hoc ideo ut inhabitem.

PSALM XXII.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of David. (CASS.) The Prophet foretold the return of the people from Babylon. The Lord ruleth me. A psalm of mercy, enumerating ten graces, that all may hope in the mercy of God. (AUG.) The Church speaks of Christ.

VERS. 2.-- In a place of pasture. (CASS.) The first grace, a place of pasture, that is, the divine word, which fattens those who meditate upon it. 876AUpon the water. The second grace, the water of refreshment.

VERS. 3.-- My soul. (ID.) The third grace, etc., as far as but first he brought me up upon the water of refreshment, first he converted my soul. He hath led. (ID.) The fourth, in that he led me upon the precepts of charity. Upon the paths. (AUG.) The narrower commandments and the more perfect counsels; as it were upon paths few just men walk, even as paths are narrower than roads.

VERS. 4.-- For though I shall walk. (CASS.) The fifth, that in the shadow of death he fears no evils. Thou art with me. (AUG.) In the heart by faith, that after the shadow of death I may be with thee. Thy rod. (CASS.) The sixth, correction; or the rod is strictness, which converts vices. The staff is governance, which upholds the faithful.

876BVERS. 5.-- Thou hast prepared in my sight. (CASS.) The seventh, the table of the Lord, the blessed banqueting, the fullness of faith, the heavenly food, of which the Apostle: He that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh judgment to himself. In my sight a table: even if not that of the wicked. Of this it is said: But these at the table of the rich man, that is, of Christ, know that thou too must prepare the like, that is, to suffer as he did. Thou hast anointed: the eighth, the anointing of the head, namely of Christ, which was dried up by no barrenness of sin, whence the rest of the members rejoice, because from the head the ointment ran down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron, and unto the skirt of his garment. And my chalice. The ninth, the chalice, the blood of Christ, which so inebriates that it makes men sober. Mine, because I receive it. Or, thine, because thou givest it. The table and the chalice, flesh and blood, although they are one sacrament, yet under diverse 876Cspecies, because both are taken, are here set down separately.

VERS. 6.-- And mercy. (CASS.) The tenth, mercy following after unto keeping, which goes before unto the conferring of grace.

VERS. 7.-- And that I may dwell. (HIER.) This is joined to all the things above. As though: thou hast placed, thou hast brought up, thou hast led, etc., and this to the end that I may dwell.

PSALMUS XXIII.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus David. (AUG.) In prima sabbati mundus conditus, in eadem homo restauratus per resurrectionem Christi: (CASS.) unde monet victorem cum triumpho suscipere. Domini est terra. Primo dicit totum orbem esse Dei, etc., usque ad 876Dsed quis in monte ejus, nisi innocens?

VERS. 2.-- Et super flumina. (AUG.) Ut flumina in mare, ita cupidi labuntur in saeculum; et eos etiam superat Ecclesia, quae victis cupiditatibus ad immortalitatem paratur.

VERS. 3.-- Quis ascendet? Determinat quibus virtutibus praediti sunt in Ecclesia.

VERS. 4.-- Quis stabit? (HIER.) Multi enim ascendunt, qui non permanent. (ID.) Innocens: ad proximum, manu et corde, et qui sibi innocens, etc., usque ad praesentiam et cognitionem desiderent. Qui non accepit. (AUG., HIER.) Id est, qui non deputavit animam rebus non permanentibus, sed eam sentiens immortalem aeterna desiderabit, et ideo 877Anon juravit in dolo. In vano. (HIER.) Id est, qui nullis eam fecibus peccaminum post baptismum maculavit.

VERS. 7.-- Attollite. Diapsalmus. Christiana religione declarata, etc., usque ad quae a principe diabolo positae sunt. Et elevumini. Contra portas mortis. Portae aeternales: omnis gratia quae, veniente Christo, data est.

VERS. 8.-- Quis est? interrogat. Propheta ad convincendam Judaeorum perfidiam, et ut amplius eum commendando alios invitet.

VERS. 10.-- Dominus fortis per virtutes describitur quasi proprio nomine. Fortis, (AUG.) etsi cum gladiis cepistis.

Potens, etsi Pilato tradidistis.

877BPotens in praelio, ne in pugna vos superasse putetis. Virtutes. (Hier., AUG.) Ministrae praecedentes Christum in ascensione ad alias coelestes clamant, ut viam Domino venienti aperiant: quae novo mysterio carne induti stupefactae, quaerunt, quis est?

Attollite. (CASS.) Congeminatio, etc., usque ad qui omnibus omnia dat bona, vel coelestium virtutum, id est, angelorum.

PSALM XXIII.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of David. (AUG.) On the first day of the week the world was founded, on the same day man was restored through the resurrection of Christ: (CASS.) whence he admonishes us to receive the conqueror with triumph. The earth is the Lord's. First he says that the whole world is God's, etc., as far as 876Dbut who shall be in his mountain, save the innocent?

VERS. 2.-- And upon the rivers. (AUG.) As rivers glide into the sea, so the covetous glide into the world; and these too the Church overcomes, which, its covetous desires being conquered, is made ready for immortality.

VERS. 3.-- Who shall ascend? He determines with what virtues they are endowed in the Church.

VERS. 4.-- Who shall stand? (HIER.) For many ascend who do not abide. (ID.) The innocent: toward his neighbour, in hand and in heart, and he who is innocent toward himself, etc., as far as they should desire his presence and his knowledge. Who hath not taken. (AUG., HIER.) That is, who has not reckoned his soul among things that do not abide, but perceiving it immortal shall desire things eternal, and therefore 877Ahas not sworn deceitfully. In vain. (HIER.) That is, who has stained it with no dregs of sins after baptism.

VERS. 7.-- Lift up. Diapsalmus. Christian religion having been declared, etc., as far as which were set there by the prince the devil. And be ye lifted up. Against the gates of death. Ye everlasting gates: all the grace which, at Christ's coming, was given.

VERS. 8.-- Who is? he asks. The Prophet, to convict the perfidy of the Jews, and that by commending him the more he may invite others.

VERS. 10.-- The Lord strong is described by his powers as though by his proper name. Strong, (AUG.) even if ye took him with swords.

Mighty, even if ye delivered him to Pilate.

877BMighty in battle, lest ye think ye have overcome him in the fight. The powers. (Hier., AUG.) The ministering powers going before Christ in the ascension cry out to the other heavenly ones, that they may open the way to the Lord as he comes: and these, astonished at the new mystery of one clothed in flesh, ask, who is he?

Lift up. (CASS.) A doubling, etc., as far as who gives all good things to all, or of the heavenly powers, that is, of the angels.

PSALMUS XXIV.

VERS. 1.-- In finem. (Hier.) Hic flagellatus poenitens praeponitur aliis, ne murmurent in adversis: qui in se expertus per misericordiam blanditur, per justitiam terret.

877CAd te, Domine, levavi. (AUG.) Psalmus contra adversa saeculi, etc., usque ad qui non per omnes, minus perfectos.

(CASS.) Primo petit doceri vias Domini, quia ad Deum erectus.

(ID.) Ad te contemplandum; facile terrena despicit, qui divina conspicit.

VERS. 2.-- Confido. (ID.) Expertus in malis meam infirmitatem, non erubescam de inimicis.

Neque irrideant me inimici: et certus sum quia in nullo sustinente patienter fallit.

Supervacue. (ID.) Quia omnia sunt vana et infructuosa quae a Deo sunt aliena.

Vias tuas, Domine, demonstra. (CASS.) Viae sunt de ordine vitae, etc., usque ad: Dirige, ad vitam pertinet, 877Ddoce ad scientiam.

VERS. 5.-- Doce. (AUG.) Ipsam veritatem, ut quod credo intelligam, quia sustinui, et si hoc non sufficit: Reminiscere.

Deus salvator meus. (CASS.) Duae res sunt, quae bonos faciunt, ut Deum salvatorem credamus, et patienter ejus retributionem exspectemus.

VERS. 6.-- Reminiscere. (ID.) De peccatis prioribus et quae quotidie fiunt, orat per misericordiam antiquis factam, et quia timet verum judicem.

Miserationum. Miseratio proprie in bonorum exhibitione.

Quae a saeculo. (AUG.) Id est, ab initio saeculi sunt: non ergo in me fallat.

878AVERS. 7.-- Delicta. (CASS.) Sunt quando linquitur via aequitatis.

Juventutis. Non pro aetate, sed pro praecipitationis audacia, quae est tunc, cum calor animi modestiam excedit.

Ignorantias. Facimus ea quae mala esse non scimus. Vel delicta ignorantiae in parvulis, qui vel originali peccato tenentur.

(HIER.) Juventutis. Antequam de domo patris iniqui exirem.

Memento mei, tu. (AUG.) Cujus opus est misereri et peccata dimittere.

Secundum misericordiam. Id est, ampla est misericordia tua. Misericordia erga miseros, bonitas erga quoslibet. Facit autem Deus bonum et a miseris 878Bimploratus, et bonitate ductus: nemo bonus nisi Deus.

VERS. 8.-- Dulcis. (ID.) Quia omnia priora dimittit, ubi gratia sine meritis.

Rectus. Quia post misericordiam, etc., usque ad Dulcis, quia suavia dat; rectus, quia corrigit.

Propter hoc. (CASS.) Quia dulcis et rectus; non ex crudelitate, sed benignitate.

In via. Id est, fide, vel praeceptis Dei. Vel in via hujus vitae, ubi recte vivendum, dabit legem.

VERS. 9.-- In judicio. Dum punit, diriget ad meliora. Sed mansueti sint, qui corripiuntur: quod ex feris domiti, ut tolerent. Quia si mites, id est, lenis animi quasi naturaliter hoc habentes: docebit eos praecepta, pro quorum neglectu venerunt 878Cflagella.

VERS. 10.-- Misericordia et veritas. (AUG.) Quas autem vias docebit, etc., usque ad et deinde cavet severitatem judicis.

Testamentum. (CASS.) Novum, quod egregie dicitur Testamentum, ubi clara et certa promissio haereditatis quod et morte firmatur.

Et Testamentum. Legis veteris, ubi fuerunt Prophetae testes promissionum.

VERS. 11.-- Propter nomen tuum, Domine. (AUG.) Id est, gloriam tuam, etc., usque ad et interpretantur mundi, qui se ab omni peccato mundos asserunt.

VERS. 12.-- Quis est homo? (CASS.) Hic agit de aeternis; quomodo habentur, laborans et orans, ut et 878Dipse, et totus Israel ab his malis liberetur.

VERS. 13.-- Anima. (ID.) et si non statim, etc., usque ad quidquid alii faciant, etc.

Semen. (Hier.) Bonum est, unde fructus colligitur.

Firmamentum est. (AUG.) Videtur infirmorum esse timor, sed Dominus est firmamentum timentibus eum, et facit ut Testamentum ejus manifestetur illis.

Oculi. Sal. Oculi sapientis in capite, id est, in corde ejus.

VERS. 16.-- Unicus. (ID.) Unicus plus amatur, pauper plus doletur.

VERS. 17.-- De necessitatibus. Id est, ab adversis, 879Aquae necessaria sunt omnibus, qui pie in Christo vivere volunt.

VERS. 19.-- Respice. (AUG.) Tot hominum perditio sine dolore, esse non potest, et ideo pro eis orat.

VERS. 21.-- Innocentes et recti adhaeserunt. (ID.) Mali tolerati sunt; non adhaeserunt.

VERS. 22.-- Israel. (AUG.) Populum, quem ad tuam visionem praeparasti.

PSALM XXIV.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end. (Hier.) Here the penitent who has been scourged is set before the rest, lest they murmur in adversities: he who, having had the trial in himself, coaxes through mercy and terrifies through justice.

877CTo thee, O Lord, have I lifted up. (AUG.) A psalm against the adversities of the world, etc., as far as who not through all, the less perfect.

(CASS.) First he asks to be taught the ways of the Lord, because he is raised up toward God.

(ID.) Toward the contemplating of thee; he easily despises earthly things who beholds things divine.

VERS. 2.-- I trust. (ID.) Having had trial of my own weakness in evils, I shall not blush because of my enemies.

Neither let my enemies laugh at me: and I am sure that he deceives none that endures patiently.

In vain. (ID.) Because all things are vain and unfruitful which are alien from God.

Shew me thy ways, O Lord. (CASS.) The ways are of the order of life, etc., as far as: Direct, belongs to life, 877Dteach to knowledge.

VERS. 5.-- Teach. (AUG.) Truth itself, that I may understand what I believe, because I have endured; and if this suffices not: Remember.

God my saviour. (CASS.) There are two things which make men good, that we believe God our saviour, and that we patiently await his retribution.

VERS. 6.-- Remember. (ID.) Of former sins and of those which are daily done, he prays through the mercy shewn to the ancients, and because he fears a true judge.

Of thy tender mercies. Compassion is properly in the shewing forth of good things.

Which are from of old. (AUG.) That is, they are from the beginning of the world: therefore let him not fail in me.

878AVERS. 7.-- Sins. (CASS.) They are when the way of equity is forsaken.

Of my youth. Not for age, but for the rashness of headlong haste, which is then, when the heat of the mind exceeds moderation.

Ignorances. We do those things which we do not know to be evil. Or the sins of ignorance in little ones, who are held at any rate by original sin.

(HIER.) Of my youth. Before I went out of the house of my wicked father.

Remember me, thou. (AUG.) Whose work it is to have mercy and to forgive sins.

According to thy mercy. That is, thy mercy is ample. Mercy is toward the wretched, goodness toward any whatsoever. But God does good both when 878Bimplored by the wretched, and when led by his goodness: none is good but God.

VERS. 8.-- Sweet. (ID.) Because he forgives all former things, where grace is without merits.

Right. Because after mercy, etc., as far as Sweet, because he gives sweet things; right, because he corrects.

Therefore. (CASS.) Because he is sweet and right; not out of cruelty, but out of kindness.

In the way. That is, faith, or the precepts of God. Or in the way of this life, where one must live rightly, he will give a law.

VERS. 9.-- In judgment. While he punishes, he will direct to better things. But let them be meek who are corrected: for from wild beasts they are tamed, that they may bear it. For if they are mild, that is, of a gentle mind, as though having this by nature: he will teach them the precepts for the neglect of which came 878Cthe scourges.

VERS. 10.-- Mercy and truth. (AUG.) But what ways he will teach, etc., as far as and then he guards against the severity of the judge.

Testament. (CASS.) The New, which is excellently called a Testament, where there is a clear and certain promise of an inheritance, which is confirmed by death also.

And the Testament. Of the old law, where the Prophets were witnesses of the promises.

VERS. 11.-- For thy name's sake, O Lord. (AUG.) That is, thy glory, etc., as far as and they are interpreted the clean, who assert themselves clean of all sin.

VERS. 12.-- Who is the man? (CASS.) Here he treats of things eternal; how they are had, labouring and praying, that both 878Dhe himself, and all Israel, may be freed from these evils.

VERS. 13.-- Soul. (ID.) and if not at once, etc., as far as whatever others may do, etc.

Seed. (Hier.) It is good, whence fruit is gathered.

Is a firmament. (AUG.) Fear seems to belong to the weak, but the Lord is a firmament to them that fear him, and he brings it about that his Testament be made manifest to them.

Eyes. Sal. The eyes of a wise man are in his head, that is, in his heart.

VERS. 16.-- Only. (ID.) An only one is the more loved, a poor man the more pitied.

VERS. 17.-- From necessities. That is, from adversities, 879Awhich are necessary for all who wish to live godly in Christ.

VERS. 19.-- Behold. (AUG.) The perdition of so many men cannot be without grief, and therefore he prays for them.

VERS. 21.-- The innocent and the upright have adhered. (ID.) The evil were borne with; they did not adhere.

VERS. 22.-- Israel. (AUG.) The people, whom thou hast prepared for the vision of thee.

PSALMUS XXV.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus. (CASS.) Psalmus iste monet vitari consortia iniquorum, jungi justis, quia ex convictu mores formantur.

Judica. (AUG.) Quia post misericordiam, etc., usque ad a vento superbiae rapiuntur.

879B(CASS.) Judica: non est praesumptio justi, sed certitudo misericordiae Dei, quod ibi ostendit in Domino sperans; deinde, non infirmabor.

In innocentia. (AUG.) Non angelorum, sed qualis est hominum.

VERS. 2.-- Proba me. (CASS.) Id est, prius vires inspice, etc., usque ad non merita, sed misericordiam quae talem me fecit, attendo.

(CASS.) Proba me. Tu vero, proba in tentationibus, ne quid delicti remaneat, etc., usque ad ne quis de eis murmuret.

Ure renes. (ID.) Igne verbi tui, cor calore spiritus. Cor pro cogitationibus, renes pro delectationibus.

VERS. 3.-- Misericordia. (CASS.) Quae non sinit 879Ctentari super vires, vel ipsa ustio est misericordia, non asperitas

Complacui in veritate. (AUG.) Cui displicet mendacium suum, et placet ipse cum illa et in illa.

VERS. 4.-- Non sedi. (CASS.) Complacui in veritate, quia non sedi. Odivi, quod est vitare mala. Et lavabo, quod est agere recta.

Vani. (CASS.) Vani qui de caducis rebus laborant; impii haeretici, qui Scripturas pervertunt: illi superflua quaerunt, hi venenosa.

VERS. 5.-- Malignantium. (ID.) Qui mala proximis agunt.

VERS. 6.-- Lavabo. (AUG.) Poenitendo. Et altare, mentem virtutibus ornabo, vel fidem, quia non est locus veri sacrificii extra catholicam Ecclesiam.

879DInter innocentes. (AUG.) Conversans; ut audiam ab eis, id est, ut discam qua voce sis laudandus; vel, ut audiam: Venite, benedicti Patris mei.

VERS. 7.-- Vocem laudis Spiritus sancti, qui docet laudare te.

VERS. 8.-- Domine. (CASS.) Petit ne malis in judicio misceatur, quia non eis, sed concordat domui Dei.

Dilexi decorem. (CASS.) Haec ideo faciam, quia dilexi me facere decoram domum tibi, et locum, quo gloriose habites, ut de gloria et essentia Dei aliquid capiam.

VERS. 9.-- Ne perdas. (CASS.) Et si modo simul esse pateris, ne simul perdas.

880A(CASS.) Ne perdas in futuro cum impiis, quibus hic non communico.

VERS. 10.-- Dextera eorum, (AUG.), id est, si quid boni agunt, etc., usque ad misericordia in omnibus comitetur, quod debes, quia:

VERS. 12.-- Pes, id est, affectio, quae facile labi solet, stetit immobilis contra omnia scandala, tendens ultra, et persistens in directo. Et quia sic redimis in Ecclesiis, benedicam.

Stetit. (CASS.) Etsi undique concussus, vel confusus scandalis.

PSALM XXV.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm. (CASS.) This psalm admonishes that the fellowships of the wicked be shunned, and that we be joined to the just, because from living together manners are formed.

Judge. (AUG.) Because after mercy, etc., as far as they are carried off by the wind of pride.

879B(CASS.) Judge: it is not the presumption of a just man, but the certainty of God's mercy, which he shews there in hoping in the Lord; then, I shall not be weakened.

In innocence. (AUG.) Not that of angels, but such as is of men.

VERS. 2.-- Prove me. (CASS.) That is, first look upon my strength, etc., as far as I regard not merits, but the mercy which has made me such.

(CASS.) Prove me. But do thou prove me in temptations, that no sin remain, etc., as far as lest any man murmur about them.

Burn my reins. (ID.) With the fire of thy word, the heart with the heat of the spirit. Heart for thoughts, reins for delights.

VERS. 3.-- Mercy. (CASS.) Which suffers not 879Cthat we be tempted above our strength; or that very burning is mercy, not harshness

I have been well pleased in truth. (AUG.) He to whom his own lie is displeasing, and who himself is pleasing along with her and in her.

VERS. 4.-- I have not sat. (CASS.) I have been well pleased in truth, because I have not sat. I have hated, which is to shun evils. And I will wash, which is to do right things.

The vain. (CASS.) The vain are they who labour about perishable things; the wicked are heretics, who pervert the Scriptures: those seek superfluous things, these poisonous.

VERS. 5.-- Of the malignant. (ID.) Who do evils to their neighbours.

VERS. 6.-- I will wash. (AUG.) By doing penance. And the altar, I will adorn my mind with virtues, or faith, because there is no place of true sacrifice outside the catholic Church.

879DAmong the innocent. (AUG.) Conversing; that I may hear from them, that is, that I may learn with what voice thou art to be praised; or, that I may hear: Come, ye blessed of my Father.

VERS. 7.-- The voice of praise of the Holy Ghost, who teaches to praise thee.

VERS. 8.-- Lord. (CASS.) He asks that he be not mingled with the wicked in the judgment, because it is not with them, but with the house of God, that he agrees.

I have loved the beauty. (CASS.) These things therefore will I do, because I have loved to make for thee a comely house, and a place wherein thou mayest dwell in glory, that I may take in something of the glory and the essence of God.

VERS. 9.-- Destroy not. (CASS.) And if for the present thou sufferest us to be together, destroy us not together.

880A(CASS.) Destroy me not in time to come with the wicked, with whom here I have no fellowship.

VERS. 10.-- Their right hand, (AUG.), that is, if they do any good, etc., as far as let mercy accompany in all things, which thou owest, because:

VERS. 12.-- Foot, that is, affection, which is wont easily to slip, hath stood unmoved against all scandals, stretching beyond, and persisting in the right way. And because thou so redeemest in the churches, I will bless.

It hath stood. (CASS.) Even though shaken on every side, or confounded by scandals.

PSALMUS XXVI.

VERS. 1.-- In finem. (AUG., CASS.) Primo, David electus, etc., usque ad unde in sacramento gemens et laborans; ut in re gaudeat.

880BDominus illuminatio, etc. (CASS.) De prima unctione per quam certificatur secunda, hic loquitur.

Dominus protector vitae meae. (AUG.) Dat vitam virtutum, quam et protegit, sine quo omnia dona ejus perduntur.

A quo trepidabo? (ID.) Quem trepidet, caro, cum induerit corruptionem.

VERS. 2.-- Super me nocentes. (ID.) Ut se mihi praeferant insultantes: quod vertit Deus in melius, ut maledico dente non me, sed carnalia desideria consumant. Vel edant, id est, delectetur in morte mea crudelitas inimicorum, carnes; animam non possunt.

Infirmati sunt. (ID.) Dum Christus carnem accepit, nutantes facti, et post ex toto se fidei subdiderunt.

880C(CASS.) Vel, debilitati paulatim ad ruinam animae pervenerunt.

VERS. 3.-- Castra. (CASS.) Molimina, praelium, conflictus.

In hoc ego. (AUG.) Habeo spem victoriae in Domino remunerationis aeternae.

VERS. 4.-- Unam petii. (AUG.) Haec una domus aeterna, in qua semper maneatur, ubi aeterni dies, cur ibi? ut contempler delectationem Dei, quod est verum bonum.

Omnibus diebus vitae meae. (AUG.) Ut quandiu vivo, etc., usque ad opus manifestabo.

Ut videam. (ID.) Alia littera: Ut contempler delectationem Domini, id est, eo fine, ut demum appareat, 880Detc., usque ad et ideo non temere peto unam, etsi peccator.

VERS. 5.-- In abscondito: (AUG.) quasi multae partes sunt, etc., usque ad quem mox vocat petram.

VERS. 6.-- Circumivi. (AUG.) Quia mihi se praebuit ducem, etc., usque ad ut omnes voluntates ejus implerem.

(HIER.) Vel circumspexi omnia creata, vel exempla sanctorum.

(AUG.) Circumivi animo omnia creata, etc., usque ad tanto ardentius appetit.

VERS. 7.-- Exaudi, Domine, vocem meam, etc. (CASS.) Quis labor, quis gemitus? Oratio ante secundam 881Aunctionem, ut possit haberi quam et sibi prophetiae spiritu promittit.

VERS. 8.-- Tibi dixit. (CASS.) Cor, ratio a te edocta tibi confabulatur de una, non aliud quam doces pertractet.

VERS. 9.-- Ne avertas. (AUG.) Alius petit hic bona temporalia a Deo, et de datis gaudet, hic non nisi unam. Alius habens timet iratum, ne tollat ea; iste non putat iram, nisi si avertat vultum, etiam si quid in eo vindicet; nil divinius poterat dicere.

Ne declines. (AUG.) Non in ira declinat, quando a peccatis faciem avertit; vel, ne declines, ut me labi sinas in ira, id est, quod punias; sed ut nostra infirmitas cautior fiat.

881BSalutaris meus, etc. (AUG.) Quasi, frustra creasti et recreasti, etc., usque ad a Domino est per Samuelem electus.

VERS. 10.-- Quoniam pater, etc. Fecit se parvulum Deo, ipsum fecit sibi patrem: quia jubet, vocat, condidit, et regit. Matrem, quia fovet, continet, collactat et nutrit; sed saeculum pater vel diabolus, mater Babylonia, id est, societas impiorum.

VERS. 11.-- Legem pone mihi, etc.

VERS. 12.-- Tribulantium. (CASS.) Ut Saulis et adjutorum, etc., usque ad quia falsi.

VERS. 13.-- Credo videre. (AUG.) Sed inter omnia pericula, Deo dirigente, credo videre.

Bona. (ID.) Bona, quae sunt vera, aeterna. Illi 881Csuadent beatitudinem in terra ista, quae est morientium.

VERS. 14.-- Exspecta. (CASS.) Ut ego certus sum de illa, etc., usque ad sustine quod pateris.

PSALM XXVI.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end. [Vulg. Ps 26:1 heads this psalm Psalmus David, priusquam liniretur, "before he was anointed"] (AUG., CASS.) First, David chosen, etc., as far as whence groaning and labouring in the sacrament; that he may rejoice in the reality.

880BThe Lord is my light, etc. (CASS.) Of the first anointing, through which the second is made sure, he speaks here.

The Lord is the protector of my life. (AUG.) He gives the life of the virtues, which he also protects, without which all his gifts are lost.

Of whom shall I be afraid? (ID.) Whom should the flesh fear, when it shall have put on corruption [corruptionem; read incorruptionem, "incorruption"].

VERS. 2.-- The wicked upon me. (ID.) That, insulting, they may prefer themselves to me: which God turns to the better, so that with their cursing tooth they consume not me, but my carnal desires. Or let them eat, that is, let the cruelty of my enemies take its delight in my death, the flesh; the soul they cannot.

They were weakened. (ID.) While Christ took flesh, they were made to waver, and afterwards submitted themselves wholly to faith.

880C(CASS.) Or, being weakened little by little they came to the ruin of the soul.
