VERS. 3.-- Camps. (CASS.) Efforts, battle, conflicts.

In this will I hope. (AUG.) I have hope of victory in the Lord of the eternal reward.

VERS. 4.-- One thing I have asked. (AUG.) This one house is eternal, in which one may abide always, where the days are eternal; why there? That I may contemplate the delight of God, which is the true good.

All the days of my life. (AUG.) That as long as I live, etc., as far as I will make manifest the work.

That I may see. (ID.) Another reading: That I may contemplate the delight of the Lord, that is, to this end, that at last he may appear, 880Detc., as far as and therefore not rashly do I ask one thing, though a sinner.

VERS. 5.-- In secret: (AUG.) as it were there are many parts, etc., as far as him whom presently he calls a rock.

VERS. 6.-- I have gone round. (AUG.) Because he offered himself to me as a leader, etc., as far as that I might fulfil all his wills.

(HIER.) Or I have looked round upon all created things, or the examples of the saints.

(AUG.) I have gone round in mind all created things, etc., as far as the more ardently it desires.

VERS. 7.-- Hear, O Lord, my voice, etc. (CASS.) What labour, what groaning? The prayer before the second 881Aanointing, that he may be able to have that which he also promises himself by the spirit of prophecy.

VERS. 8.-- To thee hath said. (CASS.) The heart, the reason taught by thee, converses with thee of the one thing, that it may handle nothing other than what thou teachest.

VERS. 9.-- Turn not away. (AUG.) Another asks here for temporal goods from God, and rejoices in what is given; this man asks nothing but one thing. Another, having them, fears him angered, lest he take them away; this man thinks there is no anger unless he turn away his countenance, even if he punish something in him; nothing more divine could he have said.

Turn not aside. (AUG.) He does not turn aside in anger, when he turns his face from sins; or, turn not aside, so as to let me slip in anger, that is, in what thou mayest punish; but that our weakness may be made more wary.

881BMy saviour, etc. (AUG.) As though: in vain hast thou created and re-created, etc., as far as he was chosen by the Lord through Samuel.

VERS. 10.-- For my father, etc. He made himself a little one to God, and made him his own father: because he commands, calls, founded and rules. A mother, because he cherishes, contains, suckles and nourishes; but the world is a father, or the devil, the mother Babylon, that is, the fellowship of the wicked.

VERS. 11.-- Set me a law, etc.

VERS. 12.-- Of them that trouble me. (CASS.) As of Saul and his helpers, etc., as far as because they are false.

VERS. 13.-- I believe to see. (AUG.) But among all perils, God directing, I believe to see.

Good things. (ID.) Good things which are true, eternal. Those men 881Cpersuade to a blessedness in this earth, which is the earth of the dying.

VERS. 14.-- Expect. (CASS.) As I am sure of it, etc., as far as endure what thou sufferest.

PSALMUS XXVII.

Psalmus huic. Per David aliquando intelligitur caput, id est, Christus; aliquando corpus, id est, Ecclesia; interdum utrumque simul, id est, totus Christus intelligitur, ut hic.

(CASS.) Psalmus tertius, qui breviter de passione et resurrectione.

(ID.) Hic proponitur Christus (et si adeo dignus) non in se confidere, sed totum a Deo petere; utile exemplum justis.

VERS. 1.-- Ad te, Domine. (ID.) Oratio tempore 881Dpassionis habita.

Ne sileas. Minus est in Hebraeo, etc., usque ad et a morte resuscitationem.

Ne sileas, etc., et assimilabor, etc. (HIER.) Ex eo, quod verbum mihi semper unitur, non talis homo sum quales caeteri, qui nascuntur in profundam miseriam saeculi.

(AUG.) Ubi quasi si sileas non cognoscitur verbum tuum.

VERS. 2.-- Ad templum. (CASS.) Secundum morem Judaeorum, quibus praeceptum est ut ubicunque essent ad illam partem orarent, ubi Jerusalem esse scirent: quod et Jesus legem implens fecit. Vel ad coelum, unde auxilium speramus.

882AVERS. 4.-- Da illis. ( Ibid. ) Praedicere est, non optare, secundum quod intenderunt, non secundum quod inde pervenit: vel optat justitiam Dei in hoc servari.

VERS. 5.-- Quoniam non, etc. (ID.) Et si deessent opera, hoc sufficeret damnationi, quod non intellexerunt per legem et Prophetas, quae invisibiliter Deus operatur per me, nec etiam visibilia.

Destrues. (AUG.) Ut nihil mihi noceat, nec post Ecclesiae tuae, vel meae.

Benedictus. (CASS.) Auditus in resurrectione gratias agit, subdens de salute credentium.

Dominus. (ID.) Idem qui adjutor meus, et protector est fortitudo plebis, quae in eo confidit, et 882Bprotector ne laedantur, et tu, o Domine:

VERS. 9.-- Salvum. Ecce quanta spes credentium cum pro eis orat: passus pro eis judex est et advocatus.

Et rege, etc. (ID.) Ne declinent ad prava.

Extolle, etc., a terrenis ad petenda aeterna, et intellectu Scripturarum, et bono opere per totum hoc saeculum usque in finem.

PSALM XXVII.

A psalm to this one. [Vulg. Ps 27:1 heads it Psalmus ipsi David] By David is sometimes understood the head, that is, Christ; sometimes the body, that is, the Church; sometimes both together, that is, the whole Christ is understood, as here.

(CASS.) The third psalm, which treats briefly of the passion and the resurrection.

(ID.) Here Christ is set forth (and though he is so worthy) as not trusting in himself, but asking the whole from God; a useful example to the just.

VERS. 1.-- To thee, O Lord. (ID.) A prayer had in the time 881Dof the passion.

Be not silent. Less is in the Hebrew, etc., as far as and the raising up from death.

Be not silent, etc., and I shall be likened, etc. (HIER.) From this, that the Word is always united to me, I am not such a man as the rest, who are born into the deep misery of the world.

(AUG.) Where, as it were, if thou be silent, thy word is not known.

VERS. 2.-- To the temple. (CASS.) According to the custom of the Jews, to whom it was commanded that wheresoever they were they should pray toward that quarter where they knew Jerusalem to be: which Jesus also did, fulfilling the law. Or toward heaven, whence we hope for help.

882AVERS. 4.-- Give to them. ( Ibid. ) It is to foretell, not to wish, according to what they intended, not according to what came of it: or he wishes the justice of God to be preserved in this.

VERS. 5.-- Because not, etc. (ID.) And if works were wanting, this would suffice for damnation, that they understood not through the law and the Prophets the things which God invisibly works through me, nor even the visible things.

Thou shalt destroy. (AUG.) That nothing hurt me, nor afterwards thy Church, or mine.

Blessed. (CASS.) Having been heard, in the resurrection he gives thanks, adding of the salvation of them that believe.

The Lord. (ID.) The same who is my helper, and my protector, is the strength of the people which trusts in him, and 882Ba protector that they be not hurt, and thou, O Lord:

VERS. 9.-- Save. Behold how great is the hope of them that believe, when he prays for them: he who suffered for them is judge and advocate.

And rule them, etc. (ID.) Lest they turn aside to crooked things.

Lift up, etc., from earthly things to the seeking of things eternal, and by the understanding of the Scriptures, and by good work, through this whole world unto the end.

PSALMUS XXVIII.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus David in consummatione. (ID.) Arca a Philistaeis reducta, etc., usque ad ut se offerant tali consummatori.

Afferte Domino. (ID.) Prius monet sacrificia offerre.

882CFilios arietum. (AUG.) Quia non deest impugnatio, etc., usque ad et septuaginta duo discipuli ad praedicandum missi significantur.

Vox Domini. (CASS.) Praedicatio Christi intus mentes terruit, quod est, spiritum timoris dedit Judaeis et gentibus.

(GREG.) Iste ab imo ascendit, id est, spiritu timoris ad spiritum sapientiae, etc., usque ad id est, spiritualem intellectum, hos Dominus concutit.

(HIER.) Ut agricola sterilem terram, etc., usque ad et dabit virtutem, et eamdem benedicet in pace aeterna.

VERS. 3.-- Vox Domini super aquas, etc. (CASS.) De constitutione Ecclesiae, ubi virtutes Spiritus sancti 882Dcum magno praeconio enumerat.

Libani. Libanus interpretatur candidatio. Cedri Libani, id est, alti homines in terrenis elati, quos Deus confringendo comminuet, id est, de superbia ad se per dilectum filium reducet: et hoc spiritu fortitudinis comminuet, sicut unicornis captus comminuitur.

VERS. 7.-- Desertum. (CASS., AUG.) Judaicum populum, etc., usque ad unde emanat aqua viva.

VERS. 10.-- Dominus. Quid constitutae Ecclesiae fiat ostendit.

Dedi, enim ait, vobis potestatem conculcare super serpentes. Ut autem est inauditum, ut cervi omne genuo ferarum cornu feriant; sic ut Apostoli omnem philosophiam illiterati redarguerent.

883ADiluvium. (CASS.) Aquas baptismi, qui purgat crimina mundi.

PSALM XXVIII.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of David in the consummation. (ID.) The ark brought back from the Philistines, etc., as far as that they may offer themselves to such a consummator.

Bring to the Lord. (ID.) First he admonishes that sacrifices be offered.

882CThe sons of rams. (AUG.) Because assault is not wanting, etc., as far as and the seventy-two disciples sent to preach are signified.

The voice of the Lord. (CASS.) The preaching of Christ terrified minds within, which is, that it gave the spirit of fear to the Jews and to the Gentiles.

(GREG.) This man ascends from the lowest, that is, from the spirit of fear to the spirit of wisdom, etc., as far as that is, spiritual understanding: these the Lord shakes.

(HIER.) As a husbandman a barren land, etc., as far as and he will give strength, and will bless the same in eternal peace.

VERS. 3.-- The voice of the Lord upon the waters, etc. (CASS.) Of the establishing of the Church, where he enumerates the powers of the Holy Ghost 882Dwith great proclamation.

Of Libanus. Libanus is interpreted a whitening. The cedars of Libanus, that is, high men lifted up in earthly things, whom God by breaking will crush small, that is, will bring them back from pride to himself through his beloved Son: and this he will crush by the spirit of fortitude, as a unicorn taken is crushed.

VERS. 7.-- The desert. (CASS., AUG.) The Jewish people, etc., as far as whence flows the living water.

VERS. 10.-- The Lord. He shews what is done for the Church now established.

I have given, he says, you power to tread down upon serpents. [Vulg. Lc 10:19 has calcandi supra serpentes, "to tread upon serpents"] But as it is unheard of that stags should strike every kind of wild beast with the horn; so that the Apostles, unlettered, should refute all philosophy.

883AA flood. (CASS.) The waters of baptism, which purges the crimes of the world.

PSALMUS XXIX.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus cantici in dedic. (AUG.) Supra de consummatione tabernaculi tempore belli: hic autem est psalmus laetitiae, quia domus dedicatur, id est, confirmatur, quae in aeterna pace manebit: corpore innovato non tantum Christi, sed etiam totius Ecclesiae. Totus Christus loquitur in hoc psalmo, quia quaedam capiti, quaedam corpori, quaedam utrique conveniunt.

(ID.) Psalmus breviter de passione et resurrectione: ut passio non terreat quos spes resurrectionis laetificat.

Domus David. (CASS.) Totus Christus sponsus, etc., 883Busque ad secundum statum futurum quando in ea quiescitur.

(CASS.) Primo agit de dedicatione sua: et jubet sanctos idem sperantes laudes dicere.

VERS. 3.-- Domine, Deus meus, clamavi ad te, etc. (AUG.) Christus, etc., usque ad sed non in dedicatione.

VERS. 4.-- In lacum. (HIER.) Id est, de lacu inferni, ubi animae peccatorum sunt, ne, sicut illi, praeceps caderem in mortem.

VERS. 5.-- Confitemini, etc. (AUG.) Quia ex bonitate et sanctitate sua, non nostra memor fuit nostri.

VERS. 6.-- Quoniam ira. (ID.) Id est, vindicta, qua vindicavit in nos primum peccatum, quod morte 883Csolvistis.

Ad vesperum. (ID.) Quia ira, etc., usque ad id est, tempore gratiae post tempus ante legem, et sub lege.

(HIER.) Ad vesperum. Quia passo et sepulto Domino, Apostoli et mulieres in fletu et gemitu morabantur. Et ad matutinum laetitia. Quia mane venientes ad sepulcrum, gloriam resurrectionis ab Angelis acceperunt. Fletus. (CASS.) Demorabitur hominibus respicientibus ad vesperum, quo Adam declinavit, et a paradiso exivit: sed laetitia erit respicientibus ad matutinum, quo Christus surrexit.

VERS. 7.-- Ego autem. Quomodo ante dedicationem egerit et eam meruerit. (AUG., CASS.) Vespere facit. Sed ego, dum in paradiso esset mihi abundantia, 883Ddixi: Non movebor ad hoc bono, credens diabolo dicenti: Non morte morieris (Gen. III). Sed, o Domine, in voluntate tua praestitisti decori meo virtutem; quod est, non ex me bonus eram et fortis, sed ex te. Quod ut ostenderes: Avertisti faciem tuam, hoc est, foras misisti me de paradiso: jam vero hic positus clamabo ad te, etc.

VERS. 8.-- Avertisti. (CASS.) Deus a Christo faciem, exponendo eum passioni et morti; et sic Christus turbatus est: Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem. (Matth. XVI.) Conturbatus. (AUG.) Quod tempus conturbationis et miseriae recolens, et in eo positus, audio vocem capitis pro me morituri, dicentis: Ad te, Domine, clamabo.

884AVERS. 10.-- Quae utilitas in sanguine meo. (ID.) Necessitatem ostendit per quam non sinit eum descendere in corruptionem. Dum descendo in corruptionem. Si enim statim non resurgo, et corpus corrumpitur, nemini annuntiabo, nullum lucrabor. Confessio gemina est, nunquam sine ea simus: quando male est nobis in tribulationibus, confiteamur peccata nostra; quando bene est, in exsultatione justitiae confiteamur laudem Deo.

VERS. 11.-- Audivit Dominus. (CASS.) Quomodo eam accepit, scilicet dedicationem, pertractat. Dixit: Clamabo, deprecabor, sed me deprecantem exaudivit Dominus.

VERS. 12.-- Conscidisti saccum meum. (ID.) Saccus vestis est aspera, in usum laboris vel tempore 884Btristitiae concessa, ut Ninivitis, id est, caro humana, quae scissa est moriendo: et prodiit frumentum gloriosae resurrectionis, vel divinitatis. Vel, poena peccati, qua in resurrectione destructa, prolata est divinitas ante occulta: sicut quod saccus integer celat, scissus aperit. (AUG.) Saccus de capris vel haedis, mortalitas; quam de peccatoribus Christus traxit vel accepit; unde: Dum mihi molesti essent, induebar cilicio (Psal. XXXIV), ut quod intus erat, non viderent.

VERS. 13.-- Non compungar. (ID.) Non moriar jam in finem. Domine Deus, in aeternum confitebor tibi. Quid est: in aeternum confitebor tibi? in aeter num laudabo te.

PSALM XXIX.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of a canticle, at the dedic. (AUG.) Above, concerning the finishing of the tabernacle in a time of war: but this is a psalm of gladness, because the house is dedicated, that is, made firm, which shall abide in eternal peace: the body being made new, not only Christ's but also the whole Church's. The whole Christ speaks in this psalm, because some things belong to the head, some to the body, some to both.

(ID.) The psalm is briefly of the passion and the resurrection: that the passion may not terrify those whom the hope of the resurrection gladdens.

The house of David. (CASS.) The whole Christ is the bridegroom, etc., 883Bas far as the second state, the state to come, when there is rest in it.

(CASS.) First he treats of his own dedication: and bids the saints who hope for the same to utter praises.

VERS. 3.-- O Lord my God, I have cried to thee, etc. (AUG.) Christ, etc., as far as but not in the dedication.

VERS. 4.-- Into the pit. (HIER.) That is, out of the pit of hell, where the souls of sinners are, lest, like them, I should fall headlong into death.

VERS. 5.-- Confess ye, etc. (AUG.) Because out of his own goodness and holiness, not ours, he was mindful of us.

VERS. 6.-- For wrath. (ID.) That is, vengeance, by which he avenged upon us the first sin, which by death you have 883Cloosed.

At evening. (ID.) Because wrath, etc., as far as that is, in the time of grace after the time before the law and under the law.

(HIER.) At evening. Because, when the Lord had suffered and been buried, the Apostles and the women continued in weeping and groaning. And in the morning gladness. Because coming to the sepulchre in the morning they received from the Angels the glory of the resurrection. Weeping. (CASS.) It shall abide for men who look toward the evening, at which Adam turned aside and went out from paradise: but there shall be gladness for those who look toward the morning, at which Christ rose again.

VERS. 7.-- But I. How he acted before the dedication and deserved it. (AUG., CASS.) He acts at evening. But I, while abundance was mine in paradise, 883Dsaid: I shall not be moved from this good, believing the devil who said: Thou shalt not die the death (Gen. III) [Vulg. Gn 3:4 has the plural and a stronger negative, "ye shall by no means die the death"]. But, O Lord, in thy will thou hast given strength to my beauty; which is, I was good and strong not of myself, but of thee. And that thou mightest show it: Thou hast turned away thy face, that is, thou hast sent me forth out of paradise: but now, set here, I will cry to thee, etc.

VERS. 8.-- Thou hast turned away. (CASS.) God turned away his face from Christ, by exposing him to the passion and to death; and thus Christ was troubled: My soul is sorrowful even unto death. (Matth. XVI.) Troubled. (AUG.) Calling to mind that time of trouble and of misery, and set in it, I hear the voice of the head who is to die for me, saying: To thee, O Lord, will I cry.

884AVERS. 10.-- What profit is there in my blood. (ID.) He shows the necessity by which he does not suffer him to go down into corruption. Whilst I go down into corruption. For if I do not rise again at once, and the body is corrupted, I shall announce to no one, I shall gain no one. Confession is twofold, let us never be without it: when it is ill with us in tribulations, let us confess our sins; when it is well, let us confess praise to God in the exultation of justice.

VERS. 11.-- The Lord hath heard. (CASS.) He treats of how he received it, namely the dedication. He said: I will cry, I will beseech, but the Lord heard me beseeching.

VERS. 12.-- Thou hast cut my sackcloth. (ID.) Sackcloth is a rough garment, granted for the use of labour or in a time of 884Bsadness, as to the Ninivites; that is, human flesh, which was rent by dying: and there came forth the corn of the glorious resurrection, or of the godhead. Or else, the penalty of sin, which being destroyed in the resurrection, the godhead before hidden was brought forth: just as what the sack conceals whole, it opens when rent. (AUG.) Sackcloth of goats or of kids is mortality, which Christ drew or took from sinners; whence: Whilst they were troublesome to me, I was clothed with haircloth (Psal. XXXIV), that they might not see what was within.

VERS. 13.-- I shall not be pricked. (ID.) I shall not now die unto the end. O Lord God, I will confess to thee for ever. What is: I will confess to thee for ever? For ever I will praise thee.

PSALMUS XXX.

884CVERS. 1.-- In finem psalmus. (AUG.) Exstasis hic accipitur pavor perturbati populi de persecutione omnium gentium, et defectu fidei per orbem.

(CASS.) Contra pavorem spes et oratio praemittitur, etc., usque ad: Erunt duo in carne una (Gen. II), ergo et in voce una. (AUG.) Prior loquitur Redemptor, inde redempti, gratias agentes. Inde diu de perturbatione Prophetae vox interponitur prope finem, et in fine. Hic describitur humiliatio Christi martyrumque: unde sequitur exaltatio.

VERS. 2.-- In te, Domine, speravi, etc. (ID.) Est confusio aeterna, de qua liberari petit: et est temporalis ad horam, scilicet quae prodest.

VERS. 3.-- Accelera. (ID.) In faciendis, in solvendis 884Danimabus et hujusmodi, ut eruas tertia die, non differas in communem resurrectionem; quod ut sit, esto mihi protector tantus, quantum decet esse Deum. Esto mihi. Dixit: Justitiam da, etc., usque ad affirmat liberationem.

VERS. 5.-- Educes. (CASS.) De morte ad superna, ut frustra sint Judaeorum consilia. De laqueo quem absconderunt. (AUG.) Per duas portas diabolus tentat, etc., usque ad unde: Educes me de laqueo.

VERS. 6.-- In manus. (CASS.) Nota eum hic loqui qui in passione eadem verba protulit. (AUG.) In manus. Ex his verbis quae in cruce dixit, admonet se in hoc psalmo locutum esse.

VERS. 8.-- Ego autem, in Domino, etc. (CASS.) De 885Agaudio, quia sperat in Domino, qui odit vanos. Exsultabo et laetabor. Exsultare est cum magna alacritate animi gaudere: laetari, temperata affectione. Humilitatem meam. Pro infirmitate, et pro ipsa virtute humilitatis accipit. Necessitatibus. (AUG.) Necessitates sunt infinitae, etc., usque ad et in futuro plenarie.

VERS. 9, 10.-- In loco spatioso. (CASS.) Locus spatiosus libere eundi ad patriam virtutum, charitas: sed, quia caro infirma, et urgent mala: Miserere mei, Domine. Jam pavor enarratur, id est, quot et quanta ea perturbant, contra quae est oratio, Tribulor. (AUG.) Cum prius dixit: Statuisti in loco spatioso, etc. Sed aliis locus spatiosus, ex liberationis gratulatione; aliis ex tribulatione, angustia. Conturbatus. Irascitur 885Bpro peccatis palearum, etc., usque ad nam vita perfectorum est profectus aliorum. In ira oculus. In ira persecutorum, etc., usque ad ut ab omnibus gradibus quaeratur Deus. (CASS.) Vel intellectus turbatur, et animus confunditur, etc., usque ad nec in animo, nec in corpore ulla potest esse hominis praesumptio. (AUG.) Ira per vitium oculum mentis caecat; ira per zelum turbat: quia et haec, concussa mente, contemplationem dissipat, quae non est nisi inquieta mente; sed inde post paululum plus proficit ad videndum.

VERS. 11.-- Paupertate. (ID.) Vel egestate. Egeo sanitate corporis, nec parcitur cruciatibus. Egeo resolutione, et parcitur morti; et in hoc infirmata est fiducia mea.

885CVERS. 12.-- Super omnes inimicos meos. (ID.) Pejus paganis et Judaeis vivunt, etc., usque ad pro quibus timent et noti, ne omnes tales sint. (CASS.) Vel apud omnes inimicos, vel majori opprobrio habitus, quam illi qui digni eo; et vicinis, parentibus, vel jam credituris; et notis, familiaribus.

VERS. 13.-- Qui videbant me foras. (HIER.) Foras, Christum, id est, qui hominem purum putabant. Oblivioni datus sum tanquam mortuus a corde. (CASS.) Vel excidi a corde eorum, ut mortuus cujus memoria cum corpore sepelitur, de cujus reparatione desperatur. Vas perditum, mortuus Jesus abjiciendus putatur.

VERS. 14.-- Vituperationem multorum. (AUG.) 885DVituperantur, etc., usque ad non quisquam homo. In circuitu. In eo dum convenirent simul. (CASS.) Errorum, etc., usque ad id est, appetitu temporalium.

VERS. 16.-- Sortes meae. (ID.) Vel tempora vitae. (AUG.) Quia quando vis, vivimus, vel morimur: ideo eripe. Etsi justus, et occultus ordo electionis apud te est, ego tamen, etc., usque ad quae, sine meritis, quos vult elegit.

VERS. 17.-- Illustra. (CASS.) Manifestam fac benevolentiam tuam super me, ut sicut de moriente desperant, ita de resurgente confidant. (AUG.) Illustra. Appareat, qui ad te pertineat cum modo sit confusio; unde alibi: Discerne causam meam (Psal. XLI); ne 886Atamen se justificare videatur, subdit: Salvum me fac in misericordia, non in mea justitia.

VERS. 18.-- Invocavi. (ID.) Invocas Deum, quando in te vocas eum, et quando in domum cordis tui eum invitas.

VERS. 19.-- Muta fiant. (CASS.) Quae hic garrula, dum non timent judicium. Muta in poenis, in inferno.

Quae loquuntur. Apte opponit justo iniquitatem.

In superbia et in abusione. (CASS.) Quia creatura contra creatorem, et perverso usu beneficiorum Dei, qui, praeter caetera, propter eos venit.

VERS. 20.-- Quam magna. (CASS.) Quae bona Dei contra praedicta mala, quae leviant ipsa mala. (AUG.) Ista cernens et mirans exclamat Propheta, etc., usque ad in futuro vero patebit.

886B--VERS. 21. A conturbatione. (AUG.) Ut jam nullam conturbationem humanam patiatur, etiam modo tribulati, mente intrantes ad vultum Dei non turbantur. Proteges. (CASS.) Ne promissio tantum futuri turbaret, hoc addit: proteges, ne noceantur.

VERS. 22.-- Benedictus. (ID.) Quasi, quid ultra? Plenitudinem beneficii laude concludit, comparans illud suae imbecillitati. Et loquitur Propheta, vel populus fidelis. Mirificavit. (AUG.) Misso Spiritu, totum mundum replevit, etc., usque ad unde: Unguentum effusum est nomen tuum. (CASS.) Vel, mirificavit Deus Pater misericordiam, etc., usque ad juxta illud: Requievit in corde terrae.

VERS. 23.-- Ego dixi in excessu. (AUG.) Timoris nostri typum, etc., usque ad: Ideo exaudisti vocem orationis 886Cmeae. (AUG.) In excessu mentis. Vel rapta mente vidit altitudinem ex qua sentit se projectum valde longe: vel excessit a ratione timendo. A facie oculorum tuorum. Si in facie tua essem, etc., usque ad sed meum cor accusavi.

VERS. 24.-- Diligite Dominum, omnes, etc. (CASS.) Conclusio oratoria, vel hortatoria, pro praedictis obtinendis. (AUG.) Praedicta expertus jam nos hortatur; quasi: tribulatus sum, timui, clamavi, non sum confusus: ita vos. Sancti ejus, quorum est diligere Deum, quia non amant mundum, neque quae in mundo sunt; amicus mundi hujus, inimicus Dei constituitur. Disce ergo non diligere mundum, ut discas diligere Deum: averte, ut convertaris; funde, ut implearis. Requiret Dominus, etc. Etiam hic aliquando, 886Dsi nulli hoc faceret, non videretur vigilare divina providentia, si omnibus non servaretur divina patientia.

Abundanter facientibus. Qui non cito poenitent.

Superbiam. Pro omni vitio, quia radix omnium.

VERS. 25.-- Viriliter agite, etc. Virtus totius psalmi, ne carnis fragilitas timeat tot mala saeculi.

PSALM XXX.

884CVERS. 1.-- Unto the end, a psalm. (AUG.) Ecstasy is here taken as the dread of a people troubled by the persecution of all the nations and by the failing of faith throughout the world.

(CASS.) Against dread, hope and prayer are set first, etc., as far as: They shall be two in one flesh (Gen. II), therefore in one voice also. (AUG.) The Redeemer speaks first, then the redeemed, giving thanks. Then, at length concerning the disturbance, the voice of the Prophet is put in near the end, and at the end. Here is described the humbling of Christ and of the martyrs: whence follows the exaltation.

VERS. 2.-- In thee, O Lord, have I hoped, etc. (ID.) There is an eternal confusion, from which he asks to be delivered: and there is a temporal one, for an hour, namely the kind that profits.

VERS. 3.-- Make haste. (ID.) In the things to be done, in the 884Dsouls to be loosed and the like, that thou mayest rescue me on the third day and not defer it to the common resurrection; and that this may be, be thou to me a protector as great as it befits God to be. Be thou to me. He said: Give justice, etc., as far as he affirms the deliverance.

VERS. 5.-- Thou wilt bring out. (CASS.) From death to the things above, so that the counsels of the Jews may be in vain. Out of the snare which they have hidden. (AUG.) The devil tempts by two gates, etc., as far as whence: Thou wilt bring me out of the snare.

VERS. 6.-- Into thy hands. (CASS.) Note that he speaks here who uttered these same words in the passion. (AUG.) Into thy hands. From these words which he said on the cross, he gives notice that he has spoken in this psalm.

VERS. 8.-- But I, in the Lord, etc. (CASS.) Of 885Ajoy, because he hopes in the Lord, who hates the vain. I will exult and be glad. To exult is to rejoice with great eagerness of soul: to be glad, with a tempered affection. My humility. He takes it for weakness, and for the very virtue of humility. From necessities. (AUG.) Necessities are unbounded, etc., as far as and fully in the world to come.

VERS. 9, 10.-- In a spacious place. (CASS.) The spacious place of going freely to the fatherland of the virtues is charity: but because the flesh is weak and evils press: Have mercy on me, O Lord. Now the dread is recounted, that is, how many and how great are the things that disturb, against which is the prayer, I am troubled. (AUG.) Since he said before: Thou hast set my feet in a spacious place, etc. But for some the place is spacious, out of the thanksgiving of deliverance; for others, out of tribulation, it is a narrow strait. Troubled. He is angry 885Bfor the sins of the chaff, etc., as far as for the life of the perfect is the advancement of others. In anger the eye. In the anger of the persecutors, etc., as far as that God may be sought from every degree. (CASS.) Or the understanding is disturbed and the mind confounded, etc., as far as neither in mind nor in body can there be any presumption of man. (AUG.) Anger through vice blinds the eye of the mind; anger through zeal troubles it: because this too, the mind being shaken, scatters contemplation, which is not except with an unquiet mind; but thereafter, after a little, it profits the more toward seeing.

VERS. 11.-- In poverty. (ID.) Or in want. I lack health of body, and the torments are not spared. I lack release, and death is spared; and in this my confidence has been weakened.

885CVERS. 12.-- Above all my enemies. (ID.) They live worse than the pagans and the Jews, etc., as far as for whom even their acquaintance are afraid, lest all be such. (CASS.) Or, among all my enemies, or, held in greater reproach than those who are worthy of it; and to my neighbours, to kinsfolk, or to those about to believe; and to my acquaintance, to those of the household.

VERS. 13.-- They that saw me without. (HIER.) Without, Christ, that is, those who thought him a mere man. I am forgotten as one dead from the heart. (CASS.) Or, I have fallen out of their heart, like a dead man whose memory is buried with his body, of whose restoration there is despair. A vessel that is destroyed, Jesus dead is thought fit to be cast away.

VERS. 14.-- The blame of many. (AUG.) 885DThey are blamed, etc., as far as not any man. Round about. In that while they assembled together. (CASS.) Of errors, etc., as far as that is, by the appetite of temporal things.

VERS. 16.-- My lots. (ID.) Or, the times of life. (AUG.) Because we live or die when thou wilt: therefore deliver. Although the order of election is with thee, just and hidden, yet I, etc., as far as which, without merits, chooses whom it will.

VERS. 17.-- Illumine. (CASS.) Make thy good will manifest upon me, that as they despair of the dying, so they may have confidence in the rising. (AUG.) Illumine. Let it appear who belongs to thee, since now there is confusion; whence elsewhere: Distinguish my cause (Psal. XLI); yet 886Alest he seem to justify himself, he adds: Save me in mercy, not in my own justice.

VERS. 18.-- I have called upon. (ID.) Thou callest upon God when thou callest him into thyself, and when thou invitest him into the house of thy heart.

VERS. 19.-- Let them be made dumb. (CASS.) Which here are talkative, while they do not fear the judgment. Dumb in punishments, in hell.

Which speak. He fitly sets iniquity over against the just man.

In pride and in abuse. (CASS.) Because the creature is against the Creator, and by a perverse use of the benefits of God, who, besides all else, came for their sake.

VERS. 20.-- How great. (CASS.) Which are the goods of God against the evils aforesaid, and they lighten those very evils. (AUG.) Seeing these things and marvelling, the Prophet cries out, etc., as far as but in the world to come it will lie open.

886B--VERS. 21. From the disturbance. (AUG.) That he may now suffer no human disturbance, even those who are now in tribulation, entering with the mind to the face of God, are not troubled. Thou shalt protect. (CASS.) Lest the promise only of what is to come should trouble them, he adds this: thou shalt protect, that they be not harmed.

VERS. 22.-- Blessed. (ID.) As if to say, what more? He concludes the fullness of the benefit with praise, comparing it to his own feebleness. And it is the Prophet that speaks, or the faithful people. He hath made wonderful. (AUG.) The Spirit being sent, he filled the whole world, etc., as far as whence: Thy name is ointment poured out. [Vulg. Ct 1:2 has oil, not ointment, and no verb: "oil poured out is thy name"] (CASS.) Or else, God the Father made his mercy wonderful, etc., as far as according to that saying: He rested in the heart of the earth.

VERS. 23.-- I said in my excess. (AUG.) A figure of our fear, etc., as far as: Therefore thou hast heard the voice of my 886Cprayer. (AUG.) In the excess of my mind. Either, his mind being caught up, he saw a height from which he feels himself cast very far off: or, he went out from reason by fearing. From the face of thy eyes. If I were in thy face, etc., as far as but I accused my own heart.

VERS. 24.-- O love the Lord, all ye, etc. (CASS.) An oratorical or hortatory conclusion, for the obtaining of the things aforesaid. (AUG.) Having experienced the things aforesaid, he now exhorts us; as if to say: I was in tribulation, I feared, I cried out, I was not confounded: so you also. His saints, whose part it is to love God, because they do not love the world, nor the things that are in the world; the friend of this world is set down as the enemy of God. Learn therefore not to love the world, that thou mayest learn to love God: turn away, that thou mayest be converted; pour out, that thou mayest be filled. The Lord will require, etc. Even here sometimes, 886Dif he did this to none, the divine providence would not seem to be watchful, if to all, the divine patience would not be preserved.

Abundantly to them that do. Those who do not quickly repent.

Pride. For every vice, because it is the root of all.

VERS. 25.-- Do ye manfully, etc. The force of the whole psalm, that the frailty of the flesh may not fear so many evils of the world.

PSALMUS XXXI.

Intellectus David. (AUG.) Psalmus de gratia qua Christiani sumus, ut ait Apostolus (Rom. IV). Incipit ergo per indulgentiam hic psalmus contra vitium hominum agens, qui peccata nesciunt vel defendunt, et merita jactant. (CASS.) Contra vitium ergo hominum 887Ahic psalmus opponitur, etc., usque ad in quo stantes confirmat.

VERS. 1.-- Beati quorum remissae sunt, etc. (AUG.) Non in quibus non invenit peccatum, sed quibus remitit. Iniquitates. Dicit fomitem peccati, scilicet concupiscibilitatem, etc., usque ad sed ut peccatum ultra non sit. (HIERON.) Iniquitates, ante fidem et baptismum: peccatum, post fidem et baptismum.

VERS. 2.-- Beatus vir. (HIERON.) Cui remittit Deus, non enim per se. Tegit, ne in judicio reveletur; et sic non imputabitur ad poenam. Non est dolus qui se accusat: corde tenet quod ore fatetur hic.

Beatus: quia olim non confitens Deo, veni in peccatum, dum clamarem, si quid boni egi.

VERS. 3.-- Tacui. (AUG.) Qui non vult confiteri 887Bpeccata, laborat sine causa in defensione peccatorum: in quo cum et jactet merita, amplius deficit fortitudo. (CASS.) Beatus cui non imputavit. Aliis, qui gravia habent, Deus imputat; aliis per misericordiam non imputat, etsi habent aliqua, his scilicet qui non justos se praedicant, cum sint mali, sed se agnoscentes satisfaciunt, modo hoc profiteor, sed olim: Quoniam tacui, etc. (AUG.) Vel, tacui, voce peccatum, dum clamarem tota die: dum poena peccati, vel interior excaecatio ostenderet me peccatorem, vel dum prava vita me tacente clamaret, si quid boni egi.

Dum clamarem tota die, etc. Etsi non sit sibi conscius quis, non tamen justus: quia delicta quis intelligit? Unde: Est justus qui perit in justitia sua. Et Apostolus: Nihil mihi conscius sum, etc.

887CVERS. 4.-- Configitur spina. (CASS.) Spina, quae totum corpus erigit, id est, superbia. (AUG.) Item aerumna, etc., usque ad: in manibus temulenti.

VERS. 5.-- Delictum meum. Diapsalma. Confessio, unde venia, sicut supra de rectione inveteratio. Feci cognitum. (CASS.) Dixi enim prius, etc., usque ad et Deus audit.

VERS. 6.-- Pro hac orabit. (ID.) Diapsalma. poenitudinem commendans, omnibus sanctis dicit communem; quam variae sectae respuunt, contra quas ad Deum refugit. (AUG.) Pro hac. Inde orat omnis sanctus, quia dimisisti, aliter non esset sanctus. Tempore, etc. Tempus est gratiae, lex premens, convincens reos, coegit clamare, gratia sanat. Verumtamen in diluvio, etc. (AUG.) Licet sanctus oret, 887Detc., usque ad sanctus orabit, dicens: Tu es refugium. Ad eum. Deum, mutat enim personam ut saepe. Non appropiant qui dicunt fatum facit peccare, vel fortuna, quae omnia regit, vel gens tenebrarum, quae Deo rebellat.

VERS. 8.-- Intellectum tibi dabo. (ID.) Diapsalma. Respondetur poenitenti: Intellectum tibi dabo, etc. Ecce psalmus intelligentiae, ne putetur supplicans negligi, teste Deo. Tu, erue. (CASS.) Qui promisisti, intellectum tibi dabo. Vel respondet Christus poenitenti: Laetus finis, dat Deus intellectum: unde alios adhortatur ad idem.

VERS. 9.-- Nolite fieri sicut equus et mulus, etc. (AUG.) Accepto intellectu, convertit se iste poenitens 888Aad superbos peccata defendentes: ergo vos, quos invito, etc. Equus, gentilis indomitus; mulus, Judaeus piger ad credendum. (CASS.) Equus, sine discretione sessorum; mulus, quaelibet onera accipit, etc., usque ad id est, jactantiam de viribus suis. Maxillas. Vel, maxillas quibus mandunt, id est, parcius, da victualia, ut necessitate coacti redeant. (AUG.) Vel hic confringes, et in futuro erunt multa flagella. Vel: Nolite fieri sicut equus, quia multa flagella hic et in futuro. Qui non approximant ad te. (CASS.) Sunt enim qui, si peccant carnis imbecillitate, a piis precibus non recedunt.

VERS. 10.-- Multa flagella peccatoris, etc. (AUG.) Post frenum adduntur flagella ad domandum, ne sit de illis impunitis quibus modo vaga datur licentia 888Bviae suae: sic iste supra dixit se domitum.

PSALM XXXI.

The understanding of David. [Vulg. Ps 31:1 heads the psalm with the dative, "to David himself, understanding"] (AUG.) A psalm concerning the grace by which we are Christians, as the Apostle says (Rom. IV). This psalm therefore begins with pardon, treating against the vice of men who do not know their sins or else defend them, and who boast of their merits. (CASS.) Against the vice of men, then, 887Athis psalm is set, etc., as far as he strengthens those who stand in it.

VERS. 1.-- Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, etc. (AUG.) Not those in whom he finds no sin, but those to whom he forgives it. Iniquities. He means the tinder of sin, namely concupiscence, etc., as far as but that sin may be no more. (HIERON.) Iniquities, before faith and baptism: sin, after faith and baptism.

VERS. 2.-- Blessed is the man. (HIERON.) To whom God forgives, for not of himself. He covers it, that it be not revealed in the judgment; and so it will not be imputed unto punishment. There is no guile in him that accuses himself: he holds in the heart what he confesses here with the mouth.

Blessed: because formerly, not confessing to God, I came into sin, while I cried out, if I did any good.

VERS. 3.-- I was silent. (AUG.) He who will not confess 887Bhis sins labours without cause in the defence of sins: and since in this he also boasts of his merits, his strength fails the more. (CASS.) Blessed is he to whom he hath not imputed. To some, who have grievous sins, God imputes them; to others he does not impute them, through mercy, even though they have some — namely to those who do not proclaim themselves just when they are evil, but acknowledging themselves make satisfaction. This I now profess, but formerly: Because I was silent, etc. (AUG.) Or, I was silent, as to sin with my voice, while I cried out all the day: while the penalty of sin, or an inward blinding, showed me a sinner, or while my evil life cried out, though I was silent, whether I had done any good.

While I cried out all the day, etc. Although a man be not conscious to himself of anything, yet he is not just: for who understands his offences? Whence: There is a just man that perisheth in his own justice. And the Apostle: I am conscious to myself of nothing, etc.

887CVERS. 4.-- The thorn is fastened in. (CASS.) The thorn, which lifts up the whole body, that is, pride. (AUG.) Likewise misery, etc., as far as: in the hands of a drunken man.

VERS. 5.-- My sin. Diapsalma. Confession, whence pardon, as above the growing old from governance. I have made known. (CASS.) For I said before, etc., as far as and God hears.

VERS. 6.-- For this shall he pray. (ID.) Diapsalma. Commending repentance, he says it is common to all the saints; which sundry sects reject, against whom he flees for refuge to God. (AUG.) For this. Therefore every saint prays, because thou hast forgiven, otherwise he would not be a saint. In the time, etc. It is the time of grace, the law, pressing and convicting the guilty, compelled them to cry out, grace heals. But yet in the flood, etc. (AUG.) Although the saint pray, 887Detc., as far as the saint will pray, saying: Thou art a refuge. To him. That is, to God, for he changes the person, as often. They do not draw near who say that fate makes them sin, or fortune, which rules all things, or the people of darkness, which rebels against God.

VERS. 8.-- I will give thee understanding. (ID.) Diapsalma. It is answered to the penitent: I will give thee understanding, etc. Behold a psalm of understanding, lest the suppliant be thought neglected, with God for witness. Thou, deliver. (CASS.) Thou who hast promised, I will give thee understanding. Or Christ answers the penitent: A glad end, God gives understanding: whence he exhorts others to the same.

VERS. 9.-- Become ye not as the horse and the mule, etc. (AUG.) Having received understanding, this penitent turns himself 888Ato the proud who defend their sins: therefore you, whom I invite, etc. The horse, the untamed Gentile; the mule, the Jew slow to believe. (CASS.) The horse, without discernment of its riders; the mule, takes any burdens whatever, etc., as far as that is, boasting of one's own strength. Their jaws. Or, the jaws with which they chew, that is, give victuals more sparingly, that being compelled by necessity they may return. (AUG.) Or, thou wilt break them here, and in the world to come there will be many scourges. Or: Become ye not as the horse, because there are many scourges here and in the world to come. Who come not near to thee. (CASS.) For there are those who, if they sin through the weakness of the flesh, do not withdraw from devout prayers.

VERS. 10.-- Many are the scourges of the sinner, etc. (AUG.) After the bridle, scourges are added for taming, lest he be of those unpunished ones to whom a roving licence 888Bof their own way is now given: so this man above said that he was tamed.

PSALMUS XXXII.

In finem. (CASS.) Hic propheta potentiam et facta Dei enumerat, et sic ad laudem Dei invitat; primo, justos et rectos monet laudare, quia exsultare in illo nisi laudando non possumus: rectos, inquit, decet collaudatio.

VERS. 1.-- Exsultate, etc. (AUG.) Curvus laudat Deum quando sibi bene est; blasphemat quando male: rectus semper ut Job.

VERS. 2.-- Cithara. (ID.) Ab inferiori sonat, et ex terra est, unde laudemus, id est, prosperitas et adversitas, quae ab eo sunt nobis. In psalterio. Dum attendis superiora quae tibi dedit, coelestem doctrinam. 888CPer citharam caro, per psalterium charitas intelligitur: ad quae decem praecepta legis pertinent: tria in prima tabula ad Deum, septem in secunda ad proximum.

VERS. 3.-- Cantate ei, etc. Quasi, quid plus dicam? de incarnatione specialiter laetamini. Canticum novum. (CASS.) Quia non sufficit, nisi abundet justitia vestra plus quam Scribarum et Pharisaeorum (Matth. V).

Cantate canticum novum. De incarnatione, de qua mundus exsultat, de qua Angeli cantaverunt.

VERS. 4.-- Quia rectum est. Modum laudis exposuit: nunc cur sit laudandus? Et omnia opera. (AUG.) Ne quis putet se meritis ad fidem venisse, cum in fide sint omnia opera quae diligit Deus, id est, 888Dremunerat, (ID.) quia non nisi in fidelibus operatur; unde: Fides tua te salvum fecit (Matth. X). Vel, omnia opera sunt recta, etc., usque ad quia remanet iniquus, et ideo nequior, quia justum favere sibi videt.

In fide. Quasi exterioribus, si causa justitiae fuerit fidelis, interiorem fidem adjiciet ille, quem non cognoscens timuit; unde: quis non dabit ei quae sua sunt, qui in alieno fidelis fuit? (AUG.) Fidelis est Deus dans homini quod promisit: fidelis est homo credens promittenti, ex promisso vero Deus est nobis debitor.

VERS. 5.-- Terra. (ID.) Ecclesia ubique terrarum.

VERS. 6.-- Verbo. Id est sapientia Dei Patris, 889ACoeli. Apostoli instructi sunt plene, cum eo etiam corporaliter conversando: et post, omnis virtus eorum habita roborata est spiritu Filii, per coelos firmatos congregat et consolidat in unitate fidei, spei et charitatis. Uter, Ecclesia, in qua est caro mortua. Etiam abyssos, id est, profundos tenebris vitiorum, ponit inter eos, qui sunt thesaurus, unde alios ditat sapientia. (AUG.) Terra. Coeli non indigent misericordia, etc., usque ad quod operatur. Virtus eorum. Cum inter lupos essent, etc., usque ad licentia.

VERS. 7.-- Sicut in utre. (CASS.) Ad litteram: sicut littoribus mare, claudit in Ecclesia fluctuantes populos; et in thesauris sapientiae suae ponit profundas altitudines, ut probet quis Scripturas pietatis studio inquirat.

889BVERS. 8.-- Timeat omnis terra. (ID.) Ecclesia de mari, etc., usque ad sed Dominum timeat terra. Timeat, imo commoveantur manu misericordiae a similitudine dormientis. Ab eo, quia ipse creavit: et ideo utiliter administrat, quia et a diabolo aliquid commovetur, sed quod a Deo utiliter, ideo ab eo. Commoveantur. (AUG.) Non terroribus hominum, etc., usque ad potestatem non nisi a Deo.

VERS. 9.-- Dixit et facta sunt. Creationem simul et formationem notat. Mandavit recreationem.

VERS. 10.-- Dissipat consilia. (CASS.) Ne habeant effectum consilia contra se, ut Judaeorum, et contra suos. Gentium. Dum idololatriam destruxit. Populorum. Judaeorum, quorum voluntas, etsi impleta, tamen resurrectione est reprobata. Principum. Tyrannorum 889Cvel daemonum.

VERS. 11.-- Consilium autem Domini, etc. (ID.) Incarnationis arcanum in quo consuluit homini.

Manet in aeternum. Quia ad aeternam salutem nobis obtinendam.

Cogitationes. Praedestinatio, in qua omnia reposita sunt, quae et sic permanent, ut praevisa sunt.

VERS. 12.-- Beata gens. (CASS.) Beatum dicit, qui ad cultum Dei pervenit: quod fit temporibus Christianis, in quibus gentes conversae, hi sunt justi et recti quos decet laudatio. (AUG.) Beatitudo omnis in animo, etc., usque ad beatus populus de Deo possessore.

VERS. 13.-- De coelo. (AUG.) Homine Christo. Prospexit in adventu Filii et vidit misericorditer, 889Dnon peccata, (CASS.) a quibus faciem avertit; sed vidit omnes filios hominum, id est, omnes qui ad novam vitam volunt renasci. (AUG.) Quomodo elegit? etc., usque ad inspiravit omnem bonam voluntatem.

VERS. 15.-- Finxit. (AUG.) Manu gratiae formavit. Sigillatim, singulis singula quaedam dans. (HIER.) Unde tamen unitas corporis, id est, Ecclesiae fiat. Sigillatim, id est, non ex Adam, ut quidam dicunt animam ex anima, et simul omnes cognoscit, et omnes actus earum.

VERS. 16.-- Non salvatur rex. Sic fiunt justi, sed nec facti sua virtute salvantur. Non modo spiritualia sunt a Deo, sed et exteriora. (HIER.) Nemo quidquam habet nisi ab eo, quia nec potens ut rex, nec fortis, 890Aetc., usque ad etiam si sit in multa abundantia virtutis.

VERS. 17.-- Fallax equus. (AUG.) Animal, in cujus velocitate vel virtute confiditur, figurate quaelibet amplitudo saeculi unde superbitur: sed quanto in eo altius erigeris, tanto gravius cadis. (CASS.) Vel, equus est corpus hominis quantumcunque speciosum et bene formatum, tamen fallax est ad salutem corporalem, spiritualem. (AUG.) Vel, equus mundana felicitas, quae homines vehit, et dum nimis properat, cadit equus et sessorem perdit. Equus, humana sapientia. Gigas, superbus aliquis extollens se contra Deum.

VERS. 18.-- Ecce oculi. In sua in virtute nullus salvatur, sed: Ecce unde est salus, oculi, etc. Oculi, 890Brespectus divinitatis quae proteget eos. Metuentes eum. (CASS.) Timere Dominum, et semper sperare conjuncta sunt.

VERS. 19.-- Ut eruat, etc. (ID.) Haec duo sunt vota fidelis: ut in judicio eripiatur a morte, et hic spiritualibus alatur, ubi est indigentia eorum.

VERS. 20.-- Anima nostra sustinet Dominum. Quid de praedictis sentiat, quasi conclusio.

VERS. 21.-- Quia in eo. (AUG.) Quia absentibus per fidem misit nomen suum.

Speravimus. Nos venturos ad Deum, non meritis nostris. (CASS.) Quia in eo ne quis mussitet de patientia, subjicit munus, scilicet quod laetatur hic in Domino. Et speramus in nomine Christi, quem patienter Propheta laetus venturum sustinuit: Speravimus. 890CContinuum tempus notat, quia non est fas desinere, unde semper potest anima fessa recreari.

Fiat misericordia tua, Domine, super nos, etc. Incarnationem compleri desiderat, ut perfectus possit esse. In te. Hoc dicit ideo ut omnis superstitio et pravitas excludatur.

PSALM XXXII.

Unto the end. [Vulg. Ps 32:1 heads this psalm as a psalm of David, with no such title] (CASS.) Here the prophet enumerates the power and the works of God, and so invites to the praise of God; first he admonishes the just and the upright to praise, because we cannot exult in him save by praising: praise together, he says, becomes the upright.

VERS. 1.-- Exult ye, etc. (AUG.) The crooked man praises God when it is well with him; he blasphemes when it is ill: the upright man always, like Job.

VERS. 2.-- On the harp. (ID.) It sounds from below, and is of the earth, whence we may praise, that is, prosperity and adversity, which are ours from him. On the psaltery. When thou attendest to the higher things which he has given thee, the heavenly doctrine. 888CBy the harp the flesh is understood, by the psaltery charity: to which the ten precepts of the law belong: three in the first table toward God, seven in the second toward the neighbour.

VERS. 3.-- Sing ye to him, etc. As if to say, what more shall I say? Be glad especially over the incarnation. A new canticle. (CASS.) Because it does not suffice, unless your justice abound more than that of the Scribes and Pharisees (Matth. V).

Sing ye a new canticle. Of the incarnation, over which the world exults, of which the Angels sang.

VERS. 4.-- For it is right. He has set out the manner of praise: now, why is he to be praised? And all his works. (AUG.) Lest anyone think that he has come to faith by merits, since in faith are all the works which God loves, that is, 888Drewards, (ID.) because he does not work save in the faithful; whence: Thy faith hath made thee whole (Matth. X). Or, all works are right, etc., as far as because he remains wicked, and the more wicked for this, that he sees the just man favour him.

In faith. As if in outward things, if a man has been faithful for the sake of justice, He will add inward faith, whom not knowing he feared; whence: who will not give him the things that are his own, who was faithful in another's? (AUG.) God is faithful in giving to man what he promised: man is faithful in believing him that promises, and by the promise God is our debtor.

VERS. 5.-- The earth. (ID.) The Church everywhere upon the earth.

VERS. 6.-- By the word. That is, by the wisdom of God the Father. 889AThe heavens. The Apostles were fully instructed, by conversing with him even bodily: and afterward all their power, once had, was strengthened by the Spirit of the Son, through the heavens made firm he gathers and consolidates men into the unity of faith, hope and charity. The bottle, the Church, in which is dead flesh. Even the depths, that is, those deep in the darkness of vices, he sets among those who are a treasure, whence wisdom enriches others. (AUG.) The earth. The heavens do not need mercy, etc., as far as which he works. Their power. Since they were among wolves, etc., as far as licence.

VERS. 7.-- As in a bottle. (CASS.) According to the letter: as he shuts in the sea by its shores, so he shuts within the Church the wavering peoples; and in the treasures of his wisdom he places the deep heights, that he may prove who searches the Scriptures with a zeal for godliness.

889BVERS. 8.-- Let all the earth fear. (ID.) The Church out of the sea, etc., as far as but let the earth fear the Lord. Let it fear — nay rather, let them be moved by the hand of mercy out of the likeness of one asleep. By him, because he himself created it: and therefore he governs it profitably, because something is moved by the devil also, but what is moved by God is moved profitably, therefore by him. Let them be moved. (AUG.) Not by the terrors of men, etc., as far as power not save from God.

VERS. 9.-- He spoke and they were made. He notes creation and formation together. He commanded the re-creation.

VERS. 10.-- He scatters the counsels. (CASS.) That the counsels against himself, as those of the Jews, and against his own, may have no effect. Of the Gentiles. When he destroyed idolatry. Of the peoples. Of the Jews, whose will, though fulfilled, was yet reproved by the resurrection. Of the princes. Of tyrants 889Cor of demons.

VERS. 11.-- But the counsel of the Lord, etc. (ID.) The secret of the incarnation, in which he took counsel for man.

Standeth for ever. Because it is unto the obtaining of eternal salvation for us.

The thoughts. Predestination, in which all things are laid up, which also so abide as they were foreseen.

VERS. 12.-- Blessed is the nation. (CASS.) He calls him blessed who has come to the worship of God: which happens in Christian times, in which the Gentiles are converted, these are the just and the upright whom praise becomes. (AUG.) All blessedness is in the mind, etc., as far as blessed is the people that has God for its possessor.

VERS. 13.-- From heaven. (AUG.) From the man Christ. He looked forth in the coming of the Son and saw mercifully, 889Dnot the sins, (CASS.) from which he turns away his face; but he saw all the children of men, that is, all who wish to be born again unto a new life. (AUG.) How did he choose? etc., as far as he inspired every good will.

VERS. 15.-- He hath fashioned. (AUG.) He formed them with the hand of grace. Severally, giving to single ones certain single things. (HIER.) Whence nevertheless the unity of the body, that is, of the Church, may come to be. Severally, that is, not out of Adam, as some say that a soul comes from a soul, and he knows them all at once, and all their acts.

VERS. 16.-- The king is not saved. Thus are the just made, but neither, once made, are they saved by their own strength. Not only spiritual things are from God, but outward things also. (HIER.) No one has anything except from him, because neither the powerful, like a king, nor the strong, 890Aetc., as far as even if he be in great abundance of strength.

VERS. 17.-- The horse is deceitful. (AUG.) An animal in whose swiftness or strength trust is put, figuratively, any greatness of the world whereof men are proud: but the higher thou art lifted up upon it, the heavier thou fallest. (CASS.) Or, the horse is the body of a man, however comely and well formed, yet it is deceitful for bodily health, and for spiritual. (AUG.) Or, the horse is worldly happiness, which carries men, and while it hurries too much, the horse falls and destroys its rider. The horse, human wisdom. A giant, someone proud, lifting himself up against God.

VERS. 18.-- Behold the eyes. In his own in strength no one is saved, but: Behold whence salvation is, the eyes, etc. The eyes, 890Bthe regard of the godhead, which will protect them. Them that fear him. (CASS.) To fear the Lord and always to hope are joined together.

VERS. 19.-- That he may deliver, etc. (ID.) These are the two desires of the faithful man: that in the judgment he may be snatched from death, and that here he may be fed with spiritual things, where there is want of them.

VERS. 20.-- Our soul waiteth for the Lord. What he thinks of the things aforesaid, as it were a conclusion.

VERS. 21.-- For in him. (AUG.) Because to those who were absent he sent his name through faith.

We have hoped. That we shall come to God, not by our own merits. (CASS.) Because in him — lest anyone murmur about patience — he adds the gift, namely that he is glad here in the Lord. And we hope in the name of Christ, whom the Prophet, glad and patient, awaited as one to come: We have hoped. 890CIt notes a continuous time, because it is not lawful to leave off, whence the weary soul can always be refreshed.

Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, etc. He desires that the incarnation be accomplished, that he may be able to be perfect. In thee. He says this to the end that every superstition and depravity be shut out.

PSALMUS XXXIII.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus David. (AUG.) Loquitur Christus, et in eo Christianus: docet humilitatem, dum commendat corpus et sanguinem. Cum immutavit vultum Christus, id est, sacrificium, coram Judaeis, qui regnum patris sui David sunt, juxta illud: Et dabit illi Dominus sedem David, Ecclesia est regnum Patris.

890DVERS. 2.-- Benedicam. (CASS.) Psalmus secundus per alphabetum imperfectum, etc., usque ad glorificatur cum ipso.

VERS. 3.-- In Domino laudabitur anima mea. (ID.) Sua enim laus est praedicatio Domini sui, ut bonus famulus de bona fama Domini sui glorietur. Mansueti. Non docti, non jejunantes, quia sunt superbi: sed mansueti, quia temperantiam habent omnium rerum. Mansueti, non de sua intelligentia superbientes; non jugum Dei, indomitorum more, ferentes.

VERS. 4-6.-- Magnificate Dominum. Spiritualis gratia non vult sola facere quod multis proficit; unde vocat alios: Magnificate ut invitatos traheret, 891Adicit, quae inde bona sibi: Exquisivi Dominum. Ex omnibus. Non possunt particulatim dici quanta impetravit qui non aliud quam Deum quaesivit. Accedite. (CASS.) Jam particulatim de novo vultu admonet sanctos. Quasi, Magnificate: et si in primis in jucundum accedite. Vel, Magnificate, et quo ordine? ecce: Accedite per fidem. (AUG.) Accedite fide inhaerendo, et duobus pedibus geminae charitatis currendo. (CASS.) Praemissis laudibus, ad communionem hortatur. Non confundantur. (AUG.) Quidquid hic fiat justo, non erubescit, quia semper superior apud Deum: superbus vero in adversis erubescit, quia ad Deum non accessit.

VERS. 7.-- Pauper. (CASS.) Iste spiritualis hic est, quia accedit et illuminatur, nec erubescet; quia, 891Bquando clamat, liberatur ab omnibus angustiis saeculi in obitu, dum jam transit ad Deum.

VERS. 8.-- Immittet Angelum. Accedite, et sicut iste pauper clamavit et exauditus est, eodem modo immittet Angelum, etc. (AUG.) Immittet Angelum. Alii interpretes sic transtulerunt: Circumdat Angelus Domini gyro timentes eum. Angelus de coelo, vel homo, qui est minister voluntatis Dei. Mendosi codices habent. Immittet Angelum Dominus.

VERS. 9.-- Gustate et videte. Hic aperte de sacramento quod ferebat manibus. Gustate carnem et sanguinem Christi. Suavis est Dominus. (ID.) Et dulcis: quia est vita sumenti, pellens omnes molestias in futuro, id est: Sperate per hoc vitam aeternam. (CASS.) Et quia Deus est vita, caro quam sibi 891Cunivit est vivificatrix.

VERS. 10.-- Omnes sancti ejus. (CASS.) Nullus, licet bene meritus, ab hoc desistet, non securitatem praesumat. Quoniam. (AUG.) Pascebat Dominus contemnentem se, et deseret timentem. Promittit autem non superflua, sed necessaria. Non est inopia. Quia etiam in praesenti habent quantum exigit natura.

VERS. 11.-- Divites eguerunt et esurierunt. (CASS.) Quia fidem non habent. Esurierunt, quia corpore Domini non satiantur. Quid enim habent, qui Deum non habent? Vel, divites eguerunt, id est, carebunt summo bono, licet esuriant, id est, desiderent. Sed toto studio quaerentes sine imminutione habebunt bonum, quod est omne bonum.

891DVERS. 12.-- Venite, filii, audite me. Diapsalmus. Tractatis Ecclesiae sacramentis, admonet eos qui extra sunt, qui prima rudimenta fidei capiunt, ne nomen timoris horreatur addit: Docebo vos, filios timorem Domini, ut rem utilem.

(CASS.) Jam et incipientes monet a quibus abstineant.

VERS. 13.-- Dies videre bonos. Quia omnes fatentur se velle.

VERS. 14.-- Prohibe. (ID.) Nota quod prius cohiberi linguam dicit, quoniam, cum loqui volumus, ante commovemus labia, quae mox sequuntur linguae motus. Prohibe qui vitam cupis. Ecce quomodo debeant timere.

892AVERS. 15.-- Diverte a malo. (CASS.) Hoc culpam vitat, etc., usque ad aliter in futuro non capietur.

VERS. 16.-- Oculi Domini, etc. (ID.) De retributionibus bonorum et malorum, ne in periculis justus aliqua dubietate mollescat.

Oculi Domini. Nec ex infirmitate tua diffidas, quia oculi.

In preces. (ID.) Celeritas audiendi, cum in ipsis auditor habitat.

VERS. 17.-- Memoriam. (AUG.) Ut nec mentio, etc., usque ad quae admiserunt.

VERS. 19.-- Juxta est Dominus. Liberavit: nam pronus est ad hoc, quia juxta est; vel, est allusio ad clamorem.

VERS. 20.-- Multae tribulationes justorum. Sicut 892Bet in Novo Testamento, juxta est, et salvabit, quod necesse est, quia multae tribulationes. (CASS.) Multae; a diabolo, ab invidis hominibus, et a se. Liberabit. (AUG.) Non corporaliter, sed dando eis patientiam: vel, liberabit spiritualiter.

VERS. 21.-- Ossa. (ID.) Virtutes. Et unum, etc., ut nec patientia pereat.

VERS. 22.-- Pessima. (ID.) Non modo mala, etsi in divitiis, et odoribus, et lamentis hominum finiatur, tamen pessima est, quia in peccatis ad infernum trahit.

Qui oderunt. Quorum? Non omnium, quia peccatores; sed eorum qui oderunt justum, qui justificat, id est, Christum, per quem qui non reconciliatur perit: sed redimet animas, secundum quas est mors 892Cpessima.

PSALM XXXIII.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of David. [Vulg. Ps 33:1 heads the psalm with the dative alone, "to David," and names no psalm] (AUG.) Christ speaks, and in him the Christian: he teaches humility, while he commends the body and the blood. When he changed the countenance — Christ, that is, the sacrifice — before the Jews, who are the kingdom of his own father David, according to that saying: And the Lord shall give unto him the seat of David, the Church is the kingdom of the Father.

890DVERS. 2.-- I will bless. (CASS.) The second psalm through an imperfect alphabet, etc., as far as he is glorified together with him.

VERS. 3.-- In the Lord shall my soul be praised. (ID.) For his own praise is the preaching of his Lord, as a good servant glories in the good repute of his lord. The meek. Not the learned, not those who fast, because they are proud: but the meek, because they have temperance in all things. The meek, not being proud of their own understanding; not bearing the yoke of God after the manner of the untamed.

VERS. 4-6.-- O magnify the Lord. Spiritual grace does not wish to do alone what profits many; whence it calls others: Magnify, that it might draw those invited, 891Ait tells what goods came to it thereby: I sought the Lord. Out of all. It cannot be told piecemeal how great things he obtained who sought nothing other than God. Come ye. (CASS.) Now piecemeal he admonishes the saints concerning the new countenance. As if to say, Magnify: and if among the first, come ye into what is pleasant. Or, Magnify, and in what order? behold: Come ye by faith. (AUG.) Come ye by cleaving with faith, and by running with the two feet of a twin charity. (CASS.) The praises being set first, he exhorts to communion. Let them not be confounded. (AUG.) Whatever happens here to the just man, he does not blush, because he is always the higher with God: but the proud man blushes in adversities, because he has not drawn near to God.

VERS. 7.-- The poor man. (CASS.) This one is here the spiritual man, because he draws near and is enlightened, and shall not blush; because, 891Bwhen he cries out, he is freed from all the straits of the world at his death, when he now passes over to God.

VERS. 8.-- He shall send in an Angel. Come ye, [Vulg. Ps 33:8 has the nominative and no such object: "the angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him"] and as this poor man cried out and was heard, in the same way he shall send in an Angel, etc. (AUG.) He shall send in an Angel. Other interpreters have rendered it thus: The Angel of the Lord surroundeth in a ring them that fear him. An Angel from heaven, or a man, who is a minister of the will of God. Faulty codices have it. The Lord shall send in an Angel.

VERS. 9.-- Taste and see. Here openly of the sacrament which he bore in his hands. Taste the flesh and blood of Christ. The Lord is sweet. (ID.) And delightful: because he is life to him that takes him, driving away all troubles in the world to come, that is: Hope through this for eternal life. (CASS.) And because God is life, the flesh which he 891Cunited to himself is life-giving.

VERS. 10.-- All ye his saints. (CASS.) No one, however well deserving, shall leave off from this, let him not presume upon security. For. (AUG.) The Lord was feeding him that despised him, and he will forsake him that fears him. But he promises not superfluous things, but necessary ones. There is no want. Because even in the present they have as much as nature requires.

VERS. 11.-- The rich have wanted and have suffered hunger. (CASS.) Because they have not faith. They have suffered hunger, because they are not filled with the body of the Lord. For what have they who have not God? Or, the rich have wanted, that is, they shall lack the highest good, although they hunger, that is, desire. But those who seek with their whole zeal shall have without diminution the good which is every good.

891DVERS. 12.-- Come, children, hear me. Diapsalmus. The sacraments of the Church having been treated, he admonishes those who are outside, who take the first rudiments of faith, lest the name of fear be shuddered at, he adds: I will teach you, the sons, the fear of the Lord, as a useful thing.

(CASS.) Now he warns beginners also from what things they should abstain.

VERS. 13.-- To see good days. Because all confess that they wish it.

VERS. 14.-- Keep. (ID.) Note that he says the tongue is to be restrained first, since, when we wish to speak, we first move the lips, which the motions of the tongue soon follow. Keep thou who desirest life. Behold how they ought to fear.

892AVERS. 15.-- Turn away from evil. (CASS.) This avoids fault, etc., as far as otherwise he will not be received in the world to come.

VERS. 16.-- The eyes of the Lord, etc. (ID.) Of the retributions of the good and of the evil, lest in dangers the just man grow soft with any doubt.

The eyes of the Lord. Nor shouldst thou distrust out of thy weakness, because the eyes.

Unto the prayers. (ID.) The swiftness of hearing, since the hearer dwells in them.

VERS. 17.-- The memory. (AUG.) That not even the mention, etc., as far as which they have committed.

VERS. 19.-- The Lord is nigh. He delivered: for he is inclined to this, because he is nigh; or, there is an allusion to the crying out.

VERS. 20.-- Many are the tribulations of the just. As 892Balso in the New Testament, he is nigh, and he will save, which is necessary, because many are the tribulations. (CASS.) Many; from the devil, from envious men, and from oneself. He will deliver. (AUG.) Not bodily, but by giving them patience: or, he will deliver spiritually.

VERS. 21.-- The bones. (ID.) The virtues. And one, etc., that not even patience may perish.

VERS. 22.-- Most evil. (ID.) Not merely evil, although it end amid riches and perfumes and the lamentations of men, yet it is most evil, because in sins it drags down to hell.

That hate. Whose? Not of all, because they are sinners; but of those who hate the just one, who justifies, that is, Christ, through whom he that is not reconciled perishes: but he will redeem the souls, in respect of which the death is 892Cmost evil.

PSALMUS XXXIV.

VERS. 1.-- Judica, Domine. (CASS.) Incipit ab oratione pro utraque parte pugnae, cum commemoratione culpae, et erat unicuique quod meretur, ostendens quanta tulit ab adversariis, et poenas quae eis pro iniquitate restituuntur.

VERS. 2.-- Arma et scutum (HIER.) Armis hostes percutit, scuto nos protegit. Scutum alibi dicit: bonae voluntatis; arma nos sumus, quia ut nos ab eo, ita ipse armatur de nobis. (AUG.) Vel, anima Christi, quae hostes debellavit, quae nihil agit nisi Deus pugnet de ea.

Arma apprehende. Fac me habere arma, doctrinam, miracula. Scutum. Constantiam.

892DExsurge. Fac uti acceptis.

VERS. 3.-- Effunde. Me, qui modo sum in obscuro, clarifica ita evidenter, ut concludas et convincas, ne habeant quid oblatrent: et dicas animae ita, ut omnes sciant quod salus ei; contra hoc, quod illi: Non est salus ipsi in Deo ejus (Psal.III.) Frameam. (AUG.) Framea est anima justi. Abundantibus justis, framea effunditur, dum vita coruscat: unde concluditur hostis non habens de nobis male loqui. (ID.) Prophetia est non optatio, vel hoc de convertendis.

VERS 5.-- Fiant. (ID.) Prophetia: vel eo modo, quo Deus facit, justo judicio, non amaro animo. Tanquam pulvis ante faciem venti. (CASS.) A Deo 893Adissoluti, ut nec invicem cohaereant, quos divina gratia non humectat.

VERS. 8.-- Veniat illi laqueus quem ignorat. (CASS.) Vel in bono, laqueus veritatis, quam peccator ignorat. Et captio quam abscondit. Id est, abscondita mors, scilicet Christi. Apprehendat eos. Ne scilicet suis sceleribus relinquantur. Et in laqueum cadat. Bonum quo a malis cohibeantur. In ipsum. Id est, ex ipsa morte. In ipsum. (AUG.) Non in alium, sed in eum, quem tetenderunt. Nemo enim malus, qui non prius sibi noceat.

VERS. 9.-- Anima autem mea exsultabit. (CAS.) Praemissa spe boni et gaudio, enarrat quam maligne erga benignum agat. In Domino. (AUG.) Quo nihil suavius: nec defecit, qui omnia fecit: ipsum ergo 893Bpete, et in illo habebis omnia.

VERS. 10.-- Omnia ossa mea dicent. Carnales non habent verbum laudis et confessionis, quia infirma apud te penitus silent; sed fortia, te magnum laudant et tremunt. (ID.) Omnia ossa. Omnis fortitudo mentis, quia hoc alius dicere nequit, scilicet: o Domine, quis? etc., quasi nullus, quia ipse solus eripuit: Inopem de manu. (CASS., AUG.) Genus humanum inops, quia mortale; egenum, quia in sudore quaerit panem; pauper, quia, de pura sapientia dejectus, tenuem et umbratilem habet rationem.

VERS. 11.-- Surgentes testes iniqui. (CASS.) Dictis calamitatibus hominis, ne ipse Christus alienus ab eis videatur, passionem suam exponit. Quae ignorabam. (AUG.) Peccata sunt, etc., usque ad sed non 893Ccommittendo.

VERS. 12.-- Retribuebant. (ID.) Cum ego attulissem fecunditatem, ipsi retribuebant sterilitatem: ego vitam, ipsi mortem retribuerunt; ego honores, ipsi contumelias; ego medicinam, ipsi vulnera. Sterilitatem. In ficu maledixit Dominus, ubi cum quaereret fructum non invenit, sed folia: sic in Synagoga verba non facta; unde: Qui praedicas non furandum, furaris.

VERS. 13.-- Cilicio. (ID.) Caro, cilicium, propter similitudinem carnis peccati. Oratio mea. (CASS.) Ut dixit: Pax vestra ad vos revertetur (Matth. X); ita ejus oratio, Judaeis non accepta, ad eum rediit. In sinu meo. (AUG.) Sinus est secretum, in quo orare jubemur. 893DSecretum vero Christi, divinitas, ad quam orat humanitas.

VERS. 14.-- Quasi proximum et quasi fratrem, etc. Casus pro casu. Quasi: de proximo et fratre nostro, ita mihi complacebam, id est, de eorum affinitate gaudebam, qui me insequebantur. Ecce gratia pro odio, beneficium pro laesione. (AUG.) Quasi proximum. Hoc dicere convenit propinquanti ad Deum, et gaudenti, qui placet Deo, quasi fratri et proximo.

Quasi lugens. (CASS.) Alii interpretes, quasi lugens mater filium, incurvabar super eos. Quasi lugens. Cum haec omnia facerem, tamen nolebant converti; et tamen cum nollent converti, sic humiliabar, id est, dolebam, sicut pater lugens filium.

894AVERS. 15.-- Et adversum, etc. Cum pie contristor, Judaei impie laetantur.

VERS. 16.-- Dissipati sunt. (CASS.) Dissoluti, visis miraculis in passione, nec tamen prae duritia compuncti.

Vel, dissipati per totum orbem: nec tamen compuncti sunt, id est, poenituerunt. Vel, dissipati, id est, divisi: alii dicunt quod bonus est, alii non.

Tentaverunt me. (AUG.) Quae capiti in cruce facta, corpori ubique fiunt. Frenduerunt. Mos saevitiae, quando ratio deficit, dentibus frendet: et quod vult, tacens ostendit. In oratione finit haec:

VERS. 17.-- Domine, quando respicies. (ID.) Quando videbimus vindictam de eis qui nobis insultant. Unicam meam. (CASS.) Unica est anima Christi, 894Bquae sola immunis a peccato.

VERS. 18.-- Confitebor tibi. (AUG.) Jam de fructu praemittit confessionem totius Ecclesiae: inde precatur, cum commemoratione culpae, confusionem persecutorum et exsultationem fidelium.

VERS. 19.-- Non supergaudeant. (ID.) Repetit de passione, ut de poena eorum addat. Annuunt. (CASS.) Quoniam vicissim se tacitis nutibus admonent ad decipiendum et tentandum.

VERS. 20.-- Loquentes. (CASS.) Id est, dum loquerentur pacifice. In iracundia. Id est, exitialiter. Cogitat enim quis dolum qui non vult occidere: sed isti sic cogitabant, quia interficere volebant.

VERS. 21.-- Et dilataverunt. (ID.) Prius annuentes, cogitantes dolos dilataverunt os suum, libera 894Cet aperta voce mortem inclamantes: Crucifige, crucifige.

VERS. 22.-- Vidisti, Domine. (ID.) Hoc dicitur, quando aliquid in memoriam revocare volumus: vidisti quoniam crudeles, ne sileas, ne differas dare sententiam.

VERS. 23.-- Intende. (ID.) Reddendo nomen super omne nomen, ut ego intensus immerito. In causam meam. (Ibid.) Poena similis sceleris, sed non causa: martyrem enim non facit poena, sed causa.

VERS. 24.-- Tuam, Domine Deus. (ID.) Quae in se est, vel quam ei dedit. Non super gaudeant. (CASS.) Magis defleant, quam gaudeant implesse mala.

894DVERS. 25.-- Devoramus. (AUG.) Devorantur incorporati.

VERS. 26.-- Erubescant et revereantur simul. (CASS.) Potius erubescant in clarificatione resurrectionis, et revereantur, id est, timeant poenas. Erubescant. Qui erubescit, actus suos propria existimatione damnat: sed potest erubescere qui non habet reverentiam; ideo addit: reverentiam, ut conversionem notet. Reverentia est timor Domini cum amore. Induantur confusione et reverentia. Pudore, quasi cilicio poenitentiae et veste lugubri. Pudor, contra audaciam quam habuerunt furentes; reverentia, contra impudentiam falsitatis, ut his illa curent.

VERS. 27.-- Exsultent et laetentur. (ID.) In In spe magna fidelium finis, sicut alii de passione. Exsultent et laetentur. Illi dicunt, euge animae suae quae 895Alaetitia fugit, isti non suae animae, sed vota ad Deum convertunt, et in ejus laudibus, non in se, suam laetitiam ponunt, quae est perpetua.

VERS. 28.-- Et lingua mea meditabitur justitiam tuam. (AUG.) Hoc fiat, et mei praedicatores ex studio nuntiabunt te justum, qui promissa implesti, et omnia universaliter in quibus laudandus. (CASS.) Lingua mea. Lingua ejus meditata est justitiam, quando Novum Testamentum populus praedicavit.

PSALM XXXIV.

VERS. 1.-- Judge, O Lord. (CASS.) He begins from a prayer for both sides of the battle, with a recalling of the fault, and there was for each one what he deserves, showing how much he bore from his adversaries, and the punishments that are repaid to them for their iniquity.

VERS. 2.-- Arms and shield (HIER.) With arms he strikes the enemies, with the shield he protects us. The shield he calls elsewhere: of good will; the arms are we ourselves, because as we are armed by him, so he himself is armed from us. (AUG.) Or, the soul of Christ, which vanquished the enemies, which does nothing unless God fight on its behalf.

Take hold of arms. Make me to have arms, teaching, miracles. Shield. Steadfastness.

892DArise. Make me to use the things received.

VERS. 3.-- Pour out. Me, who am now in obscurity, make clear so evidently that thou mayest shut them in and convict them, that they may not have what to bark at: and speak to my soul in such wise that all may know that salvation is hers; against this, which they say: There is no salvation for him in his God (Psal.III.) The sword. (AUG.) The sword is the soul of the just man. When the just abound, the sword is poured out, while life flashes forth: whence the enemy is shut in, having nothing to speak ill of us. (ID.) It is a prophecy, not a wish, or this concerns those who are to be converted.

VERS 5.-- Let them be. (ID.) A prophecy: or in that manner in which God does it, by just judgment, not with a bitter mind. As dust before the face of the wind. (CASS.) Loosed 893Aby God, so that they do not even cleave to one another, they whom divine grace does not moisten.

VERS. 8.-- Let the snare which he knoweth not come upon him. (CASS.) Or in a good sense, the snare of truth, which the sinner knows not. And the net which he hath hidden. That is, the hidden death, namely of Christ. Let it lay hold on them. [Vulg. apprehendat eum, "lay hold on him," singular where Migne prints the plural (Ps 34:8)] Namely, that they be not left to their own crimes. And let him fall into the snare. A good one, by which they may be restrained from evils. Into that very one. That is, out of that very death. Into that very one. (AUG.) Not into another, but into the one which they stretched out. For there is no evil man who does not first hurt himself.

VERS. 9.-- But my soul shall rejoice. (CAS.) Having set forth the hope of good and the joy, he relates how malignantly it acts toward the kind one. In the Lord. (AUG.) Than whom nothing is sweeter: nor has he failed, who made all things: seek him therefore, 893Band in him thou shalt have all things.

VERS. 10.-- All my bones shall say. Carnal men have not the word of praise and confession, because things weak before thee are utterly silent; but strong things praise thee as great and tremble. (ID.) All the bones. All the strength of the mind, because another cannot say this, namely: O Lord, who? etc., as if none, because he alone delivered: The helpless out of the hand. (CASS., AUG.) The human race is helpless, because mortal; needy, because it seeks bread in sweat; poor, because, cast down from pure wisdom, it has a thin and shadowy reason.

VERS. 11.-- Unjust witnesses rising up. (CASS.) The calamities of man having been told, lest Christ himself should seem a stranger to them, he sets forth his passion. Which I knew not. (AUG.) They are sins, etc., as far as but not 893Cby committing them.

VERS. 12.-- They repaid. (ID.) When I had brought fruitfulness, they repaid barrenness: I life, they repaid death; I honors, they insults; I medicine, they wounds. Barrenness. In the fig tree the Lord cursed, where, when he sought fruit, he found none, but leaves: so in the Synagogue, words and not deeds; whence: Thou that preachest that men should not steal, thou stealest.

VERS. 13.-- With haircloth. (ID.) The flesh, a haircloth, on account of the likeness of the flesh of sin. My prayer. (CASS.) As he said: Your peace shall return to you (Matth. X); so his prayer, not accepted by the Jews, returned to him. In my bosom. (AUG.) The bosom is a secret place, in which we are commanded to pray. 893DBut the secret place of Christ is his divinity, to which his humanity prays.

VERS. 14.-- As a neighbor and as a brother, etc. Case for case. As it were: as concerning our neighbor and brother, so I was well pleased, that is, I rejoiced in the kinship of those who were persecuting me. Behold grace for hatred, a benefit for injury. (AUG.) As a neighbor. It befits one drawing near to God to say this, and one rejoicing, who pleases God, as to a brother and a neighbor.

As one mourning. (CASS.) Other translators, as a mother mourning her son, I was bowed down over them. As one mourning. Though I did all these things, yet they would not be converted; and yet, though they would not be converted, so was I humbled, that is, I grieved, as a father mourning a son.

894AVERS. 15.-- And against, etc. When I am piously saddened, the Jews impiously rejoice.

VERS. 16.-- They were scattered. (CASS.) Loosed, when the miracles had been seen at the passion, and yet not, for their hardness, pricked to the heart.
