Or, scattered through the whole world: nor yet were they pricked to the heart, that is, did not repent. Or, scattered, that is, divided: some say that he is good, others not.

They tempted me. (AUG.) The things done to the head on the cross are done everywhere to the body. They gnashed. It is the way of savagery, when reason fails, to gnash with the teeth: and what it wills, it shows in silence. In prayer he ends these things:

VERS. 17.-- Lord, when wilt thou look. (ID.) When shall we see vengeance upon those who insult us. My only one. (CASS.) The only one is the soul of Christ, 894Bwhich alone is free from sin.

VERS. 18.-- I will confess to thee. (AUG.) Now from the fruit he sends before the confession of the whole Church: thence he prays, with a recalling of the fault, for the confounding of the persecutors and the exultation of the faithful.

VERS. 19.-- Let them not rejoice over me. (ID.) He repeats concerning the passion, that he may add concerning their punishment. They wink. (CASS.) Because by turns they warn one another with silent nods, to deceive and to tempt.

VERS. 20.-- Speaking. (CASS.) That is, while they were speaking peaceably. In wrath. That is, destructively. For a man plots guile who does not wish to kill: but these were plotting thus, because they wished to slay.

VERS. 21.-- And they have opened wide. (ID.) First winking, then plotting guiles, they opened wide their mouth, crying out death with free 894Cand open voice: Crucify, crucify.

VERS. 22.-- Thou hast seen, O Lord. (ID.) This is said when we wish to call something back to memory: thou hast seen that they are cruel, be not silent, delay not to give sentence.

VERS. 23.-- Attend. (ID.) By restoring the name above every name, that I, undeservedly stretched out. In my cause. (Ibid.) The punishment of a like crime, but not the cause: for it is not the punishment that makes a martyr, but the cause.

VERS. 24.-- According to thy justice, O Lord God. (ID.) Which is in himself, or which he gave to him. Let them not rejoice over me. super gaudeant (CASS.) Let them rather weep than rejoice at having fulfilled evils.

894DVERS. 25.-- We devour. (AUG.) Those who are incorporated are devoured.

VERS. 26.-- Let them blush and stand in awe together. (CASS.) Let them rather blush at the glorification of the resurrection, and stand in awe, that is, fear the punishments. Let them blush. He who blushes condemns his own acts by his own estimation: but he can blush who has not reverence; therefore he adds: reverence, that he may mark conversion. Reverence is the fear of the Lord with love. Let them be clothed with confusion and reverence. With shame, as with the haircloth of penitence and a mourning garment. Shame, against the boldness which they had in their raging; reverence, against the shamelessness of falsehood, that by these they may cure those.

VERS. 27.-- Let them rejoice and be glad. (ID.) In great hope is the end of the faithful, as others are concerning the passion. Let them rejoice and be glad. Those say, Well done, to their own soul, from which 895Agladness flees, these not to their own soul, but they turn their vows to God, and place their gladness in his praises, not in themselves, which gladness is perpetual.

VERS. 28.-- And my tongue shall meditate thy justice. (AUG.) Let this be done, and my preachers out of zeal will announce thee just, who hast fulfilled thy promises, and all things universally in which thou art to be praised. (CASS.) My tongue. His tongue meditated justice, when it preached the New Testament to the peoples.

PSALMUS XXXV.

VERS. 1.-- In finem sermo. (CASS.) Agit hic de errore quorumdam, etc., usque ad qui tamen imminet omnibus.

Non est timor ante oculos: quia dolus, id est, quia 895Bcarni obedit non Deo, cum ratio aliud insinuet, quod videat Deus etsi non alius: vel, quod videt ipse injustus, a Deo scit, ut inveniatur ab ipso eodem quod iniquitas sua est habenda odio apud Deum et omnes homines.

(ID.) Primo, asserit mala esse ex homine.

VERS. 2.-- Dixit injustus, etc. (CASS.) Duo sunt genera peccantium: quia vel infirmitate carnis non possunt sequi jussa legis; vel blasphemi qui libere peccant, quasi Deus non curet hoc; unde est: Dixit, etc. (AUG.) Descriptio iniqui viri. Non est timor Dei. (CAS.) Quia dolus noluit studere legi, qua per ignorantiam excusetur.

VERS. 3.-- Quoniam dolose. (AUG.) Multi inquirunt iniquitates suas, etc., usque ad nec excusantur de 895Cignorantia.

VERS. 4.-- Verba. (ID). Ostendit iniquitatem, etc., usque ad ut bene ageret.

VERS. 5.-- In cubili. Id est, in corde, in quo sibi complacent opera mala; et hoc est, astitit omni viae, cum studio et mora: invenit quidem, et scivit esse mala, sed tamen non odivit. Noluit. (AUG.) Non quod non potuit; perniciosius agit contra seipsum qui quod potest non vult. Sunt enim quaedam quae, etsi volunt, non intelligere homines possunt, ut: In principio erat Verbum, et ut tamen bene agerent, intelligere possunt. In cubili suo. (ID.) Id est, corde, ubi praecepit Dominus orare clauso ostio, etc., usque ad sapientia, scilicet carnis, quae est inimica Deo.

VERS. 6.-- Domine, in coelo. (Cass.) Bona ex Deo 895Dper misericordiam. Quasi dicat: Mala sunt ex homine, sed bona ex misericordia. O Domine, in his, qui coelum sunt, id est, arcana scientes, est misericordia tua: et quod ipsi sunt nubes, est a te. (AUG.) Vel in coelo, id est, misericordia, etc., usque ad nuntiat vero missa veritate sua.

Usque ad nubes. Id est praedicatores, per quos tonat Deus nuntiando, coruscat miraculis, pluit doctrinis. Qui sunt etiam montes, quos prius sol luce vestit, quae post, de eis et si non ab eis, ad infima vallium descendit: ministri enim sunt doctrinae, sed Deus illuminat.

VERS. 7.-- Judicia tua. (AUG.) Quod horum misereris, hos excaecas; nulli sunt penitus scrutabilia: 896Atamen utrosque salvas, hos corporaliter tantum, illos et spiritualiter, in quo magna misericordia.

VERS. 8.-- Homines, etc. Etiam temporalia a Deo esse ostendit.

VERS. 9.-- Inebriabuntur. (ID.) Non potest res exprimi, sed per hanc similitudinem innuit, ut pleni mentem perdant, ne suos jam agnoscant patres, filios, caeterosque amicos. Vel, tunc in re ebrii, qui modo sperant. Torrente. Quasi: Impetus erit gratiae et misericordiae ad inebriandos. (ID.) Torrente. Non ut transitoria sit beatitudo, sed copiosa. Vel, voluntas tua in homine omnia rumpit obstacula. Vel, sapientia Christi torrens, quia subita et rapida.

VERS. 10.-- Quoniam apud te est fons vitae. (CAS.) Apud te, Christe, est fons, id est, initium omnis boni; 896Bet in tuo lumine, quia per ejus praedicationem videmus lumen Patris et Spiritus sancti, et ideo praetende, ut in hoc saeculo tutius eatur.

PSALM XXXV.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end, a word. [Vulg. Ps 35:1 In finem. Servo Domini ipsi David., "to the servant of the Lord, to David himself"] (CASS.) He treats here of the error of certain men, etc., as far as which nevertheless hangs over all.

There is no fear before the eyes: because there is guile, that is, because 895Bhe obeys the flesh and not God, though reason suggests otherwise, namely that God sees even if no other does: or, that the unjust man himself, what he sees, knows from God, so that it may be found by that same one that his own iniquity is to be held in hatred with God and with all men.

(ID.) First, he asserts that evils are from man.

VERS. 2.-- The unjust hath said, etc. (CASS.) There are two kinds of sinners: because either through the weakness of the flesh they cannot follow the commands of the law; or they are blasphemers who sin freely, as though God cared not for this; whence it is: He hath said, etc. (AUG.) A description of the wicked man. There is no fear of God. (CAS.) Because guile was unwilling to study the law, by which it might be excused through ignorance.

VERS. 3.-- For he hath done deceitfully. (AUG.) Many search out their iniquities, etc., as far as nor are they excused for 895Cignorance.

VERS. 4.-- The words. (ID). He shows the iniquity, etc., as far as that he might act well.

VERS. 5.-- On his bed. That is, in the heart, in which evil works please them; and this is, he hath set himself in every way, with zeal and with lingering: he found indeed, and knew them to be evil, but nevertheless he did not hate them. He was unwilling. (AUG.) Not that he could not; he acts more perniciously against himself who does not will what he can. For there are certain things which men cannot understand even if they will, as: In the beginning was the Word, and yet, that they might act well, they can understand. On his own bed. (ID.) That is, in the heart, where the Lord commanded us to pray with the door shut, etc., as far as wisdom, namely of the flesh, which is an enemy to God.

VERS. 6.-- O Lord, in heaven. (Cass.) Good things are from God 895Dthrough mercy. As if he should say: Evils are from man, but goods from mercy. O Lord, in those who are heaven, that is, who know hidden things, is thy mercy: and that they themselves are clouds, is from thee. (AUG.) Or in heaven, that is, mercy, etc., as far as but announces by sending forth his truth.

Even to the clouds. That is, the preachers, through whom God thunders in announcing, flashes in miracles, rains in teachings. Who are also mountains, whom the sun first clothes with light, which afterward, from them and yet not by them, descends to the lowest of the valleys: for they are ministers of teaching, but God enlightens.

VERS. 7.-- Thy judgments. (AUG.) That thou hast mercy on these, and blindest those; they are utterly searchable to none: 896Ayet thou savest both, these bodily only, those spiritually as well, wherein is great mercy.

VERS. 8.-- Men, etc. He shows that temporal things also are from God.

VERS. 9.-- They shall be inebriated. (ID.) The thing cannot be expressed, but by this likeness he intimates that, being full, they lose their mind, so that they no longer recognize their own fathers, sons, and other friends. Or, then they are drunk in reality, who now hope. With the torrent. As if: There shall be a rush of grace and mercy to inebriate them. (ID.) With the torrent. Not that the beatitude should be passing, but plentiful. Or, thy will breaks all obstacles in man. Or, the wisdom of Christ is a torrent, because it is sudden and swift.

VERS. 10.-- For with thee is the fountain of life. (CAS.) With thee, O Christ, is the fountain, that is, the beginning of every good; 896Band in thy light, because through his preaching we see the light of the Father and of the Holy Spirit, and therefore hold forth, that in this world one may go more safely.

PSALMUS XXXVI.

(CASS.) Psalmus tertius, alphabeti imperfectio: totus de correctione morum.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus David. Psalmus hic est quasi vestis Christi, quae totum corpus ejus operiat praeceptis, et protegat ab adversis, et quasi sinu consilii foveat. Potio contra illos qui murmurant de flore malorum, labore bonorum, quasi omnia casu agantur, ut mundo, spreto Deo, adhaereant. Monet igitur Ecclesia ne quis malignantes imitetur, sed quidquid boni speratur, a Domino postuletur, qui profutura et 896Caeterna dat.

VERS. 2.-- Olera herbarum. (AUG.) Modo est hiems, etc., usque ad quia nondum apparuit quod erimus.

(AUG., CASS.) Olera non hortorum, sed herbarum, id est, vilissima, quae per agros sponte nascuntur. Fenum, nobiles, qui facile proficiunt; olera, mediocres: sed et illi cito arescunt, et hi decidunt.

VERS. 8.-- Desine. (AUG.) Ira subita, furor diutinus; sed utraque deserenda, per quae peccatur. (CASS.) Hoc dicitur ei qui adhuc infirmus, etc., usque ad faciendo ad tempus floret.

VERS. 10.-- Et adhuc pusillum, etc. (AUG.) Post istam vitam parvam, etc., usque ad nec vermem conscientiae corrodentis sentiebat.

896DVERS. 12.-- Observabit, etc. (CASS.) Dicto, quod boni non debent malos aemulari, etc., usque ad conatur occidere.

VERS. 13.-- Dominus autem, etc. (ID.) Sic et nos videntes perituros, irrideamus et praesentes, grandis consolatio.

VERS. 14.-- Gladium, etc. (ID.) Si neque blanditiis neque minis aget, poena aggreditur. Si nec sic proficit, insidiatur dolis, quando bene loquendo mala intendit.

VERS. 16.-- Melius est, etc. (ID.) Paulo ante de malitia et sustinentia: hic de divitiis et paupertate.

VERS. 17.-- Confirmat autem, etc. (AUG.) Maxime per exemplum crucis suae. Crux enim Christi finita 897Aest in poena, et manet in gloria: a locis enim suppliciorum transit ad frontes imperatorum.

VERS. 18.-- In diebus famis. (CASS.) Id est, in hac vita, etc., usque ad quanto plus elevantur, tanto citius ut fumus deficient.

VERS. 21.-- Mutuabitur. (ID.) Audit verbum Dei, non reddit operibus. Et non solvet. Id est, non reddit operibus quod auditu percepit. Miseretur et retribuet, etc. De his quae accipit, etc., usque ad sequitur largitas.

VERS. 23.-- Gressus. (ID.) Qui per se tortuosi, quia in peccatis nati. Viam ejus. (AUG.) Via terrae non dura, sed latronibus plena est: vel, viam hominis volet Deus.

VERS. 25.-- Junior fui, etc. (ID.) Tractat hic 897Bjustum nunquam deseri, praemia bonorum et poenas malorum commiscens cum interjectis adhortationibus. (AUG.) Ecclesia quasi unus homo loquitur, quae in primis temporibus junior fuit, in fine saeculi senuit, in senecta uberi, quia per omnes gentes dilatata. (ID.) Junior fui. Puer in Abel; in prophetis et patriarchis juvenis; tempore martyrum quasi senex; in fine mundi quasi in decrepita aetate. (CASS.) Junior, quando initia legis in Adam suscepi; senui, cum in honorabili aetate ad ultimum suscepi Christum.

VERS. 26.-- Tota die miseretur. Vel, de eleemosyna dicit, quae a misericordia incipit, et post manum aperit: vel, de spiritualibus.

VERS. 28.-- Amat judicium et non derelinquet 897Csanctos suos. (CASS.) Ideo: et tu ama, ut bonis tuis gaudeas.

VERS. 31.-- Supplantabuntur. (ID.) Supplantare, est plantis foveas insidiarum praetendere.

VERS. 33.-- Dominus autem (ID.) Consolatio justi. In manibus ejus. (AUG.) Job terra tradita est in manus impii, id est, caro: sed animam invictam educit Deus, ne cedat.

Cum judicabitur. (CASS.) Vel, non permittit damnari justum cum judicabitur ille ab impio; vel, illi impio, scilicet ad malum ejus.

VERS. 34.-- Et exaltabit. (ID.) Quia non nisi exaltatus coelestem potest habitare. Videbis (ID.) Quod modo credis; dupliciter notat gaudia bonorum; 897Dprimo, quia tunc sentient in quantis sint jucunditatibus. Inde, quia videbunt poenas iniquorum, unde gratior est beatitudo liberatis ab hujusmodi malo.

VERS. 35.-- Vidi impium superexaltatum. (ID.) Contra hoc, etc., usque ad cui religato locus nocendi est ablatus.

VERS. 36.-- Transivi. Mundum, meliori conversatione ad Deum tendens: et vidi nihil posse, cum nihil omnia sint in quibus homo gloriatur. Quaesivi. In memoriam reduxi: quia boni tunc magis dolent de impiis, quod ab eis sunt separati, cum in melius immutantur. Locus. Eorum mundus est, qui et dissolvetur. Transivi. (AUG.) Transit, qui praesentiam non 898Aattendit, sed novissima, etc., usque ad cui haec virtus est, loco beati ponitur.

VERS. 37.-- Reliquiae. Bona quae post hanc vitam relinquentur, vel memoria bona post obitum.

VERS. 39.-- Salus autem justorum a Domino. Haec omnia justis, totum tamen a Deo, et colligit summatim.

PSALM XXXVI.

(CASS.) The third psalm, an imperfection of the alphabet: wholly concerning the correction of morals.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of David. [Vulg. Ps 36:1 Psalmus ipsi David., "a psalm for David himself"] This psalm is as it were the garment of Christ, which covers his whole body with precepts, and protects it from adversities, and cherishes it as in the bosom of counsel. It is a draught against those who murmur at the flowering of the wicked and the toil of the good, as though all things were done by chance, so that, spurning God, they cleave to the world. The Church therefore admonishes that no one imitate the malignant, but that whatever good is hoped for be sought from the Lord, who gives things profitable and 896Ceternal.

VERS. 2.-- The herbs of the grasses. (AUG.) It is now winter, etc., as far as because it hath not yet appeared what we shall be.

(AUG., CASS.) Herbs not of gardens, but of grasses, that is, the meanest, which spring up of themselves through the fields. Hay, the noble, who prosper easily; herbs, the middling: but both those quickly wither and these fall away.

VERS. 8.-- Cease. (AUG.) Anger is sudden, fury lasting; but both are to be forsaken, through which men sin. (CASS.) This is said to him who is still weak, etc., as far as by doing it he flourishes for a time.

VERS. 10.-- And yet a little while, etc. (AUG.) After this short life, etc., as far as nor did he feel the worm of a gnawing conscience.

896DVERS. 12.-- He shall watch, etc. (CASS.) It having been said that the good ought not to emulate the wicked, etc., as far as he strives to slay.

VERS. 13.-- But the Lord, etc. (ID.) So let us also, seeing that they are to perish, laugh even at those who are present, it is a great consolation.

VERS. 14.-- The sword, etc. (ID.) If he prevail neither by flatteries nor by threats, he proceeds to punishment. If he does not prosper so either, he lies in wait with guiles, when by speaking well he intends evil.

VERS. 16.-- Better is, etc. (ID.) A little before, concerning malice and endurance: here, concerning riches and poverty.

VERS. 17.-- But the Lord confirmeth, etc. (AUG.) Chiefly by the example of his cross. For the cross of Christ was ended 897Ain punishment, and abides in glory: for from the places of tortures it has passed to the brows of emperors.

VERS. 18.-- In the days of famine. (CASS.) That is, in this life, etc., as far as by how much the more they are lifted up, by so much the more quickly shall they fail like smoke.

VERS. 21.-- He shall borrow. (ID.) He hears the word of God, he does not repay it in works. And shall not pay. That is, he does not repay in works what he received by hearing. He sheweth mercy and shall repay, etc. Concerning those things which he receives, etc., as far as bounty follows.

VERS. 23.-- The steps. (ID.) Which of themselves are crooked, because we are born in sins. His way. (AUG.) The way of the earth is not hard, but is full of robbers: or, God shall will the way of man.

VERS. 25.-- I have been young, etc. (ID.) He treats here 897Bthat the just man is never forsaken, mingling the rewards of the good and the punishments of the wicked with exhortations set between. (AUG.) The Church speaks as one man, which in the first times was younger, at the end of the world grew old, in a plentiful old age, because she was spread through all nations. (ID.) I have been young. A boy in Abel; in the prophets and patriarchs a young man; in the time of the martyrs as it were an old man; at the end of the world as it were in decrepit age. (CASS.) Young, when I received the beginnings of the law in Adam; I grew old, when in an honorable age I received Christ at the last.

VERS. 26.-- All the day he sheweth mercy. Or, he speaks of almsgiving, which begins from mercy, and afterward opens the hand: or, of spiritual things.

VERS. 28.-- He loveth judgment and will not forsake 897Chis saints. (CASS.) Therefore: do thou also love, that thou mayest rejoice in thy good things.

VERS. 31.-- They shall be supplanted. (ID.) To supplant is to spread pits of ambush before the soles of the feet.

VERS. 33.-- But the Lord (ID.) The consolation of the just man. In his hands. (AUG.) Job's earth was delivered into the hands of the impious, that is, his flesh: but God brings forth his soul unconquered, that it may not yield.

When he shall be judged. (CASS.) Or, he does not permit the just man to be condemned when he is judged by the impious; or, for that impious man, namely to his own harm.

VERS. 34.-- And he shall exalt. (ID.) Because none but one exalted can dwell in heaven. Thou shalt see (ID.) What thou now believest; in two ways he marks the joys of the good; 897Dfirst, because then they shall feel in how great delights they are. Thence, because they shall see the punishments of the wicked, whence the beatitude of those set free from such evil is the more welcome.

VERS. 35.-- I have seen the wicked highly exalted. (ID.) Against this, etc., as far as from whom, being bound, the place of harming has been taken away.

VERS. 36.-- I passed by. The world, striving toward God by a better manner of life: and I saw that it could do nothing, since all those things are nothing in which man glories. I sought. I called back to memory: because the good then grieve the more over the impious, that they are separated from them, when they are changed for the better. The place. Their world is what shall also be dissolved. I passed by. (AUG.) He passes by who attends not to the present, 898Abut to the last things, etc., as far as he who has this virtue is set in the place of the blessed.

VERS. 37.-- The remnants. The good things which shall be left after this life, or a good memory after death.

VERS. 39.-- But the salvation of the just is from the Lord. All these things are for the just, yet the whole is from God, and he gathers it up summarily.

PSALMUS XXXVII.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus David in rememoratione de sabbato. (AUG., CASS.) Ut peccatum, quod prorsus fugere nequimus, semper in memoria habeamus, ut nos ab eo saltem temperemus, hic poenitentiae inducit multis modis cruciatum, ita ut ipsum Job videatur proponere tironibus in exemplum, ut cruciatus amplectantur, minores quidem meritis, quibus ab 898Baeterna poena liberamur. (AUG.) Sabbatum est requies aeternitatis, quam perdere formidat peccati conscius, et habere desiderat graviter afflictus.

VERS. 2.-- Domine, ne in furore tuo arguas me. Primum, captat misericordiam per poenas summatim. Arguas me. (CASS.) Ut poena sit a misericordia ad correctionem, non ab ira ad ultionem.

VERS. 3.-- Sagittae. (AUG.) Vindictae quas minabaris Adae, dicens: In quacumque die comederitis, morte moriemini. Quia comedit, infixae sunt et nobis; et non ad horam, sed confirmasti, ut sit usque in finem saeculi. (AUG., CASS.) Quoniam sagittae. Numerat quae patitur, etc., usque ad quod leviter potest laedi.

VERS. 4.-- Non est sanitas, etc. (AUG., CASS.) Ab 898Cinstantia vindictae in Adam exertae. Vel, timore futurae irae terretur, sic ut non sit sanitas in carne: more verecundi, qui futuris flagellis jam affligitur. Vel, a facie irae, quia praevidi faciem irae, id est, quod minaris, ne videam iram. Non est pax. Gravis dolor ad interiora pervenit a facie peccatorum, quia sanctus super poenas corporis affligitur peccatis, putans se graviora mereri. Non est sanitas. (CASS.) Captat hic misericordiam a potestate judicis, et ab infirma persona. Non est pax ossibus. Accipit ossa pro carne. Et exponit quod dixerat, aliud addens: scilicet a facie peccatorum.

VERS. 5.-- Supergressae sunt. (AUG.) Vel sustulerunt, id est, quia iniquitas elevavit caput superbi contra Deum, Deus gravavit, ut fasce, et compressit 898Dne jam erigatur.

VERS. 6.-- Putruerunt. (CASS.) Narratio, in qua enumerantur miseriae. Cicatrices meae. (AUG.) Vel livores mei; alia littera, id est, peccata mea. Non est sanus qui cicatrices habet, quae putruerunt et fetent: ut ab eis aversi adoremus sabbatum, et gemamus: Currentes cum sponso post odorem unguentorum.

VERS. 7.-- Miser factus sum. (ID.) Dicto qualiliter iniquitates supergressae, dicit quomodo aggravatae.

VERS. 8.-- Quoniam lumbi. (CASS., AUG.) Non solum mea infirmitate pecco, sed et diabolus, qui corpus affligit et animam fatigat vanis imaginationibus; et per hoc non est iterum sanitas, sicut et 899Asupra per sagittas. (AUG.) Lumbi, vel, anima impleta est, etc., usque ad cum videbimus veritatem ut est.

VERS. 9.-- Rugiebam a gemitu. (CASS., AUG.) Gemitus corde, rugitus voce: a similitudine bestiarum, quibus se comparat: ut fortior gemitus ostendatur: virtus patientiae quod in gemitum, non in verba pro rumpit.

VERS. 10.-- Ante te omne. (CASS.) Tale est, quod meretur esse ante te, quia pro peccatis petit. (AUG.) et ideo non est absconditus, sed auditus gemitus, quia pius est pro liberatione animae: alios non curat Deus. Desiderium meum. (ID.) Est oratio, nec unquam desinit orare qui non desinit amare: charitas clamor est.

899BVERS. 11.-- Cor meum conturbatum est. (CASS.) Exponit dolores animi, quia virtus patientiae reliquit. Conturbatum, quia mens succubuit passioni suae. Lumen, id est, ratio nuper turbata, quam non habet secum pro ingentibus molestiis.

VERS. 12.-- Amici mei et proximi. (ID.) Et pro his duobus solatiis gaudet humanitas, sed huic sunt cumulus passionis. (AUG.) Amici mei. Hactenus confessus est quae patitur a se intus, etc., usque ad et haec etiam cuique versanti inter homines convenit.

VERS. 14.-- Tanquam surdus non audiebant, et sicut mutus non aperiens os suum. (CASS.) Ad iniquitatem consulentium non aperiens, etc., usque ad contra 899Cdolores corporis rugiebat.

VERS. 16.-- Quoniam in te, Domine, speravi, etc. (ID.) Quia inter tot mala speravit in Domino, affirmat se audiendum in commemoratione emendationis. Speravi. Salutaris medicina malis, sperare, non deficere. In te, Domine, qui mutas tristia in laeta.

VERS. 17.-- Quia dixi: Ne quando supergaudeant mihi inimici mei. (AUG.) Item caput de infirmis pedibus, cum sit in coelo. Non deserit illud quod habet in terra. Dum commoventur pedes mei. (CASS.) Si commoventur aliquando humana infirmitate, irrident impii unde dolent pii.

VERS. 18.-- Paratus sum. (ID.) Sciens me deliquisse. 899DDolor, quia deliquit: impius se defendit; justus contra se irascitur.

VERS. 19.-- Quoniam iniquitatem meam. (ID.) Duo modi perfectae poenitentiae, confessio et emendatio, per fletus, eleemosynas, et hujusmodi.

VERS. 20.-- Vivunt. (AUG.) Fruuntur mundo, firmati in mundanis, et quotidie plures fiunt.

VERS. 22.-- Ne derelinquas. (ID.) De praeteritis absolutus, cum actione gratiarum auctorem salutis profitens Deum, laetus exclamat ne jam relinquatur. (CASS.) Quia gravior offensio post veniam. (AUG.) Exsultativa conclusio, ut certa spes sit imitantibus.

Ne discesseris a me. Quomodo ergo supra: Ut quid me dereliquisti? Vox est veteris hominis qui 900Acum eo crucifixus, hic autem in persona propria loquitur.

PSALM XXXVII.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of David, in the remembrance of the sabbath. (AUG., CASS.) That we may always have in memory the sin which we are utterly unable to flee, so that we may at least restrain ourselves from it, he here brings in the torment of penitence in many ways, so that he seems to set forth Job himself as an example to recruits, that they may embrace torments, less indeed than their deserts, by which we are freed from 898Beternal punishment. (AUG.) The sabbath is the rest of eternity, which he who is conscious of sin dreads to lose, and he who is grievously afflicted desires to have.

VERS. 2.-- Lord, rebuke me not in thy indignation. First, he seeks mercy through punishments summarily. Rebuke me. (CASS.) That the punishment may be from mercy unto correction, not from anger unto vengeance.

VERS. 3.-- The arrows. (AUG.) The vengeances which thou wast threatening to Adam, saying: In whatsoever day ye shall eat, ye shall die the death. [Vulg. Gn 2:17 in quocumque enim die comederis ex eo, morte morieris, "in what day soever thou shalt eat of it, thou shalt die the death," singular where Migne prints the plural] Because he ate, they are fixed in us also; and not for an hour, but thou hast confirmed them, that it may be even to the end of the world. (AUG., CASS.) For the arrows. He numbers the things he suffers, etc., as far as that which can lightly be hurt.

VERS. 4.-- There is no health, etc. (AUG., CASS.) From 898Cthe pressing of the vengeance put forth upon Adam. Or, he is terrified by the fear of the wrath to come, so that there is no health in his flesh: after the manner of a modest man, who is already afflicted by the scourges to come. Or, from the face of wrath, because I have foreseen the face of wrath, that is, what thou threatenest, that I may not see the wrath. There is no peace. A grievous sorrow reaches to the inward parts from the face of sins, because the holy man is afflicted with sins beyond the punishments of the body, thinking that he deserves heavier things. There is no health. (CASS.) Here he seeks mercy from the power of the judge, and from the weakness of the person. There is no peace in the bones. He takes the bones for the flesh. And he expounds what he had said, adding another thing: namely, from the face of sins.

VERS. 5.-- They are gone over. (AUG.) Or, they have lifted up, that is, because iniquity lifted up the head of the proud man against God, God weighed him down, as with a bundle, and pressed him 898Dthat he should not now be raised up.

VERS. 6.-- They are putrefied. (CASS.) A narration, in which the miseries are enumerated. My scars. (AUG.) Or my bruises; another reading, that is, my sins. He is not sound who has scars, which have putrefied and stink: that, turned away from them, we may adore the sabbath, and groan: Running with the bridegroom after the odor of the ointments.

VERS. 7.-- I am become miserable. (ID.) It having been said in what manner qualiliter the iniquities are gone over, he says how they are made heavy.

VERS. 8.-- For my loins. (CASS., AUG.) Not only do I sin by my own weakness, but also the devil, who afflicts the body and wearies the soul with empty imaginings; and through this there is again no health, as also 899Aabove through the arrows. (AUG.) The loins, or, the soul is filled, etc., as far as when we shall see the truth as it is.

VERS. 9.-- I roared from the groaning. (CASS., AUG.) The groaning is of the heart, the roaring of the voice: from a likeness of the beasts, to which he compares himself: that a stronger groaning may be shown: the virtue of patience, which breaks forth into a groan, not into words.

VERS. 10.-- Before thee is all. (CASS.) Such is it as deserves to be before thee, because he asks for sins. (AUG.) and therefore it is not hidden, but the groaning is heard, because it is godly, for the liberation of the soul: others God cares not for. My desire. (ID.) It is prayer, nor does he ever cease to pray who ceases not to love: charity is a cry.

899BVERS. 11.-- My heart is troubled. (CASS.) He expounds the sorrows of the mind, because the virtue of patience has left him. Troubled, because the mind has succumbed to its own suffering. The light, that is, reason lately disturbed, which he has not with him because of the huge troubles.

VERS. 12.-- My friends and my neighbors. (ID.) And in these two comforts human nature rejoices, but to this man they are a heaping up of suffering. (AUG.) My friends. Thus far he has confessed the things he suffers from himself within, etc., as far as and these things also befit anyone living among men.

VERS. 14.-- As one deaf they heard not [Vulg. Ps 37:14 audiebam, "I heard not"], and as one dumb not opening his mouth. (CASS.) Not opening it to the iniquity of those who counselled him, etc., as far as against 899Cthe sorrows of the body he roared.

VERS. 16.-- For in thee, O Lord, have I hoped, etc. (ID.) Because amid so many evils he hoped in the Lord, he affirms that he is to be heard in the recalling of his amendment. I have hoped. A saving medicine in evils, to hope, not to fail. In thee, O Lord, who changest sad things into glad.

VERS. 17.-- For I said: Lest at any time my enemies should rejoice over me. (AUG.) Likewise the head concerning the weak feet, though it be in heaven. It does not forsake that which it has on earth. While my feet are moved. (CASS.) If they are at any time moved by human weakness, the impious laugh at that whereof the godly grieve.

VERS. 18.-- I am ready. (ID.) Knowing that I have offended. 899DSorrow, because he has offended: the impious man defends himself; the just man is angry against himself.

VERS. 19.-- For my iniquity. (ID.) The two modes of perfect penitence, confession and amendment, through weeping, alms, and the like.

VERS. 20.-- They live. (AUG.) They enjoy the world, being established in worldly things, and daily they become more.

VERS. 22.-- Forsake me not. (ID.) Absolved from things past, professing God with thanksgiving to be the author of salvation, he joyfully cries out that he may not now be left. (CASS.) Because the offense is heavier after pardon. (AUG.) An exultant conclusion, that there may be a sure hope for those who imitate.

Depart not from me. How then is it said above: Why hast thou forsaken me? It is the voice of the old man who was crucified 900Awith him, but here he speaks in his own person.

PSALMUS XXXVIII.

VERS. 1.-- In finem. (AUG.) Quia hic est de aeterna beatitudine, pro qua jucundum est transilire, etsi grave sit carni. Docet autem inde de mundo ad Deum transire. Transilitor autem de bona opinione semper contrahit invidiam iniquorum et calumniam: unde deliberat inter malos tacere, ne quid dicat male. Idithun. (ID.) Transiliens eos, id est, remanentes in mundo. (CASS.) In primis de continentia linguae inter blasphemos et calumniosos: unde et optat noscere finem, ubi haec non sunt.

VERS. 2.-- Dixi: Custodiam vias meas, etc. (AUG., CASS.) Monet hic psalmus inter blasphemos, 900Biniquos, et calumniosos linguae continentiam, certamina, rixas, comprimere: hoc enim silentium multum est utile. (CASS.) Dixi: in corde deliberavi: ubi sapientes prius deliberant, quam loquantur. Vias (HIER.) Id est, actiones et verba. Ut non delinquam per fatua, vel otiosa.

In lingua. (AUG.) Non frustra est lingua in verbo: quia facile labitur. Posui ori meo. Postquam transivi terrenas delectationes, etc., usque ad docens nos cavere hoc non imitari. (CASS.) Posui usque eo quod obmutui, etc., usque ad qui causam contentionis quaerit.

VERS. 3.-- A bonis, et dolor meus, etc. (ID.) Annuntiandis, etc., usque ad id est, transilientium, locutus sum. (AUG.) Quod est, malis invitus silui, 900Cetc., usque ad et si actus transilientis aliquid sunt.

VERS. 4.-- Concaluit cor meum intra me. (AUG.) Si damnabitur piger, etc., usque ad fit avarus dispensator.

VERS 5.-- Locutus sum. (ID.) Non auditori erudiendo, sed exauditori Deo, a quo intus audior. Et numerum dierum meorum. (HIER.) Numerus dierum, qui modo sunt, non est vere transilienti; haerenti autem esse videtur.

VERS. 6.-- Ecce mensurabiles. (CASS.) Quasi, noto fine, et diebus qui sunt, attendit ad haec quae reliquit, et comparat invicem. Et substantia, etc. (AUG.) Qui videt nihil esse hanc substantiam, etc., usque ad quae ante te erit.

900DVERS. 7.-- Verum tamen. (CASS.) Videns adventum Christi, redit ad infirmitatem quam inter virtutes habet. (AUG.) Magna sunt quae diximus et credimus; sed tamen non est illud aeternum, sed universa vanitas. Et pro mutabilitate desiderans aeternam, exprobrat humanae vitae, cui subest, quod dicit. Ne quis putet sanctos a tentationibus alienos. Vel, licet mensurabiles dies, licet substantia, nihil: tamen universa vanitas est in rationali creatura, quae secundum diversos universam appetit creaturam. Verumtamen. Quamvis aeternis inhio, etc., usque ad cujus conversatio in coelis est. Omnis homo. (AUG.) Si malus, in saecularibus vanus est; si bonus, cum Christo volenti esse, vana est vita.

901A-- Verumtamen. (AUG.) Diapsalmus. Quomodo omnes sub vanitate et casu; et inde opponit se exspectare Dominum, et petit liberari. In imagine pertransit. (ID.) Quamvis ita studeat vanitati, etc., usque ad quia cum miseria et labore appetit terrena. Thesaurizat. (ID.) De caeteris vitiis elegit Propheta avaritiam, ad ostendendum quod intendit: ipsa enim est radix omnium malorum.

VERS. 8.-- Exspectatio. (ID.) Primi adventus, vel secundi, etc., usque ad non in sacculis nostris.

VERS. 9.-- Ab omnibus iniquitatibus meis erue me. (CASS.) Non solum ab eis, ne revolvat in ea quae transilivi, sed ab omnibus omnino. Imperfectus enim est homo: quia non accepit quod optat; perfectus, qui scit hoc ipsum quod sibi deficit.

901BVERS. 10.-- Obmutui. (ID.) Habitus opprobrio, etc., usque ad et necesse est, quia defeci.

Amove a me plagas tuas. (AUG.) Quia tu fecisti me, noli exterminare; tantum cede ut producar; non ut comminuar

VERS. 11.-- Increpationibus propter iniquitatem. Quibus humanum genus increpuisti: quod tamen ex merito nostro, propter iniquitates nostras increpuisti, quae sunt ad correctionem; aliter enim iniquitas incorrecta permaneret. Corripuisti hominem. (AUG.) Est dolor informis qui non emendat: formatus, qui eruditionibus formam praestat. Et talis dolor est praeceptum, id est, vicem et imaginem praecepti habet.

VERS. 12.-- Et tabescere fecisti sicut araneam animam. (ID.) Siccatam ab amore virtutum, et cognitionis. 901CSicut aranea texit inanem telam in congregatione temporalium. Vel, dum extrahit a se iniquitatem sicut aranea, egestione viscerum moritur. (CASS.) Vel, aranea tenue corpus habet, nec in terra, sed in alto stat, telas egestione viscerum texit: sic anima conversi et afflicti terrena deserit, subtiles operationes timore Dei tabeficata perficit. Verumtamen. (AUG., CASS.) Licet increpetur, licet tabefiant, tamen humana infirmitate variis rebus confunditur, nisi qui Deum pura mente contemplatur.

VERS. 14.-- Exaudi orationem. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. Iter mala saeculi petit sibi adesse et peccata dimitti, ut prospero fine exeat. (ID.) Sed quia ego ista non peto, etc., usque ad movendam misericordiam.

901DNe sileas, quoniam advena ego sum. (AUG.) Jam apud te, sed adhuc inquilinus: quia hinc transiturus ad aeterna, ubi non ero inquilinus. Advena apud te. (CASS.) Non in diaboli civitate, sed in tua receptus, de Babylonia ad Jerusalem translatus. Sicut omnes patres. Ne quis ab hac conditione putetur exceptus. Advena. Meum regnum pro tuo desero. Peregrinus. Adhuc non eligens mihi sedem hic.

Remitte mihi. (ID.) Hic sibi petit dimitti, ut certus dijudicium perveniat.

PSALM XXXVIII.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end. (AUG.) Because here it is concerning eternal blessedness, for which it is delightful to leap across, even if it be hard to the flesh. And thence he teaches to pass over from the world to God. But the leaper always draws upon himself, from his good repute, the envy of the wicked and their slander: whence he resolves to keep silence among the wicked, lest he say anything amiss. Idithun. (ID.) Leaping over them, that is, those who remain in the world. (CASS.) First, concerning the restraint of the tongue among blasphemers and slanderers: whence he also desires to know the end, where these things are not.

VERS. 2.-- I said: I will take heed to my ways, etc. (AUG., CASS.) This psalm admonishes, among blasphemers, 900Bthe wicked, and slanderers, restraint of the tongue, and the repressing of contentions and brawls: for this silence is very useful. (CASS.) I said: I deliberated in my heart: where wise men deliberate before they speak. Ways (HIER.) That is, actions and words. That I may not offend by foolish or idle things.

In my tongue. (AUG.) Not without cause is the tongue in the word: because it easily slips. I have set to my mouth. After I passed over earthly delights, etc., as far as teaching us to beware not to imitate this. (CASS.) I have set even to the point that I was dumb, etc., as far as who seeks an occasion of contention.

VERS. 3.-- From good things, and my sorrow, etc. (ID.) To be announced, etc., as far as that is, of those who leap over, I have spoken. (AUG.) Which is, unwillingly I kept silence from the wicked, 900Cetc., as far as and if the acts of one leaping over are anything.

VERS. 4.-- My heart grew hot within me. (AUG.) If the slothful man shall be condemned, etc., as far as he becomes a greedy steward.

VERS 5.-- I have spoken. (ID.) Not to a hearer who is to be instructed, but to God who hears, by whom I am heard within. And the number of my days. (HIER.) The number of the days which now are, is not truly for him who leaps over; but to him who clings it seems to be.

VERS. 6.-- Behold, measurable. (CASS.) As it were, the end being known, and the days which are, he attends to those things which he has left, and compares them one with another. And the substance, etc. (AUG.) He who sees that this substance is nothing, etc., as far as which shall be before thee.

900DVERS. 7.-- But yet. (CASS.) Seeing the coming of Christ, he returns to the weakness which he has among the virtues. (AUG.) Great are the things we have said and believe; but nevertheless that is not eternal, but all is vanity. And, desiring the eternal in place of mutability, he reproaches human life, to which he is subject, in what he says. Lest anyone think the saints strangers to temptations. Or, though the days be measurable, though there be substance, it is nothing: yet all is vanity in the rational creature, which according to divers men craves the whole creation. But yet. Although I gape after eternal things, etc., as far as whose conversation is in heaven. Every man. (AUG.) If he is evil, he is vain in worldly things; if he is good, since he wills to be with Christ, his life is vain.

901A-- But yet. (AUG.) Diapsalmus. How all are under vanity and chance; and thence he sets over against it that he waits for the Lord, and asks to be delivered. He passeth in an image. (ID.) Although he thus pursues vanity, etc., as far as because with misery and toil he craves earthly things. He layeth up treasure. (ID.) Out of the other vices the Prophet chose avarice, to show what he intends: for it is itself the root of all evils.

VERS. 8.-- Expectation. (ID.) Of the first coming, or of the second, etc., as far as not in our purses.

VERS. 9.-- Deliver me from all my iniquities. (CASS.) Not only from these, lest he roll back into those things which I leapt over, but from all altogether. For man is imperfect: because he has not received what he desires; perfect, who knows this very thing that is wanting to him.

901BVERS. 10.-- I was dumb. (ID.) Held in reproach, etc., as far as and it is necessary, because I have failed.

Remove thy scourges from me. (AUG.) Because thou hast made me, do not destroy me; only yield that I may be brought forth; not that I may be broken small

VERS. 11.-- With rebukes for iniquity. With which thou hast rebuked the human race: which nevertheless thou hast rebuked out of our own desert, on account of our iniquities, which rebukes are unto correction; for otherwise iniquity would remain uncorrected. Thou hast corrected man. (AUG.) There is a formless sorrow which does not amend: a formed one, which by its instructions supplies a form. And such a sorrow is a precept, that is, it holds the place and the image of a precept.

VERS. 12.-- And thou hast made the soul to waste away like a spider. (ID.) Dried up from the love of the virtues and of knowledge. 901CAs a spider weaves an empty web in the gathering of temporal things. Or, while it draws forth iniquity from itself like a spider, it dies by the voiding of its bowels. (CASS.) Or, the spider has a slender body, and stands not on the ground but on high, and weaves its webs by the voiding of its bowels: so the soul of one converted and afflicted forsakes earthly things, and, wasted away by the fear of God, accomplishes subtle works. But yet. (AUG., CASS.) Although he be rebuked, although they waste away, yet he is confounded by human weakness in various things, save he who contemplates God with a pure mind.

VERS. 14.-- Hear my prayer. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. A journey. He asks for himself the evils of the world to be at hand, and his sins to be forgiven, that he may go forth with a prosperous end. (ID.) But because I do not ask these things, etc., as far as mercy to be moved.

901DBe not silent, for I am a stranger. (AUG.) Already with thee, but still a lodger: because I am to pass hence to eternal things, where I shall not be a lodger. A stranger with thee. (CASS.) Not received in the city of the devil, but in thine, translated from Babylon to Jerusalem. As all my fathers. Lest anyone be thought excepted from this condition. A stranger. I forsake my own kingdom for thine. A pilgrim. Not yet choosing a seat for myself here.

Forgive me. (ID.) Here he asks that it be forgiven him, so that being sure he may come to the judgment.

PSALMUS XXXIX.

VERS. 1.-- In finem psalmus. (CASS.) Primum inducit Ecclesiam exspectasse Dominum, et accepisse 902Aeum, et ab eo Novum Testamentum, quod et multi secuturi sunt: unde percutit omnes superstitiones et invitat ad mirabilia Dei.

(ID.) Hic Christus ex membris.

VERS. 2.-- Exspectans exspectavi. (ID.) Exspectat, et ingratus: sed exspectans exspectat. (AUG.) Auctoritas ab antiquis in Abraham et caeteris, etc., usque ad qui noster est per cultum, non aliorum.

Dominum. (ID.) Non hominem, qui potest fallere et falli, et qui mecum indiget. Intendit. (ID.) Mihi, ut prodesset: non me, ut et malos.

VERS. 3.-- Lacu. (ID.) Tenebrae iniquitatum, infidelitatis scilicet et ignorantiae, etc., usque: ad petra contra lutum. (HIER.) In lacu vero et in luto, gentes idola colentes: vel, omnes terrena amantes.

902BVERS. 4.-- Carmen. (HIER.) Non turpe, non theatrale, sed per Novum Testamentum. Videbunt. (CASS.) Mirabilia tempore incarnationis facta. (AUG.) Videbunt, hoc quod primo de prioribus dixit, videbunt multi populi posteri.

VERS. 5.-- Nomen. (ID.) Quod est salvator. Quasi: Beatus, etc., qui non temporalia sperat ab eo, sed salutem, quod ejus nomen indicat. In Hebraeo saepe duplicantur hoc modo genitivi: vel, beatus, est cui est nomen, id est, quo est laus Dei, ut ab eo solo credat salutem, unde est et spes ejus. Insanias. (CASS.) Idola, quae fallunt a veritate: vel, insaniae, in spectaculis fallacibus. Ideo pluraliter, ut de omnibus accipiatur. Haec falsa, sed opera tua mirabilia, coelum, terra, elidit superstitiones.

902CVERS. 6.-- Mirabilia tua. (AUG.) Petrum ambulare super aquas in signo, non in saeculo, id est, fructibus saeculi. (AUG.) Salus verax, insania mendax, non est quod putatur. (HIER.) Vana sunt terrena, insaniae, irae et rixae, etc.

Non est qui similis tibi. (AUG.) Nulli auctores artium. Annuntiavi. Hic Christus in capite et membris. Haec sunt miro Dei, hae cogitationes quibus nemo est similis. (CASS.) Ecce mirabilia: incarnatio, justitia praedicationis, liberatio hominum ab iniquitatibus, confusio inimicorum, laetitia sperantium. Primo, rudes et incompositi praeparati sunt, ut verba Christi libenter susciperent. (AUG.) Vide mirabilia Dei. Annuntiavi prius per Prophetas, et post locutus egomet. Multiplicati sunt numerum. (HIER., AUG.) Super numerum 902Dsalvandorum: vel, super hoc quod aliquis enumerare possit: vel, me loquente plures quam olim crediderunt.

VERS. 7.-- Sacrificium et oblationem noluisti. (AUG.) Ut venit res, noluit quasi verba promittentia, etc., usque ad sed ille, qui fudit, surdus, non audit. Aures autem perfecisti mihi. Id est, perfecte me intelligere fecisti quid velles. Vel corpus aptasti mihi, ut ait Apostolus ad Hebraeos (Heb. X), id est, corpus aptum ad offerendum mihi dedisti.

VERS. 8.-- Holocaustum. Holocausta etiam non petisti pro peccato. Pro peccato. Quod supra oblationem, ut de hirco ἀποπομπάιohgr;ι, id est, emissario, qui cum peccatis populi in desertum mittebatur: vel, possunt 903Aesse duae dictiones pro peccato. Ecce venio (CASS.) Cum sacrificia cessent, constat venire Christum.

VERS. 9.-- In capite libri scriptum est de me. Ecce statim venio ut facerem voluntatem tuam, quia in capite hujus libri. Vel, sic est praefinitum apud Deum Patrem, qui est caput mei, qui sum liber, id est, forma justitiae hominibus.

VERS. 10.-- Ecclesia magna. (AUG.) Toto orbe terrarum, non parva ut prius: et siquidem insurget timor, non prohibebit loqui. Domine, tu scisti. (ID.) Labia sonant hominibus, etc., usque ad ut ad hoc non sim piger.

VERS. 11.-- Non abscondi. (CASS.) (Quando potui prodesse) veritatem, promissionem, et salvationem.

903BVERS. 12. Misericordia tua. (AUG.) Amor et timor perducunt me ad te.

VERS. 13.-- Capillos. (AUG.) Bene in comparatione delictorum capilli ducti sunt. Nam ideo in Veteri Testamento sacerdotes radebantur, ut sic carnis vitia deposuisse viderentur.

VERS. 14.-- Complaceat. (CASS.) Complaceat, Trinitatem personarum; tibi, singulariter unitatem essentiae signat. (AUG.) Complaceat, ait, non diffidens de potentia Dei, si adsit voluntas. Quasi: Si tu vis, potes, Domine. Respice. (CASS.) Respectus ejus nostrum est auxilium.

VERS. 16.-- Qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge. (AUG.) Et qui bona dicit malo animo, et qui mala dolose laudando, uterque malus est et cavendus. De primis 903Cdixit: Qui volunt mihi mala; de secundis: Qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.

VERS. 17.-- Et dicant. (CASS.) Haec est eorum exsultatio: haec enim professio in aeternum gaudentes efficit Christianos.

VERS. 18.-- Ego autem. (CASS.) Hoc Christus ex forma servi: ne quis gloriam praedictae laetitiae sibi arrogaret. Mendicus, qui sibi non sufficit. Ne tardaveris. (AUG.) Nisi breviati essent dies, etc., usque ad qui jam quaesita nutriunt.

PSALM XXXIX.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end, a psalm. (CASS.) First he brings in the Church as having awaited the Lord, and as having received 902Ahim, and from him the New Testament, which many also are to follow: whence he strikes at all superstitions and invites to the wonders of God.

(ID.) Here Christ, out of his members.

VERS. 2.-- Waiting I have waited. (ID.) He waits, and is ungrateful: but waiting he waits. (AUG.) Authority from the ancients, in Abraham and the rest, etc., as far as who is ours by worship, not of others.

The Lord. (ID.) Not a man, who can deceive and be deceived, and who is in need together with me. He gave heed. (ID.) To me, that he might profit me: not me, as the wicked also.

VERS. 3.-- The pit. (ID.) The darkness of iniquities, that is, of unbelief and of ignorance, etc., as far as: to a rock against mire. (HIER.) But in the pit and in the mire, the Gentiles worshipping idols: or, all who love earthly things.

902BVERS. 4.-- A song. (HIER.) Not a shameful one, not a theatrical one, but through the New Testament. They shall see. (CASS.) The wonders wrought in the time of the incarnation. (AUG.) They shall see: this which he first said of those before, many later peoples shall see.

VERS. 5.-- A name. (ID.) Which is Saviour. As if: Blessed, etc., who hopes not for temporal things from him, but for salvation, which his name indicates. In the Hebrew genitives are often doubled in this manner: or, blessed is he to whom the name belongs, that is, by whom is the praise of God, that from him alone he may believe salvation to be, whence also is his hope. Madnesses. (CASS.) Idols, which deceive away from the truth: or, madnesses, in deceitful spectacles. Therefore in the plural, that it may be taken of them all. These things are false, but thy wonderful works, heaven, earth, dashes superstitions to pieces.

902CVERS. 6.-- Thy wonders. (AUG.) Peter walking upon the waters in a sign, not in the world, that is, in the fruits of the world. (AUG.) Salvation is truthful, madness lying; it is not what it is thought to be. (HIER.) Earthly things are vain, madnesses, angers and brawls, etc.

There is none like unto thee. (AUG.) No authors of the arts. I have declared. Here Christ in the head and in the members. These are the wonders of God, these the thoughts to which no one is like. (CASS.) Behold the wonders: the incarnation, the justice of preaching, the deliverance of men from iniquities, the confounding of enemies, the gladness of those who hope. First, the rude and unformed were prepared, that they might willingly receive the words of Christ. (AUG.) See the wonders of God. I declared beforehand through the Prophets, and afterward I myself spoke. They are multiplied in number. (HIER., AUG.) Above the number 902Dof those to be saved: or, above what anyone could count: or, while I speak, more have believed than of old.

VERS. 7.-- Sacrifice and oblation thou didst not desire. (AUG.) When the thing came, he did not want, as it were, the words that promise, etc., as far as but he who poured it out, being deaf, hears not. But ears thou hast perfected for me. That is, thou hast made me perfectly understand what thou wouldst. Or, a body thou hast fitted to me, as the Apostle says to the Hebrews (Heb. X), that is, thou hast given me a body fit for offering.

VERS. 8.-- A holocaust. Holocausts also thou didst not require for sin. For sin. Which stands above oblation, as concerning the goat ἀποπομπάιῳ, that is, the emissary, which was sent into the desert with the sins of the people: or, for sin 903Amay be two words. Behold I come (CASS.) Since the sacrifices cease, it is established that Christ comes.

VERS. 9.-- In the head of the book it is written of me. Behold, I come at once to do thy will, because in the head of this book. Or, it is thus predetermined with God the Father, who is my head, I who am the book, that is, the form of justice for men.

VERS. 10.-- A great church. (AUG.) In the whole round of the lands, not a small one as before: and if indeed fear shall rise up, it will not forbid speaking. Lord, thou hast known. (ID.) Lips sound to men, etc., as far as that I be not slothful unto this.

VERS. 11.-- I have not hidden. (CASS.) (When I could profit) the truth, the promise, and the salvation.

903BVERS. 12. Thy mercy. (AUG.) Love and fear lead me through unto thee.

VERS. 13.-- Hairs. (AUG.) Rightly are hairs brought in by way of comparison with offences. For therefore in the Old Testament the priests were shaven, that so they might be seen to have laid aside the vices of the flesh.

VERS. 14.-- May it be pleasing. (CASS.) May it be pleasing, marks the Trinity of persons; to thee, in the singular, marks the unity of essence. (AUG.) May it be pleasing, he says, not distrusting the power of God, if the will be present. As if: If thou wilt, thou canst, Lord. Look. (CASS.) His regard is our help.

VERS. 16.-- Who say to me: Well done, well done. (AUG.) Both he who speaks good things with an evil mind, and he who evil things by praising them deceitfully, each is evil and to be guarded against. Of the first sort 903Che said: Who wish me evils; of the second: Who say to me: Well done, well done.

VERS. 17.-- And let them say. (CASS.) This is their exultation: for this profession makes Christians rejoicing unto eternity.

VERS. 18.-- But I. (CASS.) This Christ, out of the form of a servant: lest any should arrogate to himself the glory of the aforesaid gladness. A beggar, who does not suffice for himself. Delay not. (AUG.) Unless the days had been shortened, etc., as far as who now nourish the things they have sought.

PSALMUS XL

VERS. 1.-- In finem. (HIER.) Intellectus filiis Core, ut quamvis pauper et passus, etc., usque ad Apostolo dicente: Mihi autem, etc.--(AUG.) Quasi 903Dunius homini vox est capitis et corporis.

VERS. 2.-- Beatus. Irridetur qui colit pauperem mortuum; sed beatus. (AUG.) Propheta intelligentem super egenum et pauperem concelebrat. (HIER.) Prius Propheta a se, post inducet Christum. Qui intelligit. (AUG.) Nota qui intelligit, ut et non petentibus detur: qui petenti dat bene facit, qui tacentem intelligit, beatus sine dubio est.

VERS. 3.-- Dominum conservet. (ID.) Bene optat Propheta intelligenti super egenum et pauperem, quod est certa promissio. Et vivificet. (ID.) In futura vita, vel, hic per justificationem.

VERS. 4.-- Dominus opem. (CASS.) Ne putes beatum requiem hic habere: dolores ei mitigat, et precatur 904Ane hominis infirmitas durio superetur; quasi, lectus quietis sunt haec bona temporalia: quasi, facit haec doloribus plena, ne eis spes habeatur. Lectum. (AUG.) Universum enim stratum, id est, mundanam felicitatem provide convertit Deus in angustias. (CASS.) Hic trepidus ipse misericordiam petit: quia qui se peccasse sciebat, his jure tradi timebat: sed ne famuli Dei his afflicti videantur a Deo deserti, cum ipse Deus pertulit talia; unde dicit: Inimici mei dixerunt. Vel, lectus doloris. (AUG.) Caro, in qua peccatum, etc., usque ad quando Adam infirmatus est praevaricando. Opem (AUG., HIER.) In infirmitate carnis, quae gravat animam. Stratum. (AUG.) Est aliquod terrenum quod infirmus, etc., usque ad pro domo aeternae habitationis.

904BVERS. 6.-- Inimici mei. (CASS.) Dominus de passione sua, quae secundum egenum fuit. (AUG.) Inimici mei. Haec de Christo specialiter dicta sunt, sed et de membris dici possunt: et hodie fit tribulatio, ut nomen Christi exstinguatur: sed per mortem suam et suorum magis Ecclesia crevit.

VERS. 7.-- Et si ingrediebatur. (CASS.) Nota tolerandos malos.

(ID.) Non solum aperti inimici, sed et qui simulabant se amicos.

VERS. 8.-- Egrediebatur foras. A sinu veritatis, malus ingressus, malus egressus. In idipsum. (AUG.) Id est, uno consilio omnes adversum me susurrabant. Susurrabant. (CASS.) Non audent detegere consilium, quia in scelere socii sunt omnes: cum pauci 904Csoleant esse auctores scelerum.

VERS. 9.-- Nunquid. (AUG.) Qui habet potestatem ponendi animam, nonne habet et resumendi eam?

VERS. 10.-- Speravi. (AUG.) In membris, quia alii fratres in aliquid sperabant, quia talis videbatur ut caeteri. Sic et esurire in pauperibus se dicit.

VERS. 11.-- Tu autem, Domine. (AUG.) De resurrectione, quae est gloria egeni, ad confirmandam spem fidelium. Et retribuam eis. (AUG.). Quia enim dispersi sunt per mundum, ad admonitionem est, nondum ad damnationem.

VERS. 13.-- Me autem. (ID.) Affirmat quod oravit.

VERS. 14.-- Benedictus. (CASS.) Laudativa conclusio, exposita passione et resurrectione. Deus Israel. 904D(AUG.) Judaei sunt capsarii nostri, qui nobis codices portant: nos Israel. Aliter putassent pagani ficta quae dicuntur de Christo et Ecclesia, sed vincuntur testimonio inimicorum. A saeculo, etc. (CASS.) Ex quo omnia coepta sunt administrari usque in saeculum futurum, ubi omnia aeterna.

Fiat. (HIER.) Geminatio ostendit hoc ab omnibus esse faciendum. Pro fiat, in Hebraeo scribitur, amen, amen, quod Aquila, vere, vere, transtulit, vel fideliter. Et finit hic primus liber Psalterii secundum Hieronymum.

PSALM XL

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end. (HIER.) An understanding for the sons of Core, that although poor and suffering, etc., as far as the Apostle saying: But to me, etc.--(AUG.) It is as it were 903Dthe voice of one man, of the head and of the body.

VERS. 2.-- Blessed. He is mocked who reverences a dead poor man; but blessed. (AUG.) The Prophet celebrates him that understands concerning the needy and the poor. (HIER.) First the Prophet from himself, afterward he will bring in Christ. Who understandeth. (AUG.) Note who understandeth, that it may be given even to those who do not ask: he who gives to one asking does well; he who understands one that is silent is without doubt blessed.

VERS. 3.-- May the Lord preserve. (ID.) Well does the Prophet wish it for him that understands concerning the needy and the poor, which is a sure promise. And may he quicken. (ID.) In the life to come, or, here through justification.

VERS. 4.-- The Lord bring help. (CASS.) Do not think that the blessed man has rest here: he mitigates his sorrows, and prays 904Athat the infirmity of man be not overcome by hard things; as it were, these temporal goods are a bed of rest: as it were, he makes them full of sorrows, that hope be not had in them. The bed. (AUG.) For the whole indeed couch, that is, worldly happiness, God providently turns into straits. (CASS.) Here he himself, trembling, asks for mercy: because he who knew that he had sinned feared to be handed over to these things by right: but lest the servants of God, afflicted by these things, should seem deserted by God, since God himself bore such things; whence he says: My enemies have spoken. Or, a bed of sorrow. (AUG.) The flesh, in which is sin, etc., as far as when Adam was weakened by transgressing. Help (AUG., HIER.) In the infirmity of the flesh, which weighs down the soul. The couch. (AUG.) There is some earthly thing which the sick man, etc., as far as for the house of eternal habitation.

904BVERS. 6.-- My enemies. (CASS.) The Lord concerning his passion, which was after the manner of the needy one. (AUG.) My enemies. These things are said specially of Christ, but they can be said also of his members: and today tribulation is made, that the name of Christ may be extinguished: but through his own death and that of his own the Church has grown the more.

VERS. 7.-- And if he came in. (CASS.) Note that the wicked are to be borne with.

(ID.) Not only open enemies, but also those who feigned themselves friends.

VERS. 8.-- He went forth abroad. From the bosom of truth; an evil entrance, an evil going out. Unto the selfsame. (AUG.) That is, with one counsel they all whispered against me. They whispered. (CASS.) They do not dare to uncover their counsel, because in the crime all are partners: whereas few 904Care wont to be the authors of crimes.

VERS. 9.-- Shall he. (AUG.) He who has the power of laying down his soul, has he not also the power of taking it up again?

VERS. 10.-- I have hoped. (AUG.) In the members, because other brethren hoped somewhat in him, because he seemed such as the rest. So too he says that he hungers in the poor.

VERS. 11.-- But thou, O Lord. (AUG.) Of the resurrection, which is the glory of the needy one, for the confirming of the hope of the faithful. And I will requite them. (AUG.). For because they are scattered through the world, it is for admonition, not yet for damnation.

VERS. 13.-- But me. (ID.) He affirms what he prayed for.

VERS. 14.-- Blessed. (CASS.) A concluding praise, the passion and resurrection having been set forth. The God of Israel. 904D(AUG.) The Jews are our book-carriers, who carry the codices for us: we are Israel. Otherwise the pagans would have thought the things said of Christ and the Church to be feigned, but they are overcome by the testimony of enemies. From the age, etc. (CASS.) From which all things began to be administered, unto the age to come, where all things are eternal.

Let it be done. (HIER.) The doubling shows that this is to be done by all. In place of let it be done, in the Hebrew is written amen, amen, which Aquila translated truly, truly, or faithfully. And here ends the first book of the Psalter according to Jerome.

PSALMUS XLI.

VERS. 1.-- In fine intellectus. (CASS.) Core interpretatur Calvaria. Filii ergo, etc., usque ad, cui 905Aobviat malorum insultatio. (HIER.) Filii Core, id est, filii calvi, etc., usque ad verbum puerorum deridentium Eliseum.

VERS. 2.-- Quemadmodum desiderat, etc. (AUG.) Vox haec convenit catechumenis, et etiam omnibus adhuc peregrinantibus.

Cervus. Cervus senio gravatus, excrescentibus pilis et cornibus, serpentem naribus haurit: unde veneno aestuans, fontem ad bibendum ardentissime desiderat; quo hausto, cornua et pilos deponit.

VERS. 3.-- Sitivit. (AUG.) Determinat desiderium suum, quia poterat intelligi desiderare cervus fontem causa bibendi, vel lavandi; hic omne desiderium esse ad Deum ostenditur. Quando veniam. Quod citius est Deo, tardum est hominis desiderio. 905BTalis cervus dum currit, patitur insultantes; unde: Fuerunt mihi lacrymae meae panes. In prosperis etiam, quae despicit, sicut in adversis. Panes. (CASS.) Non amaritudo, vel peremptio, sed panes.

VERS. 5.-- Haec recordatus sum. (AUG.) Dum quaerunt, Ubi est Deus tuus? ego etiam sum meditatus per omnia visibilia haec, et per ipsam animam meam, ut per ea exteriora, invisibilia Dei inveniam. Ecce intellectus tituli. Effudi. (Ibid.) Ad intelligendum et attingendum dilatavi super seipsam. Effudi. (CASS.) Vel laetatus sum. Liquefacta est anima mea in me; non extra, sed in se compuncta revertitur. Etsi visibiliter Deum non videam, cogito tamen quod per Ecclesiam, in qua admirabiles sunt sancti, ad Jerusalem coelestem perveniam, 905Ccaptus suavitate laudis angelicae, quae suscipitur mente. In locum tabernaculi. (AUG.) Tabernaculum Dei in terra, etc., usque ad, id est, de refectione aeterna gaudentium. In voce exsultationis. (Ibid.) De aeterna festivitate sonat quid dulce cordi: unde rapitur cervus ad fontes aquarum, et mulcetur. Sed quia perstrepit mundus, et caro gravat animam: comparans haec tristitia illis jucundis, ait:

VERS. 6.-- Quare tristis? etc. (CASS.) De perturbationibus contra quas ratio confirmat animam sensualem spe Dei. Quare conturbas? (AUG.) Qui, si investigas, nihil est in mundo quare hoc debeas: spera potius salutare remedium adhuc, et si non modo, plene in futuro. Spera. (CASS.) Vel sperare potest, quia adhuc in praesenti confitebor, id est, de 905Dpeccatis poenitentiam agam, ut tibi non obsistam.

VERS. 7.-- Ad meipsum. Conversus ad Deum dicit ex seipso conturbationes, ex Deo finem earum: unde in eo est ei spes. Et hoc est ad meipsum, vel a meipso. (CASS.) Ecce qui superius corrigebat animam ad conditionem hominis, reversus dicit hic animam a se turbari, quae nisi vitia carnis essent, tranquilla permaneret. Ecce ex qua diversitate constat homo. Quasi: propterea, id est, propter conturbationes animae, memor ero. (AUG.) Id est, festino ad te, quia excludis mala omnia. Ecce remedium, quo evadat conturbationes: unde pro quibus sit memor, subdit: De terra Jordanis, ubi Dominus consecravit baptismum, in quo humiliati lavantur, et 906Afiunt terra fructifera. (CASS.) Horum memor malis non turbatur. Propterea memor. (AUG.) Qua ad me turbatur anima, ideo memor, etc. Nemo currit ad remissionem, nisi qui sibi displicet, nisi qui se fatetur peccatorem: quod notat Hermoniim; nemo confitetur nisi se humiliet, quod notantur in modico. Jordanis. (Ibid.) Descensio. Descende ergo ut eleveris. (CASS.) In Jordane Dominus baptisma consecravit, in quo humiliati lavantur, et fiunt terra fructifera, quae reddit fructum tricesimum, sexagesimum et centesimum (Matth. XIII). Hermoniim. (AUG.) Parvus mons juxta Jordanem, etc., usque ad quia non in superbis, sed in humilibus memor Dei est.

VERS. 8.-- Abyssus abyssum. (Ibid.) Decet ut 906Bsim memor, etc., usque ad et propter haec omnia oro in adversis, et hoc est: Apud me oratio. (Ibid.) Vel abyssus abyssum invocat, id est, judicium quod intulit Deus peccanti, etc., usque ad quia timet judicia. Cataractarum. Cataractae ad litteram sunt ostia fluviorum.

VERS. 9.-- In die. (Ibid.) Id est, in prosperis, etc., usque ad unde vivamus in adversitate. Apud me oratio. (Ibid.) Oratio in conturbationibus est mihi, et haec apud me.

VERS. 10.-- Quare oblitus. (CASS.) Quare nunc me pateris his miseriis vexari? Videbat quae dulcedo patriae, et pericula mundi horrebat.

VERS. 11.-- Dum confringuntur ossa. (AUG.) Quasi ossa franguntur, dum virtus patientiae affligitur, 906Cquod irrident mali. Haec est exprobratio illa: Dum dicitur mihi: Ubi est? vel nullus est, vel de te non curat.

PSALM XLI.

VERS. 1.-- At the end, an understanding. [Vulg. Ps 41:1 reads "In finem" in the accusative and adds "filiis Core": "unto the end; an understanding for the sons of Core"] (CASS.) Core is interpreted Calvary. Therefore the sons, etc., as far as, whom 905Athe insult of the wicked meets. (HIER.) Sons of Core, that is, sons of the bald man, etc., as far as the word of the boys mocking Elisha.

VERS. 2.-- As the hart desireth, etc. (AUG.) This voice suits catechumens, and also all who are still journeying abroad.

The hart. The hart, burdened with age, its hairs and horns growing out, draws in a serpent by its nostrils: whence, burning with the venom, it most ardently desires a fountain from which to drink; and when it has drunk, it lays aside its horns and its hairs.

VERS. 3.-- It hath thirsted. (AUG.) He determines his desire, because the hart could be understood to desire a fountain for the sake of drinking, or of washing; here all desire is shown to be toward God. When shall I come. What is quicker to God is slow to the desire of man. 905BSuch a hart, while it runs, suffers those who insult; whence: My tears have been my bread. In prosperity also, which he despises, as in adversity. Bread. (CASS.) Not bitterness, or destruction, but bread.

VERS. 5.-- These things I remembered. (AUG.) While they ask, Where is thy God? I also have meditated through all these visible things, and through my own soul, that through those outward things I may find the invisible things of God. Behold the understanding of the title. I poured out. (Ibid.) For understanding and attaining I have spread it out above itself. I poured out. (CASS.) Or, I have rejoiced. My soul is melted within me; not outside, but pricked with compunction it returns into itself. Although I do not see God visibly, yet I consider that through the Church, in which the saints are wonderful, I shall come to the heavenly Jerusalem, 905Ctaken captive by the sweetness of the angelic praise, which is received by the mind. Into the place of the tabernacle. (AUG.) The tabernacle of God on earth, etc., as far as, that is, of those rejoicing in the eternal refreshment. In the voice of exultation. (Ibid.) Of the eternal festival there sounds something sweet to the heart: whence the hart is snatched away to the fountains of waters, and is soothed. But because the world makes a din, and the flesh weighs down the soul, comparing this sorrow with those joyful things, he says:

VERS. 6.-- Why art thou sad? etc. (CASS.) Of the disturbances against which reason strengthens the sensual soul with hope of God. Why dost thou trouble? (AUG.) Who, if thou searchest, there is nothing in the world for which thou shouldst owe this: hope rather for the saving remedy still, and if not now, fully in time to come. Hope. (CASS.) Or he can hope, because still in the present I will confess, that is, I will do penance 905Dfor my sins, that I may not withstand thee.

VERS. 7.-- To myself. Turned to God he tells the troublings from himself, the end of them from God: whence in him is his hope. And this is to myself, or from myself. (CASS.) Behold, he who above was correcting the soul to the condition of man, having turned back says here that the soul is troubled by itself, which, were there not the vices of the flesh, would remain tranquil. Behold out of what diversity man is composed. As if: therefore, that is, on account of the troublings of the soul, I will be mindful. (AUG.) That is, I hasten to thee, because thou shuttest out all evils. Behold the remedy by which he may escape the troublings: whence he subjoins for what things he is mindful: Of the land of Jordan, where the Lord consecrated baptism, in which the humbled are washed, and 906Abecome fruitful earth. (CASS.) He who is mindful of these things is not troubled by evils. Therefore mindful. (AUG.) Whereby the soul is troubled toward me, therefore mindful, etc. No one runs to remission, save he who is displeasing to himself, save he who confesses himself a sinner: which Hermoniim denotes; no one confesses unless he humbles himself, which is denoted in the little one. Jordan. (Ibid.) A going down. Descend therefore that thou mayest be lifted up. (CASS.) In the Jordan the Lord consecrated baptism, in which the humbled are washed, and become fruitful earth, which yields fruit thirtyfold, sixtyfold and a hundredfold (Matth. XIII). Hermoniim. (AUG.) A small mountain beside the Jordan, etc., as far as because it is not among the proud, but among the humble, that one is mindful of God.

VERS. 8.-- Deep unto deep. (Ibid.) It is fitting that 906BI be mindful, etc., as far as and on account of all these things I pray in adversities, and this is: With me a prayer. (Ibid.) Or deep calleth unto deep, that is, the judgment which God brought upon the sinner, etc., as far as because he fears the judgments. Of the cataracts. Cataracts, according to the letter, are the mouths of rivers.

VERS. 9.-- In the day. (Ibid.) That is, in prosperity, etc., as far as whence we may live in adversity. With me a prayer. (Ibid.) Prayer in troublings is mine, and this is with me.

VERS. 10.-- Why hast thou forgotten. (CASS.) Why dost thou now suffer me to be vexed with these miseries? He saw what sweetness of the fatherland there was, and shuddered at the perils of the world.

VERS. 11.-- While my bones are broken. (AUG.) As it were bones are broken, while the strength of patience is afflicted, 906Cat which the wicked laugh. This is that reproach: While it is said to me: Where is he? either there is none, or he cares not for thee.

PSALMUS XLII.

In finem psalmus David. (AUG.) Corporis Christi, quod hic gemit inter zizania, id est, inter malos, habens cum eis multa communia, nasci, mori, prospera et adversa: cum quibus (quia non habet communem causam meritorum) exclamat: Judica me, etc. (Ibid.) Psalmus iste contra pressuras, ne et ipsae retrahant nos a Deo. (CASS.) Conqueritur de commistione malorum, et precatur separationem.

VERS. 1.-- Judica me. (Ibid.) Non petit peccata sua discuti, quod periculosum est, sed causam ab impiis parari, ut sit cum electis: unde addit: Et 906Ddiscerne. Gens non sancta est iniquus, et dolosus, a quibus in judicio separatur: sed et hic ne ab eis corrumpatur.

VERS. 2.-- Quare tristis incedo? (AUG.) Causam tristitiae quaerit, quae est peccatum, ut causa laetitiae justitia. Isaias propter peccatum: Modicum quidem contristavi illum, sic enim punit Deus.

VERS. 3.-- Emitte lucem tuam. (CASS.) Quia, eo veniente, tolletur omnis tristitia confusionis. (AUG.) Quia certi jam pignus habemus, quia ea ipsa, id est, lux et veritas, deduxerunt a peccatis Ecclesiam praesentem, quae est tabernaculum.

VERS. 4.-- Et introibo. Sicut pontifex ad Sancta sanctorum. (CASS.) Et introibo. De laetitia finali, 907Apro qua laudat in tribulatione, qui supra tristis erat unde et se confortat.

VERS. 5.-- Confitebor tibi in cithara. (AUG.) Qui praecepta Dei facit, et non patitur, in psalterio confitetur: qui vero facit et patitur, quod est ex inferiori natura, in cithara, quae ab inferiori resonat, sicut psalterium a superiori. In cithara. (CASS.) Ecce qui supra fuit tristi de malis saeculi, de bono intellectu sibi gaudium facit. Quare conturbas me? (Ibid.) Frequenter, et vehementer persuadet saeculi tristitiam fugiendam, quae patientiam, charitatem et spem exstinguit, et totam vitam confundit. Salutare vultus mei. (AUG.) Et alibi: Miserere mei, etc., usque ad eleemosyna, et oratio quae illis duabus alis volat ad Deum.

PSALM XLII.

Unto the end, a psalm of David. (AUG.) Of the body of Christ, which groans here among the tares, that is, among the wicked, having many things in common with them: to be born, to die, prosperity and adversity: with whom (because it has not a common cause of merits) it cries out: Judge me, etc. (Ibid.) This psalm is against pressures, lest they too draw us back from God. (CASS.) He complains of the mingling of the wicked, and prays for separation.

VERS. 1.-- Judge me. (Ibid.) He does not ask that his own sins be examined, which is dangerous, but that his cause be made ready apart from the impious, that he may be with the elect: whence he adds: And 906Ddistinguish. The nation that is not holy is the unjust and deceitful man, from whom he is separated in the judgment: but here too lest he be corrupted by them.

VERS. 2.-- Why do I go sorrowful? (AUG.) He seeks the cause of sadness, which is sin, as justice is the cause of gladness. Isaias on account of sin: For a little while indeed I made him sorrowful, for so God punishes.

VERS. 3.-- Send forth thy light. (CASS.) Because, when he comes, all the sadness of confusion will be taken away. (AUG.) Because we now have a sure pledge, since those very things, that is, light and truth, have led the present Church away from her sins, which is the tabernacle.

VERS. 4.-- And I will go in. As the high priest to the Holy of holies. (CASS.) And I will go in. Of the final gladness, 907Afor which he gives praise in tribulation, he who above was sad, whence also he strengthens himself.

VERS. 5.-- I will confess to thee on the harp. (AUG.) He who does the precepts of God, and does not suffer, confesses on the psaltery: but he who does and suffers, which is from the lower nature, on the harp, which sounds from below, as the psaltery from above. On the harp. (CASS.) Behold, he who above was sad about the evils of the world, makes joy for himself out of good understanding. Why dost thou trouble me? (Ibid.) Frequently and vehemently he urges that the sadness of the world must be fled, which extinguishes patience, charity and hope, and confounds the whole life. The salvation of my countenance. (AUG.) And elsewhere: Have mercy on me, etc., as far as almsgiving, and prayer which flies to God on those two wings.

PSALMUS XLIII.

  • 907B

VERS. 1.-- Ad intellectum. (AUG.) Non sic quaerant sibi fieri, etc., usque ad et haec non amentur. (CASS.) Distinguit beneficia Dei, quae incipientibus data sunt in mundo, perfectis in coelo.

Ut magis sit mirum relinqui praesentes, recolit praeterita.

VERS. 2.-- Deus, auribus. (AUG., CASS.) Primum dicit: Deus, quod facere solet laetus vel graviter afflictus.

Audivimus. Ut major fides sit rei, ne putetur ambigua.

Patres. Non juvenes, ut videantur veri nostri, qui suis certa dicerent.

907COpus quod, etc. (Ibid.) Et si semper operetur, tamen operari dicitur, quando aliquod signum novitatis ostendit.

VERS. 4.-- Sed dextera tua. (AUG.) Id est, bonus successus, quem eis dedisti. Et brachium tuum, etc. (Ibid.) Id est, fortitudo; et illuminatio, id est, sapiens consilium: quod totum fecisti ex benevolentia tua.

VERS. 5.-- Tu es ipse rex meus et Deus meus. (AUG.) Tempora mutata sunt; auctor non mutatur.

VERS. 7.-- Non enim in arcu meo sperabo. (CASS.) Minor virtus hominis, quia minus valet in bello.

Gladius. Major virtus, quae in bello plus creditur valere. (AUG.) Vel, gladius meus non salvabit me, sed tu, quia et in hoc saeculo salvasti, ne nos traherent 907Dpost se, et eos pudere fecisti: et ideo tunc laudabimur.

VERS. 8.-- Salvasti, etc. (AUG.) Nota etiam praeterita dicta, pro futuris esse accipienda.

VERS. 10.-- Nunc autem repulisti. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. Enumerat mala quae hic fecerunt boni, non tamen obliti Dei. (CASS.) Exaggerat mala, ut benevolentiam judicis impetret. Confudisti, dum hic ab iniquis habentur opprobrio. (AUG.) Haec vere futura, etc., usque ad hoc est jejunium non abstinentiae, sed luxuriae.

VERS. 11.-- Avertisti. (CASS.) Pro deficientibus. Vel, averti, est hostem fugere; unde: Si vos persecuti fuerint in una civitate, fugite in aliam.

908ADiripiebant. Hoc fugatis contingit, ut cadant in praedam, qui hostibus nequeunt resistere.

VERS. 12.-- Dedisti nos tanquam oves escarum. (CASS.) Persistentes in fide. Hic diversi martyres, id est diversa martyrii genera: alii esca feris, alii traditi gentibus in servitutem; unde dicit: Tanquam oves escarum, ubi notatur quorumdam mactatio.

VERS. 13.-- Vendidisti populum tuum sine pretio. (AUG.) Dum dantur alienigenis et nullus acquirit: quod fit ad probationem vel correctionem; vel nullus pro eis acquiritur, vel si quis, pauci tamen.

VERS. 14.-- Opprobrium vicinis. (CASS.) Gravis afflictio a vicinis ingeritur, quia non transitorie dicitur, quod a circumstantibus irrogat. Derisum his qui in circuitu. (CASS.) Derisus est vox confusa laetitiae, 908Binsultationem immoderata hilaritate denuntians. Contemptus est abjecta vilitas.

VERS. 15.-- In similitudinem gentium. (Ibid.) In similitudine Christi gentibus sunt appositi, quando eos comparibus poenis affecerunt.

VERS. 17.-- Exprobrantis. (Ibid.) Exprobrare est in faciem maledicere; obloqui est absenti detrahere, et dolose mordere.

VERS. 18.-- Venerunt super nos. (Ibid.) Quia non erant in nobis per culpam.

VERS. 19.-- Non recessit. (Ibid.) Ita quod retroiret, etsi aliquando descendit contemplatione deitatis. Declinasti. (AUG.) Semitae nostrae erant in voluptatibus et prosperitatibus saeculi: sed tulisti eas de sua via, et ostendisti arctam viam, quae ducit ad 908Cvitam. (HIER.) Vel et declinasti, id est, opera nostra de lege tua pendere fecisti. Vel, non declinasti (alia littera), id est, non permisisti declinare et deviare semitas nostras. Semitas, id est, opera; a via tua, id est, a lege; ideo quoniam humiliasti nos.
