VERS. 20.-- Umbra mortis. (AUG.) Vel, haec mortalitas, umbra mortis est: vera autem mors est damnatio cum diabolo.

VERS. 21.-- Si obliti sumus nomen Dei. (Ibid.) Iste est intellectus filiorum Core, qui propter haec omnia mala non obliviscuntur Deum, scientes quia Deus requiret ista.

VERS. 22.-- Novit. (Ibid.) Nocere dicitur Deus et quod novit et quod te facit noscere. Novit, quoniam requiret propter te, ut tu invenias te, et gratias 908Dagas ei qui te fecit, ut in Petro actum est, qui probavit quid posset. Propter te mortificamur. (CASS.) Non pro criminibus nostris, sed ut fides tua gentibus augeatur.

VERS. 23.-- Exsurge. (Ibid.) Precatur auxilium, ut hic afflictis tempore resurrectionis subveniat. (AUG.) Hactenus non obliti; et ut perseveremus: Exsurge, quia propter te mortificamur. (AUG., HIER.) Et si sciunt Christum non dormire, et sibi resurrexisse, precantur tamen resurgere per fidem, non sibi, sed gentibus, quae putant mortuum. Si enim et illi crederent surrexisse, credentes in eum non persequerentur, sed et ipsi crederent. (AUG.) Vel exsurge, conforta.

909AObdormis. Negligere videris. Quare etsi nesciamus, tu scis quare: vel pro culpa, vel pro utilitate. Quod si pro culpa, utinam abesset; si pro utilitate, utinam adesset. Quosdam repellis, quia faciem, id est, cognitionem tuam, ab eis subtrahis: obdormis quibusdam qui gemunt de malis.

VERS. 24.-- Quare oblivisceris? id est, non das spiritum fortitudinis, sine quo inopes. Et tribulationis. (CASS.) Quia eam non mitigas, etc., usque ad qui facile cedunt illicitis motibus, et haerent terrenis.

VERS. 26.-- Exsurge, Domine. Hic sine dormitione exsurge ponitur, quod ad resurrectionem pertinet, in qua est spes omnium fidelium; in qua humana destruitur captivitas; per quam sumus adjuti 909Bet liberati. In terra venter. (AUG.) Qui genua figit terrae, habet quo plus humilietur: qui vero plus humiliatur ut et venter haereat terrae, non habet ultra quo plus humilietur. Exprimit ergo nimiam humiliationem, ut quia venit ad summam, jam adsit Dei miseratio. Vel plangit eos qui sunt venter, id est, carnales, et haeserunt, id est consenserunt iniquis.

PSALM XLIII.

  • 907B

VERS. 1.-- Unto understanding. (AUG.) Let them not so seek these things to be done for themselves, etc., as far as and let not these things be loved. (CASS.) He distinguishes the benefits of God, which were given to beginners in the world, to the perfect in heaven.

That it may be the more wonderful that present things are left behind, he recalls things past.

VERS. 2.-- God, with our ears. (AUG., CASS.) First he says: God, which one is wont to do when glad or heavily afflicted.

We have heard. That there may be greater faith in the matter, lest it be thought doubtful.

Fathers. Not young men, that they may be seen as our true ones, who would tell sure things to their own.

907CThe work which, etc. (Ibid.) And although he always works, yet he is said to work when he shows some sign of newness.

VERS. 4.-- But thy right hand. (AUG.) That is, the good success which thou gavest them. And thy arm, etc. (Ibid.) That is, strength; and illumination, that is, wise counsel: all which thou hast done out of thy good will.

VERS. 5.-- Thou art thyself my king and my God. (AUG.) The times are changed; the author is not changed.

VERS. 7.-- For I will not hope in my bow. (CASS.) The lesser strength of man, because it avails less in war.

A sword. The greater strength, which in war is believed to avail more. (AUG.) Or, my sword shall not save me, but thou, because in this world also thou hast saved us, lest they should drag us 907Dafter them, and thou hast made them ashamed: and therefore then we shall be praised.

VERS. 8.-- Thou hast saved, etc. (AUG.) Note also that things said in the past are to be taken for things to come.

VERS. 10.-- But now thou hast cast us off. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. He enumerates the evils which the good did here, yet not having forgotten God. (CASS.) He exaggerates the evils, that he may obtain the good will of the judge. Thou hast confounded, while here they are held in reproach by the wicked. (AUG.) These things are truly to come, etc., as far as this is a fast not of abstinence, but of luxury.

VERS. 11.-- Thou hast turned away. (CASS.) For those who fail. Or, to be turned away is to flee the enemy; whence: If they shall have persecuted you in one city, flee into another. [Vulg. Mt 10:23 reads "Cum autem persequentur vos in civitate ista, fugite in aliam": "and when they shall persecute you in this city, flee into another"]

908AThey plundered. This happens to those put to flight, that they fall as prey, who cannot resist their enemies.

VERS. 12.-- Thou hast given us like sheep for food. (CASS.) Those persisting in faith. Here diverse martyrs, that is, diverse kinds of martyrdom: some food for beasts, others delivered to the Gentiles into servitude; whence he says: Like sheep for food, where the slaughter of certain ones is noted.

VERS. 13.-- Thou hast sold thy people without a price. (AUG.) While they are given to foreigners and no one gains: which is done for proving or for correcting; or no one is gained for them, or if any, yet few.

VERS. 14.-- A reproach to our neighbours. (CASS.) A grievous affliction is heaped on by neighbours, because that is not uttered in passing which one inflicts from among those standing round. A derision to those who are round about. (CASS.) Derision is a confused voice of gladness, 908Bannouncing insult with immoderate hilarity. Contempt is abject vileness.

VERS. 15.-- Into the likeness of the Gentiles. (Ibid.) [Vulg. Ps 43:15 has the dative, "in similitudinem gentibus": "for a likeness to the Gentiles"] In the likeness of Christ they are set beside the Gentiles, when they afflicted them with equal punishments.

VERS. 17.-- Of him that reproacheth. (Ibid.) To reproach is to curse to the face; to speak against is to detract from one absent, and to bite deceitfully.

VERS. 18.-- They have come upon us. (Ibid.) Because they were not in us through fault.

VERS. 19.-- It hath not gone back. (Ibid.) So that it should go backward, although sometimes it descends from the contemplation of the deity. Thou hast turned aside. (AUG.) Our paths were in the pleasures and prosperities of the world: but thou hast taken them away from their own way, and hast shown the narrow way which leads to 908Clife. (HIER.) Or and thou hast turned aside, that is, thou hast made our works to hang upon thy law. Or, thou hast not turned aside (another reading), that is, thou hast not permitted our paths to turn aside and go astray. Paths, that is, works; from thy way, that is, from the law; therefore because thou hast humbled us.

VERS. 20.-- The shadow of death. (AUG.) Or, this mortality is the shadow of death: but true death is damnation with the devil.

VERS. 21.-- If we have forgotten the name of God. (Ibid.) This is the understanding of the sons of Core, who on account of all these evils do not forget God, knowing that God will require these things.

VERS. 22.-- He hath known. (Ibid.) God is said to harm Nocere both what he knows and what he makes thee know. He hath known, because he will require on account of thee, that thou mayest find thyself, and give 908Dthanks to him who made thee, as was done in Peter, who proved what he could do. For thy sake we are put to death. (CASS.) Not for our crimes, but that thy faith may be increased among the Gentiles.

VERS. 23.-- Arise. (Ibid.) He prays for help, that he may succour those afflicted here at the time of the resurrection. (AUG.) Thus far not forgetting; and that we may persevere: Arise, for on thy account we are put to death. (AUG., HIER.) And although they know that Christ does not sleep, and that he has risen for himself, yet they pray him to rise through faith, not for himself, but for the Gentiles, who think him dead. For if they too believed that he had risen, believing in him they would not persecute, but they too would believe. (AUG.) Or arise, strengthen.

909AThou sleepest. Thou seemest to neglect. Wherefore, even if we know not, thou knowest why: either for fault, or for benefit. But if for fault, would that it were absent; if for benefit, would that it were present. Some thou dost repel, because thou withdrawest thy face, that is, thy knowledge, from them: thou sleepest to certain ones who groan over evils.

VERS. 24.-- Why dost thou forget? that is, thou givest not the spirit of fortitude, without which we are helpless. And of tribulation. (CASS.) Because thou dost not mitigate it, etc., as far as who easily yield to unlawful motions, and cleave to earthly things.

VERS. 26.-- Arise, O Lord. Here arise is set without sleeping, which pertains to the resurrection, in which is the hope of all the faithful; in which human captivity is destroyed; through which we are helped 909Band set free. In the earth our belly. (AUG.) He who fixes his knees on the earth has whereby he may be more humbled: but he who is more humbled, so that his belly also cleaves to the earth, has nothing further whereby he may be more humbled. He expresses therefore an exceeding humiliation, so that, since it has come to the highest point, the mercy of God may now be present. Or he laments those who are the belly, that is, the carnal, and they have cleaved, that is, consented to the wicked.

PSALMUS XLIV.

VERS. 1.-- In finem, etc. (AUG.) Epithalamium, id est, laus thalami. Canticum pro commutandis et pro dilecto, id est, sponsa et sponso, scribitur filiis Core, ut venerentur. Hic enim describitur per quem commutabuntur, quia laus sponsi et sponsae hic cantatur. (CASS.) Propheta praeconia Dei se eructaturum 909Cpromittit.

VERS. 2.-- Eructavit. (AUG., HIER.) Intus enim fatur Propheta, etc., usque ad antequam sit quod facturus est. Consilium vero Patris est Verbum.

Bonum. Quo omnia bona facta sunt. Dico. Id est, Verbum profero: idem hic quod prius; sed in ipso verbo omnia opera Dei esse dicit; unde: Quod factum est in ipso vita erat, ut nihil sit in opere quod non prius fuit in consilio. De hoc dicitur: Semel locutus est Deus.

Calamus. Non sono, qui transit, comparat Verbum: sed scripto, quod manet. Vel, velociter, quia non aliud post aliud, sed omnia simul in uno Verbo aeterno.

Velociter. Virtus prophetiae, quae non sub cruciatu 909Dhumano cogitat quod de arcano divinitatis aliis divulgat.

VERS. 3.-- Speciosus forma. (CASS.) Incipit de laude sponsi prius a forma. Benedixit. Priora dixit Propheta ex persona Dei, haec ex sua; vel omnia ex se. Vel, eructat verbum, qui dicit Deo hymnum.

Dico opera. (AUG.) ad laudem ejus, qui ex eo. Lingua, calamus. Quia quod dico, et scribo. Vel, velociter: quia cito ventura quae scribo.

(CASS.) In labiis. Quia, eo loquente, mundus gratiam reconciliationis accepit.

VERS. 4.-- Accingere. (Ibid.) Hic laudat eum a potestate; et tu talis accingere.

VERS. 5.-- Specie tua et pulchritudine. Species ad 910Ahumanitatem, in qua mundo apparuit; pulchritudo ad Deitatem, qua omnia decorat.

Intende. Hominem pereuntem miseratus respice.

Prospere. Liberans homines.

Procede. De utero Virginis, ut sponsus: vel, ab his victis ad alios vincendos.

Regna. In fide hominum tuam potentiam ostende, qui semper regnasti. Et per hoc, quia et per te, et per tuos veritatem doces, qua falsitatem nostram destruis. Et quia mansuetus ferendo malos, ut quando pro inimicis oravit, sic et sui: Et quia justitiam vitae ostendit. Et quia deducet te inoffense per cursum totius vitae, vel de populo ad populum

Mirabiliter. Quia omnes mirabuntur, vel, quia miracula faciet.

910BVERS. 6.-- Populi sub te cadent. (AUG.) Id est multi de suis inimicis supponent se sibi, et hoc ratione vel voluntate. Hoc est quod titulus dixit: Pro his qui commutabuntur ex filiis Core. -- In corda. (CASS.) Inimicorum tuorum, ut sint amici, sicut Saulus.

VERS. 7.-- Sedes. (Ibid.) Hic a judicio: Sedes ad judicium pertinet. Virga. (Ibid.) Regula divinae aequitatis, quae vere recta et nunquam curvatur: haec justos regit, iniquos percutit. (AUG.) Nemo sibi multum de misericordia praesumat, blandiatur: quia virga directionis, si alios regit, alios conterit: regit spirituales, conterit carnales.

VERS. 8.-- Dilexisti. (Ibid.) Vel, quia dilexisti justitiam, etc., reddita sunt haec praemia, fecit te regem, 910Cdando nomen quod est super omne nomen.

Et odisti. Si homo iniquitatem in se odit, cum Deo facit: odit Deus iniquitetem, oderis et tu.

O Deus. (AUG.) Bis ponitur in Graeco aperte, alter vocativus, alter nominativus. Iste unctus est, ille lapis quem Jacob unxit.

VERS. 9.-- Myrrha, etc. (CASS.) Hic laudat Propheta sponsum ab uxore et ornatu; primo ab ornatu. (AUG.) Myrrha et gutta. Odores bene adhibentur nuptiali thalamo, etc., usque ad id est, redemptio, per aquam baptismi. Eburneis. (HIER.) In ebore castitas, quod prius obscurum serris et limis lucidum fit, ita sancti per sectiones et attritiones diversorum suppliciorum elimati, virtutum varietate fiunt lucidi. Filiae regum. (AUG.) Terrenorum, non curantes honorem 910Dpatrum, etc., usque ad et ad semen excitandum susceperunt.

VERS. 10.-- Astitit regina, etc. (CASS.) Hic ab uxore commendat sponsum. Varietate. (Ibid.) Etsi sit unitas in charitate, tamen auro, id est, doctrina Apostolorum, cocco martyrum, gemmis virginum, purpura poenitentium ornatur.

VERS. 11.-- Audi, filia. (CASS.) Laus sponsae summissior, sed quadruplex, a forma, a gloria, ab adolescentulis, a prole. (AUG.) Audi, filia. Alloquitur Propheta reginam, tanquam unus de patribus. Judaei viderunt et occiderunt, tu audi Evangelium, et credendo videbis Deum: hic per imaginem, in futuro 911Aper speciem. Vel, Audi prophetias, quae incarnationem praedixerunt, et vide impletas.

VERS. 12.-- Et concupiscet rex. (CASS.) Hic laudat eam a forma.

VERS. 13.-- Tyri. (CASS.) Per Tyrum, vicinam Judaeae, gentes designantur; unde mulier Chananaea Ecclesiae figura. (CASS.) Tyri, gentium, a parte totum. In muneribus. (AUG.) Ut se offerant, etc., usque ad gentes scilicet, quae sunt in angustia peccatorum.

VERS. 14.-- Omnis gloria. (CASS.) A gloria sponsae, ut supra a potestate sponsi. Ab intus. (AUG.) Vel intrinsecus. Sit ergo eleemosyna in occulto, ubi Deus videt. Vel non in circumcisione manufacta, sicut in veteri lege, sed in spiritualibus. Fimbriis. (CASS.) Finis vestis significat finem mundi vel hominis. 911BAureis. Non deauratis, ut supra, sed aureis, quia in fine tota perfectio est, ubi charitas invenitur plena.

VERS. 15.-- Adducentur regi. (Ibid.) Hic laudatur sponsa ab amicabus, ut supra a judicio. (Ibid.) Adducentur, oportuna praedicatione. Post eam. (Ibid.) Prius unitas dicitur, post enumeratio partium est distincta, cum dicitur: Virgines et proximae.

VERS. 17.-- Pro patribus tuis nati sunt tibi filii. (Ibid.) Vel pro antiquis patribus, idolorum cultoribus, nati sunt Apostoli, principes praedicationis. (AUG.) Vel post prophetas Apostoli, post Apostolos alii.

Cantatur hic psalmus de festo beatae Mariae Virginis, quia quae de Ecclesia generaliter hic dicuntur, ad Mariam specialiter referri possunt. Cantatur etiam 911Cpro virginibus, quia ibi dicitur: Adducentur regi virgines. Et pro Apostolis, quia ubi dicitur: Nati sunt tibi filii. Item de nativitate Domini, quia ibi agitur de laude sponsi et sponsae et de nuptiis Christi et Ecclesiae, quarum desponsatio facta est in Verbi incarnatione.

PSALM XLIV.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end, etc. (AUG.) An epithalamium, that is, the praise of the bridal chamber. A canticle for those who are to be changed and for the beloved, that is, for the bride and the bridegroom, is written for the sons of Core, that they may venerate. For here is described through whom they shall be changed, because the praise of the bridegroom and of the bride is here sung. (CASS.) The Prophet promises that he will utter forth 909Cthe heraldings of God.

VERS. 2.-- It hath uttered forth. (AUG., HIER.) For the Prophet speaks within, etc., as far as before that is which he is about to do. But the counsel of the Father is the Word.

Good. By which all good things were made. I speak. That is, I bring forth the Word: the same here as before; but he says that in that very word are all the works of God; whence: What was made in him was life, so that nothing may be in the work which was not first in the counsel. Of this it is said: God hath spoken once.

A pen. He compares the Word not to sound, which passes away, but to writing, which remains. Or, swiftly, because not one thing after another, but all things together in one eternal Word.

Swiftly. The power of prophecy, which does not under 909Dhuman torment devise what it divulges to others out of the secret of the Godhead.

VERS. 3.-- Beautiful in form. (CASS.) He begins the praise of the bridegroom first from his form. He hath blessed. The former things the Prophet said in the person of God, these from his own; or all from himself. Or, he uttereth forth the word, who says a hymn to God.

I speak my works. (AUG.) to the praise of him who is from him. Tongue, a pen. Because what I say, I also write. Or, swiftly: because the things which I write are quickly to come.

(CASS.) In the lips. Because, when he spoke, the world received the grace of reconciliation.

VERS. 4.-- Gird thyself. (Ibid.) Here he praises him from his power; and do thou, being such, gird thyself.

VERS. 5.-- With thy comeliness and beauty. Comeliness to 910Athe humanity, in which he appeared to the world; beauty to the Deity, by which he adorns all things.

Attend. Pitying, look upon man as he perishes.

Prosperously. Setting men free.

Proceed. From the womb of the Virgin, as a bridegroom: or, from these conquered to others to be conquered.

Reign. Show thy power in the faith of men, thou who hast always reigned. And through this, because both through thyself and through thine own thou teachest the truth, by which thou destroyest our falsehood. And because meek in bearing with the wicked, as when he prayed for his enemies, so also his own: And because he showed the justice of life. And because it shall lead thee on without stumbling through the course of the whole life, or from people to people

Wonderfully. Because all shall wonder, or, because he will do miracles.

910BVERS. 6.-- The peoples shall fall under thee. (AUG.) That is, many of his enemies shall put themselves under him, and this by reason or by will. This is what the title said: For those who shall be changed out of the sons of Core. [Vulg. Ps 44:1 has no preposition and divides the clause: "pro iis qui commutabuntur. Filiis Core": "for those who shall be changed; for the sons of Core"] -- Into the hearts. (CASS.) Of thy enemies, that they may be friends, as Saul was.

VERS. 7.-- A throne. (Ibid.) Here from judgment: A throne pertains to judgment. A rod. (Ibid.) The rule of divine equity, which is truly straight and is never bent: this governs the just, strikes the unjust. (AUG.) Let no one presume much to himself concerning mercy, or flatter himself: because the rod of direction, if it governs some, crushes others: it governs the spiritual, it crushes the carnal.

VERS. 8.-- Thou hast loved. (Ibid.) Or, because thou hast loved justice, etc., these rewards have been rendered, he made thee king, 910Cgiving the name which is above every name.

And thou hast hated. If a man hates iniquity in himself, he acts with God: God hates iniquity, do thou also hate it.

O God. (AUG.) It is set twice openly in the Greek, the one a vocative, the other a nominative. This one is anointed, that one is the stone which Jacob anointed.

VERS. 9.-- Myrrh, etc. (CASS.) Here the Prophet praises the bridegroom from his wife and from his adornment; first from the adornment. (AUG.) Myrrh and stacte. Perfumes are fitly applied to the bridal chamber, etc., as far as that is, redemption, through the water of baptism. Of ivory. (HIER.) In ivory, chastity, which, being dark before, is made bright by saws and files; so the saints, filed down by the cuttings and rubbings of divers punishments, are made bright by the variety of virtues. The daughters of kings. (AUG.) Of earthly ones, not caring for the honour 910Dof their fathers, etc., as far as and they took them for the raising up of seed.

VERS. 10.-- The queen stood, etc. (CASS.) Here he commends the bridegroom from his wife. With variety. (Ibid.) Although there be unity in charity, yet she is adorned with gold, that is, the doctrine of the Apostles, with the scarlet of the martyrs, with the gems of virgins, with the purple of the penitent.

VERS. 11.-- Hear, O daughter. (CASS.) The praise of the bride is lower, but fourfold: from her form, from her glory, from the maidens, from her offspring. (AUG.) Hear, O daughter. The Prophet addresses the queen, as one of the fathers. The Jews saw and slew; do thou hear the Gospel, and by believing thou shalt see God: here through an image, in time to come 911Athrough sight. Or, Hear the prophecies which foretold the incarnation, and see them fulfilled.

VERS. 12.-- And the king shall desire. (CASS.) Here he praises her from her form.

VERS. 13.-- Of Tyre. (CASS.) By Tyre, the neighbour of Judaea, the Gentiles are designated; whence the Canaanite woman is a figure of the Church. (CASS.) Of Tyre, of the Gentiles, the whole from a part. With gifts. (AUG.) That they may offer themselves, etc., as far as the Gentiles, namely, who are in the straits of their sins.

VERS. 14.-- All the glory. (CASS.) From the glory of the bride, as above from the power of the bridegroom. From within. (AUG.) Or inwardly. Let almsgiving therefore be in secret, where God sees. Or not in a circumcision made by hand, as in the old law, but in spiritual things. In fringes. (CASS.) The end of the garment signifies the end of the world or of man. 911BGolden. Not gilded, as above, but golden, because in the end is the whole perfection, where charity is found full.

VERS. 15.-- They shall be brought to the king. (Ibid.) Here the bride is praised from her friends, as above from judgment. (Ibid.) They shall be brought, by opportune preaching. After her. (Ibid.) First unity is spoken of, afterward the enumeration of the parts is distinct, when it is said: Virgins and her neighbours. [Vulg. Ps 44:15 has no connective: "virgines post eam ; proximae ejus", "virgins after her; her neighbours"]

VERS. 17.-- Instead of thy fathers sons are born to thee. (Ibid.) Or in place of the ancient fathers, worshippers of idols, the Apostles were born, princes of preaching. (AUG.) Or after the prophets the Apostles, after the Apostles others.

This psalm is sung on the feast of blessed Mary the Virgin, because the things which are here said generally of the Church can be referred specially to Mary. It is sung also 911Cfor virgins, because it is there said: Virgins shall be brought to the king. And for the Apostles, because where it is said: Sons are born to thee. Likewise of the nativity of the Lord, because there it treats of the praise of the bridegroom and of the bride and of the nuptials of Christ and the Church, whose espousal was made in the incarnation of the Word.

PSALMUS XLV.

VERS. 1.-- In finem. (CASS.) Psalmus David, alicujus fidelis de Judaea, ut sit certius testimonium.

Pro arcanis. Pro manifestatione arcanorum, quod Deus sit homo, quod salus promissa utrique populo, quod caecitas contigit in Israel, quod Apostoli transierunt ad gentes, quod pax in terra; unde: Conflabunt gladios suos in vomeres et lanceas suas in falces 911D(Isa. II).

Filiis Core. (CASS.) Filii crucis. De arcanis, id est, de adventu Christi loquitur.

VERS. 2.-- Deus noster. (CASS., AUG.) In adventu Domini omnis spes habenda ostenditur, etiam in transitu Apostolorum ad gentes. Invenerunt nos nimis. (AUG.) Nos enim fugiebamus eas. Vel, invenerunt nos expositos per Adam. Nimis, tanto potentior qui liberat.

VERS. 3.-- Turbabitur terra, et transferentur montes, etc. (CASS.) Judaea, quasi arida: sine idololatria, amaritudine gentium circumdata. Vel, mare. (AUG.) saeculum.

Cor maris. Immanitas gentium

912AVERS. 4.-- Sonuerunt et turbatae, etc. Contradicentes, gentes: vel Apostoli praedicando.

Et turbatae sunt aquae eorum. Ad sensum fit relatio, non ad vocem: id est, aquae maris, scilicet populi, vel doctrinae eorum, quae infatuatae sunt, coruscante doctrina Salvatoris; unde: Absorpti sunt, etc. Et haec est virga Moysi, quae devoravit virgas Magorum.

VERS. 5.-- Fluminis impetus. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. Quia Ecclesia in Christo fundatur, cui gentes et regna subjiciuntur. (AUG.) Quasi dicat: Ita saevit mare; sed inter hos fluctus et sonitus non timent, qui ad illud refugium confugerunt.

VERS. 6.-- Adjuvabit eam. (CASS.) Vel, vultu, id est, demonstratione auxilii sui, cum adjuvando se 912Bindicat. Mane. In ipso boni operis principio; et hoc, diluculo, id est, per illuminationem sancti Spiritus, qui est lux quasi diei.

VERS. 7.-- Dedit. Quasi magnum praemium. Vocem. Praedicationem, ad quam tremuit terrenus. Tremet metu judicis.

VERS. 8.-- Dominus virtutum. (Ibid.) Breviter definit quid sit Christus. Nobiscum. Quasi: Qui misit angelos, jam ipse venit, et est nobiscum, quia nobiscum susceptor; ergo: Venite, quasi jam securos vos invito. Noster. Non nisi filiorum crucis. Deus Jacob. Qui tanta nobis dedit quanta dedit Jacob: non enim illius tantum est Deus.

VERS. 9.-- Venite et videte. (Ibid.) Diapsalmus. Magnalia incarnationis. Posuit. Quasi signa, ad vocandum 912Cpopulum. Prodigia. Ut de partu Virginis, et stella, et caeteris. Auferens bella. (AUG.) Quia per ejus adventum idololatria et superstitio totius orbis perit, vel, tunc temporis pro ejus praesentia orbis pacatus fuit.

VERS. 11.-- Vacate. (Ibid.) Si combusta sunt arma, vacate, non habentes unde pugnetis.

PSALM XLV.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end. (CASS.) A psalm of David, of some faithful man of Judea, that the testimony may be the more certain.

For the hidden things. For the manifestation of the hidden things, that God is man, that salvation is promised to both peoples, that blindness has befallen Israel, that the Apostles passed over to the Gentiles, that peace is on earth; whence: They shall turn their swords into ploughshares and their spears into sickles 911D(Isa. II).

For the sons of Core. (CASS.) The sons of the cross. Of the hidden things, that is, he speaks of the coming of Christ.

VERS. 2.-- Our God. (CASS., AUG.) In the coming of the Lord all hope is shown to be had, even in the passing over of the Apostles to the Gentiles. They have found us exceedingly. (AUG.) For we were fleeing them. Or, they have found us exposed through Adam. Exceedingly, by so much the more powerful is he who delivers.

VERS. 3.-- The earth shall be troubled, and the mountains shall be removed, etc. (CASS.) Judea, as it were dry land: without idolatry, hemmed about by the bitterness of the Gentiles. Or, the sea, (AUG.) the world.

The heart of the sea. The savagery of the Gentiles

912AVERS. 4.-- They have sounded, and are troubled, etc. Those who contradict, the Gentiles: or the Apostles by preaching.

And their waters were troubled. The reference is made to the sense, not to the word: that is, the waters of the sea, namely the peoples, or their doctrines, which have been made foolish, the doctrine of the Saviour flashing forth; whence: They were swallowed up, etc. And this is the rod of Moses, which devoured the rods of the Magi.

VERS. 5.-- The stream of the river. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. Because the Church is founded in Christ, to whom the nations and kingdoms are made subject. (AUG.) As if he should say: Thus the sea rages; but amid these waves and noises they fear not, who have fled to that refuge.

VERS. 6.-- He shall help her. (CASS.) Or, with his countenance, that is, by the showing forth of his help, when by helping he 912Bdeclares himself. In the morning. In the very beginning of a good work; and this, at daybreak, that is, through the illumination of the Holy Spirit, who is light as it were of day.

VERS. 7.-- He gave. As it were a great reward. His voice. Preaching, at which the earthly man trembled. He shall tremble for fear of the judge.

VERS. 8.-- The Lord of hosts. (Ibid.) Briefly he defines what Christ is. With us. As it were: He who sent the angels, now he himself has come, and is with us, because with us as our upholder; therefore: Come, as it were I invite you now secure. Ours. Not save of the sons of the cross. The God of Jacob. Who gave us as great things as he gave Jacob: for he is not the God of him alone.

VERS. 9.-- Come and see. (Ibid.) Diapsalmus. The mighty works of the incarnation. He hath set. As it were signs, for the calling of 912Cthe people. Prodigies. As concerning the birth from the Virgin, and the star, and the rest. Making wars to cease. (AUG.) Because through his coming the idolatry and superstition of the whole world perished, or, at that time for his presence the world was at peace.

VERS. 11.-- Be still. (Ibid.) If the arms are burnt up, be still, not having wherewith you may fight.

PSALMUS XLVI.

VERS. 2.-- Omnes gentes. (AUG.) Quasi diceret: insultant, pueri, dicentes: Calve, calve, vos omnes gentes ad quas transivit gratia: Plaudite, etc. Gentes ad quas transivit gratia, et quos in priori psalmo ad fidem vocavit, invitat ad laudem.

VERS. 3.-- Excelsus. (HIER.) Potens quod vult. 912DTerribilis. (REMIG.) Quia judicaturus in potestate.

VERS. 4.-- Subjecit populos nobis. (CASS.) Hoc hominibus fidelibus convenit, quibus omnes extrinseci subjecti sunt, vel, sibi subjecit nobis associandos. Populos, Judaeos. Nobis. (Ibid.) Universali scilicet Ecclesiae; hoc dicere convenit omnibus fidelibus, quibus extrinseci subjecti sunt. Sub pedibus. (Ibid.) Per pedes, praedicatores accipe, quibus populi subjecti sunt. (AUG.) Sub pedibus. Sic est exaltata Ecclesia, ut nondum credentes sub pedibus habeat.

VERS. 5.-- Elegit nobis, etc. Vel in persona Apostolorum, elegit nobis dare haereditatem suam, multorum populorum, ut colamus eam, gladio praedicationis corda eorum ferientes, et malitiam destruentes. 913AHaereditatem. (AUG.) Coelestis haereditas, pulchritudo est Christiani populi, in qua speciosus erit fulgens ut sol, qui nunc est abjectus. Speciem Jacob quam, etc. Id est, similes Jacob vel signatos per Jacob, qui terrena dant pro coelestibus, ut Jacob fecit, quod fuit gratia Dei, quia eum dilexit, Esau reprobato.

VERS. 6.-- Ascendit. (CASS.) Diapsalma ascensio et regnum Dei describitur, unde instanter monet psallere. In jubilo. (AUG.) Gaudium admirantium Apostolorum, etc., usque ad quod nec taceri potest, nec exprimi valet.

VERS. 7.-- Psallite. (CASS.) Operibus laudate: valde est salutare quod tam crebro repetitur, quia Deus est qui creat, et rex creata gubernans.

VERS. 8.-- Omnis. (Ibid.) Non ut Jupiter Cretae, 913BMars Thraciae. Sapienter. Docet quomodo sit psallendum. Olim sine sensu psallebant, dum lapides colerent. (AUG.) Nemo sapienter facit quod non intelligit.

VERS. 9.-- Regnabit. (Ibid.) Modo impleta est haec prophetia: Deus sedet super sedem sanctam. Sedem sanctam. (AUG.) Throni, Virtutes, et sancti.

VERS. 10.-- Principes populorum. (CASS.) Primitivi omnium gentium convenerunt credendo in Christo, quia, expulsis Judaeis, gentes in filios Abrahae succedunt, habentes promissionem, quia Judaei superbierunt. (HIER., CASS.) Vel dii fortes, Apostoli scilicet, quos neque mors, neque vita separabit a charitate Christi. Elevati, miraculis et doctrina.

PSALM XLVI.

VERS. 2.-- All ye Gentiles. (AUG.) As if he should say: they insult, the boys, saying: Bald head, bald head, you, all the Gentiles to whom grace has passed over: Clap your hands, etc. The Gentiles to whom grace has passed over, and whom in the former psalm he called to faith, he invites to praise.

VERS. 3.-- High. (HIER.) Powerful in what he wills. 912DTerrible. (REMIG.) Because he is to judge in power.

VERS. 4.-- He hath subdued the peoples unto us. (CASS.) This befits faithful men, to whom all outsiders are made subject, or, he has subjected to himself those who are to be associated with us. The peoples, the Jews. Unto us. (Ibid.) Namely to the universal Church; this it befits all the faithful to say, to whom outsiders are made subject. Under the feet. (Ibid.) By feet, understand preachers, to whom the peoples are made subject. (AUG.) Under the feet. So is the Church exalted, that it has those not yet believing under its feet.

VERS. 5.-- He hath chosen for us, etc. Or in the person of the Apostles, he chose to give us his inheritance, of many peoples, that we may cultivate it, striking their hearts with the sword of preaching, and destroying their malice. 913AThe inheritance. (AUG.) The heavenly inheritance is the beauty of the Christian people, in which he shall be comely, shining as the sun, who now is abject. The beauty of Jacob which, etc. That is, those like to Jacob or signed by Jacob, who give earthly things for heavenly, as Jacob did, which was the grace of God, because he loved him, Esau being reprobate.

VERS. 6.-- He is ascended. (CASS.) Diapsalma, the ascension and the kingdom of God is described, whence he urgently admonishes to sing psalms. In jubilation. (AUG.) The joy of the wondering Apostles, etc., as far as what can neither be kept silent nor be uttered.

VERS. 7.-- Sing ye psalms. (CASS.) Praise by works: very salutary is that which is so often repeated, because it is God who creates, and a king governing the things created.

VERS. 8.-- Of all the earth. (Ibid.) Not as Jupiter of Crete, 913BMars of Thrace. Wisely. He teaches how one ought to sing psalms. Of old they sang psalms without understanding, while they worshipped stones. (AUG.) No one does wisely what he does not understand.

VERS. 9.-- He shall reign. (Ibid.) Now is this prophecy fulfilled: God sitteth upon the holy seat. The holy seat. (AUG.) Thrones, Virtues, and the saints.

VERS. 10.-- The princes of the peoples. (CASS.) The first-fruits of all the Gentiles came together by believing in Christ, because, the Jews being cast out, the Gentiles succeed into the sons of Abraham, having the promise, because the Jews were lifted up in pride. (HIER., CASS.) Or the strong gods, namely the Apostles, whom neither death nor life shall separate from the charity of Christ. Lifted up, by miracles and doctrine.

PSALMUS XLVII.

  • 913C

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus vel laus cantici filiis Core secunda, etc. (AUG.) Primo die, fecit Deus lucem, etc., usque ad de qua hic cantatur filiis Core. (CASS.) De fundatione civitatis, quam commendative describit. (AUG.) Commendat civitatem, etc., usque ad a stabilitate aeterna.

VERS. 2.-- In monte sancto, etc. (Ibid.) Hic est mons ille, etc., usque ad super quem fundata est Ecclesia.

VERS. 3.-- Fundatur exsultatione. (HIER.) Quasi dicat, quae prius maledictionibus subjecta, etc., usque ad ipse est Christus, qui per universam Ecclesiam gaudia dilatat. Mons Sion latera. (AUG.) Quicunque 913Dalicui haerent, latera ejus dicuntur, etc., usque ad item ab aquilone pandetur omne malum, etc.

VERS. 4.-- In domibus. Vel, in gradibus, id est, secundum gradus meritorum, quia in singulis distinctim dabit cognitionem sui. Cum suscipiet eam. Tutandam, et quid opus est? Quoniam reges contra. Sed videntes per fidem, sic scilicet quod tam digna est haec civitas admirati sunt, etc.

VERS. 5.-- Reges. (AUG., CASS.) Principes Judaeorum. Congregati. Ab Herode sciscitante locum nativitatis. Convenerunt. Concorditer dicendo: In Bethlehem Judae secundum Scripturas.

VERS. 6.-- Videntes. Quae in prophetis legerant. Admirati sunt. De tanta gloria, non leviter vel otiose. 914ASed conturbati. Pro peccato, et Commoti sunt. Ad fidem, et tantus fuit pavor, ut corpus tremeret.

VERS. 7.-- Ibi dolores ut parturientis, Poenitentiae, videntes ita; sed:

VERS. 8.-- In spiritu vehementi, Herodis. Conteres naves Tharsis. Quia, in Tharso, Ciliciae naves quae Magos transposuisse in patriam suam credebantur, confractae sunt ab Herode. Tharsis. (AUG.) Cilicia regio a Tharso, etc., usque ad decursis omnibus concludit. Ergo:

VERS. 9.-- Sicut audivimus. In civitate Domini virtutum, quia ibi custodes angelos deputat. Repetit. In civitate Domini virtutum, in civitate Dei nostri. Id est, Catholica Ecclesia, ne sibi hoc nomen conventus haereticorum usurpet. Ne autem putetur temporalis, 914Baddit: Deus fundavit eam in aeternum. Non ad horam, ut prius tabernaculum Moysi

VERS. 10.-- Suscepimus, Deus, misericordiam tuam. (CASS.) Agens gratias de adventu Christi, monet de gradibus Ecclesiae distribuendis, per quos Salvator possit agnosci. In medio templi. Jerusalem: gravius accusantur, qui contemnunt eum, qui in medio eorum conspectus est. Per hoc notatur incarnatio Christi, qui secundum quod homo, praesentatus est in templo.

VERS. 11.-- Dextera. (CASS.) Hac parte justi locantur.

(AUG.) Suscepimus, Deus. Quo ordine fundata, vel quod audivimus et vidimus. Templi tui. (Ibid.) Id est, populi non sucipientis misericordiam, qui multis: 914Cut nulla videantur esse grana, sed tamen nonnulla, quia secundum nomen. Secundum nomen. (CASS.) Quod ubique diffusum est, quia nullus est, et si nesciat cultum, qui huic nomini non se subjiciat. Vel secundum nomen. Hoc est, sicut reverentia tui nominis, etc., usque ad tua propitiatio justificavit multos, qui omnes laudant.

VERS. 12.-- Laetetur. (AUG.) Etsi laborent justi inter spinas, etc., usque ad eorum est modo colligere, Dei est separare. Mons Sion et exsultent. (CASS.) Ecclesia, quae est in speculatione populi. Filiae Judae propter judicia tua, Domine. Sanctae feminae. Per Judam, gens earum ostenditur, quae est propter Christum, qui de Juda, et hae exsultent, ut in utroque sexu Ecclesia sit. (AUG.) Causa laetitiae judicia 914Dfutura, ubi se sciunt ad beatitudinem venturas. Qui intus sunt, laetentur; vos qui extra, circumdate.

VERS. 13.-- Circumdate. Honores exhibendo. Complectimini eam. Charitate. Narrate in turribus ejus. Ponite corda vestra. (CASS.) Praedicate aliis in concordia Apostolorum, etc., usque ad ne per laetitiam remissi lentescant.

VERS. 14.-- Virtute ejus. (AUG.) Virtus civitatis charitas est, quam nihil vincit; unde Salomon: Dilectio fortis est ut mors. (CASS.) In virtute Ecclesiae monet ponere corda. Distribuite domos ejus, ut enarretis in progenie altera. Id est, officia distincta, etc., usque ad quem primum Dominus elegit.

VERS. 15.-- Quoniam hic est, etc. Hoc est quod 915Anarrandum est, brevis sententia, sed quae omnia concludi. In aeternum, contra illos qui temporales homines Deos faciebant.

PSALM XLVII.

  • 913C

VERS. 1.-- A psalm, or the praise of a canticle, for the sons of Core, the second, etc. (AUG.) On the first day, God made light, etc., as far as of which it is here sung to the sons of Core. (CASS.) Concerning the founding of the city, which he describes commendingly. (AUG.) He commends the city, etc., as far as from its eternal stability.

VERS. 2.-- In the holy mount, etc. (Ibid.) This is that mountain, etc., as far as upon which the Church is founded.

VERS. 3.-- It is founded with the joy. (HIER.) As if he should say, she who before was subject to curses, etc., as far as he himself is Christ, who through the universal Church spreads joys abroad. Mount Sion, the sides. (AUG.) Whosoever 913Dcleave to anyone are called his sides, etc., as far as likewise from the north shall every evil be spread abroad, etc.

VERS. 4.-- In the houses. Or, in the degrees, that is, according to the degrees of merits, because in each one severally he will give the knowledge of himself. When he shall receive her. To be guarded, and what need is there? For the kings against. But seeing by faith, namely thus, that this city is so worthy, they wondered, etc.

VERS. 5.-- The kings. (AUG., CASS.) The princes of the Jews. Being gathered together. By Herod inquiring the place of the nativity. They came together. Saying with one accord: In Bethlehem of Juda according to the Scriptures.

VERS. 6.-- Seeing. The things which they had read in the prophets. They wondered. At so great glory, not lightly or idly. 914ABut they were troubled. For sin, and They were moved. To faith, and so great was the dread, that the body trembled.

VERS. 7.-- There pains as of a woman in labour, Of penance, seeing thus; but:

VERS. 8.-- With a vehement spirit, Of Herod. Thou shalt break the ships of Tharsis. Because, in Tharsus, the ships of Cilicia which were believed to have carried the Magi over into their own country, were broken by Herod. Tharsis. (AUG.) Cilicia is a region named from Tharsus, etc., as far as having run through all he concludes. Therefore:

VERS. 9.-- As we have heard. In the city of the Lord of hosts, because there he appoints angels as guards. He repeats. In the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God. That is, the Catholic Church, lest the assembly of heretics usurp this name to itself. But lest it be thought temporal, 914Bhe adds: God hath founded it for ever. Not for an hour, as before the tabernacle of Moses

VERS. 10.-- We have received, O God, thy mercy. (CASS.) Giving thanks for the coming of Christ, he admonishes concerning the degrees of the Church that are to be distributed, through which the Saviour may be known. In the midst of the temple. Jerusalem: they are the more grievously accused, who despise him who was beheld in the midst of them. By this the incarnation of Christ is noted, who according as he is man was presented in the temple.

VERS. 11.-- The right hand. (CASS.) On this side the just are placed.

(AUG.) We have received, O God. In what order she was founded, or what we have heard and seen. Of thy temple. (Ibid.) That is, of a people not receiving sucipientis mercy, who to many: 914Cso that no grains seem to be there, but nevertheless some, because according to the name. According to the name. (CASS.) Which is everywhere spread abroad, because there is none, even if he know not the worship, who does not submit himself to this name. Or according to the name. This is, as the reverence of thy name, etc., as far as thy propitiation hath justified many, who all praise thee.

VERS. 12.-- Let it be glad. (AUG.) Although the just labour among thorns, etc., as far as it is theirs now to gather, God's to separate. Mount Sion, and let them rejoice. (CASS.) The Church, which is in the beholding of the people. The daughters of Juda, because of thy judgments, O Lord. Holy women. By Juda their nation is shown, which is on account of Christ, who is of Juda, and let these rejoice, that in both sexes the Church may be. (AUG.) The cause of gladness is the judgments 914Dto come, wherein they know that they shall come to blessedness. Let those who are within be glad; you who are without, encompass.

VERS. 13.-- Encompass. By showing honours. Embrace her. With charity. Tell in her towers. Set your hearts. (CASS.) Preach to others in the concord of the Apostles, etc., as far as lest, being remiss through gladness, they grow slack.

VERS. 14.-- Her strength. (AUG.) The strength of the city is charity, which nothing overcomes; whence Solomon: Love is strong as death. (CASS.) He admonishes to set the hearts on the strength of the Church. Distribute her houses, that you may relate it in another generation. That is, the offices distinguished, etc., as far as whom the Lord first chose.

VERS. 15.-- For this is, etc. This is what 915Amust be related, a brief sentence, but one which concludes all things. For ever, against those who made temporal men gods.

PSALMUS XLVIII.

In finem, psalmus, etc. (CASS.) Agit Propheta de amatoribus mundi, et Christo redemptore, non illorum, sed contemptorum mundi, ut dejectus in mundo non appretietur elatos. (AUG.) Qui colunt Deum, etc., usque ad attentos facit ad nova et ad ingentia.

VERS. 2.-- Odite haec, omnes gentes. (CASS.) Nullum excipio, etc., usque ad quando scilicet separabuntur zizania a tritico, oves ab haedis.

VERS. 3.-- Quique terrigenae. ((AUG.) Nulli sermonem subtraho, audiat haeres terrae, propter judicium: 915Bjustus, propter regnum.

VERS. 4.-- Os meum loquetur. (CASS.) Commendat dicenda. Sapientia ad divinas res, Prudentia ad mores instruendos; in his duobus omnis sermo divinus indicatur.

VERS. 5.-- Inclinabo. (HIER.) Humiliabo me veritati intus loquenti, quae docet loqui in parabolis, ne omnibus pateat.

VERS. 6.-- Cur timebo. (CASS.) Incipit narrare quae promisit, dicens quod Christus non redimet impios; hic propheta, in sua persona generalem agens causam, quaerit causam damnationis et timoris malorum, quae est iniquitas. (AUG.) Cur timebo? quasi non est quod timeam, cum iniquitatem vitare sit in mea potestate; pro qua tantum timebitur in die 915Cnovissima, quae erit mala damnatis, non justis. Calcanei. (Ibid.) Alludit verbis, etc., usque ad id est, opprimet et timere faciet.

VERS. 7.-- Qui confidunt. Hi, scilicet, qui confidunt, etc., usque ad in quibus adeo stulti sunt.

VERS. 8.-- Frater non redimit. Si frater, id est Christus, non redimit, etc., usque ad quia talis non dat Deo placationem.

VERS. 9.-- Et vivet adhuc. (Ibid.) Post finem vitae, vivet secundum animam, quia non peribit anima cum corpore, sed dolori salvabitur, usquequo accepto corpore utrinque crucietur.

VERS. 11.-- Non videbit. (Ibid.) Id est non intelligit, etc., usque ad cum sapiens transit vitam. Vel, insipiens. (Ibid.) Qui non attendit. Stultus. Qui, si attendit, non 915Dcavet. Divitias (CASS.) Propter quas fecerunt mala. Suas: quae non secundum Deum.

VERS. 12.-- Vocaverunt nomina sua. (AUG.) Haeredes, qui ad sepulcra mortuorum inebriant se in memoriam eorum, sed nec gutta pervenit ad linguam in inferno ardentis.

VERS. 13.-- Et homo cum. Et tam in hoc, quam in caeteris, homo non intelligit; vel, inde non est accusandus Deus, non intellexit suam dignitatem, non intelligenter egit, sed comparatus, amissa ratione, jumentis, non in alia re, sed in sapientia.

VERS. 14.-- Haec via. (CASS.) Hic jam omnia dicta colligit, in unum. Via, id est, vita, quia ducit ad mortem. Scandalum. Stimulus et dolor, etc., usque 916Aad: Populus hic labiis me honorat, cor autem eorum longe est a me. In ore suo complacebunt. (AUG.) Cum tales sint, etc., usque ad et pejores sunt apertis malis.

VERS. 15.-- Sicut oves. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. Quae impiis angustia reddenda. Se jactant, sed mihi jam constat quod in inferno positi sunt. Oves, amissa lana, manent, sic in istis, sine consumptione substantiae, poena invenit quod cruciet. Mors. (AUG.) Ut Christus vita, ita diabolus mors; qui pastor est eis, ut ovibus, quas trahit ad pascua mortis. Depascet. (CASS.) A similitudine jumentorum, etc., usque ad de poena ad poenam ducet. In matutino. (AUG.) Quia modo nox, dum non apparent merita justorum, et quasi felicitas nominatur impiorum. Veterascet in 916Binferno a gloria eorum, etc. (AUG.) Quantam visus est habere gloriam, etc., usque ad: A gloria sua expulsi sunt.

VERS. 17.-- Ne timueris. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. Admonitio, ne timeantur potentes, qui omnia cum luce relinquunt. Cur enim haec peccatoribus permissa sint, communis querela est. Dives factus. Haec enim et abjecti habent. Gloria. In honoribus saeculi. Domus. Quia non solum ipse, sed omnes qui ad eum pertinent.

VERS. 19.-- Benedicetur. (Ibid.) Non de bono actu, sed de deliciis benedicetur, favore luxuriantium, qui inter epulas pastoribus bene optant. Confitebitur tibi cum benefeceris ei. (AUG.) Despecta confessione, quam prosperitas facit; sed illa est 916Cmagni meriti, quam non tollit vis doloris.

VERS. 20.-- In progenies patrum. (Ibid.) Qui patres sequuntur pessimos, eorum societate damnandi sunt.

Et homo. (CASS.) Iterat deformitatem hominis ut malus a malo quiescat.

PSALM XLVIII.

Unto the end, a psalm, etc. (CASS.) The Prophet treats of the lovers of the world, and of Christ the redeemer, not of those, but of the despisers of the world, that he who is cast down in the world may not set a price upon the exalted. (AUG.) They who worship God, etc., as far as he makes them attentive to new things and to mighty things.

VERS. 2.-- Hate these things, all ye nations. [Vulg. Ps 48:2 Audite haec, omnes gentes, "Hear these things, all ye nations"] (CASS.) I except none, etc., as far as when, namely, the cockle shall be separated from the wheat, the sheep from the goats.

VERS. 3.-- And ye that are earthborn. ((AUG.) I withhold my speech from none, let the heir of the earth hear, because of the judgment: 915Bthe just man, because of the kingdom.

VERS. 4.-- My mouth shall speak. (CASS.) He commends the things to be said. Wisdom for divine things, Prudence for instructing morals; in these two the whole divine discourse is signified.

VERS. 5.-- I will incline. (HIER.) I will humble myself to the truth speaking within, which teaches to speak in parables, lest it lie open to all.

VERS. 6.-- Why shall I fear. (CASS.) He begins to narrate the things he promised, saying that Christ will not redeem the ungodly; here the prophet, in his own person pleading a general cause, seeks the cause of the damnation and the fear of the wicked, which is iniquity. (AUG.) Why shall I fear? as though there is not what I should fear, since to avoid iniquity is in my own power; for that alone shall there be fear in the 915Clast day, which shall be evil to the damned, not to the just. Of the heel. (Ibid.) He alludes to the words, etc., as far as that is, it shall oppress and shall make to fear.

VERS. 7.-- They that trust. These, namely, who trust, etc., as far as in which they are so foolish.

VERS. 8.-- A brother doth not redeem. If a brother, that is Christ, does not redeem, etc., as far as because such a one gives not to God a propitiation.

VERS. 9.-- And shall live still. (Ibid.) After the end of life, he shall live according to the soul, because the soul shall not perish with the body, but shall be saved unto grief, until, the body being received, he be tormented on both sides.

VERS. 11.-- He shall not see. (Ibid.) That is, he does not understand, etc., as far as when the wise man passes through life. Or, the unwise. (Ibid.) Who attends not. The fool. Who, if he attends, does not 915Dbeware. Riches (CASS.) For the sake of which they did evil. His own: which are not according to God.

VERS. 12.-- They have called their names. (AUG.) The heirs, who at the sepulchres of the dead make themselves drunk in memory of them, but neither does a drop reach the tongue of him that burns in hell.

VERS. 13.-- And man when. And both in this, and in the rest, man does not understand; or, therefore God is not to be accused, he understood not his own dignity, he acted not understandingly, but was compared, reason being lost, to beasts, not in another thing, but in wisdom.

VERS. 14.-- This way. (CASS.) Here now he gathers into one all that has been said. Way, that is, life, because it leads to death. A stumbling block. A goad and a grief, etc., as far 916Aas: This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. In their own mouth they shall be well pleased. (AUG.) Since they are such, etc., as far as and they are worse than open evils.

VERS. 15.-- Like sheep. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. What straitness is to be rendered to the ungodly. They boast themselves, but to me it is already clear that they are placed in hell. Sheep, their wool being lost, remain, so in these, without the consuming of their substance, punishment finds what it may torment. Death. (AUG.) As Christ is life, so the devil is death; who is a shepherd to them, as to sheep, whom he draws to the pastures of death. He shall feed upon. (CASS.) From the likeness of beasts, etc., as far as he shall lead them from punishment to punishment. In the morning. (AUG.) Because now it is night, while the merits of the just do not appear, and the felicity of the ungodly is as it were named. He shall grow old in 916Bhell from their glory, etc. (AUG.) How great glory he seemed to have, etc., as far as: From his own glory they were cast out.

VERS. 17.-- Fear not. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. An admonition, that the powerful be not feared, who leave all things behind with the light. For why these things are permitted to sinners, is a common complaint. He is made rich. For these things the abject also have. Glory. In the honours of the world. House. Because not he only, but all who pertain to him.

VERS. 19.-- He shall be blessed. (Ibid.) Not for a good act, but for delights shall he be blessed, by the favour of the luxurious, who amid banquets wish well to those who feed them. He will praise thee when thou shalt do well to him. (AUG.) Despised is the confession which prosperity makes; but that is of 916Cgreat merit, which the force of grief takes not away.

VERS. 20.-- Into the generations of his fathers. (Ibid.) They who follow the worst fathers are to be damned by their fellowship.

And man. (CASS.) He repeats the deformity of man, that the evil man may rest from evil.

PSALMUS XLIX.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus Asaph. (HIER.) Asaph, Latine congregatio; Graece, synagoga, quae fidelis hic loquitur, quae Christum exspectat, per quam magis confutantur increduli Judaei. (CASS.) Asaph, vocem Dei inducturus de mutatione sacrificiorum, prius agit de utroque adventu per primum invitans, per secundum terrens. Deus Deorum. (CASS.) Ne quis mediocriter 916Dde incarnatione aestimet, etc., usque ad nuncupative, ut falsi dii, Jupiter, Venus. Locutus est, et vocavit terram. (AUG.) Per se, per praecones. A solis ortu usque ad occasum. (CASS.) Quasi dicat, etc., usque ad: exibit de Sion lex, et Verbum Domini de Jerusalem.

VERS. 2.-- Ex Sion, species decoris ejus, etc. (AUG.) Coepit decus Evangelii, etc., usque ad ut testes essent in Jerusalem et in tota terra.

VERS. 3, 4.-- Ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet et in circumitu ejus. (Ibid.) Ante eum praeibit; poena ergo terreat, quos praemia non invitant, etc., usque ad malos comitabitur ad inferos. Tempesta valida. Advocabit coelum desursum, et terram. (CASS.) Non ventus, etc., usque ad prius omnes communiter vocavit, 917Atunc vocabit ut discernat. Discernere populum suum. (AUG.) Primo commistos vocavit a solis ortu usque ad occasum, tunc autem ut discernat.

VERS. 5.-- Congregate illi sanctos ejus. (Ibid.) Videns Propheta futura, etc., usque ad de malis dicitur, de quo non implevit manum suam. Qui ordinant testamentum ejus super sacrificia. (Ibid.). Novum Testamentum super Vetus, etc., usque ad qui pluris habent opere charitatis quam sacrificia pecudum.

VERS. 6.-- Et annuntiabunt coeli justitiam ejus, etc. (Ibid.) Jam coeli nuntiaverunt nobis hanc justitiam Dei, etc., usque ad et si nunc permista, quia Deus est judex justus.

VERS. 7.-- Audi, populus meus, etc. (CASS.) Vox Christi, ut, relictis sacrificiis pecudum, fiat sacrificium laudis. (AUG.) Vel, repetit sub alio verbo, Audi 917Bsicut Israel, id est, sicut videns Deum, et Testificabor, haec, scilicet, Deus tuus ego sum.

Deus tuus. (AUG.) Prius dicit simpliciter: Sum Deus. Et postea dicit: Sum Deus tuus. Quasi diceret: Etsi non sum Deus tuus, tamen sum Deus. Bono enim meo sum Deus, malo autem tuo non sum Deus tuus. Sum. (CASS.) Esse est proprium Deitatis. Audi, Israel. (Ibid.) Quasi diceret: Si es Israel, id est, si me vides, audire non negligis. Deus ille generalis, Deus tuus proprie.

VERS. 8.-- Holocausta autem. (AUG.) Si anima inflammatur, et membra in usum suum rapit, ne serviant cupiditati: unde praecipitur in Levitico, ut adipem cum renunculis offerant, quibus interna 917Ccharitas signatur.

VERS. 9.-- Non accipiam, etc. (CASS.) Etsi sic feceris: Non accipiam de domo tua vitulos, quasi significatos acciperem, non illos de domo. Quoniam meae: ac si diceret, quia non sunt tua, sed mea. Quoniam meae sunt, etc. (AUG.) Mea sunt quae non possides, indomita, scilicet: Ferae silvarum, jumenta, boves, etc. (CASS.) Hic similitudinibus figurat Ecclesiam, etc., usque ad: Carnes taurorum non vult in sacrificiis, sed in pauperibus.

VERS, 11.-- Cognovi omnia volatilia. (AUG.) Cum illo sunt omnia, cognitione quadam ineffabilis sapientiae.

VERS. 12.-- Si esuriero, non. (Ibid.) Si haec datis forsitan esurire putatis, quod est insania?

917DVERS. 13.-- Nunquid manducabo carnes taurorum? Olim haec sacrificabantur, non ideo quod Deus inde delectaretur, sed ne daemonibus offerentur, et tantum Deo sacrificabantur, in quibus erat aliqua significatio.

Immola Deo. (CASS.) Non dicit mihi, sed de se, quasi de alio ut et post: Peccatori autem dixit, Deus, non ego.

VERS. 15.-- Tribulationis. (AUG.) Nostra tribulatio proprie est timore salutis, non carnalium.

VERS. 16.-- Peccatori autem. (Ibid.) A quibus sacrificium velit, ubi peccatori suae nequitiae imputantur

918A(CASS.) Haec populo suo dixit, etc., usque ad Non enim lectio negatur corrigendis.

VERS. 17.-- Tu vero odisti. (Ibid.) Tu vero ore dicis, sed facto negas disciplinam: si corrigo, murmuras.

Furem, currebas. (Ibid.) In his omnia tonat vitia; a parte totum, vel furem sani intellectus Scripturae. Adulteris. Qui ponunt falsum, auferendo verum.

VERS. 19.-- Os tuum abundavit, etc. (Ibid.) Accusat conscientiam, et linguam, etc., usque ad non casu alii derogat, sed studio.

VERS. 20.-- Sedens. (Ibid.) Quod transiens vel stans facit, non cum voluntate facit. Fratrem. (Ibid.) Omnem hominem. Et adversus filium matris, Ecclesiae, cui charitate jungimur. Ponebas scandalum, haereses vel alia quibus innocens capiatur.

918BLoquebaris adversus. (AUG.) Dum detrahit qui doctus videtur, etc., usque ad validioris doctrinae cibo.

Tui similis. (CASS.) Consentiendo malis.

Statuam contra tuam. (AUG.) Quod post dorsum posuisti, ante faciem ponam.

VERS. 22.-- Rapiat. (CASS.) Deus ad poenam, et non sit qui eripiat. Quando diabolus rapit, Deus eripit; sed cum Deus rapit, nemo valet liberare.

VERS. 23.-- Sacrificium laudis. (CASS.) Non quod scelerati cantant, sacrificium laudis, non animalium. Et haec est via ad Deum, scala Jacob, qua angeli, id est, fideles, ascendunt ad laudem divinitatis, et descendunt ad laudem humanitatis. Illic iter quo, etc. (Ibid.) In sacrificio laudis. Salutare Dei. (AUG.) Christus, qui cum gratia venit, quem novit, qui aliquid 918Calii quam gratiae Dei attribuit.

PSALM XLIX.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of Asaph. (HIER.) Asaph, in Latin a congregation; in Greek, a synagogue, which here speaks as faithful, which awaits Christ, through which the unbelieving Jews are the more confuted. (CASS.) Asaph, about to bring in the voice of God concerning the change of the sacrifices, first treats of both comings, by the first inviting, by the second terrifying. God of gods. (CASS.) Lest anyone think meanly 916Dof the incarnation, etc., as far as by way of appellation, as the false gods, Jupiter, Venus. He hath spoken, and hath called the earth. (AUG.) By himself, by heralds. From the rising of the sun unto the going down. (CASS.) As if he should say, etc., as far as: the law shall come forth from Sion, and the Word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

VERS. 2.-- Out of Sion, the loveliness of his beauty, etc. (AUG.) The comeliness of the Gospel began, etc., as far as that they might be witnesses in Jerusalem and in the whole earth.

VERS. 3, 4.-- Fire shall blaze in his sight and round about him. (Ibid.) It shall go before him; let punishment therefore terrify those whom rewards do not invite, etc., as far as it shall accompany the wicked to hell. A mighty tempest. He shall call heaven from above, and the earth. Tempesta (CASS.) Not a wind, etc., as far as first he called all in common, 917Athen he shall call that he may separate. To judge his people. (AUG.) First he called the mingled from the rising of the sun unto the going down, but then that he may separate.

VERS. 5.-- Gather ye together his saints unto him. (Ibid.) The Prophet seeing things to come, etc., as far as it is said of the wicked, of whom he hath not filled his hand. Who set his covenant above sacrifices. (Ibid.). The New Testament above the Old, etc., as far as who hold the works of charity of more worth than the sacrifices of cattle.

VERS. 6.-- And the heavens shall declare his justice, etc. (Ibid.) Already the heavens have declared to us this justice of God, etc., as far as and if now things are mingled, because God is a just judge.

VERS. 7.-- Hear, O my people, etc. (CASS.) The voice of Christ, that, the sacrifices of cattle being left, there may be made a sacrifice of praise. (AUG.) Or, he repeats under another word, Hear 917Bas Israel, that is, as one seeing God, and I will testify, these things, namely, I am thy God.

Thy God. (AUG.) First he says simply: I am God. And afterwards he says: I am thy God. As if he should say: Even if I am not thy God, yet I am God. For to my own good I am God, but to thy evil I am not thy God. I am. (CASS.) To be is proper to the Deity. Hear, O Israel. (Ibid.) As if he should say: If thou art Israel, that is, if thou seest me, thou dost not neglect to hear. That God is general, thy God properly.

VERS. 8.-- But the holocausts. (AUG.) If the soul is inflamed, and seizes the members into its own use, that they may not serve concupiscence: whence it is commanded in Leviticus, that they offer the fat with the little kidneys, by which the inward 917Ccharity is signified.

VERS. 9.-- I will not take, etc. (CASS.) Even if thou shalt so do: I will not take calves out of thy house, as though I took the things signified, not those out of the house. For mine are: as if he should say, because they are not thine, but mine. For mine are, etc. (AUG.) Mine are the things which thou dost not possess, the untamed, namely: The beasts of the woods, the cattle, the oxen, etc. (CASS.) By these likenesses he figures the Church, etc., as far as: The flesh of bullocks he wills not in sacrifices, but in the poor.

VERS, 11.-- I know all the fowls. (AUG.) With him are all things, by a certain knowledge of ineffable wisdom.

VERS. 12.-- If I should be hungry, I would not. (Ibid.) If you give these things, perhaps you think that I hunger, which is madness?

917DVERS. 13.-- Shall I eat the flesh of bullocks? Of old these things were sacrificed, not for this reason that God was delighted therein, but lest they should be offered to demons, and they were sacrificed to God only, in which there was some signification.

Sacrifice to God. (CASS.) He says not "to me," but of himself, as of another, as also afterwards: But to the sinner God hath said, not I.

VERS. 15.-- Of tribulation. (AUG.) Our tribulation is properly by the fear of salvation, not of carnal things.

VERS. 16.-- But to the sinner. (Ibid.) From whom he would have sacrifice, where to the sinner his own wickednesses are imputed

918A(CASS.) These things he said to his own people, etc., as far as For reading is not denied to those who are to be corrected.

VERS. 17.-- But thou hast hated. (Ibid.) But thou sayest with the mouth, and deniest discipline in deed: if I correct, thou murmurest.

The thief, thou didst run. (Ibid.) In these he thunders against all vices; the whole from a part, or the thief of the sound understanding of Scripture. With adulterers. Who set down the false, by taking away the true.

VERS. 19.-- Thy mouth hath abounded, etc. (Ibid.) He accuses the conscience, and the tongue, etc., as far as he detracts from another not by chance, but of set purpose.

VERS. 20.-- Sitting. (Ibid.) What he does passing by or standing, he does not do with the will. Brother. (Ibid.) Every man. And against thy mother's son, of the Church, to whom we are joined by charity. Thou didst lay a scandal, heresies or other things by which the innocent may be caught.

918BThou didst speak against. (AUG.) While he detracts who seems learned, etc., as far as with the food of stronger doctrine.

Like unto thee. (CASS.) By consenting to the wicked.

I will set against thy face. (AUG.) What thou hast put behind thy back, I will set before thy face.

VERS. 22.-- Let him snatch away. (CASS.) God unto punishment, and there be none to deliver. When the devil snatches, God delivers; but when God snatches, none avails to set free.

VERS. 23.-- The sacrifice of praise. (CASS.) Not that which the wicked sing, the sacrifice of praise, not of animals. And this is the way to God, the ladder of Jacob, by which the angels, that is, the faithful, ascend to the praise of the divinity, and descend to the praise of the humanity. There is the way by which, etc. (Ibid.) In the sacrifice of praise. The salvation of God. (AUG.) Christ, who came with grace, whom he knows, who attributes anything 918Cto another than to the grace of God.

PSALMUS L.

VERS. 1.-- In finem psalmus. (CASS.) Arguente Nathan, rex non erubuit peccata publice confiteri, etc., usque ad quae a Deo valet poenitentibus. David. (AUG.) Proponitur in exemplum, non cadendi, sed, etsi cecideris, resurgendi ne desperes. (CASS.) Prima est deprecatio, etc., usque ad plena praestatur peccatorum remissio.

VERS. 3.-- Miserere mei, Deus. (Ibid.) Hic poenitentialis psalmus, etc., usque ad quia praevidit per hunc psalmum plures perituros. Secundum magnam misericordiam tuam. De gravi peccato desperandum 918Desset, nisi magna misericodia esset. Magna non potest diffiniri quanta sit. Magnam misericordiam. (Ibid.) Magna misericordia Deum de coelo deposuit, etc., usque ad cum secundum se rogatur Deus ignoscere? Miserationum etc. (CASS.) Per misericordiam et miserationem petit. Et est misericordia in natura, miseratio in effectu.

VERS. 4.-- Amplius lava me. (CASS.) Quem modum delendi velit, subdit: Munda me, etc. (HIER.) Sic lava ut mundes, lavantur enim quaedam, quae tamen non sunt pura.

VERS. 5.-- Quoniam iniquitatem. (AUG., CASS.) Cujus misericordiam petit ut ignoscat, quia scit justum ut peccata puniat, subdit: Tu ne punias, quia 919Aego punio. Quoniam iniquitatem meam, etc. Contra me. (AUG.) Post tergum peccatum habuit, cum rex sententiam in divitem, qui rapuit ovem pauperis dedit, oblitus sui.

VERS. 6.-- Tibi soli peccavi. (HIER.) Solus enim ille juste punit, qui non habet in se, quod reprehendatur, hic est inter homines solus Christus. Tibi soli. (CASS.) Quia rex omnibus superior, tantum a Deo puniendus est. Coram te. Quia ubique esse scit, unde se arguit, quia eo praesente peccare non erubuit. Ut justificeris, etc. Cujus verba non transeunt, sed implentur. Vincas cum judicaris. Deus t antae justitiae est, etc., usque ad ut vincat inter se et eum, si judicentur.

Tibi soli. (AUG.) Christo nullum habenti peccatum, 919Betc., usque ad eo quod tam graviter Deum offenderat. Et vincas. (AUG.) Vel adeo justus es, ut vincas diabolum, et mortem, et Judaeos, cum judicaris: et in judicio, quo judicatus es.

VERS. 7.-- In iniquitatibus. (CASS.) Minuitur invidia peccati, etc., usque ad de uno arguitur et omnia confitetur.

VERS. 8.-- Ecce enim, etc. (AUG.) Sic misericordiam dat, ut servet veritatem, ut nec peccata sint impunita ejus cui ignoscit. Ignoscit enim seipsum punienti. Misericordia ergo etiam est quod homo liberatur; veritas quod peccatum punitur. Veritatem, etc. (CASS.) Quia in confitendo, veritatem dixit, quam Deus super sacrificia quaerit, supplicat sibi subveniri. Incerta et occulta. (AUG.) Sunt et occulta quod 919Ctalibus, etc., usque ad unde magis a peccato erat sibi cavendum. Occulta. (CASS.) Ex auctoritate manifestantis, confidentia ablutionis et dealbationis.

VERS. 9.-- Asperges me. (CASS.) Secunda est confidentia misericordiae Dei, quae multum est utilis: ne subrepat desperatio, quae omnibus peccatis gravior est. Hyssopo. (Ibid.) Immolato sanguine intincta, super corpus leprosi aspergebatur, significans sanguine Christi maculas peccatorum abluendas. (AUG.) Hyssopus herba humilis, etc., usque ad in quibus est inflatio, sic humilitas superbiam. Super nivem. (Ibid.) Incomparabiliter: unde et in monte vestis Christi fulsit sicut nix.

VERS. 10.-- Auditui meo. (AUG.) Nota humilem. Audiam te, etc., usque ad et quia jam humilis jam 919Dexsultant ossa humiliata.

VERS. 11.-- Averte. (CASS.) Ex confidentia securus, petit deletionem omnium peccatorum et plenam restitutionem.

VERS. 12.-- In visceribus meis. (Ibid.) Unde adulterium exiit. In utrisque partibus, anima et corpore remedium curationis petit, quia in eis peccavit. Sic desiderat expiari, ut videatur nil tale ultra velle committere.

VERS. 13.-- Ne projicias me a facie tua. (CASS.) A peccatis faciem averte, sed non me a facie tua, unde lumen et sanitas veniat.

VERS. 14.-- Spiritu principali. (AUG.) Notant hic quidam Trinitatem in Deo, qui est spiritus, cum 920Anon corpus; per spiritum rectum, Filium; Spiritum sanctum, suo nomine, per spiritum principalem, Patrem. (CASS.) Spiritum prophetiae qui sibi omnibus pretiosior est, robur solum petit non auferri, tacens de caeteris.

VERS. 15.-- Docebo. (Ibid.) Quid restitutus persolvat; prius plorans, jam fit doctor.

VERS. 16.-- De sanguinibus. (Ibid.) Quia multa sunt carnalia peccata, etc., usque ad quae de corruptione carnis et sanguinis veniunt. Justitiam tuam. (Ibid.) Justitiam laudat, cum pietati deberet gratias agere; sed et justitiae fuit confitentem suscipere; et hae duae res semper in judicio Domini adjunctae sunt.

VERS. 17.-- Laudem tuam. (AUG.) Quod me creasti; 920Bquod peccantem non reliquisti; quod confiteri monuisti; quod mundasti.

VERS. 19.-- Sacrificium Deo. (CASS.) Quod illo tempore pro expiatione ponebatur. Contribulatus (Ibid.) Laetus et lascivus spiritus obligat peccato. Sequitur hujus sacrificii promissio: Cor contritum.

VERS. 20.-- Benigne fac. (Ibid.) Jam gaudens, de aedificatione Jerusalem prophetat, ubi sacrificium justitiae. Muri. (Au.) Munimenta immortalitatis nostrae construantur in fide, spe, et charitate.

VERS. 21.-- Tunc acceptabis sacrificium. (Ibid.) Modo sacrificium pro iniquitate, etc., usque ad tunc justitia erit sacrificium, oblationes minores sancti, holocausta, perfecti.

920CTunc imponent. (CASS.) Sacerdotes, vitulos innocentes, etc., usque ad fideles pro tuo nomine patientes, tibi erunt grati. Altare. (AUG.) Coelestem Jerusalem.

PSALM L.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end, a psalm. (CASS.) When Nathan rebuked him, the king did not blush to confess his sins publicly, etc., as far as what avails with God for the penitent. Of David. (AUG.) He is set forth as an example, not of falling, but of rising again if thou hast fallen, that thou despair not. (CASS.) The first thing is entreaty, etc., as far as full remission of sins is granted.

VERS. 3.-- Have mercy on me, O God. (Ibid.) This is a penitential psalm, etc., as far as because he foresaw that through this psalm many would perish. According to thy great mercy. Of a grave sin one would have to despair, 918Dwere there not a great mercy misericodia. A great one cannot be defined, how great it is. Great mercy. (Ibid.) A great mercy brought God down from heaven, etc., as far as when God is asked to pardon according to himself? Of thy tender mercies, etc. (CASS.) He asks through mercy and through tender mercy. And mercy is in the nature, tender mercy in the effect.

VERS. 4.-- Wash me yet more. (CASS.) What manner of blotting out he would have, he adds: Cleanse me, etc. (HIER.) So wash that thou make clean; for certain things are washed which nevertheless are not pure.

VERS. 5.-- For iniquity. (AUG., CASS.) Whose mercy he asks that he may pardon, because he knows him just, that he punishes sins, he adds: Punish thou not, because 919AI punish. For my iniquity, etc. Against me. (AUG.) He had his sin behind his back, when the king gave sentence against the rich man who had seized the poor man's ewe, forgetful of himself.

VERS. 6.-- To thee only have I sinned. (HIER.) For he alone punishes justly who has not in himself anything that may be reproved; and among men this is Christ alone. To thee only. (CASS.) Because a king is superior to all, he is to be punished by God alone. Before thee. Because he knows that he is everywhere; whence he accuses himself, because in his presence he did not blush to sin. That thou mayest be justified, etc. Whose words do not pass away, but are fulfilled. And mayest overcome when thou art judged. God is of such great justice t antae, etc., as far as that he may overcome as between himself and him, if they be judged.

To thee only. (AUG.) To Christ, who had no sin, 919Betc., as far as in that he had so grievously offended God. And mayest overcome. (AUG.) Or, thou art so just that thou overcomest the devil, and death, and the Jews, when thou art judged: and in the judgment wherein thou wast judged.

VERS. 7.-- In iniquities. (CASS.) The odium of the sin is lessened, etc., as far as he is accused of one and confesses all.

VERS. 8.-- For behold, etc. (AUG.) He so gives mercy that he keeps truth, so that not even the sins of him whom he pardons are unpunished. For he pardons the man who punishes himself. Mercy therefore it is that a man is set free; truth, that the sin is punished. Truth, etc. (CASS.) Because in confessing he spoke the truth, which God seeks above sacrifices, he entreats that help be brought him. The uncertain and hidden things. (AUG.) There are hidden things also, in that 919Cto such men, etc., as far as whence he had the more to beware of sin. The hidden things. (CASS.) From the authority of him who makes them manifest, the confidence of washing and of being made white.

VERS. 9.-- Thou shalt sprinkle me. (CASS.) The second thing is confidence in the mercy of God, which is very profitable: lest despair creep in, which is graver than all sins. With hyssop. (Ibid.) Dipped in the blood of the victim, it was sprinkled over the body of the leper, signifying that the stains of sins are to be washed away by the blood of Christ. (AUG.) Hyssop is a lowly herb, etc., as far as in which there is a swelling, so humility, pride. Above snow. (Ibid.) Incomparably: whence also on the mountain the garment of Christ shone as snow.

VERS. 10.-- To my hearing. (AUG.) Mark the humble man. Let me hear thee, etc., as far as and because he is now humble, now 919Dthe bones that were humbled rejoice. [Vulg. Ps 50:10 exsultabunt, "shall rejoice"]

VERS. 11.-- Turn away. (CASS.) Made secure by that confidence, he asks the blotting out of all sins and a full restoration.

VERS. 12.-- In my bowels. (Ibid.) Whence the adultery went forth. In both parts, in soul and in body, he asks the remedy of healing, because in them he sinned. He so desires to be cleansed that he may be seen to wish to commit no such thing further.

VERS. 13.-- Cast me not away from thy face. (CASS.) Turn thy face from my sins, but not me from thy face, whence light and health may come.

VERS. 14.-- With a principal spirit. (AUG.) Some here note the Trinity in God, who is spirit, since 920Anot body: by a right spirit, the Son; the Holy Spirit, by his own name; by a principal spirit, the Father. (CASS.) The spirit of prophecy, which is more precious to him than all things, he asks that its strength alone be not taken away, saying nothing of the rest.

VERS. 15.-- I will teach. (Ibid.) What he pays when restored: before, weeping; now he becomes a teacher.

VERS. 16.-- From blood. (Ibid.) Because carnal sins are many, etc., as far as which come from the corruption of flesh and blood. Thy justice. (Ibid.) He praises justice, when he ought to give thanks to mercy; but it belonged to justice also to receive one confessing; and these two things are always joined together in the judgment of the Lord.

VERS. 17.-- Thy praise. (AUG.) That thou didst create me; 920Bthat thou didst not forsake me when I sinned; that thou didst admonish me to confess; that thou didst cleanse me.

VERS. 19.-- A sacrifice to God. (CASS.) Which at that time was offered for expiation. Afflicted (Ibid.) A glad and wanton spirit binds a man to sin. There follows the promise of this sacrifice: A contrite heart.

VERS. 20.-- Deal favourably. (Ibid.) Now rejoicing, he prophesies of the building of Jerusalem, where is the sacrifice of justice. The walls. (Au.) Let the defences of our immortality be built up in faith, hope, and charity.

VERS. 21.-- Then shalt thou accept a sacrifice. (Ibid.) Now the sacrifice is for iniquity, etc., as far as then justice shall be the sacrifice, oblations the lesser saints, holocausts, the perfect.

920CThen shall they lay. (CASS.) The priests; calves, the innocent, etc., as far as the faithful who suffer for thy name shall be acceptable to thee. The altar. (AUG.) The heavenly Jerusalem.

PSALMUS LI

In finem pro, etc. (HIER., AUG.) Doeg prodidit David, etc., usque ad Non est hic oratio pro malis, sed prophetia quid sit eis futurum.

VERS. 2.-- Doeg. (CASS.) Adversarius David significat Antichristum, qui totum orbem movebit; qui veniet per signa, et miracula ante adventum judicii, et auxilium a Saule, id est, a diabolo petens, nuntiabit venisse David, id est, Christum in domum Achimelech, id est, ad Eccesiam, quae est regnum 920DPatris.

Abimelech. (HIER.) Dicit; in Hebraeo Achimelech, etc., usque ad ergo Abimelech patris mei regnum, et significat Judaeos.

VERS. 3.-- Quid gloriaris in malitia, etc. (CASS.) Prima est invectio in Doeg, ut fideles corroboret, contra Antichristum et ejus complices.

VERS. 4.-- Cogitavit. (Ibid.) Levis mens, praeceps dictio, non ante cogitat quam loquatur, unde: In ore stulorsorum est cor eorum.

Sicut novacula, etc. (Ibid.) Quae dum promittit innovationem, incidit ita ille dolosus, Antichristus scilicet, beatitudinem, et occidit.

VERS. 5.-- Dilexisti malitiam, etc. (CASS.) Non deserit 921Amalum, qui diligit super benignitatem; et si benignitas tangit animum, refugit.

VERS. 6.-- Lingua dolosa. (Ibid.) Id est, dolosa verba fallaciae ministra, aliud in corde gestantium, aliud in ore promentium.

VERS. 7.-- Propterea Deus. (CASS.) De celeri fine iniqui. Et radicem tuam de terra viventium. (AUG.) Radix nostra charitas est, etc., usque ad hic enim pulvis, quem projicit ventus a facie terrae. (Ibid.) Radix mali cupiditas, quae non fructum parit in terra viventium. Vel, loquitur de Antichristo, cujus radix ministri, qui cum eo nihil habebunt cum sanctis.

VERS. 8.-- Videbunt justi. (Ibid.) Pro dejectione ejus irrisio. (Ibid.) Videbunt justi. Quid malis sit, etc., usque ad quia plus omnibus aliis malis fideles 921Bdecipiet.

VERS. 10.-- Ego autem, etc. (Ibid.) Quomodo contra eum bonus se habeat. (CASS.) Hucusque vituperatio illius, hic laus contrariae partis: ecce perfecta demonstratio. Oliva fructifera. (AUG.) Populus Dei oliva, unde fracti sunt superbi rami, id est, Judaei, et insertus est oleaster de gentibus. (CASS.) Oliva fructifera, de cujus germine Dominus Christus effloruit, qui spirituali oleo perunctus est prae consortibus suis.

In aeternum et in saeculum saeculi. (AUG.) Quod dixit in aeternum, repetit in saeculum saeculi: ut repetendo confirmet, quam fundatus est in amore regni coelorum.

921CVERS. 11.-- Fecisti, et exspectabo nomen. (Ibid.) Praedicta scilicet, quod sim oliva, quod speravi in misericordia in aeternum.

PSALM LI

Unto the end, for, etc. (HIER., AUG.) Doeg betrayed David, etc., as far as This is not here a prayer for the wicked, but a prophecy of what shall come upon them.

VERS. 2.-- Doeg. (CASS.) The adversary of David signifies Antichrist, who shall stir up the whole world; who shall come by signs and wonders before the coming of the judgment, and seeking help from Saul, that is, from the devil, shall announce that David, that is, Christ, has come into the house of Achimelech, that is, to the Church Eccesiam, which is the kingdom 920Dof the Father.

Abimelech. (HIER.) He says, in the Hebrew Achimelech, etc., as far as therefore Abimelech is the kingdom of my father, and it signifies the Jews. [Vulg. Ps 51:2 Achimelech, the form the gloss itself contrasts]

VERS. 3.-- Why dost thou glory in malice, etc. (CASS.) The first is an invective against Doeg, that he may strengthen the faithful against Antichrist and his accomplices.

VERS. 4.-- It hath devised. (Ibid.) A light mind, a headlong utterance: it does not think before it speaks, whence: In the mouth of fools is their heart. stulorsorum

As a razor, etc. (Ibid.) Which, while it promises renewal, cuts: so does that deceitful one, namely Antichrist, cut blessedness, and slay.
