VERS. 5.-- Thou hast loved malice, etc. (CASS.) He does not forsake 921Aevil who loves it above kindness; and if kindness touches his mind, he flees.

VERS. 6.-- A deceitful tongue. (Ibid.) That is, deceitful words, the ministers of falsehood, of men who bear one thing in the heart and bring forth another in the mouth.

VERS. 7.-- Therefore God. (CASS.) Of the swift end of the wicked man. And thy root out of the land of the living. (AUG.) Our root is charity, etc., as far as for here is the dust which the wind drives from the face of the earth. (Ibid.) The root of evil is covetousness, which does not bring forth fruit in the land of the living. Or, he speaks of Antichrist, whose root is his ministers, who with him shall have nothing with the saints.

VERS. 8.-- The just shall see. (Ibid.) Derision for his casting down. (Ibid.) The just shall see. What shall befall the wicked, etc., as far as because more than by all other evils he shall deceive the faithful 921B.

VERS. 10.-- But I, etc. (Ibid.) How the good man bears himself against him. (CASS.) Thus far the censure of that man; here the praise of the contrary part: behold a perfect demonstration. A fruitful olive tree. (AUG.) The people of God is an olive tree, from which the proud branches were broken off, that is, the Jews, and the wild olive of the Gentiles was grafted in. (CASS.) A fruitful olive tree, from whose shoot the Lord Christ came into flower, who was anointed with spiritual oil above his fellows.

For ever and for ever and ever. (AUG.) What he said for ever, he repeats for ever and ever: that by repeating he may confirm how firmly he is founded in the love of the kingdom of heaven.

921CVERS. 11.-- Thou hast done, and I will wait on thy name. (Ibid.) The things foretold, namely, that I am an olive tree, that I have hoped in mercy for ever.

PSALMUS LII.

VERS. 1.-- In finem pro, etc. (CASS.) Intellectus David prophetae, etc., usque ad hic de adventu judicii. (AUG.) Vel pro mahalath, etc., usque ad consolatio in fine psalmi.

Dixit insipiens. (Ibid.) Increpatio malorum.

(Ibid.) Insipiens, omnis qui male vivit, etc., usque ad ille dicit, non est Deus.

VERS. 3.-- Deus de. (CASS.) Vel de coelo, id est, per sanctas animas admonuit, ut videat, etc. Si est, etc. (Ibid.) Aut si non intelligit, si saltem est requirens 921Dintelligere Deum.

VERS. 4.-- Omnes declinaverunt. (Ibid.) Congruus ordo. Prius declinant; tunc inutiles; inde non est qui faciat bonum.

VERS. 5.-- Nonne scient. (Ibid.) Comminatio malorum per finem. (AUG.) Minatur illis, etc., usque ad. Sed merito hoc eis, quia:

VERS. 6.-- Deum non invocaverunt. (Ibid.) Consolatur gementes, ne prosperantes imitentur, quia Deum non invocaverunt, unde cito perituri sunt, consolatio fidelium. Ossa eorum qni hominibus placent. (CASS.) Boni sibi displicent, dum carnem castigant: placent mali.

Confusi sunt. (Ibid.) Id est, confundentur, separabuntur, 922Aut generaliter legatur de omnibus malis, sed Israel salvabitur.

VERS. 7.-- Quis dabit ex, etc. (AUG.) Salus autem parturienti Ecclesiae.

PSALM LII.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end, for, etc. (CASS.) The understanding of David the prophet, etc., as far as here of the coming of the judgment. (AUG.) Or, for mahalath, etc., as far as consolation at the end of the psalm.

The fool hath said. (Ibid.) A rebuke of the wicked.

(Ibid.) The fool, every one who lives ill, etc., as far as he says, there is no God.

VERS. 3.-- God from. (CASS.) Or from heaven, that is, through holy souls he gave warning, that he might see, etc. If there be, etc. (Ibid.) Or, if he does not understand, if at least he is one seeking 921Dto understand God.

VERS. 4.-- They are all gone aside. (Ibid.) A fitting order. First they go aside; then they are become unprofitable; thence there is none that doth good.

VERS. 5.-- Shall they not know. (Ibid.) A threatening of the wicked by the end. (AUG.) He threatens them, etc., as far as. But deservedly this befalls them, because:

VERS. 6.-- They have not called upon God. (Ibid.) He consoles those who groan, lest they imitate the prosperous, because they have not called upon God, whence they shall quickly perish: a consolation of the faithful. The bones of them that please men. qni (CASS.) The good displease themselves while they chastise the flesh: the wicked please.

They have been confounded. (Ibid.) That is, they shall be confounded, they shall be separated, 922Aso that it may be read generally of all the wicked; but Israel shall be saved.

VERS. 7.-- Who shall give out of, etc. (AUG.) But salvation is to the Church in her travail.

PSALMUS LIII.

VERS. 2.-- Ziphaei. (HIER., AUG.) Florente interpretantur, etc., usque ad monet in adversis Deum laudare.

VERS. 3.-- Deus, in nomine. (AUG.) Inter Ziphaeos orat. (AUG., HIER.) Hic salva in nomine, post non timeo judicari in virtute. (AUG.) Deus in nomine, verba Ecclesiae latentis inter Ziphaeos, cujus bonum intus est, et merces occulta, alii aliis petunt liberari: ego in tuo nomine.

VERS. 4.-- Deus, exaudi. (CASS.) Item Deus, nomen 922Bpotentiae, repetit ne tardet auxilium. Percipe. (AUG.) Ziphaei ea etsi audiunt, non tamen intelligunt, qui non nisi temporalia noverunt.

VERS. 5.-- Alieni. (AUG.) Ziph viculus erat, qui pertinebat ad tribum Juda, unde Ziphaei.

VERS. 6.-- Ecce enim. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. Quid sibi et Ziphaeis faciat Deus unde solvit laudes. Adjuvat. (AUG.) Quod ipsi nesciunt inter quos lateo; sed hoc quod me adjuvat viderent, si Deum ante oculos ponerent.

VERS. 7.-- Averte mala inimicis. (Ibid.) Vel averte, pro convertendis praecatur: et haec est hostia quam pro liberatione solvit. In veritate. (AUG.) Vel secundum aliam litteram: In virtute, perde quos 922Cin tua infirmitate tolerasti. Voluntarie sacrificabo. (Ibid.) Quia propter se, non propter aliud, quod ab eo velim. Qui propter aliud laudat, ex necessitate laudat; si illud haberet, non laudaret. Mihi autem, et quae dedit propter dantem placent.

PSALM LIII.

VERS. 2.-- The Ziphites. (HIER., AUG.) They are interpreted the flourishing ones Florente, etc., as far as he admonishes us to praise God in adversities.

VERS. 3.-- O God, in thy name. (AUG.) He prays among the Ziphites. (AUG., HIER.) Here, save me in thy name; afterwards, I fear not to be judged in thy strength. (AUG.) O God, in thy name: the words of the Church hiding among the Ziphites, whose good is within and whose reward is hidden; others ask to be delivered by other means: I, in thy name.

VERS. 4.-- O God, hear. (CASS.) Again God, a name 922Bof power; he repeats it that the help may not be slow. Give ear, (AUG.) The Ziphites, even if they hear these things, yet do not understand, who know nothing except things temporal.

VERS. 5.-- Strangers. (AUG.) Ziph was a hamlet which belonged to the tribe of Juda, whence the Ziphites.

VERS. 6.-- For behold. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. What God does for him and for the Ziphites, whence he pays his praises. He helpeth. (AUG.) Which they themselves know not, among whom I lie hid; but this, that he helps me, they would see, if they set God before their eyes.

VERS. 7.-- Turn back the evils upon mine enemies. (Ibid.) Or, turn back: he prays for such as are to be converted; and this is the victim which he pays for his deliverance. In thy truth. (AUG.) Or according to another reading: In thy strength, destroy those whom 922Cin thy weakness thou hast borne with. I will freely sacrifice. (Ibid.) Because for his own sake, not for anything else that I might wish from him. He who praises for the sake of something else praises of necessity; if he had that thing, he would not praise. But to me, and the things he gave are pleasing for the giver's sake.

PSALMUS LIV.

VERS. 1.-- In finem in carminibus. (AUG.) Intellectus. Magna cura debet intelligere Ecclesia, etc., usque ad qui pro molestis civium fugit in solitudinem.

VERS. 2.-- Exaudi, Deus, orationem meam. (CASS.) Oratio, praemissa contra mala, vel fluctus saeculi. Ne despexeris deprecationem. (Ibid.) Si enim Deus dat temporalia alicui petenti, ejus tamen oratio ei non est accepta, quia caret debito fine.

922DVERS. 3, 4.-- In exercitatione, etc. (AUG.) Omnis malus vivit, vel ut corrigatur, vel ut per eum bonus exerceatur. Conturbatus sum a voce inimici. (AUG.) In ipsa pugna, dum et inimicos vult diligere, et abundante militia incipit odisse, et ita incipit in fluctibus mergi. (HIER.) Conturbatus. Vel, conturbatus sum a voce inimici, qui me Samaritanum et daemonium habentem dicebant.

VERS. 5.-- Cor meum conturbatum. (CASS.) Lege carnis, animus turbatur in me, non exit a me.

VERS. 6.-- Timor et tremor. (Ibid.) Proprietas mortis est, ut eam prius timeamus, unde contremiscamus. Contexerunt me tenebrae. (HIER.) Tenebrae sunt mali homines, qui persequuntur Ecclesiam, 923Aet qui contegunt ipsam: qui odit fratrem, in tenebris est.

VERS. 7.-- Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut? (AUG.) Sed in hac infirmitate quid ait? Quis dabit mihi pennas? Vult ad tempus separari a tot scandalis, ne peccata infirmus augeat manens inter ea. Sicut columbae, etc. (Ibid.) Non sicut corvo, etc., usque ad sed manere necesse est propter vos, et sic est meritum ex desiderio.

(CASS.) Columba. Vel columba emissa inveniens lutosa ad arcam reversa, sic Christus inveniens lutosa corda Judaeorum avolavit ad gentes.

VERS. 8.-- Ecce elongavi. (CAS.) Illud tangit, quod Christus vitabat, persequentes, ut occasionem irae demeret, et manebat in desertis orans: in quo 923Bdocebat nos in secreto conscientiae orare et quiescere, cum a malis premimur. Et mansi in solitudine, gentium; unde: Laetetur disertum et floreat tanquam lilium. Et alibi: Laetare, sterilis, quae non paris (Isai. XXXV. Ibid. XXXIV).

VERS. 9.-- Exspectabam eum. Diapsalmus. Jam in solitudine salvus sperat auxilium Dei, et imprecatur civibus. (CASS.) Exspectabam (ut ex persona Christi legatur) in solitudine, non ex me securus praesidium patris sustinui, qui salvum me fecit a pusillanimitate spiritus, ne caderem vel cederem malis in passione, a tempestate ne irascerer.

VERS. 10.-- Praecipita. (CASS.) Ne muniant cogitationes machinando. Divide. (Ibid.) Ne sit superba unitas, ne malitia habeat effectum. In civitate. Haec 923Cest civitas de qua per prophetam Dominus: Ego Deus et non homo, et civitatem non ingredior. Est tamen alia, quam Deus inhabitat, de qua dicitur: Non potest abscondi civitas supra montem posita.

VERS. 11.-- Et labor in medio ejus, etc. (AUG.) Jam labor in medio, quia iniquitas: quies autem in humilitate.

VERS. 12.-- Usura, etc. (Ibid.) Quia plus exigit in injuria. Vel qualibet re, quam accepit, non dimittit, ut sibi dimittatur.

VERS. 13.-- Quoniam si inimicus. (CASS.) Exprobratio Judae, dum ex persona Christi legitur; vel, hucusque de apertis inimicis egit Ecclesia, jam nunc de occultis. Abscondissem me forsitan ab eo, etc. (Ibid.) Magna patientia ita locum daret 923Dverbis, ut se absconderet ne videret adversarium.

VERS. 14.-- Tu vero, homo. (AUG.) Olim, quia aliquando bonum consilium dedisti. Unanimis. (CASS.) Quia inter Apostolos fuit dux, ad castella et vicos praemissus. Notus, quia praescivit traditorem, ut sic Christus specialiter contra Judam loquatur.

(HIER.) Vel sic, generaliter contra quemlibet virum Judaicum, etc., usque ad legis instituta vel buccellam. Unanimis. (AUG.) Qui aliquando bene monuisti; Dux: feci te ducem super populum meum. Notus, de eadem gente.

Notus meus. Qui simul. (Ibid.) Qui in eadem Ecclesia mecum fuisti.

924AVERS.15.-- Cibos. (CAS.) Corporales, qui solis iniquo poterant esse dulces. Solet vir iniquitatis comessationibus mitescere, unde huic gravior culpa.

VERS. 16.-- Veniat. (Ibid.) Sicut supra apertis, ita hic occultis imprecatur. Et ne putetur unus de quo agebat, communicat poenas Judaeis, id est, communiter Judaeis cum aliis imprecatur.

(AUG., HIER.) Veniat mors. Tangit hic initium schismatis, etc., usque ad et loquitur in eadem voce Christus et Ecclesia.

(AUG.) Veniat: Ut super illos, qui initium schismatis fuerunt et sese superbi separaverunt, venit nova mors; aperuit enim terra, et vivos absorpsit. Descendant in infernum viventes. (Ibid.) Ut duces terra absorpsit, etc., usque ad ita hi scienter peccantes 924Bdescendunt. Viventes. (Ibid.) Scientes quia pereunt, et tamen pereuntes terrenae cupiditatis hiatu absorbeantur. In habitaculis. Alienae sunt, non naturales, sed hospitio susceptae, quasi adventitiae, vel prius in habitaculis, id est, in occulto, post in medio, id est in aperto.

Ego autem, etc. (CASS.) Affirmat, quid sibi et illis fiat, alternatim procedendo.

VERS. 18.-- Vespere et mane. (HIER.) Quia salvavit, ideo vespere, quo captus; mane, quo judicatus; meridie, quo crucifixus. Narrabo, praeterita opera. Nuntiabo, virtutes et opera quae faciet: et ideo exaudiet, etc.

(AUG.) Vespere. De praeteritis narrabo, etc., usque ad contra illos qui non amant pacem, quia amavi 924Cpacem.

(CASS.) Narrare, ad vesperam pertinet, quo dixit omnia quae Judas disponebat. Nuntiare de mane, quando dixit Pilato: In hoc natus sum, ut testimonium perhibeam veritati.

VERS. 19.-- Appropinquant mihi. Nomine, non numine; corpore, non mente; numero, non merito. Quoniam inter multos erant mecum. (HIER., AUG.) Quia in multis, mecum, id est, baptismo Evangelii, lectione, festis et hujusmodi, sed non in paucis, mecum. In omnibus sacramentis mecum, sed non in fide, spe et charitate, sine qua nihil sunt omnia.

(AUG.) Vel, in multis, id est, in paleis, etc., usque ad ita et illi in multis mecum.

VERS. 20.-- Exaudiet Deus, etc. (CASS.) Ad meridiem, 924Dquando emisit Spiritum. Ecce quanta breviter mysteria: vel, salvabis mane, et vespere, et meridie: unde non ingratus narra, et annuntia, et ipse exaudiet, etc. Humiliabit illos qui est ante saecula. (Ibid.) De superbia, ut credant. Vel humiliabit ut tollat locum et gentem. Non enim est illis commutatio, et non timuerunt Deum, extendit manum suam in retribuendo, etc. (AUG.) Quia sensus perfidorum incommutabilis.

VERS. 21.-- Contaminaverunt: (CASS.) quia illi contaminaverunt et divisi sunt: armantur amplius justi, liberantur infirmi, qui curam habent in Deum.

VERS. 22.-- Ira. (Ibid.) Vindicta judicii, etc., usque ad suis appropriat. Cor. (AUG.) Voluntas secreta 925ADei, quae in Scripturis continetur. Molliti sunt sermones. (CASS.) Vel ideo hoc illis, quia mollierunt sermones adulando, qui sunt jacula dum dicunt: Reus est mortis. (AUG.) Sed si tibi puero qui lacte minoris doctrinae nutriris adhuc duri sunt, ne irascaris uberibus Ecclesiae; sed jacta in Dominum, non alium qui portus est, vel saxum navi, non portus fluctuati in saeculo. Ipsi sermones, etc. (CASS.) Quia molliti non perdunt virtutem, sed eis armantur evangelistae, et feriunt corda hominum ad amorem pacis, et a perplexis haereticorum quaestionibus liberant infirmos.

VERS. 23.-- Curam tuam (Ibid.) Cura saeculi, etc., usque ad: ita viri tristia nocet cordi. Fluctuationem. Et si hic, verba fluctuationis fuerunt: 925BContristatus sum in exercitatione, etc.

VERS. 24.-- Tu vero, etc. (AUG.) Hi tunc non fluctuabunt, etc., usque ad Vae! qui peccant et non poenitent. Dies suos, ego autem, etc. (Ibid.) Voluntarios non a Deo constitutos.

PSALM LIV.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end, in songs. (AUG.) Understanding. The Church ought with great care to understand, etc., as far as who for the troublesomeness of the citizens fled into the wilderness.

VERS. 2.-- Hear, O God, my prayer. (CASS.) A prayer sent before against evils, or against the waves of the world. Despise not my supplication. (Ibid.) For if God gives temporal things to one who asks, his prayer is nevertheless not acceptable to him, because it lacks its due end.

922DVERS. 3, 4.-- In my exercise, etc. (AUG.) Every wicked man lives either that he may be corrected, or that through him a good man may be exercised. I was troubled at the voice of the enemy. (AUG.) In the very battle, while he wishes to love his enemies too, and, as the warfare grows, begins to hate them, and so begins to be sunk in the waves. (HIER.) Troubled. Or, I was troubled at the voice of the enemy, who called me a Samaritan and one having a devil.

VERS. 5.-- My heart is troubled. (CASS.) By the law of the flesh the mind is disturbed within me, it does not go forth from me.

VERS. 6.-- Fear and trembling. (Ibid.) It is the property of death that we first fear it, whence we tremble. Darkness hath covered me. (HIER.) The darkness is wicked men, who persecute the Church, 923Aand who cover it over: he that hates his brother is in darkness.

VERS. 7.-- Who will give me wings as? (AUG.) But in this weakness what does he say? Who will give me wings? He wishes to be parted for a time from so many scandals, lest, being weak, he should increase his sins by remaining among them. As of a dove, etc. (Ibid.) Not as to a raven, etc., as far as but it is necessary to remain for your sakes, and so the merit is from the desire.

(CASS.) The dove. Or, the dove that was sent out, finding muddy places, returned to the ark; so Christ, finding the muddy hearts of the Jews, flew away to the Gentiles.

VERS. 8.-- Lo, I have gone far off. (CAS.) He touches on this, that Christ avoided his persecutors, to take away the occasion of their anger, and remained praying in the desert places: wherein 923Bhe taught us to pray and be still in the secret of the conscience, when we are pressed by the wicked. And I remained in the wilderness, of the Gentiles; whence: Let the desert disertum rejoice, and flourish as the lily. [Vulg. Isa 35:1 Laetabitur deserta et invia, et exsultabit solitudo, et florebit quasi lilium, "the desert shall rejoice"] And elsewhere: Rejoice, thou barren, that bearest not (Isai. XXXV. Ibid. XXXIV).

VERS. 9.-- I waited for him. Diapsalmus. Now safe in the wilderness he hopes for the help of God, and calls down curses on his fellow citizens. (CASS.) I waited (that it may be read in the person of Christ) in the wilderness, not secure of myself, the protection of the Father I looked for, who saved me from faintness of spirit, that I might not fall nor yield to the wicked in the passion, from the tempest lest I should be angry.

VERS. 10.-- Cast down. (CASS.) Lest they fortify their thoughts by contriving. Divide. (Ibid.) Lest their unity be proud, lest their malice have its effect. In the city. This 923Cis the city of which the Lord says by the prophet: I am God and not man, and I do not enter the city. [Vulg. Os 11:9 Deus ego, et non homo; in medio tui sanctus, et non ingrediar civitatem, "I will not enter the city"] Yet there is another, which God inhabits, of which it is said: A city set upon a mountain cannot be hid.

VERS. 11.-- And labour in the midst thereof, etc. (AUG.) Now labour is in the midst, because iniquity is there: but rest is in humility.

VERS. 12.-- Usury, etc. (Ibid.) Because he exacts more, to another's hurt. Or, whatever thing he has received, he does not let it go, that it may be let go to him.

VERS. 13.-- For if mine enemy. (CASS.) A reproach of Judas, while it is read in the person of Christ; or, thus far the Church has dealt with open enemies, now with hidden ones. I would perchance have hidden myself from him, etc. (Ibid.) Great patience would so give place 923Dto words, that it would hide itself, that it might not see the adversary.

VERS. 14.-- But thou, a man. (AUG.) Once, because at some time thou gavest good counsel. Of one mind. (CASS.) Because among the Apostles he was a leader, sent before to the strongholds and villages. Familiar, because he knew the traitor beforehand, so that Christ speaks thus especially against Judas.

(HIER.) Or thus, generally against any Jewish man, etc., as far as the ordinances of the law, or the morsel. Of one mind. (AUG.) Thou who once didst admonish well; Leader: I made thee leader over my people. Familiar, of the same nation.

My familiar. Who together. (Ibid.) Thou who wast with me in the same Church.

924AVERS.15.-- Meats. (CAS.) Bodily ones, which could be sweet to the wicked alone. The man of iniquity is wont to be softened by banquetings, whence his guilt is the heavier.

VERS. 16.-- Let come. (Ibid.) As above against the open enemies, so here he imprecates against the hidden. And lest the one man he was dealing with be thought to be meant, he makes the punishments common to the Jews, that is, he imprecates against the Jews in common with others.

(AUG., HIER.) Let death come. Here he touches the beginning of the schism, etc., as far as and Christ and the Church speak in one voice.

(AUG.) Let come: As upon those who were the beginning of the schism and in their pride separated themselves, a new death came; for the earth opened, and swallowed them alive. Let them go down alive into hell. (Ibid.) As the earth swallowed the leaders, etc., as far as so these, sinning knowingly, 924Bgo down. Alive. (Ibid.) Knowing that they perish, and yet, as they perish, being swallowed up by the gulf of earthly desire. In their dwellings. They are alien, not natural, but received as guests, as it were newcomers; or, first in their dwellings, that is, in secret, afterwards in the midst, that is, in the open.

But I, etc. (CASS.) He affirms what shall be done to him and what to them, proceeding by turns.

VERS. 18.-- Evening and morning. (HIER.) Because he saved, therefore evening, when he was taken; morning, when he was judged; noonday, when he was crucified. I will tell, the works that are past. I will declare, the powers and works which he shall do: and therefore he will hear, etc.

(AUG.) Evening. Of things past I will tell, etc., as far as against those who love not peace, because I have loved 924Cpeace.

(CASS.) To tell belongs to the evening, when he said all that Judas was contriving. To declare belongs to the morning, when he said to Pilate: For this was I born, that I should give testimony to the truth.

VERS. 19.-- They draw near to me. In name, not in the divine power; in body, not in mind; in number, not in merit. Because they were with me among many. (HIER., AUG.) Because in many things, with me, that is, in the baptism of the Gospel, in reading, in feast days and the like, but not in the few things, with me. In all the sacraments with me, but not in faith, hope and charity, without which all things are nothing.

(AUG.) Or, in many things, that is, among the chaff, etc., as far as so are they also with me in many things.

VERS. 20.-- God shall hear, etc. (CASS.) At noonday, 924Dwhen he sent forth the Spirit. Behold how great mysteries in few words: or, thou shalt save at morning, and at evening, and at noonday: whence, being not ungrateful, tell, and declare, and he himself will hear, etc. He shall humble them, he that is before the ages. (Ibid.) From their pride, that they may believe. Or he shall humble them so as to take away their place and their nation. For there is no change with them, and they have not feared God: he hath stretched out his hand in repaying, etc. (AUG.) Because the mind of the faithless is unchangeable.

VERS. 21.-- They have defiled: (CASS.) because they defiled and were divided: the just are the more armed, the weak are set free, who have their care upon God.

VERS. 22.-- Wrath. (Ibid.) The vengeance of the judgment, etc., as far as he appropriates to his own. The heart. (AUG.) The secret will 925Aof God, which is contained in the Scriptures. His words are softened. (CASS.) Or, this befalls them because they softened their words by flattery, which words are darts when they say: He is guilty of death. (AUG.) But if to thee, a child who art nourished with the milk of a lesser teaching, they are still hard, be not angry with the breasts of the Church; but cast [thy care] upon the Lord, not another — he it is who is a harbour; the other is a rock to a ship, not a harbour, to one tossed about in the world. The same words, etc. (CASS.) Because, being softened, they do not lose their power, but by them the evangelists are armed, and they strike the hearts of men to the love of peace, and set the weak free from the entangled questions of heretics.

VERS. 23.-- Thy care. (Ibid.) The care of the world, etc., as far as: so the sadness of a man harms his heart tristia. Wavering. And if here, the words of wavering were: 925BI was made sorrowful in my exercise, etc.

VERS. 24.-- But thou, etc. (AUG.) These then shall not waver, etc., as far as Woe! to them that sin and do not repent. Their days, but I, etc. (Ibid.) Days of their own choosing, not appointed by God.

PSALMUS LV.

VERS. 1.-- In finem, etc. (AUG.) Populus, qui a sanctis longe fit in tituli inscriptione: cui contradicit tam Judaeus, quam omnis qui non vult habere regem Christum; et ipsi, qui tribulant Ecclesiam: contra quos hic psalmus confirmat Ecclesiam. In tituli inscriptione ipsi David cum tenerent eum. Tituli inscriptio, etc., usque ad persecutores qui Ecclesiam, sicut uvas, calcant. Allophyli. Idem quod 925Cpopulus qui a sanctis longe factus est. Geth, id est, in torculari. Legitur David, etc; usque ad sed, cum premitur, sterilis non est.

VERS. 2.-- Miserere mei, Deus. (CASS.) Orat Ecclesia, summatim tangens tribulationes, in quibus per spem Dei finit se non timere, id est, in fine primae partis dicit se non timere. Impugnans tribulavit me, etc. (AUG.) Homo visibiliter: diabolus invisibiliter, unde periculosior est tribulatio.

VERS. 4.-- Ab altitudine. (CASS.) Altitudo diei mundus, ubi superbiae tumor: ut gravior sit tribulatio, dicit se a superbis conculcari. (AUG.) Ab altitudine. Alia littera, etc., usque ad non ait: Non timebo, sed, sperabo in te. Diei Dies, Christus est, cujus duodecim horae, duodecim sunt Apostoli: unde ipse ait: 925DNonne duodecim horae sunt diei? Hujus diei altitudinem inimici non possunt attingere, unde in passione Christi: Tenebrae factae sunt.

VERS. 6.-- Tota die, etc. (CASS.) Enumerat mala, quae sustinendo fit et inimicorum conversio, unde et per spem Dei dicit se non timere, sicut prius fecerat.

VERS. 7.-- Inhabitabunt. (AUG.) Vel, aliqui ex his qui longe a sanctis, etc., usque ad si enim falsa dicunt de te, coelum non auferunt, nec isti nocent.

VERS. 8.-- Pro nihil. (Ibid.) Quia nullus inde tibi labor, quasi nihil inde tibi sit, quia, etsi desperati, tamen verbo curas; vel pro nullis eorum meritis, sed gratis per pietatem. In ira populos confringes, 926Adum per flagella Dei resipiscunt, vel dum iram Dei praevident. In ira populos confringes. Quia terres tribulationibus, etc., usque ad et ira consumptionis, qua mali puniuntur ad peremptionem.

VERS. 9.-- Deus, vitam meam annuntiavi tibi. Triplex vita hominis: naturae, qua vivimus et spiramus; gratiae, qua in Christo vivimus; peccati, quae in vitiis agitur. Duae sunt a Deo, quia bonae, vita scilicet naturae, et vita gratiae: tertia est ab homine, quia mala. Ha omnes Deo annuntiare debemus. (CASS.) Deus, vitam. Confringes, et ego ad institutionem eorum vitam meam ante, quae semper mala. Vitam Deo nuntiat, qui peccatum confitetur: non Deum docens, sed se damnans, ut solvatur. Posuisti lacrymas, etc. (AUG.) Piae lacrymae, quae 926Bpro inimicis rogant: et ideo acceptae Deo, sicut ipse promisit.

VERS. 10.-- In quacunque die, etc. (CASS.) Sive in pueritia, sive in media aetate, sive in fine vitae. Mira clementia, quae quodlibet tempus conversionis nostrae exspectat, et quandocunque rogatur, indulget! Deus meus es, tu. (AUG.) Etsi omnium, meus proprie, qui mihi subvenis, quem colo et amo. Alii alieni sunt.

VERS. 11.-- In Deo laudabo verbum. (Ibid.) Verbum, id est, doctrinam et sermonem; quidquid loquar, laudabo in Domino, id est, et attribuam: et si quid urget speravi, et ideo non timebo. (AUG., HIER.) Vel, in Deo Patre Verbum, id est Filium, quia quidquid de Patre, et Filio dicitur secundum substantiam, et de Spiritu sancto. Hoc de potentia 926CVerbi dicitur, qua est aeternum et consubtantiale Patri, et postea de humanitate, subdit: In Domino, id est, in Christo, qui Verbum caro factum est. Laudabo sermonem, etc., id est, praedicationes, quibus regulam vivendi et salutem mundo dedit. Haec duo praedicat iste, potentiam verbi, et humanitatem Christi. In Deo laudabo. Vel ita, ut Trinitas naturae personaliter per tria verba, quae ponit. In Deo Patre laudabo Verbum, id est, Filium; In Domino, id est, in Spiritu sancto laudabo sermonem, id est, Filium.

VERS. 12.-- In me sunt. Intus, quae a nobis nunquam recedunt; Vota laudationis quae in aeternitate reddentur. (CASS.) In me sunt. Ecclesia jam de malis saeculi libera in futura beatitudine, vel etiam hic, 926Dlaudem Dei cantaturam se dicit.

VERS. 13.-- Quoniam eripuisti. (CASS.) Vel de futuro potest accipi sic, etc., usque ad ubi etiam perfecte Deo placet, unde addit: Ut placeam, etc.

PSALM LV.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end, etc. (AUG.) The people that is made far from the holy ones, in the inscription of a title: [Vulg. Ps 55:1 pro populo qui a sanctis longe factus est, the perfect where Migne prints the present] whom the Jew contradicts, and every one who will not have Christ for king; and those also who afflict the Church: against whom this psalm strengthens the Church. In the inscription of a title, to David himself, when they held him. The inscription of the title, etc., as far as the persecutors who tread the Church as grapes. The Allophyli. The same as 925Cthe people that was made far from the holy ones. Geth, that is, in the winepress. We read of David, etc., as far as but, when it is pressed, it is not barren.

VERS. 2.-- Have mercy on me, O God. (CASS.) The Church prays, touching summarily on her tribulations, in which through hope in God she ends by declaring that she fears not, that is, at the end of the first part she says that she fears not. Fighting against me he hath afflicted me, etc. (AUG.) Man visibly, the devil invisibly, whence the tribulation is the more dangerous.

VERS. 4.-- From the height. (CASS.) The height of the day, the world, where is the swelling of pride: that the tribulation may be the graver, she says that she is trodden down by the proud. (AUG.) From the height. Another reading, etc., as far as he does not say: I will not fear, but, I will hope in thee. Of the day. The Day, is Christ, whose twelve hours are the twelve Apostles: whence he himself says: 925DAre there not twelve hours in the day? The height of this day his enemies cannot reach, whence in the passion of Christ: There was darkness.

VERS. 6.-- All the day, etc. (CASS.) She enumerates the evils, by the enduring of which the conversion of her enemies also comes about, whence again through hope in God she says that she fears not, as she had done before.

VERS. 7.-- They shall dwell. (AUG.) Or, some of those who are far from the holy ones, etc., as far as for if they say false things of thee, they do not take away heaven, nor do these men hurt thee.

VERS. 8.-- For nothing. (Ibid.) Because thou hast no labour from it, as though it were nothing to thee, because, even though they are past hope, yet thou healest them by a word; or, for no merits of theirs, but freely, out of thy mercy. In thy wrath thou shalt break the peoples in pieces, 926Awhile by the scourges of God they come to their senses, or while they foresee the wrath of God. In thy wrath thou shalt break the peoples in pieces. Because thou terrifiest by tribulations, etc., as far as and the wrath of consuming, whereby the wicked are punished unto destruction.

VERS. 9.-- O God, I have declared my life to thee. The life of man is threefold: of nature, whereby we live and breathe; of grace, whereby we live in Christ; of sin, which is passed in vices. Two are from God, because good, namely the life of nature and the life of grace: the third is from man, because evil. All these we ought to declare to God. Ha (CASS.) O God, my life. Thou shalt break them in pieces, and I, for their instruction, declare my life beforehand, which was always evil. He declares his life to God who confesses his sin: not teaching God, but condemning himself, that he may be loosed. Thou hast set my tears, etc. (AUG.) Devout tears, which 926Bplead for enemies: and therefore acceptable to God, as he himself promised.

VERS. 10.-- In whatsoever day, etc. (CASS.) Whether in boyhood, or in middle age, or at the end of life. Wonderful clemency, which waits for whatever time of our conversion, and whensoever it is asked, forgives! Thou art my God, thou. (AUG.) Though thou art the God of all, mine properly, who succourest me, whom I worship and love. Others are strangers.

VERS. 11.-- In God I will praise the word. (Ibid.) The word, that is, teaching and discourse; whatever I speak, I will praise in the Lord, that is, and I will attribute [et; read ei, "to him"]: and if anything presses me, I have hoped, and therefore I shall not fear. (AUG., HIER.) Or, in God the Father the Word, that is the Son, because whatever is said of the Father and of the Son according to substance, is said of the Holy Spirit also. This is said of the power 926Cof the Word, whereby it is eternal and consubstantial with the Father consubtantiale; and afterwards, of the humanity, he adds: In the Lord, that is, in Christ, who is the Word made flesh. I will praise the discourse, etc., that is, the preachings by which he gave to the world a rule of living and salvation. These two things this man preaches, the power of the word and the humanity of Christ. In God I will praise. Or thus, that the Trinity of the nature stands personally in the three words which he sets down. In God the Father I will praise the Word, that is, the Son; In the Lord, that is, in the Holy Spirit, I will praise the discourse, that is, the Son.

VERS. 12.-- They are in me. Within, things which never depart from us; Vows of praise [Vulg. Ps 55:12 vota tua, quae reddam, laudationes tibi, "thy vows, which I will render, praises to thee"] which shall be rendered in eternity. (CASS.) They are in me. The Church, now free from the evils of the world, says that in the beatitude to come, or even here, 926Dshe will sing the praise of God.

VERS. 13.-- Because thou hast delivered. (CASS.) Or it may be taken thus of the future, etc., as far as where also she pleases God perfectly, whence he adds: That I may please, etc.

PSALMUS LVI.

VERS. 1.-- In finem. (AUG.) Psalmus de resurrectione et passione breviter. Hoc agit psalmus ne, tu, Pilate, vel tu quicunque, corrumpas David, etc., negando regem, quia tectus carne fugit a cognitione Judaeorum (Ibid.) Nullus titulus inscriptus est David, etc., usque ad ubi latuit Christus incognitus Judaeis.

VERS. 2.-- Miserere mei. (CASS.) Propheta in persona Domini, quia in eo Dominus, quasi inter 927Amala, exclamat, et praedicit liberationem. (CASS.) Christus secundum quod homo orat, de passione ita humilis, ut unus de fidelibus clamare putetur. Et in umbra. Vox corporis adjungitur capiti: et loquens in persona membrorum et sua, quomodo possit liberari dicet, misit Verbum.

VERS. 4.-- Misit Verbum de coelo. (AUG., HIER.) De occulta essentia sua, etc., usque ad quem putabant se exstinxisse. Misit de coelo. (HIER.) Diapsalmus. Jam declarat quid misit et de quibus eripuit, et loquitur in persona membrorum. Liberavit. (Ibid.) Quia jam Misit Verbum, certum est, quasi jam sit qui liberavit, id est, liberavit: et dedit, id est, dabit in opprobrium conculcantes me. Misit Deus. (AUG.) Verbum, in quo misericorditer egit, in quo et promissiones 927Bimplevit. Misericordiam, quia ex misericordia pro nobis mortuus est. Veritatem, quia, ut praedixit, surrexit, ad justificandos nos. Misericordiam suam, etc. (HIER., AUG.) Utraque enim in eo continentur. Si enim sola fuisset misericordia, licentia esset nobis peccandi; si sola veritas, non potuisset homo sustinere.

VERS. 5.-- Dormivi. (AUG.) Alta quiete facile excitandus: Conturbatus passione, dormivi. David non dormivit in spelunca, sed Christus in morte. (CASS.) Conturbatus, secundum carnem passionis memoria et angustia, unde; Tristis est anima mea, etc. Et coepit Jesus taedere et pavere. Filii hominum. Rectus ordo est: filii hominum laqueos paraverunt; sed interserit qualiter turbaverint. Lingua. Voces illae 927CCrucifige, crucifige, et hujusmodi, etiam fecerunt mortem, ut gladius acutus (Matth. XXVI; Marc. XIV).

VERS. 6.-- Exaltare. (Ibid.) Ex persona prophetae visis injuriis, visoque quod in resurrectione inanes facti sunt Judaei, gaudens exclamat homo in cruce: Exaltare, Deus super coelos, ut judicet in terra Judaeos. Exaltare. Superiora Dominus, propheta quidem, sed in persona Domini, quia Dominus in propheta loquitur. Quando etiam ex sua persona loquitur propheta, Dominus per eum loquitur, qui ei dicta. (AUG.) Exaltare. Verba Christi. Sed, o Pater, etc., usque ad quia totus mundus ei subjectus est.

VERS. 7.-- Laqueum paraverunt. Interposita exaltatione, coeptam narrationem exsequitur. Pedibus 927D(CASS.) Domini sunt increpationes malorum, et promissiones fidelium, quibus dolos paraverunt, ut de adultera. Incurvaverunt, dum eis compatiens sterilis reddebatur ab eis. Ante faciem meam foveam, etc. Dum in os ejus dixerunt: Reus est mortis.

VERS. 8.-- Paratum. (Ibid.) Diapsalmus. Post resurrectionem laudes promittit. Vel, paratum ad agendas gratias (quod ibi ostendit) cantabo.

VERS. 9.-- Exsurge, gloria mea. (Ibid.) Et ideo, o caro, quae es causa gloriae meae, Exsurge, potenter, quasi ad miraculum faciendum congratulatio, qui certus, unde idem affirmando, repetit. Exsurge dico, quia certus sum et de hora, quia exsurgam diluculo. Exsurge, psalterium et cithara. (AUG.) Una 928Acaro Christi surrexit, etc., usque ad surrexit ergo psalterium et cithara, et confitetur Domino.

VERS. 11.-- Ad coelos. (Ibid.) Qui supra nubes, ubi sedes angelorum, etc., usque ad coelos misericordia ascendit.

PSALM LVI.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end. (AUG.) A psalm of the resurrection and the passion, in brief. This the psalm does, lest thou, Pilate, or thou whosoever thou art, shouldst corrupt David, [Vulg. Ps 56:1 ne disperdas, "destroy not"] etc., by denying him king, because, being covered with flesh, he escaped the knowledge of the Jews (Ibid.) No title was inscribed to David, etc., as far as where Christ lay hid, unknown to the Jews.

VERS. 2.-- Have mercy on me. (CASS.) The prophet in the person of the Lord, because in him the Lord, as it were amid 927Aevils, cries out and foretells deliverance. (CASS.) Christ prays according to that which is man, so humble concerning the passion that he might be thought to be one of the faithful crying out. And in the shadow. The voice of the body is joined to the head: and speaking in the person of the members and in his own, he will say how he can be delivered, he sent his Word.

VERS. 4.-- He sent his Word from heaven. (AUG., HIER.) Out of his own hidden essence, etc., as far as whom they thought they had put out. [Vulg. Ps 56:4 Misit de caelo, et liberavit me, without Verbum] He sent from heaven. (HIER.) Diapsalmus. Now he declares what he sent and from what he rescued them, and he speaks in the person of the members. He hath delivered. (Ibid.) Because He hath sent his Word is now certain, it is as though he already were who hath delivered, that is, hath delivered [liberavit; read liberabit, "will deliver"]: and he hath given, that is, will give for a reproach them that trod upon me. God hath sent. (AUG.) His Word, in whom he dealt mercifully, in whom also he fulfilled the promises 927B. Mercy, because out of mercy he died for us. Truth, because, as he had foretold, he rose again, to justify us. His mercy, etc. (HIER., AUG.) For both are contained in him. For if there had been mercy alone, there would have been licence for us to sin; if truth alone, man could not have borne it.

VERS. 5.-- I slept. (AUG.) Easy to be roused out of a deep rest: Troubled by the passion, I slept. David did not sleep in the cave, but Christ in death. (CASS.) Troubled, according to the flesh, by the memory and the anguish of the passion, whence; My soul is sorrowful, etc. And Jesus began to be weary and to fear. The sons of men. The right order is this: the sons of men prepared snares; but he inserts in what manner they troubled him. The tongue. Those cries 927CCrucify, crucify, and the like, wrought death also, as a sharp sword (Matth. XXVI; Marc. XIV).

VERS. 6.-- Be thou exalted. (Ibid.) In the person of the prophet, the injuries being seen, and it being seen that in the resurrection the Jews were made empty, the man on the cross cries out rejoicing: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, that he may judge the Jews on the earth. Be thou exalted. The Lord [speaks] the things above; the prophet indeed, but in the person of the Lord, because the Lord speaks in the prophet. Even when the prophet speaks out of his own person, the Lord speaks through him, who dictates dicta to him. (AUG.) Be thou exalted. The words of Christ. But, O Father, etc., as far as because the whole world is made subject to him.

VERS. 7.-- They prepared a snare. The exaltation being interposed, he pursues the narration he had begun. For the feet 927D(CASS.) of the Lord are the rebukes of the wicked and the promises to the faithful, for which they prepared deceits, as in the matter of the adulteress. They bowed down, while he, having compassion on them, was made barren by them. A pit before my face, etc. When they said to his face: He is guilty of death.

VERS. 8.-- Prepared. (Ibid.) Diapsalmus. After the resurrection he promises praises. Or, prepared to give thanks (which he there shows) I will sing.

VERS. 9.-- Arise, my glory. (Ibid.) And therefore, O flesh, that art the cause of my glory, Arise, mightily, as it were a rejoicing together at a miracle to be wrought, being certain: whence, affirming the same thing, he repeats it. Arise, I say, because I am certain also of the hour, because I will arise early. Arise, psaltery and harp. (AUG.) The one 928Aflesh of Christ rose again, etc., as far as the psaltery and harp, therefore, rose again, and give praise to the Lord.

VERS. 11.-- To the heavens. (Ibid.) Which are above the clouds, where is the seat of the angels, etc., as far as mercy ascends to the heavens.

PSALMUS LVII.

VERS. 1.-- In finem ne disperdas David in tituli, etc. (CASS.) Monet ne quis Christi regno contradicat. Prima est exprobratio Judaeorum, ne similia faciamus.

VERS. 2.-- Si vere utique justitiam loquimini. (AUG.) Omnibus facile est loqui justitiam, etc., usque ad quia rex vester sum, ut titulus ait: Recte. Judaei sic de Christo judicaverunt, ut ficte de eo locuti probentur.

VERS. 3.-- Manus vestrae. Cor sequitur manus: 928Bquidquid vis, et non potes, Deus factum putat. Concinnant. Vel connectunt, scilicet, aliud alii adjungentes, etc., usque ad unde flagello de resticulis cecidit Dominus ementes et vendentes in templo.

VERS. 4.-- Alienati sunt peccatores a vulva. Vel, alienati sunt a vulva Ecclesiae, etc., usque ad abortivi excutiuntur.

VERS. 5.-- Furor illis. (Ibid.) Non laudatur ipsa res a Scriptura, undecunque datur similitudo, ut de iniquo judice, qui rogantem viduam vix audivit. Surdae et obturantis. (CASS.) Non solum non faciunt, sed nec audire volunt. (AUG.) Terra, praesentia, quibus delectatur homo; canda, praeterita.

VERS. 6.-- Venefici incantantis, (Ibid.) Vel secundum aliam litteram: Medicamenti medicati a 928Csapiente. Medicamentum medicatum, etc., usque ad hic est ergo sapiens a quo medicatur medicamentum.

VERS. 7.-- Deus conteret. (CASS.) Quae eis retributio. (AUG.) Aspides, Judaei, dum insidiosa tentabant; leones, dum mortem inclamaverunt; horum Molae fractae, quando surrexit Christus. Dentes. Dolosa verba. In ore. Verbis suis capiet eos. Molas leonum confringet Dominus. Ad nihilum devenient: Iuclamationes mortis. Confringet, ne ad effectum veniant; quod exponit. Ad nihilum, dicens.

VERS. 8.-- Tanquam aqua. (Ibid.) Torrentibus etiam comparantur, quia sonantes ad saxa superbiae improvisi sunt et praecipites, sed cito transeunt. Tot malis comparantur. Intendit arcum. Vindicta donec 928Dintus et extra infirmentur, et auferantur, a conspectu Dei, missi in gehennam, hic in praesenti, a terra sua.

VERS. 10.-- Priusquam spinae. (Ibid.) Id est, peccata intelligant. Rhamnum, id est, acutam damnationem, in extremo ignia vitiorum absorbet eos, id est, devorat. Rhamnum. Genus herbae prius mollis sed quae post in spinas vertitur: sic et peccata modo delectant, sed post pungunt. Sicut viventes, sic, etc. Quia non vera, sed falsa est impiorum vita: videntur vivere, nec vivunt. Sic in ira absorbet eos, quia Deus tranquillus judicat, vel quia non est ira comparatione futurae.

VERS. 11.-- Laetabitur justus cum viderit vindictam (CASS.) Correctio justorum de ultione iniquorum.

929AVERS. 12.-- Et dicet homo. (AUG.) Sicut justo Dei judicio fit, etc., usque ad et quia ignis absorbet malos, ergo est Deus judicans eos in terra.

PSALM LVII.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end, destroy not, of David, in the inscription of a title, etc. (CASS.) He warns that no one contradict the kingdom of Christ. The first thing is a reproach of the Jews, that we may not do the like.

VERS. 2.-- If in very deed you speak justice. (AUG.) It is easy for all to speak justice, etc., as far as because I am your king, as the title says: Rightly. The Jews so judged of Christ that they are proved to have spoken of him feignedly.

VERS. 3.-- Your hands. The hands follow the heart: 928Bwhatever thou willest and canst not do, God accounts as done. They frame together. Or they knit together, that is, joining one thing to another, etc., as far as whence with a scourge of little cords the Lord beat out those buying and selling in the temple.

VERS. 4.-- Sinners are alienated from the womb. Or, they are alienated from the womb of the Church, etc., as far as they are cast out as untimely births.

VERS. 5.-- They have fury. (Ibid.) The thing itself is not praised by Scripture, from whatever quarter a likeness is taken, as in the case of the unjust judge, who scarcely heard the widow that asked him. Of the deaf one, and that stoppeth. (CASS.) Not only do they not do, but they will not even hear. (AUG.) The earth, present things, in which man delights; the tail, things past. canda

VERS. 6.-- Of the sorcerer that charmeth. (Ibid.) Or according to another reading: Of the medicine compounded by a 928Cwise man. The medicine compounded, etc., as far as this therefore is the wise man by whom the medicine is compounded.

VERS. 7.-- God shall break. (CASS.) What their recompense is. (AUG.) Asps, the Jews, while they were attempting treacherous things; lions, while they clamoured for his death; of these are the Grinders broken, when Christ rose again. Teeth. Deceitful words. In the mouth. By their own words he shall take them. The Lord shall break the grinders of the lions. They shall come to nothing: The clamourings for death. Iuclamationes He shall break them, lest they come to effect; which he expounds, To nothing, saying.

VERS. 8.-- As water. (Ibid.) They are compared also to torrents, because, sounding against the rocks of pride, they are sudden and headlong, but quickly pass away. To so many evils are they compared. He hath bent his bow. Vengeance, until 928Dthey be weakened within and without, and be taken away from the sight of God, sent into hell, and here in the present, from their own land.

VERS. 10.-- Before your thorns. (Ibid.) That is, before they understand their sins. The bramble, that is, sharp damnation: at the last the fire of vices swallows them up ignia, that is, devours them. The bramble. A kind of herb, soft at first, but which afterwards turns into thorns: so also sins delight for a while, but afterwards prick. As living, so, etc. Because the life of the ungodly is not true but false: they seem to live, and they do not live. So in his wrath he swallows them up, because God judges in tranquillity, or because it is not wrath in comparison with that which is to come.

VERS. 11.-- The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge (CASS.) The correcting of the just by the punishment of the wicked.

929AVERS. 12.-- And man shall say. (AUG.) As it is done by the just judgment of God, etc., as far as and because fire swallows up the wicked, therefore there is a God that judgeth them on the earth.

PSALMUS LVIII.

VERS. 1.-- In finem ne. (CASS.) Frustra tentat aliquis disperdere quod toties divina prohibet auctoritas. Ne disperdas. (AUG.) Cum Pilatus dixit: Quod scripsi, scripsi, etc., usque ad et famam habere in omnibus gentibus. (CASS.) Orat primo liberari ascendendo ab imis ad alta: orat etiam pro salute gentium. (AUG.) Loquitur hic integer Christus, scilicet caput et corpus.

VERS. 2.-- Eripe. (Ibid.) Dum qui sine macula est, hoc petit, quid necessario petamus, ostendit. De inimicis. (CASS.) Quatuor genera sunt adversariorum, 929Betc., usque ad de his ergo ait: Eripe me, etc.

VERS. 4.-- Fortes. (AUG.) Etiam sunt, qui praesumunt de justitia sua, etc., usque ad sed sperantes in divitiis praevaluerunt in vanitate sua.

VERS. 5.-- Iniquitas. (CASS.) Malivolenti : peccatum, operis.

VERS. 6.-- Exsurge. (AUG.) Quia dormire videris, In occursum. Quasi curro ad te merendo: Et tu, occurre mihi, id est, redde pro merito. Vide. (Ibid.) Id est, fac videri quomodo ad te curro, etc., usque ad postquam vidisti me mori, credis me patri aequalem.

VERS. 7.-- Convertentur. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. Orata salus gentium affirmatur, et oraturo Judaeorum salus. Ad vesperam, id est, serius post ascensionem et missum 929CSpiritum, etc., usque ad jejuno bis in sabbato. Circumibunt. (AUG.) Munient Ecclesias contra haereticas impugnationes. Et, ecce in manifesto loquentur.

VERS. 8.-- Et gladius. Ut mactent et manducent. Quoniam qui audivit? Quasi nullus, ita omnes mirabuntur, etc., usque ad ad nihilum deduces vel convertes. Gladius. (Ibid.) Hic est gladius bis acutus utroque incidens Testamento, quo mactat Petrus reptilia sibi in disco ostensa, quando dictum est ei: Surge, Petre, macta et manduca.

VERS. 9.-- Deridebis eos ad nihilum. (Ibid.) Eos dicentes, Quis audivit? quare? Quia pro nihilo habebit convertere omnes gentes, quia omnes gentes Christianae futurae sunt; et dicitis, quis audivit?

929DVERS. 10.-- Fortitudinem meam ad te custodiam, quia Deus susceptor meus es, Deus. (Ibid.) Etsi possem perdere Judaeos, quid irruerunt in me fortes; permitto tamen eos vivere, servans fortitudinem ad te, id est, ad tuam dispositionem.

VERS. 12.-- Ostendit. (Ibid.) id est, quantam circa me habeat misericordiam demonstravit mihi in illis, circa quos non habet; unde Apostolus: Sustinuit vasa irae apta, et ad interitum, in multa patientia, ut notas faceret divitias suas in vasa misericordiae (Rom. IX). Ne occidas. Potest de Judaeis accipi, etc., usque ad ostenditur quae misericordia sit insertis. (CASS.) Consideranti quid de eis sit agendum, si non sint testes legis et mortis Christi. Ne quando obliviscantur. 930A(AUG.) Etsi non modo obliti sunt, cum non sint testes legis et mortis Christi. In virtute tua. Quia tu fortis, non ipsi. Depone, ibi fuit opprobrium omnibus. Vel, depone eos in eo quod mali sunt, ut boni surgant: ut in Paulo, quia non surgeret Paulus, nisi prius caderet Saulus (Act. IX).

VERS. 13, 14.-- Delictum oris eorum. (Ibid.) Non eos, sed delictum occide, ut, resuscitatum quem perdere voluerunt, paveant. (CASS.) Et comprehendantur conversi; quia factum eorum, etc., usque ad facinus vero delevit venia. In superbia. (AUG.) Superbia comes est invidiae: nec fieri potest ut superbus non invideat: unde et diabolus invidet homini. Et de exsecratione. Vel maledicto, quod putastis maledictum, etc., usque ad quia in his deprehensi sunt. 930BAnnuntiabuntur in consummatione. Vel, annuntiabuntur consummationes, id est, praedicabitur ab Apostolis: Ubi abundavit delictum exercitationis et mendacii, superabundavit gratia perfectionis; et pertinuit ad medicinam humilitatis et infirmitatis hominis. In ira consummationis. Est enim ira, id est, vindicta Dei consummationis, quia aliquando vindicat Deus, ut perficiat; est et consumptionis ut cum dicet: Ite, maledicti, in ignem aeternum. Et scient. Antea enim justi sibi videbantur Judaei: sed ostenditur eis, quod non sine Christo, qui dominatur Jacob: et deposita superbia, sciunt se pares gentibus, quia omnes peccaverunt.

VERS. 15.-- Convertentur ad vesperam. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. Affirmatur salus Judaeorum, et utroque 930Cpariete collecto grates aguntur.

VERS. 16.-- Murmurabunt. (Ibid.) Vel, murmurabunt, id est, dolebunt, quod etiam nunc tantum dispergentur; vel, murmurabunt contra pigros, id est, increpabunt alios nolentes credere.

VERS. 17.-- Ego autem. (Ibid.) Concluditur hic psalmus, ubi utroque pariete in angulari lapide conjuncto jam tota Ecclesia gaudet. Et exaltabo. Transactis temporibus cum nox saeculi transierit, ut et Christus mane surrexit: unde Ad vesperum demorabitur fletus, et ad matutinum laetitia. Apostoli, vespere fleverunt mortuum, mane ad resurgentem exsultaverunt. Misericordiam. Quia totum gratis das: cum multa dixerit, non tamen omnia, in hoc uno omnia comprehendit.

PSALM LVIII.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end, destroy not. (CASS.) In vain does any man attempt to destroy what the divine authority so often forbids. Destroy not. (AUG.) When Pilate said: What I have written, I have written, etc., as far as and to have renown among all nations. (CASS.) He prays first to be delivered, ascending from the lowest things to the highest: he prays also for the salvation of the Gentiles. (AUG.) Here the whole Christ speaks, namely the head and the body.

VERS. 2.-- Deliver me. (Ibid.) While he who is without stain asks this, he shows what we must needs ask. From my enemies. (CASS.) There are four kinds of adversaries, 929Betc., as far as of these therefore he says: Deliver me, etc.

VERS. 4.-- The mighty. (AUG.) There are also those who presume upon their own justice, etc., as far as but hoping in riches they have prevailed in their vanity.

VERS. 5.-- Iniquity. (CASS.) To the ill-willing [Malivolenti; read malivolentiae, "of ill-will"]: sin, of the deed.

VERS. 6.-- Arise. (AUG.) Because thou seemest to sleep, To meet me. As though I run to thee by deserving: and do thou run to meet me, that is, render according to my desert. See. (Ibid.) That is, cause it to be seen how I run to thee, etc., as far as after thou hast seen me die, thou believest me equal to the Father.

VERS. 7.-- They shall be converted. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. The salvation of the Gentiles that was prayed for is affirmed, and, for him who is yet to pray, the salvation of the Jews. At evening, that is, later, after the ascension and the sending of 929Cthe Spirit, etc., as far as I fast twice in the week. They shall go round about. (AUG.) They shall fortify the Churches against the assaults of heretics. And, behold, they shall speak openly.

VERS. 8.-- And a sword. That they may slay and eat. For who hath heard? As though none had: so shall all wonder, etc., as far as thou shalt bring to nothing, or convert. A sword. (Ibid.) This is the sword twice sharpened, cutting with either Testament, wherewith Peter slays the creeping things shown to him in the dish, when it was said to him: Arise, Peter, slay and eat. [Vulg. Act 10:13 occide, et manduca, "kill, and eat"]

VERS. 9.-- Thou shalt laugh them to scorn unto nothing. (Ibid.) Those who say, Who hath heard? Why? Because he will count it as nothing to convert all the Gentiles, because all the Gentiles are to be Christian; and you say, who hath heard?

929DVERS. 10.-- I will keep my strength to thee, for God is my protector, O God. (Ibid.) Even though I could destroy the Jews — why have the mighty rushed in upon me? — [quid; read qui, "who"], yet I permit them to live, keeping my strength for thee, that is, for thy disposing.

VERS. 12.-- He hath shown. (Ibid.) that is, how great a mercy he has toward me he has shown me in those toward whom he has none; whence the Apostle: He endured the vessels of wrath, fitted, and unto destruction, with much patience, that he might make known his riches upon the vessels of mercy (Rom. IX). [Vulg. Rom 9:22–23 sustinuit in multa patientia vasa irae, apta in interitum, ut ostenderet divitias gloriae suae, "the riches of his glory"] Slay them not. It may be taken of the Jews, etc., as far as it is shown what mercy belongs to those grafted in. (CASS.) To one considering what is to be done concerning them, if they be not witnesses of the law and of the death of Christ. Lest at any time they forget. 930A(AUG.) Even though they have not just now forgotten, since they are not witnesses of the law and of the death of Christ. In thy strength. Because thou art strong, not they. Bring them down, there was a reproach there to all. Or, bring them down in that wherein they are evil, that the good may rise: as in Paul, because Paul would not rise, unless Saul first fell (Act. IX).

VERS. 13, 14.-- The sin of their mouth. (Ibid.) It is not them, but the sin, that thou art to slay, so that they may fear him whom they wished to destroy, now raised up again. (CASS.) And let them be taken when converted; because their deed, etc., as far as but pardon blotted out the crime. In their pride. (AUG.) Pride is the companion of envy: nor can it come about that a proud man should not envy: whence the devil also envies man. And of cursing. Or of the curse, which you thought a curse, etc., as far as because in these things they were caught. 930BThey shall be declared in consummation. Or, consummations shall be declared, that is, it shall be preached by the Apostles: Where the sin of exercise and of lying abounded, the grace of perfection did more abound; and it belonged to the medicine of man's humility and weakness. In the wrath of consummation. For there is a wrath, that is, a vengeance of God, of consummation, because God sometimes takes vengeance in order to perfect; and there is one of consuming, as when he shall say: Go, ye cursed, into everlasting fire. And they shall know. [Vulg. Mt 25:41 Discedite a me maledicti in ignem aeternum, "Depart from me, ye cursed"] For before this the Jews seemed just to themselves: but it is shown to them that this is not so without Christ, who rules over Jacob: and, their pride laid aside, they know themselves equal to the Gentiles, because all have sinned.

VERS. 15.-- They shall be converted at evening. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. The salvation of the Jews is affirmed, and, both 930Cwalls being gathered in, thanks are given.

VERS. 16.-- They shall murmur. (Ibid.) Or, they shall murmur, that is, they shall grieve that even now they are so far scattered; or, they shall murmur against the slothful, that is, they shall rebuke others who are unwilling to believe.

VERS. 17.-- But I. (Ibid.) Here this psalm is concluded, where, both walls being joined in the corner stone, the whole Church now rejoices. And I will exalt. When the times are past, when the night of the world shall have gone by, as Christ also rose in the morning: whence In the evening weeping shall have place, and in the morning gladness. The Apostles wept in the evening for him who was dead; in the morning they rejoiced at him rising again. Mercy. Because thou givest all things freely: though he has said many things, yet not all, in this one thing he has comprehended all.

PSALMUS LIX.

930DVERS. 1.-- In finem pro his. (AUG.) In historiis non legitur, etc., usque ad hominem ad fidem; terrenos, ut vivant coelestes.

(BASIL. et THEOD.) Haec regum historia describit. Praevidet autem populum praevaricaturum, captivum abducendum, et poenitentem reducendum. Ideo inscripsit: Pro iis qui mutabuntur. Doctrinam. (AUG.) Mutantur in doctrinam, etc., usque ad Edom terrenus vitam in coelestem. Et percussit. Cum percussit Edom gladio spiritus, etc., usque ad docet beatam esse contritionem per quam probat commutandos ad aeterna.

931AVERS. 3.-- Deus, repulisti nos. (CASS.) Primo referuntur percussiones factae pro aeternis poenis vitandis: Repulisti. In Adam. Et destruxisti ab immortalitate. Quia iratus es pro peccatis, et tamen misertus, per filium, sic quod commovisti ab errore: Et turbasti, poenitentiam: ut ergo coepisti, perfice, sana.

VERS. 5.-- Ostendisti. (AUG.) Mutato enim homine in melius, etc., usque ad ferre adversa usque in finem. Dura. (CASS.) Id est, temporis miserias, quae nobis per charitatem sunt delectabiles, et per infirmitatem carnis graves. Vino, id est, tribulatione, qua purgatur patiens, ut vulnus vino: Viuo, spirituali, unde non vitia, sed compunctio.

VERS. 6.-- Arcus. (AUG.) Quanto plus retro tenditur, 931Btanto impetuosius sagitta in priora fertur, id est, quanto magis differtur judicium, tanto gravius venturum est. Et liberentur. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. De liberatione quam precatur et affirmatur, pro qua gratae sunt percussiones.

VERS. 7.-- Dextera tua. (AUG.) Ut stemus ad dexteram, etc., usque ad de terrenis non nisi utiliter.

VERS. 8.-- Deus locutus est. (Ibid.) Hac fiducia oro, quam Deus in Christo promisit, etc., usque ad vox est Ecclesiae: Laetabor. Sichimam. Interpretatur humeri, id est, onus Christi, etc., usque ad alii jugum Christi ferant. Convallem tabernaculorum: propter oves Jacob signat Judaeos, qui etiam dividuntur; quia alii credunt, alii non, id est, de Judaeis 931Chabebo non paucos.

VERS. 9.-- Manasses. (Ibid.) Vel, Manasses omnis ille qui, oblitus prioris vitae, etc., usque ad: et opprobrii viduitatis tuae non recordaberis. Ephraim. Fructificatio: et haec est fortitudo capitis, id est, Christi: granum enim moriens virtutem in se habet, ut fructum faceret.

VERS. 10.-- Moab olla spei meae. (Ibid.) Filiae male utentes patre, etc., usque ad cum charitas ardet contra ollam iniquitatis. (CASS.) Moab olla spei meae. Vel per Moab, etc., usque ad unde spes mihi vitae est. (HIER.) Olla, unde: Ollam succensam ego video, etc., usque ad: Ab illo ergo tribulationum olla in Ecclesia ebullit.

VERS. 11.-- Civitatem munitam. (CASS.) Futuram 931DJerusalem. In Idumaeam, id est, usque ad terrenos, ut impleto numero simul ad beatitudinem veniret.

VERS. 12.-- Non egredieris. (AUG.) Sed intus operaberis, et sic melius deducet, quia sic videtur non pro temporali vita pugnare, sed pro futura.

PSALM LIX.

930DVERS. 1.-- Unto the end, for these. (AUG.) It is not read in the histories, etc., as far as a man unto the faith; earthly men, that they may live as heavenly.

(BASIL. et THEOD.) The history of the kings describes these things. But he foresees that the people will transgress, that they are to be led away captive, and that, repenting, they are to be brought back. Therefore he inscribed it: For those who shall be changed. Doctrine. [Vulg. Ps 59:1 pro his qui immutabuntur … in doctrinam, "for them that shall be changed … unto doctrine"] (AUG.) They are changed into doctrine, etc., as far as Edom, the earthly man, his life into a heavenly one. And he smote. When he smote Edom with the sword of the spirit, etc., as far as he teaches that blessed is the contrition through which he proves those who are to be changed for things eternal.

931AVERS. 3.-- O God, thou hast cast us off. (CASS.) First are recounted the strokes inflicted for the avoiding of eternal punishments: Thou hast cast off. In Adam. And thou hast destroyed from immortality. Because thou art angry for our sins, and yet hast had mercy, through the Son, in such wise that thou hast moved us out of error: And thou hast troubled, [Vulg. Ps 59:4 conturbasti, "hast disturbed"] penitence: as therefore thou hast begun, complete it, heal.

VERS. 5.-- Thou hast shewn. (AUG.) For when a man has been changed for the better, etc., as far as to bear adversities even unto the end. Hard things. (CASS.) That is, the miseries of time, which are delightful to us through charity, and grievous through the infirmity of the flesh. With wine, that is, with tribulation, by which the sufferer is purged, as a wound is by wine: with wine, spiritual Viuo, whence not vices, but compunction.

VERS. 6.-- A bow. (AUG.) The further back it is drawn, 931Bthe more violently is the arrow carried forward, that is, the longer judgment is deferred, the more heavily will it come. And that they may be delivered. [Vulg. Ps 59:6 ut liberentur, a purpose clause, "that they may be delivered"] (CASS.) Diapsalmus. Concerning the deliverance which he prays for and which is affirmed, for the sake of which the strokes are welcome.

VERS. 7.-- Thy right hand. (AUG.) That we may stand at the right hand, etc., as far as concerning earthly things not save profitably.

VERS. 8.-- God hath spoken. (Ibid.) With this confidence I pray, which God promised in Christ, etc., as far as it is the voice of the Church: I will rejoice. Sichem. It is interpreted shoulders, that is, the burden of Christ, etc., as far as others may bear the yoke of Christ. The vale of tabernacles: because of the sheep of Jacob it signifies the Jews, who also are divided; because some believe, others do not, that is, of the Jews 931CI shall have not a few.

VERS. 9.-- Manasses. (Ibid.) Or, Manasses is every man who, having forgotten his former life, etc., as far as: and thou shalt not remember the reproach of thy widowhood. Ephraim. Fruit-bearing: and this is the strength of the head, that is, of Christ: for the dying grain has power in itself, that it might bring forth fruit.

VERS. 10.-- Moab is the pot of my hope. (Ibid.) Daughters ill-using their father, etc., as far as when charity burns against the pot of iniquity. (CASS.) Moab is the pot of my hope. Or by Moab, etc., as far as whence there is hope of life for me. (HIER.) A pot, whence: I see a boiling pot, etc., as far as: From him, therefore, the pot of tribulations boils up in the Church.

VERS. 11.-- A fortified city. (CASS.) The 931DJerusalem that is to come. Into Idumaea, that is, even to earthly men, that, the number being filled, it might come together unto blessedness.

VERS. 12.-- Thou wilt not go forth. (AUG.) But thou wilt work within, and so he will lead thee better, because thus he is seen to fight not for the temporal life, but for the life to come.

PSALMUS LX.

VERS. 3.-- Clamavi dum anxiaretur. (CASS.) In anxietate, etc., usque ad sequitur clamoris exaudito in petra Christo. Exaltasti me. (AUG.) De imo vitiorum. (CASS.) Et exaltatum deduxisti. (AUG.) In petra, et ideo non vincor; Exaltasti: per exemplum istius magna spes audiendi praestatur aliis. Deduxisti (Ibid.) me, per te viam, ad te veritatem et vitam.

932AVERS. 5.-- Inhabitabo. (CASS.) De beneficiis Dei confidit, ut contra pericula mundi in tabernaculo Dei tutus perseveret. In saecula. Quousque saecula peragantur; quia etsi multi contra: Protegar in velamento. Protegar in velamento alarum. Quae nec onerant, et omnem laesionem avertunt. In saecula, non unus homo usque in saecula, sed Ecclesia, quae usque ad finem mundi accolit terra, et nunquam eradicatur per adversa.

VERS. 6.-- Quoniam tu, Deus meus, exaudisti orationem, etc. (Ibid.) Diapsalma. Jam audita de haereditate habita vel habenda, affirmat, unde laudes promittit. Dedisti. Nec dicam, dabis: adeo certus sum, quasi jam essem in ipsa.

VERS. 7.-- Dies super dies. (AUG.) Quidquid vis 932Bdicis de aeternitate, etc., usque ad sed regnent cum illo sancti in aeternum. Vel dabis haereditatem. (CASS.) Hanc scilicet, quia super dies, Christi, etc., usque ad quia rex ille permanet in aeternum, sic et illi. Misericordiam et veritatem. (AUG.) Misericordia est, quia non meritis, sed bonitate peccata dimittit, et vitam promittit. Veritas, quia non fallit, sed reddit quod promisit. Misericordiam sequi debemus circa infirmos et circa inimicos. Veritatem, non peccando, ut sit justus. (CASS.) Misericordiam et veritatem. Est hic conclusio psalmi, etc., usque ad: quis requiret ei? (AUG.) Ut non quaerat aliquis discere haec in libris, et post sibi vivat, non illi.

PSALM LX.

VERS. 3.-- I cried while my heart was in anguish. (CASS.) In anguish, etc., as far as there follows, of the cry heard, on the rock Christ. Thou hast exalted me. (AUG.) Out of the depth of vices. (CASS.) And thou hast led me exalted. (AUG.) On a rock, and therefore I am not overcome; Thou hast exalted: by the example of this man a great hope of being heard is afforded to others. Thou hast led (Ibid.) me, through thee the way, unto thee the truth and the life.

932AVERS. 5.-- I will dwell. (CASS.) He trusts in the benefits of God, that against the perils of the world he may persevere safe in the tabernacle of God. For ever. Until the ages be accomplished; for although many are against him: I shall be protected under the covering. I shall be protected under the covering of the wings. Which neither burden, and turn away every hurt. For ever, not one man for ever, but the Church, which until the end of the world dwells on the earth, and is never rooted up by adversities.

VERS. 6.-- For thou, my God, hast heard my prayer, etc. (Ibid.) Diapsalma. He now affirms what has been heard concerning the inheritance possessed or to be possessed, whence he promises praises. Thou hast given. Nor will I say, thou wilt give: so certain am I, as though I were already in it.

VERS. 7.-- Day upon day. (AUG.) Whatever thou wilt, 932Bthou sayest of eternity, etc., as far as but let the saints reign with him for ever. Or thou wilt give an inheritance. (CASS.) This one, namely, because it is upon the days of Christ, etc., as far as because that king abides for ever, so also do they. Mercy and truth. (AUG.) It is mercy, because he forgives sins not by merits but by goodness, and promises life. Truth, because he does not deceive, but renders what he promised. Mercy we ought to follow toward the weak and toward enemies. Truth, by not sinning, that he may be just. (CASS.) Mercy and truth. Here is the conclusion of the psalm, etc., as far as: who shall seek them for him? [Vulg. Ps 60:8 misericordiam et veritatem ejus quis requiret, "who shall seek his mercy and truth"] (AUG.) That no one may seek to learn these things in books, and afterwards live to himself, not to him.

PSALMUS LXI.

932CVERS. 1.-- In finem pro Idithun. (AUG.) Transiliens, videns tot occurrentia, Deo se subdit, qui altior eo; et inferioribus se, quasi de alto respondet increpando. Transiliens, invidis respondet, volentibus decipere.

VERS. 2.-- Nonne. (Ibid.) Hoc est, non veniat mihi pes superbiae. Non movebor amplius, hoc est, et manus peccatoris non moveat me. Deo subjecta semper, nil praeter eum cupiens. Erit quidem, quia ab ipso salutare meum, a Patre Filius auctor salutis, quia et Deus, ne minor putetur.

VERS. 4.-- Quousque irruitis. (Ibid.) Vel, secundum aliam litteram: Quousque apponitis, et idem sensus. Apponunt enim mali super hominem, id est, super Ecclesiam, onera passionum: ut usque in finem 932Dimpleat quisque fidelis in corpore suo quod deest passionum Christi. Universi vos. (CASS.) Vel, secundum aliam litteram: Omnes vos, quasi vos omnes interficitis hominem illum, quantum ad hominem, non omnes unum, sed Ecclesiam; sed quis Deus susceptor non movebor. (AUG.) Quousque, a sanguine Abel, etc., usque ad non scilicet quod est fundator altissimus. In hominem. (CASS.) In corpus potestas vobis data est, non in animam. Irruitis. Non leviter, sed interficitis innocentem; putatis quod sine defensore sit, et quod facile corruat, ut paries inclinatus, qui etiam non impulsus caderet. Et quasi maceria, quae est constructio saxorum sine ligamine caementi; et ne de ipsa novitate firmam 933Aputes, addit impulsae, vel, non vobis irruendum, quia vos ipsos interficitis universi, etiam consentientes.

VERS. 5.-- Pretium. (CASS.) Christum, ne coleretur, vel, beatitudinem tollere. Cogitaverunt. (AUG.) Nota diversa genera hostium, etc., usque ad de hac propheta ait: Gloriosa dicta sunt de te, civitas. Cucurri in siti. Quia etsi semper eos bibit, tamen semper sitit ultra. Ore suo. Quia nequeunt per aperta mala, tentant per blanda.

VERS. 6.-- Verumtamen Deo, etc. (CASS.) Diapsalma. Item se, id est, animam suam subjici hortatur, et admonet reliquos. Subjecta est anima mea. Haec petitio menti nostrae robur infigit.

VERS. 8.-- In Deo, salutare meum. (Ibid.) Tunc 933Bsalvus et gloriosus in eo: modo quid? ipse Deus auxilii.

VERS. 9.-- Sperate. (Ibid.) Sua fide vulgata monet omnes, qui superstitionibus laborant, sperare in Domino. Effundite. (AUG.) Per lacrymas cor effunditur, etc., usque ad: Unde, Punge oculum, et producit lacrymam; punge cor, et producit scientiam (Eccl. XXII). Corda, etc., pravas cogitationes.

VERS. 10.-- Verumtamen vani. (HIER.) Vel, sic junge, Deus est adjutor noster; et licet sic cooperetur nobis, tamen filii Adae sunt vani et mendaces in statera, pervertentes Scripturas, quibus probent falsa. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. Errantes exprobrat, et monet in Deo, non in caducis, confidere, quod psalmus intendit. Mendaces in stateris. Qui iniquis ponderibus 933Cementes decipiunt, vel justi videri volunt, cum sint fallaces. In stateris. In libra justitiae, quo facilius decipiunt, In idipsum, quo credentur aequi.

VERS. 11.-- Nolite sperare in. (AUG.) Quasi diceret: Nec speretis, nec cupiatis, quae congregata ab aliis rapiuntur. Nolite, sitiens convertit se ad eos. Nolite. Rapinas. Praedam quam vis rapere, in muscipula est, tenes et teneris; tenes, alienum scilicet, et teneris a diabolo. O lucra damnosa! invenis pecuniam, perdis justitiam. Affluant. Nolite cor. (CASS.) Non dicit: Nolite habere, non enim damnat divitias, unde mercamur coelum; sed cor appositum, quod non expendit, sed recondit.

VERS. 12.-- Semel locutus est. (AUG.) Nolite cor apponere. Cur? quia potestas judicandi est Dei filii, 933Detc., usque ad nec pro potestate de misericordia desperetur. Potestas Dei est: non est potestas cuiquam nisi a Deo aequo, etsi te lateat aequitas.

PSALM LXI.

932CVERS. 1.-- Unto the end, for Idithun. (AUG.) Leaping over, seeing so many things that meet him, he submits himself to God, who is higher than he; and to those beneath him he answers as from on high, by rebuking. Leaping over, he answers the envious, who wish to deceive.

VERS. 2.-- Shall not. (Ibid.) That is, let not the foot of pride come to me. I shall not be moved any more, that is, and let not the hand of the sinner move me. Subject to God always, desiring nothing besides him. It shall be indeed, because from him is my salvation, from the Father the Son, the author of salvation, because he is God also, lest he be thought less.

VERS. 4.-- How long do ye rush in. (Ibid.) Or, according to another reading: How long do ye lay on, and the sense is the same. For the wicked lay upon a man, that is, upon the Church, the burdens of sufferings: so that unto the end 932Devery faithful man may fill up in his own body what is wanting of the sufferings of Christ. All ye together. (CASS.) Or, according to another reading: All of you, as though ye all kill that man, so far as concerns the man, not all one man, but the Church; but because God is my upholder I shall not be moved [quis; read quia, "because"]. (AUG.) How long, from the blood of Abel, etc., as far as not, namely, that which is the most high founder. Upon a man. (CASS.) Power has been given you over the body, not over the soul. Ye rush in. Not lightly, but ye kill the innocent; ye think that he is without a defender, and that he easily falls, like a leaning wall, which would fall even if it were not pushed. And as a fence, which is a construction of stones without the binding of mortar; and lest by its very newness thou 933Ashouldst think it firm, he adds pushed, [Vulg. Ps 61:4 depulsae, "thrust down"] or, ye must not rush in, because ye kill your own selves, all of you, even those who consent.

VERS. 5.-- The price. (CASS.) Christ, that he should not be worshipped, or, to take away blessedness. They have thought. (AUG.) Note the diverse kinds of enemies, etc., as far as of her the prophet says: Glorious things are said of thee, O city. I ran in thirst. For although he always drinks them, yet he always thirsts beyond. With their mouth. Because they are not able by open evils, they attempt by soft ones.

VERS. 6.-- But yet to God, etc. (CASS.) Diapsalma. Again he exhorts himself, that is, his own soul, to be made subject, and admonishes the rest. My soul is subject. [Vulg. Ps 61:6 Verumtamen Deo subjecta esto, anima mea, an imperative, "be thou subject to God, O my soul"] This petition fixes strength in our mind.

VERS. 8.-- In God is my salvation. (Ibid.) Then 933Bsafe and glorious in him: but now what? He himself is the God of my help.

VERS. 9.-- Hope ye. (Ibid.) His own faith being published abroad, he admonishes all who labour under superstitions to hope in the Lord. Pour out. (AUG.) Through tears the heart is poured out, etc., as far as: Whence, Prick the eye, and it produces a tear; prick the heart, and it produces knowledge (Eccl. XXII). [Vulg. Sir 22:24 Pungens oculum deducit lacrimas, et qui pungit cor profert sensum, "he who pricks the eye draws out tears, and he who pricks the heart brings forth understanding"] Hearts, etc., evil thoughts.

VERS. 10.-- But yet vain. (HIER.) Or, join it thus, God is our helper; and although he so works with us, yet the sons of Adam are vain and lying in the balance, perverting the Scriptures, by which they may prove false things. (CASS.) Diapsalmus. He reproaches those who go astray, and admonishes them to trust in God, not in things that perish, which is what the psalm intends. Lying in the balances. Who with unjust weights 933Cdeceive buyers, or wish to seem just, though they are deceitful. In the balances. In the scale of justice, whereby they deceive the more easily. Unto the same thing, whereby they may be believed fair.

VERS. 11.-- Hope ye not in. (AUG.) As if he should say: Neither hope ye, nor desire ye, the things which, when gathered, are snatched away by others. Do not, thirsting he turns himself to them. Do not. Rapines. The prey which thou wilt seize is in a trap, thou holdest and art held; thou holdest, another's goods that is, and art held by the devil. O ruinous gains! thou findest money, thou losest justice. Let them abound. Set not your heart. (CASS.) He does not say: Do not possess, for he does not condemn riches, whereby we purchase heaven; but the heart set upon them, which does not spend but hoards.

VERS. 12.-- He hath spoken once. (AUG.) Set not your heart upon them. Why? Because the power of judging belongs to the Son of God, 933Detc., as far as nor let mercy be despaired of on account of that power. Power belongeth to God: there is no power to any man save from God who is just, although his equity lie hidden from thee.

PSALMUS LXII.

Psalmus David. (CASS.) Loquitur de Ecclesia, quae in ariditate sitit saeculi, et misericordiam expetit, donec aeterna capiat, docens bene conversari in medio pravae nationis. (AUG.) Psalmus ex persona capitis et membrorum; vox ipsius nostra est, et nostra ipsius est.

VERS. 2.-- Deus, Deus meus, ad te de luce, etc. (Ibid.) Quomodo se habeat in deserto, scilicet sponsa, Deum videre desiderat, quem et laudat, et id amplius 934Aagere optat. Deus. (Ibid.) Communis Deus meus quodam modo specialiori; vide affectum piae deprecationis per hanc geminationem. De luce. Vel diluculo, quando surrexit Christus, ut tunc laudet eum Ecclesia quando exemplo suae resurrectionis eam ad surgendum animavit. Vigilo, dummodo dormio, non amans quae mundi sunt. (CASS.) Et sitio animo et corpore. De luce. (AUG.) Non enim vigilares, nisi lux oriretur, quae te excitaret. Sitivit in te anima mea: et hic caro Deo, dum ab eo quaerit hic necessaria.

VERS. 3.-- Deserta. (Ibid.) Ubi nullus sanctorum habitat. Invia, quia non est qua inde exeas. Inaquosa, quia nec, dum ubi moraris, est ibi aqua. Sed Deus hic fecit viam Christum, et misit aquam 934BVerbi sui Spiritu sancto implens praedicatores: Ut fieret in eis fons aquae salientis in vitam aeternam (Joan. IV). Sic in sancto apparui tibi ut viderem, etc. (AUG.) Cui non apparet Deus sit in sancto desiderio, etc., usque ad Sol enim sua luce facit nos videre, ita et Deus.

VERS. 4.-- Super vitas. (Ibid.) Humanitatis, quae multae sunt, ut militis, agricolae et caeterorum: melius est quod das correctis, quam quod eligunt perversi. Labia mea.
