Post beneficia Dei: laudem promittit. Laudabunt, ad proximum, de quo etiam sollicitor, quia nisi misericordia tua me praeveniret, te laudare non possem, et sicut labiis, sic benedicant in vita. Vel sic, Quia super vitas.

VERS. 5.-- Sic benedicam. (Ibid.) Ut dedisti per 934Cmisericordiam laudare te, sic benedicam, ut misericordiae tribuam vitam, in qua laudo. In nomine tuo levabo manus meas. (Ibid.) Levat manus qui, bonis operibus insistens, tensis manibus in figura crucis, Deum unde adorat; unde Apostolus: Levantes puras manus in oratione, sine ira et disceptatione.

VERS. 6.-- Adipe. (Ibid.) In intestinis. Pinguedo in carne, id est, sapientia, quae in abscondito et fortitudo spiritus.

Levabo manus. (Ibid.) In Exod. Moyses, dum levaret manus ad Dominum, etc., usque ad pro terrenis operatur, vincitur ab Amalech.

VERS. 7.-- Si memor fui. (CASS.) Exponit bona malaque utriusque partis, etc., usque ad nisi qui in 934DChristo operatur.

(CASS.) In matutinis, id est, in luce Christi, ut supra de luce vigilo ad te, ut filius lucis, id est Christi, ad lucis auctorem vigilet, ad Deum.

VERS. 8.-- Adjutor, etc. (AUG.) In periculis Idumaeae, atc., usque ad quia me suscepit a periculis dextera tua, id est propitiatio.

VERS. 10.-- Ipsi vero in vanum quaesierunt animam. Rex vero. Confert in his duobus versibus bona et mala diversarum partium.

In inferiora terrae. (CASS.) Quia non ad coelos evecti sunt. A terra sorbentur malae cogitationes, quia de terra natae, in ima terrae, quasi in coenum, vergunt.

VERS. 11.-- Partes vulpium erunt, etc. (CASS.) 935APrincipium saeculi, etc., usque ad dum se dolosis prava voluntate conjungunt.

VERS. 12.-- In Deo. (CASS.) Patre, unde: Ego in Patre, et Pater in me. Jurant, non per eum, ne imperet juramentum, sed in eo, promittendo ei obsequium.

PSALM LXII.

A psalm of David. (CASS.) He speaks of the Church, which in the drought of the world thirsts, and seeks after mercy, until she lay hold of things eternal, teaching men to converse well in the midst of a depraved nation. (AUG.) A psalm in the person of the head and of the members; his voice is ours, and ours is his.

VERS. 2.-- O God, my God, to thee from the light, etc. (Ibid.) How she fares in the desert, namely the bride, she desires to see God, whom she also praises, and she wishes to do this 934Athe more. God. (Ibid.) Common, my God in a somewhat more particular way; see the affection of devout entreaty through this doubling. From the light. Or at daybreak, when Christ rose again, that the Church may praise him then, when by the example of his own resurrection he quickened her to rise. I watch, even while I sleep, not loving the things that are of the world. (CASS.) And I thirst in mind and in body. From the light. (AUG.) For thou wouldst not watch; unless the light arose, which should rouse thee. My soul hath thirsted for thee: and here the flesh for God, while it seeks from him the things needful here.

VERS. 3.-- Desert. (Ibid.) Where none of the saints dwells. Trackless, because there is no way by which thou mayest go out thence. Waterless, because neither, while thou tarriest where thou art, is there water there. But God here made a way, Christ, and sent the water 934Bof his Word, filling the preachers with the Holy Ghost: That there might be made in them a fountain of water springing up into life everlasting (Joan. IV). [Vulg. Jo 4:14 fiet in eo fons aquae salientis in vitam aeternam, "shall become in him a fountain", indicative and singular] So in the sanctuary have I appeared to thee, that I might see, etc. (AUG.) He to whom God does not appear, let him be in holy desire, etc., as far as For the sun by its own light makes us to see, and so also does God.

VERS. 4.-- Above lives. (Ibid.) Of human life, of which there are many, as that of the soldier, of the husbandman and of the rest: better is what thou givest to the corrected than what the perverse choose. My lips. After the benefits of God: he promises praise. Shall praise, toward my neighbour, for whom also I am solicitous, because unless thy mercy went before me, I could not praise thee, and as with the lips, so let them bless in life. Or thus, Because above lives.

VERS. 5.-- Thus will I bless. (Ibid.) As thou hast granted, through 934Cmercy, that I should praise thee, so will I bless, that I may ascribe to mercy the life in which I praise. In thy name I will lift up my hands. (Ibid.) He lifts up his hands who, persevering in good works, with hands stretched out in the figure of the cross, adores God unde; whence the Apostle: Lifting up pure hands in prayer, without anger and contention.

VERS. 6.-- With fatness. (Ibid.) In the inward parts. Fatness is in the flesh, that is, wisdom, which is in secret, and the strength of the spirit.

I will lift up my hands. (Ibid.) In Exodus. Moses, while he lifted up his hands to the Lord, etc., as far as he works for earthly things, he is overcome by Amalec.

VERS. 7.-- If I have remembered. (CASS.) He sets forth the good things and the evil of either party, etc., as far as save he who works in 934DChrist.

(CASS.) In the mornings, that is, in the light of Christ, as above, from the light I watch unto thee, that the son of light, that is, of Christ, may watch unto the author of light, unto God.

VERS. 8.-- A helper, etc. (AUG.) In the perils of Idumaea, etc., atc. as far as because it hath upheld me from perils, thy right hand, that is, propitiation.

VERS. 10.-- But they have sought my soul in vain. But the king. In these two verses he compares the good things and the evil of the different parties.

Into the lower parts of the earth. (CASS.) Because they were not carried up to the heavens. Evil thoughts are swallowed up by the earth, because, born of the earth, they sink into the depths of the earth, as into mire.

VERS. 11.-- They shall be the portions of foxes, etc. (CASS.) 935AThe beginning of the world, etc., as far as while by a perverse will they join themselves to the deceitful.

VERS. 12.-- In God. (CASS.) The Father, whence: I am in the Father, and the Father in me. They swear, not by him, lest he should command an oath, but in him, by promising him obedience.

PSALMUS LXIII.

(CASS.) Psalmus isto breviter agit, etc., usque ad ut in passionibus speremus in Domino. (AUG.) Ut caput nostrum, ita nos in tribulationibus rogemus.

VERS. 2.-- Exaudi, Deus, orationem. Ut exaltes, et eripe, quia deprecor. A timore inimici. (CASS.) Sed non a timore mortis.

VERS. 3.-- Protexisti me. (AUG.) Hoc in capite 935Bfactum, quod et membra experiuntur: hoc exemplo reliqui firmantur.

VERS. 4.-- Quia exacuerunt ut gladium linguas. Vel qui scilicet malignantes et operantes iniquitatem. Arcum. Occultas insidias, ut per discipulum, quod est res amara, ut conviva sit proditor. Amaram.

VERS. 6.-- Subito sagittabunt. (Ibid.) Insidiose, quasi nescientem ut eis videtur qui se credunt Deum fallere. Non timebunt. (Ibid.) O cor durum! occidere hominem, qui mortuos suscitabat, et inde non timere. Firmaverunt. (CASS.) Obstinatione, non veritate, sermonem. Reus est mortis: vel, Expedit ut unus moriatur. Sibi. (Ibid.) Non Domino, sed sibi, cum dicunt: Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios 935Cnostros. Ut absconderent. Mos malorum; qui dolum parat, putat se fallere.

VERS. 7.-- Scrutati. (CASS.) Quomodo accusarent justum, vel quomodo perderent, ne mundus post eum iret. (AUG.) Scrutina, id est, acerba et occulta consilia; sed quanto acutius cogitant, tanto plus deficiunt a veritate et aequitate, et in tenebras merguntur: quia cum non vident Deum, putant se non videri a Deo. Accedet homo. (CASS.) Nam qui scrutatur iniqua, etc., usque ad sed in corde hominis grandescit. (AUG.) Scrutati, sed frustra, quia sponte accedet homo ad passionem. Ad cor altum. (Ibid.) Erat ei, quia hoc faciebat secundum altum consilium.

Sagittae parvulorum factae. (CASS.) Enumeratam 935Dpravitatem irridet Judaeorum, qui magis turbati sunt nuntiata resurrectione, justi laetati.

VERS. 9.-- Conturbati. (Ibid.) Fuerunt illi qui, salutis suae consilium quaerentes, dixerunt: Quid faciemus, viri fratres?

VERS. 10.-- Et timuit omnis. (AUG.) Si timet homo, non terreat homo, quin annuntiet, sicut Apostoli, quibus comminaverunt principes sacerdotum, dicentes, ne praedicarent in nomine Jesu.

Et facta ejus intellexerunt. (Ibid.) Cur passus? cur non descendit de cruce? quia moriendum erat et resurgendum: quod tunc non fuit intellectum.

VERS. 11.-- Laetabitur justus in Domino. (CASS.) Conclusio ex praedictis, et ostenditur promissio justorum. 936AOmnes. (Ibid.) Ne putes de solis Apostolicis dici.

PSALM LXIII.

(CASS.) This psalm treats briefly [isto; read iste], etc., as far as that in sufferings we may hope in the Lord. (AUG.) As our head did, so let us pray in tribulations.

VERS. 2.-- Hear, O God, my prayer. That thou mayest exalt, and deliver, because I entreat. From the fear of the enemy. (CASS.) But not from the fear of death.

VERS. 3.-- Thou hast protected me. (AUG.) This was done in the head, 935Bwhich the members also experience: by this example the rest are made firm.

VERS. 4.-- For they have whetted their tongues like a sword. Or, those namely who are malicious and who work iniquity. A bow. Hidden snares, as through a disciple, which is a bitter thing, that a guest at table should be a betrayer. Bitter.

VERS. 6.-- They will shoot suddenly. (Ibid.) Treacherously, as at one who does not know, so it seems to them who believe that they deceive God. They will not fear. (Ibid.) O hard heart! to kill a man who raised the dead, and thereafter not to fear. They have made firm. (CASS.) By obstinacy, not by truth, their word. He is guilty of death: or, It is expedient that one should die. For themselves. (Ibid.) Not for the Lord, but for themselves, when they say: His blood be upon us and upon our 935Cchildren. That they might hide. The way of the wicked; he who prepares a deceit thinks that he deceives.

VERS. 7.-- They have searched out. (CASS.) How they might accuse the just man, or how they might destroy him, lest the world should go after him. (AUG.) Searchings, that is, bitter and hidden counsels; but the more keenly they think, the more do they fall away from truth and equity, and are plunged into darkness: for because they do not see God, they think that they are not seen by God. A man shall come. (CASS.) For he who searches out unjust things, etc., as far as but it grows great in the heart of man. (AUG.) They searched out, but in vain, because of his own accord the man shall come to the passion. To a deep heart. (Ibid.) He had one, because he did this according to a deep counsel.

The arrows of little ones are made. (CASS.) He derides the enumerated 935Dwickedness of the Jews, who were the more troubled when the resurrection was announced, while the just rejoiced.

VERS. 9.-- Troubled. (Ibid.) They were, who, seeking counsel for their own salvation, said: What shall we do, men and brethren?

VERS. 10.-- And every man feared. (AUG.) If a man fears, let not a man terrify him from proclaiming, as the Apostles did, whom the chief priests threatened, saying that they should not preach in the name of Jesus.

And they understood his doings. (Ibid.) Why did he suffer? why did he not come down from the cross? because he had to die and to rise again: which then was not understood.

VERS. 11.-- The just shall rejoice in the Lord. (CASS.) A conclusion from the things aforesaid, and the promise of the just is shown. 936AAll. (Ibid.) Do not think that it is said of the apostolic men alone.

PSALMUS LXIV.

In finem. (AUG.) Prophetavit Jeremias (XXV, XXIX) post septuaginta annos rediturum populum. Inter captivos erat Ezechiel et alii prophetae. Completis septuaginta annis restitutum est templum. Figura est nostri, qui de Babylonia ad Jerusalem suspiramus, de saeculo et corpore peccati ad coelum.

VERS. 1.-- Jeremiae. (AUG., HIER.) Excelsus; et significat eos, qui dicunt: Nostra conversatio in coelis est. Aggoeus, festus. Illos significat, qui sunt spe gaudentes, qui in reliquiis cogitationum diem festum agunt Domino; Ezechiel, roboravit me Dominus, et 936Bsignificat illos, qui sunt roborati in Domino; hi prophetaverunt reditum in Jerusalem.

De populo transmigrationis. (AUG.) Id est, qui transmigravit de coelo ad terram, de perfectione ad miseriam et confusionem. Cum inciperet. (Ibid.) Incipit exire, qui incipit amare; charitas civem facit Jerusalem, cupiditas Babylonis: et sic ergo corpore permisti, desiderio sunt separati. (CASS.) Consolatio in exsilio; ne quis desperet: quia certificat reditum, et per quem, et quae divitiae reversis. Affirmat reditum, et precatur.

VERS. 2.-- Te decet. Non deos gentium et non alibi, nisi in contemplatione, id est, fide, et ibi de bonis operibus reddetur votum, in coelesti Jerusalem, quod illi solvebant Marti post praelia, et caeteris 936Cdiis in hunc modum. Sion. Patria coelestis est Sion, eadem est Jerusalem

VERS. 3.-- Exaudi orationem meam. (CASS.) Prius facit quod a caeteris faciendum dicit, scilicet, exaudi. Omnis caro. (AUG.) Id est, homo, id est ex omni genere: pauperes, divites, viri, feminae, docti, indocti, pueri, senes.

VERS. 4.-- Verba iniquorum. (CASS.) Qua spe hoc oras? quia ad te omnis caro veniet, non solum anima, sed etiam malus homo. Necesse est ut audias. Verba enim iniquorum, diaboli et primitivorum parentum Adae et Evae. Praevaluerunt. Id est, in exsilium projecerunt, vel pagani, ritus suos filiis suis suaserunt, sed propitiaberis in hostia Christi. (AUG.) Verba iniquorum, id est, malos ritus et mores parentum nostrorum 936D(qui ut aetate, ita auctoritate praestant pueris) secuti sumus. Propitiaberis. (AUG.) Propitiatio fit per sacrificium, quod sacerdos Christum obtulit. Idem est ergo sacerdos et hostia.

VERS. 5.-- Beatus quem elegisti, etc. (CASS.) Et beatus omnis ille quem elegisti a massa perditorum. Non vos me elegistis, sed ego vos (Joan. XV), et assumpsisti in sortem tuam, in aeternam requiem. (AUG.) Vel sic, propitiaberis per beatum virum: etc., usque ad quae non possunt dici. In bonis. (CASS.) Quae bona sunt, sanctitas in se, aequitas ad proximum. Templum. Ecclesia, vel caro Christi.

VERS. 6.-- Mirabile. (AUG.) Non in exterioribus, ut domus terrae, sed in justitia, quae pulchrior interiori 937Aoculo et amabilior quam modo debemus esurire, ut tunc ea satiemur. In aequitate. (CAS.) Cum unicuique digna retribuet, cui et dicet: Exaudi nos, qui es Salvator. Spes omnium. Laudes Dei, et virtutes describit. Et in mari longe. (AUG.) Ideo longe, quia in mari. Mare dicitur in figura saeculi amari falsitate iniquitatum, et tempestuosi procellis tentationum, ubi pisces invicem se devorant.

VERS. 7.-- Praeparans montes. (AUG.) Ad usus competentes. In virtute tua. Quia per eos fecit miracula. Quomodo praeparavit? Accinctus potentia, id est Deitate, quia humanitas Verbi majestate praecincta est, ut quod homo non habuit, Deitas daret. Accinctus. (Ibid.) Christus in medio undique cinctus, quia omnes illum communiter habemus qui in 937Beum credimus, sed quia fides non a nobis, sed ab eo, potentatu suo cinctus dicitur.

VERS. 8.-- Qui conturbas profundum maris. Ecce qui per illos paratos fecit, conturbans ad poenitentiam. Profundum maris, non superficiem, sed corda profundius mersa, vel corda principum. Haec conturbata sunt, cum viderent et deos suos et spes suas ad nihilum venire. Sonum. (AUG.) Sonantes contradictione, fluctuantes persecutione, etc., usque ad dum istos plus diis suis valere cernunt.

VERS. 9.-- Matutini et vespere. (AUG.) Mane est prosperitas, quia laetum est mane post tristitiam noctis. Vespere adversitas; in his tentatur homo, sed datur ei exire inde, ne lucris capiatur, cui divitiae sunt Deus: ne adversis terreatur, pro quo passus 937Cest Dominus. Delectabis. Delectabiles facies jam in vita hac. Si enim non delectet hominem ipse exitus, non laborat inde exire, sed capitur lucris, cui non placet promissio Christi. Et terretur adversis, quem non delectat ille qui pro eo voluit pati, ut faceret exitum ei.

VERS. 10.-- Visitasti terram et inebriasti eam. Per praedicatores hoc facies, nam intus doces quibus praedicant.

Flumen. Profundi ad recipiendum repletum est aquis, donis Spiritus sancti, tu enim parasti cibum. Flumen Dei. (CAS.) Misericordia Dei pleno fluvio comparatur, etc., usque ad sicut ab eo disponitur, sine quo nihil ibi fit.

VERS. 11, 12.-- Rivos ejus. Apostolos et alios, qui 937Dde flumine biberunt. Inebria, ut sibi et aliis sufficiant. Multiplica, ut per successiones praedicatio non deficiat. Coronae anni, totus mundus, ubi Ecclesia. Rivos ejus. (Ibid.) Parasti, etc. Et, o Domine, etc., usque ad quo crescit Verbum Dei. Coronae anni. (Ibid.) Quia gloria victoriae est vincenti diabolum. Benignitatis tuae, etc. (AUG.) Ne quis glorietur de meritis suis.

Campi tui replebuntur. (CASS., AUG.) Homines, propter aequalitatem, id est, justi. Colles, quia Deus erigit humiles Desertum: omnes gentes, quibus nullus propheta missus.

VERS. 13.-- Pinguescent speciosa deserti. Quando Apostoli ad eos venerunt, per quos decorae factae sunt.

938AVERS. 14.-- Valles. (Ibid.) Humiles populi multum fructum afferent. Clamabuut. (Ibid.) Non in blasphemia, sed in hymno, inde abundant frumento.

Psalmus iste in exsequiis fidelium decantatur, quia agit de reditu a Babylonia hujus mundi ad patriam coelestem, ad quam sancti in obitu de carne educti, feliciter migrant, stolam simplam recipientes, donec in resurrectione geminae beatitudinis stola glorificentur.

PSALM LXIV.

Unto the end. (AUG.) Jeremias prophesied (XXV, XXIX) that after seventy years the people would return. Among the captives was Ezechiel and other prophets. When the seventy years were completed the temple was restored. It is a figure of us, who sigh from Babylon toward Jerusalem, from the world and from the body of sin toward heaven.

VERS. 1.-- Of Jeremias. (AUG., HIER.) Exalted; and it signifies those who say: Our conversation is in heaven. Aggoeus, festal. It signifies those who are rejoicing in hope, who in the remnants of their thoughts keep a feast day to the Lord; Ezechiel, the Lord strengthened me, and 936Bit signifies those who are strengthened in the Lord; these prophesied the return to Jerusalem.

Of the people of the transmigration. (AUG.) That is, which passed over from heaven to earth, from perfection to misery and confusion. When he began. (Ibid.) [Vulg. Ps 64:1 cum inciperent exire, plural, "when they began to go out"] He begins to go out who begins to love; charity makes a citizen of Jerusalem, cupidity a citizen of Babylon: and so therefore, mingled in body, they are separated in desire. (CASS.) A consolation in exile; lest any despair: because it makes the return certain, and by whom it is, and what riches there are for those who return. He affirms the return, and prays.

VERS. 2.-- It becometh thee. Not the gods of the nations, and not elsewhere, save in contemplation, that is, in faith, and there out of good works the vow shall be paid, in the heavenly Jerusalem, the vow which those men used to pay to Mars after battles, and to the other 936Cgods in this fashion. Sion. Sion is the heavenly country, the same is Jerusalem.

VERS. 3.-- Hear my prayer. (CASS.) He first does what he says is to be done by the rest, namely, hear. All flesh. (AUG.) That is, man, that is, out of every kind: poor, rich, men, women, learned, unlearned, boys, old men.

VERS. 4.-- The words of the wicked. (CASS.) In what hope dost thou pray this? Because to thee all flesh shall come, not the soul only, but the evil man also. It is necessary that thou hear. For the words of the wicked are the words of the devil and of our first parents Adam and Eve. They have prevailed. That is, they cast us into exile, or the pagans persuaded their own rites to their sons, but thou wilt be merciful in the sacrifice of Christ. (AUG.) The words of the wicked, that is, we have followed the evil rites and manners of our parents 936D(who, as in age, so in authority, surpass boys). Thou wilt be merciful. (AUG.) Propitiation is made through the sacrifice which the priest offered, Christ. The priest and the victim are therefore the same.

VERS. 5.-- Blessed is he whom thou hast chosen, etc. (CASS.) And blessed is every man whom thou hast chosen out of the mass of the lost. You have not chosen me, but I you (Joan. XV), and thou hast taken him into thy lot, into eternal rest. (AUG.) Or thus, thou wilt be merciful through the blessed man: etc., as far as things which cannot be told. In the good things. (CASS.) Which things are good, holiness in oneself, equity toward one's neighbour. The temple. The Church, or the flesh of Christ.

VERS. 6.-- Wonderful. (AUG.) Not in outward things, like a house of earth, but in justice, which is fairer to the inward 937Aeye and more lovely, and which we ought now to hunger for, that then we may be filled with it. In equity. (CAS.) When he shall render to each what is worthy, to whom [each] shall also say: Hear us, thou who art the Saviour. The hope of all. [Vulg. Ps 64:6 Exaudi nos, Deus, salutaris noster, "Hear us, O God our saviour"] He describes the praises of God, and his powers. And in the sea afar off. (AUG.) Therefore afar off, because in the sea. The sea is spoken of as a figure of the world, bitter with the falsehood of iniquities, and stormy with the tempests of temptations, where the fishes devour one another.

VERS. 7.-- Preparing the mountains. (AUG.) For fitting uses. In thy strength. Because through them he wrought miracles. How did he prepare them? Girded with power, that is, with Deity, because the humanity of the Word is girded about with majesty, so that what the man had not, the Deity might give. Girded. (Ibid.) Christ in the midst, girded on every side, because we all alike have him who 937Bbelieve in him, but because faith is not from us, but from him, he is said to be girded with his own might.

VERS. 8.-- Who troublest the depth of the sea. Behold, he who through those prepared ones wrought it, troubling them unto penitence. The depth of the sea, not the surface, but hearts more deeply sunk, or the hearts of princes. These were troubled, when they saw both their gods and their hopes come to nothing. The noise. (AUG.) Sounding with contradiction, tossing with persecution, etc., as far as while they perceive that these prevail more than their own gods.

VERS. 9.-- The morning and the evening. (AUG.) The morning is prosperity, because the morning is glad after the sadness of the night. The evening is adversity; in these a man is tempted, but it is granted him to go out thence, lest he be caught by gains, he to whom riches are God: lest he be terrified by adversities, he for whom the Lord 937Csuffered. Thou wilt delight. Thou wilt make them delightful even in this life. For if the going out itself does not delight a man, he does not labour to go out thence, but is caught by gains, he to whom the promise of Christ is not pleasing. And he is terrified by adversities, whom he does not delight who was willing to suffer for him, that he might make a going out for him.

VERS. 10.-- Thou hast visited the earth and hast inebriated it. Through preachers wilt thou do this, for within thou teachest those to whom they preach.

A river. Of the deep, for the receiving, it is filled with waters, with the gifts of the Holy Ghost, for thou hast prepared food. The river of God. (CAS.) The mercy of God is compared to a river in full flood, etc., as far as as it is disposed by him, without whom nothing is done there.

VERS. 11, 12.-- Its streams. The Apostles and others, who 937Ddrank of the river. Inebriate them, that they may suffice for themselves and for others. Multiply, that through successions preaching may not fail. The crown of the year, the whole world, where the Church is. Its streams. (Ibid.) Thou hast prepared, etc. And, O Lord, etc., as far as whereby the Word of God grows. The crown of the year. (Ibid.) Because the glory of victory belongs to him who conquers the devil. Of thy bounty, etc. (AUG.) Let no one glory in his own merits.

Thy fields shall be filled. (CASS., AUG.) Men, because of their evenness, that is, the just. The hills, because God raises up the humble The desert: all the Gentiles, to whom no prophet was sent.

VERS. 13.-- The beautiful places of the wilderness shall grow fat. When the Apostles came to them, through whom they were made comely.

938AVERS. 14.-- Valleys. (Ibid.) Lowly peoples shall bring forth much fruit. They shall cry out. (Ibid.) Clamabuut Not in blasphemy, but in a hymn, thence they abound with corn.

This psalm is sung at the funerals of the faithful, because it treats of the return from the Babylon of this world to the heavenly country, to which the saints, led forth from the flesh at their death, happily pass over, receiving the single robe, until in the resurrection they be glorified with the robe of a twofold beatitude.

PSALMUS LXV.

In finem. (AUG.) Judaei ex legis justitia sperabant sibi bona temporalia, et resurrectionem, etc., usque ad pro fide gentium ad eamdem spem resurrectionis vocaturum.

938BVERS. 1.-- Jubilate Deo, omnis terra, etc. (CAS.) Primo monet omnes de resurrectione Christi gaudere, quae omnibus dat vitam.

VERS. 3.-- Date gloriam. (AUG.) Non ut Judaei, qui meritis suis dant justitiam, et invident gentibus gratiam. Quam terribilia. (Ibid.) Si gaudes et time, ne quod datum est humili auferatur superbo: sicut factum est Judaeis. Ne ergo insultes fractis ramis, sed time, ne forte nec tibi parcat. Opera tua, Domine. (CAS.) Breviter mysteria incarnationis dicit opera, quod Deus homo, quod passus, mortuus, et hujusmodi. In multitudine virtutis tuae. (AUG.) Hic innuit resurrectionem ad quam, exclusis mendacibus Judaeis, adhibentur gentes.

(BEDA.) Resurrexit Dominus; multi crediderunt in eum, etc., usque ad per gratiam biberunt. Mentientur. 938COpera sunt terrae, quae inimici mentiuntur, contra mentientes, omnis terra adoret, etc. (AUG.) Mentientur. Solent mentiri inimici, etc., usque ad adoret omnis terra.

VERS. 5.-- Venite. (CAS.) Diapsalma. Incipientes ad opera Dei consideranda invitat, ut una fides jungat, quos unum praemium exspectat: ubi exponens illa opera, aperte dicit ressurrectionem pertinere ad gentes, repressis Judaeis.

VERS. 6.-- Qui convertit. (Ibid.) Opera, in quibus terribilis, et quae sunt ea, subdit: Qui convertit mare. In flumine Jordani ad litteram, mystice in labenti mundo. In flumine. (Ibid.) Licet remissa sint peccata, tamen in decursu mortalitatis adhuc sunt, non enim mox immortalitai.

938DIn flumine. (AUG.) Flumen est mortalitas saeculi ubi alii veniunt, alii recedunt: sed qui in Christum credit, transit pede in se humilis, non equo superbus. Ibi laetabimur. (Ibid.) Vel sic: Terribilia sunt opera, etc., usque ad et in his laetantur Christiani. In ipso. (Ibid.) Quando erit omnia in omnibus, vel in ipso qui dominatur, in virtute sua.

VERS. 7.-- Non exaltentur. (Ibid.) Pro lege quasi plus illis debeatur. Omnes enim peccaverunt, etc. (Rom. III.)

VERS. 8.-- Benedicite. (CAS.) Diapsalma. Monet gentes benedicere Deum, qui licet probet tribulationibus, tamen ducit ad regnum; haec enim videntur obviare promissae resurrectioni. Auditam facite. 939A(AUG.) Palam, ut qui diligit Deum, diligit et proximum. Vocem laudis ejus. Quam dicit Pater de Filio: Hic est Filius meus.

VERS. 9.-- Qui posuit animam. (Ibid.) Enumerat hic quibus causis debeat praedicari.

VERS. -- Quoniam probasti nos. (AUG.) Non dedisti in commotionem. Quoniam probasti, non in praeceps dedisti, probasti adversis, igne charitatis, qui non sinit sentire tormenta, vel, igne tribulationis nos examinasti, etc.

VERS. 12.-- Laqueum. (AUG.) Non qui decipit, sed qui probat. Transivimus. (CAS.; AUG.) Tu haec omnia, et nos, etc., usque ad hoc in tentationibus nobis fit.

VERS. 13.-- Introibo. (CAS.) Ecce quae bona contra 939Bpraecedentia mala, ut roboret. In holocaustis. Id est, ut me offeram conspectui tuo, etc., usque ad sed se quod charius est substraxit.

VERS. 14.-- Distinxerunt. (AUG.) Distinguit, qui se dicit nihil esse, Deum omnia; et, se eo egere, non illum se. Et locutum est os meum. Quem prae omnibus manifestavi praevalere omnibus aliis votis in tribulatione mea, non victus tribulatione.

VERS. 15.-- Holocausta medullata. Meipsum cum medullis intimi amoris. Incenso arietum. (Ibid.) Vel, cum incenso, quod est oratio; et arietibus, quia duces gregis maxime orant pro grege. Cum incenso. (HIER., AUG.) Cum oratione Apostolorum, quia Deo placet quod traditione eorum fit. Vel cum incensione et destructione bestialitatis et repugnantiae. 939CBoves; cervicositatem; cum hircis, petulantiam; haec in me mactando vitia. Offeram tibi boves. (AUG.) Si offeruntur triturantes, non remanent tamen peccatores: sed per poenitentiam sanati offeruntur; et ipsi non per se, sed potius adjuncti bobus, quia fecerunt sibi amicos de mammona iniquitatis.

VERS. 16.-- Venite, audite. Diapsalma. Jam expositis omnibus, item monet non tam rudes, sed devotos, ut exemplo suae liberationis amplius confidant in Domino: benedicens eum de exauditione. Ita ego facio, et o vos gentes, venite.

VERS. 17.-- Ad ipsum ore meo clamavi. (CAS.) Exponit quanta fecit animae suae, subdens: Ad ipsum, etc. Hoc fecit animae meae, ut clamarem ad ipsum, cum gentes ad idola: et quod extra loquor 939Dintus habeo, et non iniquitatem, quia sic puritas orationis, auditur. Clamavi et exaltavi in corde. (AUG.) Id est, ipsum publice praedicavi, et in secreto confessus sum. Quod in ore, hoc et in corde habeo: tamen holocausta medullata offeram. His duobus perfectus est Christianus.

VERS. 18.-- Meo. Suum est, quod non est perversum; proponit merito, ut discant prius laborare quam praemium quaerant.

VERS. 20.-- Orationem meam, etc. Haec duo connexa sunt; si non suspenditur oratio, nec protelatur misericordia.

PSALM LXV.

Unto the end. (AUG.) The Jews from the justice of the law hoped for themselves temporal goods, and the resurrection, etc., as far as that for the faith of the Gentiles he would call them to the same hope of resurrection.

938BVERS. 1.-- Shout with joy to God, all the earth, etc. (CAS.) First he admonishes all to rejoice over the resurrection of Christ, which gives life to all.

VERS. 3.-- Give ye glory. (AUG.) Not as the Jews, who give justice to their own merits, and envy the Gentiles their grace. How terrible. (Ibid.) If thou rejoicest, fear also, lest what has been given to the humble be taken away from the proud: as was done to the Jews. Do not therefore insult over the broken branches, but fear, lest perchance he spare not thee either. Thy works, O Lord. (CAS.) Briefly he calls the mysteries of the incarnation works, that God is man, that he suffered, died, and the like. In the multitude of thy strength. (AUG.) Here he hints at the resurrection, to which, the lying Jews being shut out, the Gentiles are admitted.

(BEDA.) The Lord rose again; many believed in him, etc., as far as they drank through grace. They shall lie. 938CThey are works of the earth, which the enemies belie, against those who lie, let all the earth adore, etc. (AUG.) They shall lie. Enemies are wont to lie, etc., as far as let all the earth adore.

VERS. 5.-- Come ye. (CAS.) Diapsalma. He invites beginners to consider the works of God, that one faith may join those whom one reward awaits: where, setting forth those works, he plainly says that the resurrection pertains to the Gentiles ressurrectionem, the Jews being repressed.

VERS. 6.-- Who turneth. (Ibid.) The works in which he is terrible, and what they are, he subjoins: Who turneth the sea. In the river Jordan according to the letter, mystically in the passing world. In the river. (Ibid.) Although sins are forgiven, yet in the course of mortality they are still there, for immortality is not at once immortalitai.

938DIn the river. (AUG.) The river is the mortality of the world, where some come and others depart: but he who believes in Christ passes over on foot, humble in himself, not on horseback and proud. There we shall rejoice. (Ibid.) Or thus: The works are terrible, etc., as far as and in these Christians rejoice. In him. (Ibid.) When he shall be all in all, or in him who rules, in his own strength.

VERS. 7.-- Let them not be exalted. (Ibid.) On account of the law, as though more were owed to them. For all have sinned, etc. (Rom. III.)

VERS. 8.-- Bless ye. (CAS.) Diapsalma. He admonishes the Gentiles to bless God, who, although he tries them by tribulations, yet leads them to the kingdom; for these things seem to stand in the way of the promised resurrection. Make ye heard. 939A(AUG.) Openly, so that he who loves God loves his neighbour also. The voice of his praise. Which the Father speaks of the Son: This is my Son.

VERS. 9.-- Who hath set my soul. (Ibid.) Here he enumerates for what causes he ought to be preached.

VERS. -- For thou hast proved us. (AUG.) Thou hast not given us over unto commotion. Because thou hast proved us, thou hast not cast us headlong, thou hast proved us by adversities, by the fire of charity, which does not suffer us to feel torments, or, thou hast tried us by the fire of tribulation, etc.

VERS. 12.-- A snare. (AUG.) Not one that deceives, but one that proves. We have passed over. (CAS.; AUG.) Thou all these things, and we, etc., as far as this happens to us in temptations.

VERS. 13.-- I will go in. (CAS.) Behold what good things against 939Bthe evils that went before, that he may strengthen us. In holocausts. That is, that I may offer myself to thy sight, etc., as far as but he withdrew that which is dearer, himself.

VERS. 14.-- They have distinguished. (AUG.) He distinguishes who says that he himself is nothing, and God all things; and that he himself has need of God, not God of him. And my mouth hath spoken. Whom before all men I have declared to prevail above all other vows in my tribulation, not overcome by tribulation.

VERS. 15.-- Marrowy holocausts. Myself, with the marrow of inmost love. With the burnt offering of rams. (Ibid.) Or, with the burnt offering, which is prayer; and with rams, because the leaders of the flock pray most of all for the flock. With the burnt offering. (HIER., AUG.) With the prayer of the Apostles, because that pleases God which is done by their tradition. Or with the burning and destruction of brutishness and of resistance. 939COxen; stiffness of neck; with he-goats, wantonness; these vices being slain in me. I will offer thee oxen. (AUG.) If those who thresh are offered, yet they do not remain sinners: but healed through penance they are offered; and they not by themselves, but rather joined to the oxen, because they have made themselves friends of the mammon of iniquity.

VERS. 16.-- Come ye, hear. Diapsalma. All things now being set forth, he again admonishes not so much the untaught, but the devout, that by the example of his own deliverance they may trust the more in the Lord: blessing him for the hearing of his prayer. So do I, and O ye Gentiles, come ye.

VERS. 17.-- To him I have cried with my mouth. (CAS.) He sets forth how great things he did for his own soul, subjoining: To him, etc. This he did for my soul, that I should cry to him, while the Gentiles cried to idols: and what I speak without 939DI have within, and not iniquity, because thus is the purity of prayer, it is heard. I have cried and exalted in my heart. [Vulg. Ps 65:17 et exaltavi sub lingua mea, "and I extolled under my tongue"] (AUG.) That is, I have preached him publicly, and confessed him in secret. What I have in the mouth, this I have in the heart also: yet I will offer marrowy holocausts. By these two the Christian is made perfect.

VERS. 18.-- Mine. That is a man's own which is not perverse; he sets it forth with reason, that they may learn to labour first before they seek the reward.

VERS. 20.-- My prayer, etc. These two are joined together; if prayer is not suspended, neither is mercy deferred.

PSALMUS LXVI.

In finem. (CAS.) Post canticum resurrectionis, deprecationem 940Asuam Propheta subdit, ut benedicti ad Dei cognitionem ducantur. Prophetat benedictionem omnium per adventum Christi. (AUG.) Quia in praecedenti psalmo monuerat nos benedicere Deum; quod non possumus, nisi ipse prior benedicat nos; ideo hoc precatur benedici, dicens: Deus misereatur nostri et benedicat, etc.

VERS. 2.-- Deus misereatur. (Ibid.) Prior est benedictio Dei, quae est quasi pluvia terram nostrae mentis irrigans: inde nos benedicimus eum, quod quasi fructus est, et in utroque nos crescimus, non ipse. Dicat ergo desiderans pluviam Dominicae benedictionis: Deus misereatur, etc. Deus misereatur nostri et benedicat. (CAS.) Sed qui multi volunt, etc., usque ad et quia cognoscitur in gentibus Christus: 940BConfiteantur, etc. Benedicat nobis. (Ibid.) Benedicit Creator creaturae, multiplicando, numero et merito. Benedicit creatura Creatori, eum corde, voce et opere, laudando, et omne bonum, quod habet, ei ascribendo.

VERS. 4.-- Confiteantur tibi populi, Deus. (Ibid.) Post notitiam hortatur confiteri pro directione et judicio.

VERS. 5.-- Laetentur et exsultent. (AUG.) Quia jam confessi non timent futura judicia, quibus Christus est advocatus, non judex, laetentur.

VERS. 6.-- Confiteantur tibi populi, Deus. (CAS.) Eadem admonitio ad aliud tendens, quia terra dedit fructum, et si idem initium sensus, tamen ad diversa tendit.

940CVERS. 7.-- Terra dedit fructum suum. (HIER.) Mariae Christum, etc., usque ad: Sed non illa sola hoc debet, imo, Benedicat etiam nos. Deus, Deus noster. (Ibid.) Ter trinitas, eum, unitas. Et metuant eum. (CAS.) Metus inter beneficia postulatur, ut credita caute custodiantur: Timor Dei incipit, et consummat; qui timere novit, amare non desinit.

PSALM LXVI.

Unto the end. (CAS.) After the canticle of the resurrection, the Prophet subjoins his own 940Aentreaty, that the blessed may be led to the knowledge of God. He prophesies the blessing of all through the coming of Christ. (AUG.) Because in the preceding psalm he had admonished us to bless God, which we cannot do unless he first bless us; therefore he prays for this, to be blessed, saying: May God have mercy on us and bless us, etc.

VERS. 2.-- May God have mercy. (Ibid.) The blessing of God is first, which is as it were a rain watering the earth of our mind: thence we bless him, which is as it were the fruit; and in both it is we that grow, not he. Let him therefore who desires the rain of the Lord's blessing say: May God have mercy on us, etc. May God have mercy on us and bless us. (CAS.) But many who wish, etc., as far as and because Christ is known among the nations: 940BLet them confess, etc. May he bless us. (Ibid.) The Creator blesses the creature, by multiplying it, in number and in merit. The creature blesses the Creator, by praising him with heart, voice and work, and by ascribing to him every good thing that it has.

VERS. 4.-- Let the peoples confess to thee, O God. (Ibid.) After knowledge he exhorts them to confess, for direction and for judgment.

VERS. 5.-- Let them be glad and rejoice. (AUG.) Because, having now confessed, they do not fear the judgments to come, to whom Christ is an advocate, not a judge, let them be glad.

VERS. 6.-- Let the peoples confess to thee, O God. (CAS.) The same admonition, tending to another thing, because the earth has given her fruit, and although the beginning of the sense is the same, yet it tends to different things.

940CVERS. 7.-- The earth hath given her fruit. (HIER.) To Mary, Christ, etc., as far as: But not she alone owes this, nay rather, let him bless also us. God, our God. (Ibid.) Three times, the Trinity, him, the unity. And let them fear him. (CAS.) Fear is asked for in the midst of benefits, that what is entrusted may be warily kept: the fear of God begins and completes; he who has learned to fear does not cease to love.

PSALMUS LXVII.

VERS. 1.-- In finem. (CAS.) Psalmus David prophetae ne exsultatione Christi et Ecclesiae hic et in futuro, ut omnes Deo cantent. Surgente Christo, quasi elevata arca, etc., usque ad verbis his similibus Moyses usus fuisse dicitur.

VERS. 2.-- Exsurgat Deus et dissipentur. (Ibid.) 940DConfidenter optat quod scit futurum. Et fugiant qui oderunt. (HIER.) Vel de poenitentibus legi potest, etc., usque ad ut lacrymis poenitentiae admoto igne Spiritus sancti duritia eorum solvatur. Qui oderunt. (AUG.) Pertinaces a praesentia tollantur ejus, qui ubique praesens; grave maledictum, ut velint et conentur, quod nullatenus fieri potest.

VERS. 3.-- Sicut deficit fumus. (CAS.) Fumus ex flamma ascensu vanescit; ita peccatores ex flamma nequitiae fumiferas actiones producunt, et ipsa elatione deficiunt. Sicut fluit. (AUG.) De poenitentibus dici potest; vel in judicio a facie Dei tollentur mali: qui erit ignis ad poenam impiorum, et lumen justorum.

941AVERS. 4.-- Epulentur. (CASS., AUG.) In deliciis, quae sunt in conspectu Dei. Et delectentur, hoc potest eos delectare, qui laeti sunt quia non est finienda eorum laetitia.

VERS. 5.-- Cantate Deo. (AUG.) Convertit se ad eos, quibus tantam spem dedit et hortatur. Qui ascendit. Non eum excipiet nova vita, nisi vetus occiderit; vel, resurgendo casum corporis vicit. Super occasum. (CAS.) Occasus mortis cadit illi, super quem sol justitiae oritur. Et ne dubites quis iste sit, quia Dominus nomen illi essentiale, quem Judaei ut communem hominem occiderunt. In conspectu. Consideratio praemii futuri aerumnas mitigat.

VERS. 6.-- Orphanorum. (AUG.) Quibus mortuus est pater, mundus et diabolus, et mater concupiscentia. 941BViduae, quibus error maritus moritur; in quibus habitat Deus, quos colligit, quos trahit, quia de viduis et orphanis facit sibi templum, in quo est.

VERS. 7.-- Deus qui inhabitare. (HIER.) In Hebraeo habetur: Dominus autem inhabitare facit monachos in domo, in quibus non cohabitat peccatum. Unius moris. (AUG.) Unanimes, unum sentientes, etc., usque ad non meritis, unde subdit: Qui educit vinctos. Educit vinctos. (CAS.) De inferno ligato diabolo. Qui exasperant. Blasphemos in Deum. Vel persequendo in sepulcris in carnalibus fetidis sepulti, ut nec velint nec possint ambulare. Exasperant. (AUG.) Resistendo justitiae, cum omnino sint mortui in operibus mortuis; vincti vero volunt ambulare, nec possunt; hi solvuntur per gratiam, illi resuscitantur.

941CVERS. 8.-- Deus, cum egredereris. (CAS.) Diapsalmus de verbo Evangelii per egressum Christi. Deus, cum egredereris. Vere educis, quia praefiguratus est egressus ejus coram Israel, dum in columna nubis et ignis apparuit in deserto, et manna satiavit. (AUG.) Egressus dum apparuit hominibus per humanitatem, vel dum educit vinctos, id est, suscitat. Transiit in desertum, cum ad gentes venit. (BASIL.) Egredereris. Quasi dicat: cum transiturus esses solitudinem illam, quae nondum lucis splendorem acceperat, terram quidem concussisti ac commovistis, coelitus vero gratiae tuae guttas distillasti.

VERS. 9.-- Terra mota est. Quia tunc terreni videndo tanta mirabilia moti sunt. Coeli distillaverunt 941Da facie Dei: Manna, dum in modum stillicidii, manna descendit a facie Dei, cujus praesentia per columnam noscebatur. (AUG.) Mons Sina a facie Dei fumavit, (secundum aliam litteram) quando Moyses ibi legem accepit.

VERS. 10.-- Pluviam. Hoc est quod coeli distillaverunt manna, voluntariam quae satisfaceret voluntati illius gentis avide comedendi. Segregabis Deus haereditati tuae. Quia non aliis gentibus dedit, quod tunc Judaeis. Infirmata, etc. Ad tempus, dum Christo non credidit. (CAS.) Perfecit. Deus haereditatem suam, dum gentes in supplementum admisit. Subdit unde perfecit.

VERS. 11.-- Animalia. Id est, gentes tuae, dum 942Acredunt, habitant in haereditate, id est, in Ecclesia. Quae sunt animalia exponit. Parasti: praedestinatos dicit, quia ab origine mundi praeparati sunt. (AUG.) Vel, mons a facie Dei Israel, subaudi distillavit, etc., usque ad in quo superabundavit gratia. (CAS.) Haec mystice, sed secundum figuram, etc., usque ad mittit ergo ad mysterium. (AUG.) Quidam libri non habent mons, sed a facie Dei Sina Israel; id est, qui legem dedit populo Israel: quia qui legem dedit per Moysem, qua terreret, dedit et benedictionem per Apostolos, qua liberet. In dulcedine (CAS.) Dulcedo est, qua bonum fit, non timore poenae, sed delectatione justitiae.

VERS. 12.-- Dominus dabit verbum. Virtutes multas evangelizantibus verbum.

942BVERS. 13.-- Rex virtutum. (HIER.) Apostolorum, vel dilecti. (CAS.) Pater est rex angelorum, quibus imperat et ipse dilectus. (AUG.) Rex virtutum dilecti. Filii, id est, pater vel more veteris Scripturae Christus rex virtutum; Christi, id est, suarum, ut fecit Moyses, sicut praecepit Dominus Moysi. Dilecti, dilecti. (CAS.) Repetitio dilecti ad commendationem; sed non est haec repetitio in omnibus libris, sed sive sit, sive non, hic est sensus, dilecti non solum ad alia, sed etiam ad dividenda spolia, quae dividendo, speciosam fecit Ecclesiam.

VERS. 14.-- Si dormiatis. (AUG.) Dormire inter medios cleros est in auctoritate duorum Testamentorum requiescere et pacifice acquiescere. Pennae columbae deargentatae, praedicatores quorum praedicatione 942Cin coelum fertur gloria Ecclesiae. Columbae (AUG., CAS.) Columba Ecclesia, etc., usque ad praedicatione in coelum fertur. Et posteriora. (AUG.) Ubi radices alarum etc., usque ad vigor sapientiae est charitas. Inter medios cleros. (AUG.) Latinae linguae esset inter cleros, etc., usque ad vobis erunt pennae ambiguum est.

VERS. 15.--(CAS.) Diapsalmus, dum discernit, de donationibus Christi ascendentis, qui solus potest, et non alius. (AUG.) Dum gratia Spiritus sancti reges discernuntur, etc., usque ad et in eum credentes proteguntur.

VERS. 17.-- Mons Dei mons pinguis. (AUG., CAS.) Commendationem montis subdit, etc., usque ad Hic enim est mons qui in Ezechiele vulnerat principem 942DTyri. Beneplacitum est Deo, etc. (AUG.) Etenim Dominus habitabit eum in finem, id est usque ad terminum majestatis suae, qui est finis sine fine, et plenitudo omnium. Etenim Dominus habitavit. Nullus ut iste, quia iste mons, scilicet Dominus, habitabit illos montes usquequo ducat in finem, id est, in se Deum contemplandum. Alii autem montes sunt currus per quos vehitur Deus in universum mundum. Currus, quia unanimes copulati charitate, quos ad ministerium voluntatis suae moderatur Deus, decem millibus, innumeris populis; multitudo sanctorum.

In finem. Quia personaliter unitus est ei, in quo habitavit omnis plenitudo divinitatis corporaliter.

943AVERS. 18.-- Millia laetantium. (AUG., CAS.) Magnam multitudinem significat sanctorum, etc., usque ad et ideo laetantur. Sina in sancto (CAS.) Est mons in quo data est lex. Dicitur mandatum in quo requiescit Dominus, quia in sanctis mandatis ejus praesentia solet contueri. In Sina. (HIERON.) Vel in Sina sancto, id est, qui in Sina monte olim dedit legem, ipse idem est in sancto, id est, in Christo, qui est Sanctus sanctorum.

VERS. 19.-- Ascendisti. (AUG.) Qui propter nos erudiendos descendit. In altum. Super omnes coelos. Cepisti captivitatem. (CAS.) Prius apud inferos captos: haec sunt spolia, similitudo triumphi; accepisti dona in hominibus a patre, id est, homines. Vel dedisti, secundum quod Deus, dona hominibus, 943Bquod etiam fit in triumphis.

Cepisti captivitatem. (AUG.) Unde captivi dicuntur, quia capti retibus Petri, et sub leve jugum missi: unde in hoc curru sunt millia laetantium; non plorantium.

Accepisti. Paulus apostolica auctoritate, etc., usque ad: Quod uni ex minimis fecistis, mihi fecistis.

VERS. 20.-- Quotidie. (Ibid.) Quia quotidie captivat captivos usque in finem saeculi. Et quia currum illum ducit in finem, addit prosperum iter. Iter. Cursum vitae, quae vere prosperum, cum dux sit salutaris.

VERS. 21.-- Deus noster. (CAS.) Diapsalma. Exponit operationes, quae ex supradictis eveniunt: conquassatio inimicorum, conversiones peccantium; 943Cmartyria ab utroque sexu. Salvos faciendi. (AUG.) Commendat gratiam, quia nullus salvus nisi per eum; sed ne dicas, Cur ergo morituri? patienter fer, et mortem non indigneris quia et Domini, qui sine peccato fuit, exitus non alius, quam mortis, tamen voluntate, ne homo timeret mortem. Exitus mortis. (CAS.) Id est, resurrectio, ne queraris de morte, quia Christus inde exivit, et inde exire dedit. Ne mala pertinacium credas impunita, subdit, verumtamen capita, superbiam, vel auctores Judaicae sectionis, vel seditionis, vel haeresis.

VERS. 22.-- Verticem capilli. (Ibid.) Versutias inanium quaestionum, quae tales inimicitias calumniarum quaerunt, ut capillos videantur perscrutari.

VERS. 23.-- Ex Basan. (AUG.) Id est, confusione, 943Detc., usque ad ad eos, qui erant desperatissimi.

VERS. 24.-- Pes tuus. (Ibid.) Id est, ut qui prius erant inimici, fiant pes tuus, praedicando usque ad sanguinem, scilicet, usque ad mortem: et canes, pro Deo latrantes, qui edunt de micis, etc. Pes tuus. Illi soli ad officium regiminis assumendi sunt, qui quod percipiunt, aliis praedicant, qui manibus bonorum operum exsequuntur, quod ore praedicant, vel docent; unde in Levitico: Os turturis retorquetur ad ascellas.

In sanguine. (BASIL.) Quoniam ostendit Deum, etc., usque ad: et cum eos vincerem, aspersa sunt vestimenta mea. Canum. (AUG.) In magno sacramento eos ducere jussus est Gedeon, qui ut canes 944Aaquam lamberent, trecentos tantum et non plures, in signo crucis propter thau, quae trecentos significat. Ab ipso. Quasi si quaeras unde tantum bonum, ut canes ejus sint erant inimici? ait: Ab ipso, id est, ejus gratia, non a seipsis.

VERS. 25.-- Viderunt in gressus tuos, Deus. (Ibid.) Vel visi sunt gressus tui, Deus, quibus venisti in mundum. Haec gratia latebat in Veteri Testamento: modo patet, cum missus Filius annuntiatur in gentibus. Qui. Deus. Est in sancto, corpore, licet perfidi non videant, secundum quod passus. In hoc etiam, patiendo vel credendo, praevenerunt eos principes, vel praevenerunt ad te laudem.

VERS. 26.-- Principes. (BASIL., EUTHYM.) Apostolos Principes appellat, etc., usque ad et praedicatione 944Billos consecuti sunt. In medio. Ministri praepositi novarum ecclesiarum Deum laudantium, carne domita et corio siccato ab humore peccati, et extenso a ruga duplicitatis.

VERS. 27.-- In ecclesiis benedicite. (CAS.) Diapsalma. Precatur et affirmat, ut haec inceptio dilatetur et confirmetur, pro qua et haeretici destruantur. (AUG.) In ecclesiis. Haec sunt juvenculae tympanistriae, ne quis carnaliter choros luxuriae cogitet. Ecclesiae quippe sunt adolescentulae nova gratia decoratae. In ecclesiis, non alibi, non in aliis conventiculis. De fontibus Israel. (CAS.) Ut ad eorum imitationem praedicetis, quae decet: quia sunt principes fidei, spei et charitatis, et per hoc Benjamin, id est, filius dextrae.

944CVERS. 28.-- Ibi Benjamin, etc. Principes, etc. (Ibid.) Per nomina tribuum, Christum et Apostolos indicat. Ibi, scilicet in templo Jerusalem vel in Ecclesia. Interpretatio etiam nominum Ecclesiae convenit. (CAS.) Forsan ex his tribubus fuerunt Apo-toli, etc., usque ad: confessio in fide, fortitudo in spe, latitudo in charitate. In mentis excelsu, seu, ut proprie est Graeca dictio, etc., usque ad ut fidelis ac prudens distributor, divisit.

VERS. 29.-- Manda Deus virtuti tuae. (Ibid.) O Deus, notifica Filium, quasi quod enuntio futurum, perfice. Vel, virtuti tuae, id est, fortibus tuis injunge, ut te annuntient. Vel, o Pater, manda tuum opus virtuti tuae, Filio, vel Spiritui sancto. (AUG.) Commendat enim Deus charitatem suam in nobis, quoniam, 944Dcum peccatores essemus, Christus pro nobis mortuus est: quod bene et confidenter orat. Confirma hoc, Deus, quod operatus es. Incipiendo.

VERS. 30.-- A templo tuo in Jerusalem. Quae est libera, mater nostra, quae est templum, a quo omne datum optimum; ab illo ergo templo. Reges terrae. Vel speciales tibi offerent munera, id est, sacrificia laudis. Sed quia huic laudi obstrepunt haeretici.

VERS. 31.-- Increpa feras arundinis. (AUG.) Id est, eos qui moventur omni vento doctrinae. Ut excludant eos qui probati sunt. Hoc est quod Apostolus ait: Qui probati sunt, manifesti fiant (I Cor. XI); vel a vaccis excludant probati. Nam stabiles, fortes, et graves non habent seducere: In populo gravi laudabo 945Ate. Dissipa. Increpa feras, et etiam dissipa dissentientes. Gentes quae bella volunt. Haereticos et alios eis consentientes, quos gentes vocat, propter genera diversarum sectarum, ne ibi series successionum confirmet errorem.

VERS. 32.-- Ex Aegppto, Aethiopia. (AUG.) Aegypti vel Aethiopiae nomine fide omnium gentium signat, a parte totum. Non ergo ex solis Judaeis, sed de gentibus praecones futuros prophetat. (HIER.) Aethiopia Gentilitas nigra peccatis, festinat manus dare Deo. Similitudo a victis, qui armis depositis eas dant victoribus, ne intereant. Praeveniet manus ejus. (Ibid.) Id est, vindictam ejus, per confessionem, ne manentes in peccatis puniantur.

VERS. 33.-- Deo regna. Ut Deo sit in principio 945Bsequentis versus. Vel magis in fine praecedentis versus est, Deo. Commendaturque fides (quasi, non praecedentibus operibus justificatur homo) quae per dilectionem incipit operari. Credet ergo Aethiopia Deo, et sic praeveniet opera ejus, id est, Aethiopiae, quod in Graeco non est ambiguum, id est, credendo in Deum, praeveniet opera sua. Vel ejus Aegypti Deo, id est, in Deum. Regna terrae, cantate Deo. (AUG.) Decursis omnibus, quae jam impleta cernimus, hortatur ad laudem Christi, et futurum ejus adventum praenuntiat.

Psallite. (CASS.) Diapsalma. Psallite: veniet qui ascendit, ubi sanctos consummabit.

VERS. 34.-- Ascendit. (Ibid.) secundum quod homo. Nam secundum quod Deus, Patri aequalis, 945Csuper coelum coeli, excelsiores creaturas, ut nihil supra se haberet. (HIER., CAS.) Oriens. Verbum a Patre genitum. Et ascendit ab oriente Virtute Verbi.

Ad orientem. Locum expressit, ubi surrexit et unde ascendit.

(AUG.) Ad orientem, nostrae illuminationis. Vel quia Jerusalem est in Oriente. Voci suae. (Ibid.) Qui fuit humilis in passione: dabit vocem virtutis in communi resurrectione. Vocem virtutis. (CAS.) Efficaciam resuscitandi omnes mortuos.

VERS. 35.-- Magnificentia ejus et virtus. (AUG.) Quoniam jam tunc non erit commistio malorum, inde evidens erit magnificentia ejus super verum Israel. In nubibus. Quia non solus veniet ad judicium, sed 945Dcum senioribus populi, qui sunt nubes: quas ne aliter acciperes, addit: Mirabilis in sanctis.

(EUTHYM.) Per nubes. Hic ipsos Aposlos intelligit, veluti supra exsistentes, atque eminentes a terrenis negotiis, ac veluti spirituali aqua plenos, quam ex sancti Spiritus profundis hauserunt, ut animarum arva ac campos, hoc est, ut ipsos credentes, irrigarent.

VERS. 36.-- Ipse dabit virtutem et fortitudinem plebi suae benedictus Deus. (CAS). Magna promisit, ne quis pro humana infirmitate desperet se ad tanta praemia pervenire.

PSALM LXVII.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end. (CAS.) A psalm of David the prophet, concerning the exultation ne of Christ and of the Church here and in time to come, that all may sing to God. When Christ was rising, as though the ark were lifted up, etc., as far as Moses is said to have used words like these.

VERS. 2.-- Let God arise, and let them be scattered. (Ibid.) 940DHe confidently wishes for what he knows will be. And let them that hate him flee. (HIER.) Or it can be read of the penitent, etc., as far as that, when the fire of the Holy Spirit is applied by the tears of penitence, their hardness may be dissolved. That hate him. (AUG.) Let the obstinate be taken away from the presence of him who is everywhere present; a grave curse, that they should will and strive after what can in no wise come to pass.

VERS. 3.-- As smoke faileth. (CAS.) Smoke from a flame vanishes in its rising; so sinners bring forth smoky deeds out of the flame of wickedness, and by that very lifting up they fail. As it melteth. (AUG.) It can be said of the penitent; or, in the judgment the wicked will be taken away from the face of God: who will be a fire for the punishment of the ungodly, and a light for the just.

941AVERS. 4.-- Let them feast. (CASS., AUG.) In the delights which are in the sight of God. And let them be delighted, this can delight them, that they are glad qui because their gladness is not to be ended.

VERS. 5.-- Sing ye to God. (AUG.) He turns himself to those to whom he has given so great a hope, and exhorts them. Who ascendeth. The new life will not receive him unless the old has died; or, by rising again he overcame the fall of the body. Upon the going down. (CAS.) The going down of death befalls him upon whom the sun of justice rises. And lest thou doubt who this may be, because the Lord is his name, a name essential to him, whom the Jews slew as a common man. In the sight. The consideration of the reward to come mitigates hardships.

VERS. 6.-- Of orphans. (AUG.) Whose father, the world and the devil, is dead, and their mother, concupiscence. 941BWidows, for whom their husband, error, dies; in whom God dwells, whom he gathers, whom he draws, because out of widows and orphans he makes himself a temple, in which he is.

VERS. 7.-- God who maketh to dwell. (HIER.) In the Hebrew it stands: But the Lord maketh monks to dwell in a house, in whom sin does not dwell together. Of one manner. (AUG.) Of one mind, thinking one thing, etc., as far as not by merits, whence he adds: Who bringeth out them that were bound. He bringeth out them that were bound. (CAS.) Out of hell, the devil being bound. Who provoke. Blasphemers against God. Or, by persecuting, buried in tombs, in stinking carnal things, so that they neither will nor can walk. They provoke. (AUG.) By resisting justice, since they are altogether dead in dead works; but the bound do will to walk, and cannot; these are loosed by grace, those are raised up.

941CVERS. 8.-- O God, when thou didst go forth. (CAS.) A Diapsalmus concerning the word of the Gospel, by the going forth of Christ. O God, when thou didst go forth. Truly thou bringest out, because his going forth was prefigured before Israel, when he appeared in the pillar of cloud and of fire in the desert, and filled them with manna. (AUG.) A going forth, when he appeared to men through his humanity, or when he bringeth out them that were bound, that is, raises them up. He passed into the desert, [Vulg. Ps 67:8 cum pertransires in deserto, "when thou didst pass over in the desert"] when he came to the Gentiles. (BASIL.) Thou didst go forth. As if he should say: when thou wast about to pass over that solitude which had not yet received the splendour of light, the earth indeed thou didst shake and stir [commovistis; read commovisti, 2nd sg.], but from heaven thou didst distil the drops of thy grace.

VERS. 9.-- The earth was moved. Because then earthly men were moved at seeing such great wonders. The heavens dropped down 941Dat the face of God: manna, when in the manner of a dripping manna came down from the face of God, whose presence was known by the pillar. (AUG.) Mount Sinai smoked at the face of God (according to another reading) when Moses received the law there.

VERS. 10.-- A rain. This is what the heavens dropped down, manna, a voluntary rain which would satisfy the will of that nation, greedy to eat. Thou shalt set apart, O God, for thine inheritance. Because he did not give to other nations what he then gave to the Jews. It was weakened, etc. For a time, while it did not believe in Christ. (CAS.) He hath made it perfect. [Vulg. Ps 67:10 tu vero perfecisti eam, "but thou hast made it perfect"] God made his inheritance perfect, when he admitted the Gentiles to fill it up. He adds whereby he made it perfect.

VERS. 11.-- Living creatures. That is, thy nations, when they 942Abelieve, dwell in the inheritance, that is, in the Church. He sets forth what the living creatures are. Thou hast prepared: he means the predestined, because from the origin of the world they were made ready. (AUG.) Or, mount at the face of the God of Israel, supply "dropped down", etc., as far as in whom grace superabounded. (CAS.) These things mystically, but according to the figure, etc., as far as he sends therefore to the mystery. (AUG.) Certain books do not have mount, but at the face of the God of Sinai, of Israel; that is, he who gave the law to the people of Israel: because he who gave the law through Moses, whereby he might terrify, gave also the blessing through the Apostles, whereby he might set free. In sweetness (CAS.) Sweetness is that whereby good is done, not from fear of punishment, but from delight in justice.

VERS. 12.-- The Lord shall give the word. Many powers to them that preach the word.

942BVERS. 13.-- The king of hosts. (HIER.) Of the Apostles, or of the beloved. (CAS.) The Father is the king of the angels, over whom the Beloved himself also commands. (AUG.) The king of hosts of the beloved. Of the Son, that is, the Father; or, after the manner of the old Scripture, Christ is the king of hosts; of Christ, that is, of his own, as Moses did, "as the Lord commanded Moses." Of the beloved, of the beloved. (CAS.) The repetition of of the beloved is for commendation; but this repetition is not in all the books, yet whether it be there or not, this is the sense: of the beloved not only for other things, but also for dividing the spoils, by dividing which he made the Church beautiful.

VERS. 14.-- If you sleep. (AUG.) To sleep among the midst of the lots is to rest in the authority of the two Testaments and peaceably to acquiesce. The wings of a dove covered with silver, the preachers, by whose preaching 942Cthe glory of the Church is borne up to heaven. Of a dove (AUG., CAS.) The dove is the Church, etc., as far as by preaching it is borne up to heaven. And the hinder parts. (AUG.) Where the roots of the wings, etc., as far as the vigour of wisdom is charity. Among the midst of the lots. (AUG.) It would be of the Latin tongue "among the lots", etc., as far as "there shall be wings for you" is ambiguous.

VERS. 15.--(CAS.) A Diapsalmus, while he distinguisheth, concerning the gifts of the ascending Christ, who alone can do it, and no other. (AUG.) While by the grace of the Holy Spirit kings are distinguished, etc., as far as and those who believe in him are protected.

VERS. 17.-- The mountain of God, a fat mountain. (AUG., CAS.) He adds a commendation of the mountain, etc., as far as For this is the mountain which in Ezechiel wounds the prince 942Dof Tyre. It is well pleasing to God, etc. (AUG.) For the Lord shall inhabit it unto the end, [Vulg. Ps 67:17 etenim Dominus habitabit in finem, without eum; the gloss construes the verb transitively] that is, even to the term of his majesty, which is an end without end, and the fullness of all things. For the Lord hath dwelt. None is such as he, because this mountain, namely the Lord, will inhabit those mountains until he lead them unto the end, that is, into himself, God to be contemplated. But the other mountains are the chariots by which God is carried into the whole world. Chariots, because they are of one mind, coupled together by charity, whom God guides to the ministry of his will, by ten thousands, by countless peoples; a multitude of saints.

Unto the end. Because he is personally united to him in whom dwelt all the fullness of the Godhead bodily.

943AVERS. 18.-- Thousands of them that rejoice. (AUG., CAS.) It signifies a great multitude of saints, etc., as far as and therefore they rejoice. Sinai in the holy place (CAS.) It is the mountain on which the law was given. It is called a commandment in which the Lord rests, because in his holy commandments his presence is wont to be beheld. In Sinai. (HIERON.) Or, in Sinai the holy, that is, he who once gave the law on mount Sinai is himself the same in the holy one, that is, in Christ, who is the Holy of holies.

VERS. 19.-- Thou hast ascended. (AUG.) He who came down that we might be instructed. On high. Above all the heavens. Thou hast led captivity captive. (CAS.) Those formerly held captive among the dead: these are the spoils, the likeness of a triumph; thou hast received gifts in men from the Father, that is, men. Or thou hast given, according as thou art God, gifts to men, 943Bwhich also is done in triumphs.

Thou hast led captivity captive. (AUG.) Whence they are called captives, because they were caught in Peter's nets and put under a light yoke: whence in this chariot there are thousands of them that rejoice, not of them that weep.

Thou hast received. Paul by apostolic authority, etc., as far as: What you have done to one of the least, you have done to me.

VERS. 20.-- Daily. (Ibid.) Because daily he takes captives captive until the end of the world. And because he leads that chariot unto the end, he adds a prosperous journey. Journey. The course of life, which is truly prosperous, since the leader is one who brings salvation.

VERS. 21.-- Our God. (CAS.) Diapsalma. He sets forth the workings which come about from the things said above: the shattering of enemies, the conversions of sinners; 943Cmartyrdoms from either sex. Of saving. (AUG.) He commends grace, because none is saved but through him; but lest thou say, Why then are we to die? bear it patiently, and be not indignant at death, because even of the Lord, who was without sin, the issue was none other than of death, yet by his own will, lest man should fear death. The issue from death. (CAS.) That is, the resurrection; do not complain of death, because Christ went out thence, and granted a going out thence. Lest thou believe the evils of the obstinate unpunished, he adds, "but yet the heads": pride, or the authors of the Jewish division, or of sedition, or of heresy.

VERS. 22.-- The crown of the hair. (Ibid.) The subtleties of empty questions, which seek such enmities of calumnies that they seem to scrutinize hairs.

VERS. 23.-- From Basan. (AUG.) That is, from confusion, 943Detc., as far as to those who were most desperate.

VERS. 24.-- Thy foot. (Ibid.) That is, that they who before were enemies may become thy foot, preaching even unto blood, that is, even unto death: and dogs, barking for God, which eat of the crumbs, etc. Thy foot. Those alone are to be taken up to the office of rule who preach to others what they perceive, who carry out with the hands of good works what they preach or teach with the mouth; whence in Leviticus: The mouth of the turtledove is twisted back to its armpits. [Vulg. Lev. 5:8 retorquebit caput ejus ad pennulas, "shall turn back its head to the little wings"]

In blood. (BASIL.) Since he shows God, etc., as far as: and when I overcame them, my garments were sprinkled. Of the dogs. (AUG.) In a great sacrament Gedeon was commanded to lead those who lapped water like dogs, 944Athree hundred only and no more, in the sign of the cross, because of thau, which signifies three hundred. From him. As if thou shouldst ask whence so great a good, that they should be dogs of him they were enemies? [sint erant; read sint cujus erant, "should be of him whose they were"] he says: From him, that is, by his grace, not from themselves.

VERS. 25.-- They have seen thy goings, O God. (Ibid.) in gressus Or, thy steps have been seen, O God, by which thou camest into the world. This grace lay hidden in the Old Testament: now it is manifest, when the Son, being sent, is announced among the Gentiles. Who. God. Is in the holy place, in the body, though the faithless see it not, according to that in which he suffered. In this also, by suffering or by believing, the princes went before them, or they went before unto praise of thee.

VERS. 26.-- Princes. (BASIL., EUTHYM.) He calls the Apostles Princes, etc., as far as and by preaching 944Bthey followed after them. In the midst. The ministers set over the new churches of them that praise God, with the flesh tamed and the hide dried from the moisture of sin, and stretched out from the wrinkle of duplicity.

VERS. 27.-- In the churches bless ye. (CAS.) Diapsalma. He prays and affirms that this beginning may be enlarged and confirmed, and for its sake that the heretics also may be destroyed. (AUG.) In the churches. These are the young maidens playing on timbrels, lest anyone should think carnally of the dances of luxury. For the churches are young girls adorned with new grace. In the churches, not elsewhere, not in other conventicles. From the fountains of Israel. (CAS.) That you may preach unto their imitation, as is fitting: because they are the princes of faith, of hope and of charity, and through this Benjamin, that is, the son of the right hand.

944CVERS. 28.-- There Benjamin, etc. Princes, etc. (Ibid.) By the names of the tribes he points to Christ and the Apostles. There, namely in the temple of Jerusalem, or in the Church. The interpretation of the names also suits the Church. (CAS.) Perhaps the Apostles were of these tribes Apo-toli, etc., as far as: confession in faith, fortitude in hope, breadth in charity. In the height of mind, [Vulg. Ps 67:28 in mentis excessu, "in ecstasy of mind"] or, as the Greek word properly stands, etc., as far as as a faithful and prudent steward, he divided.

VERS. 29.-- Give command, O God, to thy strength. (Ibid.) O God, make the Son known; as it were: what I announce as to come, do thou perfect. Or, to thy strength, that is, enjoin it upon thy strong ones, that they may announce thee. Or, O Father, commit thy work to thy strength, to the Son, or to the Holy Spirit. (AUG.) For God commendeth his charity toward us, since, 944Dwhen we were sinners, Christ died for us: which he prays well and confidently. Confirm this, O God, which thou hast wrought. By making the beginning.

VERS. 30.-- From thy temple in Jerusalem. Which is free, our mother, which is the temple, from which is every best gift; from that temple, therefore. The kings of the earth. Or, particular ones shall offer thee gifts, that is, sacrifices of praise. But because the heretics clamour against this praise.

VERS. 31.-- Rebuke the wild beasts of the reeds. (AUG.) That is, those who are moved by every wind of doctrine. That they may shut out them that are approved. This is what the Apostle says: That they who are approved may be made manifest (I Cor. XI); or, let the approved shut them out from among the cows. For the stable, the strong, and the grave have not wherewith to seduce: In the mighty people I will praise 945Athee. Scatter thou. Rebuke the wild beasts, and also scatter those that dissent. The nations that will wars. Heretics and others consenting to them, whom he calls nations because of the kinds of the diverse sects, lest a series of successions there confirm the error.

VERS. 32.-- Out of Egypt, Ethiopia. Aegppto (AUG.) By the name of Egypt or of Ethiopia he signifies the faith of all nations, the whole from a part. He prophesies therefore that the heralds to come are not from the Jews alone, but from the Gentiles. (HIER.) Ethiopia, the Gentile world black with sins, hastens to give her hands to God. A likeness taken from the conquered, who, their arms laid down, give them to the victors, lest they perish. His hand shall prevent. (Ibid.) That is, his vengeance, through confession, lest, remaining in their sins, they be punished.

VERS. 33.-- To God, kingdoms. That to God may stand at the beginning 945Bof the following verse. Or rather it stands at the end of the preceding verse, to God. And faith is commended (as if to say, a man is not justified by preceding works) which begins to work through love. Ethiopia therefore will believe God, and so shall prevent his works, that is, Ethiopia's, which in the Greek is not ambiguous — that is, by believing in God she shall prevent her own works. Or his, Egypt's, to God, that is, unto God. Ye kingdoms of the earth, sing to God. (AUG.) Having run through all the things which we now behold fulfilled, he exhorts to the praise of Christ, and foretells his coming that is to be.

Sing ye psalms. (CASS.) Diapsalma. Sing ye psalms: he will come who ascended, where he will make the saints perfect.

VERS. 34.-- He ascendeth. (Ibid.) according as he is man. For according as he is God, equal to the Father, 945Cabove the heaven of heaven, above the loftier creatures, so that he had nothing above himself. (HIER., CAS.) The East. The Word begotten of the Father. And he ascended from the east [Vulg. Ps 67:34 ad orientem, "to the east"; the gloss takes up that reading next] by the power of the Word.

To the east. He has expressed the place where he rose again and whence he ascended.

(AUG.) To the east, of our illumination. Or because Jerusalem is in the East. To his voice. (Ibid.) He who was lowly in the passion will give the voice of power in the common resurrection. The voice of power. (CAS.) The efficacy of raising up all the dead.

VERS. 35.-- His magnificence and power. (AUG.) Because then there will no longer be a mingling of the wicked, thence his magnificence over the true Israel will be evident. In the clouds. Because he will not come alone to the judgment, but 945Dwith the elders of the people, who are the clouds: and lest thou take them otherwise, he adds: Wonderful in his saints.

(EUTHYM.) By clouds. Here he understands the Apostles themselves Aposlos, as existing above, and standing high away from earthly affairs, and as it were full of spiritual water, which they drew from the depths of the Holy Spirit, that they might water the fields and plains of souls, that is, the believers themselves.

VERS. 36.-- He himself will give power and strength to his people; blessed be God. (CAS). He has promised great things, lest anyone, because of human infirmity, should despair of coming to such great rewards.

PSALMUS LXVIII.

VERS. 1.-- In finem. (AUG.) Commutatus est ex 946Aforma Dei in deterius Adam, etc., usque ad pati secundum Graecos. (CAS.) Quartus psalmus qui latius de passione, et resurrectione. Agitur de causa commutationibus, id est, passione Christi. Hic loquitur Christus caput et corpus. Salvum me fac. Primo, precatur salvus fieri, quia multa patitur, quantum ad se gratis, sed quod alius rapuit, ipse solvit. Haec est vox grani sinapis contempti, dum in horto obruitur, quod crescit in magnum olus: hoc fuscum et aspernabile prorsus. Sic et Christus, de quo: Vidimus eum non habentem speciem neque decorem, sed tamen occupavit faciem terrae, factus mons magnus.

Aquae usque ad animam meam. (AUG.) Id est, turbae, etc., usque ad ultra quam non habent qui quid eis faciant.

946BVERS. 3.-- In limo. (AUG.) Homo factus est delimo terrae, etc., usque ad id est, virtus carnis evadendi passionem. Substantia. Dicuntur divitiae, etc., usque ad id est, non inveni in eis quod fecit. Veni. Quia sponte. In altitudinem. Profundum insani populi.

VERS. 4.-- Laboravi. (AUG.) Diu clamavit: Vae vobis! Scribae et Pharisaei, ut raucus quantum ad illos, quia non est ab eis intellectus. Clamans, etc. (CAS.) Laborat, cujus votum non impletur. Oculi mei. Ut oculi duorum eum in via non agnoscentium, quibus factum est extra quod erat intra, id est, caecitas quae in corde facta est et in oculis. Dixerunt enim: Sperabamus quod redempturus esset Israel (Luc. XXIV.) [AUG]. Sed spem eis reddidit, etc., usque 946Cad quia perditi fuissent. Dum spero. (CAS.) Causa subditur, praestolor misericordiam, non exoro potentiam.

VERS. 5.-- Multiplicati. (AUG.) Quod prius typice, nunc in re aperte dicit. Super capillos. Pro infinito, vel plures sunt his qui sunt ornatui. Rapui. Rapere voluerunt divinitatem, et perdiderunt felicitatem: rapuit Adam, praesumens, ut diabolus, de divinitate.

VERS. 6.-- Deus, tu scis. (CAS.) Quia pro aliis solvit, precatur, exspectantes antiquos, et quaerentes alios, scilicet, modernos, in se non frustrari, cum tanta tam aequanimiter ferat.

Insipientiam. (AUG.) Ex membris. Vel, quod stultum 946Dest Dei, sapientius est hominibus. Quod in me irriserunt, qui sibi sapientes videbantur, tu scisti quare fieret irrisio, scilicet, talis et mors (CAS.) Insipientiam. Quod mei ignari Dei, hi sunt qui commutantur in sapientes et justos.

VERS. 7.-- Non erubescant. (Ibid.) Quae solverit, exponit; hic ostendit quod superius de membris dixerat. (AUG.) Non erubescant, id est, non dicatur eis: Ubi est Christus vester? vel non prematur Ecclesia, ut filii erubescant. Qui exspectant. (CAS.) Quod oculis videre non potuerunt prophetae et justi. Ne ergo aliter eveniat quam Spiritus sanctus per eos praedixit, sequitur: Deus virtutum, cui nihil est impossibile. Deus Israel. (AUG.) Ut qui Deitatem ejus intueri 947Apossunt, non seducantur infirmitate ejus carnali.

VERS. 8.-- Quoniam propter te sustinui opprobria. (CAS.) Congregat in unum multa quae pertulit, ad invidiam in Judaeos excitandam; opprobrium, in Beelzebub ejicit daemonia, potator, vorax. (Matth. XI.)

Operuit. Hoc solet evenire in bono laceratis, qui solent tanto amplius ad tempus effici tristes quanto cognoscunt in se iniqua confingi.

VERS. 9.-- Peregrinus. Vel hospes, qui in domo ad tempus recipitur; non ut frater charissimus, quod eram.

VERS. 10.-- Zelus domus tuae comedit me. Quando funiculo vendentes ejecit. Quid istum zelum sequitur, 947Bsubjungit: Et opprobria exprobrantium tibi ceciderunt super me. Quia increpati Judaei convicia, quasi tela, super eum miserunt, ut: Nonne hic est filius Joseph? (Luc. IV.) Exprobrantium tibi. Quando dixerunt: Nunquid potest Deus parare mensam in deserto? (Psal. LXXVII.) Isti sunt dii tui, Israel (Exod. XXXII). Unde nunc dicit eadem convicia cadere super se, quae olim exprobrabant, ut ex consuetudine impia videas eos et non noviter hoc fecisse.

Ceciderunt. (CAS.). Cadunt super nos mala, quando non possumus vitare illa: ceciderunt igitur, id est, effectum habuerunt.

VERS. 11.-- Et operui in jejunio, etc. (AUG.) Praeelegi jejunare potius quam fel et acetum accipere; 947Cid est, veteres et amaros, qui non intrant in corpus ejus. (CAS.) Et operui. Non exercui potentiam vindicando. Et factum est, quod patuit in sputis, in opprobrium. (AUG.) Detrahentium et derisorum.

VERS. 12.-- Et posui. (AUG.) Illis carnem apposui, in quam saevirent, et occului Deitatem. Cilicium. (AUG., HIER.) Mortalis caro, ut de peccato damnaret peccatum.

Cilicium, lugubris caro, ut quando flevit super Jerusalem (Luc. XIX), et pro Lazaro (Joan. XI).

In parabolam. (AUG., HIER.) Irrisoriam, ut cuilibet maledicendo, dicerent: Sic contingat ut crucifixo. Vel, quia parabolas eos docebam; unde: Vobis datum est nosse mysterium Verbi Dei, caeteris autem in 947Dparabolis. Et tunc adversum me loquebantur.

VERS. 13.-- Qui sedebant. (CAS.) In porta sedent, qui conventibus hominum sedula curiositate miscentur. Dicit ergo passionem suam Judaeorum esse fabulam, ut nullus exciperetur, qui hujusmodi locutionis esset alienus; unde Cleophas ait: Tu solus peregrinus es in Jerusalem, et ignoras, etc. (Luc. LXXXIV).

In porta. Civitatis: ubi solent judices sedere ad judicandas causas, id est in publico judicio.

(HIERON.) Sicut Scribae et Pharisaei habentes clavem scientiae: sed nec intrantes, nec alios intrare sinentes.

Et in me psallebant. (CAS.) De me aiebant in publicis 948Aconventibus, et in conviviis psallebant: irrisio mea erat psalterium. Qui bibebant vinum. (AUG.) Qui inebriantur temporali voluptate. Vel, (CAS.) in Deum probabili opere psallant, qui vinum spirituale bibunt.

VERS. 14.-- Ego vero. (CAS.) Praedictis malis opposita est oratio pro parte sua, ut discamus non rixas, sed orationes opponere jurgiis. Tempus beneplaciti. (AUG.) Ideo nunc est tempus beneplaciti et reconciliationis per incarnationem, per sanguinem, per mortem; deinde quomodo hoc tempus provenerit, exponit: In multitudine misericordiae. In veritate. Praemisit de misericordia, nunc subjungit de veritate, quia universae viae misericordia et veritas misericordia, dimittendo peccata; veritas, reddendo promissa.

948BVERS. 15.-- Ut non infigar. (AUG.) Mente, supra dixit infixum corpore; dicitur hoc et infirmitate membrorum. De luto, id est, lutosis desideriis. De profundis aquarum. (CAS.) Judaei malignitate consilii profundi sunt, seditionibus turbulenti.
