VERS. 16.-- Profundum. (CAS.) Peccatorum, quod deglutit animas; unde: Peccator cum venerit in profundum peccatorum, contemnit (Prov. XVIII). Haec pericula membris ejus imminent. Neque urgeat super me, etc. (AUG.) Et si cecidisti, non claudit super te puteus os suum, si non claudis os tuum; sed confitere et dic: De profundis clamavit ad te, Domine, et evades. Claudit super illum, qui in profundo contemnit, a quo mortuo, velut qui non sit, perit confessio.

948CVERS. 17.-- Exaudi me, Domine, etc. (CAS.) Periculis hominum expositis, voce eorum precatur: Exaudi me, Domine, quia benigna misericordia, non quia merui. Benigna. (AUG.) Suavis est tribulato misericordia, ut panis esurienti. Venit tribulatio; differt Deus subvenire, ut moveat desiderium, et sit dulce auxilium; quod cum fit, jam non est quo differat.

VERS. 18.-- A puero, etc. (AUG.) quolibet sancto, parvo, non superbo; a quo superbiam tollit disciplina tribulationis.

VERS. 19.-- Propter inimicos, etc. (AUG.) Ut confundantur liberatione mea, etc., usque ad unde ipse Nabuchodonosor conversus Deum praedicat. Propter inimicos. (ID.) Hoc ad apertam, ut caro resurgat, et 948Dascendens spiritum mittat; unde inimici conversi sunt, quibus non proderit, si solam animam liberaveris.

VERS. 20.-- Tu scis improperium. (ID.) Quia quare sint ista mihi, tu nosti, illi non norunt. Et quia ipsi in conspectu tuo sunt, ista nescientes non poterunt confundi vel corrigi, nisi manifeste eruas. Et ideo ait: Propter inimicos. (ID.) Improperium, vel opprobrium, etc., usque ad sed adjuvando perficiat. Reverentiam. (ID.) Alii ignominiam, ut alapas, flagella, et quod Pilato tanquam reus traditus est: haec non pro suo reatu, sed pro nobis sustinuit, ut in talibus nos instrueret.

VERS. 21.-- In conspectu tuo. (CAS.) Invidiam ex 949Acitat contra eos, ut tantum scelus praesente Deo committerent.

Cor meum. Quia voluntate sustinuit, secundum illud: Desiderio desideravi hoc pascha manducare vobiscum.

VERS. 21.-- Qui simul contristaretur, et non fuit; et qui consolaretur, et non inveni. (AUG.) Contristati sunt discipuli et mulieres quae super eum flebant, sed non simul. Carnaliter enim contristabantur de vita mortali, quae erat mutanda morte, cum deberent cum eo contristari de caeteris, qui medicum occidebant, quod nemo tunc fecit.

VERS.--22.-- Et dederunt in escam meam fel, et in siti mea potaverunt me aceto. (AUG.) Quod non inveni simul tristes et consolantes, hoc fuit mihi 949Bfel amarum propter moerorem.

Acetum, etc. Id est, acidum, propter vetustatem eorum. Legitur in Evangelio fel ei oblatum, sed in potu, non in esca. Mystice ergo dicitur, id est, super escam suavem quam cum discipulis acceperat, quae est esca unitatis Christi, injecerunt fel: quod adhuc hodie facit, et gravius peccat contemptor sedentis in coelo, quam qui crucifixit ambulantem in terra. Dant bibendum amarum potum, qui male vivendo scandalum faciunt Ecclesiae, ut haeretici.

Gustavit Dominus, docens et nos gustare, id est, pati tales: sed non bibit, quia non possunt tales in corpus ejus recipi. Mystice ergo hoc praedicitur, sicut et mystice factum est in passione.

949C(CAS.) Et dederunt. Haec est consummatio passionis; cum dixisset: Sitio, fel cum aceto obtulerunt, hoc facto mores suos amarissimos indicantes.

VERS. 23.-- Fiat mensa. (CAS.) Prophetia contra adversarios. (AUG.) Fiat mensa. Mensa, Scriptura: hanc Judaei habuerunt, dum mandatum Dei coluerunt; postquam a lege jejuni sunt, haec mensa coram ipsis gentibus data est, ut gravius dolerent.

In laqueum. Ut qui littera legis alios stringebant, in ea obligati caderent. In retributiones. Quia illis ablata, et gentibus data. Malorum fuit retributio, dum nolentes in ea epulari, ab ea sunt exclusi. In scandalum. Quia deserentes pacis auctorem, rixas sibi et prava opera concitant.

949DVERS. 24.-- Oculi. (AUG.) Doctores qui praeeunt. Obscurentur, id est, lumen scientiae perdant. Et dorsum eorum, etc. Id est, minores. Cum enim lumen scientiae perdunt qui praeeunt, ad portanda peccatorum onera, et ad appetenda terrena inclinantur sequentes; vel, dorsum, mens eorumdem. Semper hoc de illis qui non poenitent.

VERS. 25.-- Effunde, etc. (CASS.) Ut in morem fluminis sit copiosa.

Comprehendat. Ut non liceat effugere.

VERS. 26.-- Fiat habitatio. (AUG.) Hoc jam in manifesto, etc., usque ad in quo superbierunt contra Deum. In tabernaculis. (CAS.) Templo et regio palatio. Ad hoc ponit inhabitare, quod fit devotae 950Amentis affectu; ad domos habitare, quod fit corporea mansione.

VERS. 27.-- Tu percussisti. (CAS.) Non sua culpa: percussisti passione, ad salutem gentium; hoc illi crudeli voto impleverunt.

Et super dolorem. Quia erat pro perditione eorum.

Addiderunt. Inferre mortem. Vel super dolorem vulnerum meorum, id est, quae mihi infixerat lancea, et clavis, addiderunt custodes sepulcri.

VERS. 28.-- Appone iniquitatem super iniquitatem, etc.) (AUG.) Iniquitas eorum fuit, ut hominem occiderent, et super hoc apposuit Deus, ut Filium suum occiderent, ut sicut servos praemissos, ita ipsum haeredem.

950BVERS. 29.-- Deleantur, etc. (ID.) Quia scriptos se putant, etc., usque ad et staturos ad dexteram. De libro viventium, etc. (CAS.) Notitia Dei, quae praedestinavit ac vitam, quos praescivit conformes fieri imagini Filii sui. Non sic tamen accipiendum est, tanquam in hoc libro aliquem scribat Deus, quem postea deleat: sed secundum spem illorum, qui scriptos se putant.

VERS. 30.-- Ego sum pauper, etc. (CAS.) Hic dispensationem incarnationis et sanctitatem propositi exponit, dicens: Quis finis passionis? Dolens. (AUG.) Hoc secundum caput, pro omnibus dolet: unde: Dolores nostros ipse portavit (Isa. LIII), quod nullus alius. Ideo dicit:

VERS. 32.-- Et placebit. (CAS.) Laus puri cordis 950Cplus placet quam mactatio pecudum. Vitulum novellum. (AUG.) Pro peccatis offerebatur novellus vitulus, qui significabat novitatem secuturam; quae defensionem habet in cornibus, munimen pedum in ungulis (per quas aspera saeculi calcet); producentem, quia fidelis quotidie virtute Dei augetur. (AUG.) Vitulus ungulis terram excitat, sic qui non contradicit, sed tamen terrenum abjecte sapit, ungulis excitandus est: et super hunc vitulum placebit laudatio mea cum angelis, ubi nec adversarius erit ventilandus, nec piger de terra excitandus.

VERS. 33.-- Videant. (CAS.) Quod oblatio jam est in mente, non in rebus, ubi pauper aequatur diviti. Et, o pauperes, hoc tamen contuitu Dei facite, quaerite Dominum. Vel, ut videatis, quaerite Deum, 950Descam mentis. Vinctos. (AUG.) Qui ultra necessaria quaerit, compedes onerat; sed sufficit diei malitia sua. Vinctos. (ID.) Vinctos mortalitate, qua Dominus offensus servos compedivit: sed inde clamantes audit.

VERS. 35.-- Caelum, terra, mare. (CAS.) Ad litteram, id est, coelestia, terrestria, et natantia, haec laudant, dum ex eis laudatur creator. (ID.) Divitiae sunt pauperis videre creata, et inde laudare creatorem. Laudent illum, etc. (ID.) Quod prius simul, nunc sigillatim monet; vel, laudent coelestia, terrestria, natantia. Et, ut perfecte omnia concludat, addit: Omnia quae in eis sunt: sic omnis creatura ad laudes invitatur. (HIER., CAS.) Ac si diceret: Omne 951Agenu flectatur, coelestium, terrestrium et infernorum (Phil. II). Et omnia reptilia in eis. (CAS.) Omnes modi monstruosi, in peccatis haerentes terrenis.

VERS. 36.-- Quoniam Deus salvam faciet Sion, etc. (AUG.) In spe fidelis populi finitur constructio Ecclesiae: unde omnis creatura laudare monetur.

VERS. 37.-- Et qui diligunt nomen ejus, etc. (CAS.) Quid per singula? omnes qui diligunt nomen tuum habitabunt. (AUG.) Hi sunt semen servorum. Iste enim versus exponit praecedentem.

PSALM LXVIII.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end. (AUG.) Adam was changed from 946Athe form of God for the worse, etc., as far as "to suffer", according to the Greeks. (CAS.) The fourth psalm, which treats more at large of the passion and the resurrection. The cause of the change is handled [commutationibus; read commutationis], that is, the passion of Christ. Here Christ speaks, head and body. Save me. First he prays to be made safe, because he suffers many things — as touching himself, without cause — but what another had seized, he himself pays. This is the voice of the mustard seed despised, while it is buried in the garden, which grows into a great herb: this seed dark and altogether contemptible. So also Christ, of whom: We saw him having no beauty nor comeliness, but nevertheless he took up the face of the earth, being made a great mountain.

Waters even unto my soul. (AUG.) That is, the crowds, etc., as far as beyond which they have not who may do anything to them.

946BVERS. 3.-- In the mire. (AUG.) Man was made of the slime of the earth, etc., as far as that is, the power of the flesh to escape the passion. Substance. Riches are so called, etc., as far as that is, I have not found in them what he made. I am come. Because willingly. Into the deep. The depth of a mad people.

VERS. 4.-- I have laboured. (AUG.) Long he cried: Woe to you! Scribes and Pharisees, so as to be hoarse as touching them, because he was not understood by them. Crying out, etc. (CAS.) He labours whose desire is not fulfilled. My eyes. Like the eyes of the two who did not know him on the way, in whom that which was within came to be also without, that is, the blindness which was made in the heart was also in the eyes. For they said: We hoped that he would have redeemed Israel (Luc. XXIV.) [AUG]. But he restored hope to them, etc., as far 946Cas because they would have been lost. While I hope. (CAS.) The reason is added: I wait for mercy, I do not entreat power.

VERS. 5.-- They are multiplied. (AUG.) What before he said figuratively, now he says openly in the fact. Above the hairs. For an unlimited number; or, they are more than those which are for adornment. I have seized. They willed to seize the Godhead, and lost happiness: Adam seized, presuming, as the devil did, upon Godhead.

VERS. 6.-- O God, thou knowest. (CAS.) Because he pays for others, he prays that they that wait, the ancients, and they that seek, the others, namely the moderns, be not disappointed in him, since he bears such great things so evenly.

Foolishness. (AUG.) From the members. Or, that which is foolish 946Dof God is wiser than men. What they mocked in me, who seemed to themselves wise, thou hast known why the mockery came to be, namely, such mockery and death too. (CAS.) Foolishness. That they who are ignorant of me who am God, these are they who are changed into wise and just men.

VERS. 7.-- Let them not be ashamed. (Ibid.) He sets forth what things he has paid; here he shows what he had said above concerning the members. (AUG.) Let them not be ashamed, that is, let it not be said to them: Where is your Christ? or, let the Church not be pressed so that her sons are ashamed. That wait. (CAS.) What the prophets and the just could not see with their eyes. Lest therefore it turn out otherwise than the Holy Spirit foretold through them, there follows: the God of hosts, [Vulg. Ps 68:7 Domine virtutum, "O Lord of hosts"] to whom nothing is impossible. The God of Israel. (AUG.) That they who are able to behold his Godhead 947Amay not be led astray by his carnal infirmity.

VERS. 8.-- Because for thy sake I have borne reproaches. (CAS.) [Vulg. Ps 68:8 opprobrium, singular; the gloss argues from the many things gathered into one] He gathers into one the many things he endured, to stir up odium against the Jews; reproach: he casts out demons in Beelzebub, a wine-bibber, a glutton. (Matth. XI.)

It hath covered. This is wont to befall those torn in a good cause, who are wont to be made so much the sadder for a time as they know that wicked things are being fabricated against them.

VERS. 9.-- A stranger. Or a guest, who is received into a house for a time; not as a most dear brother, which I was.

VERS. 10.-- The zeal of thy house hath eaten me up. When with a cord he cast out them that sold. What follows upon this zeal he 947Bsubjoins: And the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me. Because the Jews, being rebuked, cast their insults upon him like darts, as: Is not this the son of Joseph? (Luc. IV.) Of them that reproach thee. When they said: Can God furnish a table in the wilderness? (Psal. LXXVII.) These are thy gods, O Israel (Exod. XXXII). Whence he now says that the same insults fall upon himself which they formerly cast as reproaches, that thou mayest see that they did this out of impious custom and not newly.

They are fallen. (CAS.). Evils fall upon us when we cannot avoid them: they are fallen, therefore, that is, they took effect.

VERS. 11.-- And I covered it in fasting, etc. (AUG.) I chose rather to fast than to take gall and vinegar; 947Cthat is, the old and the bitter, who do not enter into his body. (CAS.) And I covered. I did not exercise power by avenging. And it became, which appeared in the spittings, a reproach. (AUG.) Of detractors and mockers.

VERS. 12.-- And I put on. (AUG.) I set flesh before them, against which they might rage, and I hid my Godhead. Haircloth. (AUG., HIER.) Mortal flesh, that of sin he might condemn sin.

Haircloth, mournful flesh, as when he wept over Jerusalem (Luc. XIX), and for Lazarus (Joan. XI).

Into a parable. (AUG., HIER.) A mocking one, so that, in cursing anyone, they would say: So may it befall as it did the crucified. Or, because I was teaching them in parables; whence: To you it is given to know the mystery of the Word of God, but to the rest in 947Dparables. [Vulg. Lc 8:10 mysterium regni Dei, "the mystery of the kingdom of God"] And then they spoke against me.

VERS. 13.-- They that sat. (CAS.) They sit in the gate who mingle in the assemblies of men with busy curiosity. He says therefore that his passion was the talk of the Jews, so that none was excepted who was a stranger to speech of this kind; whence Cleophas says: Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and knowest not, etc. (Luc. LXXXIV).

In the gate. Of the city: where judges are wont to sit to judge causes, that is, in public judgment.

(HIERON.) As the Scribes and Pharisees having the key of knowledge: but neither entering themselves, nor suffering others to enter.

And they sang against me. (CAS.) They spoke of me in public 948Aassemblies, and at banquets they sang: my mockery was their psaltery. Who drank wine. (AUG.) Who are made drunk with temporal pleasure. Or, (CAS.) let them sing to God with approved work who drink spiritual wine.

VERS. 14.-- But as for me. (CAS.) Against the aforesaid evils prayer is set on his own part, that we may learn to oppose to wranglings not brawls but prayers. A time of good pleasure. (AUG.) Therefore now is the time of good pleasure and of reconciliation, through the incarnation, through the blood, through the death; then he sets forth how this time came about: In the multitude of mercy. In truth. He set down first concerning mercy, now he subjoins concerning truth, because all ways are mercy and truth [Vulg. Ps 24:10 universae viae Domini, "all the ways of the Lord"]: mercy, in forgiving sins; truth, in rendering what was promised.

948BVERS. 15.-- That I may not stick fast. (AUG.) In mind; above he said he was fixed fast in body; and this is said from the infirmity of the members. Out of the mire, that is, out of miry desires. Out of the deep waters. (CAS.) The Jews are deep in the malignity of their counsel, turbulent with seditions.

VERS. 16.-- The deep. (CAS.) Of sins, which swallows down souls; whence: The sinner, when he is come into the depth of sins, contemneth (Prov. XVIII). These dangers hang over his members. Nor let it shut her mouth upon me, etc. (AUG.) Even if thou hast fallen, the pit does not shut its mouth upon thee if thou dost not shut thy mouth; but confess and say: Out of the depths he hath cried to thee, O Lord, [Vulg. Ps 129:1 clamavi, "I have cried"] and thou shalt escape. It shuts upon him who contemns in the deep, from whom, being dead, as though he were not, confession perishes.

948CVERS. 17.-- Hear me, O Lord, etc. (CAS.) The dangers of men being set forth, he prays with their voice: Hear me, O Lord, for mercy is kind, not because I have deserved it. Kind. (AUG.) Mercy is sweet to the afflicted, as bread to the hungry. Tribulation comes; God defers to succour, that he may stir up desire, and that the help may be sweet; and when this is done, there is now nothing for which he should defer.

VERS. 18.-- From the child, etc. (AUG.) any holy one, little, not proud; from whom the discipline of tribulation takes away pride.

VERS. 19.-- Because of my enemies, etc. (AUG.) That they may be confounded by my deliverance, etc., as far as whence Nabuchodonosor himself, being converted, proclaims God. Because of my enemies. (ID.) This unto the open deliverance, that the flesh may rise again, and, 948Dascending, may send the Spirit; whence enemies were converted, to whom it will profit nothing if thou deliver the soul alone.

VERS. 20.-- Thou knowest my reproach. (ID.) Because why these things are mine, thou knowest; they know not. And because they themselves are in thy sight, not knowing these things they will not be able to be confounded or corrected, unless thou plainly rescue me. And therefore he says: Because of my enemies. (ID.) Reproach, or shame, etc., as far as but by helping may perfect. Reverence. (ID.) Others [read] ignominy, as the buffets, the scourges, and that he was handed over to Pilate as a guilty man: these things he bore not for his own guilt, but for us, that in such things he might instruct us.

VERS. 21.-- In thy sight. (CAS.) He stirs up odium 949Aagainst them, that they committed so great a crime with God present.

My heart. Because he endured of his own will, according to that: With desire I have desired to eat this pasch with you.

VERS. 21.-- One that would grieve together with me, and there was none; and one that would comfort me, and I found none. (AUG.) The disciples were grieved, and the women who wept over him, but not together with him. For they were grieved carnally over the mortal life which was to be changed by death, whereas they ought to have been grieved with him over the rest, who were slaying the physician — which no one then did.

VERS.--22.-- And they gave me gall for my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink. (AUG.) That I found none at once grieving and comforting, this was to me 949Bbitter gall by reason of sorrow.

Vinegar, etc. That is, sour, because of their oldness. It is read in the Gospel that gall was offered him, but in drink, not in food. Mystically therefore it is said, that is, upon the sweet food which he had taken with his disciples, which is the food of the unity of Christ, they cast gall: which is still done to this day, and the despiser of him that sits in heaven sins more grievously than he who crucified him that walked upon the earth. They give a bitter draught to drink who by living ill make scandal for the Church, as heretics do.

The Lord tasted, teaching us also to taste, that is, to bear such men: but he did not drink, because such men cannot be received into his body. Mystically therefore is this foretold, as it was also mystically done in the passion.

949C(CAS.) And they gave. This is the consummation of the passion; when he had said: I thirst, they offered gall with vinegar, showing by this deed their most bitter manners.

VERS. 23.-- Let their table become. (CAS.) A prophecy against the adversaries. (AUG.) Let their table become. The table is Scripture: this the Jews had, while they cherished the commandment of God; after they were fasting from the law, this table was given to the Gentiles before their very eyes, that they might grieve the more bitterly.

A snare. That they who were binding others by the letter of the law might fall bound in it. A recompense. Because it was taken from them and given to the Gentiles. It was a recompense of evils, since, being unwilling to feast at it, they were shut out from it. A stumbling block. Because, forsaking the author of peace, they stir up for themselves brawls and depraved works.

949DVERS. 24.-- Eyes. (AUG.) The teachers who go before. Let them be darkened, that is, let them lose the light of knowledge. And their back, etc. That is, the lesser ones. For when they who go before lose the light of knowledge, those who follow are bowed down to bear the burdens of sins and to seek after earthly things; or, the back, the mind of the same. Always this concerns those who do not repent.

VERS. 25.-- Pour out, etc. (CASS.) That it may be abundant after the manner of a river.

Let it take hold. That it may not be permitted to escape.

VERS. 26.-- Let their habitation become. (AUG.) This now in the open, etc., as far as in which they grew proud against God. In their tabernacles. (CAS.) The temple and the royal palace. To this he applies to dwell within, which is done by the affection of a devout 950Amind; to houses, to dwell, which is done by bodily abiding.

VERS. 27.-- Thou hast smitten. (CAS.) Not by his own fault: thou hast smitten him by the passion, unto the salvation of the Gentiles; this they fulfilled with a cruel purpose.

And upon the sorrow. Because it was for their perdition.

They have added. To inflict death. Or, upon the sorrow of my wounds, that is, of those which the lance and the nails had fixed in me, they added the guards of the sepulchre.

VERS. 28.-- Add thou iniquity upon iniquity, etc.) (AUG.) Their iniquity was that they should kill a man, and upon this God added that they should kill his Son, so that, as the servants sent before, so also the heir himself.

950BVERS. 29.-- Let them be blotted out, etc. (ID.) Because they think themselves written down, etc., as far as and that they shall stand at the right hand. Out of the book of the living, etc. (CAS.) The knowledge of God, which predestined and life, those whom he foreknew to be made conformable to the image of his Son. Yet it is not so to be taken, as though God writes anyone in this book whom he afterwards blots out: but according to the hope of those who think themselves written down.

VERS. 30.-- I am poor, etc. (CAS.) Here he sets forth the dispensation of the incarnation and the holiness of his purpose, saying: What is the end of the passion? Sorrowful. (AUG.) This according to the head: he sorrows for all: whence: He himself hath borne our sorrows (Isa. LIII), which no other did. Therefore he says:

VERS. 32.-- And it shall please. (CAS.) The praise of a pure heart 950Cpleases more than the slaying of cattle. A young calf. (AUG.) For sins a young calf was offered, which signified the newness that was to follow; which has its defence in its horns, the guard of its feet in its hoofs (by which it may tread down the rough things of the world); bringing forth, because the faithful man is daily increased by the power of God. (AUG.) The calf stirs up the earth with its hoofs; so he who does not contradict, but nevertheless has a base earthly relish, is to be stirred up with hoofs: and upon this calf my praise will be pleasing among the angels, where neither will there be an adversary to be winnowed, nor a sluggard to be stirred up out of the earth.

VERS. 33.-- Let them see. (CAS.) That the offering is now in the mind, not in things, where the poor man is made equal to the rich. And, O ye poor, do this nevertheless with your gaze upon God: seek ye the Lord. [Vulg. Ps 68:33 quaerite Deum, "seek ye God"] Or, that you may see, seek God, 950Dthe food of the mind. The bound. (AUG.) He who seeks beyond what is needful loads on fetters; but sufficient for the day is its own evil. The bound. (ID.) Bound by mortality, wherewith the Lord, being offended, put fetters on his servants: but from thence he hears them crying out.

VERS. 35.-- Heaven, earth, sea. (CAS.) According to the letter, that is, the heavenly things, the earthly, and the swimming things: these praise him, while from them the creator is praised. (ID.) It is the riches of a poor man to see created things, and thence to praise the creator. Let them praise him, etc. (ID.) What before he urged all together, now he urges one by one; or, let the heavenly things, the earthly, the swimming things praise him. And, that he may perfectly include all things, he adds: All things that are in them: [Vulg. Ps 68:35 et omnia reptilia in eis, "and all the creeping things in them"] thus every creature is invited to praise. (HIER., CAS.) As if he should say: Let every 951Aknee bow, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth (Phil. II). And all the creeping things in them. (CAS.) All monstrous kinds, sticking fast in earthly sins.

VERS. 36.-- For God will save Sion, etc. (AUG.) In the hope of the faithful people the building of the Church is brought to its end: whence every creature is urged to praise.

VERS. 37.-- And they that love his name, etc. (CAS.) Why go through them one by one? all who love thy name shall dwell there. (AUG.) These are the seed of the servants. For this verse expounds the preceding one.

PSALMUS LXIX.

VERS. 1.-- In rememoratione. (CAS.) Memoria duobus modis, etc., usque ad et spem resurrectionis assumunt. (AUG.) Vox tribulatorum pro Christo, etc., 951Busque ad primo petentes se adjuvari, malos erubescere.

VERS. 2.-- Deus in adjutorium. Monet ut in Deo, non in nobis, gloriemur. (CAS.) Hic omnis petitio affirmatio est, unde non sunt timendae tribulationes. Hic versiculus ante omnes horas in initio praedicitur, quia, cum orare solemus, maxime tentare nititur diabolus, ut muscae morientes perdant suavitatem unguenti.

VERS. 3.-- Confundantur. (CAS.) Confundi, est de perversitate turbari. Revereantur, ne proles a justitia poena sequatur. Qui quaerunt, etc. (AUG.) Diversa sunt tempora in Ecclesia: primo, fuit impetus persequentium, unde, qui quaerunt; modo, remansit malevolentia cogitantium, unde, qui volunt. (ID.)

951CVERS. 4.-- Avertantur. (ID.) Duo genera sunt persequentium, etc., usque ad exit integer, qui neutro capitur.

VERS. 5.-- Exsultent et laetentur in te omnes. (CAS.) Monet laetari bonos, quos egenos Deus adjuvat et liberat. Semper. Quia non unquam debet cessare a laude ejus. Magnificetur Deus. (CAS.) Nostro more dictum, ubi quis laudibus crescit; quod non Deus, sed nos laudando proficimus.

VERS. 6.-- Ego vero egenus. (CAS.) Quod hortor, facio, etc., usque ad ubi est dives, semper ambit, desiderat et accipit. Ne moreris. (ID.) Tardum videtur, quod magno desiderio quaeritur. (AUG.) Ne mihi tardius videatur, quod venturus es, quod fit per patientiam; qua qui caret, tardum ei videtur, et 951Ddeflectitur ab eo: ut uxor Lot, quae fit statua salis, ut te condiat: exemplo enim tibi est ne retro aspicias.

PSALM LXIX.

VERS. 1.-- In remembrance. (CAS.) Memory in two ways, etc., as far as and they take up the hope of the resurrection. (AUG.) The voice of those in tribulation for Christ, etc., 951Bas far as first asking that they be helped, and that the wicked be put to shame.

VERS. 2.-- O God, unto my help. He urges that we glory in God, not in ourselves. (CAS.) Here every petition is an affirmation, whence tribulations are not to be feared. This little verse is said beforehand at the beginning of all the hours, because, when we are wont to pray, the devil strives most of all to tempt us, so that dying flies may spoil the sweetness of the ointment.

VERS. 3.-- Let them be confounded. (CAS.) To be confounded is to be troubled over one's perversity. Let them be ashamed, lest punishment, an offspring from justice, follow them. That seek, etc. (AUG.) The times in the Church are diverse: first there was the onset of persecutors, whence, that seek; now there remains the ill will of those who plot, whence, that will. (ID.)

951CVERS. 4.-- Let them be turned backward. (ID.) There are two kinds of persecutors, etc., as far as he comes forth whole who is caught by neither.

VERS. 5.-- Let all rejoice and be glad in thee. (CAS.) He urges the good to be glad, whom, being needy, God helps and delivers. Always. Because he ought not ever to cease from his praise. Let God be magnified. (CAS.) [Vulg. Ps 69:5 Magnificetur Dominus, "Let the Lord be magnified"] Said after our manner, where one grows by praises; for it is not God, but we, who by praising make progress.

VERS. 6.-- But I am needy. (CAS.) What I exhort, I do, etc., as far as where he is rich, he ever goes about, desires and receives. Delay not. (ID.) That seems slow which is sought with great desire. (AUG.) Lest what thou art to come should seem to me too slow — which comes about through patience; and he who lacks it, to him it seems slow, and 951Dhe is turned aside from it: like Lot's wife, who became a pillar of salt, that she might season thee: for she is an example to thee, that thou look not back.

PSALMUS LXX.

VERS. 1.-- In finem. (AUG.) De commendatione gratiae, etc., usque ad fere singulis syllabis commendatur gratia.

Filiorum Jonadab. (ID.) Filiis spontaneis, etc., usque ad qui ex se mali.

(CAS.) Vel ita, monemur in titulo habere devotionem filiorum Jonadab, etc., usque ad illi vero consueta malitia in obstinatione permanserunt.

VERS. 2.-- In te, Domine, speravi. Generalis justus 952Aloquitur a principio mundi usque ad finem: totam spem in Deo ponens, gratiam ejus commendat, ne falsa in nobis praesumamus.

(CAS.) Vel priores captivi sunt in mundo, unde evadi potest: secundi in inferno. Vel, priorum, id est, eorum qui ante capti vitiis, quam filii Christi. Totus hic psalmus gratiam Dei, quae gratis datur, summa intentione commendat.

VERS. 3.-- Esto mihi in Deum protectorem, et in locum munitum, etc. Duo promisit, duo alia reddit.

VERS. 4.-- Peccatoris. (AUG.) Duo sunt genera peccatorum: alii legem acceperunt, ut Judaei et Christiani; alii non, ut pagani.

VERS. 5.-- A juventute. (CAS.) Id est, a conversione, vel ex quo contra diabolum coepi pugnare. 952B(AUG.) A juventute, ex quo coepi sperare in te, etc., usque ad juvenis pugnat, sed cadit, nisi sit Deus spes ejus.

VERS. 7.-- In te cantatio. (CAS.) Delectationi est mihi esse in te. Semper. Ut continua sint beneficia. Semper. (AUG.) Et in praesenti, etc., usque ad contra quam nil stat.

VERS. 8.-- Repleatur os meum. (CAS.) Dixit beneficia, nunc petit ut gratias agere possit. Nam si Deus os non replet, non ardet desiderium. Tota die magnitudinem tuam. (AUG.) Id est, sine intermissione, etc., usque ad nomine ergo magnitudinis omnia includit.

VERS. 9.-- Ne projicias me. (CAS.) De gratia tempore senectutis et senii danda. Senectutis. (AUG.) 952CSenectus in Christo, dum prodigium factus est, dum infirmatus in cruce et irrisus; quod dicitur senectus, quia ex vetustate assumpsit, unde: Vetus homo noster simul crucifixus est (Rom. VI).

VERS. 10.-- Quoniam dixerunt inimici mei. (AUG.) Dicitur hoc de Christo, qui inter manus inimicorum infirmus factus est, et quasi nihil posset comprehensus. Sed hic de membris ejus dicitur hoc, quia et illa talia ex nostra persona habuit.

VERS. 11.-- Deus dereliquit eum. (AUG.) Unde alibi: Quare me dereliquisti? id est, quare me derelictum putant malo suo. Si enim cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriae crucifixissent.

VERS. 12.-- Ne elongeris a me. (CAS.) Longe putant, dum tardat; ne elongeris, ut gravioribus 952Dexponat.

VERS. 13.-- Confundantur, etc. (CAS.) Quia disposita Dei non mutantur. Detrahentes animae meae. Alias, committentes animam meam. (AUG.) Id est provocantes nos ut Deo resistamus, quod est contra Deum committere bellum; ut illi faciunt quibus non placet Deus in suis adversis, quod est eum habere injustum. Committitur etiam anima, si odit eos a quibus patitur. Qui quaerunt. (ID.) Ut fecit uxor Job, quae ait: Dic aliquid in Deum et morere (Job. VII). Ut etiam ait uxor Tobiae: Ubi sunt justitiae tuae? (Tob. IV, 2.) Hoc dicebat ut displiceret illi Deus.

VERS. 14.-- Et adjiciam. (AUG.) Adjectio laudis est, post creationem omnium rerum, laus de incarnatione 953Aet resurrectione, quod inferiora docent. Omnem. (AUG.) Quia si laudatus in omnibus aliis, nondum in eo quod suscitavit carnem nostram in viam aeternam, quae est laus adjecta pro resurrectione Christi. Vel omnis laus esset, et nihil laudi deesset, si damnaret peccantes, quia justitia esset; sed quia et hos liberas: Adjiciam super omnem laudem tuam.

VERS. 15.-- Os meum annuntiabit justitiam. Christum, sed ne aliter acciperes, addit: Salutare. Quare? quia non approbatur ex operibus legis justificari quemquam. Et hoc est: Quoniam non cognovi litteraturam, id est, figuras legis per quod fiam potens. Tota die. (AUG.) Vel ita, etc., usque ad justitiae serviat. Quoniam non cognovi litteraturam. (ID.) Praedicabo salutem tuam tota die, etc., usque ad quia 953Bhabitu inventus est ut homo (Philip. II), et surgit mortuus.

VERS. 17, 18.-- Docuisti. (CAS.) Per libros, vel inspirando usque nunc: per spatia temporum crevit doctrina. Mirabilia. Quod de iniquo justus. Mirabilia. (AUG.) Quid mirabilius quam mortuos suscitare? etc., usque ad hoc est a juventute et nunc. Juventute. (ID.) Aliqui notant quatuor tempora Ecclesiae, aliqui tantum tria distingui, idem significantes per nunc et senectam. Unde juventus Ecclesiae fuit quando virtus martyrum dimicavit. (CAS.) Progrediens vero tempus, nunc, cum fides per Ecclesias proficit. (AUG.) Senecta, id est, gravis aetas, quando incipiet frigescere charitas multorum, cum mundi tempora decrescunt. Senium. (CAS.) Occiduum tempus, etc., 953Cusque ad contra quos Dominus: Vobiscum sum usque ad consummationem saeculi, etc. (Matth. XXI).-- Donec annuntiem brachium tuum. (CAS.) Dum per incarnationem captivos liberat. Et justitiam judicii, puniendi scilicet, qua hominem peccantem justo judicio damnat.

VERS. 19, 20.-- Usque in altissima. Et ne putes quod solus homo egeat gratia, etc., usque ad continet in eo quod sunt.

Usque in altissima. Quia homo Deus sedet ad dexteram Patris regnans cum eo. Quae fecisti magnalia. Utrumque mirabile, per gratiam redimi hominem, qui per justitiam damnatus erat.

Deus, quis similis tibi? Quantas ostendisti mihi tribulationes multas et malas, et conversus vivificasti me, 953Det de abyssis terrae, etc. Cui personae quae gratia sit, captivae scilicet, utraque resurrectio mentis et corporis; unde promittit gratias.

VERS. 22.-- In vasis psalmi. (CAS.) In vivificatione spiritus vel contemplativa vita.

VERS. 23.-- Anima mea quam redemisti. (AUG.) Ipsis internis labiis quibus tacite clamat Deum.

VERS. 24.-- Cum confusi et reveriti fuerint. Tunc locus est verae et securae exaltationis, cum non licet impiis dominari.

PSALM LXX.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end. [Vulg. Ps 70:1 has no In finem; the title begins Psalmus David, filiorum Jonadab, et priorum captivorum] (AUG.) Concerning the commendation of grace, etc., as far as grace is commended in almost every single syllable.

Of the sons of Jonadab. (ID.) To sons that are willing, etc., as far as who of themselves are evil.

(CAS.) Or thus: we are admonished in the title to have the devotion of the sons of Jonadab, etc., as far as but they, by their accustomed malice, remained in obstinacy.

VERS. 2.-- In thee, O Lord, have I hoped. The just man in general 952Aspeaks, from the beginning of the world unto its end: placing all his hope in God, he commends his grace, lest we presume upon false things in ourselves.

(CAS.) Or, the former captives are in the world, from which one can escape: the second in hell. Or, of the former, that is, of those who were taken by vices before they became sons of Christ. This whole psalm commends with the utmost earnestness the grace of God, which is given freely.

VERS. 3.-- Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a place of strength, etc. Two things he promised, two others he renders.

VERS. 4.-- Of the sinner. (AUG.) There are two kinds of sinners: some received the law, as the Jews and the Christians; others did not, as the pagans.

VERS. 5.-- From my youth. (CAS.) That is, from my conversion, or from the time when I began to fight against the devil. 952B(AUG.) From my youth, from the time when I began to hope in thee, etc., as far as a young man fights, but falls, unless God be his hope.

VERS. 7.-- In thee is my song. (CAS.) It is a delight to me to be in thee. Always. That the benefits may be unbroken. Always. (AUG.) Both in the present, etc., as far as against which nothing stands.

VERS. 8.-- Let my mouth be filled. (CAS.) He has told the benefits; now he asks that he may be able to give thanks. For if God does not fill the mouth, desire does not burn. All the day thy greatness. (AUG.) That is, without intermission, etc., as far as under the name of greatness therefore he includes all things.

VERS. 9.-- Cast me not off. (CAS.) Concerning the grace to be given in the time of old age and of decrepitude. Of old age. (AUG.) 952COld age was in Christ, when he was made a wonder, when he was made weak upon the cross and mocked; and it is called old age because he took it on from oldness, whence: Our old man is crucified with him (Rom. VI).

VERS. 10.-- For my enemies have said. (AUG.) This is said of Christ, who among the hands of his enemies was made weak, and, once seized, as though he could do nothing. But here this is said of his members, because he had such things also from our person.

VERS. 11.-- God hath forsaken him. (AUG.) Whence elsewhere: Why hast thou forsaken me? that is, why do they think me forsaken, to their own hurt. For if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.

VERS. 12.-- Depart not from me. (CAS.) They think him far off while he delays; depart not, that he may expose [them] to graver things 952D.

VERS. 13.-- Let them be confounded, etc. (CAS.) Because the things ordained of God are not changed. That detract my soul. Otherwise, that set my soul at strife. (AUG.) That is, provoking us to resist God, which is to wage war against God; as those do to whom God is not pleasing in their adversities, which is to hold him unjust. The soul is also set at strife if it hates those from whom it suffers. That seek. (ID.) As Job's wife did, who said: Say somewhat against God, and die (Job. VII). [Vulg. Job 2:9 Benedic Deo, et morere, "Bless God, and die"] As also Tobias's wife says: Where are thy justices? (Tob. IV, 2.) [Vulg. Tob 2:22 Manifeste vana facta est spes tua, "Manifestly thy hope is become vain"] She said this that God might be displeasing to him.

VERS. 14.-- And I will add. (AUG.) The addition of praise is, after the creation of all things, the praise concerning the incarnation 953Aand the resurrection, which the lines below teach. All. (AUG.) Because, though he be praised in all other things, not yet in this, that he raised up our flesh unto the eternal way [viam; read vitam, "life"], which is the praise added for the resurrection of Christ. Or, all praise would be there, and nothing would be lacking to praise, if he condemned sinners, because it would be justice; but because thou deliverest even these: I will add above all thy praise.

VERS. 15.-- My mouth shall show forth justice. Christ; but lest thou take it otherwise, he adds: Salvation. Why? because it is not approved that any man is justified by the works of the law. And this is: Because I have not known learning, that is, the figures of the law, through which I might be made mighty. All the day. (AUG.) Or thus, etc., as far as let him serve justice. Because I have not known learning. (ID.) I will preach thy salvation all the day, etc., as far as because 953Bin habit he was found as a man (Philip. II), and the dead man rises.

VERS. 17, 18.-- Thou hast taught me. (CAS.) Through books, or by inspiring even until now: through the spaces of the times doctrine has grown. Wondrous things. That out of an unjust man a just man is made. Wondrous things. (AUG.) What is more wonderful than to raise the dead? etc., as far as this is "from my youth" and "now". Youth. (ID.) Some mark four ages of the Church, others that only three are distinguished, signifying the same by now and old age. Whence the youth of the Church was when the courage of the martyrs did battle. (CAS.) But the time going forward is "now", when faith advances through the churches. (AUG.) Old age, that is, the heavy time of life, when the charity of many shall begin to grow cold, as the times of the world diminish. Decrepitude. (CAS.) The declining time, etc., 953Cas far as against whom the Lord says: I am with you even unto the consummation of the world, etc. (Matth. XXI).-- Until I show forth thy arm. (CAS.) While through the incarnation he sets the captives free. And the justice of judgment, that is, of punishing, whereby by a just judgment he condemns the sinning man.

VERS. 19, 20.-- Even unto the highest. And lest thou think that man alone stands in need of grace, etc., as far as he holds them together in that which they are.

Even unto the highest. Because the man who is God sits at the right hand of the Father, reigning with him. The great things thou hast done. Both are wonderful: that man is redeemed through grace, who through justice had been condemned.

O God, who is like to thee? How great troubles hast thou shown me, many and grievous, and turning thou hast brought me to life again, 953Dand out of the depths of the earth, etc. To what person what grace belongs — namely to the captive person: the twofold resurrection of mind and of body; whence he promises thanksgiving.

VERS. 22.-- In the vessels of psalm. (CAS.) In the quickening of the spirit, or in the contemplative life.

VERS. 23.-- My soul which thou hast redeemed. (AUG.) With those inward lips with which it silently cries out to God.

VERS. 24.-- When they shall be confounded and put to shame. Then is there place for true and secure exaltation, when it is not permitted to the ungodly to bear rule.

PSALMUS LXXI.

VERS. 1.-- In Salomonem, etc. (AUG.) Verum pacificum, etc., usque ad qui hic commendatur secundum 954Autramque naturam. (CAS.) Quartus psalmus de duabus naturis Christi monet ut Christum verum Deum et verum hominem regem credamus, et est prophetia de Christo.

VERS. 2.-- Deus judicium. (CAS.) De judicio, optando illud dari Filio. Justitiam tuam, etc. (AUG.) Nota repetitiones ejusdem, vel aliis verbis, multum commendant divina eloquia, quae maxime sunt in psalmis: et in eo genere sermonis, quo affectus animi est movendus.

VERS. 3.-- Montes. (AUG.) Prophetae, Apostoli, qui coelo altitudine proximant; pacem nuntiandam populo fideli, Christum. Et colles. Suscipiant justitiam, id est, Christum, vel montes pacem populo: et colles de utrisque praedicatoribus praecedentibus et 954Bsequentibus dicit. Vel suscipiant montes, id est, majores.

Pacem. Verbum reconciliationis, scilicet verbum Evangelii, ad hoc ut nuntient populo.

Et colles. Id est, minores; justitiam, id est, obedientiam, ut obediant doctrinae veritatis.

Tuum et tuos dicendo, ostendit omnia quae sunt Patris esse et Filii, et e converso.

VERS. 4.-- Judicabit pauperes populi. (CAS.) Idem agit de eodem judicio affirmando. Post optationem, virtute prophetiae, dicit quae sunt adventu Domini praestanda. (AUG.) Vel secundum aliam litteram: Justitia judicabit pauperem. Sed codices qui habent in littera magis approbantur. Pauperes populi. Id est, eos qui pauperes in populo, in quo boni malique 954Ccommisti. Humiliabit calumniatorem. Dum enim gratia sua adjuvat, etc., usque ad qui innocentes nititur trahere in culpam. (HIERON., AUG.) Vel, humiliabit, et, victo diabolo, permanebit cum sole splendor; id est, Filius cum Patre, sedens ad dexteram Patris in aeternum, hoc est ante lunam, in generatione et generationem.

VERS. 7.-- Descendet sicut pluvia, etc. (CAS.) Ecce quis et qualis ille rex, qui judicaturus est. (AUG.) Alludit facto Gedeonis, etc., usque ad et postea complueretur gentilitas sicco vellere Judaeorum. (CAS.) Descendet Christus, etc., usque ad quis ergo post tam apertas similitudines dubitet de partu Virginis? In vellus, et sicut stillicidia. (AUG.) Vellus, Judaea, quae auctoritate doctrinae exspolianda erat, ut ovis 954Dvellere: vel, quia doctrinae pluviam detinebat, quam nolebat gentibus praedicare.

VERS. 8.-- Et dominabitur a mari usque ad mare. (CAS.) Ostendit quae sit amplitudo regni. A flumine. (AUG.) A Jordane, ubi vox:. Hic est Filius meus dilectus. Inde ergo doctrina ejus coepit: inde auctoritas magistri dilatatur usque ad terminos orbis terrae, praedicato Evangelio regni. (CAS.) Inde regula baptismi per totum orbem manavit. Paucis verbis magna docet sacramenta.

VERS. 10.-- Reges Tharsis et insulae munera offerent. (CAS.) Pertinaces dicuntur inimici, etc., usque ad vel, historialiter potest accipi de regibus qui venerunt adorare Christum.

955AVERS. 12.-- Quia liberabit pauperem a potente, etc. (CASS.) De operibus ejus agit, etc., usque ad in participatione justitiae.

VERS. 14.-- Ex usuris. (AUG.) Usurae, peccata, etc., usque ad juvando per gratiam ad justitiam faciendam. Vel, ex usuris, de futuro, id est, poenis aeternis; et iniquitate, id est, peccato ipso, pro quo poena debebatur. Nomen. Christianum. Coram illo. Quia in ejus regno ante ipsum victuri sunt.

VERS. 15.-- Et vivet, et dabitur ei de auro, etc. (CAS.) De honorificentia regis. Arabiae. (AUG.) Per Arabiam, gentes; per aurum, sapientiam, quae excellit inter doctrinas. De ipso semper. (ID.) Multiplicando, vel consequendo, vel de ejus institutione, quia ipse orare docuit.

955BVERS. 16.-- Firmamentum. (AUG.) Prophetarum est, quia quod praedixerunt, implevit. In summis montium. (ID.) Auctores Scripturarum Prophetae et Apostoli; quos firmat, quia omnia ab illis praedicta in illo sunt impleta.

In terra. Quia propter eos qui in terra sunt, omnia scripta sunt. Unde et ipse in terram venit, ut ea impleret.

Super Libanum. (AUG.) Sicut Libanus proceras cedros producit, sic Christus sanctos ad coelum. Sicut fenum. (CAS.) Non aetas seni sed viriditas sanctis comparatur. Boni de ista civitate praesentis Ecclesiae migrantes in illa beatitudine florebunt. (AUG.) In Genesi feni nomine et frumentum intelligitur, etc., usque ad et corparabitur feno terrae quidquid 955Cpro magno habetur in saeculo.

VERS. 17.-- Sit nomen ejus benedictum, etc. (CAS.) Monet omnes laudes ei dicere, quia omnes in eo benedicentur. Ante solem. (ID.) Id est, ante omnem creaturam, ne putes temporalem Dei Filium. Omnes gentes. (AUG.) Ne tribus duodecim accipias, addit omnes gentes.

VERS. 18.-- Benedictus Dominus Deus Israel, etc. (AUG.) A parte sua laudat. Nota exclamatoriam benedictionem, cum admonitione et prophetia. Fiat, fiat, etc. (CAS.) Magnificum est, quod sic concludit: Optantis est semel dicere, nimium desiderantis repetere. Quasi dicat: Quod jussisti, Domine, ita fiat, fiat, donec quod coepit a flumine perveniat usque ad terminos orbis terrae. (HIER.) Sciendum quod septuagesimus 955Dprimus psalmus secundi libri finis est: unde et in extremo habet: Fiat, fiat, pro quo in Hebraeo dicitur: Amen, amen.

VERS. 20.-- Defecerunt laudes. (ID.) Etiam hoc diligentius observandum est, quod illud: Defecerunt hymni David filii Jesse, ad finem septuagesimi primi psalmi pertineat. Id vero quod sequitur: Psalmus Asaph, initium sit sequentis.

Hymnus tria habet: laudem Dei cum cantico: nisi enim cantetur hilariter, non est hymnus: non cantat autem qui non amat. Si sit laus, et non est Dei, non est hymnus: et si sit Dei, et non cum cantico, non hymnus. Praeter solitum addit: Filii Jesse; David enim homo, quidam filius Jesse, regnavit in 956AIsrael tempore Veteris Testamenti in quo Novum erat, sed occultum: sicut et Christus in David et in Abraham, sed occultus, ut fructus est in radice, sed non apparet. Noverunt autem pauci Prophetae et Christum, et Novum Testamentum, scilicet in occulto, et pronuntiaverunt revelandum. Illo ergo tempore, pro regno illo, ubi regnavit homo filius Jesse, pro hujusmodi carnalibus carnalis populus laudabat Deum. Sed regno illo et caeteris hujusmodi deficientibus, deficit laus, non Filii Dei, sed filii Jesse. His autem deficientibus quae Deus subtraxit ut quaererentur ea quae occulta in illis tegebantur, loquitur Asaph, id est Synagoga, sed fidelis, quae pie Deum coluit, licet propter terrena, quae a Deo, non a daemonibus, ut gentes, quaerebat. Attendens autem 956Bblasphemos his abundare, pro quibus serviebat, coepit nutare, nesciens quid in his figuris lateret, quasi non esset aliquid melius quod Deus daret: sed admonitus per haec sibi subtracta quaerere ea quae non habet cum malis communia, castigans se cum admiratione, dicit: Quam bonus Israel! Sed quibus? Rectis corde. Primo ergo describens nequitiam malorum, dicit se zelasse prospera eorum; tamen inde correctum, et correctus alios corrigit.

(CAS.) Hic agitur, quod laudes defecerunt: quia jam non dat Deus blanda, ut pueris ad serviendum alliciendis, et hoc dicit Synagoga quae jam sibi contra hoc quod prius agebat testatur, ut credibilius sit.

PSALM LXXI.

VERS. 1.-- Unto Solomon, etc. (AUG.) The true peaceable one, etc., as far as he who is here commended according to 954Aeach nature. (CAS.) The fourth psalm concerning the two natures of Christ admonishes that we should believe Christ, true God and true man, to be king, and it is a prophecy about Christ.

VERS. 2.-- O God, judgment. (CAS.) Concerning the judgment, in wishing that it be given to the Son. Thy justice, etc. (AUG.) Note that repetitions of the same thing, or in other words, greatly commend the divine utterances, which are chiefly in the psalms: and in that kind of speech by which the affection of the mind is to be moved.

VERS. 3.-- Mountains. (AUG.) The Prophets, the Apostles, who by their height come near to heaven; peace to be announced to the faithful people, Christ. And the hills. Let them receive justice, that is, Christ, or the mountains peace for the people: and hills he says of both sorts of preachers, those going before and 954Bthose following. Or let the mountains receive, that is, the greater ones.

Peace. The word of reconciliation, namely the word of the Gospel, to this end, that they may announce it to the people.

And the hills. That is, the lesser ones; justice, that is, obedience, that they may obey the teaching of truth.

By saying thine and thy own, he shows that all things which are the Father's are the Son's also, and conversely.

VERS. 4.-- He shall judge the poor of the people. (CAS.) He treats the same matter concerning the same judgment, by affirming it. After the wish, by the power of prophecy, he says what things are to be furnished at the Lord's coming. (AUG.) Or according to another reading: Justice shall judge the poor man. But those codices which have [it] in the letter are the more approved. The poor of the people. That is, those who are poor among the people, in which the good and the bad are 954Cmingled together. He shall humble the calumniator. For while he helps by his grace, etc., as far as he who strives to drag the innocent into guilt. (HIERON., AUG.) Or, he shall humble, and, the devil being conquered, there shall remain with the sun a brightness; that is, the Son with the Father, sitting at the Father's right hand for ever, that is before the moon, unto generation and generation.

VERS. 7.-- He shall come down like rain, etc. (CAS.) Behold who and of what sort is that king who is to judge. (AUG.) He alludes to the deed of Gedeon, etc., as far as and afterwards the Gentile world was rained upon, the fleece of the Jews being dry. (CAS.) Christ shall come down, etc., as far as who then, after such open likenesses, doubts of the Virgin's childbearing? Into the fleece, and like drops. (AUG.) The fleece, Judaea, which was to be despoiled of the authority of doctrine, as a sheep 954Dof its fleece: or, because it withheld the rain of doctrine, which it was unwilling to preach to the Gentiles.

VERS. 8.-- And he shall rule from sea to sea. (CAS.) He shows what the breadth of the kingdom is. From the river. (AUG.) From the Jordan, where the voice was:. This is my beloved Son. Thence therefore his teaching began: thence the authority of the master is spread as far as the ends of the earth, the Gospel of the kingdom being preached. (CAS.) Thence the rule of baptism flowed out through the whole world. In few words he teaches great sacraments.

VERS. 10.-- The kings of Tharsis and the islands shall offer presents. (CAS.) The obstinate are called enemies, etc., as far as or, it can be taken historically of the kings who came to adore Christ.

955AVERS. 12.-- For he shall deliver the poor man from the mighty, etc. (CASS.) He treats of his works, etc., as far as in the participation of justice.

VERS. 14.-- From usuries. (AUG.) Usuries, sins, etc., as far as by helping through grace to the doing of justice. Or, from usuries, concerning what is to come, that is, eternal punishments; and iniquity, that is, sin itself, for which the punishment was owed. Name. The Christian name. Before him. Because in his kingdom they shall live before him.

VERS. 15.-- And he shall live, and to him shall be given of the gold, etc. (CAS.) Concerning the honour paid to the king. Of Arabia. (AUG.) By Arabia, the Gentiles; by gold, wisdom, which excels among the teachings. Of him always. (ID.) By multiplying, or by obtaining, or concerning his institution, because he himself taught us to pray.

955BVERS. 16.-- A firmament. (AUG.) It belongs to the Prophets, because what they foretold he fulfilled. On the tops of the mountains. (ID.) The authors of the Scriptures, the Prophets and Apostles; whom he strengthens, because all things foretold by them have been fulfilled in him.

In the earth. Because for the sake of those who are on the earth all things were written. Whence he himself also came into the earth, that he might fulfil them.

Above Libanus. (AUG.) As Libanus brings forth tall cedars, so Christ brings forth saints to heaven. Like hay. (CAS.) It is not age that is compared to the old man, but greenness to the saints. The good, departing from this city of the present Church, shall flourish in that blessedness. (AUG.) In Genesis under the name of hay grain also is understood, etc., as far as and whatever 955Cis held for great in this world shall be compared to the hay of the earth corparabitur.

VERS. 17.-- Let his name be blessed, etc. (CAS.) He admonishes all to speak praises to him, because all shall be blessed in him. Before the sun. (ID.) That is, before every creature, lest thou think the Son of God temporal. All nations. (AUG.) Lest thou take it of the twelve tribes, he adds all nations.

VERS. 18.-- Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, etc. (AUG.) He praises from his own part. Note the exclamatory blessing, with admonition and prophecy. So be it, so be it, etc. (CAS.) It is a magnificent thing, that he concludes thus: it belongs to one who wishes, to say it once; to one who desires exceedingly, to repeat it. As if he said: What thou hast commanded, Lord, so let it be done, let it be done, until what began from the river may reach as far as the ends of the earth. (HIER.) It is to be known that the seventy-955Dfirst psalm is the end of the second book: whence also at the end it has: So be it, so be it, for which in the Hebrew it is said: Amen, amen.

VERS. 20.-- The praises have failed. (ID.) This also is to be observed the more diligently, that that saying: The hymns of David the son of Jesse have failed, [Vulg. Ps 71:20 laudes, "praises"] belongs to the end of the seventy-first psalm. But that which follows: A psalm of Asaph, is the beginning of the next one.

A hymn has three things: the praise of God with a song: for unless it be sung joyfully, it is not a hymn: and he does not sing who does not love. If there be praise, and it is not of God, it is not a hymn: and if it be of God, and not with a song, it is not a hymn. Beyond his custom he adds: the son of Jesse; for David, a man, a certain son of Jesse, reigned in 956AIsrael in the time of the Old Testament, in which the New was, but hidden: just as Christ also was in David and in Abraham, but hidden, as the fruit is in the root, yet does not appear. Now few of the Prophets knew both Christ and the New Testament, namely in secret, and they declared that it was to be revealed. In that time, therefore, for that kingdom in which the man, the son of Jesse, reigned, for carnal things of this sort a carnal people praised God. But that kingdom and the rest of this sort failing, the praise fails, not of the Son of God, but of the son of Jesse. And these things failing which God withdrew, that those things might be sought which lay hidden in them, Asaph speaks, that is, the Synagogue, but a faithful one, which piously worshipped God, although for the sake of earthly things, which it sought from God, not from demons, as the Gentiles did. But observing 956Bblasphemers to abound in these things, for the sake of which it served, it began to waver, not knowing what lay hidden in these figures, as though there were not anything better which God might give: but admonished by these things withdrawn from it to seek those things which it does not have in common with the wicked, chastising itself with wonder, it says: How good is Israel! But to whom? To the upright in heart. [Vulg. Ps 72:1 his qui recto sunt corde, "to them that are of a right heart"] First therefore, describing the wickedness of the wicked, it says that it was jealous of their prosperity; yet corrected from that, and being corrected it corrects others.

(CAS.) Here it is treated, that the praises have failed: because God now does not give pleasant things, as to boys who are to be enticed to serve; and this the Synagogue says, which now bears witness against itself against that which it did before, that it may be the more credible.

PSALMUS LXXII.

956CVERS. 1.-- Quam bonus. (CAS.) Monet ut non pro temporalibus, sed aeternis Deum laudemus.

VERS. 2.-- Pedes. (CAS.) Pro arbitrio mentis, quod a veritate discrepabat. Gressus, actus praecipitati; pene, quia cito rediit.

VERS. 3, 4.-- Pacem peccatorum. (AUG.) Temporalem, fluxam, caducam. Videns. Non intelligens. Quia haec pax videtur, non intelligitur, oculos eludit, est enim fluxa et caduca. (CAS.) Pacem peccatorum quia non est declinatio morti eorum. Id est, non cito moriuntur, sed diu vivunt; etsi plaga aliquando non firma, ut durat flagellum correctionis. Et firmamentum in plaga eorum. Non miseretur Deus consolidando plagas eorum: vel, a simili incurabilis, 956Dcui nihil prohibetur.

VERS. 6.-- Operti sunt iniquitate et impietate sua. (CAS.) Ne resipiscant : non amicti, ut vel liberum caput haberent, sed toti operti.

VERS. 7.-- Prodiit quasi, etc. (AUG.) Sunt quidam mali ex macie, id est, necessitate: alii ex abundantia, ut pauper egestate furatur, dives ex cupiditate. Transierunt. (CAS.) Quasi a rectis semitis.

VERS. 8.-- In excelso. (AUG.) Palam in manifesto: vel, contra Deum blasphemi.

VERS. 9.-- In coelum. (ID.) Ac si dii essent; vel, contra Deum, quem blasphemant, dicentes: Deum vel nescire sua mala, vel non punire. Lingua transivit super terram, etc. (ID.) Quae ultra mensuram humanitatis 957Aloquitur, etc., usque ad sed transit lingua eorum humanam fragilitatem.

VERS. 10.-- Ideo convertetur. (CAS.) Exponens Asaph, etc., usque ad revertetur ad eam. Hic. (AUG.) In hac sententia in qua modo sum. Dies pleni invenientur in eis. (HIERON.) Perfecti inveniuntur, etsi modo non appareat. (CAS.) Vel, dies pleni sunt, quando Christus venit: hi ergo sunt in Judaeis, qui Christum noverunt.

VERS. 11.-- Et dixerunt. (AUG.) Unde convertentur? etc., usque ad hoc est quare videbatur eis nescire hoc. Quomodo scit. (ID.) Non dicit, nescit: sed adhuc haesitat et prope est sanitati: et de tam gravi infirmitate vicinior est salus, sicut vicina sanitate magis aestuant aegri.

957BVERS. 13.-- Et dixi: Ergo sine causa justificavi cor meum, etc. (CAS.) Haec dixerunt, quibus confutandis haec ego: vel adhuc ex persona dubitantis. Fatuis cogitationibus se dicit illusum, ut cum haec repudiaverit, melius nos procuraverit.

VERS. 14.-- Et castigatio. Alias et index meus in matutino. (CAS.) Ecce jam remedium, Christus index, qui viam veritatis indicavit, et, mane surgens, spem nostram de mundo ad coelos transtulit.

VERS. 15.-- Si dicebam. (ID.) Ecce jam se reprimit auctoritate sanctorum, et jam vicina veritate deliberat sic: Si dicebam. Ecce nationem. (AUG.) Aliud inconveniens incipit solvere. Reprobavi; judicavi quod non est. Existimabam, per praedicta volo probare Deum non justum; sed hoc modo cogito, non 957Cabsolvo. Ante me, id est, quantum ad praesentia; vel, major me, me superans, nisi Deus aperiat. Vel, ecce natio filiorum tuorum, cui disposui, et concinui, subaudis, occurrit et obvia mihi, id est, occurrit mihi prior praedicatio, quam Israelitis feci, ut Deum colerent, qui omnia creavit, et omnibus secundum opera sua restituit: obviat mihi doctrina, cui congrui, et accommodatus sum. Sed ne ego reprobarem nationem priorum patrum, vel priori doctrinae meae contradicerem: Existi, etc.

Filiorum tuorum. Omnes enim, Abraham et caeteri, aliter docent, quibus credere debeo: non enim omnibus prudentior. Sed ne reprobarem: Existimabam, vel, suscepi cognoscere; jam revocatur a lapsu, qui non praesumit se scientem contra sanctos. Ut cognoscerem 957Dhujus rei veritatem, quod non ante, dum dicebat Deum haec non curare. Cogitabam ut scirem hoc: prior gradus scientiae, dum scit nescire se, quod prius videbatur scire: repudiat autem priorem sensum, dum quaerit alium.

VERS. 16.-- Labor est ante me. (AUG.) Quasi murus mihi obstat, etc., usque ad videt in judicio illos damnatos.

VERS. 17.-- Sanctuarium. (AUG.) Christus, qui ut Deus singulorum merita dignoscit. Vel sanctuarium, Sancta sanctorum, id est, secretum divinae dispositionis.

VERS. 17.-- Verumtamen. (AUG., CASS.) Ecce quid didicit iste in sanctuario: malos hic decipi, postea 958Ain fine ab omnibus deserendos; a quo malo ipse liberatus est, qui et terrena quaesivit, sed a Deo; hic dicit, in hoc mundo malos non esse immunes et impunitos; quia etsi felices, tamen reatum gestant et frequenter ruinas incurrunt. Verumtamen, id est, sed: et hic posuisti eis hunc florem et copiam temporalium, propter dolos, etc.

Propter dolos. (AUG.) Vel, juxta lubricum. Quasi: Modo doloso fecisti eis, sub specie boni dans mala. Vel, juxta lubricum, ut sunt temporalia: ubi cadunt, qui amore sunt juxta; dum enim dolosus alium vult dejicere, juxta lubricum eum ponit.

VERS. 20.-- Velut somnium. (ID.) Aperta comparatio. Clausis oculis, videmus bona quae mo apertis non invenimus; in vita somnium: in morte evigilant, 958Bscientes quid est. In civitate. In contuitu populi tui, vel, dum constituitur tua civitas. (HIER.) Vel in coelesti Jerusalem imaginem eorum, effigies deformitatum quas sibi faciunt: alius leo ferocitate, alius aper sorde libidinis. (CAS.) Vel gloriam temporis, quae non vera, sed similitudo gloriae: quia cum deerit veritas eis, peribit imago; nec similitudinem retinebunt, qui de beatitudine nil habebunt, ideo perdes eos, quia per eos.

VERS. 21.-- Inflammatum est cor meum. Id est, invidi felicibus. Et renes mei commutati sunt. Quibus status, id est, constantia mentis resoluta est, ut prospera amarem; gravis culpa praebere aliis occasionem peccandi. Ad nihilum redactus sum. Vanis haerens, injurius Deo factus. Nescivi. Magna et profunda 958Cignorantia nescire quod pecces. (CAS.) In civitate tua imaginem. Vel de haereticis potest hoc accipi, etc., usque ad vel in super coelesti Ecclesia. Quia inflammatum. (AUG.) Ecce conversio hujus Asaph, etc., usque ad commutatae sunt in spirituales

VERS. 24.-- Cum, etc. (ID.) Quia prius ad nihilum redactus sum, id est, ad ea quae nihil sunt descendi: qui nescivi nihil esse, et post ut jumentum mansuetus factus sum ferendo oneri, et semper ero tecum.

Jumentum. (CAS.) Apud Deum, vice pecudum sunt, qui contra Deum sentiunt: et tamen in his errans, nesciens judicia Dei, semper fui tecum quodammodo, ab idolis alienus, et tibi credens, et tu tenuisti.

Tenuisti manum. (AUG.) Quia licet pecus non recessit 958Da Deo. Tenuisti manum, id est, potestatem dexterae, id est, texisti, quod semper tecum, quod filius. Dedit enim potestatem filios Dei fieri his qui credunt in nomine ejus. In sinistra, pecus, amans haec temporalia. Vel manum dexteram.

(CAS.) Non sinistram. Tenet dexteram Deus, dum ad bona opera dirigit, et ne mergamur liberat, ut Petrum. (ID.) Viso malo impiorum, bonoque suo, arguit se de prioribus, quod terrena a Deo quaesivit, et invitat in contrarium.

(AUG.) Comparat terrenae voluptati suae praemium coeleste, et se arguit.

In aeternum, etc. Ab eo nunquam ultra separabor.

Qui fornicantur abs te, etc. Huic fornicationi contrarius 959Aest castus timor, qui gratis ipsum amat, in quo habet omnia.

VERS. 28.-- In portis filiae Sion. (AUG.) In publico, vel in concordia Apostolorum, qui sunt portae Ecclesiae. Quia praedicatio, quae est praeter unitatem Ecclesiae, inanis est. Vel, virtutibus Ecclesia est filia Sion, id est, speculationis.

PSALM LXXII.

956CVERS. 1.-- How good. (CAS.) He admonishes that we should praise God not for temporal things, but for eternal ones.

VERS. 2.-- Feet. (CAS.) For the judgment of the mind, which was at variance with the truth. Steps, headlong acts; almost, because he quickly returned.

VERS. 3, 4.-- The peace of sinners. (AUG.) Temporal, fleeting, perishable. Seeing. Not understanding. Because this peace is seen, it is not understood, it eludes the eyes, for it is fleeting and perishable. (CAS.) The peace of sinners, for there is no turning aside to their death. [Vulg. Ps 72:4 quia non est respectus morti eorum, "no regard for their death"] That is, they do not die quickly, but live long; although a stroke is sometimes not firm, as the scourge of correction lasts. And a firmament in their stroke. God does not have mercy by consolidating their strokes: or, by a likeness, that of an incurable man, 956Dto whom nothing is forbidden.

VERS. 6.-- They are covered with their iniquity and impiety. (CAS.) Lest they come to their senses; not merely wrapped about, so as at least to have the head free, but wholly covered.

VERS. 7.-- Their iniquity hath come forth as it were, etc. (AUG.) There are some who are evil out of leanness, that is, out of need: others out of abundance, as the poor man steals out of want, the rich out of covetousness. They have passed over. (CAS.) As it were from the straight paths.

VERS. 8.-- On high. (AUG.) Openly, in the open: or, blasphemers against God.

VERS. 9.-- Into heaven. (ID.) As if they were gods; or, against God, whom they blaspheme, saying that God either does not know their own evils, or does not punish them. The tongue hath passed over the earth, etc. [Vulg. Ps 72:9 lingua eorum transivit in terra, "their tongue hath passed on the earth"] (ID.) Which speaks beyond the measure of humanity, 957Aetc., as far as but their tongue passes beyond human frailty.

VERS. 10.-- Therefore shall [my people] be converted. (CAS.) Expounding Asaph, etc., as far as he shall return to it. Here. (AUG.) In this opinion in which I now am. Full days shall be found in them. (HIERON.) They are found perfect, although it does not now appear. (CAS.) Or, the days are full, when Christ came: these therefore are among the Jews, who have known Christ.

VERS. 11.-- And they said. (AUG.) Whence shall they be converted? etc., as far as this is why it seemed to them that he did not know this. How doth he know. (ID.) He does not say, He knows not: but he still hesitates and is near to health: and from so grave an infirmity health is the nearer, just as the sick are more feverish when health is at hand.

957BVERS. 13.-- And I said: Then have I in vain justified my heart, etc. (CAS.) These things they said, for the confuting of whom I say these: or still in the person of one doubting. He says that he was deluded by foolish thoughts, so that, when he shall have repudiated them, he may the better provide for us.

VERS. 14.-- And chastisement. Otherwise also my discloser in the morning. (CAS.) Behold now the remedy, Christ the discloser, who disclosed the way of truth, and, rising in the morning, transferred our hope from the world to the heavens.

VERS. 15.-- If I said. (ID.) Behold, now he restrains himself by the authority of the saints, and now, with the truth near at hand, he deliberates thus: If I said. Behold the nation. (AUG.) He begins to resolve another incongruity. I have reproved; I judged that which is not. I thought, by the things aforesaid I wish to prove God not just; but in this manner I think, I do not 957Cabsolve. Before me, that is, as regards present things; or, greater than I, surpassing me, unless God open it. Or, behold the nation of thy sons, to which I have appointed, and with which I have sung together, understand it, meets and is over against me [obvia; read obviat, "meets"], that is, my former preaching meets me, which I made to the Israelites, that they should worship God, who created all things, and who renders to all according to their works: the teaching comes against me, to which I agreed and to which I was fitted. But lest I should reprove the nation of the former fathers, or contradict my former teaching: I thou[ght], etc.

Of thy sons. For all, Abraham and the rest, teach otherwise, whom I ought to believe: for I am not wiser than all. But lest I should reprove: I thought, or, I undertook to know; he is now called back from his fall, who does not presume himself to be knowing against the saints. That I might know 957Dthe truth of this matter, which I did not before, while he was saying that God did not care for these things. I was thinking that I might know this: the first degree of knowledge, when a man knows that he does not know what he seemed before to know: and he repudiates the former sense, while he seeks another.

VERS. 16.-- Labour is before me. (AUG.) As it were a wall stands in my way, etc., as far as he sees them condemned in the judgment.

VERS. 17.-- The sanctuary. (AUG.) Christ, who as God discerns the merits of each. Or the sanctuary, the Holy of holies, that is, the secret of the divine disposition.

VERS. 17.-- But yet. (AUG., CASS.) Behold what this man learned in the sanctuary: that the wicked are deceived here, and afterwards 958Aat the end are to be forsaken by all; from which evil he himself was freed, who also sought earthly things, but from God; here he says that in this world the wicked are not free and unpunished; because although they are happy, yet they bear guilt and frequently run into ruins. But yet, that is, but: and here thou hast set for them this flower and abundance of temporal things, because of deceits, etc.

Because of deceits. (AUG.) Or, beside a slippery place. As if: In a deceitful manner thou hast dealt with them, giving evils under the appearance of good. Or, beside a slippery place, such as temporal things are: where they fall who are near by love; for while a deceitful man wishes to cast down another, he sets him beside a slippery place.

VERS. 20.-- As a dream. (ID.) An open comparison. With our eyes closed we see goods which presently, when they are opened, we do not find mo; in life a dream: in death they awake, 958Bknowing what it is. In the city. In the sight of thy people, or, while thy city is being established. (HIER.) Or in the heavenly Jerusalem their image, the likenesses of the deformities which they make for themselves: one a lion by ferocity, another a boar by the filth of lust. (CAS.) Or the glory of time, which is not true, but a likeness of glory: because when truth shall be wanting to them, the image shall perish; nor shall they retain the likeness, who shall have nothing of blessedness, therefore thou wilt destroy them, because through them,

VERS. 21.-- My heart hath been inflamed. That is, I envied the happy. And my reins have been changed. By which the standing, that is, the constancy of the mind, was dissolved, so that I loved prosperity; it is a grave fault to afford to others an occasion of sinning. I am brought to nothing. Clinging to vain things, made injurious to God. I knew not. It is a great and deep 958Cignorance not to know that thou sinnest. (CAS.) In thy city the image. Or this can be taken of the heretics, etc., as far as or in the supercelestial Church. For it hath been inflamed. (AUG.) Behold the conversion of this Asaph, etc., as far as they have been changed into spiritual ones

VERS. 24.-- With, etc. (ID.) Because before I was brought to nothing, that is, I went down to those things which are nothing: because I knew not that it was nothing, and afterwards I was made gentle as a beast of burden for the bearing of a load, and I shall always be with thee.

A beast of burden. (CAS.) With God they are in the place of cattle, who think against God: and yet, erring in these things, not knowing the judgments of God, I was always with thee in a manner, a stranger to idols, and believing thee, and thou didst hold me.

Thou hast held my hand. (AUG.) Because, although a beast, he did not depart 958Dfrom God. Thou hast held my hand, that is, the power of the right hand, that is, thou hast covered him, in that he is always with thee, in that he is a son. He gave, indeed, power to be made the sons of God to them that believe in his name. On the left, a beast, loving these temporal things. Or the right hand.

(CAS.) Not the left. God holds the right hand, while he directs to good works, and delivers us lest we be drowned, as he did Peter. (ID.) Having seen the evil of the impious, and his own good, he accuses himself of his former state, because he sought earthly things from God, and he invites to the contrary.

(AUG.) He compares the heavenly reward with his own earthly pleasure, and accuses himself.

For ever, etc. From him I shall never be separated any more.

Who go a-fornicating from thee, etc. Contrary to this fornication 959Ais chaste fear, which loves him freely, in whom it has all things.

VERS. 28.-- In the gates of the daughter of Sion. (AUG.) In public, or in the concord of the Apostles, who are the gates of the Church. Because preaching which is outside the unity of the Church is empty. Or, by virtues the Church is the daughter of Sion, that is, of contemplation.

PSALMUS LXXIII.

VERS. 1.-- Intellectus Asaph. (AUG.) Synagogae, etc., usque ad ut duritia Judaeorum vel calamitatibus terreretur, vel molliretur. (CAS.) Monet, relictis figuris, transire ad veritatem.

Ut quid Deus. (ID.) Describens eversionem Jerusalem irreparabilem, quaerit causam, quare admirans et conquerens; et precatur pro repulso populo, et ultionem 959Bin destructores, quae quidem eis utilis est, et jam facta est. Repulisti nos. (ID.) Quasi alienos a tua defensione. In finem. Nec templo parcitur. Interitum et captivitatem significat, quae a Tito et Vespasiano. Oves nominat, ut pii pastoris misericordiam commoveat. Tuae. In eos temperantius vindicamus, quos aliquando fuisse nostros meminimus.

VERS. 2.-- Possedisti. (CASS.) Vel, creasti, etsi omnes creat et disponit, Judaeos tamen specialiter, quibus legem et Prophetas dedit. Redemisti. (HIER.) Te pretio, id est, per te pretium. Mons. (AUG.) Eminentia, Sion speculatio est, in quo, in qua re habitasti. Vel vacat in eo. (HIER.) Montem vel montis Sion, sive in eo. Hucusque veri Testamenti facta, quae sequitur, veritas promissa. Per Sion, Jerusalem 959Csignat, in qua praesentia Christi habitavit, et ideo ne daret eam vastitati supplicat. Virgam haereditatis. (AUG.) Ipsa congregatio, virga haereditatis dicit: quam volens possidere virgam Moysi in serpentem vertit, sed apprehensa cauda rediit in virgam. (HIER.) Quia mors suasu serpentis intravit in mundum, virga in serpente, Christus in morte. Unde et qui intuebatur serpentem, id est, Christum mortuum credit, sanatur a serpentibus, id est, a morte aeterna. Expavit Moyses et fugit, sic Apostoli moriente Christo. Retenta cauda, id est, posterioribus, fit virga, quia primo occisus, postea surrexit. Cauda etiam est finis saeculi, in quo redimus ad manum Dei, et stabilimur, qui per mortem quasi per serpentem fluximus. (AUG.) Sed quia haec et de gentibus: exprimit, de quibus 959Ddicat, Mons Sion. Id est, non de gentibus. Vel, montem Sion istum, quem inhabitasti in ipso: Leva manum tuam in superbias eorum, a quibus eversa est Jerusalem, id est, regibus gentium. In finem, quia et ipsi Christum jam noverunt.

VERS. 3.-- Leva. (CAS.) Potentiam, ut superbiam eorum vertas ad humilitatem, ducens eos in finem, id est, Christum, quod et impletum est, quia Romae Christiana religio effloruit. Leva, quia ex multum superstitiosa facta est sanctissima. Quanta malignatus est, etc. (AUG.) Sacerdotes et ministeria templi praeda fuerunt. Tota gens, vel occisa vel captivata. Inimicus, Romanus exercitus, ad hoc per prolepsim praemisit eorum.

960AVERS. 4.-- Gloriati sunt. (AUG., CASS.) De victoria sua. Ecce quod non bono zelo fecerunt. Gloriati, cum scelus soleat sequi poenitudo, hi ad gloriam vertunt; qui te oderunt, servi daemonum, qui nullatenus sunt tolerandi. In medio solemnitatis tuae. Non in extremo loco, sed in medio atrio. Alia littera, sacrilegia commiserunt. In sancto. (CAS.) In sanctuario per contemptum sancti templi, ubi Deitas videtur despici, in praesumptores concitat invidiam. Signa, etc. (AUG.) Aquilas, etc., usque ad id est, per edita loca.

VERS. 5.-- In exitu. (CAS.) Vel sicut in egressu desuper, id est, non cognoverunt, quod haec licentia a Deo egrederetur. Quasi in silva, etc. (CASS.) Antequam construeretur, prophetat eversionem templi.

In securi et ascia polluerunt tabernaculum nominis 960Btui, etc. (AUG.) Securis caedit trabes: ascia minutius persequitur. Per hoc ergo, et magnas res et minimas dicit dejectas, ut civitas funditus sit devastata, prius incisa, post ignis omnia voravit.

VERS. 7.-- In terra, etc. Usque ad terram dejecerunt culmina ad laudem Dei erecta. Auget scelus, ut atrocius vindicetur. (CAS.) Vel potest totum legi ex persona desperantium Judaeorum, etc., usque ad qui inter haec non poenitent. (AUG.) Haec dixerunt, sed usquequo pateris opprobria Judaeorum: Non hoc dixit, ut eos velit perdi, sed commutari. In finem mundi, vesperam scilicet, quando Judaei convertentur.

VERS. 9.-- Signa nostra non vidimus. (AUG., CASS.) 960CQuasi dicerent: Merito haec mala nobis contigerunt, Quia non vidimus signa; quasi dica : Vidimus, sed non intelleximus: et vere vidimus, quia hoc signum, quia non est Propheta, vel sacerdos, vel unctio; unde: Cum venerit Sanctus sanctorum, cessabit unctio (Dan. IX) vestra. Et nos non cognoscet amplius Propheta aliquis, vel Deus per Prophetam; id est, non annuntiabit Christum venturum, quia jam venit. Amplius. (ID.) Vel non cognoscet adhuc, donec scilicet Judaeus agnoscat eum.

VERS. 10.-- Usquequo? etc. (CAS.) Et quasi subito cognoverit. Usquequo, supposuit, irritat adversarius? quasi diceret: Tandiu improperabit, quandiu adversarius, id est, Judaeus, irritat nomen tuum. Ut quid avertis. (AUG.) Post signum virgae, additum 960Dest signum manus Moysi, hic est populus Dei: qui foras ab eo missus immundus est, sed revocatus redit in suum colorem. Dicit ergo: Quousque non revocas manum, ut agnoscat Salvatorem. Manum tuam et dexteram, id est, Judaeos.

VERS. 12.-- Deus autem rex noster. (CAS.) Destructis signis, ostendit rem ipsam, scilicet, in adventu Christi salutem ubique factam. (AUG.) Deus autem. Dicit Asaph intelligens, etc., uque ad si ergo non praecessit, saltem sequatur.

In medio terrae. (CAS.) Homo factus, Jerusalem dicitur esse in medio.

VERS. 13.-- Tu confirmasti. (AUG.) Lapsus maris Rubri firmavit, ut esset inter siccum. Cujus 961Amysterium subdit, quod in aquis baptismi capita immundorum spirituum annihilavit.

VERS. 14.-- Escam. (AUG.) Christus est esca, etc., usque ad vel ipsum mordent reprehendendo, accusando. (CAS.) Vel dum tentat, esca est, quia inde proficitur. Vel, populis Aethiopum. (HIERON.) Nolentibus converti dedisti eum escam, in quo delectentur.
