VERS. 15.-- Fontes et torrentes. (AUG.) In aliis fit verbum, etc., usque ad et notat abundantiam praedicationis. (CAS.) Vel totum de malis. Fontes, quorum mala jugiter influebant: Torrentes qui subito et rapide peccant: hos Deus dirumpit et siccat. Fluvii Ethan. Inundationes et consilia diaboli.

Tuus est dies et tua est nox. (AUG.) Diem illustrat 961Bsed incommutabilis sapientiae. Noctem consolatur luna, id est, carnis manifestatio: Verbum caro factum est et habitavit in nobis (Joan. I). Et item: Nox nocti indicat scientiam (Psal. XXVIII). Auroram et solem. (AUG.) Vel lunam, id est carnalem, qui ut luna mutatur, qui tamen non deserendus. Vel auroram et solem, id est initium et profectum sapientiae insipientes et perfectos.

VERS. 17.-- Tu fecisti omnes. (CAS.) Vel omnia historialiter ab hoc loco: Tuus est dies. Terminos terrae, etc. (CAS.) Apostoli et Prophetae ut termini fines distinguunt, ita hi fidei jura custodiunt: vel omnia historice.

VERS. 18.-- Memor esto. (CAS.) Jam quod ubique fit: precatur Judaeis, per numerata beneficia, pium judicem 961Cprovocat. Quasi diceret: Memor esto hujus creaturae tuae. Hujus. (AUG.) Creaturae tuae, cujus creaturae tuae? Inimicus improperavit Domino, et populus insipiens incitavit nomen tuum, etc. (AUG.) Asaph intellectu dolet pristinam caecitatem, et sic pro Judaeis orat, ut eorum confiteantur errata. Hoc orat, quod scit futurum; erant enim inter Judaeos vasa misericordiae.

VERS. 20.-- Respice in Testamentum tuum. (ID.) Reliquiae salvae fiant, quia multi, qui tendunt ad terram, obscurati sunt et repleti terra. (CAS.) Respice. Imple quae promisisti; ut Testamentum Novum, quod est de aeternis, constituas. Meminit promissionis, quia merita deficiunt. Item ideo, quia repleti sunt iniquitatibus, unde sequitur obscuritas, 961Dquia lumen sapientiae perdunt repleti iniquitatibus, quia obscurati sunt domus terrae terrena habitatione, id est, caeci amore terrenitatis.

VERS. 21.-- Ne avertatur humilis, factus confusus. (CAS.) Gratus pro odioso ponitur, ut dilectio devoti temperet odium contumacis. Confusus. (ID.) Confundi non est humilis, sed superbi, qui non Deo sed sibi attribuit.

VERS. 22.-- Exsurge, Deus. (CASS.) Jam excutit Asaph (intelligens) terrena promissa Veteris Testamenti. Causam tuam. Dicunt enim: Ubi est Deus tuus? Contemptus est a Judaeis ambulans in terra, et a falsis Christianis sedens in coelo. Judica ergo, non fallatur spes mea, qui credidi quod non vidi. Causam 962Atuam. Post omnia, facit causam judicis, cui negotii sui qualitas intimatur. Causam tuam, contra illos, qui obmurmurant, ut manifesta veritate praedicent quod stulte abnuebant. Tota die. (AUG.) Ideo dicit, ut ipsa continuatio mansuetudinem patientis judicis incitaret.

VERS. 23.-- Superbia eorum qui te oderunt. (CAS.) In fine ponit exsecrabile malum, quod est superbia.

PSALM LXXIII.

VERS. 1.-- The understanding of Asaph. (AUG.) Of the Synagogue, etc., as far as that the hardness of the Jews might either be terrified by calamities, or softened. (CAS.) He admonishes, the figures being left behind, to pass over to the truth.

Why, O God. (ID.) Describing the irreparable overthrow of Jerusalem, he asks the cause, wherefore, wondering and complaining; and he prays for the people cast off, and for vengeance 959Bupon the destroyers, which indeed is useful to them, and has already been done. Thou hast cast us off. [Vulg. Ps 73:1 Ut quid, Deus, repulisti in finem, without nos] (ID.) As it were strangers to thy protection. Unto the end. Not even the temple is spared. He signifies the destruction and the captivity, which came from Titus and Vespasian. He names sheep, that he may move the mercy of the loving shepherd. Thine. We take vengeance more temperately upon those whom we remember to have been ours at some time.

VERS. 2.-- Thou hast possessed. (CASS.) Or, thou hast created, although he creates and disposes all, yet the Jews especially, to whom he gave the law and the Prophets. Thou hast redeemed. (HIER.) Thee for a price, that is, through thee a price. Mount. (AUG.) An eminence; Sion is contemplation, in which, in which thing thou hast dwelt. Or it is redundant in it. (HIER.) The mount, or of mount Sion, or in it. Thus far the deeds of the true Testament; what follows is the truth promised. By Sion he signifies Jerusalem, 959Cin which the presence of Christ dwelt, and therefore he entreats that he give it not over to devastation. The rod of inheritance. (AUG.) That congregation itself is called the rod of inheritance: wishing to possess which, he turned the rod of Moses into a serpent, but when the tail was seized it returned into a rod. (HIER.) Because death entered into the world by the persuasion of the serpent, the rod is in the serpent, Christ in death. Whence he also who looked upon the serpent, that is, believes Christ dead, is healed from serpents, that is, from eternal death. Moses was terrified and fled, so the Apostles when Christ was dying. The tail being held, that is, the later things, it becomes a rod, because first he was slain, afterwards he rose. The tail also is the end of the world, in which we return to the hand of God, and are made stable, we who through death, as through a serpent, have flowed away. (AUG.) But because these things are also of the Gentiles, he expresses of whom he 959Dspeaks, Mount Sion. That is, not of the Gentiles. Or, this mount Sion, which thou hast inhabited in it: Lift up thy hand against their pride, [Vulg. Ps 73:3 Leva manus tuas, plural] by whom Jerusalem was overthrown, that is, the kings of the Gentiles. Unto the end, because they too have now known Christ.

VERS. 3.-- Lift up. (CAS.) Thy power, that thou mayest turn their pride to humility, leading them unto the end, that is, Christ, which also has been fulfilled, because at Rome the Christian religion flourished. Lift up, because from being exceedingly superstitious she has been made most holy. How greatly he hath done wickedly, etc. (AUG.) The priests and the ministries of the temple were plunder. The whole nation was either slain or led captive. The enemy, the Roman army; and to this end he set their beforehand by prolepsis.

960AVERS. 4.-- They have gloried. (AUG., CASS.) Of their own victory. Behold that they did it not with a good zeal. Having gloried: whereas repentance is wont to follow a crime, these turn it to glory; who hate thee, the slaves of demons, who are by no means to be tolerated. In the midst of thy solemnity. Not in the outermost place, but in the middle court. Another reading: they committed sacrileges. In the holy place. (CAS.) In the sanctuary, through contempt of the holy temple, where the Godhead seems to be despised, it stirs up ill-will against the presumptuous. Signs, etc. (AUG.) Eagles, etc., as far as that is, through the high places.

VERS. 5.-- In the going out. (CAS.) Or as in a going forth from above, that is, they did not know that this licence went forth from God. As in a wood, etc. (CASS.) Before it was built, he prophesies the overthrow of the temple.

With axe and hatchet they have defiled the tabernacle of thy name, 960Betc. [Vulg. Ps 73:6 in securi et ascia dejecerunt eam; Ps 73:7 in terra polluerunt tabernaculum nominis tui] (AUG.) The axe cuts beams: the hatchet follows up more minutely. By this therefore he says that both great things and the least were cast down, so that the city was utterly laid waste, first cut down, afterwards the fire devoured all.

VERS. 7.-- On the ground, etc. Down to the ground they cast the roofs raised for the praise of God. He magnifies the crime, that it may be more atrociously avenged. (CAS.) Or the whole can be read in the person of the despairing Jews, etc., as far as who amid these things do not repent. (AUG.) These things they said, but how long dost thou endure the reproaches of the Jews: He did not say this in order that he might wish them to perish, but to be changed. Unto the end of the world, namely the evening, when the Jews shall be converted.

VERS. 9.-- We have not seen our signs. (AUG., CASS.) 960CAs if they should say: Deservedly have these evils befallen us, Because we have not seen the signs; as if he should say: We have seen, but we have not understood dica: and truly we have seen, because this is the sign, that there is no Prophet, nor priest, nor unction; whence: When the Holy of holies shall have come, there shall cease the unction (Dan. IX) of yours. [Vulg. Dn 9:24 et impleatur visio et prophetia, et ungatur Sanctus sanctorum] And he shall no more know us, some Prophet, or God through a Prophet; that is, he shall not announce Christ as about to come, because he has already come. Any more. (ID.) Or he shall not know as yet, until, namely, the Jew acknowledge him.

VERS. 10.-- How long? etc. (CAS.) And as if he had suddenly come to know. How long, he subjoined, doth the adversary provoke? as if he should say: So long shall he reproach, as long as the adversary, that is, the Jew, provokes thy name. Why dost thou turn away. (AUG.) After the sign of the rod there was added 960Dthe sign of the hand of Moses; this is the people of God: which, sent forth outside from him, is unclean, but being called back returns into its own colour. He says therefore: How long dost thou not call back thy hand, that it may acknowledge the Saviour. Thy hand and thy right hand, that is, the Jews.

VERS. 12.-- But God is our king. (CAS.) The signs being destroyed, he shows the thing itself, namely, that in the coming of Christ salvation was made everywhere. (AUG.) But God. Asaph, understanding, says, etc., as far as uque ad if therefore he did not go before, let him at least follow.

In the midst of the earth. (CAS.) Made man; Jerusalem is said to be in the midst.

VERS. 13.-- Thou hast confirmed. (AUG.) He made firm the fallings of the Red Sea, that there might be dry ground between. Whose 961Amystery he subjoins, that in the waters of baptism he annihilated the heads of the unclean spirits.

VERS. 14.-- Meat. (AUG.) Christ is meat, etc., as far as or they bite him by reproving, by accusing. (CAS.) Or while he tempts, he is meat, because thereby profit is made. Or, to the peoples of the Ethiopians. (HIERON.) To those unwilling to be converted thou hast given him for meat, in whom they may take delight.

VERS. 15.-- Fountains and torrents. (AUG.) In others the word is made, etc., as far as and he notes the abundance of preaching. (CAS.) Or the whole of the wicked. Fountains, whose evils flowed in continually: Torrents, who sin suddenly and rapidly: these God breaks up and dries. The rivers of Ethan. The floods and counsels of the devil.

Thine is the day and thine is the night. (AUG.) He illumines the day 961Bbut of unchangeable wisdom. The moon consoles the night, that is, the manifestation of the flesh: The Word was made flesh and dwelt among us (Joan. I). And likewise: Night to night sheweth knowledge (Psal. XXVIII). The dawn and the sun. (AUG.) Or the moon, that is, the carnal man, who like the moon is changed, who nevertheless is not to be forsaken. Or the dawn and the sun, that is, the beginning and the advance of wisdom, the unwise and the perfect.

VERS. 17.-- Thou hast made all. (CAS.) Or all things historically from this place: Thine is the day. The bounds of the earth, etc. (CAS.) The Apostles and Prophets: as boundary-marks distinguish the limits, so these guard the laws of the faith: or all things historically.

VERS. 18.-- Be mindful. (CAS.) Now what is done everywhere: he prays for the Jews, and by the benefits reckoned up he provokes the merciful judge 961C. As if he should say: Be mindful of this thy creature. Of this. (AUG.) Of thy creature; of what creature of thine? The enemy hath reproached the Lord, and a foolish people hath provoked thy name, etc. (AUG.) Asaph with understanding grieves over the former blindness, and so prays for the Jews, that they may confess their errors. This he prays, which he knows will come to pass; for there were among the Jews vessels of mercy.

VERS. 20.-- Have regard to thy testament. (ID.) Let the remnant be saved, because many who tend toward the earth have been darkened and filled with earth. (CAS.) Have regard. Fulfil what thou hast promised; that thou mayest establish the New Testament, which is concerning eternal things. He calls the promise to mind, because merits are wanting. Likewise for this reason, because they have been filled with iniquities, whence darkness follows, 961Dbecause they lose the light of wisdom, being filled with iniquities, because the houses of the earth have been darkened by an earthly habitation, that is, blind through love of earthliness.

VERS. 21.-- Let not the humble be turned away, made confounded. (CAS.) The acceptable is set for the hateful, that the love of the devout may temper the hatred of the obstinate. Confounded. (ID.) To be confounded belongs not to the humble, but to the proud, who attributes not to God but to himself.

VERS. 22.-- Arise, O God. (CASS.) Now Asaph (understanding) shakes off the earthly promises of the Old Testament. Thy cause. For they say: Where is thy God? He was despised by the Jews as he walked on the earth, and by false Christians as he sits in heaven. Judge therefore; let not my hope be deceived, who have believed what I have not seen. Thy 962Acause. After all things, he makes it the judge's cause, to whom the character of his own business is made known. Thy cause, against those who murmur, that with the truth made manifest they may preach what they foolishly denied. All the day. (AUG.) He says this for this reason, that the very continuance might rouse the mildness of the patient judge.

VERS. 23.-- The pride of them that hate thee. (CAS.) At the end he sets the execrable evil, which is pride.

PSALMUS LXXIV.

VERS. 1.-- In finem, ne corrumpas, etc. (AUG.) Monet hic psalmus, etc., usque ad ut Judaei credant, non corrumpant fidem.

VERS. 2.-- Confitebimur tibi, Deus. (AUG.) Certus ergo de praemissis incipit: Confitebimur. Repetitio 962Baffirmatio est, ne poeniteat te esse confessum: unde et Dominus congeminat. Amen, amen. Fiat, fiat. Et Joseph de somno Pharaonis, qui vidit septem spicas, et totidem steriles. Et septem boves pingues et totidem macilentas. (CAS.) Repetitio confirmatio est ad significationem veritatis. Sufficeret unum ad significationem firmitatis, accessit alterum. Confiteri peccata vel semel terreno judici mortem inducit, sed Deo frequens confessio vitam? Inde invocatio, post narratio; unde sequitur: Narrabimus. Invocabimus nomen tuum. (ID.) Post confessionem potest invocari Deus, in hominem sic mundatum: et sicut per confessionem evacuatur a malis, sic per invocationem impletur bonis.

Nafrubimus mirabilia tua, etc. (CAS.) Terretur 962Csuperbus judicio, etc., usque ad in cujus persona subditur:

VERS. 3.-- Cum accepero tempus, secundum hominem accipit, quod ipse Deus dat, id est, potestatem judicium faciendi. Justitias. Judicandi igitur ante precentur absolvi.

VERS. 4.-- Liquefacta est terra. (CAS.) Ostendit omnes inexcusabiles in judicio, per hoc, quod praemisit Apostolos et Prophetas. Terra et omnes. (AUG.) Prius firma, in diversas diffluit concupiscentias. Vel, terra prius vitiis constricta, flante Spiritu sancto, liquefacta est, ut germina virtutum emitteret.

VERS. 5.-- Inique agere. (AUG.) Malum est peccare; pejus est perseverare, perniciosus defendendo 962Dse, in Deum culpam refundere. Nolite exaltare cornu. (CAS.) Maximum est vitium excusationis, quasi cornu erigit qui peccata sua per alios nititur excusare, ut per diabolorum persuasiones, vel per necessitatem stellarum.

VERS. 6.-- Loqui. Ut qui non sua culpa, sed necessitate stellarum, dicunt se peccasse, ut Deo, non sibi imputetur. Vel, qui sciunt peccata sua, sed impunitatem sibi promittunt.

VERS. 7.-- Quia neque ab oriente. (CAS.) Cur haec? quia judex talis est, qui vitari non potest: quia ubique est; Deus enim est. (AUG.) De nullo loco divisim judicat, qui ubique praesens est ut Deus. (CAS.) Mystice. Oriens, quibus sol justitiae 963Aoritur, etc., usque ad quia Deus praesens et cognitor est.

VERS. 9.-- Quia calix. (AUG.) Calix, lex et omnis Scriptura, etc., usque ad quod ante, et hunc exaltat. (CAS.) Calix, lex; vinum merum, mysterium coeleste, etc., usque ad non solum Judaei.

VERS. 10.-- Ego autem annuntiabo in saeculum: cantabo Deo Jacob. (CAS.) Omnes bibent, sed seorsum: ego, id est Christus, cum corpore, annuntiabo in saeculum quandiu saeculum erit.

VERS. 1.-- Cornua justi, id est, munera Christi, quae sunt sublimitas justi.

PSALM LXXIV.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end, destroy not, etc. (AUG.) This psalm admonishes, etc., as far as that the Jews may believe, and not corrupt the faith.

VERS. 2.-- We will praise thee, O God. (AUG.) Certain therefore of what has gone before, he begins: We will praise. Repetition 962Bis affirmation, lest it repent thee of having confessed: whence the Lord too doubles it. Amen, amen. So be it, so be it. And Joseph concerning the dream of Pharao, who saw seven ears of corn, and as many barren ones. And seven fat oxen and as many lean. (CAS.) Repetition is confirmation for the signifying of truth. One would suffice for the signifying of firmness; a second was added. To confess sins even once to an earthly judge brings in death, but frequent confession to God, life? Thence invocation, afterwards narration; whence follows: We will narrate. We will call upon thy name. (ID.) After confession God can be called upon, into a man thus cleansed: and as by confession he is emptied of evils, so by invocation he is filled with good things.

We will narrate Nafrubimus thy wonders, etc. (CAS.) The proud man is terrified 962Cby the judgment, etc., as far as in whose person it is subjoined:

VERS. 3.-- When I shall take a time, he receives after the manner of man what God himself gives, that is, the power of executing judgment. Justices. Therefore let those who are to be judged pray beforehand to be absolved.

VERS. 4.-- The earth is melted. (CAS.) He shows all to be inexcusable in the judgment, through this, that he sent before the Apostles and Prophets. The earth and all. (AUG.) Firm before, it flows away into divers concupiscences. Or, the earth, bound before by vices, when the Holy Spirit blew, was melted, that it might send forth the buds of virtues.

VERS. 5.-- To do wickedly. (AUG.) It is evil to sin; it is worse to persevere; pernicious, by defending 962Doneself, to pour back the fault upon God. Lift not up your horn. (CAS.) The vice of excusing is the greatest; he as it were raises a horn who strives to excuse his own sins through others, as through the persuasions of devils, or through the necessity of the stars.

VERS. 6.-- To speak. As those who say that they have sinned not by their own fault, but by the necessity of the stars, that it may be imputed to God, not to themselves. Or, those who know their own sins, but promise themselves impunity.

VERS. 7.-- For neither from the east. (CAS.) Why these things? because the judge is such that he cannot be avoided: because he is everywhere; for he is God. (AUG.) He judges from no place separately, who is everywhere present as God. (CAS.) Mystically. The east, those for whom the sun of justice 963Arises, etc., as far as because God is present and is a knower.

VERS. 9.-- For a cup. (AUG.) The cup, the law and all Scripture, etc., as far as what went before, and he exalteth this one. (CAS.) A cup, the law; pure wine, the heavenly mystery, etc., as far as not only the Jews.

VERS. 10.-- But I will declare for ever: I will sing to the God of Jacob. (CAS.) All shall drink, but severally: I, that is Christ, with the body, will declare for ever, as long as the world shall be.

VERS. 1.-- The horns of the just, that is, the gifts of Christ, which are the loftiness of the just.

PSALMUS LXXV.

VERS. 1.-- Canticum. Quia agit de bonis Christi, 963Bscilicet quod notus, quod habitat, quod illuminat, quod salvat. Frangit gloriam Judaeorum. Ad Assyrios. (CAS.) Contra Judaeos, qui non dirigentes, sed errantes. Vel, quod erigunt se, quia sine gratia quaerunt salutem et persequuntur Ecclesiam, ut olim Assyrii Judaeos. Qui confutantur hic ablatis nominibus gloriae, et nihil posse sine gratia probantur.

VERS. 2.-- Notus in Judaea. (AUG.) Gloriatur Judaeus, quod Judaeo notus est Deus, et verum est; sed Judaeo intus, non in carne. (AUG.) Propheta; si Judaei, tunc in vobis notus est Deus: quod si non est, tunc non Judaei. In Judaea. (ID.) Susceptis filiis Joseph duobus, cum reliquis undecim filiis Jacob duodecim tribus sunt, exspecta tribu Levi, quae sacerdotalis, et de decimis vivebat. Duodecim tribubus terra 963Cdivisa est. In his una est Juda, unde reges, et a regno omnes Judaei dicuntur. Confessi sunt Caesarem, non Christum, qui de Juda jam non Judaei.

VERS. 3.-- In Sion. (AUG.) Congruum verborum ordinem attende: Judaea confessio; postquam, Israel, id est, videns Deum, et sic in pacato cum Deo locus est: unde sequitur: In pace, post in Sion, id est in contemplatione (cum facie ad faciem videbit Deum), erit habitatio.

VERS. 4.-- Ibi confregit potentias. (CAS.) In Judaea, in Israel, in Salem, in Sion, ubi Deus pacis auctor venit, haec omnia (quae et nomina gloriae eorum) fugiunt.

VERS. 5.-- Illuminans tu mirabiliter a montibus aeternis turbati sunt, etc. Diapsalma. Illuminat Christus, 963Ddormit Judaeus, Christus judicat, perit ille. (AUG.) Tu illuminas, sed per montes, qui prius lumen excipiunt per Prophetas, scilicet, et Apostolos. Sed de illuminatione turbati sunt omnes insipientes corde. Praemittit inde quare in futuro terribilis, etc. Dormierunt. (CASS.) A bonis aeternis refrigescentes, carni acquieverunt, profutura non videntes. Somnum suum, qui distat a quiete bonorum: quia iste fallax est; videntes per somnium se habere thesauros, dum evigilant nihil inveniunt, unde dicit: Et nihil invenerunt omnes viri divitiarum. Definitio avarorum. Nihil invenerunt. Quia nihil posuerunt in manibus Christi, qui dicit: Esurivi, etc. (REM.) In pauperibus namque esuriit, qui in coelo dives est. Viri divitiarum. 964AQui solam spem suam ponunt in incerto divitiarum. Unde non ait, habentes divitias: Multi enim habent qui non amant. In manibus, etc. (CAS.) Quasi adhuc in manibus quaerant, cum se jam nihil tenuisse cognoscant.

VERS. 7.-- Ab increpatione, etc. (AUG.) Strepitus increpationis solet excitare, sed tantum pondus est increpantis Dei, quod dormitant, id est, cor habent induratum. Qui ascenderunt. (ID.) Quorum superbia crevit, humili Christo non humiliati. Equos. (CAS.) Quaslibet saeculares extollentias: unde praeceptum erat in lege filiis Israel, ut non multiplicarent sibi equos. Salomon quoque de Judaea non habebat equos, sed emebat de Aegypto.

VERS. 9.-- De coelo auditum. (AUG.) Unde Apostolus: 964BIn revelatione Domini nostri Jesu de coelo cum angelis venient ad judicium exercendum (I Thes. I).

VERS. 10.-- Cum exsurgeret, id est, cum potens apparebit, qui hic humilis. Vel, cum exsurgeret hic a morte, postea venturus ad judicium. (AUG.) Quando veniens de coelo facies auditum, id est, omnibus notum. Virtus judicii exponitur, unde terreni terrentur, et perdita potestate quiescunt; quievit, cum exsurgeret. Mansuetos terrae. (ID.) Qui mentis pacem habent, non detractantes jugum Dei.

VERS. 11.-- Quoniam cogitatio. (CAS.) Diapsalma. Admonet jam devotos offerre vota. Quasi, merito salvat mansuetos. Quoniam cogitatio, id est, laudabunt te cogitatione et opere, hoc est, reliquiae cogitationis, 964Cetc. Cogitatio hominis. (ID.) Conceptio voti. Reliquiae, redditio voti, operatio, reliqua post cogitationem. Reliquiae cogitationis. (AUG.) Quoniam cogitatio prima, etc., usque ad quod est solemnia celebrare. (CAS.) Quia solus Dominus est, cui festivitas debetur: reddent vota Deo. Prima cogitatio damnat mala. Reliquia. Quia post semper debet homo recordari praeterita mala, ut lugeat: licet mundus hic agat diem festum, quando sentit se peccato liberum, ut post emendationem Judaei jubentur offerre festivum munus Deo.

VERS. 12.-- Vovete et reddite. (AUG.) Alia sunt communia vota de his, sine quibus non est salus; alia propria, ut vovere castitatem, et hujusmodi. (CAS.) Vovete. Quaedam sunt, quae nec promittentes 964Ddebemus solvere: ut: Non occides, et hujusmodi, etc., usque ad qui in circuitu sunt, ut famuli offerent, vel offerant, etc. (AUG.) Sunt quasi medii, etc., usque ad habens spiritum Dei, non principum, id est superbum. Munera. (ID.) Qui altaribus offeruntur. Terribili et ei qui aufert. Quem timent boni, mali vero non timent. Spiritum principum. (CAS.) Superbiae vel timoris tollit, et facit renes sui, qui corpus suum moderantur.

PSALM LXXV.

VERS. 1.-- A canticle. Because it treats of the good things of Christ, 963Bnamely that he is known, that he dwelleth, that he enlighteneth, that he saveth. It breaks the glory of the Jews. To the Assyrians. (CAS.) Against the Jews, who are not directing themselves, but erring. Or, because they raise themselves up, since without grace they seek salvation and persecute the Church, as of old the Assyrians persecuted the Jews. And these are here confuted, the names of glory being taken away, and are proved to be able to do nothing without grace.

VERS. 2.-- Known in Judea. (AUG.) The Jew glories that God is known to the Jew, and it is true; but to the Jew within, not in the flesh. (AUG.) The Prophet: if ye are Jews, then God is known among you: but if he is not, then ye are not Jews. In Judea. (ID.) The two sons of Joseph being taken up, with the remaining eleven sons of Jacob there are twelve tribes, await [exspecta; read excepta, "the tribe of Levi being excepted"] the tribe of Levi, which was priestly, and lived on the tithes. Among twelve tribes the land 963Cwas divided. Among these one is Juda, whence the kings, and from the kingdom all are called Jews. They confessed Caesar, not Christ, and being of Juda they are now not Jews.

VERS. 3.-- In Sion. (AUG.) Mark the fitting order of the words: Judea is confession; after that, Israel, that is, seeing God, and thus there is a place in one at peace with God: whence follows: In peace, after in Sion, that is in contemplation (when he shall see God face to face), there shall be a habitation.

VERS. 4.-- There he broke the powers. (CAS.) In Judea, in Israel, in Salem, in Sion, where God the author of peace came, all these things (which are also the names of their glory) flee away.

VERS. 5.-- Thou enlightening wonderfully from the everlasting hills, they were troubled, etc. Diapsalma. Christ enlightens, 963Dthe Jew sleeps, Christ judges, that man perishes. (AUG.) Thou enlightenest, but through the mountains, who first receive the light, namely through the Prophets and the Apostles. But from the enlightening all the foolish of heart were troubled. He sets down thence why he is terrible in the time to come, etc. They have slept. (CASS.) Growing cold from eternal goods, they acquiesced in the flesh, not seeing the things that would profit them. Their sleep, which differs from the rest of the good: because this one is deceitful; seeing in a dream that they have treasures, when they awake they find nothing, whence he says: And all the men of riches have found nothing. The definition of the covetous. They have found nothing. Because they placed nothing in the hands of Christ, who says: I was hungry, etc. (REM.) For he hungered in the poor, who in heaven is rich. Men of riches. 964AWho place their only hope in the uncertainty of riches. Whence he does not say, having riches: for many have who do not love. In their hands, etc. (CAS.) As though they still sought in their hands, when they now know that they have held nothing.

VERS. 7.-- At the rebuke, etc. (AUG.) The noise of a rebuke is wont to arouse, but so great is the weight of the God who rebukes, that they slumber, that is, they have a hardened heart. Who have mounted. (ID.) Whose pride grew, not humbled by the humble Christ. Horses. (CAS.) Any secular exaltations whatsoever: whence it had been commanded in the law to the children of Israel, that they should not multiply horses to themselves. Solomon too had no horses from Judea, but used to buy them from Egypt.

VERS. 9.-- Hearing from heaven. (AUG.) Whence the Apostle: 964BIn the revelation of our Lord Jesus from heaven they shall come with angels to execute judgment (I Thes. I). [Vulg. 2Thes 1:7 in revelatione Domini Jesu de caelo cum angelis virtutis ejus, "with the angels of his power"]

VERS. 10.-- When he should rise up, that is, when he shall appear as mighty, who here was humble. Or, when he should rise up here from death, afterwards to come to judgment. (AUG.) When, coming from heaven, thou shalt make a hearing, that is, [make it] known to all. The power of the judgment is set forth, whence earthly men are terrified, and, their power lost, are still; it was still, when he should rise up. The meek of the earth. (ID.) Who have peace of mind, not refusing the yoke of God.

VERS. 11.-- For the thought. (CAS.) Diapsalma. He now admonishes the devout to offer vows. As if: deservedly he saves the meek. For the thought, that is, they shall praise thee in thought and in work, that is, the remainders of the thought, 964Cetc. The thought of man. (ID.) The conception of a vow. The remainders, the rendering of the vow, the working, the things remaining after the thought. The remainders of the thought. (AUG.) Since the first thought, etc., as far as which is to celebrate solemnities. (CAS.) Because the Lord alone is he to whom festivity is owed: they shall render vows to God. The first thought condemns evils. A remainder. Because afterwards a man ought always to remember past evils, that he may mourn: although the clean man here keeps a feast-day, when he feels himself free from sin, as after amendment the Jews are commanded to offer a festal gift to God.

VERS. 12.-- Vow ye and pay. (AUG.) Some vows are common, concerning those things without which there is no salvation; others proper, as to vow chastity, and things of this kind. (CAS.) Vow ye. There are certain things which, not even promising them, 964Dwe ought to fulfil: as, Thou shalt not kill, and things of this kind, etc., as far as who are round about, that as servants they shall offer, or let them offer, etc. (AUG.) There are, as it were, middling ones, etc., as far as having the spirit of God, not of princes, that is, a proud spirit. Gifts. (ID.) Which are offered upon the altars. To him that is terrible and to him that taketh away. Whom the good fear, but the wicked do not fear. The spirit of princes. (CAS.) He takes away the spirit of pride or of fear, and makes them reins of his own, who govern their own body.

PSALMUS LXXVI.

VERS. 1.-- In finem pro Idithum. (AUG.) Congregatio loquitur transiliens, ut perveniat ad finem, qui est Christus. Docet igitur desideria et illecebras mundi calcare, nihil sibi praeponere, nisi ex quo sunt 965Aomnia. (CAS.) Transcendens omnia, Deum quaerit et invenit.

VERS. 2.-- Voce mea ad Dominum clamavi. (AUG.) Intentione devotionis ad Dominum non aliud ab eo petens, quia Dominus, et quia Deus. Vox mea ad eum. Ad hoc est vox, propter quod editur, hoc addit, ne putetur propter aliud clamare ad Deum, quam propter ipsum, supra quem nihil est. (CAS.) Non dicit quid petat, quia non opus est dici ei, qui novit quod expedit. Intendit mihi. (CAS.) Intendere Dei est dare totum quod petitur, et plusquam petatur.

VERS. 3.-- In die tribulationis exquisivi. (AUG.) Quomodo exquisisti? etc., usque ad qui non facit justitiam coram hominibus, ut videatur. Renuit consolari. (ID.) Exponit tribulationem, etc., usque ad 965Bqui in omnibus hominibus scandalum vel invenit, vel timet, in nullo securus est.

VERS. 4.-- Et exercitatus sum. (AUG.) Vel, garrivi, id est, exsultavi, loquendo ut garrulus, qui, prae laetitia, nec vellet nec posset tacere: et rursus in garriendo defecit spiritus, qui prius contabuerat taedio malorum.

VERS. 5.-- Anticipaverunt vigilias. (CAS.) Diapsalma. Invento Deo, qui solus bonus est, deliberat an sit eum reducturus? (AUG.) Anticipaverunt vigilias aliorum. Oculi mei, ut ille, qui ante tempus surgit ad negotium. Vel, oculi mei, affectiones meae. Anticipaverunt, sedulitatem aliorum. Vel, per vigilias, nocturnos significat, quos facimus, et usualiter sic vocamus in laudibus Dei, et ideo: Turbatus. (CAS.) 965CQuia consequi non potui quod quaero. Non sum locutus. Non murmuravi contra Dum. Vel, turbatus sum, quia dum nocte secreta animi perquirit, videt humanum genus in peccata ruere: et pio dolore pro aliis cruciatur, qui jam vitia transilivit. Tacet, quia nocte non habet solatium humani colloquii, quo tempore cautius cogitat; ideo subdit: Cogitavi dies, etc. Oculi mei. Alias inimici mei anticipaverunt vigilias. (AUG.) Id est, vigilaverunt super me, etc., usque ad non tamen cessat, vult et hoc transcendere, unde subdit:

VERS. 6.-- Cogitavi dies antiquos, etc. Ideo turbatus: quia cogitavi dies antiquos Adae, in quibus corruit homo. Sed contra dies antiquos, annos ponit aeternos: ideo turbatus, quia hos desiderat homo, aeternos 965Dnegligit. Dies antiquos, et annos aeternos in mente habui. (CAS.) Quid contigit Adae pro inobedientia? Ex illo cognovi hunc hominis defectum esse. Et annos aeternos, quos persistens haberet, in mente habui, quod non stulti. Et etiam meditatus sum nocte, id est, in hoc defectu. Cum corde, id est, cum ratione, si quomodo possem redire ad annos aeternos. Cum ratione tacitus loquitur, qui in ea quietus exercetur.

VERS. 7.-- Et exercitabar. In ipsa meditatione: Scopebam spiritus meum; purgabam mentem. Alii ventilabam spiritum meum, sic apud me tractans:

VERS. 8.-- Nunquid in aeternum projiciet, genus humanum? ut complacitior. Quasi qui jam placitus 966Afuit sua gratia in Veteri Testamento, nonne addet ut plus sit in Novo per adventum Filii? hoc sentit, qui de pietate tractat. Exercitabar et scopebam. (AUG.) Vel, garriebam, non jam foris, etc., usque ad ubi hoc invenit, quod non in aeternum projiciet Deus. Ut complacitior sit, scilicet ut ipse, qui fuit iratus repellendo, mala inferendo, sit mansuetior liberando, revocando.

VERS. 10.-- Aut obliviscetur misereri Deus. (AUG.) In alio modo, non est misericordia, nisi Deus eam donet: et ipse erit sine ea. Rivus currit, fons siccatus est.

VERS. 11.-- Et dixi: Nunc coepi. (CASS.) Quid deliberando invenerit, scilicet quod Christus mutat homines, et redimit. (ID.) Et dixi. Huic meditationi, 966Betc., usque ad cum et me transiliens ad Deum veni, hic nullum periculum. Coepi. (AUG.) Aliquid, ubi securus sum, ubi non anticipant inimici, modo coepit me mutare Excelsus. Mutatio dexterae, etc. (CAS.) Ab ira ad misericordiam, quod de servis filii. (ID.) Hujus mutationis, etc., usque ad haec sunt quae sanctum mulcent.

VERS. 13.-- In adinventionibus. (AUG.) Id est, in praeceptis, quae invenisti, vel quibus inveniris. (CAS.) Vel observationibus, id est, praeceptis quae observanda sunt, exercebor: quia non satis est legere Scripturas, sed fructus operum demonstrare oportet: his eruditus in laudes prorumpit. (AUG.) In adinventionibus vel affectionibus tuis, non in meis, vel in terrenis est affectio: ita in operibus et meditatione 966CDei est interior quaedam affectio, cum inspicitur mundus, et in creaturis quaeritur creator, et invenitur nusquam displicens, sed undique placens.

VERS. 14.-- Deus in sancto. (AUG.) Per praedicta certus sum quod veniam, et hoc duce. (ID.) Deus in sancto, id est, in Christo, via redeundi ad te. Et cum hoc sit, quis Deus magnus? etc. Via tua. (ID.) Colendi te et ad te veniendi, unde potentiam Dei laetus praefert simulacris, quae falso colebantur.

VERS. 15.-- Mirabilia. (AUG.) Sanati sunt surdi, caeci, languidi, mortui, paralytici. Ista in corporibus facta sunt. In anima quidam sobrii sunt, qui paulo ante ebriosi, infideles, adoratores simulacrorum. Populis virtutem. (ID.) Infidelibus, ut cognoscant 966DChristum tantum corpore, fidelibus, re et Deitate; subdit: Quid praestiteris, redemisti.

VERS. 16.-- Filios Joseph. (AUG.) Id est, Gentilem populum. Vel, per Joseph intelligitur Christus: quia, sicut Joseph venditus in Aegyptum regnavit, ita Christus in gentibus, prius humiliatus in martyribus. (ID.) Joseph qui pervenit ad gentes augmentum interpretatur: et significat gentes, de quibus augmentatus est populus Dei. Vel, Joseph, Christus a Judaeis venditus, et pulsus ad gentes, filii ejus, quos ex gentibus elegit.

VERS. 17.-- Viderunt. (CAS.) Diapsalma. Quae in mundo Christus operatur, exponit. (AUG.) Quasi diceret: Quoniam notam fecisti virtutem, vel per eum 967Aviderunt te, o Deus Pater, vel, te, o Christe, qui es virtus et brachium, etc.

VERS. 18.-- Multitudo. (CAS.) Non pauci, sed multitudo. Sonitus, in gemitu culparum, in actione gratiarum: quasi enim mare confragosum sonant diversa vota populorum. Sonitus aquarum. (AUG.) Unde isti sonitus aquarum, turbatio abyssorum? quia vocem dederunt nubes, de quibus: Mandabo nubibus meis ne pluant super eam imbrem.

VERS. 19.-- Vox tonitrui. (CAS.) Tonitrui vox revolvitur, ut rugatus et sinuosus sonus sentiatur. Allegoria: in rota totius mundi. Rota. (HIER., AUG.) Est quod exponit orbis terrae, quem circumierunt nubes tonando praeceptis, coruscando miraculis. Contremuit terra. (CAS.) Qui habitant in terra. Ipsa 967Bterra mare dicitur per similitudinem, quia humana vita amara, tempestatibus subdita, ubi major piscis minorem devorat.

VERS. 20.-- In mari. (AUG.) Ad litteram, dum Christus super aquas ambulavit. Vel, in cordibus hominum, quos sibi subdit. Vel, per terram, Judaei; per mare, gentes accipiuntur. Et vestigia tua non cognoscentur. Increpatio tacita Judaeorum; quasi dicat: Licet palam venerit, et se miraculis ostenderit: non est cognitus a Judaeis infidelibus quos deduxit in manu Moysi et Aaron, id est, operatione miraculorum quae fecerunt. Vestigia tua, etc. Tetigit aliquos, id est, Judaeos, qui dicunt, Nondum venit Christus, non vident super mare ambulantem.

VERS. 21.-- Sicut oves. Quia non vere oves, sed 967Chaedi. Moysi et Aaron. (CAS.) Moyses intrepretatur assumptus de flumine; Aaron, mons fortitudinis: his nominibus, virtutes quas fecerunt exprimuntur. Moyses inter caetera in mari viam fecit, signans per baptismum populum liberari. Aaron Ecclesiae tenebat imaginem, quae monti fortissimo comparatur.

PSALM LXXVI.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end, for Idithum. (AUG.) The congregation speaks, passing over, that it may arrive at the end, who is Christ. It teaches therefore to trample upon the desires and enticements of the world, to set nothing before itself, save him from whom 965Aall things are. (CAS.) Transcending all things, it seeks God and finds him.

VERS. 2.-- I cried to the Lord with my voice. (AUG.) With the intention of devotion toward the Lord, seeking nothing else from him, because he is Lord, and because he is God. My voice unto him. [Vulg. Ps 76:2 voce mea ad Deum, "with my voice unto God"] The voice is for this, for the sake of which it is uttered; this he adds, lest he be thought to cry to God for anything else than for himself, above whom there is nothing. (CAS.) He does not say what he asks, because there is no need that it be said to him who knows what is expedient. He hath attended to me. (CAS.) For God to attend is to give the whole of what is asked, and more than is asked.

VERS. 3.-- In the day of my trouble I sought. (AUG.) How didst thou seek? etc., as far as he who does not do justice before men, that he may be seen. He refused to be comforted. (ID.) He expounds the tribulation, etc., as far as 965Bhe who in all men either finds or fears a scandal, is secure in none.

VERS. 4.-- And I was exercised. (AUG.) Or, I chattered, that is, I exulted, speaking as a chatterer, who, for gladness, neither would nor could be silent: and again in chattering the spirit failed, which before had wasted away with weariness of evils.

VERS. 5.-- They prevented the watches. (CAS.) Diapsalma. God being found, who alone is good, he deliberates: will he bring him back? (AUG.) They prevented the watches of others. My eyes, like that man who rises before the time to his business. Or, my eyes, my affections. They prevented, the diligence of others. Or, by watches, he signifies the night offices which we make, and which we usually so call among the praises of God, and therefore: Troubled. (CAS.) 965CBecause I could not obtain what I seek. I spoke not. I did not murmur against God. Dum Or, I was troubled, because while by night he searches out the secrets of the mind, he sees the human race rushing into sins: and he is tormented with a loving grief for others, who has already passed beyond vices. He is silent, because by night he has not the solace of human conversation, at which time he thinks more warily; therefore he subjoins: I thought upon the days, etc. My eyes. Otherwise my enemies prevented the watches. (AUG.) That is, they watched over me, etc., as far as yet he does not cease, he wishes to transcend this also, whence he subjoins:

VERS. 6.-- I thought upon the days of old, etc. Therefore troubled: because I thought upon the ancient days of Adam, in which man fell. But over against the ancient days, the years he sets eternal: therefore troubled, because man desires these, and the eternal 965Dhe neglects. I thought upon the days of old, and I had in my mind the eternal years. (CAS.) What befell Adam for his disobedience? From him I have known this defect of man to be. And the eternal years, which by persisting he would have had, I had in my mind, which the foolish do not. And moreover I meditated in the night, that is, in this defect. With my heart, that is, with reason, whether in any way I might return to the eternal years. He speaks silently with reason, who is quietly exercised in it.

VERS. 7.-- And I was exercised. In that very meditation: I swept my spirit; I purged the mind. Others [read] I winnowed my spirit, thus dealing with myself:

VERS. 8.-- Will he cast off for ever, the human race? that he may be more favourable. As one who has already been 966Afavourable by his grace in the Old Testament: will he not add that he may be more so in the New through the coming of the Son? this he thinks, who treats of God's goodness. I was exercised and I swept. (AUG.) Or, I chattered, not now outwardly, etc., as far as where he finds this, that God will not cast off for ever. That he may be more favourable, namely that he himself, who was angry by casting off, by bringing in evils, may be gentler by delivering, by calling back.

VERS. 10.-- Or will God forget to shew mercy. (AUG.) In another manner, there is no mercy unless God bestow it: and he himself will be without it. The stream runs, the fountain is dried up.

VERS. 11.-- And I said: Now have I begun. (CASS.) What he found by deliberating, namely that Christ changes men, and redeems them. (ID.) And I said. To this meditation, 966Betc., as far as when, passing beyond myself also, I came to God, here there is no danger. I have begun. (AUG.) Something, where I am secure, where enemies do not prevent me, now the Most High has begun to change me. The change of the right hand, etc. (CAS.) From wrath to mercy, in that of servants there are made sons. (ID.) Of this change, etc., as far as these are the things that soothe a holy man.

VERS. 13.-- In thy inventions. (AUG.) That is, in the precepts which thou hast invented, or by which thou art found. (CAS.) Or in thy observances, that is, in the precepts which are to be observed, I shall be exercised: because it is not enough to read the Scriptures, but it behoves to show the fruit of works: instructed by these he breaks forth into praises. (AUG.) In thy inventions or thy affections, not in mine; or there is affection in earthly things: so in the works and in the meditation 966Cof God there is a certain inward affection, when the world is beheld, and in creatures the creator is sought, and is found nowhere displeasing, but everywhere pleasing.

VERS. 14.-- O God, in the holy place. (AUG.) By the things aforesaid I am certain that I shall come, and with him for guide. (ID.) O God, in the holy place, that is, in Christ, the way of returning to thee. And since this is so, who is a great God? etc. Thy way. (ID.) Of worshipping thee and of coming to thee, whence he joyfully prefers the power of God to the images, which were falsely worshipped.

VERS. 15.-- Wonders. (AUG.) The deaf, the blind, the feeble, the dead, the paralytic were healed. These things were done in bodies. In the soul certain men are sober, who a little before were drunkards, unbelievers, adorers of images. To the peoples thy power. (ID.) To the unfaithful, that they may know 966DChrist only in body, to the faithful, in reality and in Godhead; he subjoins: What thou hast bestowed, thou hast redeemed.

VERS. 16.-- The sons of Joseph. [Vulg. Ps 76:16 filios Jacob et Joseph] (AUG.) That is, the Gentile people. Or, by Joseph Christ is understood: because, as Joseph, sold into Egypt, reigned, so Christ reigned among the Gentiles, having first been humbled in the martyrs. (ID.) Joseph, who came to the Gentiles, is interpreted increase: and he signifies the Gentiles, from whom the people of God has been increased. Or, Joseph, Christ sold by the Jews, and driven to the Gentiles, his sons, whom he chose out of the Gentiles.

VERS. 17.-- They saw. (CAS.) Diapsalma. He expounds what things Christ works in the world. (AUG.) As if he should say: Since thou hast made thy power known, either through him 967Athey saw thee, O God the Father, or, thee, O Christ, who art the power and the arm, etc.

VERS. 18.-- A multitude. (CAS.) Not a few, but a multitude. The noise, in the groaning for faults, in the giving of thanks: for the divers vows of the peoples sound as it were a broken sea. The noise of waters. (AUG.) Whence are these noises of waters, this troubling of the deeps? because the clouds have uttered a voice, of which: I will command my clouds that they rain no rain upon it. [Vulg. Is 5:6 et nubibus mandabo ne pluant super eam imbrem]

VERS. 19.-- The voice of thunder. (CAS.) The voice of thunder is rolled about, so that a wrinkled and winding sound is perceived. An allegory: in the wheel of the whole world. A wheel. (HIER., AUG.) It is that which he expounds as the circle of the earth, which the clouds went about, thundering with precepts, flashing with miracles. The earth trembled. (CAS.) They who dwell in the earth. That very 967Bearth is called a sea by a likeness, because human life is bitter, subject to tempests, where the greater fish devours the lesser.

VERS. 20.-- In the sea. (AUG.) To the letter, when Christ walked upon the waters. Or, in the hearts of men, whom he subjects to himself. Or, by the land, the Jews; by the sea, the Gentiles are understood. And thy footsteps shall not be known. A silent rebuke of the Jews; as if he should say: Although he came openly, and showed himself by miracles, he was not known by the unbelieving Jews whom he led forth in the hand of Moses and Aaron, that is, by the working of the miracles which they did. Thy footsteps, etc. He touched some, that is, the Jews, who say, Christ has not yet come; they do not see him walking upon the sea.

VERS. 21.-- As sheep. Because they are not truly sheep, but 967Cgoats. Of Moses and Aaron. (CAS.) Moses is interpreted intrepretatur taken up from the river; Aaron, a mountain of strength: by these names the powers which they wrought are expressed. Moses among other things made a way in the sea, signifying that the people is delivered through baptism. Aaron held the image of the Church, which is compared to a most strong mountain.

PSALMUS LXXVII.

VERS. 1.-- Intellectus. (AUG.) Quia haec narrata, etc., usque ad quae aperta videntur, parabolae sunt et aenigmata. Attendite. (CAS.) Primo ipse Dominus loquitur, ut reverentia crescat. Popule meus, qui mihi obedis. Os Dei est Asaph, qui inferius locutus est ista: Quanta audivimus ab initio. Veteris Testamenti: vel, fidelis Synagoga malis exprobrat.

967DVERS. 2.-- In parabolis. (AUG.) Parabolae, rerum similitudines. Propositiones. Quae Graece problemata, quaestiones aliquid solvendum habentes.

VERS. 3.-- Quanta. (CAS.) Summatim dicit, quae Judaeis Deus fecit: tamen ingratis sibi, et sic, si non eis, prodest tamen filiis, ne fiant sicut patres. (AUG.) Prius Deus in homine locutus est, jam homo ipse: Quanta audivimus. Illud praedictum dixit Deus ex se, ne contemnatur ejus locutio.

VERS. 5.-- Et suscitavit, etc. (AUG.) Hoc testimonium. Initium, unde supra: Loquar propositiones ab initio. Initium est Vetus Testamentum, finis Novum. Ibi timor, qui est initium: sed hic Christus, finis legis ad justitiam omni credenti (Rom. X), qui dat spiritum, 968Aunde: Charitas, quae pellit timorem (I Joan. IV). Hujus Novi Testamenti testimonium dicitur vetus lex, quia habet testimonium a lege et Prophetis: unde tabernaculum testimonii dicebatur illud, quod tot mystica figurabat: Testimonium ergo dicitur Vetus Testamentum in quantum probat et testatur, lex in quantum jubet. (CASS., REM.) Suscitavit quasi mortuum in Adam testimonium, id est, legem, vel, dum describitur, suscitatur, prius ignorantia sopitum. Testimonium in Jacob, hoc forsan est, quod Jacob cum angelo luctatus, tacto femore claudicavit: quod significat Judaeos partim fide constare, partim a salute discedere: et ita hujus rei testimonium fuit, quod Jacob accidit. Ecce parabola. Filiis suis. Et sunt iidem filii generatio altera, scilicet populus gratiae.

968BVERS. 6.-- Generatio altera. Per generationes transmissa sunt mandata Dei, ne quis putet uni data.

VERS. 7.-- Ut ponant. Haec est utilitas paternae praedicationis. Exquirant. (AUG.) Qui dicti sunt supra cognovisse, modo exquirant, ut sperantes in Deo, adjuventur ad implendum ab eo.

VERS. 8.-- Prava. (CAS.) Quae veritatem non recipit, et ideo distorta, exasperans super omnes acerbitates, ut in Salvatorem armarentur. Unde per Ezechielem dicit Dominus: Vade et dic domui exasperanti (Ezech. II). Non direxit cor suum. (ID.) Distortum cor habet qui prave intellecta non corrigit, et quae natura docet, non perficit: Non est creditus cum Deo spiritus ejus (Joan. I), id est, et si ratio bene suasit, ei acquievit. 968CNon est creditus. (AUG.) Quando cum spiritu Dei operante spiritus hominis cooperatur, fit quod Deus jubet: et hoc non est nisi credendo in eum, qui justificat impium, quam fidem non habet generatio prava et amaricans.

(ID.) Expressius multo dicit, etc., usque ad illa autem generatio, etsi credidit Deo, non tamen in Deum.

VERS. 9.-- Mittentes arcum. (AUG.) Figurate dicit, etc., usque ad David fratribus, sic populo Judaeorum populus Christianus. Vel, Filii Ephrem. (ID.) Intendentes et mittentes arcum, id est, arcu aliquid mittentes. Vel, intendentes arcum, et mittentes sagittas, id est, promittentes servare legem, aperte dicentes: Omnia, quaecunque dixerit nobis Dominus, faciemus 968Det audiemus (Exod. XXIV). Conversi sunt et defecerunt in die belli, id est, tentationis; unde Osee propheta ait: Ephraim fuctus est facti columba insipiens, non habens cor (Ose. VII), quia promissionem obedientiae non auditio, sed tentatio probat.

Beneficiorum. (EUTHYM.) Beneficiorum, quae contulit in populum Israel, veluti, quod duxerit eos per mare Rubrum immadidos. Mirabilium autem dicit, quia Aegyptiorum flumina in sanguinem mutaverat. Quod vero ait Deum eis haec ostendisse, non ideo dicit, quasi ipsi ea propriis viderint oculis, sed quia ita a suis acceperunt majoribus.

VERS. 12.-- Coram patribus, etc. (CAS.) Incipit narrare jam, quae ab eductione de Aegypto fecit eis: 969Anec tamen destiterunt a murmure et a tentatione. (AUG.) Coram patribus. Qui sunt patres, etc., usque ad accedente ligno crucis quasi virga Moysi. In terra Aegypti. (ID.) Ut omnem dubitationem tollat, et provinciam dicit, et locum factorum. Sic Christus in terra positus coram patribus novit, humile mandatum docuit: Discit a me, quia mitis sum et humilis corde. (Joan. VII.)

VERS. 14.-- In nube. (HIER. et CASS.) Hoc futurum judicabant. Dies, Christus est, tamen nube carnis celatur perfidis; et sicut illis nubes contra aestum solis, sic nobis Christus per incarnationem dat refrigerium contra aestum vitiorum. Tota nocte, toto tempore vitae. In illuminatione ignis. Christianos in hoc saeculo nominis sui claritate custodit ignis Spiritus 969Bsancti.

VERS. 15.-- Petram. (CASS.) In eremo. Prius aqua maris quasi petra, modo petra fons. In eremo, ubi necesse ut gratius sit munus. Adaquavit. Quasi pecora, non homines, quia non egerunt gratias.

VERS. 16.-- Tanquam. (CASS.) Aqua, quae de Christo prodit, nulla imminutione deficit, sed fit fons aquae salientis in vitam aeternam.

VERS. 17.-- Adhuc peccare. (CASS.) Adjecerunt, ut inter tot beneficia non crederent: quod ut maximum intelligeretur peccatum, cum Dominus dixit in Evangelio: Spiritus arguet mundum de peccato, exponendo subjunxit: De peccato quidem, quia non credunt in me (Joann. IV, XVI). Sicut ergo peccatum dicit ibi, non credere, et hic peccare dicit, non credere. 969CIn iram. (ID.) Non credentes Deum posse difficilia sibi facere, quod gravissimum est apud Deum, sic et nos abluti per baptismum provocamus Deum ad iram. In inaquoso. (AUG.) Vel, in alia eremo ad litteram, vel potius in se, quia licet pleni utres aquae de petra, aridae tamen mentes fuerunt.

VERS. 19.-- Mensam. (CASS.) Mystice, refectionem sapientiae, vel corpus Christi.

VERS. 21.-- Ideo audivit. (CASS.) Quod dilata vindicta, dedit prius quod petebant, ne videretur non posse. Distulit. (AUG.) Poenam; dans prius quod, licet tentando, petebat, ne videretur non posse: et postquam dedit, ignis, id est ira, ascendit in Israel. Et hoc est quod prius dixit: Ignis accensus est in Jacob.

969DVERS. 23.-- Et mandavit. Utrumque breviter positum, scilicet quod audivit, quod ira ascendit; aperte hic incipit narrare. Et prius quomodo audivit exsequitur, postea in sequenti parte quomodo vindicavit. Et januas coeli. (CASS.) Januae, ipsi praedicatores, quibus intratur in coelum; vel Scripturae. Aperuit. Quia dedit spiritum suis, ut intelligerent Scripturas.

VERS. 24.-- Manna ad manducandum. (AUG.) Significat panem qui de coelo descendit, qui est cibus angelorum: quem, ut manducaret homo, Verbum caro factum (Joan. I), qui per nubes evangelicas pluitur toti mundo, et apertis eorum cordibus, quasi coelestibus januis, credenti Ecclesiae praedicatur, 970Anon tentati Synagogae. (CASS.) Manna, quid est hoc? quia hic cibus admirando requiritur, et esse corpus Christi scitur. Panis coeli. (ID.) Non aliter, quam Christus, de quo coelestes, id est angeli, reficiuntur ejus contemplatione; et hunc panem, id est verbum, quo grandi cibo pascuntur angeli, per carnem factum lac, edit homo.

VERS. 26.-- Africum. Quia ibi sunt coturnices.

VERS. 27.-- Et pluit super eos, etc. (AUG.) Sic et parvulam fidem, etc., usque ad unde: Si terrena dixi vobis, et non creditis mihi, quomodo si dico vobis coelestia? etc. (Joan. III.)

Sicut pulverem. (CASS.) Pulvis hic significat intelligentiae subtilitatem, quae ad superna conscendit. Arena, innumeram prudentiae copiam salis sapore 970Bconditam. Volatilia pennata. Coelestia desideria, quibus anima pasta pinguescit: haec intra septa Ecclesiae possumus accipere, unde subdit:

VERS. 28.-- Et ceciderunt in medio castrorum. (AUG.) Significans per hoc quod sponte veniunt venti ad homines, et portant eis verba divinitus missa, ut in suis sedibus, et circa tabernacula audiant: quia in omnem terram exivit sonus eorum.

VERS. 29.-- Et manducaverunt. Convicti sunt, qui hoc Deo impossibile putaverunt.

VERS. 30.-- Adhuc escae eorum, etc., et ira Dei, etc. (CASS.) De vindictis, et simulatis reversionibus eorum, timore poenarum: et tamen sententia Dei per misericordiam temperata. Escae. (ID.) Manna, coturnices. Electos Israel impedivit. (AUG.) Id 970Cest, impedivit ne illis prodessent, quibus paterno affectu consulere cupiebant. Vel potius, compedivit ut cum eis molestias sustinerent electi ad exemplum, non justitiae tantum, sed et patientiae. Impedivit. (ID.) Murmure eorum, ut Moyses, qui dixit: Nunquid poterimus de petra aquam vobis ejicere? (Num. XX.)

VERS. 32.-- In omnibus his peccaverunt adhuc et non crediderunt in mirabilibus ejus. Correcti post haec omnia graviora sunt peccata, quae semper accrescunt.

VERS. 33.-- Et defecerunt, etc. (AUG.) Cum possent, credendo, dies in veritate sine defectu habere. In vanitate dies eorum et anni eorum. (CASS.) A similitudine illius qui in ortu moritur, in vanum est natus. Cum festinatione. (AUG.) Et quae prolixior 970Dvidetur, vita cito praeterit.

VERS. 34.-- Quaerebant eum. (CASS. et AUG.) Non occisi, sed relicti. Sed sic loquitur, quia unus populus sunt, quasi de uno corpore. Diluculo veniebant ad eum, etc. (CASS.) Sedulo, vel ante lucem; unde: Vanum est vobis ante lucem surgere. Pius in luce, impius ante lucem rogat. Quaerebant. Revertebantur, veniebant. (AUG.) Haec omnia, propter temporalia bona acquirenda, et vitanda mala: et ita non Deus, sed illa colebantur.

VERS. 37.-- Nec fideles habiti sunt in testamento, etc. (CASS.) Qui vere credit, opera facit: unde fides dicitur quod fiant dicta; unde dicit: Nec fideles in praeceptis.

971AVERS. 38.-- Ipse autem est misericors et propitius fiet. (AUG.) Hic mali impunitatem sibi promittunt, sed misericordia est etiam malis, verum ante judicium, quia facit solem oriri super bonos et malos. Sic et illi genti perpercit, ne penitus eradicaret, sed manet in successione posterorum, sicut Cain signo accepto, ne quis eum occideret. Peccatis eorum, etc. (AUG.) Populi, qui idem est in successione filiorum; ut et post abstulit eos de Aegypto, et induxit eos in montem sanctificationis (Gen. IV), cum non eos, nisi in successione. Sic et hic cum dicitur: propitius fiet peccatis eorum, intelligimus etiam impletum esse quod dicitur ab Apostolo: Reliquiae salvae fient (Rom. IV), quae credent in Christum, quod hic praevidit, cum subdit: Et non dispersit eos. Et abundavit ut 971Baverteret, etc., quia: Non omnem iram accendit, etc. Id est, non punivit eos quantum digni erant: quia et illud remisit, quod Filium occiderunt.

VERS. 39.-- Spiritus vadens et non revertens, etc. Ideo per gratiam revocat, quia per se redire non possunt: unde in Proverbiis in via iniquitatis dicitur: Omnes qui ambulant in ea non revertentur (Prov. II), scilicet per se, sed per gratiam revocabuntur. Haec est ovis errabunda, quae humeris pii pastoris reducta est ad gregem.

VERS. 40.-- Quoties. (CASS.) Dicturus plagas Aegypti, propter eos factas, comparando mala eorum beneficiis Dei, dicit eos oblitos, et tentasse Deum. (AUG.) Quia caro vel spiritus vadens, quoties ergo? quasi multoties exacerbaverunt eum.

971CVERS. 41.-- Et conversi sunt, etc. (AUG.) Repetit eorum infidelitatem, ut memoret quas plagas intulit Deus Aegyptiis propter eos, unde deberent esse non ingrati.

VERS. 42.-- De manu tribulationis. (CASS.) Tribulatio solet esse in memoria, sed non eis. Pulchre opponit manum Dei manui Pharaonis, dicens: Manus ejus et de manu tribu; quae multum differunt. (AUG. et CASS.) Mysticationes ab hoc loco.

VERS. 44, 45.-- Et convertit, etc. Misit in eos iram, etc. Hic incipit exponere plagas propter Judaeorum liberationem in Aegypto factas, et ponit decem plagas, sicut in Exodo decem. Ponuntur aliqua tamen hic, quae non in Exodo, quae non interpretari, nisi figurate possumus, ubi et quae facta fuerunt parabolae 971Ddicuntur, sicut saepe solet non seriem historiae sequi: sed alia addere, vel quaedam mutare pro significatione. Aqua ergo in sanguinem, significat de rerum causis carnaliter sentire. Cynomia. Canini mores sunt. Rana. Loquax vanitas.

VERS. 46, 47.-- Aerugo. Quam alii rubiginem interpretantur, nocet occulte, quae comparatur vitio quod difficile apparet, ut est multum fidere de se. Aura enim noxia hoc in fructibus operatur latenter: sic in moribus occulta superbia, cum putat se aliquid esse qui nihil est. Locusta. Malitia ore laedens, infideli scilicet testimonio.

Grando. Est iniquitas res aliena auferens; unde furta, rapinae, praedae. Plus autem vitio suo vastatur 972Aipse vastator. Pruina. Vitium quo charitas proximi stultitiae tenebris quasi nocturno frigore congelascit.

VERS. 48.-- Ignis. Qui non in Exodo nisi cum grandine in fulguribus, ut fructus laederet, accipitur: qui tamen non legitur possessiones incendisse, significat immanitatem iracundiae, qua et homicidium fit. Morte pecorum, pudicitiae damnum signatur. Concupiscentia, qua foetus oritur, communis est nobis cum pecoribus: hanc habere domitam et ordinatam, pudicitiae virtus est. Mors primitivorum. Amissio est justitiae qua quisque humano generi socialis est. Decem plagis percussi sunt Aegyptii contra decem praecepta scripta in tabulis. Et hic decem plagae, licet non in eo ordine ponantur, sed pro tribus quae 972Bin Exodo, id est cyniphes, ulcera, tenebrae quae non hic. Aliae tres sunt hic, quae non ibi, rubigo, pruina, et ignis. Talia enim pro congrua intelligentia frequenter variantur. Signa. (CASS.) Sunt duris cordibus, quasi characteris impressa vestigia. Prodigia, quae signabant aliqua futura. Thanis, civitas, humile mandatum, quod hic nobis necessarium, ut in futuro erigamur. Et dedit aerugini. Haec in Exodo non leguntur, mystica ergo interpretatione tantum exponantur. Locusta. (AUG.) Se invicem comedentes, significat detractores, qui alienos fructus invide rodunt. Moros eorum in pruina. (AUG.) Morus calidae est naturae, per quod charitas intelligitur, quae in pruina occiditur. Grandini (ID.) Quae grando non potuit laedere, id est mollia, post dicit Exodus a 972Clocustis comesta. Tradidit. (CASS.) Morte pecudum, stultorum occasus ostenditur.

(ID.) Igni. Ignis, cupiditas, quae possessionem, id est, statum mentis vastat.

VERS. 49.-- Iram indignationis, etc. (CASS.) Ordo vindictae: prius peccatis Deus irascitur, quando non compunguntur, inde malitiam hominis sua indignatione, ira et tribulatione derelinquit, ut suis adversitatibus affligantur, qui Deo non obediunt, ut ibi dicitur: Propterea tradidit illos in reprobum sensum (Rom. I). Indignatio hominis pertinet ad tumidam superbiam; ira, ad nefandam audaciam; tribulatio, ad confusam desperationem: tunc per diabolum ad immissiones illicitas praecipitantur nudati defensione Dei. Per angelos malos. (AUG.) Judicio Dei 972Dhaec facta sunt, etc., usque ad per angelos ergo malos punit Deus bonos et malos homines, sed bonos tantum corporalibus poenis, malos autem corporalibus et spiritualibus poenis.

VERS. 50.-- Irae suae. (AUG.) Erat semita irae Dei, qua occulta aequitate puniret Aegyptios; cui Deus fecit viam, ut eos quasi ex abditis produceret per angelos malos in aperta scelera, et sic aperte puniret.

VERS. 51.-- Primogenitum in Aegypto. (AUG.) Primogenita sunt summa mandata, ut: Diliges Dominum Deum ex toto corde; quibus non servatis orbamur prole rationis.

VERS. 52.-- Et abstulit sicut oves populum suum, 973Aet perduxit eos tanquam gregem in deserto. (AUG.) Mystice. Hoc et in nobis intus fit, ubi eruditi de potestate tenebrarum mente transferimur in regnum Dei, oves in spiritualibus pascuis. (CASS.) Et abstulit. Quod eductos de servitute duxit in terram promissionis; et iterum offendunt.

VERS. 54.-- Et induxit eos in montem sanctificationis suae. (AUG.) Non eosdem quos abstulit, sed eos nomine et gente; significat tamen quod multi ad Ecclesiam, quam mavult intelligi, conversi sunt; ipsa est mons quem Christus acquisivit. Et ejecit a facie eorum gentes, etc. (AUG.) Vel maligni spiritus. Quae omnia Christus ejecit a facie fidelium; et sorte divisit eis terram. Per hoc significatur quod in nobis omnia operatur unus atque idem Spiritus, dividens 973Bsingulis prout vult.

VERS. 55.-- In tabernaculis. (CASS.) In quibus regnabant peccata regnare fecit virtutes.

VERS. 57.-- Quemadmodum patres eorum conversi, etc. (AUG.) Per totum loquitur quasi de eisdem: tamen nunc de his qui in terra promissionis, quorum fuerunt patres, qui in deserto amaricaverunt. Arcum pravum, etc. (ID.) Animi intentionem perversam, ut contra Deum, qui dixerat: Non erunt tibi dii alieni (Exod. XX), quod plenius aperit. In iram concita, vel, in arcum pravum, qui difficile remittitur, et ipsi facile retroibant. Vel, arcum pravum, qui non eminus jaculatur, sed in se spicula convertit, id est, malitia dolosorum.

VERS. 58.-- Ad aemulationem. Vel aemulati sunt; 973Calia littera, cum honorem Dei alii tradunt.

VERS. 59.-- Audivit Deus. (CASS.) De ultione in terra promissionis, quae et retorta est in ipsos, per quos punivit.

VERS. 60.-- Et repulit tabernaculum. (AUG.) Hoc tempore Eli sacerdotis, quando victi sunt ab Allophylis, et arca Domini capta est, et ipsi magna strage vastati. Legitur enim in libro Regum, quod tunc ceciderunt de populo triginta millia peditum. Repulit tabernaculum Silo. (BEDA.) Quod erat in Silo, etc., usque ad quia autem illud non attenderunt, nec tabernaculum Deo fecerunt: ideo Dominus merito repulit. Habitavit in hominibus. (AUG.) Cum ergo non esset dignum in quo habitaret, repulit illud quod non propter se, sed propter illos instituit. 973D(CASS.) Sic deserit corpora nostra, quae Spiritus sanctus, dum bene tractantur, inhabitat.

VERS. 61.-- Et tradidit. (CASS.) Si enim cum peccatoribus et boni traduntur captivitati, exercitium est, non in mente captivi sunt. Vel, hosti traditi, sed liberi et Deo conjuncti. Virtutum eorum. (AUG.) Arbitrii libertatem imminuit, et virtutes abstulit in malis, quod non sit in bonis, licet cum malis interdum captiventur corporaliter.

VERS. 65.-- Et excitatus est. (CASS. et AUG.) Mores hominum Domino tribuit, proptes res explanandas.

Tanquam dormiens. Hoc dicitur a persona dementium, qui ita putant, quando periclitantibus non subvenit, vino esse crapulatum, quando non tam 974Acito subvenit. Et revera sic dementer putantibus dormit, et est alienus, et negligentibus et infidelibus, qui nulla voce laudis vel operis eum excitant. Excitatur autem ad vindictam malis actibus, ut hic peccatis eorum, qui arcam inter simulacra posuerunt. Tanquam potens, quia tunc sunt homines ad iram faciles, et ad virtutes potentes, quando post crapulam de somno surgunt. (AUG.) Et excitatus est. Christus vino passionis ebrius, dormiens in sepulcro, excitatus est a morte, tanquam potens in resurrectione. (ID.) Tanquam dormiens. Visus est dormire, quando populum suum dedit in manus eorum, quos odit: ubi eis dicitur: Ubi est Deus tuus?

VERS. 66.-- Et percussit iniquitatem. (AUG.) Hac poena cruciabitur, etc., usque ad opprobrium enim 974Bsempiternum dedit illis.

VERS. 67.-- Et repulit. (CASS.) De rege David, et loco regni. (AUG.) Non dixit, etc., usque ad sic ab initio electionis Hebraeae gentis usque ad Christum procedit.

VERS. 69.-- Sicut, etc. (AUG.) Unicorni sunt quorum firma spes in unum illud erigitur, de quo dicitur: Unam petii a Domino, hanc requiram. Sanctificium. Est plebs sancta, regale sacerdotium.

VERS. 70.-- David servum. (AUG.) Qui de Juda, etc., usque ad: dentes Ecclesiae sunt illi per quos loquitur, vel per quos in corpus suum velut manducando caeteros trajicit. Grex tonsarum dicitur, quia onera saeculi velut vellera deposuit, et ad pedes Apostolorum rerum suarum venditarum pretia apposuit; 974Cascendens de lavacro baptismi, geminos creat, opera scilicet geminae charitatis; unde: sterilis non erat in eis; ab his translatus est Christus, sed pascit greges in gentibus qui sunt Jacob, et Israel.

VERS. 71.-- Jacob. Israel haereditatem suam. (AUG.) Repetit: Nisi dicatur, nunc secundum hunc statum Jacob servus: quando videbit facie ad faciem haereditas. Unde et nomen accepit: Israel enim dicitur ex contemplatione Dei. Transtulit eum ad hoc ut pasceret, et ita fecit.

VERS. 72.-- Et pavit eos, etc. (AUG.) Videtur forte, etc., usque ad et hoc docuit quod egit.

PSALM LXXVII.

VERS. 1.-- Understanding. (AUG.) Because these things narrated, etc., as far as the things that seem open are parables and riddles. Attend. (CAS.) First the Lord himself speaks, that reverence may grow. My people, who obey me. The mouth of God is Asaph, who spoke these things below: How great things we have heard from the beginning. Of the Old Testament: or, the faithful Synagogue reproaches the wicked.

967DVERS. 2.-- In parables. (AUG.) Parables are likenesses of things. Propositions. Which in Greek are problemata, questions having something to be resolved.

VERS. 3.-- How great things. (CAS.) He tells summarily what God did for the Jews: yet for men ungrateful to him, and thus, if not to them, it profits the sons nevertheless, lest they become as their fathers. (AUG.) First God spoke in a man, now the man himself: How great things we have heard. That foretold word God spoke from himself, lest his speech be despised.

VERS. 5.-- And he raised up, etc. (AUG.) This testimony. The beginning, whence above: I will utter propositions from the beginning. The beginning is the Old Testament, the end the New. There is fear, which is the beginning: but here is Christ, the end of the law unto righteousness to every one that believeth (Rom. X), who gives the Spirit, 968Awhence: Charity, which drives out fear (I Joan. IV) [Vulg. 1 Jo 4:18 perfecta caritas foras mittit timorem, "perfect charity casteth out fear"]. The old law is called the testimony of this New Testament, because it has testimony from the law and the Prophets: whence that was called the tabernacle of testimony which prefigured so many mystical things: Testimony therefore the Old Testament is called in so far as it proves and testifies, law in so far as it commands. (CASS., REM.) He raised up the testimony as though dead in Adam, that is, the law; or, while it is written down it is raised up, having been lulled asleep before by ignorance. A testimony in Jacob, this perhaps is that Jacob, having wrestled with the angel, went halt when his thigh was touched: which signifies that the Jews partly stand fast in faith, partly depart from salvation: and so what befell Jacob was a testimony of this thing. Behold a parable. To their sons. And these same sons are another generation, namely the people of grace.

968BVERS. 6.-- Another generation. Through the generations the commandments of God were handed on, lest any think them given to one only.

VERS. 7.-- That they may set. This is the profit of the fathers' preaching. Let them seek out. (AUG.) Those who were said above to have known, now let them seek out, that hoping in God they may be helped by him to fulfil it.

VERS. 8.-- Froward. (CAS.) Which does not receive the truth, and is therefore twisted, provoking beyond all bitternesses, so that they were armed against the Saviour. Whence by Ezechiel the Lord says: Go and speak to the provoking house (Ezech. II). It set not its heart aright. (ID.) He has a twisted heart who does not correct what he has ill understood, and does not perform what nature teaches: His spirit was not trusted with God (Joan. I), that is, and if reason persuaded him well, he yielded to it. 968CIt was not trusted. (AUG.) When the spirit of man works together with the Spirit of God working, that is done which God commands: and this is not save by believing in him who justifies the ungodly, which faith the froward and embittering generation has not.

(ID.) He speaks much more expressly, etc., as far as but that generation, although it believed God, yet not in God.

VERS. 9.-- Shooting the bow. (AUG.) He speaks figuratively, etc., as far as David to his brethren, so the Christian people to the people of the Jews. Or, The sons of Ephrem. (ID.) Bending and shooting the bow, that is, shooting something with a bow. Or, bending the bow, and shooting arrows, that is, promising to keep the law, saying openly: All things whatsoever the Lord shall say to us, we will do 968Dand we will hear (Exod. XXIV) [Vulg. Ex 24:7 Omnia quae locutus est Dominus, faciemus, et erimus obedientes, "all things that the Lord hath spoken we will do, and we will be obedient"]. They were turned and failed in the day of battle, that is, of temptation; whence Osee the prophet says: Ephraim is become facti a dove fuctus without understanding, not having a heart (Ose. VII) [Vulg. Os 7:11 factus est Ephraim quasi columba seducta non habens cor, "as a dove that is decoyed"], because not hearing, but temptation proves the promise of obedience.

Of his benefits. [Vulg. Ps 77:11 benefactorum, "his good deeds"] (EUTHYM.) Of the benefits which he conferred upon the people of Israel, as, that he led them through the Red Sea unwetted. Of his wonders however he says, because he had turned the rivers of the Egyptians into blood. But as to his saying that God showed these things to them, he does not say it as though they themselves had seen them with their own eyes, but because they received them so from their elders.

VERS. 12.-- Before their fathers, etc. (CAS.) He begins now to tell what he did for them from the leading out of Egypt: 969Aand yet they did not cease from murmuring and from temptation. (AUG.) Before the fathers. Who the fathers are, etc., as far as the wood of the cross coming to it as the rod of Moses. In the land of Egypt. (ID.) That he may take away all doubt, he names both the province and the place of the deeds. So Christ, set upon the earth, knew before the fathers, and taught the humble commandment: Learn of me, for I am meek and humble of heart. Discit (Joan. VII.)

VERS. 14.-- In a cloud. (HIER. et CASS.) This they judged to be future. The day is Christ, yet he is hidden from the faithless by the cloud of the flesh; and as for them the cloud against the heat of the sun, so for us Christ through the incarnation gives refreshment against the heat of vices. All the night, all the time of life. In the light of fire. The fire of the Holy 969BSpirit keeps Christians in this world by the brightness of his name.

VERS. 15.-- The rock. (CASS.) In the wilderness. Before, the water of the sea was as a rock, now the rock is a fountain. In the wilderness, where the gift must needs be the more welcome. He gave them drink. As cattle, not as men, because they gave no thanks.

VERS. 16.-- As. (CASS.) The water which comes forth from Christ fails by no diminishing, but becomes a fountain of water springing up unto life everlasting.

VERS. 17.-- To sin yet more. (CASS.) They added this, that amid so many benefits they did not believe: and that this might be understood as the greatest sin, when the Lord had said in the Gospel: The Spirit shall convince the world of sin, he added by way of exposition: Of sin indeed, because they believe not in me (Joann. IV, XVI) [Vulg. Jo 16:9 quia non crediderunt in me, "because they have not believed in me"]. As therefore he there calls sin not to believe, so here by to sin he means, not to believe. 969CUnto wrath. (ID.) Not believing that God could do hard things for them, which is most grievous in the sight of God; so we too, washed by baptism, provoke God to wrath. In the waterless place. (AUG.) Either in another wilderness according to the letter, or rather in themselves, because although the skins were full of water from the rock, their minds nevertheless were dry.

VERS. 19.-- A table. (CASS.) Mystically, the refreshment of wisdom, or the body of Christ.

VERS. 21.-- Therefore he heard. (CASS.) In that, vengeance being deferred, he gave first what they were asking, lest he should seem not to be able. He deferred. (AUG.) The punishment; giving first what it was asking, though by way of tempting, lest he should seem not to be able: and after he had given, fire, that is wrath, went up upon Israel. And this is what he said before: A fire was kindled in Jacob.

969DVERS. 23.-- And he commanded. Both were set down briefly, namely that he heard, and that wrath went up; here he begins to tell it openly. And first he follows out how he heard, afterwards in the following part how he took vengeance. And the gates of heaven. (CASS.) The gates are the preachers themselves, by whom entry is made into heaven; or the Scriptures. He opened. Because he gave his Spirit to his own, that they might understand the Scriptures.

VERS. 24.-- Manna to eat. (AUG.) It signifies the bread which came down from heaven, which is the food of angels: which, that man might eat it, the Word was made flesh (Joan. I), who is rained upon the whole world through the evangelical clouds, and, their hearts being opened as heavenly gates, is preached to the believing Church, 970Anot to the tempting Synagogue. (CASS.) Manna, what is this? because this food is sought after with wonder, and is known to be the body of Christ. The bread of heaven. (ID.) No other than Christ, by whom the heavenly ones, that is the angels, are refreshed in the contemplation of him; and this bread, that is the Word, on which great food the angels are fed, made milk through the flesh, man eats.

VERS. 26.-- The south-west wind. Because the quails are there.

VERS. 27.-- And he rained upon them, etc. (AUG.) So also a little faith, etc., as far as whence: If I have told you earthly things, and you believe me not, how, if I tell you heavenly things? etc. (Joan. III.) [Vulg. Jo 3:12 Si terrena dixi vobis, et non creditis : quomodo, si dixero vobis caelestia, credetis, "how, if I shall speak to you heavenly things, will you believe"]

As dust. (CASS.) Dust here signifies the subtlety of understanding, which climbs to the things above. Sand, the countless abundance of prudence seasoned 970Bwith the savour of salt. Feathered fowls. Heavenly desires, on which the soul is fed and grows fat: these we can receive within the enclosures of the Church, whence he adds:

VERS. 28.-- And they fell in the midst of their camp. (AUG.) Signifying by this that the winds come of their own accord to men, and carry to them the words divinely sent, that they may hear them in their own seats, and about their tents: because their sound went out into all the earth.

VERS. 29.-- And they did eat. They were convicted, who had thought this impossible to God.

VERS. 30.-- As yet their meats, etc., and the wrath of God, etc. (CASS.) Of the punishments, and of their feigned returnings, through fear of penalties: and yet the sentence of God is tempered by mercy. Their meats. (ID.) The manna, the quails. He hindered the chosen of Israel. (AUG.) That 970Cis, he hindered them from profiting those whom they desired to counsel with a father's affection. Or rather, he fettered them, that the chosen might bear troubles together with them for an example, not of righteousness only, but of patience also. He hindered. (ID.) By their murmuring, as Moses, who said: Can we bring forth water for you out of the rock? (Num. XX.)

VERS. 32.-- In all these things they sinned still, and they believed not in his wondrous works. Corrected after all these things, the sins are the graver, which ever increase.

VERS. 33.-- And they failed, etc. (AUG.) Whereas they might, by believing, have had their days in truth without failing. Their days in vanity and their years. (CASS.) From the likeness of him who dies at his rising: he was born in vain. With haste. (AUG.) And the life which seems the longer 970Dpasses quickly.

VERS. 34.-- They sought him. (CASS. et AUG.) Not those slain, but those left. Yet he speaks thus because they are one people, as of one body. Early they came to him, etc. (CASS.) Diligently, or before the light; whence: It is vain for you to rise before the light. The godly man prays in the light, the ungodly before the light. They sought. They returned, they came. (AUG.) All these things for the sake of gaining temporal goods and of avoiding evils: and so not God, but those things were worshipped.

VERS. 37.-- Neither were they counted faithful in the covenant, etc. (CASS.) He who truly believes does works: whence faith is so called because the things said are done; whence he says: Nor faithful in his precepts.

971AVERS. 38.-- But he is merciful, and will be propitious. (AUG.) Here the wicked promise themselves impunity, but there is mercy even for the wicked, yet before the judgment, because he makes the sun to rise upon the good and the evil.
