So he spared that nation also, that he might not root it out utterly, but it abides in the succession of those that come after, as Cain when he had received the sign, that none should slay him. Their sins, etc. (AUG.) Of the people, which is the same in the succession of the sons; as also afterwards he took them away out of Egypt, and brought them into the mountain of his sanctification (Gen. IV), whereas not them, save in the succession. So here too, when it is said: he will be propitious to their sins, we understand that also to be fulfilled which is said by the Apostle: The remnant shall be saved (Rom. IV), which shall believe in Christ, and this he foresaw here, when he adds: And he scattered them not. And he abounded that 971Bhe might turn away, [Vulg. Ps 77:38 et non disperdet eos, "and he will not destroy them"] etc., because: He kindled not all his wrath, etc. That is, he did not punish them as much as they deserved: because he forgave even this, that they slew the Son.

VERS. 39.-- A spirit that goeth and returneth not, etc. [Vulg. Ps 77:39 spiritus vadens et non rediens, "that goeth and cometh not again"] Therefore he calls them back by grace, because by themselves they cannot return: whence in the Proverbs it is said of the way of iniquity: All that walk in it shall not return (Prov. II) [Vulg. Pr 2:19 Omnes qui ingrediuntur ad eam non revertentur, "all that go in unto her shall not return"], namely by themselves, but by grace they shall be called back. This is the wandering sheep, which was brought back to the flock upon the shoulders of the loving shepherd.

VERS. 40.-- How often. (CASS.) Being about to tell the plagues of Egypt, wrought for their sake, by comparing their evils with the benefits of God, he says that they forgot, and that they tempted God. (AUG.) Because they are flesh, or a spirit that goes, how often then? as though to say, they provoked him many times.

971CVERS. 41.-- And they turned back, etc. (AUG.) He repeats their unbelief, that he may call to mind what plagues God brought upon the Egyptians for their sake, whence they ought to have been not ungrateful.

VERS. 42.-- From the hand of tribulation. [Vulg. Ps 77:42 de manu tribulantis, "from the hand of him that afflicted them"] (CASS.) Tribulation is wont to be kept in memory, but not by them. Beautifully he sets the hand of God against the hand of Pharao, saying: His hand and from the hand of tribu; which differ greatly. (AUG. et CASS.) Mystical interpretations from this place.

VERS. 44, 45.-- And he turned, etc. He sent upon them wrath, etc. Here he begins to set forth the plagues wrought in Egypt for the deliverance of the Jews, and he sets down ten plagues, as in Exodus ten. Yet certain things are set down here which are not in Exodus, which we cannot interpret save figuratively, where also the things that were done are called parables, 971Das he is often wont not to follow the order of the history, but to add other things, or to change certain things for the sake of the signification. Water therefore into blood signifies to think carnally of the causes of things. The dog-fly. [Vulg. Ps 77:45 coenomyiam, the common fly] They are dog-like manners. The frog. Talkative vanity.

VERS. 46, 47.-- Blight. Which others interpret as rust, harms in secret, and is likened to a vice that hardly appears, such as to trust much in oneself. For a noxious breath works this in the fruits unseen: so in manners does hidden pride, when he thinks himself to be something who is nothing. The locust. Malice hurting with the mouth, namely by faithless testimony.

Hail. It is iniquity carrying off the goods of another; whence thefts, robberies, plunderings. But the waster himself is more wasted 972Aby his own vice. Frost. The vice by which charity toward one's neighbour freezes in the darkness of folly as with the cold of night.

VERS. 48.-- Fire. Which in Exodus is not taken save with the hail in the lightnings, that it might hurt the fruits: which nevertheless is not read to have burned the possessions, signifies the monstrousness of anger, by which murder also is done. By the death of the cattle the loss of chastity is signified. Concupiscence, from which offspring arises, is common to us with the beasts: to have this tamed and ordered is the virtue of chastity. The death of the firstborn. It is the loss of the righteousness by which each man is sociable to the human race. The Egyptians were smitten with ten plagues against the ten commandments written on the tables. And here are ten plagues, though they be not set down in that order, but in place of three which 972Bare in Exodus, that is the sciniphs, the boils, the darkness, which are not here. Three others are here which are not there, rust, frost, and fire. For such things are frequently varied for a fitting understanding. Signs. (CASS.) They are, upon hard hearts, as it were the traces of a stamp impressed. Wonders, which betokened certain things to come. Thanis, [Vulg. Ps 77:12 and 43 Taneos] a city, the humble commandment, which is necessary for us here, that in the time to come we may be raised up. And he gave to the blight. These things are not read in Exodus, therefore let them be expounded only by a mystical interpretation. The locust. (AUG.) Devouring one another, it signifies detractors, who out of envy gnaw the fruits of others. Their mulberry trees with frost. (AUG.) The mulberry is of a warm nature, by which charity is understood, which is killed by the frost. To the hail (ID.) The things the hail could not hurt, that is the soft ones, Exodus afterwards says were eaten 972Cby the locusts. He delivered up. (CASS.) By the death of the cattle the fall of fools is shown.

(ID.) To fire. Fire is covetousness, which lays waste the possession, that is, the state of the mind.

VERS. 49.-- The wrath of his indignation, etc. (CASS.) The order of vengeance: first God is angry at their sins, and when they are not pricked in heart, then he abandons the malice of man in his own indignation, wrath and tribulation, that they may be afflicted by their own adversities who do not obey God, as it is said there: Therefore he delivered them up unto a reprobate sense (Rom. I). The indignation of man belongs to swollen pride; wrath, to unspeakable audacity; tribulation, to confounded despair: then through the devil they are hurled headlong into unlawful assaults, stripped of the defence of God. By evil angels. (AUG.) By the judgment of God 972Dthese things were done, etc., as far as by evil angels therefore God punishes both good and evil men, but the good with bodily punishments only, the evil with punishments both bodily and spiritual.

VERS. 50.-- Of his wrath. (AUG.) There was a path of the wrath of God, by which with hidden equity he might punish the Egyptians; and for it God made a way, that he might bring them forth as out of hidden places, through evil angels, into open crimes, and so punish them openly.

VERS. 51.-- The firstborn in Egypt. (AUG.) The firstborn are the highest commandments, as: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart; and when these are not kept we are bereaved of the offspring of reason.

VERS. 52.-- And he took away his people as sheep, 973Aand he led them like a flock in the desert. (AUG.) Mystically. This is done within us also, where, being taught, we are carried over in mind out of the power of darkness into the kingdom of God, sheep in spiritual pastures. (CASS.) And he took away. In that he led those brought out of bondage into the land of promise; and again they offend.

VERS. 54.-- And he brought them into the mountain of his sanctification. (AUG.) Not the same men whom he took away, but those of the same name and nation; yet it signifies that many were converted to the Church, which he would rather have understood; she is the mountain which Christ purchased. And he cast out the nations from before them, etc. (AUG.) Or the malignant spirits. All which things Christ cast out from before the faithful; and he divided them the land by lot. By this it is signified that one and the same Spirit works all things in us, dividing 973Bto every one according as he will.

VERS. 55.-- In their tents. (CASS.) In which sins reigned, he made virtues to reign.

VERS. 57.-- Even as their fathers were turned, etc. (AUG.) Throughout he speaks as though of the same men: yet now of those in the land of promise, whose fathers they were who embittered him in the desert. A crooked bow, etc. (ID.) The perverse intention of the mind, as against God, who had said: Thou shalt not have strange gods (Exod. XX) [Vulg. Ex 20:3 Non habebis deos alienos coram me, "thou shalt not have strange gods before me"], which he opens more fully. Provoked unto wrath, or, into a crooked bow, which is unbent with difficulty, and they themselves easily went back. Or, a crooked bow, which does not shoot from afar, but turns its darts upon itself, that is, the malice of the deceitful.

VERS. 58.-- To jealousy. Or they were jealous; 973Canother reading, when they give the honour of God to another.

VERS. 59.-- God heard. (CASS.) Of the vengeance in the land of promise, which was turned back also upon the very men through whom he punished.

VERS. 60.-- And he put away the tabernacle. (AUG.) At that time of Eli the priest, when they were overcome by the Allophyli, and the ark of the Lord was taken, and they themselves laid waste with a great slaughter. For it is read in the book of Kings that there fell then of the people thirty thousand footmen. He put away the tabernacle of Silo. (BEDA.) Which was in Silo, etc., as far as but because they did not attend to it, nor made a tabernacle for God: therefore the Lord deservedly put it away. He dwelt among men. (AUG.) Since therefore there was nothing worthy in which he might dwell, he put away that which he had appointed not for his own sake, but for theirs. 973D(CASS.) So he forsakes our bodies, which the Holy Spirit inhabits while they are well treated.

VERS. 61.-- And he delivered up. (CASS.) For if the good too are delivered into captivity along with sinners, it is a discipline; they are not captives in mind. Or, delivered to the enemy, but free and joined to God. Of their virtues. [Vulg. Ps 77:61 virtutem, "their strength"] (AUG.) He diminished the liberty of choice, and took away the virtues in the wicked, which is not so in the good, although at times they are taken captive bodily along with the wicked.

VERS. 65.-- And he was awakened. (CASS. et AUG.) He ascribes the manners of men to the Lord, for the sake of explaining the matter proptes.

As one asleep. This is said in the person of the mad, who think thus, when he does not come to the aid of those in peril, that he is drunk with wine, when he does not come to their aid so 974Aquickly. And in truth he does sleep for those who so madly think, and is a stranger, both to the negligent and to the unbelieving, who rouse him by no voice of praise or of work. But he is roused to vengeance by evil deeds, as here by the sins of those who set the ark among the idols. As a mighty man, because men are then quick to wrath, and mighty for feats of strength, when after a debauch they rise from sleep. (AUG.) And he was awakened. Christ, drunk with the wine of the passion, sleeping in the sepulchre, was awakened from death, as a mighty man in the resurrection. (ID.) As one asleep. He seemed to sleep when he gave his people into the hands of those whom he hates: where it is said to them: Where is thy God?

VERS. 66.-- And he smote iniquity. [Vulg. Ps 77:66 percussit inimicos suos in posteriora, "he smote his enemies on the hinder parts"] (AUG.) He shall be tormented with this punishment, etc., as far as: reproach indeed 974Beverlasting he gave to them.

VERS. 67.-- And he put away. (CASS.) Of king David, and of the seat of the kingdom. (AUG.) He did not say, etc., as far as thus he proceeds from the beginning of the election of the Hebrew nation down to Christ.

VERS. 69.-- As, etc. (AUG.) Unicorns are they whose firm hope is raised up unto that one thing, of which it is said: One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after. His sanctuary. It is the holy people, a royal priesthood.

VERS. 70.-- David his servant. (AUG.) Who of Juda, etc., as far as: the teeth of the Church are they through whom she speaks, or through whom she passes the rest into her own body as though by eating. A flock of shorn sheep it is called, because it laid down the burdens of the world as fleeces, and laid at the feet of the Apostles the prices of the goods it had sold; 974Ccoming up from the washing of baptism, it brings forth twins, that is, the works of the twofold charity; whence: there was not a barren one among them; from these Christ was carried over, but he feeds among the Gentiles the flocks which are Jacob and Israel.

VERS. 71.-- Jacob. Israel his inheritance. (AUG.) He repeats it: Unless it be said that now, according to this present state, Jacob is a servant: when he shall see face to face, an inheritance. Whence also he received the name: for Israel is so called from the contemplation of God. He carried him over to this end, that he might feed him, and so he did.

VERS. 72.-- And he fed them, etc. (AUG.) It seems perhaps, etc., as far as and he taught this which he did.

PSAL. LXXVIII.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus Asaph. (CASS.) Psalmus secundus de lamentatione. Genti pro duritia sua, graviter 974Daffligendae precatur Christum subvenire. Monemur bonis proximorum laetari, calamitatibus affligi.

Deus venerunt gentes. (ID.) Prima est conquestio, et enumerantur quanta tulerit Jerusalem temporibus Antiochi, ubi non destructa fuit, propter quae signatur Ecclesiae persecutio. (AUG.) Venerunt. Non dicit quasi nescienti, etc., usque ad jam vero evidenter sunt impleta.

In haereditatem tuam. (ID.) De populo Israel; haereditas Dei sunt electi, sed non excaecati; ergo possunt haec dici de temporibus post ascensionem Christi; sed antequam Christus venisset, et tunc enim haereditas, ubi Prophetae, et sancti conducti in Babylone; vel sub Antiocho maxime. (CASS.) Quod si 975Aquis, etc., usque ad cujus circumitus per totum orbem, ubi et persecutio fit.

VERS. 2.-- Morticina. (CASS.) Cadavera, quasi non modo in viventes saeviunt. Sepelire pietatis est, abjicere crudelitatis. Effuderunt. (ID.) Exaggerat, ut judicem moveat.

VERS. 4.-- Facti. (CASS.) Gloria Jerusalem toto orbe mirabilis versa est in opprobrium vicinis, quod gravius est quam si remotis, quia hi sunt assidui. Vel, vicini, affectiones, propinquis jam volentibus credere, ut martyres hoc dicant.

VERS. 5.-- Usquequo, Domine? (CASS.) Deprecatio pro parte sua contra inimicos et insultantes vicinos; quasi illi ita saeviunt: Sed, o Domine, usquequo? (AUG.) Rogat ne usque in finem irascatur, id est, ne 975Billa vastatio perseveret, sed temperet correctionem. Nomine irae, vindicta iniquitatis accipitur, nomine zeli, exactio castitatis, ne anima a Deo fornicetur. Nota, hoc pro peccatis evenire hominibus, licet justis, sicut tres pueri, et Prophetae in captivitate testantur. Velut ignis. (ID.) Ure tandiu, donec aurum virtutum perfecte purgetur, ligna, id est vitia, cinerentur.

VERS. 7.-- Comederunt. (AUG.) Ferarum dentibus tradendo. Desolaverunt, eversione civitatis, quae civibus suis nudata est, vel, quia occiderunt substitutos loco civium occisorum; Jacob pro homine, homo, scilicet pro gente, quae offendit. Gratus patriarcha, ut ejus memoria peccata populi mitiget. Jacob. (AUG.) Haec est supra dicta haereditas. Locus. (CASS.) Civitas, ubi templum, quo congregabantur ad festa.

975CVERS. 8.-- Iniquitatum nostrarum. (BEDA.) Id est, quas a patribus contraximus, quibus scilicet jam non debetur correctio, sed damnatio, nisi adsit gratiae tuae miseratio. Scriptum est enim: Anima quae peccaverit ipsa morietur. Et, Visitabo peccata patrum in filios, usque in tertiam et quartam generationem (Ezech. XVIII.) Antiquarum. (CASS.) Non dicit de praeteritis tantum, cum et hoc tempore quidam Judaei idola sequerentur; sed similium antiquis, quibus innumeris annis peccaverunt. Anticipent. (ID.) Ante judicium quod timet omnis homo, quia nisi indulgentia praeveniat in judicio, non absolvitur reus. Nimis. Ne quis de actibus praesumat.

VERS. 9.-- Adjuva. (CASS.) In bello defensionis legum, quia non in suis, sed in virtutibus Dei confidunt. 975DPropter gloriam. Non propter meritum ut erepti, tuo nomini honorem reddamus. Propter gloriam nominis tui. Pietati sancti nominis tribuatur, non nobis, quod actibus nostris non potest haberi. Adjuva nos, Deus. Per hoc nec ingratus est gratiae, nec tollit liberum arbitrium. Qui enim adjuvatur, etiam per seipsum aliquid agit. Libera nos. (AUG.) Liberat, id est, eruit a malis, cum et adjuvat ad faciendam justitiam, et propitius est peccatis, sine quibus hic non vivitur.

VERS. 10.-- Ne forte. (AUG.) Illud usitatum a perfidis: Ubi est? Vel non est, vel non potest; insultatio non ferenda. Innotescat. Vel hic in conversis perimitur iniquitas, quod ante optaverat, vel, in fine 976Apereunt, quod hic dicit non optando, sed prophetizando. (AUG.) Quia justus non delectatur de poena inimici, quia non eum odit, sed de divina justitia, quia Deum diligit, econtra injustus facit.

VERS. 11.-- Compeditorum. (AUG.) Corruptibilitate carnis, quae aggravat animam, per quam praevalet aliquando persecutor: has compedes non sentiunt nisi illi, qui ingemiscunt gravati; ab his cupiebat dissolvi Apostolus, et esse cum Christo. Vel, compedes sunt praecepta Dei, quibus colligantur sancti, quae patienter sustentata in ornamenta vertuntur, unde: Injice pedem tuum in compedes ejus (Eccli. VI). (CASS.) Compeditorum, ad litteram de his dicit, quos gentiles vinxerunt: qui cum gemitu orant, ut Ecclesia in fratribus non deficiat, et sic 976Beos poena consumit. Secundum magnitudinem. (AUG.) Res enim tam magna in Christianis secuta est, quam nunquam crederent inimici. Filios, quia accensi sunt exemplo, non territi. Posside filios mortificatorum. (ID.) Hoc semper oraverunt sancti martyres, ne infructuosus esset posteris sanguis eorum, ut inde cresceret seges, unde putabatur peritura. (CASS.) Pia precatio, ne filios eorum projiciat, qui pro eo puniti sunt. Posside, ne quo errore maculentur.

VERS. 12.-- Et redde. (CASS.) Etsi corporaliter reddit, salus est tamen animae eorum. Septuplum, perfectionem doni coelestis significat, quando Spiritu sancto replemur. In sinu. In secreto animorum, ubi fit conversio. Improperium, pro injuriis reddant laudes: gloriosa vindicatio, quando inimicorum ore 976Claudatur Deus. Vel septuplum. Septupla retributione perfectionem poenae significat, sicut et de bonis, cum dicitur septuplum accipiet in hoc saeculo: quod positum est pro omnibus bonis, quasi nihil habentes, et omnia possidentes; quia in hoc numero plenitudo significatur. Vel septuplum, pro infinito. Improperium, (AUG.) Hoc redde, id est, pro isto opprobrio da eos in reprobum sensum. Homo namque, cum datur in reprobum sensum, id est, in interiori sensu, accipit suppliciorum meritum futurorum.

VERS. 13.-- Nos autem. (CASS.) Conclusio exsultativa, non victorum, sed patientium. Et suavis conclusio lamentationis. (AUG.) Nos autem. Hae sunt reliquiae a Matathia congregatae. Vel, generaliter, de omni genere piorum ac verorum Christianorum 976Daccipiendum est, ut etiam Christianus populus ibi sit mistus; hic est grex pro quo oravit, ne diutius irasceretur. (ID.) Vel, in generatione, id est, in futuro saeculo annuntiabimus, non pro aliorum instructione, sed pro debito honore.

PSAL. LXXVIII.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of Asaph. (CASS.) The second psalm of lamentation. He prays Christ to come to the help of the nation which for its hardness is to be grievously 974Dafflicted. We are admonished to rejoice at the good things of our neighbours, and to be afflicted at their calamities.

O God, the nations are come. (ID.) The first thing is the complaint, and there are numbered how great things Jerusalem bore in the times of Antiochus, when it was not destroyed, and by these the persecution of the Church is signified. (AUG.) They are come. He does not speak as to one that knows not, etc., as far as but now they are plainly fulfilled.

Into thy inheritance. (ID.) Of the people of Israel; the inheritance of God are the elect, but not the blinded; therefore these things can be said of the times after the ascension of Christ; but also before Christ had come, for then too there was an inheritance, where the Prophets were, and the saints led away into Babylon; or most of all under Antiochus. (CASS.) But if 975Aany man, etc., as far as whose circuit is through the whole world, where the persecution also is.

VERS. 2.-- The dead bodies. (CASS.) Carcases, as though they raged not only against the living. To bury belongs to piety, to cast forth belongs to cruelty. They have poured out. (ID.) He heightens it, that he may move the judge.

VERS. 4.-- We are become. (CASS.) The glory of Jerusalem, wonderful in the whole world, is turned into a reproach to our neighbours, which is heavier than if it were to men far off, because these are always at hand. Or, the neighbours are the affections, the kinsfolk being now willing to believe, so that the martyrs say this.

VERS. 5.-- How long, O Lord? (CASS.) A prayer on his own behalf against enemies and insulting neighbours; as though they rage thus: But, O Lord, how long? (AUG.) He asks that he be not angry unto the end, that is, that 975Bthat laying waste may not continue, but that he temper his correction. By the name of wrath is understood the vengeance upon iniquity, by the name of jealousy, the exacting of chastity, that the soul may not commit fornication away from God. Note that this befalls men for their sins, though they be just, as the three children and the Prophets in the captivity bear witness. As fire. (ID.) Burn so long, until the gold of the virtues be perfectly purged, and the wood, that is the vices, be turned to ashes.

VERS. 7.-- They have devoured. (AUG.) By delivering them to the teeth of wild beasts. They have laid waste, by the overthrow of the city, which was stripped of its own citizens, or because they slew those put in the place of the citizens who had been slain; Jacob for the man, the man, that is, for the nation which offended. The patriarch is pleasing, that the memory of him may soften the sins of the people. Jacob. (AUG.) This is the inheritance spoken of above. The place. (CASS.) The city, where the temple was, to which they were gathered for the feasts.

975CVERS. 8.-- Of our iniquities. (BEDA.) That is, those which we have contracted from our fathers, to whom, that is to say, correction is no longer owed, but damnation, unless the compassion of thy grace be at hand. For it is written: The soul that shall sin, the same shall die. And, I will visit the sins of the fathers upon the children, unto the third and fourth generation (Ezech. XVIII.) Of old. [Vulg. Ex 20:5 visitans iniquitatem patrum in filios, in tertiam et quartam generationem, "visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children"] (CASS.) He does not speak of past ones only, since in this time also certain Jews were following idols; but of the like of the ancient ones, in which they sinned through countless years. Let them prevent us. (ID.) Before the judgment which every man fears, because unless indulgence go before in the judgment, the guilty man is not acquitted. Exceedingly. Lest any man presume upon his deeds.

VERS. 9.-- Help us. (CASS.) In the war for the defence of the laws, because they trust not in their own powers, but in the powers of God. 975DFor the glory. Not for our merit; that, being delivered, we may render honour to thy name. For the glory of thy name. Let it be ascribed to the goodness of the holy name, not to us, since it cannot be had by our own deeds. Help us, O God. By this he is neither ungrateful to grace, nor does he take away free choice. For he who is helped does something also through himself. Deliver us. (AUG.) He delivers, that is, he rescues from evils, since he both helps us to do righteousness, and is propitious to the sins without which there is no living here.

VERS. 10.-- Lest perhaps. (AUG.) That word customary with the faithless: Where is he? Either he is not, or he cannot; an insult not to be borne. Let it be made known. Either here iniquity is destroyed in those converted, which he had wished for before, or, at the end 976Athey perish, which he says here not by wishing it, but by prophesying. (AUG.) Because the just man is not delighted at the punishment of his enemy, since he does not hate him, but at the divine justice, since he loves God; the unjust man does the contrary.

VERS. 11.-- Of them that are in fetters. (AUG.) By the corruptibility of the flesh, which weighs down the soul, and through which the persecutor sometimes prevails: these fetters none feel save those who groan being burdened; from these the Apostle desired to be loosed, and to be with Christ. Or, the fetters are the commandments of God, by which the saints are bound together, which, patiently borne, are turned into ornaments, whence: Put thy foot into her fetters (Eccli. VI). (CASS.) Of them that are in fetters, he speaks according to the letter of those whom the Gentiles bound: who pray with groaning that the Church may not fail in her brethren, and so 976Bthe punishment consumes them. According to the greatness. (AUG.) For a thing so great followed among Christians as the enemies would never have believed. The children, because they were kindled by the example, not terrified. Possess the children of them that have been put to death. (ID.) This the holy martyrs always prayed, that their blood might not be unfruitful to those that came after, that the crop might grow from that whence it was thought that it would perish. (CASS.) A godly prayer, that he cast not away the children of those who were punished for him. Possess, that they be stained by no error.

VERS. 12.-- And render. (CASS.) Although he renders it bodily, yet it is the salvation of their souls. Sevenfold, it signifies the perfection of the heavenly gift, when we are filled with the Holy Spirit. Into their bosom. In the secret place of the mind, where conversion takes place. Their reproach, let them render praises for injuries: a glorious vindication, when God is praised by the mouth 976Cof his enemies. Or sevenfold. By the sevenfold retribution he signifies the perfection of the punishment, as also of good things, when it is said that he shall receive sevenfold in this world: which is set down for all good things, as having nothing, and possessing all things; because in this number fulness is signified. Or sevenfold, for what is without end. Their reproach, (AUG.) Render this, that is, for that reproach give them up to a reprobate sense. For man, when he is given up to a reprobate sense, that is, in his inward sense, receives the desert of the punishments to come.

VERS. 13.-- But we. (CASS.) A conclusion of exultation, not of conquerors, but of sufferers. And a sweet conclusion of the lamentation. (AUG.) But we. These are the remnant gathered by Matathias. Or, generally, it is to be taken of every kind of the godly and of true Christians, 976Dso that the Christian people also is mingled there; this is the flock for which he prayed, that he might not be angry any longer. (ID.) Or, in the generation, that is, in the world to come we shall declare it, not for the instruction of others, but for the honour that is due.

PSALMUS LXXIX.

VERS. 1.-- Intellectus pro his qui commutabuntur. (AUG.) In melius, etc., usque ad testimonium perfidiae. Asaph. Illuminatur agit de adventu Christi et de vinea ejus, bonum testimonium de capite ipso et corpore ejus, rege et plebe, pastore grege.

VERS. 2.-- Qui regis, etc. (AUG.) Hic loquitur Asaph illuminatus de adventu Christi, qui convertit 977Ahominem, et vineam de Aegypto eductam solidat: hoc est testimonium pro his qui immutantur. (CASS.) Supra trepidus, qui pro peccatis Synagogae orabat: jam praesumit, commutatis in melius testimonium dat. Hic psalmus Synagogae est testimonium de capite ipso, et corpore ejus. (ID.) Deprecatio primi adventus, per quem fit reparatio generis humani. (ID.) Peractus definit. O Deus, fili. Qui regis, spiritualiter, Israel, videntes te, Intende, id est, lumen pietatis super nos infunde, ut a te simus clari, qui per nos sumus tenebrosi. Joseph. (ID.) Fidelem populum ducis in caulas Dei, ut oves ad pascua, de quibus: Alias oves habeo quae non sunt de hoc ovili, et illas oportet me adducere, ut fiat unum ovile et unus pastor (Joan. X). Propria singulis verba: regitur Israel, 977Bducitur Joseph, id est, devotus populus. Manifestare. (ID.) Rogat, ut qui in secreto majestatis erat per incarnationem, appareat coram Judaeis ut promissum erat, faciens in eis has virtutes, quae his nominibus signantur, Ephraim, Benjamin, et Manasse. (AUG.) Manifestare coram. Angelis notus, innotesce hominibus.

VERS. 3.-- Coram Ephraim. (AUG.) Id est, gente Judaeorum, ubi hae tribus, scilicet coram fructificatione, et filio dexterae, ut et nos simus plenitudo scientiae per charitatem, quae Deus est; et coram Manasse, id est, oblito, ut jam illi venias in mentem, juxta illud: Reminiscentur, et convertentur universi fines terrae. (ID.) Excita. Repetit, etc., usque ad crucifixus ex infirmitate, resurge ex virtute. 977C(CASS.) Excita potentiam miraculorum, etc., usque ad unde: Fidelis Deus, qui non patitur vos tentari supra id quod potestis, etc. (I Cor. X).

VERS. 4.-- Faciem tuam. (AUG.) Haec facies velata fuit Asaph tempore infirmitatis Christi, et tunc aegrotavit Asaph, non valens intueri velatum nube: de qua dicitur: Ascendit Deus super nubem levem, et intrabit vel ingredietur Aegyptum, id est, carnem immunem a peccato; illuminavit vero eam cum surrexit et ascendit, et ita salvamur.

VERS. 5.-- Quousque irasceris? (AUG.) Transit ira a servo, ut non flagellet ut patet, sed ne damnet: et conversis enim durat ira, sed corrigens. Flagellat enim omnem filium quem recipit (Isa. IX, Heb. XII).

VERS. 6.-- Cibabis (AUG.) Exponit hic passiones, 977Dquas sancti tempore adventus passuri sunt. Quasi diceret: Etsi optem Christi adventum, tamen eo tempore multa passuri sumus, quia cibavit, etc. In mensura, etc. (AUG.) Pro viribus tuis ut erudiaris, non opprimaris; unde: Fidelis Deus qui non patitur vos tentari supra, etc. (I Cor. X). Vel, pro modo culparum.

VERS. 7.-- Posuisti nos in contradictionem. (CASS.) Dum vicini, qui de nobis, sunt contra nos. Irrident inimici, a quibus omnibus, ut salvi simus, Deus virtutum, etc.

VERS. 8.-- Deus virtutum. (AUG.) Desiderantis mos est frequenter repetere quae tantis precibus orat.

VERS. 9, 10.-- Vineam. (CASS.) De vinea quomodo 978Aincepta, et perfecta. (AUG. et CASS.) Vineam de Aegypto, quasi, nos salvi erimus, sed Judaeos, quibus tot fecisti, destrues: quod non pro levi culpa, sed quia adventum Christi non noverunt. Vel, salvi erimus quia ita praesignasti. Vineam de Aegypto. Sed quare, destrues? hoc de infidelibus. De Aegypto. Ut illos de Aegypto, ita Ecclesiam de tenebris ejecit vitiorum: gentes plantat in virtutibus, et ducit per hoc desertum saeculi. Radices, martyres et alios firmos facit, et implet orbem. (CASS.) Vineam de Aegypto, per mysticas figurationes, etc., usque ad quae ita per orbem dilatata est. Dux, dum eam ducit spirituali itinere. Radices, prophetas, Apostolos, martyres et alios, de quibus palmites tendens mundum occupat et operit. Dux itineris. (AUG.) Vel alia 978Blittera, etc., usque ad et non est altera, sed eadem vinea: inde Apostoli, inde et alii justi, etsi aliqui rami fracti.

VERS. 11, 12-- Operuit (CASS.) Altitudo et latitudo vineae hic exponitur. Superna est vinea, quae et montes sublimiores, vita et doctrina obumbrat, et magnis crescere facit. Vites, quae arbores ascendunt, arbusta nominantur, per quae minores in Ecclesia accipiuntur. Cedri, non superbi, sed qui sunt Dei, martyres sunt, qui in Ecclesia alti sunt, hos etiam Ecclesia in gremio suo protegit. Propagines, filios regenerationis, qui a flumine Jordane manaverunt, quia ibi coepit regula baptismi. Montes. (AUG.) Prophetae, etc., usque ad similiter operiunt cedros Dei, id est, doctores. Cedros Dei. (ID.) Quia sunt cedri 978Cevertendae, superbi scilicet qui sunt cedri saeculi, sed non Dei.

VERS. 13.-- Ut quid. Miratur cur huic tali subtracta est Domini defensio. (AUG.) Ut quid. Quia superba fuit adversus plantatorem, et servos occidit ad se missos, et tandem filium haeredem, destructa est maceria, et invenerunt eam gentes destructam, et deleverunt. Hoc primo plangit Asaph, sed non sine spe: de dirigentibus enim cor jam loquitur.

VERS. 14.-- Aper. (AUG. et CASS.) Vespasianus fortis et saevus, et contrarius Judaeis, qui hoc animal inter caetera habent immundum. Singularis ferus. Titus, qui reliquias terribili depastione consumpsit, qui dicitur singularis, id est superbus. Vel pro eodem accipitur aper, et ferus scilicet Romanus exercitus. 978DEt vide quibus peccatis laboret et pereat homo. Singularis. (AUG.) Dicit omnis superbus: Ego sum, ego sum, et nemo alius. Aper. (CASS.) Diabolus fortis et ferox, de silva, quia cogitationes ejus agrestes et aviae sunt. Sed tu, Domine Deus virtutum. Vel ita continua: Ita vastata est vinea, sed ut reliquiae salvae sint, O Deus virtutum, convertere, in finem saeculi supremi serenus aspice, commutatis in melius hoc remedium precatur.

VERS. 16.-- Et perfice eam quam plantavit dextera tua. (AUG.) Non aliam institue, sed hanc perfice. In hac enim est semen Abrahae: ibi est radix quae portat oleastrum. Perfice, quia caecitas ex parte contigit in Israel, ut plenitudo gentium intraret, et sic omnis 979AIsrael salvus fieret (Rom. XII). Super filium. (CASS.) Super et fundatam, etc., usque ad de igne autem boni amoris dicitur: Ignem veni mittere in terram, et quid volo, nisi ut ardeat? (Luc. XII.)

VERS. 18.-- Fiat manus. (CASS.) Grande sacramentum, et munus Deo, quia tandiu salus Israel dubitari potuit, donec Christus venit: sed tunc completa est promissio, nec ultra discedit ab eo Ecclesia sponso conjuncta. Dicit ergo: Fiat manus, operationem sanctae incarnationis precatur.

VERS. 19.-- Non discedimus. (CASS.) Ultra, cum filium hominis vivificabis: haec est utilitas ab eo.

VERS. 20.-- Domine Deus virtutum, converte nos, ostende faciem tuam, et salvi erimus. (CASS.) Magna suavitas hujus versiculi, in quo regulam totius religionis 979Bexponit. Primo enim Deus nos convertit, et tunc nos ante faciem ostendit, id est, lumine pietatis nos inspicit: post quod nos tandem salvat. Hunc ergo propheta iterat, quia per ipsum quisque breviter quod expedit, implorat.

PSALM LXXIX.

VERS. 1.-- Understanding, for them that shall be changed. [Vulg. Ps 79:1 In finem, pro iis qui commutabuntur, "Unto the end, for them that shall be changed"] (AUG.) For the better, etc., as far as a testimony of faithlessness. Asaph. Being enlightened Illuminatur he treats of the coming of Christ and of his vineyard, a good testimony concerning the head himself and his body, the king and the people, the shepherd and the flock.

VERS. 2.-- Thou that rulest, etc. (AUG.) Here Asaph, enlightened, speaks of the coming of Christ, who converts 977Aman, and makes firm the vineyard brought out of Egypt: this is the testimony for them that are changed. (CASS.) Above he was fearful, who was praying for the sins of the Synagogue: now he presumes, and to those changed for the better he gives a testimony. This psalm is the testimony of the Synagogue concerning the head himself, and his body. (ID.) A prayer for the first coming, through which the reparation of the human race is made. (ID.) Being finished, he makes an end. O God, O Son. Thou that rulest, spiritually, Israel, who see thee, Give ear, that is, pour the light of goodness upon us, that we may be bright from thee, who of ourselves are dark. Joseph. (ID.) Thou leadest the faithful people into the folds of God, as sheep to the pastures, of whom: And other sheep I have that are not of this fold, and them I must bring, that there may be one fold and one shepherd (Joan. X). Each has its own proper word: Israel is ruled, 977BJoseph is led, that is, the devout people. Be made manifest. (ID.) He asks that he who was in the secret of majesty may appear before the Jews through the incarnation, as it had been promised, working in them these powers which are signified by these names, Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasse. (AUG.) Be made manifest before. Known to the angels, be made known to men.

VERS. 3.-- Before Ephraim. (AUG.) That is, in the nation of the Jews, where these tribes are, namely before fruitfulness, and before the son of the right hand, that we also may be the fulness of knowledge through charity, which is God; and before Manasse, that is, the forgotten one, that thou mayest now come into his mind, according to that saying: All the ends of the earth shall remember, and shall be converted. (ID.) Stir up. He repeats, etc., as far as crucified through weakness, rise again through power. 977C(CASS.) Stir up thy power of miracles, etc., as far as whence: God is faithful, who suffereth you not to be tempted above that which you are able, etc. (I Cor. X).

VERS. 4.-- Thy face. (AUG.) This face was veiled to Asaph in the time of the weakness of Christ, and then Asaph was sick, not being able to look upon him veiled with a cloud: of which it is said: God ascended upon a light cloud, [Vulg. Is 19:1 Ecce Dominus ascendet super nubem levem, "behold, the Lord will ascend upon a light cloud"] and he shall enter, or shall go into, Egypt, that is, flesh free from sin; but he enlightened it when he rose again and ascended, and so we are saved.

VERS. 5.-- How long wilt thou be angry? (AUG.) Wrath passes from the servant, that he may not scourge, as is plain, but that he may not condemn: for wrath endures even toward those converted, but as a wrath that corrects. For he scourgeth every son whom he receiveth (Isa. IX, Heb. XII).

VERS. 6.-- Thou wilt feed (AUG.) Here he sets forth the sufferings 977Dwhich the saints are to suffer at the time of the coming. As though he said: Although I long for the coming of Christ, yet at that time we are to suffer many things, because he fed, etc. In measure, etc. (AUG.) According to thy strength, that thou mayest be instructed, not crushed; whence: God is faithful, who suffereth you not to be tempted above, etc. (I Cor. X). Or, according to the measure of faults.

VERS. 7.-- Thou hast made us a contradiction. (CASS.) While our neighbours, who are of us, are against us. Our enemies mock us, from all of whom, that we may be saved, O God of hosts, etc.

VERS. 8.-- O God of hosts. (AUG.) It is the way of one who desires, to repeat often what he prays for with such prayers.

VERS. 9, 10.-- A vineyard. (CASS.) Of the vineyard, how it was 978Abegun, and perfected. (AUG. et CASS.) A vineyard out of Egypt, as if to say, we shall be saved, but thou wilt destroy the Jews, for whom thou didst so much: and that not for a light fault, but because they did not know the coming of Christ. Or, we shall be saved because thou hast so foreshown it. A vineyard out of Egypt. But why wilt thou destroy? this is of the unbelieving. Out of Egypt. As he cast out those men from Egypt, so he cast the Church out of the darkness of vices: he plants the Gentiles in virtues, and leads them through this desert of the world. The roots, he makes the martyrs and others firm, and fills the world. (CASS.) A vineyard out of Egypt, through mystical figures, etc., as far as which has been so spread abroad through the world. A guide, while he leads her by a spiritual journey. The roots, the prophets, the Apostles, the martyrs and others, from whom, stretching out her branches, she takes and covers the world. A guide of the way. (AUG.) Or another 978Breading, etc., as far as and it is not another, but the same vineyard: thence the Apostles, thence also the other just men, although some branches were broken off.

VERS. 11, 12-- It covered (CASS.) The height and the breadth of the vineyard are here set forth. The vineyard is from above, which overshadows even the loftier mountains with life and doctrine, and makes them grow great. Vines that climb trees are called bushes, by which the lesser ones in the Church are understood. Cedars, not the proud, but those that are God's, are the martyrs, who are high in the Church, and these too the Church protects in her bosom. The shoots, the sons of regeneration, who flowed from the river Jordan, because there the rule of baptism began. The mountains. (AUG.) The prophets, etc., as far as likewise they cover the cedars of God, that is, the doctors. The cedars of God. (ID.) Because there are cedars 978Cto be overthrown, namely the proud, who are the cedars of the world, but not of God.

VERS. 13.-- Why. He wonders why the defence of the Lord was withdrawn from such a one as this. (AUG.) Why. Because she was proud against the planter, and slew the servants sent to her, and at last the son and heir, the fence was destroyed, and the nations found her destroyed, and blotted her out. This Asaph first bewails, but not without hope: for he speaks now of those who direct their heart.

VERS. 14.-- The boar. (AUG. et CASS.) Vespasian, strong and savage, and hostile to the Jews, who among other creatures hold this beast unclean. A singular wild beast. Titus, who consumed the remnant with a terrible devouring, who is called singular, that is, proud. Or the boar and the wild beast are taken for the same thing, namely the Roman army. 978DAnd see by what sins man labours and perishes. Singular. (AUG.) Every proud man says: I am, I am, and there is none other. The boar. (CASS.) The devil, strong and fierce, out of the wood, because his thoughts are wild and trackless. But thou, O Lord God of hosts. Or continue it thus: So the vineyard was laid waste, but that the remnant may be saved, O God of hosts, turn again, and at the end of the last age serenely behold, he prays this remedy for those changed for the better.

VERS. 16.-- And perfect thou that which thy right hand hath planted. (AUG.) Set up no other, but perfect this one. For in this is the seed of Abraham: there is the root that bears the wild olive. Perfect it, because blindness in part has happened in Israel, that the fulness of the Gentiles might come in, and so all 979AIsrael should be saved (Rom. XII) [Vulg. Rom 11:25 donec plenitudo gentium intraret, "until the fulness of the Gentiles should come in"]. Upon the son. (CASS.) Founded upon and [et; read te, "thee"], etc., as far as but of the fire of good love it is said: I am come to send fire on the earth, and what will I, but that it burn? (Luc. XII.) [Vulg. Lc 12:49 nisi ut accendatur, "but that it be kindled"]

VERS. 18.-- Let thy hand be. (CASS.) A great sacrament, and a gift to God, because the salvation of Israel could be doubted so long, until Christ came: but then the promise was fulfilled, nor does the Church, joined to her spouse, depart from him any more. He says therefore: Let thy hand be, he prays for the working of the holy incarnation.

VERS. 19.-- We depart not. (CASS.) Any more, when thou shalt quicken the son of man: this is the profit that comes from him.

VERS. 20.-- O Lord God of hosts, convert us, show thy face, and we shall be saved. (CASS.) Great is the sweetness of this little verse, in which he sets forth the rule of the whole of religion. 979BFor first God converts us, and then he shows us before his face, that is, he looks upon us with the light of his goodness: after which he at last saves us. This verse therefore the prophet repeats, because through it each man briefly implores what is profitable.

PSALMUS LXXX.

VERS. 1.-- Pro torcularibus. (AUG.) In quibus tria, etc., usque ad cantatur psalmus Asaph, id est, Dominicae congregationi. Asaph, etc. (CASS.) Quia secundum historiam Judaeis, spiritualiter Christianis loquitur. (AUG.) Primo dicit quid agendum electis, qui sunt, oleum, vinum, aves.

VERS. 2.-- Exsultat Deo. Asaph, proposita sibi imagine cujusdam solemnitatis, electos ad celebritatem 979Cincitat.

VERS. 3.-- Sumite psalmum. (AUG.) Verba Dei, ut humani actus conveniant in unam societatem: haec enim est pax Jerusalem, haec est ratio dati et accepti; unde Apostolus: Si spiritualia seminavimus vobis, magnum est si carnalia vestra metamus (I Cor. IX).

VERS. 4.-- Buccinate. (AUG.) Hucusque ad partitionem, vel ad litteram, simpliciter de Judaeis accipienda sunt, vel allegorice de Christianis. (AUG.) Buccinate, et annuntiate, etc., usque ad unde Isaias: Clama ne cesses, ut tuba exalta vocem tuam, etc. In neomenia tuba. (CASS.) In initio mensis jussi sunt Judaei tuba canere, id est, in initio novae lunae, quod et festum tubarum dicitur, quod celebrabant 979Din memoriam istius rei, quod Dominus ostendit Abrahae arietem inter vepres haerentem, quem pro Isaac immolavit.

VERS. 5.-- Quia praeceptum in Israel est; et judicium, etc. (ID.) Ideo tuba canendum, quia lex data est Judaeis per Moysen, et quia judex futurus est.

VERS. 6.-- In Joseph. (AUG.) Gentes sunt Joseph, etc., usque ad ubi debebat habere cor.

VERS. 7.-- Ab oneribus. (AUG.) Quibus oneribus, manus in cophino, id est, servili opere. Peccata servilia opera sunt, juxta illud: Qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati (Joan. VIII). In cophino servierunt. (ID.) In immunditiis peccatorum, in terrenis operibus et lutosis.

980AVERS. 8.-- In tribulatione, etc. (CASS.) Sic Propheta: Divertit Dominus dicens, In tribulatione, imputantur eis beneficia Dei, ut gravior aestimetur offensa. Exaudivi te in abscondito. (AUG.) Ut corde credas ad justitiam. Probavi, ut ore fiat confessio ad salutem. Tempestatis, etc. Non in tempestate maris, sed cordis: ubi exauditus debet probari, in aqua contradictionis: jam enim gradiens viam Dei, habet multis modis obsistentes. Haec est aqua contradictionis, quam senserunt antiqui, sed jam bene siccata est: tunc enim aquae populorum turbabantur, et acriter resistebant. Tunc Samsoni forti viro, id est Christo, ducere eunti uxorem de alienigenis, id est Ecclesiam de gentibus, occurrit leo fremens, id est populus gentium, sed dissipavit eum, ut haedum 980Bcaprarum: et quia populus iste fremens nihil erat, nisi languidus peccator. Occisa autem in eo illa feritate, jam non sic fremit, imo jam in ipso invenimus leges pro Ecclesia, quasi favum in ore leonis. Aqua contradictionis. Christus fuit etiam in seipso, ut de eo nato dictum est: Erit hic in ruinam, et resurrectionem multorum, in signum cui contradicetur (Luc. II), ut Judaei contradixerunt titulo crucis.

VERS. 9.-- Audi populus meus. (CASS.) Diapsalma. Hactenus de oleo torcularium, jam de amurca, quod dicitur ad cavendum, hic arguuntur reprobi. Contestabor te. Ipse Dominus judicii testem se facit veritatis, tam hic quam in futuro, ut nullus dubitet. Deinde quid velit eum intelligere, subdit: Israel si me audieris, vocando eum Israel, familiarem sibi 980Csignificat, et ad jussa invitat. In te, in corde tuo ubi veritas, non falsitas debet esse. Recens ne verbum Patris putetur sub tempore. Deum alienum, qui nomine, non essentia. Alienum: Pene par est scelus recentem Deum putare, et idolis servire.

VERS. 10.-- Non erit in te Deus recens neque, etc. (AUG.) Alii faciunt sibi recentes deos, vel idola, vel Christum imparem Patri, et alia hujusmodi fingunt in corde: et ita sunt templa simulacrorum in omnibus terrena cogitatio; opinio diversa, vanitas una. Ideo Samson caudas vulpium colligavit, ut incenderet messes Philisthaeorum. Samson interpretatur sol eorum, scilicet, quibus ipse lucet, non omnium: de quo mali dicturi sunt: Erravimus a via veritatis, et sol justitiae non illuxit nobis (Sap. V). Et alibi: Sol 980Djustitiae est, et sanitas in pennis ejus (Malac. IV). Vulpes sunt insidiosi, maxime haeretici, latentes in tortuosis cavernis, decipientes, odore putentes: qui etsi dissentire ab invicem videntur, in malum tamen, id est, in posterioribus consentiunt, simili vanitate tenentur, et incendunt messes non nostrorum, quia novit Deus qui sunt ejus; sed alienigenarum, quae sunt vasa contumeliae.

VERS. 11.-- Qui eduxi te. Factis propriis indicatur Deus.

VERS. 13.-- Et dimisit. Et si implevi ora Prophetarum, non tamen ab amurca auditi sunt, unde digna ultio: quia et dimisi, etc.

VERS. 15.-- Pro nihilo forsitan. (CASS.) Si Deo 981Aresistemus, ipse non contradicit inimicis nostris, nec manum defensionis super eos ponit.

VERS. 16.-- Inimici Domini, etc. (AUG.) Haec item Propheta. Mentiti. Non per agentes promissa: hoc non pagani, quia nihil promiserunt.

VERS. 17.-- Ex adipe frumenti, etc. (AUG.) Ad litteram, vel manna, vel corpore Christi, vel spirituali intellectu.

PSALM LXXX.

VERS. 1.-- For the winepresses. (AUG.) In which there are three things, etc., as far as a psalm is sung for Asaph, that is, for the Lord's congregation. Asaph, etc. (CASS.) Because according to the history he speaks to the Jews, spiritually to Christians. (AUG.) First he says what is to be done by the elect, who are the oil, the wine, the birds.

VERS. 2.-- He rejoiceth in God. [Vulg. Ps 80:2 Exsultate Deo adjutori nostro, the plural imperative, "rejoice ye in God our helper"] Asaph, having set before himself the image of a certain solemnity, 979Cstirs up the elect to the festival.

VERS. 3.-- Take a psalm. (AUG.) The words of God, that human acts may come together into one fellowship: for this is the peace of Jerusalem, this is the reckoning of what is given and what is received; whence the Apostle: If we have sown unto you spiritual things, is it a great matter if we reap your carnal things (I Cor. IX).

VERS. 4.-- Blow the trumpet. (AUG.) Thus far, up to the division, these things are to be taken either according to the letter, simply of the Jews, or allegorically of Christians. (AUG.) Blow the trumpet, and declare, etc., as far as whence Isaias: Cry, cease not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, etc. On the new moon with the trumpet. (CASS.) At the beginning of the month the Jews were bidden to sound the trumpet, that is, at the beginning of the new moon, which is also called the feast of trumpets, which they celebrated 979Din memory of that thing, that the Lord showed Abraham the ram sticking among the briers, which he offered up in the place of Isaac.

VERS. 5.-- For it is a commandment in Israel; and a judgment, etc. (ID.) Therefore the trumpet must be sounded, because the law was given to the Jews through Moses, and because he is to be their judge.

VERS. 6.-- In Joseph. (AUG.) The Gentiles are Joseph, etc., as far as where he ought to have had a heart.

VERS. 7.-- From the burdens. (AUG.) By what burdens: hands in the basket, that is, by servile work. Sins are servile works, according to that saying: Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin (Joan. VIII). They served in the basket. (ID.) In the uncleannesses of sins, in earthly and miry works.

980AVERS. 8.-- In tribulation, etc. (CASS.) So the Prophet: the Lord turns aside, saying, In tribulation, the benefits of God are reckoned to them, that the offence may be judged the heavier. I heard thee in the secret place. (AUG.) That with the heart thou mayest believe unto justice. I proved thee, that with the mouth confession may be made unto salvation. Of the storm, etc. Not in the storm of the sea, but of the heart: where he that is heard must be proved, in the water of contradiction: for he that already walks the way of God has men withstanding him in many ways. This is the water of contradiction, which the ancients felt, but now it is well dried up: for then the waters of the peoples were troubled, and resisted fiercely. Then to Samson, that strong man, that is, to Christ, going to take a wife from among the strangers, that is, the Church from among the Gentiles, there met a roaring lion, that is, the people of the Gentiles, but he tore him in pieces as a kid 980Bof the goats: and because that roaring people was nothing but a sickly sinner. But when that fierceness had been slain in him, he no longer roars so; nay, in that very people we now find laws in favour of the Church, as it were a honeycomb in the mouth of the lion. The water of contradiction. Christ was so even in himself, as it was said of him when he was born: This one shall be unto the ruin, and the resurrection of many, for a sign which shall be contradicted (Luc. II) [Vulg. Lc 2:34 Ecce positus est hic in ruinam et in resurrectionem multorum in Israel, "behold, this child is set for the ruin and for the resurrection of many in Israel"], as the Jews contradicted the title of the cross.

VERS. 9.-- Hear, O my people. (CASS.) Diapsalma. Thus far of the oil of the winepresses, now of the lees, which is said by way of warning; here the reprobate are reproved. I will testify unto thee. The Lord himself makes himself the witness of the judgment of truth, both here and in the world to come, that none may doubt. Then he adds what he would have him understand: Israel, if thou wilt hearken to me; and by calling him Israel he signifies one familiar to himself, 980Cand invites him to his commands. In thee, in thy heart, where truth, not falsehood, ought to be. New, lest the Word of the Father be thought to be under time. A strange god, one that is such in name, not in essence. Strange: It is well-nigh an equal crime to think God new, and to serve idols.

VERS. 10.-- There shall be no new god in thee, neither, etc. (AUG.) Some make themselves new gods, either idols, or a Christ unequal to the Father, and feign other such things in the heart: and so in all of them earthly thought is the temple of idols; the opinion is various, the vanity one. Therefore Samson bound together the tails of the foxes, that he might set fire to the harvests of the Philistines. Samson is interpreted their sun, namely of those to whom he himself shines, not of all: of whom the wicked shall say: We have erred from the way of truth, and the sun of justice hath not shined upon us (Sap. V) [Vulg. Sap 5:6 justitiae lumen non luxit nobis, et sol intelligentiae non est ortus nobis, "the light of justice hath not shined unto us, and the sun of understanding hath not risen upon us"]. And elsewhere: He is the sun 980Dof justice, and health is in his wings (Malac. IV). The foxes are the treacherous, and most of all the heretics, lurking in winding caverns, deceiving, stinking with their smell: who, although they seem to disagree with one another, yet agree in evil, that is, in their hinder parts, and are held by a like vanity, and burn the harvests, not of our own, because God knows who are his, but of the strangers, which are vessels of dishonour.

VERS. 11.-- Who brought thee out. God is pointed out by his own deeds.

VERS. 13.-- And he let them go. And although I filled the mouths of the Prophets, yet they were not heard by the lees, whence a fitting vengeance: because and I let them go, etc.

VERS. 15.-- Perhaps for nothing. (CASS.) If we shall resist God, 981Ahe himself does not contradict our enemies, nor does he lay the hand of defence upon them.

VERS. 16.-- The enemies of the Lord, etc. (AUG.) These things likewise the Prophet. They have lied. Not through men performing what was promised: this the pagans do not, because they promised nothing.

VERS. 17.-- With the fat of corn, etc. (AUG.) According to the letter, either of the manna, or of the body of Christ, or with a spiritual understanding.

PSALMUS LXXXI.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus Asaph. (CASS.) Psalmus de duabus naturis in Christo, quo Christus, vel Propheta loquens, exprobrat ipsi Asaph, id est, Synagogae, quae Dominum corporaliter vidit, et tamen eum non cognovit. Primo nuntiat Deum stetisse, et 981Barguit contrarios, stat homo, discernit Deus. Deus stetit. Cujus non est stare, qui coelum et terram complet, qui est intra omnia non inclusus, extra omnia non exclusus, sed breviter Deum hominem indicat. Stetit. (AUG.) Filius, qui missus ad oves domus Israel, spiritualis autem praesentia Deitatis, quae ubique non proprie ad Synagogam pertinet, nec tempore variatur. Cur ibi stetit: Ecce deos dijudicat, id est, secundum quod Deus, id est, non meritis, sed gratia discernit vasa, alia in honorem, alia in contumeliam. Hoc autem facit stans in medio, unde: Medius vestrum stetit, quem vos nescitis, unde et hic: Nescierunt neque intellexerunt, sed amicus sponsi stat et audit, et gaudio gaudet Deorum. Quos post filios Excelsi dicit, ibi: Ego dixi: dii estis, et 981Cfiliis Excelsi omnes. Unde etiam, filios enutrivi et exaltavi, ipsi autem spreverunt me. Filii dicuntur non solum gratia novi testamenti, sed gratia veteris, quae eos de Aegypto liberavit.

VERS. 2.-- Usquequo. (AUG.) Haec est vox discernentis: misit legem et Prophetas, et restitistis, sed quousque? Num usque ad adventum misi Prophetas, et injuriis affecistis, vel interfecistis, vel hoc agentibus consensistis? Sed cum haec agentibus nec loqui dignum sit, vos qui tacuistis, et imitari eos voluistis, usquequo judicatis iniquitatem et facies peccatorum sumitis? Num et haeres occidendus est, qui pro vobis venit, qui pro vobis sine patre esse voluit ut pupillus? qui propter vos esurivit et sitivit, ut egenus, qui propter vos pauper factus est, cum esset dives.

981DVERS. 3.-- Judicate egeno et pupillo, pauperem et humilem justificate. (CASS.) Diapsalma, monet intelligeret Christum esse Deum, et si egenus et pauper fuit, quod eos non fecisse dicit.

VERS. 4.-- Eripite pauperem. (AUG.) Ostendit, nec illos immunes qui permiserunt principibus Christum, cum prae multitudine timerentur, et possent illos a facto, et se a consensu liberare. (CASS.) Qui enim desinit obviare cum potest, consentit.

VERS. 5.-- Movebuntur. (CASS.) Hinc patet de quo dixerat: hoc signum in crucifixione contigit. Vel spiritualiter, terreni moti sunt illo tempore, viso tanto miraculo; ut centurio, qui dixit: Vere Filius Dei erat iste. (AUG.) Movebuntur omnia fundamenta. 982AQuasi dicat per hanc Israel caecitatem, movebuntur ad fidem, omnia fundamenta terrae, id est, plenitudo gentium intrabit. Vel, in morte, et passione Domini mota est terra. Vel fundamenta, id est, felices copia terrenorum movebuntur. Vel admirando coli pauperem mortuum. Vel cum contemptis terrenis sectando. Addit omnia, quia nullus est qui non miretur, vel convertatur. Terrenae autem felicitatis regnum est superbia, contra quam venit humilis Christus, exprobrans eis, quos vult facere altos per humilitatem, his verbis: Ego dixi: dii estis, vos boni: vos autem mali, sicut homines moriemini. Vel omnibus dicit: dii estis, id est, omnibus promisi coelestia; vos autem sicut homines primi, qui suasione peccaverunt, et vos majores sicut diabolus, qui superbia 982Bpeccavit.

VERS. 6.-- Ego dixi. (CASS.) Quid eis propositum? sed perierunt. Ego dixi: Nescierunt neque intellexerunt; tamen ego dixi. Has promissiones omnes accipiunt, si mandata custodiunt, ut sint filii et Dei: hoc ad justos; vos autem, hoc ad malos.

VERS. 7.-- Sicut homines. (AUG.) Quasi: Cum cito, sicut homines, sitis morituri, non inde corrigimini; sed ut diabolus, qui carne non moritur, extollimini, ut cadatis: quia per superbiam diabolicam inviderunt gloriae Christi, et viluit eis humilitas crucis. Sed, ut hoc vitium sanetur ex persona Prophetae, subditur: Surge Deus, etc., sicut unus. Turba quae cecidit dicitur unus, quia in superbia similis: Vos cadetis, sed:

982CVERS. 8.-- Surge Deus. (AUG.) Id est, damna istos, quia his repulsis, tu haereditabis. Vel judica mundum, quia tuus est, et hoc est, tu haereditabis.

PSALM LXXXI.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of Asaph. (CASS.) A psalm on the two natures in Christ, in which Christ, or the Prophet speaking, reproaches Asaph himself, that is, the Synagogue, which saw the Lord bodily, and yet did not know him. First he announces that God has stood, and 981Bconvicts the adversaries: man stands, God discerns. God hath stood. Whose part it is not to stand, who filleth heaven and earth, who is within all things not enclosed, outside all things not excluded; but briefly he indicates God as man. He hath stood. (AUG.) The Son, who was sent to the sheep of the house of Israel; but the spiritual presence of the Godhead, which, being everywhere, does not properly belong to the Synagogue, nor is varied by time. Why he stood there: Behold, he judgeth gods, [Vulg. Ps 81:1 in medio autem deos dijudicat, "but in the midst he judgeth the gods"] that is, according as he is God, that is, not by merits but by grace he distinguishes the vessels, some unto honour, some unto dishonour. But this he does standing in the midst, whence: There hath stood one in the midst of you, whom you know not, whence also here: They have not known, neither have they understood, but the friend of the bridegroom standeth and heareth, and rejoiceth with joy. Of gods. Whom afterwards he calls sons of the Most High, there: I have said: you are gods, and 981Call of you to the sons of the Most High. Whence also, I have brought up children and exalted them, but they have despised me. They are called sons not only by the grace of the New Testament, but by the grace of the Old, which delivered them out of Egypt.

VERS. 2.-- How long. (AUG.) This is the voice of him that discerneth: he sent the law and the Prophets, and you resisted; but how long? Did I send Prophets until the coming, and you afflicted them with injuries, or slew them, or consented to those who did this? But since it is not worthy even to speak to those who do such things, you who kept silence, and wished to imitate them, how long do you judge iniquity, and accept the persons of sinners? Is the heir also to be slain, who came for you, who for your sake willed to be without a father, as a fatherless child? who for your sake hungered and thirsted, as a needy man, who for your sake was made poor, when he was rich.

981DVERS. 3.-- Judge for the needy and the fatherless, justify the poor and the humble. [Vulg. Ps 81:3 humilem et pauperem justificate, the two transposed] (CASS.) Diapsalma, he admonishes that one should understand Christ to be God, even if he was needy and poor, which he says that they did not do.

VERS. 4.-- Rescue the poor. (AUG.) He shows that not even those are guiltless who left Christ to the princes, since they were feared on account of their multitude, and could have freed them from the deed, and themselves from consent. (CASS.) For he who ceases to withstand when he can, consents.

VERS. 5.-- They shall be moved. (CASS.) Hence it is plain of whom he had spoken: this sign happened at the crucifixion. Or spiritually, earthly men were moved at that time, so great a miracle being seen; as the centurion, who said: Indeed this was the Son of God. (AUG.) All the foundations shall be moved. 982AAs if he should say: through this blindness of Israel, shall be moved unto faith all the foundations of the earth, that is, the fulness of the Gentiles shall come in. Or, in the death and passion of the Lord the earth was moved. Or the foundations, that is, those made happy by abundance of earthly things, shall be moved. Or by wondering that a poor dead man is worshipped. Or by following after him, earthly things being despised. He adds all, because there is none who does not wonder, or is not converted. But the kingdom of earthly felicity is pride, against which the humble Christ came, reproaching them whom he wills to make high through humility, in these words: I have said: you are gods, you the good: but you the evil, shall die like men. Or he says to all: you are gods, that is, to all I promised heavenly things; but you as men, the first men, who sinned by persuasion, and you greater ones as the devil, who by pride 982Bsinned.

VERS. 6.-- I have said. (CASS.) What was set before them? but they perished. I have said: They have not known, neither have they understood; yet I have said. All receive these promises, if they keep the commandments, that they may be sons, and of God: this to the just; but you, this to the wicked.

VERS. 7.-- Like men. (AUG.) As if: Whereas you are quickly to die, like men, you are not corrected thereby; but like the devil, who dies not in the flesh, you are lifted up, that you may fall: because through diabolical pride they envied the glory of Christ, and the humility of the cross became vile to them. But, that this vice may be healed, there is subjoined in the person of the Prophet: Arise, O God, etc., as one. The crowd which fell is called one, because it is alike in pride: You shall fall, but:

982CVERS. 8.-- Arise, O God. (AUG.) That is, condemn these, because, these being cast off, thou shalt inherit. Or judge the world, because it is thine, and this is: thou shalt inherit.

PSALMUS LXXXII.

VERS. 1.-- Canticum psalmi. (CASS.) Quia in rebus actualibus, habenda est divina contemplatio. Deterret autem iniquos a persecutione populi Dei: bonos vero monet ad patientiam. Psalmus de adventu Christi ad judicium, ubi boni, qui hic patiuntur, coronabuntur, : mali vero, qui eos persequuntur. torquebuntur.

VERS. 2.-- Deus quis similis? (CASS.) Proposito timore futuri judicis, describit malitiam inimicorum. (AUG.) Deus quis similis? Etsi homo, ut alii; etsi 982Djudicatus, cum iniquis deputaris: quis similis, cum in claritate judicabis? ideo tunc ne taceas, qui primo tacuisti, et potestatem compescuisti, ut posses teneri et perimi. Deus quis similis? Non ad divinitatem hoc refertur, cui nullum hominem comparandum cogitavit. Ideo non ait: Quis similis est tibi? quod utique ad divinitatem referretur; sed dicit, Quis similis erit tibi? hoc ad formam servi referens, qua tunc caeteris dissimilis hominibus erit, quando judex in gloria apparebit; vel potest hoc referri ad divinitatem secundum quod dicit: O Deus, quis similis tibi? in potentia Deitatis: Christum enim, quem mali viderunt extra, iste videt intra, scilicet omnipotentem.

983AVERS. 3.-- Quoniam ecce, etc. (AUG.) Novissima tempora Antichristi designat, quando quae modo premuntur metu, in liberam vocem erumpent: quae vox quia irrationabilis erat, magis sonitus, quam locutio dicitur. Qui oderunt. (CASS.) Plures, sed unum caput Antichristus: quod elatum est, ut Deus dicatur.

VERS. 4.-- Super populum tuum. Caput suum extulerunt, sed non populum tuum depresserunt.

(AUG.) Super populum tuum. Irridenter hoc dicit: Non enim possunt nocere populo Dei pro quo est Deus, unde Apostolus: Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? (Rom. VIII.)

VERS. 5.-- Dixerunt venite. (AUG.) Ecce consilium, quo meditati sunt inania. Iste est ille sonus, 983Bqui non est sermo, sed inaniter strepit. De gente. (CASS.) Singulariter, quia omnes Christiani una gens, cum ex uno fonte baptismatis nati; vel omnes boni, quos ille Antichristus vocat unam gentem: ecce persecutio Antichristi, qui nomen Christianum quasi malum intendit tollere funditus.

VERS. 6.-- Testamentum disposuerunt. (AUG.) Testamentum, quippe in Scripturis non illud solum dicitur, quod non valet, nisi testatore mortuo, sed etiam omne pactum, et placitum quod inter vivos valet, testamentum vocatur, sicut Laban et Jacob testamentum fecerunt. Ita et mali inter se quasi pactum fecerunt, quod unanimiter bonos persequerentur.

VERS. 7.-- Tabernacula Idumaeorum. Exposuit 983Cquo studio malignaverunt: ostendit deinde jam qui sint malignantes, dicens: Tabernacula Idumaeorum, etc. Idumaeorum, et Ismaelitae. (CASS.) Per haec nomina, Christi inimicos declarat, qui temporibus Antichristi tot malis similantur: quia sicut isti contra Israel, ita illi contra Christianos tunc bellabunt. Moabitae (AUG., HIER.) Unde Moabitae, quem Lot ebrius de majore filia sua genuit. Agareni. Ab Agar, qui et proselyti interpretantur.

VERS. 8.-- Gebal. (AUG., HIER.) Vallis vana. Ge enim vallit, Bal, vana. Ammon. Unde Ammonitae, genuit Lot ebrius de filia sua minore.

Amalec. Filius Eliphaz primogeniti Esau, a quo Amalecitae.

VERS. 9.-- Assur, (AUG., HIER.) Ad litteram Nabuchodonosor, 983Dqui fuit rex Assyriorum. Idumaei. Terreni vel sanguinei. Ismaelitae. Obedientes sibi, non Deo, quia pravas cogitationes suas sequuntur. Moab, ex patre, quod in malo. Bonus, quidem pater, quo filia illicite usa est, sicut et lex bona est, si quis ea legitime utatur, non inceste. Agareni. Proselyti, id est, advenae, qui non cives, sed alieno animo subintrant, et inventa occasione nocendi se ostendunt. Gebal. Vallis vana, id est fallaciter humilis. Ammon. Populus turbidus, vel moeroris. Amalec. Populus lingens terram. Alienigenae. Licet latino nomine se indicent alienos, et ob hoc inimicos, tamen hebraice dicuntur Philisthiim, id est, cadentes potione, ut ebrii luxuria saeculari. Tyrus. Hebraice sor, tribulatio vel angustia, secundum 984Aillud. Tribulatio vel angustia in omnem animam hominis operantis malum. (Rom. II.) Assur. Deprimens, vel elatus. Lot. Declinans, angeli apostatae, filii declinationis, quia a veritate declinando in satellitium diaboli discesserunt, unde in Apocalypsi: Draco cecidit, et traxit secum tertiam partem stellarum, de quibus Apostolus: Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed adversus principatus et potestates (Ephes. VI).

VERS. 10.-- Madian. Declinans judicium. Sisara, exclusio gaudii. Jabin, sapiens, de quo: Ubi sapiens? ubi scriba? Cison, ubi victi fuerunt, duritia interpretatur. Endor, ubi perierunt, fons generationis. Et intelligitur generatio carnalis, non aqua baptismi regenerati. Oreb, siccitas, Zeb, lupus, Zebee, victima 984Blupi, non Dei. Salmana, umbra commotionis. Haec omnia congruunt malis, quos in bono vicit populus Dei. Fac illis sicut Madian, et Sisarae, sicut Jabin in torrente. (CASS.) De vindicta iniquorum; sicut omnes illi victi sunt in figura a populo Dei, sic istos precatur in veritate superari. Sicut Madian. (AUG.) Utpote illi, qui declinant judicium, se judicandos non putantes: et qui excludunt futurum judicium, et hi omnes in Cison, et in fonte Endor perierunt.

VERS. 12.-- Pone principes eorum sicut, etc. Haec omnibus communiter. Sed specialiter, pone principes eorum: hoc optat militibus Antichristi, qui non sunt convertendi.

VERS. 13.-- Haereditate possideamus sanctuarium Dei. (AUG.) Dei, invadunt ut suam.

984CVERS. 14.-- Ut rotam, et sicut stipulam ante faciem venti. (CASS.) Per hanc similitudinem, multas praedicit eorum calamitates.

Venti. Levitas peccantium vento comparatur, quia huc et illuc volitat.

VERS. 15.-- Ignis et flamma comburens montes. (AUG.) Congrue in judicio esse dicuntur, quando et densae silvae peccatorum, et montes superbiae cremabuntur.

VERS. 17.-- Imple facies. (CASS.) Poenis contumacium prophetatis, orat pro credituris, qui non habent scelerum laudatores, sed culpatores, quos saepe opprobrium corrigit. (AUG.) Melius est ruere ut poeniteat, quam sub spe religionis superbire: unde Propheta ait: Et tu, filia Sion, usque ad Babylonem venies, 984Dibique liberaberis (Mich. IV).

Imple facies. Hoc bonum et optabile eis non prophetaretur, nisi inter eos inimicos essent tales, quibus hoc ante judicium praestabitur: quia et nunc idem corpus sanat, et lavat caput, sed particulatim, non universaliter ut in fine: et tamen inde aliqui convertentur, pro quibus hic orat.

VERS. 18.-- Erubescant et conturbentur, etc. (AUG.) Hic de malis, qui non convertentur, Erubescant, in futuro de malis quae fecerunt. Et conturbentur, de poenis quas patientur. Et hoc in saeculum saeculi, id est in aeternum. Et conturbentur. Rursus redit ad eos qui in praesenti confundentur ne confundantur in aeternum; quasi dicat: Illi conturbentur in aeternum: quaerentes 985Aautem nomen Domini modo, et confundantur de peccatis salubriter, et pereant, inquantum mali sunt. Et sic cognoscant, vel, tunc confundantur mali, anima et corpore, et pereant animo irreparabiliter. Et nunc cognoscant, quod modo nolunt. (CASS.) Notandum, quia undecim superioribus psalmis introductus est Asaph, ut duritia Judaeorum, frequenti voce ipsius Synagogae mollesceret, vel ipsi nomini, cui devoti esse videbantur, crederent. Egit autem in praedictis psalmi de Domini incarnatione, et gentium fide, et de judicio, de quibus transgressio Judaeorum redarguitur. Unde congrue undecim sunt: undenarius enim numerus transgressionis est, quia et denarium transit, et ad duodenarium non pervenit, unde undecim etiam erant vela capillacea in tabernaculo 985BDomini, et in undenario fuerunt Apostoli, rejecto infelicissimo Juda tempore passionis, quando a fide defecerunt, unde: Posuisti tenebras et facta est nox (Psal. CIII).

PSALM LXXXII.

VERS. 1.-- A canticle of a psalm. (CASS.) Because in things active divine contemplation is to be held. But he deters the wicked from the persecution of the people of God: while the good he admonishes unto patience. A psalm on the coming of Christ to judgment, where the good, who here suffer, shall be crowned: but the wicked, who persecute them, shall be tormented.

VERS. 2.-- O God, who is like? (CASS.) The fear of the judge to come being set forth, he describes the malice of the enemies. (AUG.) O God, who is like? Though a man, as others; though 982Djudged, thou art reckoned with the wicked: who is like, when thou shalt judge in brightness? therefore then be not silent, thou who at the first wast silent, and didst restrain thy power, that thou mightest be held and slain. O God, who is like? This is not referred to the divinity, to which he thought that no man was to be compared. Therefore he says not: Who is like to thee? which would certainly be referred to the divinity; but he says, Who shall be like to thee? referring this to the form of a servant, in which he shall then be unlike the rest of men, when he shall appear as judge in glory; or this can be referred to the divinity according to what he says: O God, who is like to thee? in the power of the Godhead: for Christ, whom the wicked saw without, this one sees within, namely as almighty.

983AVERS. 3.-- For behold, etc. (AUG.) He designates the last times of Antichrist, when the things which are now kept down by fear shall break out into free utterance: which utterance, because it was irrational, is called rather a noise than a speech. They that hate. (CASS.) Many, but one head, Antichrist: which is lifted up, that he may be called God.

VERS. 4.-- Upon thy people. They have lifted up their own head, but they have not brought down thy people.

(AUG.) Upon thy people. He says this derisively: for they cannot hurt the people of God, for whom God is, whence the Apostle: If God be for us, who is against us? (Rom. VIII.)

VERS. 5.-- They have said, Come. (AUG.) Behold the counsel, in which they have devised vain things. This is that noise, 983Bwhich is not speech, but rattles emptily. From the nation. (CASS.) In the singular, because all Christians are one nation, since they are born from one font of baptism; or all the good, whom that Antichrist calls one nation: behold the persecution of Antichrist, who intends to take away utterly the Christian name as an evil thing.

VERS. 6.-- They have ordained a testament. (AUG.) For a testament, in the Scriptures, is not that alone which is not valid unless the testator be dead, but every compact also, and agreement which is valid between the living, is called a testament, as Laban and Jacob made a testament. So also the wicked have made as it were a compact among themselves, that with one mind they should persecute the good.

VERS. 7.-- The tabernacles of the Idumeans. He has set forth 983Cwith what zeal they have dealt maliciously: then he shows now who they are that deal maliciously, saying: The tabernacles of the Idumeans, etc. Of the Idumeans, and the Ismaelites. (CASS.) By these names he declares the enemies of Christ, who in the times of Antichrist are likened to so many evil men: because as these against Israel, so those shall then war against the Christians. The Moabites (AUG., HIER.) Whence the Moabites, whom Lot, being drunk, begot of his elder daughter. The Agarens. From Agar, who are also interpreted proselytes.

VERS. 8.-- Gebal. (AUG., HIER.) A vain valley. For Ge is valley vallit, Bal, vain. Ammon. Whence the Ammonites; Lot, being drunk, begot him of his younger daughter.

Amalec. The son of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau, from whom the Amalecites.

VERS. 9.-- Assur. (AUG., HIER.) Literally Nabuchodonosor, 983Dwho was king of the Assyrians. The Idumeans. Earthly or bloody. The Ismaelites. Obeying themselves, not God, because they follow their own depraved thoughts. Moab, from the father, which is in evil. Good indeed was the father, whom the daughter used unlawfully, as the law also is good, if a man use it lawfully, not incestuously. The Agarens. Proselytes, that is, newcomers, who are not citizens, but creep in with an alien mind, and, an occasion of hurting being found, show themselves. Gebal. A vain valley, that is, deceitfully humble. Ammon. A troubled people, or a people of grief. Amalec. A people licking the earth. Strangers. Although by a Latin name they declare themselves aliens, and for this cause enemies, yet in Hebrew they are called Philisthiim, that is, falling by drink, as men drunken with worldly luxury. Tyre. In Hebrew sor, tribulation or anguish, according to that 984Asaying. Tribulation or anguish upon every soul of man that worketh evil. (Rom. II.) Assur. [Vulg. Rom 2:9 Tribulatio et angustia, "and", not "or"] Depressing, or lifted up. Lot. Declining: the apostate angels, sons of declension, because by declining from the truth they departed into the retinue of the devil, whence in the Apocalypse: The dragon fell, and drew with him the third part of the stars, of whom the Apostle: Our wrestling is not against flesh and blood, but against principalities and powers (Ephes. VI). [Vulg. Eph 6:12 adversus principes et potestates, "princes"]

VERS. 10.-- Madian. Declining judgment. Sisara, the shutting out of joy. Jabin, wise, of whom: Where is the wise? where is the scribe? Cison, where they were overcome, is interpreted hardness. Endor, where they perished, the fountain of generation. And carnal generation is understood, not those regenerated by the water of baptism. Oreb, dryness, Zeb, a wolf, Zebee, the victim 984Bof a wolf, not of God. Salmana, the shadow of commotion. All these things suit the wicked, whom the people of God overcame in good. Do to them as to Madian and Sisara, as to Jabin at the brook. (CASS.) Of the vengeance upon the wicked; as all those were overcome in figure by the people of God, so he prays that these may be overcome in truth. As Madian. (AUG.) Namely those who decline judgment, not thinking themselves to be judged: and who shut out the judgment to come; and all these perished in Cison, and in the fountain of Endor.

VERS. 12.-- Make their princes as, etc. These things to all in common. But specially, make their princes: this he wishes for the soldiers of Antichrist, who are not to be converted.

VERS. 13.-- Let us possess by inheritance the sanctuary of God. (AUG.) God's: they invade it as their own.

984CVERS. 14.-- As a wheel, and as stubble before the face of the wind. (CASS.) By this likeness he foretells their many calamities.

Of the wind. The lightness of sinners is compared to the wind, because it flits hither and thither.

VERS. 15.-- Fire and a flame burning the mountains. [Vulg. Ps 82:15 Sicut ignis qui comburit silvam, et sicut flamma comburens montes, "as fire which burneth a wood"] (AUG.) They are fitly said to be in the judgment, when both the dense woods of sinners and the mountains of pride shall be burned.

VERS. 17.-- Fill their faces. (CASS.) The punishments of the contumacious being prophesied, he prays for those who shall believe, who have not praisers of their crimes, but blamers, whom reproach often corrects. (AUG.) It is better to fall that one may repent, than to be proud under the hope of religion: whence the Prophet says: And thou, daughter of Sion, shalt come even unto Babylon, 984Dand there shalt thou be delivered (Mich. IV).

Fill their faces.
