This good and desirable thing would not be prophesied for them, unless among those enemies there were such as this shall be granted to before the judgment: because even now the head heals and washes the same body, but in part, not universally as at the end: and yet from thence some shall be converted, for whom he here prays.

VERS. 18.-- Let them blush and be troubled, etc. (AUG.) Here of the wicked, who shall not be converted, Let them blush, in the time to come for the evils which they have done. And be troubled, for the punishments which they shall suffer. And this for ever and ever, that is, unto eternity. And be troubled. Again he returns to those who are confounded in the present that they may not be confounded unto eternity; as if he should say: Let those be troubled unto eternity: but those seeking 985Athe name of the Lord now, let them both be confounded for their sins wholesomely, and perish, in so far as they are wicked. And so let them know; or, let the wicked then be confounded, in soul and in body, and perish in soul beyond repair. And now let them know what they now will not. (CASS.) It is to be noted that Asaph has been brought in through the eleven preceding psalms, that the hardness of the Jews might be softened by the frequent voice of the Synagogue itself, or that they might believe the very name to which they seemed devoted. But in the aforesaid psalms he treated of the incarnation psalmi of the Lord, and of the faith of the Gentiles, and of the judgment, by which the transgression of the Jews is refuted. Whence they are fitly eleven: for the number eleven is the number of transgression, because it both passes the ten, and does not reach the twelve, whence there were also eleven curtains of hair in the tabernacle 985Bof the Lord, and the Apostles were in the number eleven, the most unhappy Judas being cast out at the time of the passion, when they failed from the faith, whence: Thou hast appointed darkness, and it is night (Psal. CIII).

PSALMUS LXXXIII.

VERS. 1.-- In finem. (AUG.) Nihil hic dicitur de torcularibus visibilibus, unde constat spiritualia esse. Uva in vite, oliva in arbore pendens libero fruuntur aere, nec illa est vinum, nec ista oleum ante pressuram: sic quos praescivit Deus ante saecula fieri conformes imaginis filii, antequam accedant ad servitutem Dei, fruuntur in saeculo deliciosa libertate. Sed cum accedunt ad servitutem Dei, dicitur eis: Fili, accedens ad servitutem Dei, sta in justitia et timore, et praepara animam tuam ad tentationem 985C(Eccle. II). Ecce torcular, conteruntur, exuuntur in tegumentis carnalium desideriorum, quasi vinaciis exuuntur veteri homine, et in apothecam Dei defluunt: ideo torcularia dicuntur Ecclesiae praesentis temporis. Sed qui in his filii Core, id est calvi, scilicet Christi? Calvus namque Elisaeus irrisus a pueris figura fuit Christi, qui in calvaria crucifixus. Ideo hic premitur Christianus, ut quaerat quietem, quae non est hic, et fit ei Deus refugium. Qui enim incumbit terrenis, incumbit in baculum arundinis. Pro torcularibus. (AUG.) In torculari fructus uvae vel olivae emanat: sic in pressuris merita sanctorum patent, quae in pace latebant. (CASS.) Psalmus secundus de charitate. Primo de inaestimabili desiderio aeternae domus.

985DVERS. 2.-- Quam dilecta. Ecce quanta militia. Etenim passer, quam secura.

VERS. 4.-- Etenim passer, etc. (AUG.) Duobus duo reddit: cor ut passer; caro ut turtur, cui dat et pullos: corde cogitamus Deum, quasi volet passer ad domum; carne agimus opera. (CASS.) Sicut passer deserit silvas, et inventa domo laetatur, ubi non timet insidias: sic anima laetatur, dum scit sibi domum paratam in coelo. Spiritus, qui est quasi passer volans in altum, tendens ad ipsum Deum. Nidum, etc. (AUG.) Nidus ad tempus, domus vera in aeternum. Nidum ergo dicit fidem, et conformitatem sacramentorum Ecclesiae, quem nidum quaerit turtur, ut reponat pullos suos. Non enim abjicit ubicunque, 986Ased in nido Ecclesiae facit opera bona salubriter, pro quibus salvatur: per quod differt ab aliis qui opera faciunt, sed non in nido fidei. Nam et pagani faciunt opera, vestiunt nudos, etc., et haeretici multa faciunt: sed non in nido Ecclesiae, et ideo conculcantur, non servantur. Haec caro est mulier, per quam seducitur passer, sed salvabitur per generationem operum, si in nido, id est, si perseveraverit in fide. Praebet autem Deus unde fiat nidus, induit enim se feno carnis ut ad te veniret. Altaria tua, Domine. (CASS.) Ubi animae coelesti convivio epulantur, ubi anima quasi in domo gaudeat. (AUG.) Et caro reponit opera sua, unde: Beati qui, etc., ubi ostendit ad quam beatitudinem militia ducit.

VERS. 5.-- Beati qui habitant in domo tua, Domine; 986Bin saecula saeculorum laudabunt te. (AUG.) Hoc boni jam habent, scilicet, quod habitant in domo tua. Sequitur: In saecula saeculorum laudabunt te. Hoc totum negotium est ibi sanctorum: non est ibi necessitas, quae mater est omnium humanarum actionum, quia cui faciunt ibi quippiam, ubi nulli indigent; habent ergo et agunt, unde beati sunt. Omnis autem beatus habendo vel agendo dicitur beatus.

VERS. 6.-- Beatus vir cujus est auxilium abs te: ascensiones in corde suo disposuit. (CASS.) Quo auxilio ad domum veniatur.

VERS. 7.-- In valle lacrymarum. (CASS.) Vallis lacrymarum est poenitentis humilitas. (AUG.) Unde autem ploratio, quia lege nos afflixit, per quam cognovimus peccatum repugnare spiritui, et gemimus, 986Cquomodo scilicet, veniamus ad locum quem posuit, ope ejus et auxilio utique. In loco quem posuit. Etenim benedictionem dabit. Qui non potest exponi, quem oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, id est, futurum regnum, quod disposuit et ordinavit Deus ut ad id per gradus veniatur.

VERS. 9.-- Domine Deus virtutum. (CASS.) Orat et humiliat se pro impetratione hujus auxilii. Deus Jacob. (AUG.) Quem fecisti Israel apparens ei sic fac et me Israel.

VERS. 10.-- Respice in faciem, etc. Ipse enim loquitur in nobis, unde Apostolus: An experimentum ejus quaeritis, qui in me loquitur Christus! Et in nobis recipitur, sicut ait, Qui vos recipit, me recipit. Respice. Christum Pater semper respicit. (CASS.) Sed fac 986Dpraesentia incarnationis eum ventibus respici: vel, ita per faciem innotescimus, aliis. (AUG.) Respice ergo in faciem, id est, innotescere fac omnibus Christum, ut possimus ire de virtute in virtutem

VERS. 11.-- Dies una. Immutabilis, scilicet sine ortu et occasu, cui non cedit dies hesternus, quem non urget crastinus. Super millia, super infinitos dies praesentes, qui habent finem. Propter quod elegi, etsi possem regnare, abjectus opinione hominum, in domo in Ecclesia, Ecce quam dulce, fasce torcularis premi.

VERS. 12.-- Quia misericordiam. (CASS.) Ideo in domo Dei malo esse quam alibi, quia in ea dat misericordiam, qua justificat, post veritatem promissi 987Apraemii. Sed quibus? his qui ambulant in innocentia.

VERS. 13.-- Domine virtutum, beatus homo qui sperat, etc. Qui tanta facis, quae dici non possunt.

PSALM LXXXIII.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end. (AUG.) Nothing is here said of visible winepresses, whence it is plain that they are spiritual. The grape upon the vine, the olive hanging upon the tree, enjoy the free air, and neither is that wine, nor is this oil, before the pressing: so those whom God foreknew before the ages to be made conformable to the image of his Son, before they come to the service of God, enjoy in the world a delightful liberty. But when they come to the service of God, it is said to them: Son, when thou comest to the service of God, stand in justice and in fear, and prepare thy soul for temptation 985C(Eccle. II). Behold the winepress: they are crushed, they are stripped in the coverings of carnal desires, as in husks; they are stripped of the old man, and they flow down into the storehouse of God: therefore the churches of the present time are called winepresses. But who among these are the sons of Core, that is, the bald, namely of Christ? For bald Eliseus, mocked by the boys, was a figure of Christ, who was crucified on Calvary. Therefore is the Christian pressed here, that he may seek the rest which is not here, and God becomes for him a refuge. For he who leans upon earthly things leans upon a staff of reed. For the winepresses. (AUG.) In the winepress the fruit of the grape or of the olive flows out: so in pressures the merits of the saints appear, which lay hidden in peace. (CASS.) The second psalm on charity. First, of the inestimable desire of the eternal house.

985DVERS. 2.-- How lovely. Behold how great the warfare. For the sparrow, how secure.

VERS. 4.-- For the sparrow, etc. (AUG.) To two he renders two: the heart as the sparrow; the flesh as the turtle, to which he gives also young ones: with the heart we think upon God, as the sparrow flies to the house; with the flesh we do works. (CASS.) As the sparrow forsakes the woods, and rejoices when a house is found, where it fears no snares: so the soul rejoices, while it knows that a house is prepared for it in heaven. The spirit, which is as a sparrow flying on high, reaching towards God himself. A nest, etc. (AUG.) A nest for a time, a house true unto eternity. By the nest therefore he means faith, and the conformity of the sacraments of the Church, which nest the turtle seeks, that she may lay up her young. For she does not cast them anywhere, 986Abut in the nest of the Church she does good works wholesomely, for which she is saved: wherein she differs from others who do works, but not in the nest of faith. For the pagans also do works, they clothe the naked, etc., and heretics do many things: but not in the nest of the Church, and therefore they are trodden down, they are not preserved. This flesh is the woman, by whom the sparrow is seduced, but she shall be saved by the bearing of works, if in the nest, that is, if she shall have persevered in faith. But God supplies that whereof the nest may be made, for he clothed himself with the hay of the flesh that he might come to thee. Thy altars, O Lord. (CASS.) Where souls feast at the heavenly banquet, where the soul may rejoice as in a house. (AUG.) And the flesh lays up its works, whence: Blessed are they who, etc., where he shows to what beatitude the warfare leads.

VERS. 5.-- Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord; 986Bfor ever and ever they shall praise thee. (AUG.) This the good have already, namely, that they dwell in thy house. There follows: For ever and ever they shall praise thee. This is the whole business of the saints there: there is no necessity there, which is the mother of all human actions, for whom do they do anything there, where none are in need; they have therefore and they act, whence they are blessed. But every blessed one is called blessed by having or by acting.

VERS. 6.-- Blessed is the man whose help is from thee: he hath disposed ascensions in his heart. (CASS.) By what help one may come to the house.

VERS. 7.-- In the vale of tears. (CASS.) The vale of tears is the humility of one repenting. (AUG.) But whence the weeping: because he afflicted us with the law, through which we knew that sin fights against the spirit, and we groan, 986Cnamely how we may come to the place which he has appointed, by his power and help assuredly. In the place which he hath appointed. For he shall give a blessing. Which cannot be set forth, which eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, that is, the kingdom to come, which God has disposed and ordained, that it may be come to by degrees.

VERS. 9.-- O Lord God of hosts. (CASS.) He prays and humbles himself for the obtaining of this help. God of Jacob. (AUG.) Whom thou madest Israel by appearing to him, so make me also Israel.

VERS. 10.-- Look upon the face, etc. For he himself speaks in us, whence the Apostle: Do you seek a proof of him that speaketh in me, Christ! And he is received in us, as he says, He that receiveth you, receiveth me. Look. The Father always looks upon Christ. (CASS.) But make 986Dhim to be looked upon by the nations ventibus through the presence of the incarnation: or, thus by the face we become known to others. (AUG.) Look therefore upon the face, that is, make Christ known to all, that we may be able to go from virtue to virtue

VERS. 11.-- One day. Unchangeable, namely without rising and setting, to which yesterday does not yield, which tomorrow does not press upon. Above thousands, above the infinite present days, which have an end. For which cause I have chosen, though I might reign, to be abject in the opinion of men, in the house, in the Church, Behold how sweet it is, to be pressed by the burden of the winepress.

VERS. 12.-- Because mercy. (CASS.) Therefore I had rather be in the house of God than elsewhere, because in it he gives mercy, by which he justifies, after the truth of the promised 987Areward. But to whom? to those who walk in innocence.

VERS. 13.-- O Lord of hosts, blessed is the man that hopeth, etc. Thou who dost such great things, which cannot be told.

PSALMUS LXXXIV.

VERS. 2.-- Benedixisti, Domine. (AUG.) Psalmus de nova benedictione, etc., usque ad de aversione iniquitatis.

VERS. 3.-- Remisisti. (ID.) Futura dicit ut praeterita.

VERS. 4.-- Mitigasti (CASS.) Diapsalma, de aversione irae, id est, poenae.

VERS. 5.-- Converte nos. Petit quod adhuc futurum sciebat. Quasi, quod dixi ut praeteritum, oro ut fiat. (AUG.) Converte nos. Prophetice dixi futura, ut praeterita, hic autem orat ut vere futura, dicens, Converte 987Bet averte, quasi dicat, dixi quasi facta. Et quia video futura, et quia non sunt oro ut fiant.

VERS. 6.-- Nunquid in aeternum. Praevidet iste hanc poenam transituram: Quia sicut in Adam omnes moriuntur, ita et in Christo omnes vivificabuntur. Irasceris. (AUG.) Ira Dei est omnis poena quam patitur. Sicut dictum est Adam quando peccavit: Maledicta terra in opere tuo, et in labore et sudore vultus tui vesceris pane tuo. De ira ergo mortales sumus et passibiles, sed innovati in Christo. A generatione. Prima generatio fuit mortalis de ira, erit altera immortalis de misericordia: sed nec hanc misericordiam meremur conversi per nos ad Deum, ipse enim nos convertit. Et inde subdit: Deus convertens, quasi 987Csicut vivificatio est a te, ita et conversio.

VERS. 7.-- Deus tu conversus. (CASS.) Non extendens, sed Deus convertens. Prius dat votum conversionis, post ad vitam ducit. Vel, Deus tu conversus ab ira in adventu Filii. Vivificabis nos. Tanto tempore antequam habeatur. Et tunc, Plebs tua laetabitur in te, quae prius in se male laetabitur.

VERS. 8.-- Ostende nobis, Domine. (AUG.) Hoc orando praedixit Propheta, etc., usque ad Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt (Matth. V). (CASS.) Ostende. Vel petit iste sibi spiritualiter tantum Christum ostendi, sciebat eum quidem futurum, sed petit ut puro corde intueamur, non corporeis oculis ut infideles: Judaei enim viderunt et crucifixerunt. Et in futuro: Salutare tuum da nobis, id 987Dest, Christum amplectendum et possidendum, ut non tollatur a nobis, et sic legitur partim de praesenti, et partim de futuro. Misericordiam. (AUG.) Christus dicitur misericordia, quia ostendit nobis misericordiam, docens quidquid boni habet homo ex Deo esse, et sic homo non superbit. Sed sic haerens et fruens Deo laetatur in eo.

VERS. 9.-- Audiam quid loquatur in me Dominus. (CASS.) Unde scit et per quem fiat, et quid praestet ipse veniens. Pacem. (AUG.) Christum. Pacem ad Deum et proximum, et per Christum.

VERS. 10.-- Prope timentes eum. (ID.) Ubique daemonia colebantur, etc., usque ad immortalis in corpore nostro modo mortali.

988AVERS. 11.-- Misericordia, etc. (ID.) Postquam dixit, etc., usque ad quomodo veritas de terra orta est (Luc. VIII).

VERS. 12.-- Veritas de terra orta est. (ID.) Confessio de homine, ut se accuset, etc., usque ad data est justificatio confitentis.

VERS. 14.-- Justitia ante eum. (ID.) Prima hominis justitia est, etc., usque ad et visitans ponet in via gressus. Ambulabit. Accrescet, vel praecurret, parans ei viam; et Dominus in via parata ponet gressus.

PSALM LXXXIV.

VERS. 2.-- Thou hast blessed, O Lord. (AUG.) A psalm on the new blessing, etc., as far as of the turning away of iniquity.

VERS. 3.-- Thou hast forgiven. (ID.) He speaks of things to come as of things past.

VERS. 4.-- Thou hast mitigated (CASS.) Diapsalma, of the turning away of anger, that is, of punishment.

VERS. 5.-- Convert us. He asks what he knew to be still to come. As if: what I have said as past, I pray may be done. (AUG.) Convert us. I said prophetically things to come, as past; but here he prays for them as truly to come, saying, Convert 987Band turn away, as if he should say, I have said them as though done. And because I see things to come, and because they are not, I pray that they may be done.

VERS. 6.-- Is it for ever. He foresees that this punishment will pass away: For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all shall be made alive. Thou art angry. (AUG.) The anger of God is every punishment which one suffers. As it was said to Adam when he sinned: Cursed is the earth in thy work, and in labour and in the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat thy bread. [Vulg. Gn 3:17 maledicta terra in opere tuo : in laboribus comedes ex ea; the second clause is Gn 3:19 In sudore vultus tui vesceris pane] Of anger therefore we are mortal and passible, but renewed in Christ. From generation. The first generation was mortal, of anger; the other shall be immortal, of mercy: but neither do we merit this mercy by being converted to God through ourselves, for he himself converts us. And thence he subjoins: God converting, as if 987Cto say: as the quickening is from thee, so also the conversion.

VERS. 7.-- O God, thou being turned. (CASS.) Not extending, but God converting. First he gives the will of conversion, afterwards he leads to life. Or, O God, thou being turned from anger at the coming of the Son. Thou wilt quicken us. So long a time before it is had. And then, Thy people shall rejoice in thee, which before shall rejoice wickedly in itself.

VERS. 8.-- Shew us, O Lord. (AUG.) This the Prophet foretold by praying, etc., as far as Blessed are the clean of heart, for they shall see God (Matth. V). (CASS.) Shew. Or this one asks that Christ be shewn to him spiritually only; he knew indeed that he was to come, but he asks that we may behold him with a pure heart, not with bodily eyes as the unbelievers: for the Jews saw and crucified him. And for the time to come: Give us thy salvation, that 987Dis, Christ, to be embraced and possessed, that he be not taken away from us; and thus it is read partly of the present, and partly of the future. Mercy. (AUG.) Christ is called mercy, because he showed us mercy, teaching that whatever of good a man has is from God, and so man is not proud. But cleaving thus and enjoying God, he rejoices in him.

VERS. 9.-- I will hear what the Lord speaketh in me. (CASS.) Whence he knows, and by whom it is done, and what he himself bestows in coming. Peace. (AUG.) Christ. Peace toward God and toward the neighbour, and through Christ.

VERS. 10.-- Near them that fear him. (ID.) Everywhere demons were worshipped, etc., as far as immortal in our body now mortal.

988AVERS. 11.-- Mercy, etc. (ID.) After he had said, etc., as far as how truth is sprung out of the earth (Luc. VIII).

VERS. 12.-- Truth is sprung out of the earth. (ID.) Confession from man, that he may accuse himself, etc., as far as the justification of him that confesses is given.

VERS. 14.-- Justice shall go before him. (ID.) The first justice of man is, etc., as far as and visiting he shall set his steps in the way. Shall walk. It shall increase, or shall run before, preparing the way for him; and the Lord shall set his steps in the way made ready.

PSALMUS LXXXV.

Oratio David. (AUG.) Psalmus iste, secundus eorum est qui orationis nomine intitulantur, in quo Christus Dei Filius et hominis, unus Deus cum Patre, 988Bunus homo cum hominibus, orat in forma servi, qui oratur a nobis in forma Dei. Orat pro nobis ut sacerdos noster; orat in nobis ut caput nostrum, oratur a nobis ut Deus noster.

(CASS.) Christi oratio fidelium, etc., usque ad comprimeret audaciam stultae et inconsultae temeritatis.

(AUG.) Haec dicit Christus in nobis, et nos in illo.

(CASS.) Orat ascendendo, unde concludit: Omnes gentes adorantes.

VERS. 2.-- Quoniam sanctus sum. (AUG.) Christus proprie sanctus sanctificans, etc., usque ad miserere clamantis, laetifica levatum.

VERS. 5.-- Mitis. (ID.) Portans hominem, donec perficiat eum, etc., usque ad cum nondum sit perfectus.

988CVERS. 6.-- Auribus percipe. (CASS.) Vide ordinem orationis, etc., usque ad auditum deprecationi meae.

VERS. 7.-- Tribulationis. (AUG., CASS.) Cum enixius clamatur, etc., usque ad quia non est similis tui in diis, Domine.

VERS. 9.-- Quascunque fecisti venient et adorabunt coram, etc. (AUG.) Si est gens quam non fecit Deus, illa non adorabit. Annuntiat Ecclesiam ubique diffusam, quod modo impletum est: Et nota, quia, ut ait Scriptura: In lata gente gloria regis, in diminutione populi principis contritio. Sequitur: Et glorificabunt nomen.

VERS. 10.-- Tu es Deus solus. (ID.) Vel tu solus magnus contra futuros, qui se dicunt magnos et deos.

988DVERS. 11.-- Deduc me, Domine, in via tua. (CASS.) Orat pro omnibus jam adorantibus, et loquitur in membris. Domine, deduc, etc. Aliud est duci ad viam, et aliud est duci in via, ne in ea cadatur: ubique egent homines adjuvari, sive sint in via, sive extra eam. Via autem Christus est, qui dicit: Ego sum via, veritas, et vita. Laetetur cor meum. (AUG.) In timore mundano praecedit causa, etc., usque ad qui autem timet, et non sperat, depressus est.

VERS. 13.-- Ex inferno inferiori. (ID.) Per hoc intelligimus, etc., usque ad haec sunt opiniones, non assertiones.

VERS. 14.-- Deus, iniqui insurrexerunt super me, 989Aet Synagoga potentium, etc. (CASS.) Item pro se orat facta mentione passionis suae et gloriae, unde habent hi pro quibus oravit multam misericordiam et eruuntur de inferno.

VERS. 16.-- Da imperium tuum. (AUG.) Quasi dicat: Transeat tempus patientiae, veniat tempus judicii, unde non tantum Christus, sed et sancti sedebunt judices, qui sunt filii ancillae, id est Ecclesiae.

PSALM LXXXV.

A prayer of David. [Vulg. Ps 85:1 Oratio ipsi David, "a prayer for David himself"] (AUG.) This psalm is the second of those which are entitled by the name of prayer, in which Christ, the Son of God and of man, one God with the Father, 988Bone man with men, prays in the form of a servant, who is prayed to by us in the form of God. He prays for us as our priest; he prays in us as our head; he is prayed to by us as our God.

(CASS.) The prayer of Christ, of the faithful, etc., as far as he might restrain the boldness of foolish and inconsiderate rashness.

(AUG.) These things Christ says in us, and we in him.

(CASS.) He prays by ascending, whence he concludes: All the nations adoring.

VERS. 2.-- For I am holy. (AUG.) Christ properly holy, sanctifying, etc., as far as have mercy on him that cries, gladden him that is lifted up.

VERS. 5.-- Meek. (ID.) Bearing man, until he perfect him, etc., as far as when he is not yet perfect.

988CVERS. 6.-- Give ear. (CASS.) See the order of the prayer, etc., as far as a hearing to my supplication.

VERS. 7.-- Of tribulation. (AUG., CASS.) When one cries more earnestly, etc., as far as because there is none like to thee among the gods, O Lord.

VERS. 9.-- All whom thou hast made shall come and adore before, etc. (AUG.) If there is a nation which God did not make, that one shall not adore. He announces the Church spread abroad everywhere, which is now fulfilled: And note that, as the Scripture says: In a broad nation is the glory of the king, in the diminishing of the people is the ruin of the prince. [Vulg. Pr 14:28 In multitudine populi dignitas regis, et in paucitate plebis ignominia principis, "in the multitude of the people is the dignity of the king"] There follows: And they shall glorify the name.

VERS. 10.-- Thou art God alone. (ID.) Or thou alone art great against those to come, who call themselves great and gods.

988DVERS. 11.-- Conduct me, O Lord, in thy way. (CASS.) He prays for all who now adore, and speaks in his members. O Lord, conduct, etc. It is one thing to be led to the way, and another to be led in the way, lest one fall in it: everywhere men need to be helped, whether they be in the way, or outside it. But the way is Christ, who says: I am the way, the truth, and the life. Let my heart rejoice. (AUG.) In worldly fear the cause goes before, etc., as far as but he who fears, and does not hope, is cast down.

VERS. 13.-- From the lower hell. (ID.) By this we understand, etc., as far as these are opinions, not assertions.

VERS. 14.-- O God, the wicked have risen up against me, 989Aand the Synagogue of the mighty, etc. (CASS.) Again he prays for himself, mention being made of his passion and of his glory, whence those for whom he prayed have much mercy and are rescued from hell.

VERS. 16.-- Give thy command. (AUG.) As if he should say: Let the time of patience pass, let the time of judgment come, whence not only Christ, but the saints also, shall sit as judges, who are the sons of the handmaid, that is, of the Church.

PSALMUS LXXXVI.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus. (CASS.) Quia agit de Ecclesia secundum potestatem, ubi agit opera. Cantici. Ut de saeculari Jerusalem, ad intelligentiam superne eleveris, scilicet de actione ad theoricam. Propheta praedicat coelestem Jerusalem filiis Chore, quam commendat 989Bper fundamenta, et portas, et famam ut eis augeatur affectus. Fundamenta ejus. Psalmus de coelesti Jerusalem: plenus spiritu Propheta, multa volvens apud se, de hac civitate, de qua nihil adhuc dixerat, in hoc erumpit: Fundamenta ejus, etc. Prior laus a fundamentis; soliditas totius civitatis notetur. Ejus, non refertur ad aliquod praemissum: sed ad cordis Prophetae meditationem, quia nunquam de illa corde tacuerat, etsi ore.

VERS. 3.-- Dicta. (AUG.) Haec sunt illa, quae Dominus per prophetas de ea praedixit.

VERS. 4.-- Memor ero. (ID.) Diapsalma. Dominus de eadem Jerusalem. Memor ero Raab. Ostendit quae sunt illa gloriosa; quasi dicat: Haec sunt illa: in illa civitate, inquit Propheta ex persona Dei, 989CMemor ero Raab et Babylonis, quae non pertinent ad populum Judaeorum. Gloriosa de te, ubi non solus est Judaeus, sed omnes gentes. Raab. Per fenestram emisit coccinum, id est, in fronte habet signum sanguinis Christi Ecclesia gentium.

Unde: Publicani et meretrices praecedent vos in regnum coelorum. Raab, latitudo vel impetus, gentes, quae late et impetuose vagantur per vitia. Ad Babyloniam pertinent omnes mali, ut ad Jerusalem omnes sancti. Ecce alienigenae. Memor ero. Quare hoc dixisti? Ecce alienigenae, id est, gentes : et Tyrus, angustia vitiorum, vel poenitentiae.

VERS. 5.-- Nunquid Sion. Secundum aliam litteram. Mater Sion dicet, homo.

(AUG., CASS.) Quasi dicat: Unde alieni pervenient ad 989DJerusalem? Audi unde. Est quidam homo, id est, Christus, qui dicit mater Sion, id est Synagoga mater mea secundum carnem; et per hunc veniunt; quis est homo ille? Ipse est qui in ea natus est et eam fundavit; ipse dicit, mater, civitati illi.

(CASS.) Vel, commendat Sion spirituali, etc., usque ad quorum principum?

(AUG.) Horum, (secundum aliam litteram) qui facti sunt, scilicet principes, in ea, id est, qui facti sunt principes; antequam essent in ea, non erant principes, sed abjecta mundi: Elegit enim Deus infirma mundi ut confunderet fortia.

VERS. 7.-- Sicut laetantium. (CASS.) Diapsalma. Concludit paucis verbis, tangens futuram beatitudinem. 990A(AUG.) Sicut laetantium collatis omnibus concludit: Sicut laetantium. Sicut, quia talis erit laetitia, qualem hic non novimus, et ideo cum non potuit exprimi, dicit, ut potuit, sicut laetantium.

PSALM LXXXVI.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm. (CASS.) Because it treats of the Church according to power, where it does works. Of a canticle. That from the worldly Jerusalem thou mayest be lifted up to the understanding that is from above, namely from action to contemplation. The Prophet preaches the heavenly Jerusalem to the sons of Core, which he commends 989Bby its foundations, and its gates, and its fame, that their affection may be increased. The foundations thereof. A psalm on the heavenly Jerusalem: the Prophet, full of the spirit, turning many things over with himself concerning this city, of which he had as yet said nothing, breaks out into this: The foundations thereof, etc. The first praise is from the foundations; let the solidity of the whole city be noted. Thereof, is not referred to anything set down before: but to the meditation of the Prophet's heart, because he had never been silent about it in his heart, even if in his mouth.

VERS. 3.-- Things said. (AUG.) These are those things which the Lord foretold of it by the prophets.

VERS. 4.-- I will be mindful. (ID.) Diapsalma. The Lord, concerning the same Jerusalem. I will be mindful of Rahab. He shows what those glorious things are; as if he should say: These are they: in that city, says the Prophet in the person of God, 989CI will be mindful of Rahab and of Babylon, which do not belong to the people of the Jews. Glorious things of thee, where the Jew is not alone, but all the Gentiles. Rahab. She let down the scarlet through the window, that is, the Church of the Gentiles has upon its forehead the sign of the blood of Christ.

Whence: Publicans and harlots shall go before you into the kingdom of heaven. Rahab, [Vulg. Mt 21:31 in regnum Dei, "into the kingdom of God"] breadth or violence, the Gentiles, who wander broadly and violently through vices. To Babylon belong all the wicked, as to Jerusalem all the saints. Behold the strangers. I will be mindful. Why hast thou said this? Behold the strangers, that is, the Gentiles: and Tyre, the anguish of vices, or of penance.

VERS. 5.-- Shall Sion. According to another reading. Mother Sion shall say, a man.

(AUG., CASS.) As if he should say: Whence shall strangers come to 989DJerusalem? Hear whence. There is a certain man, that is, Christ, who says Mother Sion, that is, the Synagogue is my mother according to the flesh; and through him they come; who is that man? He is the one who was born in her and founded her; he himself says, mother, to that city.

(CASS.) Or, he commends Sion spiritually, etc., as far as of what princes?

(AUG.) Of these, (according to another reading) who were made, namely princes, in her, that is, who were made princes; before they were in her, they were not princes, but the outcast things of the world: God chose indeed the weak things of the world, that he might confound the strong.

VERS. 7.-- As of those rejoicing. (CASS.) Diapsalma. He concludes in few words, touching the beatitude to come. 990A(AUG.) As of those rejoicing, all things being compared, he concludes: As of those rejoicing. As, because such shall the joy be as we do not know here, and therefore since it could not be expressed, he says, as he could, as of those rejoicing.

PSALMUS LXXXVII.

VERS. 1.-- Mahalath. (AUG.) Chorus, ut canenti chorus consonando respondeat, etc., usque ad dicitur enim fuisse quidam orientalis.

VERS. 2.-- Domine Deus. (CASS.) Monet Christi mortem imitari. Primo precatur auxilium referens contemptum ab inimicis: unde in forma servi orans ad patrem, ait: O Domine.

VERS. 3.-- Intret in conspectu. (ID.) Virtus purae orationis, quae quasi quaedam persona ad Deum intrat 990Bet mandatum peragit: quo caro pervenire nequit.

VERS. 4.-- Quia repleta est. (AUG.) Hos humanae infirmitatis affectus, etc., usque ad sed humanae infirmitatis indicia.

VERS. 5.-- Aestimatus. Quia non solum gravia, sed et contumeliosa pertuli.

VERS. 6.-- Sicut vulnerati dormientes. (CASS.) Quia et ipse lancea vulneratus, et sepulcro clausus, sed differt per hoc quod sequitur, quorum non meministi adhuc.

In sepulcro. Id est, in carnali voluptate sopiti, unde Deus non excitat eos.

Et ipsi de manu tua repulsi sunt. (AUG.) Non enim ad dormientes hoc refertur, in quibus sunt justi, 990Cquorum licet non meminerit Deus adhuc, ut resurgant: de his tamen dictum est: Justorum animae in manu Dei sunt (Sap. III). Vel, posuerunt me rei veritate, In lacu inferiori, id est, in aquis inferni, scilicet in tenebris et in umbra mortis.

VERS. 7.-- In lacu inferiori. (CASS.) Vel inferni: quia tam abjecta morte ablatus est in tenebris oblivionis, quem nemo requiret. Et umbra mortis, locus malorum, in quo puniuntur.

VERS. 8.-- Super me confirmatus est. (ID.) Putabant quod ira Dei periisset et quod Deus omnes indignationes super eum induxisset, quando pertulit eum crucifigi.

VERS. 9.-- Longe fecisti. (ID.) Quid amici ejus in passione fecerunt.

990DNotos. Non quos novit: quia tunc omnes noverat ut Deus, sed quibus notus est.

VERS. 10.-- Tota die. (AUG.) Per extensas manus continuatio bonorum operum, a quibus nunquam cessavit, intelligitur. In cruce enim nec una tota die fuit illa extensio, nec totum pro parte potest accipi cum addit tota; sed quia haec opera non omnibus profuerunt, addit.

VERS. 11.-- Nunquid mortuis. Mortuos corde dicit, quibus fiunt quidem miracula Christi, sed non prosunt eis: mortuis enim corpore facta sunt mirabilia, cum quidam revixerunt. Et cum Dominus infernum penetravit, atque inde victor mortis ascendit, magnum factum est mortuis miraculum. Nunquid 991Amortuis. (CASS.) Quibus non prosunt opera sua ostendit. Aut medici suscitabunt, etc. (AUG.) In Hebraeo non medici, etc., usque ad: Nemo potest venire ad me, nisi Pater traxerit eum.

VERS. 12.-- Sepulcro. Unde in Evangelio de talibus: Similes estis sepulcris dealbatis quae foris apparent hominibus speciosa: intus vero plena sunt ossibus mortuorum, quasi, sic et vos hypocrisi et iniquitate. Misericordiam et veritatem. (AUG.) Misericordiam et veritatem amat conjungere Scriptura: maxime in psalmis.

VERS. 13.-- In tenebris. Idem sunt mortui positi in sepulcro, et tenebrae, et terra oblivionis.

VERS. 14.-- Ego ad te, Domine, clamavi. (CASS.) Quae in suis sustinet; ecce chorus respondens praecinenti.

991B(ID.) Et ego quasi, cum illis, cum quibus unum.

(AUG.) Et ego. His mortuis non prosunt opera, etc., usque ad Ut quid, Domine, repellis.

VERS. 15.-- Ut quid. (CASS.) Ecce quantum desiderat. Ut quid, Domine. Proponit, quaerendam esse causam: quae est, ut dilatione boni, et adversis multiplicatis, quibus repulsa quasi oratio inflammetur ardentius.

VERS. 16.-- Exaltatus. (ID.) Prius tumido corde, postea, Humiliatus. Per confessionem. Conturbatus, id est, confusus de peccatis ea damnado

VERS. 17.-- Transierunt. (CASS.) Non mansuete contigerunt.

(AUG.) Quia non de fideli, sed de infideli dictum 991Cest: Ira Dei manet super eum (Joan. III). Flagellat enim filios quos recipit, unde: Quos ego amo, arguo et castigo (Apoc. III). Et alibi: Percutium et sanabo. occidam et vivere faciam (Deut. XXXII). (ID.) Transierunt et conturbaverunt. Quia aliud jam de damnatione patimur, et aliud de aeterna ultione timemus. Terrores tui. (CASS.) Quos patior: quia tibi placuit, non meo merito. (AUG.) Terrores futuri judicii, quos omnis caro timet.

Conturbaverunt me. Secundum infirmitatem carnis. (AUG.) Conturbaverunt me aliquando terrores, ita conturbant animum cogitantis circumpendentibus malis, ut sicut aquae circumfluere videantur, et simul undique circumdare, unde amici et videantur, et more deserunt, unde Apostolus: Omnes me dereliquerunt 991D(II Tim. IV).

VERS. 18.-- Circumdederunt me. (CASS.) Peccata undique copiosa inundatione concludunt.

Tota die. (AUG.) Quia nullo tempore desunt mala Ecclesiae donec finiatur saeculum. Sed haec omnia fiunt, ut oratio Ecclesiae praeveniat Deum donec illa salus veniat, ubi nihil malorum sit.

VERS. 19.-- Amicum (CASS.) Et qui pio et fideli amore conjuncti sunt.

Proximum et notos, etc. Parentela. Saepe justis humana officia timore subtracta sunt.

PSALM LXXXVII.

VERS. 1.-- Mahalath. (AUG.) A choir, that the choir may answer the singer in harmony, etc., as far as for a certain man of the East is said to have been.

VERS. 2.-- O Lord God. (CASS.) He admonishes us to imitate the death of Christ. First he prays for help, reporting the contempt he has from his enemies: whence, praying in the form of a servant to the Father, he says: O Lord.

VERS. 3.-- Let it enter in the sight. (ID.) The power of pure prayer, which as a certain person enters to God 990Band performs its charge: whither the flesh cannot come.

VERS. 4.-- For it is filled. (AUG.) These affections of human infirmity, etc., as far as but tokens of human infirmity.

VERS. 5.-- Counted. Because I have borne not only grievous things, but reproachful ones also.

VERS. 6.-- As the slain sleeping. (CASS.) Because he also was wounded with a lance, and shut in a sepulchre, but he differs by that which follows, of whom thou art not yet mindful.

In the sepulchre. That is, lulled asleep in carnal pleasure, whence God does not rouse them.

And they are cast off from thy hand. (AUG.) For this is not referred to the sleeping, among whom are the just, 990Cof whom although God is not mindful as yet, [Vulg. Ps 87:6 quorum non es memor amplius, "no more"; the gloss's ut resurgant rests on "as yet"] that they may rise again: yet of these it is said: The souls of the just are in the hand of God (Sap. III). Or, they have put me by the truth of the thing, In the lower pit, that is, in the waters of hell, namely in darkness and in the shadow of death.

VERS. 7.-- In the lower pit. (CASS.) Or of hell: because by so abject a death he was taken away into the darkness of oblivion, whom no one shall seek. And the shadow of death, the place of the wicked, in which they are punished.

VERS. 8.-- It is confirmed upon me. (ID.) They thought that he had perished by the anger of God, and that God had brought all his indignations upon him, when he suffered him to be crucified.

VERS. 9.-- Thou hast put far away. (ID.) What his friends did in the passion.

990DAcquaintances. Not those whom he knew: because then he knew all as God, but those to whom he was known.

VERS. 10.-- All the day. (AUG.) By hands stretched out is understood the continuance of good works, from which he never ceased. For on the cross that stretching out was not for even one whole day, nor can the whole be taken for the part when he adds whole; but because these works did not profit all, he adds.

VERS. 11.-- Is it for the dead. He means the dead in heart, for whom indeed the miracles of Christ are wrought, but they do not profit them: for wonders were wrought for those dead in body, when certain ones came to life again. And when the Lord pierced hell, and thence ascended a conqueror of death, a great miracle was wrought for the dead. Is it 991Afor the dead. (CASS.) He shows to whom their own works do not profit. Or shall physicians raise up, etc. (AUG.) In the Hebrew not physicians, etc., as far as: No man can come to me, unless the Father draw him.

VERS. 12.-- In the sepulchre. Whence in the Gospel of such men: You are like to whited sepulchres, which outwardly appear to men beautiful: but within are full of dead men's bones, as if to say, so also you by hypocrisy and iniquity. Mercy and truth. (AUG.) Scripture loves to join mercy and truth: especially in the psalms.

VERS. 13.-- In darkness. The dead laid in the sepulchre, and the darkness, and the land of forgetfulness, are the same.

VERS. 14.-- I, O Lord, have cried to thee. (CASS.) The things which he endures in his own; behold the choir answering the precentor.

991B(ID.) And I as it were, with those, with whom I am one.

(AUG.) And I. To these dead their works do not profit, etc., as far as Why, O Lord, dost thou cast off.

VERS. 15.-- Why. (CASS.) Behold how much he desires. Why, O Lord. He sets forth that the cause is to be sought: which is, that by the delay of good, and by adversities multiplied, by which the prayer is as it were repulsed, it may be kindled more ardently.

VERS. 16.-- Lifted up. (ID.) First with a swollen heart, afterwards, Humbled. Through confession. Troubled, that is, confounded for his sins, by condemning them damnado.

VERS. 17.-- They have passed. (CASS.) They did not happen gently.

(AUG.) Because it was not of the faithful, but of the unbeliever that it was said 991C: The anger of God abideth on him (Joan. III). For he scourges the sons whom he receives, whence: Whom I love, I rebuke and chastise (Apoc. III). And elsewhere: I will strike and I will heal Percutium: I will kill and I will make to live (Deut. XXXII). [Vulg. Dt 32:39 ego occidam, et ego vivere faciam : percutiam, et ego sanabo, the two members in the reverse order] (ID.) They have passed and troubled. Because one thing we already suffer from condemnation, and another we fear from eternal vengeance. Thy terrors. (CASS.) Which I suffer: because it pleased thee, not by my desert. (AUG.) The terrors of the judgment to come, which all flesh fears.

They have troubled me. According to the infirmity of the flesh. (AUG.) They have troubled me, sometimes, terrors: they so trouble the mind of one thinking, with evils hanging round about, that they seem like waters to flow about, and at once to surround on every side, whence they both seem to be friends, and desert after their manner, whence the Apostle: All have forsaken me 991D(II Tim. IV).

VERS. 18.-- They have surrounded me. (CASS.) Sins shut him in on every side with a copious flood.

All the day. (AUG.) Because at no time are evils wanting to the Church until the world be ended. But all these things are done, that the prayer of the Church may come before God until that salvation come, where there shall be nothing of evils.

VERS. 19.-- Friend (CASS.) Even those who are joined by a pious and faithful love.

Neighbour and acquaintances, etc. Kindred. Often have human offices been withdrawn from the just through fear.

PSALMUS LXXXVIII.

VERS. 2.-- Misericordias. (CASS.) Hic Psalmus de 992Aspe Christianorum et magnificentia Domini multa dicit, per quae nemo seducitur, qui digne supplicet, quod verus Israel ita intelligit. Primo de misericordia et veritate se cantare promittit Propheta.

In aeternum. (CASS., REM.) Quomodo misericordias in aeternum cantat, et gratias agit, qui miseriae non meminit? Quomodo autem plena beatitudo si memoria reatus mentem tangit? Sed saepe laeti tristium meminimus, et sani dolorum sine dolore, et inde amplius laeti et grati sumus; sic itaque et miseriae recordatio nil beatitudinis detrahit.

Veritatem. Promissionem. In ore, non ex ore labitur, sed in ore diu tanquam dulce versatur.

VERS. 3.-- Quoniam dixisti. Hic dicit: Unde scit? et quae misericordiae Dei per Christum sint? (AUG.) 992BQuas misericordias, et quam veritatem cantabo? Ecce.

Quoniam dixisti. Quasi dicat: Ego homo secure dico, quod tu, Deus, dixisti, per Spiritum manifestasti.

Misericordia aedificabitur. (AUG.) Utrumque repetit, quod praedixit. Quia universae viae Domini misericordia et veritas. Non exhibetur veritas in impletione promissorum, nisi praecedat misericordia in remissione peccatorum. Denique, veritas Judaeis, quibus promissa facta sunt, pertinet, misericordia, gentibus: ut ait Apostolus: Dico enim Jesum Christum ministrum fuisse circumcisionis propter veritatem Dei implendam: gentes autem super misericordia honorare Deum (Rom. XV).

In coelis. Qui enarrant gloriam Dei, per quos aedificatur 992Cmisericordia.

VERS. 4.-- Juravi David servo meo. Securus est iste, ideo quia Deus dixit: securior, quia juravit. Juratio Dei promissionis est confirmatio, ex utroque fit homo Ethan, id est, robustus.

VERS. 5.-- In aeternum. (CASS.) Non est temporalis aedificatio misericordiae, sicut ruina iniquitatis temporalis est: destruitur enim iniquitas temporalis in quibusdam, ut in eis aedificetur aeterna misericordia, unde Jeremiae Dominus dicit: Ecce ergo constitui te super gentes et regna, ut evellas et destruas, et disperdas, et dissipes, et aedifices et plantes. In generationem. (AUG.) Generatio enim non potest, etc., usque ad sedebit et tunc in sanctis.

VERS. 6.-- Confitebuntur coeli. (CAS.) Diapsalma. 992DSecundo diversis modis laudes, et potentiam Dei describit, quasi, sicut dixisti, ita fiet. Confitebuntur, laudabunt.

Confitebuntur coeli mirabilia. In omni enim misericordia perditorum, in justificatione impiorum quid laudamus nisi mirabilia Dei? Laudas quia surrexerunt mortui, plus lauda quia redempti sunt perditi. Vides enim hominem heri voraginem ebrietatis, hodie ornamentum sobrietatis. Vides enim hominem heri coenum luxuriae, hodie decus temperantiae: heri blasphematorem Dei, hodie laudatorem Dei. Vides hominem heri servum creaturae, hodie cultorem Creatoris: haec sunt mirabilia quae confitentur coeli. Etenim veritatem. (CASS.) Vel sine enim. Mirabilia 993Aquomodo omnia agit et administrat ubique. Veritas in Ecclesia ubi creditur, Verbum caro factum, et quod Trinitas, prius Deus.

VERS. 7.-- Quoniam quis. (AUG.) Notandum quod idem sunt coeli et nubes, scilicet praedicatores. Sed coeli, praedicatores, propter fulgorem veritatis. Nubes, quae nebulosae sunt propter mortalitatem carnis, et quia transeunt, ubi et abscondita, quae post in judicio clarebunt. In filiis. Vel superis, vel hominibus. Ne ergo putetur tantum homo: ille enim naturalis, nos adoptivi; ille genitus, nos creati; ille ab aeterno genitus, nos in tempore facti; ille unicus, nos multi.

VERS. 8.-- Super omnes. (ID.) Angelos, vel homines, qui sunt stipatores ejus impares, qui ei dono ejus proximant.

993BVERS. 9.-- Tibi. (ID.) Qui omnia fecisti, etc., usque ad tentari supra id quod potest homo.

VERS. 11.-- Vulneratum. Humilitatus. est perdendo, quos tenebat; vulneratus percusso corde, ubi superbiebat. Superbum. (AUG.) Scilicet draconem, qui in mari factus est ad illudendum ei, qui per humilem Christum, in quo alii sunt humiles, humiliantur; humiliavit se Christus, ut humiliaret superbum. Superbus enim superbos tenebat: vulneratur diabolus vulnerato Christo, nondum ex toto mortuus est. Inimicos. Aerias potestates vel Judaeos per mundum dispersos, vel de hominibus alios assumpsit qui sunt spolia diaboli, alios reliquisti quos post eum abire permisisti.

VERS. 12.-- Tui sunt coeli et tua est terra orbem, 993Cetc. (ID.) Ideo in coelo triumphavit de diabolo, quia ejus est coelum; in terra de Judaea, quia ejus est terra. Cur ergo illi in alienis superbierunt?

Tu fundasti. Cur ergo in eum se erigunt, cujus est ambitus mundi, et omnes creaturae quae in eo sunt?

VERS. 13.-- Aquilonem. Diabolus. Mare tu creasti. Saeculum. Stulte ergo in eum se erigunt, a quo creata sunt. Thabor et Hermon in nomine tuo. (AUG.) Montes Syriae, et per eos gentes accipiuntur a parte totum per synecdochen.

Exsultabunt. Christo veniente allegorice. Thabor, Judaei, ad quos primum lumen venit. Hermon, Gentes, quae prius fuerunt anathematizatae. In nomine tuo exsultabunt, conjunctis in angulari lapide duobus 993Dparietibus.

(AUG.) Thabor. Veniens lumen a summo scilicet lumine, quo veniente fit anathema ejus, id est diaboli, qui nos tenebat in errore suo. Quod est: a te datum est ut illuminemur, ut anathema demus diabolo.

VERS. 15.-- Praeparatio sedis tuae. (CASS.) Sedes Dei aeterna, sed in judicio apparebit parata, cum ipse videbitur juste judicare. Vel modo homines discernendo et justa tenendo, parant se sedem Domino.

Misericordia et veritas praecedent faciem tuam. A similitudine praecursoris Dominum hospitium praeparantis.

994AVERS. 16.-- Beatus populus qui scit, etc. (CASS.) Ille scit, qui suam laetitiam non in sua, sed Domini virtute ponit, vel, qui, quod ore cantat, corde intelligit: unde sequitur hoc praemium, in lumine, id est, in contemplatione Trinitatis perseverabunt.

Jubilationem. Jubilus, gaudium quod verbis explicari non potest, nec tamen penitus reticeri. Domine, in lumine vultus tui ambulabunt, et in nomine tuo exsultabunt. (CASS.) Commendat gratiam, de qua jubilus.

(AUG.) Vel in bene placito tuo, id est in Christo, ideo in ipso, quia assumpsit carnem nostram, in quo omnis spes.

VERS. 20.-- Tunc locutus est in visione. (CASS.) Diapsalma. Tertio promissiones Patris de Christo. 994BSuperior laus non est dubia, quam paterna confirmat auctoritas. (CASS.)

(AUG.) Tunc. Quando disposuisti testamentum, vel cum haec diceres mihi, tunc locutus es sanctis, reliquis prophetis in visione, non enim ignoranter locuti sunt, sicut Montanus et quidam alii haeretici dixerunt.

VERS. 21.-- David servum meum oleo sancto meo unxi eum. (AUG.) Manu fortem, servum obedientem, ideo in eo posui adjutorium.

VERS. 23.-- Inimicus in eo. (ID.) Diabolus, unde: Venit princeps mundi hujus, et in me non habet quidquam (Joan. XIV).

Filius iniquitatis non apponet nocere. Judas non apponet, non addet effectum voluntati.

994CVERS. 24.-- A facie ipsius inimicos. (AUG.) Cum facies ejus peccatores respicit, a criminibus separantur, quibus non est locus sub praesentia ejus.

VERS. 25.-- Et veritas mea et misericordia mea cum ipso, et in nomine meo exaltabitur cornu ejus. (ID.) Saepe misericordia et veritas commendantur nobis, etc., usque ad ubi haec sibi occurrunt.

VERS. 31.-- Si autem dereliquerint. Non solum de persistentibus, sed et de cadentibus haec promitto.

VERS. 33.-- In virga. Quis enim est filius? etc., usque ad: Et in verberibus, etc.

Non dispergam. (AUG.) Ipse non tollit misericordiam ei, qui Christianus quidem est: quod si homo ita iniquus est, ut fugiat accedente patre, ipse se 994Dalienat, non pater abjicit eum.

VERS. 35.-- Neque profanabo. Profana esset promissio, si esset inexpleta. Nunquid propter malos pisces nihil ex illa sagena mittitur in vascula? Mittentur utique boni pisces, id est, quos praedestinavit.

VERS. 36.-- Semel juravi. (CASS.) Homo frequenter, Deus semel, qui non variatur.

In sancto. In homine Christo, in quo complendum erat quod juravi; vel David, id est Christo, per sanctitatem. Semen, Christiani.

VERS. 38.-- Sicut sol in conspectu. (AUG.) Secundum animam, etc., usque ad in coelo, id est Christus.

Tu vero repulisti. (CASS.) Diapsalma. Quarto 995Aadversa praedictis promissionibus ponit, ne putentur in alio impleri, quam in futuro tunc Christo. Tu vero repulisti. Quasi, Christianis haec bona, sed non Judaeis, qui se privaverunt promissione, et hoc est: Tu vero Christum tuum, id est, unctum David, a regno repulisti pro peccato, quod commisit contra Uriam de Bethsabee; Et despexisti, vel sprevisti, quia multa indigna passus; distulisti, diu in tribulatione, testamentum, promissa Judaeis, ad gentes lata sunt. (AUG.) Tu vero. Vel, haec omnia de Christo et Ecclesia, repulisti, ad patibulum Christum tuum, et in despectum dedisti. Vel, distulisti a gloria, ad tempus, vel secundum membra.

VERS. 40.-- Testamentum. Promissio videtur eversa, et sancti profani reputantur. Sepes, praelatos, 995Bdestruxisti, dum occiduntur. Et posuisti firmamentum ejus formidinem. Qui firmabant alios docendo, jam sunt timori, dum affliguntur, et quidam jam sunt direpti a transeuntibus viam, quae est Christus.

VERS. 44.-- Avertisti adjutorium gladii ejus. Id est praedicationem. Non es auxiliatus ei in bello, sed dedisti ad passiones. Destruxisti eum ab emendatione, etc., id est, quidam mundi defecerunt, et in terram redacti sunt. Minorasti, ut putatur, dum cito de vita auferuntur.

(AUG.) Quare illa promisit Deus, etc., usque ad ut haec promissio in aliis exspectaretur.

VERS. 45.-- Destruxisti eum. Haec omnia venerunt Judaeis, non tamen ablato eis Christo, et aeterno 995Cregno, sed dilato. Sedem ejus in terram collisisti. Id est, regnum eorum ubique terrarum deletum est, quia jam non est de eis princeps.

VERS. 46.-- Minorasti. Quia diu staret regnum eorum, si sub Deo. Perfudisti eum confusione. Quia gestat opprobrium infidelitatis. Minorasti. (AUG.) Putabant se regnaturos in aeternum, sed minuisti dies regni eorum, ut non staret, juxta opinionem eorum.

VERS. 47.-- Usquequo, Domine? (CASS.) Diapsalma. Quinto. Ecce in quo impletae promissiones, scilicet in substantia David, quae vivit, et eruit animam, id est, in Christo. (AUG.) Sed, usquequo non resuscitas Christum? Quae substantia? quae nihil, nisi per ipsum. Quis est homo qui vivit et non videbit mortem? 995Dnullus. In his jam postulat subvenire homini, vel specialiter Judaeis.

VERS. 48.-- Memorare quae mea substantia. (ID.) Dicit hoc David, carne positus in Judaeis, spe in Christo. Quae sit mea substantia? Et si Judaei deficiunt, non deficit mea substantia, non omnino interit radix, unde veniet Maria: et de ea veniet semen cui promissum est. Nam de populo illo virgo Maria, de virgine Maria caro Christi, et caro illa non est peccatrix, sed peccatorum mundatrix. Nunquid enim vane. Omnes filii hominum ierunt in vanitatem, non tamen vane constituisti eos: unde ergo mundas eos a vanitate? per semen, in quo est mea substantia; de quo subdit: Quis est homo?

996AVERS. 49.-- Quis est hemo? (ID.) Nulli hoc convenit, nisi Christo: et si enim resurgentes invenit, et non ultra videbunt mortem: non tamen ipsi eruent animas suas de manu iuferiori, sed ille, qui potest animam ponere, et iterum sumere, cui nemo eam tollet. (CASS.) Vel sic, nullus vivet, vel eruet animam: et cum hoc sit, ubi sunt misericordiae? Jam rogat promissiones impleri, quas David fecit.

VERS. 50.-- Ubi sunt misericordiae? (ID.) Diapsalma. Sexto, in membris etiam implentur promissiones, non temporaliter, sed spiritualiter. Et loquitur in persona Ecclesiae.

VERS. 51.-- Memor esto, Domine. (AUG.) Ut remuneres, videtur oblitus, dum differt. Opprobri servorum. (CASS.) Illati servis a multis gentibus. 996B(AUG.) Quod ego (Ecclesia) Continui, id est, portavi. In sinu, in secreto mentis, quia palam non audebat loqui.

VERS. 53.-- Benedictus. (CASS.) Contra maledictiones gentium. (AUG.) Benedictus. Exclamatio ex visa claritate Christi.

PSALM LXXXVIII.

VERS. 2.-- The mercies. (CASS.) This Psalm says many things concerning the 992Ahope of Christians and the magnificence of the Lord, by which no one is led astray who prays worthily, which the true Israel so understands. First the Prophet promises that he will sing of mercy and truth.

For ever. (CASS., REM.) How does he sing the mercies for ever, and give thanks, who is not mindful of misery? And how is there full blessedness if the memory of guilt touches the mind? But we often remember sad things in gladness, and sorrows in health without sorrow, and thence we are the more glad and thankful; and so likewise the recollection of misery takes away nothing of blessedness.

Truth. The promise. In the mouth: it does not slip out of the mouth, but is turned over long in the mouth as something sweet.

VERS. 3.-- For thou hast said. Here he says: Whence does he know? and what are the mercies of God through Christ? (AUG.) 992BWhich mercies, and what truth shall I sing? Behold.

For thou hast said. As if he should say: I, a man, say securely what thou, God, hast said, hast made manifest through the Spirit.

Mercy shall be built up. (AUG.) He repeats both, which he foretold. Because all the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth. Truth is not shown forth in the fulfilling of the things promised, unless mercy go before in the remission of sins. Finally, truth pertains to the Jews, to whom the promises were made, mercy to the Gentiles: as the Apostle says: For I say that Jesus Christ was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God, which was to be fulfilled: but that the Gentiles honour God for his mercy (Rom. XV) [Vulg. Rom 15:8 has instead "to confirm the promises of the fathers"; the gloss's argument turns on the fulfilling, which it repeats two lines above].

In the heavens. They who declare the glory of God, through whom mercy is built up 992C.

VERS. 4.-- I have sworn to David my servant. This man is secure, for this reason, because God has said it: more secure, because he has sworn. God's swearing is the confirmation of the promise, and out of both is made the man Ethan, that is, the strong one.

VERS. 5.-- For ever. (CASS.) The building up of mercy is not temporal, as the ruin of iniquity is temporal: for temporal iniquity is destroyed in certain men, that in them eternal mercy may be built up, whence the Lord says to Jeremiah: Behold therefore I have set thee over the nations and over kingdoms, to root up, and to pull down, and to waste, and to destroy, and to build, and to plant. Unto generation. [Vulg. Jer 1:10 reads "Behold I have set thee this day over the nations", with no "therefore"] (AUG.) For generation cannot, etc., as far as he shall sit, and then in the saints.

VERS. 6.-- The heavens shall confess. (CAS.) Diapsalma. 992DSecondly he describes the praises and the power of God in divers ways, as if to say, as thou hast said, so shall it be done. They shall confess, they shall praise.

The heavens shall confess thy wonders. For in every mercy shown to the lost, in the justifying of the ungodly, what do we praise but the wonders of God? Thou praisest because the dead have risen; praise the more because the lost have been redeemed. For thou seest a man who yesterday was a whirlpool of drunkenness, today the ornament of sobriety. For thou seest a man who yesterday was the mire of luxury, today the grace of temperance: yesterday a blasphemer of God, today a praiser of God. Thou seest a man who yesterday was a slave of the creature, today a worshipper of the Creator: these are the wonders which the heavens confess. For thy truth also. (CASS.) Or without for. Wonders, 993Ain that he does and administers all things everywhere. Truth is in the Church where it is believed, the Word was made flesh, and that [there is] a Trinity, and before that, God.

VERS. 7.-- For who. (AUG.) It is to be noted that the heavens and the clouds are the same, namely the preachers. But heavens, that is, preachers, because of the splendour of truth. Clouds, which are cloudy because of the mortality of the flesh, and because they pass away, where also there are hidden things, which afterwards shall be made clear in the judgment. Among the sons. Either of those above, or of men. Let him not therefore be thought to be man only: for he is natural, we adoptive; he begotten, we created; he begotten from eternity, we made in time; he the only one, we many.

VERS. 8.-- Above all. (ID.) The angels, or men, who are his unequal attendants, who draw near to him by his own gift.

993BVERS. 9.-- To thee. (ID.) Thou who hast made all things, etc., as far as to be tempted above that which a man can bear.

VERS. 11.-- Wounded. He was humbled by losing those whom he held Humilitatus.; wounded by the smiting of the heart, wherein he was proud. The proud one. (AUG.) Namely the dragon, who was made in the sea to be mocked at, who through the humble Christ, in whom others are humble, are humbled; Christ humbled himself, that he might humble the proud one. For the proud one held the proud: the devil is wounded by the wounded Christ, he is not yet wholly dead. The enemies. The powers of the air, or the Jews dispersed through the world, or of men he took up some who are the spoils of the devil, and others thou didst leave, whom thou didst permit to go away after him.

VERS. 12.-- Thine are the heavens, and thine is the earth, the world, 993Cetc. (ID.) Therefore he triumphed in heaven over the devil, because heaven is his; on earth over Judea, because the earth is his. Why then were they proud in what was another's?

Thou hast founded. Why then do they raise themselves up against him, whose is the compass of the world, and all the creatures which are in it?

VERS. 13.-- The north. The devil. The sea thou hast created. The world. Foolishly therefore do they raise themselves up against him by whom they were created. Thabor and Hermon shall rejoice in thy name. (AUG.) Mountains of Syria, and by them the Gentiles are understood, the whole from a part, by synecdoche.

They shall rejoice. At Christ's coming, allegorically. Thabor, the Jews, to whom the light first came. Hermon, the Gentiles, who were formerly accursed. In thy name they shall rejoice, the two walls being joined together 993Din the corner stone.

(AUG.) Thabor. The light coming from the highest light, namely, at whose coming the anathema of him, that is, of the devil, who held us in his error, is made. Which is: it is given by thee that we should be enlightened, that we should give the devil to anathema.

VERS. 15.-- The preparation of thy seat. (CASS.) The seat of God is eternal, but in the judgment it shall appear prepared, when he himself shall be seen to judge justly. Or in this present time men, by discerning and by holding to just things, prepare themselves as a seat for the Lord.

Mercy and truth shall go before thy face. From the likeness of a forerunner preparing a lodging for the Lord.

994AVERS. 16.-- Blessed is the people that knoweth, etc. (CASS.) He knows, who places his gladness not in his own strength, but in the Lord's, or, who understands in the heart what he sings with the mouth: whence this reward follows, in the light, that is, they shall persevere in the contemplation of the Trinity.

Jubilation. Jubilation is a joy which cannot be unfolded in words, nor yet altogether kept silent. O Lord, they shall walk in the light of thy countenance, and in thy name they shall rejoice. (CASS.) He commends the grace, of which the jubilation is.

(AUG.) Or in thy good pleasure, that is, in Christ, therefore in him, because he took our flesh, in whom is all hope.

VERS. 20.-- Then he spoke in a vision. [Vulg. Ps 88:20 has the second person, "then thou didst speak" — as the gloss itself has it four lines below] (CASS.) Diapsalma. Thirdly, the promises of the Father concerning Christ. 994BThe praise above is not doubtful, which the Father's authority confirms. (CASS.)

(AUG.) Then. When thou didst appoint the testament, or when thou didst say these things to me, then thou didst speak to the saints, to the rest of the prophets in a vision, for they did not speak unknowingly, as Montanus and certain other heretics have said.

VERS. 21.-- David my servant, with my holy oil I have anointed him. (AUG.) Strong of hand, an obedient servant, therefore in him I have placed help.

VERS. 23.-- The enemy in him. (ID.) The devil, whence: The prince of this world cometh, and in me he hath not anything (Joan. XIV).

The son of iniquity shall not go on to hurt. Judas shall not go on, shall not add the effect to the will.

994CVERS. 24.-- From his face his enemies. (AUG.) When his face looks upon sinners, they are separated from crimes, for which there is no place under his presence.

VERS. 25.-- And my truth and my mercy shall be with him, and in my name shall his horn be exalted. (ID.) Often mercy and truth are commended to us, etc., as far as where these meet one another.

VERS. 31.-- But if they forsake. Not only concerning those who persist, but also concerning those who fall, do I promise these things.

VERS. 33.-- With a rod. For who is a son? etc., as far as: And with stripes, etc.

I will not scatter. (AUG.) He himself does not take away his mercy from him who is indeed a Christian: but if a man is so wicked that he flees when his father draws near, he alienates 994Dhimself, the father does not cast him off.

VERS. 35.-- Neither will I profane. The promise would be profane, if it were unfulfilled. Is nothing sent into the vessels out of that net because of the bad fishes? The good fishes shall surely be sent, that is, those whom he has predestinated.

VERS. 36.-- I have sworn once. (CASS.) Man swears often, God once, who is not changed.

In the holy one. In the man Christ, in whom was to be fulfilled what I have sworn; or David, that is Christ, through holiness. The seed, Christians.

VERS. 38.-- As the sun in the sight. (AUG.) According to the soul, etc., as far as in heaven, that is, Christ.

But thou hast rejected. (CASS.) Diapsalma. Fourthly 995Ahe sets adverse things against the promises aforesaid, lest they be thought to be fulfilled in another than in the Christ who was then to come. But thou hast rejected. As if to say, these goods are for Christians, but not for the Jews, who have deprived themselves of the promise, and this is it: But thou hast rejected thy Christ, that is, David the anointed, from the kingdom for the sin which he committed against Urias concerning Bethsabee; And thou hast despised, or hast spurned, because he suffered many unworthy things; thou hast deferred, long in tribulation, the testament, the things promised to the Jews, they have been carried over to the Gentiles. (AUG.) But thou. Or, all these things concerning Christ and the Church: thou hast rejected to the gibbet thy Christ, and hast given him over to contempt. Or, thou hast deferred him from glory, for a time, or according to his members.

VERS. 40.-- The testament. The promise seems overthrown, and the saints are reckoned profane. The hedges, the prelates, 995Bthou hast destroyed, while they are slain. And thou hast made his strength fear. They who strengthened others by teaching are now for a terror, while they are afflicted, and some are now plundered by them that pass by the way, which is Christ.

VERS. 44.-- Thou hast turned away the help of his sword. That is, preaching. Thou hast not helped him in battle, but hast given him over to sufferings. Thou hast destroyed him from amendment, etc., that is, certain clean ones have failed, and have been brought down to the earth. [Vulg. Ps 88:45 reads "from cleansing"] Thou hast lessened, as it is thought, while they are quickly taken away from life.

(AUG.) Why did God promise those things, etc., as far as that this promise might be looked for in others.

VERS. 45.-- Thou hast destroyed him. All these things came upon the Jews, yet Christ was not taken from them, nor the eternal 995Ckingdom, but deferred. Thou hast cast his seat down to the ground. That is, their kingdom has been blotted out everywhere on earth, because there is now no prince from among them.

VERS. 46.-- Thou hast lessened. Because their kingdom would stand long, if it were under God. Thou hast covered him with confusion. Because he bears the reproach of unbelief. Thou hast lessened. (AUG.) They thought that they would reign for ever, but thou hast lessened the days of their kingdom, that it should not stand, according to their opinion.

VERS. 47.-- How long, O Lord? (CASS.) Diapsalma. Fifthly. Behold in whom the promises were fulfilled, namely in the substance of David, which lives, and delivered the soul, that is, in Christ. (AUG.) But, how long dost thou not raise up Christ? What substance? which is nothing, save through him. Who is the man that liveth and shall not see death? [Vulg. Ps 88:49 has the future, "that shall live"] 995Dno one. In these things he now asks that help be brought to man, or especially to the Jews.

VERS. 48.-- Remember what my substance is. (ID.) David says this, set in the flesh among the Jews, in hope in Christ. What is my substance? And if the Jews fail, my substance does not fail, the root does not wholly perish, whence Mary shall come: and of her shall come the seed to whom the promise was made. For of that people came the Virgin Mary, of the Virgin Mary the flesh of Christ, and that flesh is not a sinner, but the cleanser of sinners. For hast thou in vain. All the sons of men have gone into vanity, yet not in vain didst thou establish them: whence then dost thou cleanse them from vanity? through the seed, in which is my substance; concerning which he adds: Who is the man?

996AVERS. 49.-- Who is the man? hemo (ID.) This befits none, save Christ: for even if he finds those rising again, and they shall not see death any more: yet they themselves do not deliver their own souls out of the lower hand, iuferiori but he does who can lay down his soul, and take it again, from whom no one shall take it away. [Vulg. Ps 88:49 has the singular throughout, "he shall deliver his soul out of the hand of hell" — the gloss's whole argument rests on the plural it prints] (CASS.) Or thus, no one shall live, or shall deliver his soul: and since this is so, where are the mercies? He now asks that the promises be fulfilled which he made to David.

VERS. 50.-- Where are the mercies? (ID.) Diapsalma. Sixthly, in the members also the promises are fulfilled, not temporally, but spiritually. And he speaks in the person of the Church.

VERS. 51.-- Be mindful, O Lord. (AUG.) That thou mayest repay; he seems to have forgotten, while he defers. Of the reproach of the servants. (CASS.) Brought upon the servants by many nations. 996B(AUG.) Which I (the Church) have held, that is, have borne. In the bosom, in the secret of the mind, because openly she did not dare to speak.

VERS. 53.-- Blessed. (CASS.) Against the curses of the nations. (AUG.) Blessed. An exclamation out of the brightness of Christ that has been seen.

PSALMUS LXXXIX.

VERS. 1.-- Oratio Moysi. (AUG.) Cum vetus vita et nova, etc., usque ad et videt mirabilia de lege Dei.

(CASS., REM.) Agit iste psalmus de defectu generis humani, qui per Christum auferetur.

Domine refugium. (CASS.) Primo, aeternum proponit refugium temporaliter homini.

VERS. 2.-- Priusquam montes. Ne autem videretur 996Cnon fuisse, antequam esset nobis refugium; adjungit priusquam. Montes, terra. (AUG.) Elcce omnis rationalis creatura hac differentia distincta est, ut montium nomine celsitudo angelorum; et terrae nomine humilitas hominum: ideoque non incongrue verba sic distinxit, ut diceret montes, id est angelos, fieri, et terram, id est homines, formari. Fierent aut formaretur. Formari, vel fingi, solet dici secundum corpora: fieri de nihilo. A saeculo. Aptius diceret, etc., usque ad hic autem ponitur saeculum pro aeterno. A saeculo. Ecce quae aeternitas nobis refugium, etc., usque ad Ne avertas, quoniam mille anni. Tu es. Optime ait, quia immutabilis. Non dicit eris, vel fuisti, cum immutabilis essentia Dei non noverit praeteritum, vel futurum; unde dictum est: Ego sum 996Dqui sum. Et, Qui est misit me ad vos? Et: Tu autem idem ipse es, et aani tui non deficient.

VERS. 3.-- Ne avertas. (CASS.) Secundo, exponit infirmitatem hominis, cui petit subveniri. In humilitatem. Id est, terrenam concupiscentiam, etc., usque ad qui docuit coelestia quaerere.

VERS. 4.-- Dies hesterna. (AUG.) Non dicit, saltem sicut crastina, etc., usque ad in sollicitudine, et trepidatione, qnasi nihil est.

VERS. 6.-- Mane sicut herba. (AUG., CASS.) Mutetur a qualitate noctis.

Vespere decidat. In extremis secta, vel fracta. (CASS.) Mane sicut herba. Dixi, quod anni habentur, etc., usque ad juventus quae floret et transit.

997AVespere. Senectus, quando refrigescit vigor hominis. Vel, mane sicut herba. Apta comparatio, quasi, sicut herba mutatur a qualitate, quam habet in nocte, in deteriorem mane orto sole: ita mutatur homo in deterius.

VERS. 7.-- Defecimus in ira tua, et in furore tuo turbati sumus. (AUG.) Mortales et passibiles facti, quod tamen morte finire timemus, unde sequitur: Et in furore tuo turbati sumus. Saeculum. Vitam nostram pravam. Vel saeculum posteros. In illuminatione vultus. (CASS.) Illa teguntur, quae veniam habent: illuminantur, quae puniuntur.

VERS. 9.-- Quoniam omnes dies. (AUG.) Cognitio nostra defecit obtenebrata ratione per peccatum, vel, tempus vitae abbreviatum est, et pene defecit, 997Bquia ad paucitatem redacti sunt dies vitae nostrae. Anni nostri sicut. (CASS., AUG.) Miseria et brevitas hujus vitae exprimitur hic per similitudinem araneae, quae texit inanes telas, ut dolo capiat muscas: unde sicut aranea, id est, in rebus corruptibilibus laborabamus, inania texebamus. (CASS.) Vita per iram Dei breviata est, quia praesumptione longioris vitae peccabant. Et nos ipsi in ira tua defecimus. (AUG.) Id est, essentia nostra defecit per aerumnas. Meditabuntur . . . anni, non operabuntur, quia sine utilitate transeunt. Vel, meditabuntur passive, id est, reputabuntur anni nostri sicut aranea, id est, sicut inanes et inutiles.

VERS. 10.-- Septuaginta. (ID.) Terrenorum appetitus quae septem diebus aguntur: si in virtutibus octoginta, id est, aeternitas petitur. Annis. Vel anni, 997Calia littera. Quo temporis spatio dicuntur longaevi, qui etiam usque ad octoginta annos aliquas vires habere videntur. Octoginta. Quia et citra octoginta annos sunt quidam infirmi, etc., usque ad redemptionem corporis exspectantes. Mansuetudo. Clementia est, si Dei: domatio, si nostra. Ipse enim per clementiam mansuetus, domando nos efficit mansuetos, et sic corripiemur.

VERS. 11.-- Quis novi. (ID.) Potestas irae hominis est corpus occidere, post nihil facere. Deus et hic punit, et post in gehennam mittit: et a paucis major ejus ira intelligitur.

VERS. 12.-- Dexteram tuam sic notam fac. (CASS.) Tertio, orat et affirmat liberationem. (AUG.) Dexteram tuam. Christum sic notum fecit, etc., usque ad 997Dut ad dexteram ponat.

Et eruditos corde in sapientia. Vel compeditos corde. Quod idem est, quia qui erudiuntur in sapientia, pedem mentis injiciunt in compedes Dei, ut a via ejus non exorbitent. Quos sic fecit Deus notos in Novo Testamento, ut pro fide omnia spernerent, quae magna habentur, in Veteri et aeterna morte quaererent: hoc attendens ait, pro eis, qui multa patiuntur a saeculo pro aeternis.

VERS. 13.-- Convertere. Quasi aversa sit facies ejus a tribulatis. Usquequo. Alias aliquantulum. (CASS.) Non ex toto, quae magis prodest, si aliqua tribulatio semper monet nos.

VERS. 14.-- Mane misericordia tua exsultavimus, 998Aet delectatio sumus. (AUG., CASS.) Modo nox, in qua esurimus: tunc autem satiabimur vultu, unde: Satiabor cum apparuerit gloria tua. Et alibi: Mane astabo tibi, et videbo. Nunc autem pro eo laetati sumus, et in malignis diebus in quibus dicimus: Respice in servos.

VERS. 16.-- Respice in servos tuos. Quod facit Deus in se, orat Propheta fieri suo populo: orat, scilicet, ut parcat Judaeis peccantibus, si non pro meritis eorum, saltem propter opera quae in eis fecit.

Et dirige filios eorum. Quasi, etsi ipsi per iniqui-tales dispersi sunt, vel filii, in fine fide corrigantur, qui per se pravi, et inconvertibiles.

VERS. 17.-- Splendor Domini Dei nostri super nos, 998Bet operamini. (HIER., CASS.) Imago Dei recreans menti imprimatur. Vel splendor Dei super nos est, dum crucis impressione decoramur, et vexillum triumphi in fronte portamus. (CASS.) Triplex quippe est imago, etc., usque ad meminerim te, intelligam te, diligam te.

PSALM LXXXIX.

VERS. 1.-- A prayer of Moses. (AUG.) When the old life and the new, etc., as far as and he sees wonders out of the law of God.

(CASS., REM.) This psalm treats of the failing of the human race, which shall be taken away through Christ.

O Lord, a refuge. (CASS.) First, he sets forth an eternal refuge for man in time.

VERS. 2.-- Before the mountains. But lest he should seem 996Cnot to have been, before he was a refuge to us, he adds before. The mountains, the earth. (AUG.) Behold, every rational creature is distinguished Elcce by this difference, that by the name of mountains is meant the loftiness of the angels; and by the name of the earth the lowliness of men: and therefore not unfittingly did he so distinguish the words, that he should say that the mountains, that is, the angels, were made, and that the earth, that is, men, was formed. They should be made, or it should be formed. To be formed, or fashioned, is wont to be said of bodies: to be made, out of nothing. From the world. He would more fitly say, etc., as far as but here the world is put for the eternal. From the world. Behold what eternity is a refuge to us, etc., as far as: Turn not away, for a thousand years. Thou art. Excellently does he say it, because he is unchangeable. He does not say thou shalt be, or thou wast, since the unchangeable essence of God has not known the past, or the future; whence it is said: I am 996Dwho am. And, He who is hath sent me to you? And: But thou art the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail. aani

VERS. 3.-- Turn not away. (CASS.) Secondly, he sets out the infirmity of man, for which he asks that help be brought. Unto lowliness. That is, earthly concupiscence, etc., as far as who taught us to seek the things of heaven.

VERS. 4.-- Yesterday's day. (AUG.) He does not say, at least as tomorrow's, etc., as far as in anxiety, and trembling, as nothing qnasi.

VERS. 6.-- In the morning as grass. (AUG., CASS.) Let it be changed from the quality of the night.

In the evening let it fall. Cut down, or broken, at the last. (CASS.) In the morning as grass. I have said that the years are held, etc., as far as the youth which flowers and passes away.

997AIn the evening. Old age, when the vigour of a man grows cold. Or, in the morning as grass. A fitting comparison, as if to say, as grass is changed from the quality which it has in the night, to a worse one in the morning when the sun is risen: so is a man changed for the worse.

VERS. 7.-- We have failed in thy wrath, and in thy fury we have been troubled. (AUG.) Made mortal and liable to suffering, which nevertheless we fear to end by death, whence follows: And in thy fury we have been troubled. The world. Our depraved life. Or the world, those who come after. In the enlightening of the countenance. (CASS.) Those things are covered which have pardon: those are enlightened which are punished.

VERS. 9.-- For all our days. (AUG.) Our knowledge has failed, darkened in its reason by sin, or, the time of life has been shortened, and has almost failed, 997Bbecause the days of our life have been brought down to fewness. Our years as. (CASS., AUG.) The misery and shortness of this life is expressed here by the likeness of the spider, which weaves empty webs, that it may catch flies by guile: whence as a spider, that is, we laboured among corruptible things, we wove empty things. (CASS.) Life has been shortened through the wrath of God, because they sinned in the presumption of a longer life. And we ourselves have failed in thy wrath. (AUG.) That is, our essence has failed through hardships. The years . . . shall meditate, they shall not work, because they pass without profit. Or, they shall meditate passively, that is, our years shall be reckoned as a spider, that is, as empty and useless.

VERS. 10.-- Seventy. (ID.) The appetite for earthly things which are done in seven days: if in virtues, eighty, that is, eternity is sought. Years. Or the years, 997Canother reading. By which space of time they are called long-lived, who even up to eighty years are seen to have some strength. Eighty. Because even short of eighty years some are infirm, etc., as far as awaiting the redemption of the body. Meekness. It is clemency, if it be God's: a taming, if it be ours. For he himself, being meek through clemency, by taming us makes us meek, and so we shall be corrected.

VERS. 11.-- Who I have known. [Vulg. Ps 89:11 has the third person, "who hath known"] (ID.) The power of a man's anger is to kill the body, and afterwards to do nothing. God both punishes here, and afterwards sends into hell: and by few is his greater anger understood.

VERS. 12.-- So make known thy right hand. (CASS.) Thirdly, he prays and affirms deliverance. (AUG.) Thy right hand. He so made known Christ, etc., as far as 997Dthat he may set him at the right hand.

And them that are learned in heart in wisdom. Or, fettered in heart. Which is the same thing, because they who are taught in wisdom thrust the foot of the mind into the fetters of God, that they may not stray from his way. These God so made known in the New Testament, that for faith they should spurn all things which are held great, in the Old, and should seek in eternal death: attending to this he speaks, on behalf of those who suffer many things from the world for the sake of eternal things.

VERS. 13.-- Turn thee. As though his face were turned away from those in tribulation. How long. Elsewhere, a little. (CASS.) Not wholly, which profits the more, if some tribulation always admonishes us.

VERS. 14.-- In the morning we have rejoiced in thy mercy, 998Aand we have been delighted. delectatio (AUG., CASS.)
