Now it is night, in which we hunger: but then we shall be filled with the countenance, whence: I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear. And elsewhere: In the morning I will stand before thee, and will see. But now instead of it we have been glad, even in the evil days in which we say: Look upon thy servants.

VERS. 16.-- Look upon thy servants. What God does in himself, the Prophet prays may be done for his people: he prays, namely, that he may spare the sinning Jews, if not for their merits, at least for the sake of the works which he has wrought in them.

And direct their children. As if to say, even if they themselves have been scattered through iniquities iniqui-tales, at least the children, at the last, may be corrected by faith, who of themselves are depraved and unconvertible.

VERS. 17.-- The brightness of the Lord our God upon us, 998Band work ye. [Vulg. Ps 89:17 reads "and direct thou the work of our hands upon us"] (HIER., CASS.) Let the image of God, restoring, be imprinted on the mind. Or the brightness of God is upon us, while we are adorned by the impress of the cross, and bear the standard of triumph on the forehead. (CASS.) For the image is threefold, etc., as far as that I may remember thee, understand thee, love thee.

PSALMUS XC.

VERS. 1.-- Laus cantici. Laus, et humana est: sed haec est cantici, quia non nisi divina. Est enim psalmus iste hymnus contra daemones. Propheta ergo de quolibet sancto ait: Qui habitat in adjutorio, etc.

(CASS.) Ostendit tentationes diaboli per humilitatem victas a Christo, et a suis, manentibus in auxilio Dei, ut et nos per eum discamus tentationes superare, quia est jauna per quam, si quis introierit, 998Cingredietur, et egredietur, et pascua eveniet.

(AUG.) Janua Christus; intrare per eum, est imitari eum, non in divinitate, et potentia, et miraculis, sed in eo quo factus est pro nobis, id est, humilitate ad quam vocat, dicens: Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde. De hoc psalmo tentavit Christum diabolus. Christi autem tentatio nostra est doctrina, quem sequentes ex eo vincimus.

Qui habitat. (CASS.) Describit primo fidentem in solo Deo, omnino protectione Dei vallatum. Qui habitat, id est, qui totam spem non in se, sed in Deo semper constituit, omnibus modis protegetur a Deo. Nota verborum correspondentiam: sicut enim semper habitat, sic et semper commorabitur. Illud affirmat, scilicet quod habitat; hoc promittit, 998Dscilicet quod protegetur.

In protectione Dei coeli commorabitur. Ut scilicet non declinet ad dexteram vel ad sinistram, sicut in Veteri Testamento praeceptum erat filiis Israel, ut incederent via regia, non declinantes ad dexteram vel ad sinistram. Via regia, via Christi regis nostri, qui sic viam mundi cucurrit, ut nec prosperis illiceretur, nec adversis frangeretur.

VERS. 2.-- Deus meus. (CASS.) Ne putes post susceptionem et refugium jam nihil esse petendum, addit: Sperabo in eum, ne aliquando de se praesumat, hoc si fecisset Adam, bene staret.

VERS. 3.-- De laqueo. (ID.) Tentatio, vel per facta, quae hic dicitur laqueus; vel per verba quae 999Ahic, a verbo aspero; quasi, etsi leve videatur, grave tamen est verbo tentari. Laqueus, versutiae spiritualium, vel carnalium inimicorum; verbum asperum, omne dictum, quod movet a regulis divinis. (AUG.) De laqueo venantium, daemonum, qui non in via Christo, sed circa, ad dexteram vel sinistram, tendunt laqueos. In quos et per verbum asperum cadunt aliqui, ut qui nolunt esse Christi, propter insultantes Christiano nomini, et qui timent detractiones hominum, ut cessent a via Dei.

VERS. 4.-- Scapulis. (AUG., CASS.) Speranti beneficia Dei promittit. Scapulae, sunt operationes mirabilium, quibus ut humeris virtus Dei ostenditur. Pennae, monita Prophetarum, quae ad coelos vehunt.

999BObumbrabit. Ut neque sol divinitatis, neque luna humanitatis te urat. In pennis protectio. Scapulis suis. Alias, Inter scapulas. (AUG.) Id est, ante pectus suum te ponit, etc., usque ad ut sub alis ejus speremus.

VERS. 5.-- Veritas. (ID.) Dei est, qui non respicit personas, nec miscet sperantes de seipsis cum his qui sperant in Deo, sed discernit humiles vel superbos. (CASS.) Vel veritas, incarnatio Christi, unde: De terra veritas orta est (Psal. LXXXIV), quod et scapulis obumbrat, et scuto defendit. Sicut notavit genera defensionum, notat et genera periculorum, ut sit gratior liberatio.

A timore nocturno. A similitudine periculi, unde tantum timor habetur. A timore nocturno. (AUG.) Qui 999Cignorans peccat, etc., usque ad Cadent a latere tuo mille.

VERS. 7.-- Cadent a latere. (CASS.) Secundo, fidentis in Deo caput, id est Christum, in coelo levatum, dicit a nullo posse contingi, qui et proles in terra protegit: sed praesumptores ab eo cadunt. Ecce certitudo protectionis fidentis in Deo per Christum. A latere. Latus Dei est corona justorum, qui cum eo judicabunt, unde dicitur: Mittite a latere vestro, id est, qui vobiscum habent consilium. Latus ergo Christi, Apostoli et eorum imitatores, quibus promisit: Sedebitis super sedes duodecim, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel (Matth. XIX). Duodecim sedes perfectio tribunalis, qui quibus sedebunt omnes qui omnia reliquerunt, et secuti sunt Christum.

999DVERS. 8.-- Verumtamen. (CASS., AUG.) Licet quidem te permittente impiis tuos persequi, sed non impune, oculis tuis considerabit malum, quod voluerunt, non bonum quod per nescientes agitur, eis retribuetur, et sanctus, qui habet oculos fidei, videt eos modo exaltari et tonare, et in fine fulminare: hoc dixit ne infirmi moveantur. (CASS.) Verumtamen oculis. Etsi cadentes tentent te duris, verumtamen. Vel, etsi daemonium non appropinquet, quod est per iniquos: sed tamen non quod faciunt, sed quod intendunt, considerabis.

VERS. 9.-- Quoniam tu es. (AUG.) Unus Christus est caput et corpus, de quo loquitur modo ut de capite, modo ut de corpore, non mutata persona. Ideo- 1000Aque diligenter adverte, ubi de Christo secundum caput, ubi secundum membra agat. Altissimum. In alto est refugium Dei, valde in occulto, ut fugiatur a ventura ira. Multi enim sic faciunt sibi refugium Dei, quo fugiunt a malis temporalibus. Altissimum posuisti refugium, id est, resurgendo, ascendendo, altum fecisti refugium, ut jam speram sequi quo praecessisti.

VERS. 10.--(ID.) Tabernaculum Dei est caro, etc., usque ad Christo hoc bene accipitur.

VERS. 11.-- Quoniam angelis. Hoc dixit tentator Domino, quando illum tentavit: hoc objecit, de Deitate ejus dubitans. Tentatus est autem Christus propter nos, ut et in eo tentatorem vincere discamus.

(AUG.) Sic et baptizari a servo voluit, non pro sua necessitate, sed pro hominis utilitate, ut non aspernemur 1000Bbaptizari a conservis.

VERS. 12.-- In manibus portabunt te. (ID.) Manibus angelorum sublatus est Christus in coelum, etc., usque ad qui vinci non potest.

VERS. 13.-- Super aspidem. Post humanam infirmitatem, divina virtus ostenditur, quae tantis imperat. Et agit de Christo secundum membra. Et conculcabit. (AUG.) Serpentem calcat Ecclesia, quae cavet astutiam ejus. Leonem. Aperte saevit in martyres.

Draco insidiatur per haereticos, ut corrumpat virginem Christi, unde Apostolus: Despondi vos uni viro, virginem castam exhibere Christo (II Cor. XI).

VERS. 14.-- Quoniam in me speravit. (AUG.) Tertio verba Dei, quibus Ecclesiam consolatur, cui et hic defensionem, et in futuro praemia promittit. (CASS.) 1000CMandat angelis de te dicens: Quoniam in me. Certitudo promissionis per promissionem Dei.

VERS. 15.-- Clamabit ad me. (AUG.) Non est timendum in tribulatione, etc., usque ad eo tempore magis laboremus ad resistendum.

PSALM XC.

VERS. 1.-- The praise of a canticle. Praise is human also: but this praise is of a canticle, because it is nothing if not divine. For this psalm is a hymn against the demons. The Prophet therefore says of any holy man whatsoever: He that dwelleth in the help, etc.

(CASS.) He shows that the temptations of the devil were overcome through humility by Christ, and by his own, who remain in the help of God, that we too through him may learn to overcome temptations, because he is the door through which jauna, if any man shall enter in, 998Che shall go in, and shall go out, and pasture shall come forth.

(AUG.) Christ is the door; to enter through him is to imitate him, not in godhead, and power, and miracles, but in that wherein he was made for us, that is, in the humility to which he calls, saying: Learn of me, because I am meek and humble of heart. Out of this psalm the devil tempted Christ. But Christ's temptation is our teaching, and following him we overcome by him.

He that dwelleth. (CASS.) He describes first the man who trusts in God alone, wholly walled about by the protection of God. He that dwelleth, that is, who sets all his hope always not in himself, but in God, shall be protected by God in every way. Note the correspondence of the words: for as he always dwelleth, so also shall he always abide. The one he affirms, namely that he dwelleth; the other he promises, 998Dnamely that he shall be protected.

He shall abide in the protection of the God of heaven. That is to say, that he turn not aside to the right hand or to the left, as in the Old Testament it was commanded to the children of Israel, that they should walk by the king's highway, not turning aside to the right hand or to the left. The king's highway is the way of Christ our king, who so ran the way of the world that he was neither enticed by prosperity, nor broken by adversity.

VERS. 2.-- My God. (CASS.) Lest thou think that after the upholding and the refuge nothing further is to be asked for, he adds: In him will I trust, lest at any time he presume of himself; and if Adam had done this, he would have stood well.

VERS. 3.-- From the snare. (ID.) Temptation, either by deeds, which is here called a snare; or by words, which is here called a sharp word; 999Aas if to say, even though it seem light, yet it is a grave thing to be tempted by a word. A snare, the craftiness of spiritual or of carnal enemies; a sharp word, every saying which moves a man from the divine rules. (AUG.) From the snare of the hunters, that is, of the demons, who set their snares not in the way, Christ, but round about it, to the right hand or to the left. Into these some fall even through a sharp word, as they who will not be Christ's because of those who insult the Christian name, and they who fear the detractions of men, so that they cease from the way of God.

VERS. 4.-- With his shoulders. (AUG., CASS.) To him that hopes he promises the benefits of God. The shoulders are the workings of wonders, by which, as by arms, the power of God is shown. The feathers are the counsels of the Prophets, which carry men to the heavens.

999BHe will overshadow. That neither the sun of the godhead, nor the moon of the humanity, may scorch thee. In the feathers is the protection. With his shoulders. Elsewhere, Between the shoulders. (AUG.) That is, he places thee before his breast, etc., as far as that we may hope under his wings.

VERS. 5.-- The truth. (ID.) It is God's, who does not regard persons, nor mingle those who hope in themselves with those who hope in God, but discerns the humble or the proud. (CASS.) Or the truth is the incarnation of Christ, whence: Out of the earth truth is sprung (Psal. LXXXIV), which both overshadows with the shoulders, and defends with the shield. As he has noted the kinds of defence, so he notes also the kinds of dangers, that the deliverance may be the more welcome.

From the fear of the night. From the likeness of a danger, whence only fear is had. From the fear of the night. (AUG.) He who 999Csins in ignorance, etc., as far as: A thousand shall fall at thy side.

VERS. 7.-- They shall fall at the side. (CASS.) Secondly, he says that the head of him who trusts in God, that is, Christ, lifted up into heaven, can be touched by none, who also protects the offspring on earth: but the presumptuous fall from him. Behold the certainty of the protection of him who trusts in God through Christ. At the side. The side of God is the crown of the just, who shall judge with him, whence it is said: Send ye from your own side, that is, they who hold counsel with you. The side of Christ, therefore, is the Apostles and their imitators, to whom he promised: You shall sit upon twelve seats, judging the twelve tribes of Israel (Matth. XIX). The twelve seats are the perfection of the tribunal, who in which shall sit [qui quibus; read in quibus, "in which"] all they who have left all things, and have followed Christ.

999DVERS. 8.-- But yet. (CASS., AUG.) Although indeed it is allowed, thou permitting, that the wicked persecute thine own, yet not unpunished: with thine eyes he shall consider the evil which they willed, not the good which is done through those who know it not, it shall be repaid to them; and the holy man, who has the eyes of faith, sees them now exalted and thundering, and at the last struck by lightning: this he said lest the weak be moved. (CASS.) But yet with thine eyes. Even if they that fall should tempt thee with hard things, yet. Or, even if the demon does not draw near, which is through the wicked: yet nevertheless not what they do, but what they intend, thou shalt consider.

VERS. 9.-- For thou art. (AUG.) One Christ is head and body, of whom he speaks now as of the head, now as of the body, the person not being changed. Therefore 1000Adiligently mark where he treats of Christ according to the head, and where according to the members. The Most High. In the height is the refuge of God, deep in secret, that flight may be made from the wrath to come. For many so make for themselves the refuge of God, whereby they flee from temporal evils. Thou hast made the Most High thy refuge, that is, by rising again, by ascending, thou hast made the refuge high, that I may now hope to follow speram whither thou hast gone before.

VERS. 10.--(ID.) The tabernacle of God is the flesh, etc., as far as this is rightly taken of Christ.

VERS. 11.-- For to his angels. This the tempter said to the Lord, when he tempted him: this he cast up against him, doubting of his Godhead. But Christ was tempted for our sake, that in him also we might learn to overcome the tempter.

(AUG.) So also he willed to be baptized by a servant, not for his own need, but for man's profit, that we should not disdain 1000Bto be baptized by our fellow servants.

VERS. 12.-- In their hands they shall bear thee up. (ID.) By the hands of angels Christ was lifted up into heaven, etc., as far as he who cannot be overcome.

VERS. 13.-- Upon the asp. After the human infirmity, the divine power is shown, which commands such creatures. And he treats of Christ according to the members. And he shall trample. [Vulg. Ps 90:13 conculcabis, "thou shalt trample"] (AUG.) The Church, which is wary of his cunning, treads upon the serpent. The lion. He rages openly against the martyrs.

The dragon lies in wait through the heretics, that he may corrupt the virgin of Christ, whence the Apostle: I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you a chaste virgin to Christ (II Cor. XI).

VERS. 14.-- Because he hoped in me. (AUG.) Thirdly, the words of God, by which he consoles the Church, to which he promises both defence here, and rewards in the world to come. (CASS.) 1000CHe gives charge to the angels concerning thee, saying: Because in me. The certainty of the promise, through the promise of God.

VERS. 15.-- He shall cry to me. (AUG.) There is no need to fear in tribulation, etc., as far as at that time let us labour the more to resist.

PSALMUS XCI.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus cantici. (AUG.) Propter fastidium animorum, etc., usque ad gloriam Dei quaerens, non tuam.

VERS. 2.-- Bonum est confiteri. (CASS.) Primo, agit quomodo bonus imperturbatus agit sabbatum mentis, sentiens omnia bene agi a Deo, quod non novit stultus. (AUG.) Bona praesentia a Deo nobis donata, consolatio sunt: cum desunt, justitia est. Consolatur enim nos Deus, et emendat: in utroque ergo simus 1000Dei grati, dicentes: Bonum est confiteri, etc.

VERS. 4.-- In decachordo. (ID.) Psallit, qui cum hilaritate bene facit. Qui cum tristitia de eo fit, non ipse facit: et portat psalterium, non cantat in eo. In decachordo. Si bene loqueris tantum, canticum est sine cithara; si operaris, et non loqueris, cithara est sine cantico; et ideo bene loquere et benefac.

VERS. 5.-- Quia delectasti. (ID.) Unde Apostolus: Ipsius figmentum sumus, etc., usque ad: Quam magnificata sunt. In factura tua. (CASS., HIER.) Et in decore ipsius mundialis fabricae, et in obedientia, et in dispositione, et in causis, et in effectibus, et in operibus manuum, quibus uior, vel quae miror.

1001AVERS. 6.-- Quam magnificata sunt. (CASS., HIER.) In substantia, et in forma, et in vi, et in caeteris. Nimis profundae sunt cogitationes tuae, quibus talia fecisti et regis.

VERS. 7.-- Vir insipiens, etc. (CASS.) Me delectasti in operibus, sed vir insipiens non cognoscet, et stultus, qui, si scit, non cavet sibi, non intelliget haec, quae dixit, vel quae dicit post. Summum genus scientiae est scire Deum tanta praestare, quae humanus sensus non valet attingere.

Insipiens est, qui coelesti sapientia vacuus, humanis versutiis plenus est; qui non scit opera Dei, quia casu putat omnia agi; Stultus est brutus, qui nec saecularia novit.

VERS. 8.-- Cum exorti fuerunt. (CASS.) Malos asserit 1001Bperituros, etc., usque ad Judaei putaverunt te communi scilicet sorte mori.

VERS. 9.-- Tu autem Altissimus. (AUG.) Exspectas desuper ex aeterno, etc., usque ad non longanimis, ex verbo aeternus.

VERS. 11.-- Et exaltabitur. (ID.) Etsi ipsi peribunt, etc., usque ad omnes haereses peribunt.

VERS. 12.-- Et despexit. (ID.) Et ideo jam nunc despexit, et audiet a veritate intus. Et ab insurgentibus. (CASS.) Vel, insurgentes in me, malignantes audiet in novissimo: quando se increpabunt, dicentes, Quid nobis profuit superbia et divitiae? (Sap. V.) Auris mea. (AUG.) Stantis ad dexteram, audiet in futuro, hoc scilicet, Ite, maledicti, in ignem aeternum. A quo malo auditu justus non timebit. Ecce hoc 1001Cistis, Quid de justis? (Matth. XXV.)

VERS. 13.-- Justus ut palma. Illi ut fenum. Justus ut palma, pro altitudine, et quia radix aspera, pulchra coma in summo et fine, et tarde fructum facit; ita et justum hic asperat labor, quem in supernis pulchritudo immortalitatis coronabit, et quasi tarde post longos labores mercedem operum recipiet. Justus ut palma. (CASS.) Tertia pars. Justos florere, ut hac promissione devote gaudeant. Cedrus. (AUG.) Palma et cedrus, hae arbores non arescunt aestate, ut fenum.

VERS. 14.-- In atriis domus. (CASS.) Atrium, initium mansionis; domus interior. In atriis ergo florebunt, id est, in ipso resurrectionis initio, dum audient: Venite, benedicti Patris mei (Matth. XXV).

VERS. 15.-- Adhuc multiplicabuntur. (ID.) Ecclesia 1001Dmagis incipiet esse uberrima, cum ad finem saeculi erit perducta: tunc enim passionibus electorum cito implebitur numerus beatorum. Et accipitur hic aliter senectus, quam supra.

VERS. 16.-- Annuntient. (ID.) Hic, vel, dum praemium capient annuntiabunt, quod justus, qui suis promissa complet. Et non est iniquitas in eo. (AUG.) Ut hic permittat pati pro se, quos non ibi ornet. Et rectus, qui remunerat, non iniquus ut fraudet praemio, sed benignus ut accumulet.

PSALM XCI.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of a canticle. (AUG.) Because of the weariness of minds, etc., as far as seeking the glory of God, not thine own.

VERS. 2.-- It is good to confess. (CASS.) First, he treats how the good man, being untroubled, keeps the sabbath of the mind, perceiving that all things are done well by God, which the foolish man does not know. (AUG.) The good things of the present, given to us by God, are a consolation: when they are lacking, it is justice. For God both consoles us, and amends us: in both, therefore, let us be 1000Dthankful to him, saying: It is good to confess, etc.

VERS. 4.-- Upon the ten-stringed instrument. (ID.) He sings a psalm who does good with cheerfulness. He with whom it is done in sadness does not himself do it: and he carries the psaltery, he does not sing upon it. Upon the ten-stringed instrument. If thou only speakest well, it is a canticle without the harp; if thou workest, and speakest not, it is a harp without the canticle; and therefore both speak well and do well.

VERS. 5.-- For thou hast delighted. (ID.) Whence the Apostle: We are his own moulding, [Vulg. Eph 2:10 reads "for we are his workmanship" — the word the gloss picks up two lines later in In factura tua] etc., as far as: How great are thy works. In thy handiwork. (CASS., HIER.) Both in the beauty of the fabric of the world itself, and in its obedience, and in its ordering, and in its causes, and in its effects, and in the works of the hands which I use uior, or which I marvel at.

1001AVERS. 6.-- How great are thy works. (CASS., HIER.) In substance, and in form, and in force, and in the rest. Thy thoughts are exceeding deep, by which thou hast made and dost govern such things.

VERS. 7.-- The senseless man, etc. (CASS.) Thou hast delighted me in thy works, but the senseless man shall not know, and the fool, who, if he knows, does not beware for himself, shall not understand these things, which he has said, or which he says afterwards. The highest kind of knowledge is to know that God bestows such great things as human sense is not able to attain to.

The senseless man is he who is empty of heavenly wisdom, and full of human craftiness; who does not know the works of God, because he thinks that all things are done by chance; the fool is a brute, who does not know even worldly things.

VERS. 8.-- When they have sprung up. [Vulg. Ps 91:8 has the future perfect, "when they shall have sprung up"] (CASS.) He asserts that the wicked shall 1001Bperish, etc., as far as the Jews thought that thou shouldst die by the common lot, that is to say.

VERS. 9.-- But thou art the Most High. (AUG.) Thou waitest from above out of eternity, etc., as far as not long-suffering, from the word eternal.

VERS. 11.-- And shall be exalted. (ID.) Even though they themselves shall perish, etc., as far as all heresies shall perish.

VERS. 12.-- And hath looked down. (ID.) And therefore even now he has looked down, and it shall hear from the truth within. And from them that rise up. [Vulg. Ps 91:12 reads "and among them that rise up"] (CASS.) Or, it shall hear at the last those that rise up against me, the malignant: when they shall rebuke themselves, saying, What hath pride profited us, and riches? (Sap. V.) My ear. (AUG.) Of him that stands at the right hand: it shall hear in the world to come this, namely, Go, ye cursed, into everlasting fire. [Vulg. Mt 25:41 reads "Depart from me, ye cursed"] From which evil hearing the just man shall not fear. Behold, this is 1001Cfor these men; what of the just? (Matth. XXV.)

VERS. 13.-- The just man as the palm tree. They as hay. The just man as the palm tree, for its height, and because its root is rough, its foliage fair at the top and at the end, and it bears fruit late; so also does labour make the just man rough here, whom in the heights the beauty of immortality shall crown, and, as it were late, after long labours he shall receive the wage of his works. The just man as the palm tree. (CASS.) The third part. That the just flourish, so that by this promise they may devoutly rejoice. The cedar. (AUG.) The palm and the cedar, these trees do not wither in the summer, as hay does.

VERS. 14.-- In the courts of the house. (CASS.) The court is the beginning of the dwelling; the house is the inner part. In the courts therefore they shall flourish, that is, in the very beginning of the resurrection, when they shall hear: Come, ye blessed of my Father (Matth. XXV).

VERS. 15.-- They shall still be multiplied. (ID.) The Church 1001Dshall the more begin to be most fruitful, when it shall have been brought to the end of the world: for then by the sufferings of the elect the number of the blessed shall quickly be filled up. And old age is here taken otherwise than above.

VERS. 16.-- That they may declare. (ID.) Here, or, when they shall receive the reward they shall declare that he is just, who fulfils to his own the things promised. And there is no iniquity in him. (AUG.) As that he should permit those to suffer here for his sake, whom he does not adorn there. And he is upright, who rewards, not unjust so as to defraud of the reward, but kind so as to heap it up.

PSALMUS XCII.

In diem, etc. (AUG.) In die ante sabbatum, etc., usque ad quod significat sextus dies.

VERS. 1.-- Dominus regnavit, etc. (CASS.) Laus 1002AChristi hic cantatur, etc., usque ad a laude domus, ibi, Domum tuam. Decorem indutus. (AUG.) Christus decorus his, etc., usque ad orbis qui non commovebitur. Decorem induit. (CASS.) Id est, pulchritudinem, etc., usque ad ab incarnatione, quando homines docuit.

Praecinxit se. Non ait, cinxit, vel succinxit, vel accinxit, sed praecinxit. Cingimur enim operaturi, accingimur pugnaturi, succingimur ituri, praecingimur ministraturi. (AUG.) Cinctio ergo opera significat, etc., usque ad quia melior est qui vincit iram quam qui capit civitatem. Praecinxit. (CASS.) Coetu angelorum ascendens, vel strenuitate operandi.

Etenim firmavit. (AUG.) Decorem et fortitudinem induit, ut fundaret terram, unde addit: Etenim firmavit.

VERS. 2.-- Ex tunc. (ID.) Vel ex illo, tempus gratiae 1002Bdesignat, forte intelligit hoc ex die ante sabbatum, id est, sexto tempore hujus mundi, quo Dominus venit: sed ne putes tunc coepisse, quando natus venit addit, a saeculo tu es.

VERS. 3.-- Elevaverunt flumina vocem. (AUG.) Quia discipuli audientes, etc., usque ad saeculi, quod coepit irasci, vel persequi. Elevaverunt flumina fluctus suos, etc. (CASS.) Hoc deest in aliis, etc., usque ad qui facit omnia bona, addit: Mirabilis in altis Dominus.

VERS. 5.-- Testimonia. (AUG.) Quia mirabilis elatio maris, etc., usque ad et coronas ex praedictione. (CASS.) Testimonia. Vel ita, etc., usque ad licet brevibus verbis, continet.

PSALM XCII.

Unto the day, etc. [Vulg. Ps 92:1 reads "on the day before the sabbath" — as the gloss itself has it in its own next words] (AUG.) On the day before the sabbath, etc., as far as which the sixth day signifies.

VERS. 1.-- The Lord hath reigned, etc. (CASS.) The praise 1002Aof Christ is sung here, etc., as far as from the praise of the house, there, Thy house. Clothed with beauty. (AUG.) Christ is beautiful in these things, etc., as far as the world which shall not be moved. He hath put on beauty. (CASS.) That is, comeliness, etc., as far as from the incarnation, when he taught men.

He hath girded himself about. He does not say, he girded, or he girded up, or he girded on, but he girded about. For we are girded when we are about to work, we are girded on when we are about to fight, we are girded up when we are about to go, we are girded about when we are about to minister. (AUG.) The girding therefore signifies works, etc., as far as because better is he that overcometh anger than he that taketh a city. He hath girded himself about. (CASS.) Ascending with the company of angels, or by strenuousness in working.

For he hath established. (AUG.) He has put on beauty and strength, that he might found the earth, whence he adds: For he hath established.

VERS. 2.-- From then. (ID.) Or from that time; it marks the time of grace, 1002Band perhaps he understands this from the day before the sabbath, that is, in the sixth age of this world, in which the Lord came: but lest thou think that he then began, when he came born, he adds, thou art from everlasting.

VERS. 3.-- The floods have lifted up their voice. (AUG.) Because the disciples, hearing, etc., as far as of the world, which began to be angry, or to persecute. The floods have lifted up their waves, etc. (CASS.) This is wanting in others, etc., as far as he who does all things well, he adds: The Lord is wonderful on high.

VERS. 5.-- Testimonies. (AUG.) Because the lifting up of the sea is wonderful, [Vulg. Ps 92:4 has the plural, "wonderful are the surges of the sea"] etc., as far as and crowns out of the foretelling. (CASS.) Testimonies. Or thus, etc., as far as it contains, though in brief words.

PSALMUS XCIII.

Psalmus David (AUG.) Infirmis, qui et murmurant 1002Ccorde, etc., usque ad totus docens patientiam. Quarto sabbati, quo die fecit Deus luminaria, etc., usque ad unde monet ad patientiam.

VERS. 1.-- Deus ultionum Dominus. Ne festines alium punire, si te laesit; sicut nolles puniri alio rogante, quem laesisti: et si ille peccat in te, ne pecces deterius blasphemans Deum, nec optes vindictam; quae si venerit, forsan te prius inveniet.

Libere egit. (AUG.) Tempore infirmitatis, ut quando in templo docuit, tanquam potestatem habens, quia nec veritati ejus, nec potestati ejus potest obviari. Et quia ita tunc, nunc Exaltare, quia, usquequo peccatores.

VERS. 4.-- Effabuntur. (CASS.) Exponit eorum peccata, etc., usque ad procedit exaggerando. Loquentur omnes qui operantur, etc. Effabuntur, aliis 1002Drespondent, (AUG.) id est, habent quod respondeant, etc., usque ad loquuntur iniqui dicentes Deum non curare haec.

VERS. 6.-- Viduam et advenam. (CASS.) Hos Deus tuetur, etc., usque ad sine patre diabolo et matre concupiscentia.

VERS. 7.-- Nec intelliget. (AUG.) Quasi, non attendet ista, negligit ista, nec attendit ut videat, non me curat Deus, quid agam?

VERS. 8.-- Intelligite. (CASS.) Secunda pars; contra blasphemos, etc., usque ad quod consilium suum malis incognitum, suis amicis aperit. Stulti. Qui aperte blasphemant, dicentes Deum non videre. Vel ita: Vos insipientes, id est nescii, intelligite, qui jam bene vivendo 1003Aestis in populo, id est, in numero bonorum. Et vos stulti, id est, improvidi, et si scitis, aliquando sapite.

VERS. 10.-- Qui corripit gentes. (AUG.) Quotidie pro originali, nonne arguet pro supradictis? Vel, Qui erudit. Propter quam eruditionem misit Filium suum Deus, etc., usque ad unde Apostolus: Omnes astabimus ante tribunal Christi, ut recipiat unusquisque, (Rom. XIV), etc.

VERS. 11.-- Dominus scit. (ID.) Tu vero nescis cogitationes Dei, quoniam justae sunt; sed amicis factis prodit Deus consilium suum, cur malis parcit. Quoniam vanae sunt. Talium cogitationes vanae sunt, quod ipsi per se non possunt scire, sed Dominus novit esse vanas.

VERS. 12.-- Beatus homo. (CASS.) Isti sunt vani, etc., 1003Busque ad omnes scient Deum, coeli ut liber plicabuntur. Et de lege tua, etc. (AUG.) Ex lege disce patientiam, donec fodiatur, non est tuum scire quomodo, et cur fodiatur illi.

VERS. 13.-- Donec. etc. (AUG.) Felicitas malorum fovea est; labor bonorum flagellum patris; felicitas est fovea, quia cum parcit Deus per impunitatem, fit homo elatus, et cum putat se altum, cadit. Fodiatur fovea. Ecce consilium Dei: ideo parcit malis, ut fodiatur fovea eis. Adhuc foditur, et tu jam vis sepelire eum: nimis festinas. Peccatori fovea, etc. Non omni, sed superbo, etc., usque ad age gratias ei a quo habes, nec alium despicias.

VERS. 16.-- Quis consurget. (CASS.) Tertia pars, ubi dicit quod fluctuatio sit justis, et fluctus saeculi, 1003Cid est, mala per iniquos, ut puncti clament ad Deum, et nihil aliud eis placeat, et tunc gratior fit liberatio. (AUG.) Quis consurget, quasi dicat, etc., usque ad sed unde vincam? Nisi quia Dominus. Stabit mecum, etc. (CASS.) In acie patiens; sed quia ille vincit, qui vim sustinet; perdit, qui ferit.

VERS. 17.-- Nisi quia Dominus. (CASS.) Vanis persuasionibus poterat decipi, nisi Dominus liberaret.

VERS. 18.-- Adjuvabat me. Sicut Petrum liberavit Dominus super aquam ambulantem, ne mergeretur, qui Domino dixit: Domine, si tu es, jube me venire ad te (Matth. XXVI).

(AUG.) Ut Christus sua potestate, etc., usque ad unde subdit, consolationes tuae laetificaverunt animam meam.

1003DVERS. 19.-- In corde. (ID.) Salubres cogitationes significat, ut scilicet cum aeternas retributiones cogitaret, mala temporalia despiceret.

VERS. 20.-- Nunquid adhaeret. (ID.) Nemo iniquus sedet tecum; et cum nihil his tecum, ad quid ergo fiunt? ut de eis pungas, et puncti ad te clament, et demum hi pereant; quae his tribus versibus subsequentibus ostenduntur. Sedes iniquitatis. (CASS.) Est possessio mundi, cum amore, quae non haeret Deo, qui suos praecipit haec fugere. Qui fingis. (AUG.) Ex hoc intelligo, quod non haeret tibi iniquus, etc., usque ad et ille dolor est praeceptum; sed alter est informis.

Dolorem, id est, de dolore vel labore praeceptum, 1004Aetc., usque ad et tunc surgit fluctus, in quo excitatur.

VERS. 22.-- Et factus est mihi Dominus in refugium, et Deus meus in adjutorium spei meae. (ID.) Quare? quia si non periclitareris, non quaereres refugium: pungeris dolore, ut quaeras remedium; recedit spes saeculi et venit spes Dei.

PSALM XCIII.

A psalm of David [Vulg. Ps 93:1 Psalmus ipsi David, quarta sabbati., "a psalm for David himself, on the fourth day of the week"] (AUG.) To the weak, who also murmur 1002Cin heart, etc., as far as the whole teaching patience. On the fourth day of the week, on which day God made the luminaries, etc., as far as whence he admonishes to patience.

VERS. 1.-- The Lord is the God of revenges. Be not hasty to punish another, if he has hurt thee; even as thou wouldst not be willing to be punished at the asking of another whom thou hast hurt: and if he sins against thee, sin not worse by blaspheming God, nor wish for vengeance; which, if it comes, will perhaps find thee first.

He hath acted freely. (AUG.) In the time of his weakness, as when he taught in the temple, as one having power, because neither his truth nor his power can be withstood. And because it was so then, now Be thou exalted, because, how long shall sinners.

VERS. 4.-- They shall utter. (CASS.) He sets forth their sins, etc., as far as it goes on by way of exaggeration. They shall speak, all that work, etc. They shall utter, they 1002Danswer others, (AUG.) that is, they have what they may answer, etc., as far as the wicked speak, saying that God does not care for these things.

VERS. 6.-- The widow and the stranger. (CASS.) These God protects, etc., as far as without the devil for a father and concupiscence for a mother.

VERS. 7.-- Neither shall he understand. (AUG.) As it were, he will not attend to these things, he neglects these things, nor does he attend that he may see, God does not care for me, what I may do?

VERS. 8.-- Understand ye. (CASS.) The second part; against blasphemers, etc., as far as that he opens to his own friends his counsel, which is unknown to the wicked. Ye foolish. Who openly blaspheme, saying that God does not see. Or thus: You unwise, that is, ignorant, understand, you who by now, by living well, 1003Aare in the people, that is, in the number of the good. And you foolish, that is, improvident, and if you know, at length be wise.

VERS. 10.-- Who correcteth the nations. (AUG.) Daily, for the original sin, will he not rebuke for the things said above? Or, Who instructeth. [Vulg. Ps 93:10 qui docet hominem scientiam, "who teacheth man knowledge"] For the sake of which instruction God sent his Son, etc., as far as whence the Apostle: We shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ, that every one may receive, (Rom. XIV), etc. [Vulg. Rm 14:10 omnes enim stabimus ante tribunal Christi, with no such clause following; "that every one may render", ut referat unusquisque, stands at 2Cor 5:10]

VERS. 11.-- The Lord knoweth. (ID.) But thou knowest not the thoughts of God, since they are just; but when friends have been made, God brings forth his counsel, why he spares the wicked. For they are vain. The thoughts of such men are vain, in that they themselves of themselves cannot know it, but the Lord knows them to be vain.

VERS. 12.-- Blessed is the man. (CASS.) These are the vain, etc., 1003Bas far as all shall know God, the heavens shall be folded up as a book. And out of thy law, etc. (AUG.) From the law learn patience, until there be dug, it is not thine to know how, and why it is dug for him.

VERS. 13.-- Until, etc. (AUG.) The happiness of the wicked is a pit; the toil of the good is the father's scourge; happiness is a pit, because when God spares by impunity, a man is made lifted up, and when he thinks himself high, he falls. Let a pit be dug. Behold the counsel of God: therefore he spares the wicked, that a pit may be dug for them. It is still being dug, and thou already wishest to bury him: thou art too hasty. A pit for the sinner, etc. Not for every one, but for the proud, etc., as far as give thanks to him from whom thou hast it, and despise not another.

VERS. 16.-- Who shall rise up. (CASS.) The third part, where he says that there is a tossing for the just, and the wave of the world, 1003Cthat is, evils through the wicked, so that being pricked they may cry to God, and that nothing else may please them, and then deliverance becomes the more welcome. (AUG.) Who shall rise up, as if he should say, etc., as far as but whence shall I conquer? Unless because the Lord. He will stand with me, etc. (CASS.) Patient in the battle line; but because he conquers who bears the violence; he loses who strikes.

VERS. 17.-- Unless because the Lord. (CASS.) By vain persuasions he could have been deceived, unless the Lord had delivered him.

VERS. 18.-- He helped me. Even as the Lord delivered Peter walking upon the water, that he might not be drowned, who said to the Lord: Lord, if it be thou, bid me come to thee (Matth. XXVI).

(AUG.) That Christ by his own power, etc., as far as whence he subjoins, thy comforts have gladdened my soul.

1003DVERS. 19.-- In the heart. (ID.) He signifies wholesome thoughts, namely, that while he thought upon the eternal recompenses, he might despise temporal evils.

VERS. 20.-- Doth there cleave. (ID.) No wicked man sits with thee; and since these have nothing with thee, to what end then are they made? that thou mayest prick by means of them, and that they who are pricked may cry to thee, and at the last that these may perish; which things are shown in these three following verses. The seat of iniquity. (CASS.) It is the possession of the world, with love of it, which does not cleave to God, who commands his own to flee these things. Who framest. (AUG.) From this I understand that the wicked man does not cleave to thee, etc., as far as and that pain is a precept; but the other is unformed.

Pain, that is, a precept out of pain or toil, 1004Aetc., as far as and then the wave rises, in which he is stirred up.

VERS. 22.-- And the Lord became my refuge, and my God the helper of my hope. (ID.) Wherefore? because if thou wert not in peril, thou wouldst not seek a refuge: thou art pricked with pain, that thou mayest seek a remedy; the hope of the world departs and the hope of God comes.

PSALMUS XCIV.

Laus. (CAS.) Devotionem. Cantus hilaritatem significat.

VERS. 1.-- Venite, exsultemus. (THEOD.) Josias rex admodum pius fuit, etc., usque ad formatus est vero psalmus ex persona Josiae, et Dei sacerdotum. (CASS.) De tempore gratiae, quo intratur in requiem, propheta 1004Blaudes Dei describens, primo invitat Judaeos, quos praevidebat posse resistere Christo.

VERS. 2.-- Faciem ejus, etc. (AUG., CASS.) Conspectum venturi judicis, ne quid tunc in nobis sit discutiendum. In confessione. (AUG.) Illum laudantes, nos accusantes, etc., usque ad de qua laude psalmus agit. In psalmi jubilemus. Quae dicimus in psalmis, vel facimus, sentiamus in jubilatione.

VERS. 3.-- Super omnes deos. Vel magis deos homines dicit, super quos rex est, non super daemonia.

VERS. 4.-- Quia in manu ejus, etc. (CASS.) Post magnitudinem Domini praedictam, venit ad clementiam.

VERS. 5.-- Mare. (AUG.) Mundus, cujus fluctus termino arctat Deus, non permittens nos tentari supra 1004Cid quod possumus (I Cor. X); qui fluctus etiam proventum nobis faciunt, Deo id agente, nec scandala tibi nocent, quae mensuram a Deo accipiunt.

VERS. 6.-- Venite, adoremus. (CASS.) Prius rudes vocavit ad exsultationem: jam ostensa gloria Dei, vocat ad poenitentiam, quod durius est. Ploremus. (AUG.) Si forte de peccatis, quae vos longe fecerunt, solliciti estis, plorate: lacryma exstinguit flammam peccati, quae in conscientia ardet. Qui fecit nos. Ecce magna fiducia: a te enim deficere potes, tu te reficere non potes, ille reficit qui te fecit.

VERS. 7.-- Et nos populus, etc. (AUG.) Eleganter ordo verborum mutatus: Non dixit oves pascuae et populum manus ejus, ut ipsos intelligas oves, qui sunt populus, oves manus, non quas eminus, quia 1004Dsunt, et oves quas non fecimus, sed ipse gratia sua nos oves fecit.

VERS. 8.-- Hodie si vocem, etc. (CASS.) Nos autem populus et oves. Sed his omnibus proponitur conditio, si vocem ejus audieritis, quam vocem subdit, Hodie. Nolite obdurare. (ID.) Jam ipse Christus monet, ne obdurentur, ne contingat eis, ut patribus.

VERS. 9.-- Sicut in irritatione. (ID.) Majestas Christi loquentis, etc., usque ad culpa parentum repetitur, ut vindicta timeatur.

VERS. 10.-- Quadraginta annis. (AUG.) Per quadraginta annos omnia saecula significat, etc., usque ad sicut ipse ait: Vobiscum sum usque ad consummationem saeculi.

PSALM XCIV.

Praise. (CAS.) Devotion. Song signifies gladness.

VERS. 1.-- Come, let us rejoice. (THEOD.) King Josias was exceedingly pious, etc., as far as but the psalm is framed in the person of Josias, and of the priests of God. (CASS.) Concerning the time of grace, in which there is an entering into rest, the prophet, 1004Bdescribing the praises of God, first invites the Jews, whom he foresaw to be able to resist Christ.

VERS. 2.-- His face, etc. (AUG., CASS.) The sight of the judge to come, lest there be anything then in us to be sifted. In confession. (AUG.) Praising him, accusing ourselves, etc., as far as of which praise the psalm treats. In psalms let us make a joyful noise. [psalmi; read psalmis, "in psalms"] What we say in psalms, or do, let us feel in jubilation.

VERS. 3.-- Above all gods. Or rather he calls men gods, over whom he is king, not over demons.

VERS. 4.-- For in his hand, etc. (CASS.) After the greatness of the Lord foretold, he comes to his clemency.

VERS. 5.-- The sea. (AUG.) The world, whose waves God confines within a bound, not suffering us to be tempted above 1004Cthat which we are able (I Cor. X); which waves also make increase for us, God working it, nor do the scandals hurt thee, which receive their measure from God.

VERS. 6.-- Come, let us adore. (CASS.) First he called the untaught to exultation: now, the glory of God being shown, he calls to penance, which is the harder. Let us weep. (AUG.) If perchance you are solicitous concerning the sins which have made you far off, weep: a tear extinguishes the flame of sin which burns in the conscience. Who made us. Behold great confidence: for of thyself thou canst fail, thyself thou canst not remake, he remakes thee who made thee.

VERS. 7.-- And we are the people, etc. (AUG.) Elegantly is the order of the words changed: He did not say the sheep of the pasture and the people of his hand, that thou mayest understand those very ones to be sheep who are the people, sheep of his hand, not those which from afar, because 1004Dthey are, and sheep which we did not make, but he himself by his own grace made us sheep.

VERS. 8.-- To-day if you shall hear the voice, etc. (CASS.) But we are the people and the sheep. But to all these a condition is set forth, if you shall hear his voice, which voice he subjoins, To-day. Harden not. (ID.) Now Christ himself admonishes, lest they be hardened, lest it befall them as it did the fathers.

VERS. 9.-- As in the provocation. (ID.) The majesty of Christ speaking, etc., as far as the fault of the parents is recalled, that the vengeance may be feared.

VERS. 10.-- Forty years. (AUG.) By forty years he signifies all the ages, etc., as far as as he himself says: I am with you unto the consummation of the world.

PSALMUS XCV.

  • 1005A

Psalmus David. (CASS.) In Veteri Testamento legitur, etc., usque ad non illa actuali agit hic psalmus.

VERS. 1.-- Cantate Domino. (ID.) Praemonuit Judaeos in praecedenti psalmo ut, deposita duritia, Christum crederent; sed quia erat mansura, nunc omnes gentes monet. Secundus psalmus de utroque adventu. Primum ad praelatos loquitur, ut ipsi cantent et annuntient. Canticum novum. (AUG.) Vetus cantat cupiditas, etc., usque ad quisquis intraverit, foris est.

VERS. 2.-- Domino et benedicite. (HIER., CASS.) Ter Domino, ad distinguendam personarum trinitatem; quia laus Christi honor est Trinitatis. Et est 1005Bfigura epimone, id est, crebra repetitio sententiae, quae exaggerat in laudem vel vituperationem.

VERS. 3.-- Annuntiate. Ad praelatos loquitur, annuntiate, quia sic crescit aedificatio domus. De die in diem. (CASS.) Vetus et Novum Testamentum dies sunt, qui aeterno sole clarescunt, illud praenuntiat, hoc factum indicat. (HIER.) Annuntiat ergo de die in diem, etc., usque ad quibus affectuum nostrorum pedes a vitiorum spinis muniuntur.

VERS. 4.-- Magnus Dominus. (AUG.) Parvulus factus, quia vos parvi, intelligite magnum, et eritis in illo magni.

VERS. 5.-- Coelos fecit. (ID.) Apostolos et angelos, unde si coelos fecit et angelos, tunc et apostolos, qui daemonibus imperant.

1005CVERS. 6.-- In conspectu. Tales enim, confitentes scilicet et justi, ipsum conspiciunt, et conspiciuntur ab eo. Sanctimonia et magnificentia. (AUG.) Quasi diceret: Qui vult esse magnificus et potens, ut sunt angeli, prius sit sanctus, quod fit ex eo sanctificante: non enim per te potes esse sanctus. Eo ergo sanctificante, aliquis fit sanctus, et ita magnificus.

VERS. 7.-- Afferte Domino patriae. (CASS.) Secunda pars, ubi ad subditos loquitur, etc., usque ad ut nullus excipiatur, indigena, vel peregrinus. Gloriam. (ID.) Quoniam bene conversatur homo, in quo glorificatur Deus. Honorem. Cum de bonis gratia refertur, unde, Non est inventus qui daret honorem Deo, nisi hic alienigena. In atria. (ID.) Atria, prophetae vel apostoli, quibus itur ad Dominum; de 1005Datriis, prophetis vel apostolis, venitur in atrium catholicae Ecclesiae, ubi majestas adoratur. (AUG.) Vel, Introite in atrio, id est, in doctrinam prophetarum et apostolorum.

VERS. 9.-- Adorate Dominum in atrio, etc. Id est, in Ecclesia catholica, vel per atria, prophetiam; per atrium Evangelium. Commoveatur. Omnibus admonitis moveri optat. Quasi diceret, introite et adorate vos, boni. Terra autem, etc. Universa terra. (CASS.) Non pars aliqua; ne quis ergo dicat: Ecce hic Christus esse illic, subdit, Etenim correxit orbem terrae, etc.

VERS. 10.-- Dicite in gentibus. (ID.) Quod regnavit et correxit, et judicavit. Regnavit. Alia littera: 1006ARegnavit a ligno (Matth. XIII). (AUG.) Crucis, quo transit homo mare, et fit orbis qui non movetur.

Populos in aequitate, etc. Alii addunt, Et gentes in ira tua.

(CASS.) Populos ergo, id est, bonos judicabit in aequitate, gentes vero, id est, malos in ira sua.

VERS. 12.-- Tunc exsultabunt. (CASS., HIERON.) Tunc, quando corriget, etc., usque ad quoniam venit, id est, veniet judicare terram. Quoniam venit. (AUG.) Primo venit in Ecclesia, in nubibus, id est, apostolis, et implevit totum orbem; unde: Amodo videbitis Filium hominis venientem in nubibus (Matth. XXVI): cui adventui qui credit, exsultabit in ultimo adventu.

VERS. 13.-- Judicabit orbem. (CASS.) Omnem 1006Bhominem generaliter includit, secundum aequitatem Dei judicandum. Sed quomodo judicetur exponit, dicendo, populos in veritate, quia in separatione duo erunt populi, quibus dabit sententiam veritatis, ut alii in vitam, alii in poenas eant. (AUG.) Orbem dicit omnes filios Adam, etc., usque ad meridiem.

PSALM XCV.

  • 1005A

A psalm of David. [Vulg. Ps 95:1 Canticum ipsi David, quando domus aedificabatur post captivitatem., "a canticle for David himself, when the house was building after the captivity"] (CASS.) In the Old Testament it is read, etc., as far as this psalm does not treat of that actual one.

VERS. 1.-- Sing ye to the Lord. (ID.) He forewarned the Jews in the preceding psalm that, their hardness being laid aside, they should believe Christ; but because it was to abide, he now admonishes all the Gentiles. The second psalm concerning both comings. First he speaks to the prelates, that they themselves should sing and declare. A new canticle. (AUG.) Cupidity sings the old, etc., as far as whosoever shall have entered in, is without.

VERS. 2.-- To the Lord, and bless. (HIER., CASS.) Thrice to the Lord, for the distinguishing of the trinity of persons; because the praise of Christ is the honor of the Trinity. And there is 1005Bthe figure epimone, that is, a frequent repetition of the same sentiment, which heightens it unto praise or unto blame.

VERS. 3.-- Declare ye. He speaks to the prelates, declare, because thus grows the building of the house. From day to day. (CASS.) The Old and the New Testament are days, which grow bright by the eternal sun, the one foretells, the other shows the thing done. (HIER.) He declares therefore from day to day, etc., as far as by which the feet of our affections are fenced from the thorns of the vices.

VERS. 4.-- Great is the Lord. (AUG.) Made little, because you are little, understand him great, and you shall be great in him.

VERS. 5.-- He made the heavens. (ID.) The apostles and the angels, whence if he made the heavens and the angels, then the apostles also, who command the demons.

1005CVERS. 6.-- In the sight. For such men, namely those confessing and just, behold him themselves, and are beheld by him. Holiness and magnificence. (AUG.) As if he should say: He who wishes to be magnificent and mighty, as the angels are, let him first be holy, which comes to pass from him who sanctifies: for of thyself thou canst not be holy. When therefore he sanctifies, a man is made holy, and so magnificent.

VERS. 7.-- Bring to the Lord, ye kindreds. (CASS.) The second part, where he speaks to the subjects, etc., as far as that none be excepted, native or stranger. Glory. (ID.) Because a man converses well, in whom God is glorified. Honor. When from good things thanks are rendered, whence, There was not found who would give honor to God, but this stranger. [Vulg. Lc 17:18 Non est inventus qui rediret, et daret gloriam Deo, nisi hic alienigena., "who returned and gave glory to God"] Into the courts. (ID.) The courts, the prophets or the apostles, by whom there is a going to the Lord; from the 1005Dcourts, that is, the prophets or the apostles, there is a coming into the court of the Catholic Church, where the majesty is adored. (AUG.) Or, Enter ye into the court, that is, into the doctrine of the prophets and the apostles.

VERS. 9.-- Adore ye the Lord in the court, etc. That is, in the Catholic Church, or by the courts, prophecy; by the court, the Gospel. Let it be moved. All being admonished, he desires that they be moved. As if he should say, enter in and adore, you that are good. But the earth, etc. The whole earth. (CASS.) Not some part of it; therefore, lest anyone say: Lo, here is Christ to be there, [Vulg. Mt 24:23 Ecce hic est Christus, aut illic, "Lo, here is Christ, or there"] he subjoins, For he hath corrected the world of the earth, etc.

VERS. 10.-- Say ye among the nations. (ID.) That he reigned and corrected and judged. He hath reigned. Another reading: 1006AHe hath reigned from the wood (Matth. XIII). (AUG.) Of the cross, by which man passes over the sea, and becomes a world which is not moved.

The peoples in equity, etc. Others add, And the nations in thy wrath.

(CASS.) The peoples therefore, that is, the good, he shall judge in equity, but the nations, that is, the wicked, in his wrath.

VERS. 12.-- Then shall they rejoice. (CASS., HIERON.) Then, when he shall correct, etc., as far as because he is come, that is, he shall come to judge the earth. Because he is come. (AUG.) First he came in the Church, in the clouds, that is, in the apostles, and filled the whole world; whence: From henceforth you shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds (Matth. XXVI): he who believes that coming shall rejoice in the last coming.

VERS. 13.-- He shall judge the world. (CASS.) He generally includes every 1006Bman, to be judged according to the equity of God. But how he is judged he sets forth by saying, the peoples in truth, because in the separation there shall be two peoples, to whom he shall give the sentence of truth, so that some go into life, others into punishments. (AUG.) By the world he means all the sons of Adam, etc., as far as the south.

PSALMUS XCVI.

Psalmus ipsi David. Ad litteram illud tangit hic, quod mortuo Absalom, iniquo filio David, qui vivens patrem persequebatur, David restituta est terra, et in pace regnavit, de quo hic non agitur, sed potius de significato. (AUG.) David Christum significat, quem iniqui filii, id est, Judaei, crucifixerunt, atque regnum adjuraverunt ei. Sed restituta est terra ei, quando Judaea, quae crucifixerat, credidit: 1006Cet apostoli, qui titubaverant, sunt confirmati: sed et aliae oves de gentibus sunt adductae.

Vel, restituta est terra, cum caro ejus resurrexit, postquam resurrectionem haec omnia quae hic cantantur, facta sunt.

(AUG.) Praevidentes in spiritu haec, gavisi sunt prophetae, etc., usque ad palato namque fidei dulce sapit mel divinae promissionis.

(CASS.) Quartus psalmus de primo adventu, quo mundus liberatus est. Describit primo virtutes Domini, ostendit omnia restituta ei, et arguit idololatras.

VERS. 1.-- Dominus regnavit. (CASS.) Videns propheta superstitiones mundi abundare ante Christi resurrectionem, opponit: Dominus regnavit. (AUG.) 1006DQuis ergo alter colendus est? quasi, nullus; inde:

Exsultet terra. Quid remanet idolis? Quasi nihil.

Insulae. Totius mundi Ecclesiae. Multae. Non omnes, propter haereticorum conventus.

(CASS.) Inde qualis sit Dominus primo adventu dicit.

VERS. 2.-- Nubes et caligo. Impiis, qui caeci sunt, nubilosus et caliginosus, quibus nulla claritate splendet; sed bonis, Justitia et judicium. Qui correcti sunt sedes ejus. Ante adventum ejus ignis praecedet, quia impii pro praedicatione prophetarum ira succensi, de nece eorum tractaverunt, et ad indignationem inflammati in circuitu, quia multi, cum pauci essent praedicatores.

1007AVERS. 3.-- Ignis ante ipsum praecedet, etc. (AUG.) Quasi correcti sunt sedes Dei, etc., usque ad si mali sunt, ad consumptionem; si boni, ad reparationem.

VERS. 4.-- Illuxerunt fulgura. (ID.) Nubes viluerunt forma humana, sed fulgor mirandus in verbis vel factis eorum apparuit, et inde mota est terra.

VERS. 5.-- Fluxerunt. (ID.) Etsi non modo credit paganus, tamen victus est.

VERS. 7.-- Confundantur. Hoc jam factum est. (AUG.) Cessat enim jam idololatria. Et erubescant qui adorant lapides, quia mortui.

VERS. 8.-- Adorate. (ID.) Cessat ergo adoratio angelorum, sed adorant. Ipsi mali angeli volunt adorari, boni adorant, nec se permittunt adorari. Vel saltem hoc exemplo idololatriae cessent.

1007BAudivi et laetata. (CASS.) Secundo post restaurationem terrae omnimoda exsultatio, etc., usque ad ut de Cornelio fratres gavisi sunt quem Petrus baptizavit. Et exsultaverunt. (AUG.) Audierunt apostoli, qui erant in Judaea fratres, quia gentes receperunt verbum Dei, et laetati sunt et magnificabant Deum.

VERS. 9.-- Terra... deos. (ID.) Per terram et deos, peccatores et justos accipe. Vel, terrenis et coelestibus significat eum imperare.

VERS. 10.-- Custodit Dominus. (AUG.) Si cum coeperis odisse malignum, subsequantur persecutiones, ne timeas, quia custodit Dominus animas sanctorum suorum, de quibus tollendis est ultimum genus persecutionis.

PSALM XCVI.

A psalm for David himself. [Vulg. Ps 96:1 Huic David, quando terra ejus restituta est., "to this David, when his land was restored to him" — the clause this gloss expounds] According to the letter he touches here upon this, that when Absalom, the wicked son of David, was dead, who while he lived persecuted his father, the land was restored to David, and he reigned in peace, of which it is not here treated, but rather of the thing signified. (AUG.) David signifies Christ, whom the wicked sons, that is, the Jews, crucified, and abjured the kingdom to him [adjuraverunt; read abjuraverunt, "renounced on oath"]. But the land was restored to him, when Judaea, which had crucified him, believed: 1006Cand the apostles, who had wavered, were confirmed: but other sheep also were led in from among the Gentiles.

Or, the land was restored, when his flesh rose again, after which resurrection all these things which are here sung were done.

(AUG.) Foreseeing these things in the spirit, the prophets rejoiced, etc., as far as for to the palate of faith the honey of the divine promise tastes sweet.

(CASS.) The fourth psalm concerning the first coming, by which the world was set free. He describes first the powers of the Lord, shows that all things are restored to him, and reproves the idolaters.

VERS. 1.-- The Lord hath reigned. (CASS.) The prophet, seeing the superstitions of the world abound before the resurrection of Christ, sets against them: The Lord hath reigned. (AUG.) 1006DWho then is another to be worshipped? as it were, none; thereupon:

Let the earth rejoice. What remains to the idols? As it were, nothing.

The islands. The Churches of the whole world. Many. Not all, because of the assemblies of the heretics.

(CASS.) Thereupon he tells what manner of Lord he is in the first coming.

VERS. 2.-- Clouds and darkness. To the wicked, who are blind, he is cloudy and dark, to whom he shines with no brightness; but to the good, Justice and judgment. They who are corrected are his seat. Before his coming fire shall go before, because the wicked, kindled with wrath at the preaching of the prophets, took counsel of their slaying, and were inflamed unto indignation round about, because they were many, whereas the preachers were few.

1007AVERS. 3.-- Fire shall go before him, etc. (AUG.) As it were, they who are corrected are the seat of God, etc., as far as if they are wicked, unto consuming; if good, unto repairing.

VERS. 4.-- His lightnings have shone forth. (ID.) The clouds grew cheap in their human form, but a wondrous brightness appeared in their words or deeds, and thereupon the earth was moved.

VERS. 5.-- They flowed down. (ID.) Even if the pagan does not believe just now, yet he is overcome.

VERS. 7.-- Let them be confounded. This has now been done. (AUG.) For idolatry now ceases. And let them blush who adore stones, because they are dead.

VERS. 8.-- Adore ye. (ID.) The adoration of the angels therefore ceases, but they adore. The evil angels themselves wish to be adored, the good adore, and do not suffer themselves to be adored. Or at least by this example let idolatry cease.

1007BI have heard and she was glad. [Vulg. Ps 96:8 Audivit, "she hath heard"] (CASS.) Secondly, after the restoration of the land, an exultation of every kind, etc., as far as as the brethren rejoiced over Cornelius, whom Peter baptized. And they rejoiced. (AUG.) The apostles heard, who were brethren in Judaea, that the Gentiles had received the word of God, and they were glad and magnified God.

VERS. 9.-- The earth . . . the gods. (ID.) By the earth and the gods understand sinners and just men. Or, he signifies that he rules over things earthly and things heavenly.

VERS. 10.-- The Lord keepeth. (AUG.) If, when thou hast begun to hate the malignant, persecutions follow after, fear not, because the Lord keeps the souls of his saints, for the taking away of whom is the last kind of persecution.

PSALMUS XCVII.

1007CPsalmus David. (CASS.) Tertius psalmus eorum qui de utroque adventu agunt: in quibus est causa spei per misericordiam primi adventus, et timoris per judicium secundi: haec, etsi saepe iterentur, tamen semper nova pro verborum et sententiarum varia descriptione.

VERS. 1.-- Cantate Domino. (CASS.) Primo ait de ostensione salvatricis dexterae.

Salvavit. (AUG.) Majus est quod totum orbem a morte aeterna erexit, quam quod mortuos suscitavit. Sibi. Multi salvantur corporaliter, sed sibi, non ei: qui accepta corporali sanitate lasciviunt, sed qui per fidem intus sanantur, ei sanantur, vel se salvant.

VERS. 2.-- Salutare . . . justitiam. (AUG.) Qui salvat et justificat. Revelavit. Futura sub velamine praedixerunt 1007Dprophetae: sed velamen ablatum est, cum veritas de terra orta est.

VERS. 3.-- Misericordiae et veritatis. (AUG.) Misericordia est quo promisit, hanc sequitur veritas, quia reddidit. Sed cui? Israeli, id est, qui modo per fidem videt veritatem, post per speciem.

VERS. 4.-- Omnes. (ID.) Quia non quibusdam tantum datus est Christus.

VERS. 5.-- Jubilate. (CASS.) Secundo dicit omnibus modis laudandum esse et annuntiandum, quia venit judex.

VERS. 6.-- In tubis ductilibus et voce tubae corneae. (AUG.) Aeris, quae tundendo producuntur, etc., usque ad ut cornu carni haeret, et eam superat. 1008A(HIERON.) In tubis ductilibus, argenteis, more Judaeorum. Mystice, productis sub malleo universae terrae, id est diabolo. (AUG.) Tribulatio, tunsio est; profectus, productio: talis tuba erat Job, unde quasi tuba insonuit, dicens: Dominus dedit, Dominus abstulit.

VERS. 7.-- Moveatur. (ID.) Id est, indulcetur mare legis, ligno crucis in eo posito. Et plenitudo ejus. Universa legis sacramenta, etc., usque ad sed flumina, etc. Terram. (CASS.) Id est, omnem peccatorem.

VERS. 9.-- Orbem terrarum. Omnes terrenos. In justitia. (AUG.) Quia non meruerunt misericordiam. Populos. (CASS.) Fideles de Judaeis et gentibus, qui capient aequa meritis.

PSALM XCVII.

1007CA psalm of David. [Vulg. Ps 97:1 Psalmus ipsi David., "a psalm for David himself"] (CASS.) The third psalm of those which treat of both comings: in which there is matter of hope through the mercy of the first coming, and of fear through the judgment of the second: these things, even if they are often repeated, are yet always new by reason of the varied setting forth of the words and of the sentiments.

VERS. 1.-- Sing ye to the Lord. (CASS.) First he speaks of the showing forth of the saving right hand.

He hath saved. (AUG.) It is a greater thing that he raised up the whole world from eternal death, than that he raised the dead. To himself. Many are saved bodily, but to themselves, not to him: they who, having received bodily health, grow wanton, but they who by faith are healed within, are healed to him, or save themselves.

VERS. 2.-- Salvation . . . justice. (AUG.) He who saves and justifies. He hath revealed. Things to come were foretold under a veil by the 1007Dprophets: but the veil has been taken away, since truth is sprung out of the earth.

VERS. 3.-- Of mercy and of truth. (AUG.) Mercy is that whereby he promised, truth follows upon this, because he rendered it. But to whom? To Israel, that is, to him who now by faith sees the truth, afterwards by sight.

VERS. 4.-- All. (ID.) Because Christ was not given to certain men only.

VERS. 5.-- Rejoice ye. (CASS.) Secondly he says that in all ways he is to be praised and declared, because the judge is come.

VERS. 6.-- With ductile trumpets and with the voice of a trumpet of horn. (AUG.) Of brass, which are drawn out by beating, etc., as far as as the horn cleaves to the flesh, and surpasses it. 1008A(HIERON.) With ductile trumpets, of silver, after the manner of the Jews. Mystically, drawn out under the hammer of the whole earth, that is, the devil. (AUG.) Tribulation is the beating; advancement, the drawing out: such a trumpet was Job, whence he sounded as a trumpet, saying: The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away.

VERS. 7.-- Let it be moved. (ID.) That is, let the sea of the law be made sweet, the wood of the cross being set therein. And the fulness thereof. All the sacraments of the law, etc., as far as but the rivers, etc. The earth. (CASS.) That is, every sinner.

VERS. 9.-- The world of the earth. All earthly men. In justice. (AUG.) Because they did not merit mercy. The peoples. (CASS.) The faithful out of the Jews and the Gentiles, who shall receive things equal to their merits.

PSALMUS XCVIII.

  • 1008B

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus David. (AUG.) Propheta describit Christum regem bona dantem, etc., usque ad sed velamen ablatum est, cum veritas de terra orta est, et justitia de coelo prospexit (Psal. XLVIII). Dominus regnavit (CASS.) De potentia et regno Christi, ut in homine adoretur. Ostendit Christum regnantem, et (quicunque repugnet) altum super omnes, unde ei cedere monet. Irascantur populi. (CASS.) Irrisio. Secure concedi potest, ut irascantur, quia non sunt ultra nocituri: permittendo dicit, non imperando. Sedet super cherubim. (ID.) Contra eum nihil potest terra, etsi ipse fuit in terra ubi passus est iram populi. Cherubim. (AUG.) Plenitudo scientiae 1008Cinterpretatur, quae est charitas. Plenitudo scientiae legis, quae est sedes Dei, erit et in te, si charitatem habueris, contra quam nihil possunt irati. Quid enim terra contra coelum?

VERS. 2.-- Dominus in Sion. (ID.) Si non intelligis quid est super Cherubim, hoc vide, quia in Sion magnus. Sion est anima quae Deum speculatur. In Sion magnus. (CASS.) Quis Dominus, exponit: In Sion natus. Magnus, ne pro passione vilescat. Vel, tamen Dominus magnus in Sion Judaeorum, et super populos gentium.

VERS. 3.-- Magno. (AUG.) Parvum erat quando irascebantur, id est, paucis diffamatum, sed jam in omni terra dilatatum. Terribile. (ID.) Quia etsi crucifixus praedicatur, judex venturus, et non errabit 1008Din judicio. Et honor regis. (CASS.) Exponit quomodo debent confiteri. Honor regis, est gloriosa praedicatio, judicium discretionem exigit; non levi voluntate colendus est, sed fixa deliberatione, quod ab ipso est; unde subdit: Tu parasti directiones. Vel honor regis est damnatio nocentium, unde regis gloria augetur.

VERS. 4.-- In Jacob. (AUG.) Non solum patriarcha, sed populo, quem significat. Tu fecisti. Haec, quae alius non posset.

VERS. 5.-- Exaltate. (CASS.) Secunda pars monet adorare eum, quia patres ejus fuerunt. Quasi, quia haec facit nobis, ergo Exaltate.

Scabellum. (AUG.) Terra scabellum pedum ejus dicit 1009AScriptura, etc., usque ad in cujus honore scabellum adorat. Pedum. (CASS.) Pedes, indefecta stabilitas deitatis. Sanctum. Ut discernas corpus a deitate, etsi una persona.

VERS. 6.-- Moyses. (CASS.) Sacerdos, quia si non hostias, populi vota obtulit, et pro populo supplicavit.

VERS. 7.-- Columna. (CASS.) Fortitudo et decor domus. In hac specie loquebatur, quae nuntiabat Ecclesiam, vel carnem, sed tunc in nube, modo aperte per Filium: Nubis loquebatur ad eos. (ID.) Ad eos ergo tunc in nube, qui jam nobis loquitur in scabello, id est, in carne assumpta aperte. Testimonia ejus et praecepta. (ID.) Testimonium est per signa aliqua praecedentis rei posita significatio: unde saepe in lege dicitur: Hoc erit vobis in testimonium. Praecepta 1009Bsunt sicut praecepta legis per Moysen data.

VERS. 8.-- Propitius fuisti eis. (AUG.) Non dicitur nisi peccatis, propitius ignoscendo, propitius et ulciscendo, ecce etsi tanti essent isti, aliquid tamen habebant peccati; unde addit, in omnes adinventiones.

Ulciscens. Ne humana elatio subriperet; unde: Datus est mihi stimulus carnis meae (II Cor. XII) Adinventiones. Alias affectiones. (AUG.) Quas solus Deus noverat in cordibus eorum; unde poena eis pati eos cum quibus erant, pro quorum peccatis quasi suis dolebant per charitatem. Non enim fuit, ut a plerisque putatur, Moysi poena non intrare in terram promissionis in quam et miseri intraverunt; sed figura, quod qui sub lege essent, et sub gratia esse nollent, non intrarent in requiem.

PSALM XCVIII.

  • 1008B

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of David. [Vulg. Ps 98:1 Psalmus ipsi David., "a psalm for David himself"] (AUG.) The prophet describes Christ the king giving good things, etc., as far as but the veil has been taken away, since truth is sprung out of the earth, and justice hath looked down from heaven (Psal. XLVIII). The Lord hath reigned (CASS.) Concerning the power and the kingdom of Christ, that he may be adored in the man. He shows Christ reigning, and (whosoever may resist) high above all, whence he admonishes to yield to him. Let the peoples be angry. (CASS.) A derision. It can safely be granted that they be angry, because they are not going to hurt any further: he speaks by permitting, not by commanding. He sitteth upon the cherubim. (ID.) Against him the earth can do nothing, even though he himself was on the earth where he suffered the wrath of the people. Cherubim. (AUG.) The fulness of knowledge 1008Cis its interpretation, which is charity. The fulness of the knowledge of the law, which is the seat of God, shall be in thee also, if thou hast charity, against which the angry can do nothing. For what is the earth against heaven?

VERS. 2.-- The Lord in Sion. (ID.) If thou dost not understand what is upon the Cherubim, see this, that he is great in Sion. Sion is the soul which beholds God. Great in Sion. (CASS.) Who the Lord is, he sets forth: In Sion born. Great, lest he grow cheap on account of the passion. Or, yet the Lord is great in the Sion of the Jews, and above the peoples of the Gentiles.

VERS. 3.-- Great. (AUG.) It was little when they were angry, that is, made known among few, but now enlarged in all the earth. Terrible. (ID.) Because even if he is preached as crucified, he is the judge to come, and he shall not err 1008Din judgment. And the honor of the king. (CASS.) He sets forth how they ought to confess. The honor of the king, is the glorious preaching, judgment requires discernment; he is to be worshipped not with a light will, but with fixed deliberation, which is from him; whence he subjoins: Thou hast prepared directions. Or the honor of the king is the damnation of the guilty, whereby the glory of the king is increased.

VERS. 4.-- In Jacob. (AUG.) Not only the patriarch, but the people whom he signifies. Thou hast done. These things, which another could not do.

VERS. 5.-- Exalt ye. (CASS.) The second part admonishes to adore him, because his fathers were. As it were, because he does these things for us, therefore Exalt ye.

The footstool. (AUG.) The earth is the footstool of his feet, says 1009AScripture, etc., as far as in whose honor it adores the footstool. Of the feet. (CASS.) The feet, the unfailing stability of the Godhead. Holy. That thou mayest distinguish the body from the Godhead, even though it be one person.

VERS. 6.-- Moses. (CASS.) A priest, because if not victims, he offered the vows of the people, and made supplication for the people.

VERS. 7.-- A pillar. (CASS.) The strength and the beauty of the house. In this appearance he spoke, which announced the Church, or the flesh, but then in a cloud, now openly through the Son: He spoke to them out of the cloud. (ID.) To them therefore then in a cloud, who now speaks to us in the footstool, that is, openly in the flesh assumed. His testimonies and precepts. (ID.) A testimony is a signification set down by certain signs of a preceding thing: whence often in the law it is said: This shall be to you for a testimony. The precepts 1009Bare as the precepts of the law given through Moses. [Vulg. Ps 98:7 praeceptum quod dedit illis, singular, "the precept which he gave them"]

VERS. 8.-- Thou wast merciful to them. (AUG.) It is not said save of sins, merciful in forgiving, merciful also in avenging, behold, even though these were so great, yet they had somewhat of sin; whence he adds, upon all their inventions.

Avenging. Lest human elation should creep upon them; whence: There was given me a sting of my flesh (II Cor. XII) Inventions. Otherwise, affections. (AUG.) Which God alone knew in their hearts; whence it was a punishment to them to bear with those among whom they were, for whose sins they grieved as for their own, through charity. For it was not, as is thought by very many, a punishment to Moses not to enter into the land of promise, into which the wretched also entered; but a figure, that they who were under the law, and were unwilling to be under grace, should not enter into rest.

PSALMUS XCIX.

  • 1009C

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus in confessione. Confessio gemina est; una est laudis, altera peccatorum. Confessio laudis convenit perfectis, confessio peccatorum inicipientibus; unde in hoc psalmo propheta monet ad confessionem. (CASS.) Docet hic psalmus, et Deum incessanter laudare, et peccata nostra incessanter plangere: quia nec in malis est desperandum, nec in bonis debet animus esse elevatus. Primo perfectis praecipuum genus confessionis, id est laudem, indicit.

Jubilate. (AUG.) Si vox jubilat exterius, etc., usque ad et quo ordine et quam mirifice fecit. Omnis terra. Ad laudem monens. Non unum angulum terrae 1009Dhortatur: sed sicut ubique novit seminatam benedictionem, ita undique exigit jubilationem. Servite in laetitia. (AUG.) Haec servitus non est amaritudinis, nec indignationis, sed felicitatis et libertatis. Servum ergo te faciat charitas, quia liberum te fecit veritas. Unde Dominus: Si manseritis in verbo meo, vere discipuli mei eritis: et cognoscetis veritatem, et veritas vos liberabit (Joan. VIII).

In laetitia. Quia liberati; non murmurantes, ut in deserto: unde praemium subdit.

VERS. 2.-- Introite in conspectu. Magnum est in conspectu tanti gaudere. Introite. (CASS.) Secundo intraturis secundum genus confessionis; nec dubitetur, quia misericordia est ei.

PSALM XCIX.

  • 1009C

VERS. 1.-- A psalm in confession. Confession is twofold; one is of praise, the other of sins. The confession of praise befits the perfect, the confession of sins those who are beginning inicipientibus; whence in this psalm the prophet admonishes to confession. (CASS.) This psalm teaches both to praise God unceasingly, and unceasingly to bewail our sins: because neither in evils is one to despair, nor in good things ought the mind to be lifted up. First he enjoins upon the perfect the chief kind of confession, that is, praise.

Rejoice ye. (AUG.) If the voice rejoices outwardly, etc., as far as and in what order and how wonderfully he made it. All the earth. Admonishing to praise. Not one corner of the earth does he 1009Dexhort: but as he knows the blessing to have been sown everywhere, so from everywhere he requires jubilation. Serve ye in gladness. (AUG.) This servitude is not of bitterness, nor of indignation, but of happiness and of liberty. Let charity therefore make thee a servant, because truth has made thee free. Whence the Lord: If you shall abide in my word, you shall be my disciples indeed: and you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free (Joan. VIII). [Vulg. Jo 8:31 Si vos manseritis in sermone meo, "in my discourse"]

In gladness. Because they are set free; not murmuring, as in the desert: whence he subjoins the reward.

VERS. 2.-- Enter ye into his sight. It is a great thing to rejoice in the sight of so great a one. Enter ye in. (CASS.) Secondly, to those about to enter, the second kind of confession; nor let it be doubted, because mercy is with him.

PSLMUS C.

  • 1010A

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus ipsi David. (CASS.) Psalmus iste continet formam perfectae sanctitatis, ut centesimus numerus perfectus est.

Ipsi David. Ut totum quod hic docetur, virtutibus Christi applicetur, nihil terreno regi. Hic docemur bona appetere, mala renuere, quae est perfecta conversatio vitae.

Misericordiam et judicium cantabo. (CASS.) Cantat hic Christus, et nos in illo. Prius de misericordia et judicio proponit. Misericordiam et judicium cantabo. Haec duo mutua societate junguntur: in his breviter omnia opera Dei includit. Et hic est praemissa causa quare sic se habet, sicut postea subdit. (AUG.) Nemo de misericordia praesumat ad impunitatem, 1010Bquia est ei judicium; nemo immutatus in melius judicium timeat, quia praecedit misericordia. Semper haec simul in eo sunt: sed per tempora secundum effectus distinguuntur, misericordia nunc, judicium in futuro.

VERS. 2.-- Psallam et intelligam. (ID.) Hoc dat psallere, ut intelligam mente, quod oculis non patet, id est, credam quod Dominus veniet, quem iste tantum desiderat, qui veniet in via immaculata. (CASS.) Quia mundum transivit sine peccato; vel, ego psallam et intelligam existens in via immaculata, quando, etc. Vel, psallam, hilariter operabor, et per hoc intelligam. Quando venies ad me. In secundo adventu, vel obitu cujusque. Vel, quando venies ad me, per carnem in primo adventu, quia in 1010Cvia immaculata. Perambulabam. (CASS.) Secundo, quae sit via immaculata exponit. (AUG.) Perambulabam. Quae est via immaculata? Ea ab innocentia incipit, et in illa consummatur; et non est opus multis verbis: Innocens esto, et perfecisti justitiam. Sed duobus modis nocet homo, videlicet si facit miserum, et si deserit miserum. Innocens est qui nec sibi nec alii nocet. (CASS.) Perambulabam. Quasi dicat: Transitoria non quaesivi, sed cucurri viam mundi, existens in medio domus tuae. Innocentia hoc potest, ut faciat habitare in medio domus Dei, quasi honorabile exemplum aliorum.

VERS. 3.-- Non proponebam. (CASS.) Innocentiam per partes exponit. Primo, quia nihil habet cum malis, dicit: Non proponebam, usque, oculi 1010Dmei. Post quod pars ei cum justis, et quod versutias diaboli de corde fugat, ibi, in mututinis. (AUG.) Non proponebam. Quasi: Perambulabam in innocentia: hac utique (dicit totus Christus,) quod non proponebam, id est, non diligebam rem injustam.

VERS. 4.-- Non adhaesit. (CASS.) Exponit praevaricationes. Cor pravum, qui praevaricatur corde; declinantem, haereticum qui a catholicis dissentit: et qui a rectis semitis deviat non agnoscebam, quia etsi signati nobiscum sacramentis, non tamen veri sunt.

VERS. 5.-- Superbo. (AUG.) Et Jesus convivatus, etc., usque ad unde: Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt justitiam (Matth. VIII).

VERS. 6.-- Oculi mei. Hic alteram partem innocentiae exsequitur, scilicet, quod cum justis habet partem. Quasi dicat: Cum talibus non edebas, unde ergo pascebaris? Terrae. (AUG.) Degentes in terra, ubi tot illecebrae, unde major corona. Vel (CASS.) qui per totum mundum sunt. Ut sedeant mecum. (AUG.) In veritate fidei mecum permaneant, vel participent mecum regno aeterno, vel judicent mecum.

VERS. 7.-- Non habitabit in medio domus meae. (CASS.) Id est, Ecclesiae. Etsi aliquandiu toleretur gratia correctionis, non praeeminet meritis, nihil potest; non est in populo meo granum, sed palea. Non habitabit, hoc maxime convenit sacerdotibus, ut pravis non cohabitent.

VERS. 8.-- In matutino. (CASS.) Tertia pars, ubi ostendit 1011Bquis finis sit malorum. Et loquitur hic Christus. In matutino. Post vitatos malos, justus ad se reversus, addit quod suggestiones daemonum de corde expulit in matutino, id est, quando in initio tentationis, quasi in crepusculo incipiunt apparere. Interficiebam. Oratione, qua debent ejici, ne crescant. Peccatores. Daemones, qui omnem carnem faciunt peccare. Civitate Domini. Anima justi, unde diabolus dispergitur et removetur. Omnes operantes iniquitatem. Id est, submissiones vel immissiones diaboli.

(AUG.) Jam enumeravit quod et non adhaeserunt nisi boni, etc., usque ad hoc et justo convenit, qui praevidet hoc futurum, et ideo se sic habet.

PSALM C.

  • 1010A

VERS. 1.-- A psalm for David himself. (CASS.) This psalm contains the form of perfect sanctity, as the hundredth number is a perfect one.

For David himself. That the whole of what is here taught be applied to the virtues of Christ, nothing to an earthly king. Here we are taught to seek good things and to refuse evil, which is the perfect converse of life.

Mercy and judgment I will sing. (CASS.) Here Christ sings, and we in him. First he sets forth concerning mercy and judgment. Mercy and judgment I will sing. These two are joined in a mutual fellowship: in them he briefly includes all the works of God. And here is set before us the cause why he so bears himself, as he afterwards subjoins. (AUG.)
