Let no one presume upon mercy unto impunity, 1010Bbecause there is judgment for him; let no one who has been changed for the better fear judgment, because mercy goes before. These are always together in him: but through the times they are distinguished according to their effects, mercy now, judgment in the time to come.

VERS. 2.-- I will sing and I will understand. (ID.) This the singing grants, that I may understand with the mind what lies not open to the eyes, that is, that I may believe that the Lord will come, whom this man so greatly desires, who will come in the unspotted way. (CASS.) Because he passed through the world without sin; or, I will sing and I will understand, being in the unspotted way, when, etc. Or, I will sing, I will work cheerfully, and through this I shall understand. When wilt thou come to me. In the second coming, or in the death of each one. Or, when wilt thou come to me, through the flesh in the first coming, because 1010Cin the unspotted way. I walked about. (CASS.) Secondly, he sets forth what the unspotted way is. (AUG.) I walked about. What is the unspotted way? It begins from innocence, and in it is consummated; and there is no need of many words: Be thou innocent, and thou hast fulfilled justice. But in two ways a man does harm, namely if he makes another wretched, and if he abandons the wretched. He is innocent who harms neither himself nor another. (CASS.) I walked about. As if he should say: I sought not transitory things, but I ran the way of the world, being in the midst of thy house. Innocence has this power, that it makes a man dwell in the midst of the house of God, as an honorable example to others.

VERS. 3.-- I did not set before me. (CASS.) He sets forth innocence by parts. First, because he has nothing with the wicked, he says: I did not set before me, down to, mine 1010Deyes. After which, that he has a part with the just, and that he drives the wiles of the devil out of his heart, there, in the mornings. mututinis (AUG.) I did not set before me. As it were: I walked about in innocence: in this indeed (the whole Christ says it,) namely that I did not set before me, that is, I did not love an unjust thing.

VERS. 4.-- It did not cleave. (CASS.) He sets forth the transgressions. A perverse heart, he who transgresses in heart; the man turning aside, the heretic who dissents from the Catholics: and him who strays from the right paths I did not acknowledge, because even if they are sealed with the sacraments along with us, yet they are not true men.

VERS. 5.-- The proud. (AUG.) And Jesus feasted, etc., as far as whence: Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after justice (Matth. VIII).

VERS. 6.-- Mine eyes. Here he pursues the other part of innocence, namely, that he has a part with the just. As if he should say: With such men thou didst not eat, whence then wast thou fed? Of the earth. (AUG.) Those living on the earth, where there are so many enticements, whence a greater crown. Or (CASS.) those who are throughout the whole world. That they may sit with me. (AUG.) That they may abide with me in the truth of faith, or share with me in the eternal kingdom, or judge with me.

VERS. 7.-- He shall not dwell in the midst of my house. (CASS.) That is, of the Church. Even if he is for a while borne with for the sake of correction, he does not stand out by merits, he can do nothing; he is not grain in my people, but chaff. He shall not dwell, this befits priests most of all, that they dwell not with the depraved.

VERS. 8.-- In the morning. (CASS.) The third part, where he shows 1011Bwhat the end of the wicked is. And here Christ speaks. In the morning. After the wicked have been shunned, the just man, returned to himself, adds that he drove the suggestions of the demons out of his heart in the morning, that is, when at the beginning of the temptation they begin to appear, as it were in the twilight. I put to death. By prayer, whereby they ought to be cast out, lest they grow. Sinners. The demons, who make all flesh to sin. The city of the Lord. The soul of the just man, whence the devil is scattered and removed. All that work iniquity. That is, the insinuations or the injections of the devil.

(AUG.) He has now recounted that none clave to him but the good [et; read ei, "to him"], etc., as far as this befits the just man also, who foresees this to be to come, and therefore so bears himself.

PSALMUS CI.

VERS. 1.-- Oratio pauperis. (AUG.) Secundum 1011Cformam servi, etc., usque ad sponsus propter caput, sponsa propter corpus. Christus pauper in nobis, et nobiscum, et propter nos, hic orat in persona poenitentis, suam dejectionem, et dejectionis causam recognoscentis, et a peccatis liberari atque in pristinum statum restitui petentis. Monet ergo suam advertere miseriam, et Dei petere misericordiam.

VERS. 2.-- Domine, exaudi orationem meam. (CASS.) Quintus psalmus poenitentiae; quartus qui oratio dicitur. Prima pars, captatio deprecativa.

Et clamor. Oratio crevit in clamorem. Veniat, non obstent nubes, quae iniquis. (ID.) Epimone per tres versus, id est crebra repetitio sententiae.

VERS. 4.-- Quia defecerunt. (CASS.) Secunda pars, in qua est flebilis oratio; in qua exponitur, 1011Dquae paupertas, quae tribulatio. Unde clamet, jam aperit. Quia defecerunt. Defecerunt sicut fumus dies mei. (AUG.) Elato enim Adam deis deficiunt, virtus animi contrahitur. Miseria pium judicem movere potest. Ossa mea sicut cremium aruerunt. Fortes, quorum frixorium sunt, qui scandalizantur, etc., usque ad jam enim frigitur homo, dum timet se arsurum.

VERS. 5.-- Percussus sum ut fenum, et aruit cor meum. (ID.) Mortalis factus. Fenum viret, sed percussum facile sentit injuriam: sic caro hominis in lege Dei virens, ab eadem succisa arescit.

VERS. 6.-- A voce gemitus. (CASS.) Natura peccantium ostenditur, quia dum peccatum appetitur, 1012Acontemplatio Dei non habetur. Mei. (AUG.) Non illorum qui de terrenis, et non de spiritualibus gemunt, etc., usque ad infirmorum portare.

VERS. 7.-- Pelicano, (AUG.) Tres aves, tria loca ponit, etc., usque ad qui si non inter homines, extra est in alto, dicens eis, qui in nocte dormiunt.

Vel, passer sagax ad alta virtutum fugit, ubi tutus a laqueis. Qui solitarius vel unicus, propter charitatem (quem ex multis unum facit) est in tecto, vel aedificio propter altitudinem fidei, ut non descendat aliquid tollere de domo, id est carne.

Domicilio. (ID.) Vel parietinis, quae vulgo dicuntur ruinae, ubi parietes stant sine tecto, ubi habitat nycticorax avis, quae noctem amat.

VERS. 9.-- Tota die. (CASS.) Vel, in persona 1012Bjusti totum accipi potest. Quasi dicat, etc., usque ad vel, in dejectione reficiebar, adeo placebat mihi.

VERS. 10.-- Cinerem. (AUG.) Per cinerem et fletum poenitentes significantur. Cinis enim et cilicium sunt arma poenitentium. Potum. (CASS.) Temporalem jucunditatem. Vel desiderium patriae pro dilatione lacrymis miscui; vel potum Scripturarum, quae antiqua recolunt.

VERS. 11.-- A facie irae. (CASS.) Ira, ultio; indignatio, motio animi, qua indignamur etiam filiis. Ira dicitur impetus in puniendos, quae in Deum non cadunt. Sed est antropopathos.

Irae. Unde et Dominus ait: Ira Dei manet super eos qui non credunt (Joan. III). Non ait, veniet; sed manet, quia non tollitur, in qua natus est.

1012CVERS. 12.-- Dies mei sicut umbra declinaverunt. Quia ego a vero die declinavi, similes mihi sunt declinantes dies mei.

VERS. 13.-- Tu autem, etc. (CASS.) Tertia pars, ubi ostenditur certitudo impetrandi veniam. Jam consurgit lapsus ad prophetandum, jam poenitens caput relevat.

(AUG.) Memoriale promissum memorabile, de te reparatio nostra, quia tu nostri, vel nos memores tui.

VERS. 14.-- Venit tempus. (AUG.) Quia omnia ordine voluit Deus fieri, et tempus ad hoc disposuit, ubi opportunitas apte ordinata est.

VERS. 15.-- Lapides ejus. (AUG.) Sunt lapides in Sion, etc., usque ad inde est quod misso Spiritu sancto multi eorum crediderunt qui Dominum crucifixerunt.

1012DVERS. 17.-- In gloria. (AUG.) Qui primo visus est in infirmitate in illa Sion; unde: Vidimus eum non habentem speciem neque decorem (Isa. LIII).

VERS. 18.-- Orationem. Hoc agitur in aedificatione Sion: orant, gemunt aedificantes, qui sunt unus pauper, et pauperes multi; unde in titulo singulariter, hic pluraliter. Sed unus dicitur propter veritatem pacis Ecclesiae, multi propter latitudinem.

VERS. 19.-- Scribantur haec. (CASS.) Qui supra poenitentia sordebat, jam honore prophetae decoratus, praecipit haec quae dixit testimonio Scripturae firmari, ut aetas futura discat. In generatione. (AUG.) Haec quando scribebantur, non sic proderant generationi 1013AVeteris Testamenti; prosunt alteri, id est novae.

VERS. 20.-- Quia prospexit, etc. (AUG.) Post gemitus dolentis, jam sunt verba consolationum, jam gaudet pauper. Et quia supra dixit: Aedificavit Dominus Sion; et item: Scribantur haec; modo utrumque declarat; quasi hoc est quod dixit scribendum, quia prospexit.

Prospexit. Ut praeterita dicit, quae erant futura.

VERS. 21.-- Compeditorum. (AUG.) Timor Dei, compedes sunt, etc., usque ad et solutis vertuntur in gloriam. (CASS.) Compediti, sancti, etc., usque ad unde in generalem Ecclesiam concurrit sermo eorum. Ut solveret filios. (AUG.) Nos autem sumus filii illorum mortificatorum, qui solvimur a nodis peccatorum, 1013Bet vinculis cupiditatum.

VERS. 23.-- Respondit ei in via virtutis suae. (CASS.) Quarta pars, ubi, post certitudinem veniae, dicit quod de sua brevitate ad aeternitatem transeat. (AUG.) Respondit. Quia: Dico, ut annuntiem nomen Domini et laudem ejus in Jerusalem, etc., usque ad non contemnit, sed fructum reddit. Respondit ei. Id est, credit resurrexisse Christum. Sed quia praevidet quosdam dicturos, fuit quidem quondam Ecclesia congregans omnes in unum, sed jam desinit.

Paucitatem, inquit, dierum meorum: non aeternitatem illorum, ubi ero, sed temporales dies, quandiu ero in hoc saeculo. Nuntia mihi. Propter illos qui dicunt, jam non esse Ecclesiam. Non vacat vox ista, non est inanis petitio. Ipsa enim via, id est Christus, 1013Csic annuntiavit: Vobiscum sum usque ad consummationem saeculi (Matth. XXVIII). Totum tempus usque ad finem, est illa exiguitas dierum: quia omne quod finitur exiguum est, ut inde transeatur in aeternitatem. Nuntia et:

VERS. 24.-- Ne revoces me in dimidio dierum meorum. Non sic fiat, ut haeretici dicunt, etc., usque ad sed non sunt nisi dimidii, si non addantur aeterni.

VERS. 25.-- In via virtutis. (AUG.) In fide, qua resurrexisse credit Christum. Via virtutis fuit Christus post resurrectionem, cum jam non infirmus, sed fortis, in coelo vocat Ecclesiam. Laus fidei est, non quia credit mortuum, quod et Paganus credit, sed glorificatum.

1013DVel, breviter diffinitur religio Christiana, cum dicitur via virtutis.

Vel, in generatione generationum. Est generatio generationum, quae non transit, collecta de omnibus, id est sancti. In illa erunt anni Domini, qui non transeant, id est aeternitas Dei, quae est ipsa substantia Dei, nihil habens mutabile.

VERS. 26.-- Initio tu, Domine. Quasi, ne revoces, quia ad aeternitatem tendo, quam exponit, dicens: Initio tu, Domine, terram fundasti.

VERS. 27.-- Ipsi peribunt. (AUG.) Ipsi coeli peribunt, de proximis terrae hoc constat; unde et Petrus: Terra autem et coeli qui nunc sunt, eodem verbo repositi sunt, igni reservati (II Petr. III). De superioribus 1014Anon est certum, sed si manent, non in se, sed in Deo manent.

VERS. 28.-- Et sicut opertorium mutabis eos. Coelos accipe, qui omnia operiunt, qui etiam mutabuntur. Et anni tui non deficient. (AUG.) Qui erunt in generatione generationum. Sed an ibi esse poterimus? Utique, quia filii servorum tuorum habitabunt.

VERS. 29.-- Filii servorum. (AUG.) Ut filii intraverunt terram promissionis, etc., usque ad cum omni novitate filiorum.

Filii. Hilaris conclusio. Filii prophetarum et apostolorum, nedum ipsi.

Semen. Opera, unde fructus aeternus.

Dirigetur. Quia nihil tortum intrat.

PSALM CI.

VERS. 1.-- A prayer of the poor man. (AUG.) According to 1011Cthe form of a servant, etc., as far as the bridegroom on account of the head, the bride on account of the body. Christ, poor in us, and with us, and for our sake, here prays in the person of one repenting, who acknowledges his own abasement and the cause of his abasement, and who asks to be set free from sins and restored to his former state. He admonishes, therefore, that a man mark his own misery, and seek the mercy of God.

VERS. 2.-- O Lord, hear my prayer. (CASS.) The fifth psalm of penance; the fourth that is called a prayer. The first part, a deprecatory bid for a hearing.

And the cry. The prayer grew into a cry. Let it come, let not the clouds be in the way, which are in the way of the wicked. (ID.) An epimone through three verses, that is, a frequent repetition of the thought.

VERS. 4.-- For they have failed. (CASS.) The second part, in which is the mournful prayer; in which is set forth 1011Dwhat the poverty is, what the tribulation. He now discloses whence he cries. For they have failed. My days have failed like smoke. (AUG.) For when Adam was lifted up, the days deis fail, the strength of the mind is drawn in. Misery can move a merciful judge. My bones are grown dry like fuel. The strong, whose frying-pan are they that are scandalized, etc., as far as for a man is already being fried, while he fears that he shall burn.

VERS. 5.-- I am smitten as grass, and my heart is withered. (ID.) Made mortal. Grass is green, but when smitten it easily feels the hurt: so the flesh of man, green in the law of God, when cut down by that same law withers away.

VERS. 6.-- From the voice of groaning. (CASS.) The nature of them that sin is shown, because while sin is sought after, 1012Athe contemplation of God is not had. My. (AUG.) Not of those who groan over earthly and not over spiritual things, etc., as far as to bear the weak.

VERS. 7.-- Like a pelican, (AUG.) He sets down three birds, three places, etc., as far as who, if not among men, is outside on high, saying to them that sleep in the night.

Or, the sagacious sparrow flees to the heights of the virtues, where he is safe from the snares. He who is solitary or single, on account of charity (which makes him one out of many), is upon the roof, or upon the building, on account of the height of faith, that he may not come down to take anything out of the house, that is, out of the flesh.

In a dwelling-place. (ID.) Or in ruined walls, which are commonly called ruins, where the walls stand without a roof, where there dwells the night-raven, a bird that loves the night.

VERS. 9.-- All the day. (CASS.) Or, the whole may be taken in the person 1012Bof the just man. As if he should say, etc., as far as or, in my abasement I was refreshed, so much did it please me.

VERS. 10.-- Ashes. (AUG.) By ashes and weeping the penitent are signified. For ashes and haircloth are the arms of penitents. Drink. (CASS.) Temporal delight. Or, I mingled with tears the longing for my homeland because of the delay; or the drink of the Scriptures, which recall ancient things.

VERS. 11.-- From the face of wrath. (CASS.) Wrath is vengeance; indignation is a movement of the soul, by which we are indignant even with our sons. Wrath is called an onset against those who are to be punished, and these do not fall upon God. But it is antropopathos.

Of wrath. Whence the Lord also says: The wrath of God abideth upon them that believe not (Joan. III). He does not say, shall come; but abideth, because it is not taken away, the wrath in which he was born.

1012CVERS. 12.-- My days have declined like a shadow. Because I have declined from the true day, my declining days are like myself.

VERS. 13.-- But thou, etc. (CASS.) The third part, where the certainty of obtaining pardon is shown. Now he that is fallen rises up to prophesy, now the penitent lifts up his head.

(AUG.) The memorial is a promise to be remembered; from thee is our restoring, because thou art mindful of us, or we of thee.

VERS. 14.-- The time is come. (AUG.) Because God willed all things to be done in order, and appointed a time for this, wherein the opportunity is fitly ordered.

VERS. 15.-- The stones thereof. (AUG.) There are stones in Sion, etc., as far as hence it is that, when the Holy Spirit had been sent, many of them believed who had crucified the Lord.

1012DVERS. 17.-- In glory. (AUG.) He who was first seen in weakness in that Sion; whence: We saw him having neither beauty nor comeliness (Isa. LIII).

VERS. 18.-- The prayer. This is done in the building of Sion: they pray, they groan who build, who are one poor man and many poor; whence in the title it stands in the singular, here in the plural. But he is called one because of the truth of the Church's peace, and many because of her breadth.

VERS. 19.-- Let these things be written. (CASS.) He who above was foul with penance, now adorned with the honour of a prophet, commands that these things which he has said be established by the testimony of Scripture, that the age to come may learn them. In the generation. (AUG.) These things, when they were being written, did not so profit the generation 1013Aof the Old Testament; they profit another, that is, the new.

VERS. 20.-- Because he hath looked forth, etc. (AUG.) After the groans of one grieving, now there are words of consolations, now the poor man rejoices. And because he said above: The Lord hath built up Sion; and again: Let these things be written; now he declares both; as if this is what he said was to be written, because he hath looked forth.

He hath looked forth. He speaks as of things past what were yet to come.

VERS. 21.-- Of them that are in fetters. (AUG.) The fear of God: these are the fetters, etc., as far as and when they are loosed, they are turned into glory. (CASS.) They that are fettered, the saints, etc., as far as whence their discourse runs together into the Church universal. That he might loose the children. (AUG.) But we are the children of those slain men, we who are loosed from the knots of sins 1013Band from the chains of desires.

VERS. 23.-- He answered him in the way of his strength. (CASS.) The fourth part, where, after the certainty of pardon, he says that from his own brevity he passes over to eternity. (AUG.) He answered. Because: I speak, that I may declare the name of the Lord and his praise in Jerusalem, etc., as far as he does not despise, but renders fruit. He answered him. That is, he believes that Christ has risen. But because he foresees that some will say, there was indeed once a Church gathering all into one, but now it ceases.

The fewness, he says, of my days: not the eternity of those days where I shall be, but the temporal days, so long as I shall be in this world. Declare unto me. Because of those who say that the Church now is not. That utterance is not idle, that petition is not empty. For the way itself, that is, Christ, 1013Chas thus declared: I am with you unto the consummation of the world (Matth. XXVIII). The whole time unto the end is that scantiness of days: because everything that comes to an end is scant, that from thence there may be a passing over into eternity. Declare and:

VERS. 24.-- Call me not back in the midst of my days. Let it not so come to pass, as the heretics say, etc., as far as but they are nothing but halves, if the eternal ones be not added.

VERS. 25.-- In the way of strength. (AUG.) In the faith by which he believes that Christ has risen. Christ was the way of strength after the resurrection, when, being now not weak but strong, he calls the Church into heaven. The praise of faith is not that it believes him dead, which the Pagan also believes, but that it believes him glorified.

1013DOr, the Christian religion is briefly defined when it is called the way of strength.

Or, in generation of generations. There is a generation of generations which passes not away, gathered out of all, that is, the saints. In it shall be the years of the Lord, which do not pass away, that is, the eternity of God, which is the very substance of God, having nothing mutable.

VERS. 26.-- In the beginning thou, O Lord. As if: call me not back, because I tend toward eternity, which he expounds, saying: In the beginning thou, O Lord, didst found the earth.

VERS. 27.-- They shall perish. (AUG.) The heavens themselves shall perish; of those nearest the earth this is certain; whence Peter also: But the earth and the heavens which now are, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire (II Petr. III). Of the higher ones 1014Ait is not certain, but if they remain, they remain not in themselves, but in God.

VERS. 28.-- And as a covering thou shalt change them. Understand the heavens, which cover all things, which also shall be changed. And thy years shall not fail. (AUG.) Which shall be in the generation of generations. But shall we be able to be there? Assuredly, because the children of thy servants shall dwell.

VERS. 29.-- The children of the servants. (AUG.) As the children entered the land of promise, etc., as far as with all the newness of the children.

The children. A cheerful conclusion. The children of the prophets and of the apostles, not to speak of those themselves.

The seed. Works, whence eternal fruit.

Shall be directed. Because nothing crooked enters in.

PSALMUS CII.

  • 1014B

VERS. 2.-- Benedic, anima. (AUG.) Post preces pauperis praeconia gaudentis. Omnes qui in Christo quasi unus homo sunt, qui excitat et hortatur animam suam, ut benedicat Dominum, volens diffinire cur benedicendus, ne quis ad hoc piger inveniatur. Clama voce, si est homo qut audiat; sine voce, si non est qui audiat homo, quia audit Deus. (CASS.) Per sua beneficia hortatur benedicere Deum. (AUG.) Propheta in persona generalis justi loquens, secundum superiorem vim animae, id est rationem, exhortatur animam ad benedicendum, dicens: Noli oblivisci. Non sit ante oculos delectatio peccati, sed damnatio et remissio Dei: cogita omnia mala tua, 1014Cquia quot ea, tot bonae retributiones Dei. Retributiones. Non tributiones. Tribuit homo mala pro bonis, et retribuit ei Deus bona pro malis. Tribuit, cum me fecit, retribuit cum justificat.

VERS. 3.-- Qui propitiatur. (AUG.) Hoc agit in baptismi sacramento. Qui sanat omnes infirmitates tuas. Hoc agit in vita fidelis hominis, dum concupiscit caro adversus spiritum, ut si quae nolumus faciamus; qui languores vetustatis de die in diem crescente novitate sanantur ex fide, quae per dilectionem operatur.

VERS. 4.-- Qui redimit, de corruptione vitam tuam. Hoc fit in ultima resurrectione mortuorum. Qui coronat, etc. Hoc fit judicio, ubi cum rex sederit in throno, redditurus unicuique secundum opera 1014Dejus, quis gloriabitur se habere gloriosum cor et mundum a peccato? Ideo necessarium fuit commemorare illic misericordiam et miserationes, ubi viderentur sic reddi debita, ut nullus esset locus misericordiae.

VERS. 5.-- Ut aquilae juventus tua. (AUG.) Similitudo tanta data est, etc., usque ad quibus vetustas clausit os, oblitis manducare panem nostrum.

VERS. 6.-- Faciens. (AUG.) Secunda pars, ubi monet benedicere par eas quae antiquis facta sunt, et posteris fiunt. Misericordias. Quas consequentur, qui inimicos diligunt, etc., usque ad post misericordiam enim subdit de judicio, dicens, Et judicium.

1015AVERS. 7.-- Moysi. (AUG.) Per Moysen omnes sanctos, etc., usque ad per quem legem dedit, ut abundaret dilectum.

VERS. 11.-- Quoniam. (ID.) Coelum undique circa terram unde etiam peccantibus lux, aer, spiritus, pluvia, unde fructus: sine coelo desinit terra, sic protectio Dei super timentes.

VERS. 12.-- Quantum distat, etc. (ID.) Quando peccatum remittitur, occidunt peccata, gratia oritur, peccata in occasu, avertere ergo ab occasu peccatorum, et tende ad ortum gratiae, et surgis.

VERS. 14.-- Recordatus est, etc. (ID.) Vel secundam aliam litteram: Memento, quoniam pulvis sumus. Quasi diceret: Cognovit figmentum, id est infirmitatem nostram: quod figmentum conversus 1015Bad Deum dicit: Memento quia pulvis sumus, id est perseveret erga nos tua misericordia, ne obliviscamur gratiae tuae. Vel, Homo sicut fenum, etc. Homo enim sicut flos egreditur, etc., usque ad Misericordia Domini. Efflorebit (CASS.) Id est, ad plus sic florebit vel efflorebit, id est deflorebit. Et sic est intentivum, vel privativum.

VERS. 16.-- Quoniam spiritus pertransivit in illo. Et non subsistet.

VERS. 17.-- Et justitia. (AUG.) Misericordia et justitia retributio est. Dicit, super filios filiorum; multi justi non habent filios, nedum filios filiorum, sed filii sunt opera; filii filiorum merces operum.

VERS. 19.-- Dominus in coelo paravit sedem suam. (CASS.) Praedicat judicium futurum, ne peccantes insolescant; 1015Cquasi, et debes esse memor ut facias quia Dominus in coelo.

VERS. 21.-- Benedicite Domino, omnes angeli ejus, potentes. (ID.) Tertio monet coelestes et omnes alias creaturas benedicere. Benedicite Domino, etc. Aggratulando dicit, non imperando, vel monendo. Ministri ejus. (AUG.) Vos benedicite, etc., usque ad ut quod habet in ore ostendat in opere.

PSALM CII.

  • 1014B

VERS. 2.-- Bless, O soul. (AUG.) After the prayers of the poor man, the proclamations of one rejoicing. All who are in Christ are as it were one man, who rouses and exhorts his own soul to bless the Lord, wishing to define why he is to be blessed, lest any be found slothful thereto. Cry with the voice, if there is a man who qut hears; without voice, if there is no man to hear, because God hears. (CASS.) By his own benefits he exhorts men to bless God. (AUG.) The prophet, speaking in the person of the just man in general, according to the higher power of the soul, that is, the reason, exhorts the soul to bless, saying: Forget not. Let not the delight of sin be before thine eyes, but the condemnation and the remission of God: think over all thine evils, 1014Cbecause as many as they are, so many are the good retributions of God. Retributions. Not bestowings. Man bestows evils for goods, and God requites him with goods for evils. He bestowed when he made me, he requites when he justifies.

VERS. 3.-- Who forgiveth. (AUG.) This he does in the sacrament of baptism. Who healeth all thy diseases. This he does in the life of a faithful man, while the flesh lusts against the spirit, so that we do such things as we would not; and those languors of the old state are healed from day to day, as newness increases, out of the faith which works through love.

VERS. 4.-- Who redeemeth thy life from corruption. This is done in the last resurrection of the dead. Who crowneth, etc. This is done at the judgment, where, when the king shall sit upon his throne, about to render to every man according to his works 1014D, who shall boast that he has a heart glorious and clean from sin? Therefore it was necessary to make mention of mercy and of compassions in that place where dues would seem to be so rendered that there should be no room left for mercy.

VERS. 5.-- Thy youth like the eagle's. (AUG.) So great a likeness is set down, etc., as far as whose mouth old age has closed, who have forgotten to eat our bread.

VERS. 6.-- He that doeth. (AUG.) The second part, where he admonishes men to bless like [par; read per, "through"] those things which were done for the men of old, and are done for those that come after. Mercies. Which they shall obtain who love their enemies, etc., as far as for after mercy he adds concerning judgment, saying, And judgment.

1015AVERS. 7.-- To Moses. (AUG.) By Moses, all the saints, etc., as far as through whom he gave the law, that the beloved [dilectum; read delictum, "the offence"] might abound.

VERS. 11.-- For. (ID.) The heaven is on every side about the earth, whence there is even for them that sin light, air, breath, rain, whence fruit: without heaven the earth comes to an end, so is the protection of God over them that fear him.

VERS. 12.-- How far distant, etc. (ID.) When sin is forgiven, sins set, grace rises, sins are in their setting; turn thyself away, therefore, from the setting of sins, and stretch toward the rising of grace, and thou risest.

VERS. 14.-- He hath remembered, etc. (ID.) Or a second [secundam; read secundum, "according to"] other reading: Remember that we are dust. As if he should say: He knew our frame, that is, our weakness: which frame, being turned 1015Bto God, says: Remember that we are dust, that is, let thy mercy persevere toward us, lest we forget thy grace. Or, Man is as grass, etc. For man goes forth as a flower, etc., as far as The mercy of the Lord. He shall flourish forth (CASS.) That is, at the most he shall thus flourish or flourish forth, that is, shall shed his flower. And so it is either intensive or privative.

VERS. 16.-- For the spirit shall pass in him. And he shall not abide.

VERS. 17.-- And justice. (AUG.) Mercy and justice are a retribution. He says, upon the children's children; many just men have no children, much less children's children, but the children are works; the children's children are the wages of works.

VERS. 19.-- The Lord hath prepared his seat in heaven. (CASS.) He proclaims the judgment to come, lest they that sin grow insolent; 1015Cas if: and thou oughtest to be mindful, so as to act, because the Lord is in heaven.

VERS. 21.-- Bless the Lord, all ye his angels, ye mighty. (ID.) In the third place he admonishes the heavenly beings and all other creatures to bless. Bless the Lord, etc. He speaks by way of congratulation, not by way of command or of admonition. His ministers. (AUG.) Bless ye, etc., as far as that what he has in his mouth he may show forth in his work.

PSALMUS CIII.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus David. (CASS.) Item benedicere Deus monet, primo per coelum et terram et ornatum eorum. (AUG.) Etsi vere hic omnia ad litteram possunt religiose accipi, etc., usque ad in omnibus spiritualis sensus quaerendus est. Benedic, anima mea, 1015DDomino, etc., mugnificatus. In notitia, quia semper magnus natura, qui non putes crescere vel minui, quia perfectus es; Confessionem, id est undique habes creaturas, quae te confitentur, et quae sunt decorae et luminosae. Vel, decor in essentia Dei, et lux undique. (CASS.) Vel incarnationem significat, per quam confessio et decus supernae majestatis innotuit, et homines eum confessi sunt, qui sunt lumen cognitione. (AUG.) Confessionem induisti, id est Ecclesiam, etc., usque ad et vestis sine macula et ruga.

VERS. 2.-- Extendens coelum sic. (CASS.) Quae confitentur? coelum, terra, mare, cum omni ornatu suo de quibus singulis subsequenter. (AUG.) Extendens 1016Acoelum sicut. Ad litteram, coelum, quasi tectum, etc., usque ad post in fine ut liber Scriptura plicabitur.

VERS. 3.-- Qui tegis. (ID.) Ad litteram sunt aquae, etc., usque ad cujus superiora sunt duo praecepta charitatis. Vel qui tegis aquis, id est, spirituali sensu, superficiem Scripturae, vel donis spiritualibus eorum munis charitatem, ne quid eos separare possit. Super pennas ventorum, etc. Ventus est motus aeris, etc., usque ad sed charitatem omnium superat charitas Christi.

VERS. 4.-- Ignem urentem. (CASS.) Id est seraphim, qui sunt superior ordo, facis ministros tuos, unde in Isaia: Volavit ad me unus de seraphim qui sunt superior ordo.

VERS. 5.-- Qui fundasti terram super stabilitatem 1016Bsuam. (ID.) Ideo Spiritus sanctus in hoc psalmo difficilia dicit secundum litteram, ut quaeramus spiritualia.

VERS. 7.-- A voce tonitrui. (ID.) Per terribiles ventos siccabuntur aquae; mali comminatione judicii timebunt.

VERS. 8.-- Ascendunt. (AUG.) Mali, ut montes, etc., usque ad ut liceat Ecclesiae libere praedicare (CASS.) Superbos permittit Deus, etc., usque ad ut jam mundum non occupent.

VERS. 10.-- In convallibus. (AUG.) De humilibus subditis gratiae et si sunt montes spirituali altitudine, fluunt fontes Spiritus sancti, qui super humilem quiescit. Inter medium. (ID.) Id est inter medium, etc., usque ad et hic talis mons non est audiendus.

1016CVERS. 11.-- Potabunt omnes. (ID.) Omnes fuerunt in disco Petri ter submisso, etc., usque ad ut Ecclesia congregetur. Onagri. (ID.) Sylvestres asini magni indomiti, etc., usque ad vel superbi Judaei different bibere in tempus ultimum.

VERS. 12.-- Super ea volucres coeli. (ID.) Non omnes aves manent, etc., usque ad alii in sinistra damnantur.

VERS. 15.-- De fructu operum tuorum. (ID.) Nemo ergo glorietur in operibus suis, sed qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur, gratia enim Dei saturatur terra. Sic igitur gratia gratis datur. Si operibus hominum redditur, merces dicitur.

VERS. 14.-- Servituti hominum. (ID.) Unde cum liber essem ex omnibus, omnium me feci servum, etc., 1016Dusque ad quibus praebuit exemplum necessaria sumendi a subditis. In oleo. Unicuique datur Spiritus ad manifestationem: gratia ergo et nitor quidam, etc., usque ad ut exhilaretur facies in oleo. Et panis. Idem est ergo panis et vinum. Panis enim iste et vinum, justitia est, veritas est Christus: et hic et illud laetificat, et confirmat cor.

VERS. 16.-- Quas plantavit. (ID.) Cur a se plantatis relinquit candorem saeculi? quia illic fulica avis, quae in aquis habitat; hi sunt qui in baptismi gratia permanent. Vel, Herodius avis rapacissima, nec tales Christus respuit.

VERS. 17.-- Illic passeres. (ID.) Minuta volatilia, etc., usque ad ut in cedris Libani nidificent. Herodii 1017Adomus. (AUG.) Dux est eorum passerum, vel cedrorum, quod tamen Latine dici non potest, quia cedri feminini generis sunt, hoc autem nullo modo ad litteram, domus enim, id est, nidus fulicae, quae est avis marina vel stagnensis, quomodo dux est passerum? sed per hoc innuit spiritualia esse quaerenda. Et si in divitibus saeculi passeres nidificent, etc., usque ad sed non peribunt, quia petra est dux eorum. (CASS.) Vel fulica avis, quae in aquis habitat, hi sunt qui in gratia baptismi permanent, quorum domus est baptismus. Et est quasi diceret: Qui sunt passeres? Illi qui baptizantur. Et hoc est, fulicae domus, id est, baptismus, qui est domus regeneratorum dux est eorum passerum, id est, Christianorum.

(HIER., CASS.) Herodius; avis rapacissima, etc., 1017Busque ad quia ipse conversus alios plures ad fidem convertit. Cervis: petra. (AUG.) Cervi sunt magni spirituales, etc., usque ad haec est de qua (ut supra dictum est) volucres coeli dant voces.

VERS. 19.-- Fecit lunam. (CASS.) Post terrena transit ad coelestia, quae tamen terrae faciunt, id est, serviunt. Post tot genera Christianorum, quae per animalia significavit, et praedictam ordinationem, ascendens subjungit de Christo et Ecclesia, quomodo scilicet hic temporalis Ecclesia crescit et decrescit, quasi faciat occasus et ortus veri solis.

VERS. 20.-- Posuisti, etc. Et facta est nox in eis, id est obscura mentis obstinatio. Et ipsa pertransibunt. (AUG.) Non ut supra, conversi, gentiles, sed daemones, qui tempore passionis invenerunt corda 1017Ctitubantium apostolorum; sed Christo surgente, quia in omnibus non possunt, in cubilibus, id est, cordibus pertinacium permanent: sic Christo in aliquo occidente, vigent mala, resurgente fugiunt. Occasum. Sol sic occidit, ut oriatur: ita qui dormit, id est, Christus, non adjiciet ut resurgat? Occidit, quia voluit, nemo tollit animam ejus; cum occidit, tenebrae factae sunt in apostolis, defecit spes eorum.

VERS. 21.-- Catuli leonum, etc. (AUG.) Sunt et principes daemoniorum, sicut et catuli contemptibilia daemonia, quae in tenebris quaerunt seducere animas; major leo semper circumit quaerens quem devoret (I Pet. V), pascuntur autem erroribus hominum.

VERS. 22.-- Ortus est sol, etc. (CASS.) Postquam 1017Ddixit quid fecit occasus veri solis, subdit de ortu.

VERS. 24.-- Possessione. (AUG.) Alias creatura. (ID.) Per Christum Pater, etc., usque ad datum est tamen lignum in quo transnavigemus.

VERS. 25.-- Hoc mare magnum, etc. (CASS.) Secunda pars ubi dicit: Quomodo Ecclesiam per mare saeculi traducit ad littus patriae. Reptilia, etc. (AUG.) Mali spiritus, quorum insidiae serpunt.

VERS. 26.-- Draco iste quem formasti. (ID.) Praeter haec animalia, etc., usque ad factus est in malitia major. Ad illudendum. (ID.) Dicitur in Job (Job XL), illudi Satanae ab angelis Dei, qui sunt praepositi super aereas potestates, ne noceant nobis.

VERS. 27.-- Escam. (ID.) Cibus draconis terra est, 1018Aquia dictum est ei: Terram comedes omnibus diebus vitae meae (Gen. III). Quia qui terrena amant, cibus diaboli sunt. Cibus autem justi verbum Dei, unde, Non in solo pane vivit homo, sed in omni verbo quod procedit de ore Dei (Deut. VIII).

VERS. 28.-- Manum tuam, omnia implebuntur bonitate. (CASS.) Vel manus est potestas quae abunde replet omnia.

VERS. 29.-- Avertente autem. (AUG.) Multi impleti bonitate, sibi tribuerunt; volens autem Deus eis probare quod non a se habent, sed a Deo, ut cum bonitate habeant humilitatem, aliquando eos perturbat, avertit faciem, et cadunt in tentationem.

VERS. 30.-- Emitte spiritum tuum. (CASS.) Pulvis suus illorum dicitur, quia ex se habent quod sunt 1018Bpulvis. Spiritus vero Domini: Ecce medicina reversis in pulverem.

VERS. 32.-- Tremere. (AUG.) Melior est tremor humilitatis, quam confidentia superbiae. Unde Apostolus: Cum tremore operamini vestram salutem (Phil. II). Montes. (ID.) Qui superbi erant, jactantes a se omnia. Quemadmodum accidit in monte Sina.

VERS. 33.-- Cantabo. (CASS.) Tertia pars, ubi promittit se semper cantaturum. Quasi diceret: Haec praedicta fecit Dominus, et his inspectis. In vita mea. (AUG.) Praesenti et futura; spei et speciei. Modo spes est vita nostra, post aeterna erit. Vita vitae mortalis, spes est vitae immortalis. Quandiu sum. (ID.) Quia in illo sine fine sum, psallam quandiu sum, ne putetur alius actus illius vitae, quam psallere: 1018Cquia non potest venire in fastidium, qui laudatur, non venit in fastidium laudare; sed semper amatur, semper laudatur.

VERS. 34.-- Jucundum sit. Alia littera: Suavis sit ei disputatio mea. (AUG.) Disputatio enim hominis ad Deum, est confessio peccatorum. Unde Isaia (Isa. I). Auferte nequitias ab animabus vestris, dicite benefacere, judicate pupillo, et venite et disputemus, dicit Dominus. Disputatio ergo tua, sacrificium humilitatis tuae, quod est Deo suave.

VERS. 35.-- Benedic, anima mea, Domino. (ID.) Iterat quod in principio psalmi: Benedic, anima mea, Domino, per hoc innuens, quod finis bonorum similis sit principio.

PSALM CIII.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of David. (CASS.) Likewise God [Deus; read Deum, "to bless God"] admonishes men to bless, first through heaven and earth and their adornment. (AUG.) Although indeed all things here may be devoutly taken according to the letter, etc., as far as in all things the spiritual sense is to be sought. Bless the Lord, 1015DO my soul, etc., magnified. mugnificatus In knowledge, because thou art always great by nature, who thinkest [putes; read potes, "thou canst"] not to grow or be lessened, because thou art perfect; Confession, that is, thou hast on every side creatures which confess thee, and which are comely and full of light. Or, comeliness is in the essence of God, and light on every side. (CASS.) Or it signifies the incarnation, through which the confession and the glory of the heavenly majesty became known, and men confessed him, who are light by knowledge. (AUG.) Thou hast put on confession, that is, the Church, etc., as far as and a garment without spot or wrinkle.

VERS. 2.-- Stretching out the heaven thus. (CASS.) What things confess him? Heaven, earth, sea, with all their adornment; of each of these in what follows. (AUG.) Stretching out 1016Athe heaven like. According to the letter, the heaven, as it were a roof, etc., as far as afterwards at the end, like a book, Scripture shall be folded up.

VERS. 3.-- Who coverest. (ID.) According to the letter they are waters, etc., as far as whose upper parts are the two precepts of charity. Or thou who coverest with waters, that is, with the spiritual sense, the surface of Scripture; or by spiritual gifts thou fortifiest their charity, that nothing may be able to separate them. Upon the wings of the winds, etc. Wind is a movement of the air, etc., as far as but the charity of Christ surpasses the charity of all.

VERS. 4.-- A burning fire. (CASS.) That is, the seraphim, who are the higher order, thou makest thy ministers, whence in Isaiah: There flew to me one of the seraphim, who are the higher order.

VERS. 5.-- Who hast founded the earth upon its own 1016Bstability. (ID.) Therefore the Holy Spirit in this psalm speaks things difficult according to the letter, that we may seek spiritual things.

VERS. 7.-- At the voice of thunder. (ID.) By terrible winds the waters shall be dried up; the wicked shall fear at the threatening of the judgment.

VERS. 8.-- They ascend. (AUG.) The wicked, as mountains, etc., as far as that the Church may be free to preach. (CASS.) God permits the proud, etc., as far as that they may no longer take possession of the world.

VERS. 10.-- In the valleys. (AUG.) From the humble, made subject to grace, even if they are mountains by spiritual height, flow the fountains of the Holy Spirit, who rests upon the humble. Between the midst. (ID.) That is, between the midst, etc., as far as and such a mountain as this is not to be heard.

1016CVERS. 11.-- All shall drink. (ID.) All were in the dish let down thrice to Peter, etc., as far as that the Church may be gathered. Wild asses. (ID.) Great untamed asses of the woods, etc., as far as or the proud Jews shall put off drinking until the last time.

VERS. 12.-- Over them the birds of the air. (ID.) Not all birds abide, etc., as far as others on the left hand are condemned.

VERS. 15.-- VERS. 15. Of the fruit of thy works. (ID.) Let no man therefore glory in his own works, but he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord, for by the grace of God the earth is filled. Thus therefore grace is given freely. If it is rendered to the works of men, it is called a wage.

VERS. 14.-- For the service of men. (ID.) Whence whereas I was free from all, I made myself the servant of all, etc., 1016Das far as to whom he gave an example of taking necessary things from those subject to them. In oil. To every man is given the Spirit unto manifestation: [Vulg. 1 Cor. 12:7 Unicuique autem datur manifestatio Spiritus ad utilitatem, "to every man the manifestation of the Spirit is given unto profit"] grace, therefore, and a certain brightness, etc., as far as that the face may be made glad with oil. And bread. Bread, therefore, and wine are the same thing. For this bread and wine is justice, is truth, is Christ: and both the one and the other gladdens and strengthens the heart.

VERS. 16.-- Which he hath planted. (ID.) Why does he leave the brightness of the world to those planted by himself? Because there is the coot, a bird which dwells in the waters; these are they who abide in the grace of baptism. Or, the heron is a most rapacious bird, and such as these Christ does not reject.

VERS. 17.-- There the sparrows. (ID.) Small flying things, etc., as far as that they may build their nests in the cedars of Libanus. The heron's 1017Ahouse. (AUG.) Is the leader of them, that is, of the sparrows, or of the cedars, which nevertheless cannot be said in Latin, because cedars are of the feminine gender; and this in no way holds according to the letter, for how is the house, that is, the nest of the coot, which is a bird of the sea or of the marsh, the leader of sparrows? But by this he hints that spiritual things are to be sought. And if the sparrows build their nests among the rich of this world, etc., as far as but they shall not perish, because the rock is their leader. (CASS.) Or the coot is a bird which dwells in the waters; these are they who abide in the grace of baptism, whose house is baptism. And it is as if he should say: Who are the sparrows? Those who are baptized. And this is it, the coot's house, that is, baptism, which is the house of the regenerate, is the leader of them, that is, of the sparrows, that is, of the Christians.

(HIER., CASS.) The heron: a most rapacious bird, etc., 1017Bas far as because he himself, being converted, converted many others to the faith. For the harts: a rock. (AUG.) The harts are great spiritual men, etc., as far as this is that from which (as was said above) the birds of the air give their voices.

VERS. 19.-- He hath made the moon. (CASS.) After earthly things he passes over to the heavenly, which nevertheless act for the earth, that is, serve it. After so many kinds of Christians, which he signified by the animals, and after the aforesaid ordering, ascending he adds concerning Christ and the Church, namely how the Church here in time waxes and wanes, as though she made the settings and risings of the true sun.

VERS. 20.-- Thou hast appointed, etc. And night was made in them, that is, the dark obstinacy of the mind. And these shall pass through. (AUG.) Not, as above, the converted, the Gentiles, but the demons, who at the time of the passion found the hearts 1017Cof the wavering apostles; but when Christ rose again, because they cannot prevail in all, they abide in the dens, that is, in the hearts of the obstinate: so, when Christ sets in some man, evils grow strong; when he rises again, they flee. The setting. The sun so sets that it may rise: shall he then that sleeps, that is, Christ, not go on to rise again? He set because he willed it, no man takes away his life; when he set, darkness came upon the apostles, their hope failed.

VERS. 21.-- The young lions, etc. (AUG.) There are also princes of the demons, as the whelps too are contemptible demons, which in the darkness seek to seduce souls; the greater lion always goeth about seeking whom he may devour (I Pet. V), and they are fed with the errors of men.

VERS. 22.-- The sun is risen, etc. (CASS.) After 1017Dhe has said what the setting of the true sun did, he adds concerning the rising.

VERS. 24.-- With possession. (AUG.) Elsewhere, creature. (ID.) Through Christ the Father, etc., as far as yet the wood was given, upon which we might sail across.

VERS. 25.-- This great sea, etc. (CASS.) The second part, where he says: How he leads the Church across the sea of this world to the shore of the homeland. Creeping things, etc. (AUG.) Evil spirits, whose snares creep.

VERS. 26.-- This dragon which thou hast formed. (ID.) Besides these animals, etc., as far as he was made greater in malice. For mocking. (ID.) It is said in Job (Job XL) that Satan is mocked by the angels of God, who are set over the powers of the air, that they may not hurt us.

VERS. 27.-- Meat. (ID.) The dragon's food is earth, 1018Abecause it was said to him: Thou shalt eat earth all the days of my life (Gen. III). [Vulg. Gen. 3:14 cunctis diebus vitae tuae, "all the days of thy life"] Because they that love earthly things are the devil's food. But the food of the just man is the word of God, whence, Not in bread alone doth man live, but in every word that proceedeth from the mouth of God (Deut. VIII).

VERS. 28.-- Thy hand, all things shall be filled with good. (CASS.) Or the hand is the power which abundantly fills all things.

VERS. 29.-- But when thou turnest away. (AUG.) Many, being filled with good, have ascribed it to themselves; but God, willing to prove to them that they have it not from themselves but from God, so that with the good they may have humility, sometimes troubles them, turns away his face, and they fall into temptation.

VERS. 30.-- Send forth thy spirit. (CASS.) The dust is called theirs, because from themselves they have it that they are 1018Bdust. But the Spirit is the Lord's: behold the medicine for those returned into dust.

VERS. 32.-- To tremble. (AUG.) Better is the trembling of humility than the confidence of pride. Whence the Apostle: With trembling work out your salvation (Phil. II). The mountains. (ID.) Those who were proud, boasting that all things came from themselves. Even as it happened on mount Sina.

VERS. 33.-- I will sing. (CASS.) The third part, where he promises that he will sing always. As if he should say: These foretold things the Lord has done, and these being beheld. In my life. (AUG.) Present and to come; of hope and of sight. Now hope is our life, afterwards it shall be eternal. The life of mortal life is the hope of immortal life. As long as I am. (ID.) Because in him I am without end, I will sing psalms as long as I am, lest any other act of that life be supposed than to sing psalms: 1018Cbecause he who is praised cannot come to be wearisome, it does not become wearisome to praise him; but he is ever loved, ever praised.

VERS. 34.-- Let it be pleasant. Another reading: Let my disputation be sweet to him. (AUG.) For the disputation of man with God is the confession of sins. Whence Isaiah (Isa. I). Take away the wickednesses from your souls, say ye to do well, judge for the fatherless, and come and let us dispute, saith the Lord. [Vulg. Isa. 1:16-18 auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis … discite benefacere … et venite, et arguite me, dicit Dominus, "learn to do well … and come and reprove me"] Thy disputation, therefore, is the sacrifice of thy humility, which is sweet to God.

VERS. 35.-- Bless the Lord, O my soul. (ID.) He repeats what stood at the beginning of the psalm: Bless the Lord, O my soul, hinting by this that the end of good men is like the beginning.

PSALMUS CIV.

  • 1018D

VERS. 1.-- Alleluia. (CASS.) Hic primo alleluia, nec ante a quoquam situm est, quod nulla lingua praesumpsit mutare. Alleluia, laudate. Ia nomen Dei invisibilis, quod ei tantum convenit. Per viginti psalmos, quibus hic titulus est, magnalia Dei dicuntur, et magna in eis est exsultatio. (CASS.) Hic commendat propheta bonos in illo populo Israel, qui cum aliis fidelibus sunt verum semen Abrahae, filii promissionis.

Confitemini Domino. (AUG.) Primus psalmus cui praenotatur alleluia, etc., usque ad quae temporalia misericordia Dei eis dedit, supponit.

VERS. 2.-- Omnia: (CASS.) omnia; nihil est pudore 1019Asilendum. Vel omnia, quae dicent, mirabilia sunt, nullus enim potest omnia narrare.

VERS. 3.-- Laudamini in nomine, id est, gaudete Christiani dici a Christo.

(AUG.) Laudamini, non vetat laudari, si boni; si non, nisi in Domino, qui bonos facit. Laudamini in nomine. Quod alibi, In Domino laudabitur anima mea: quod ibi addit, audiant mansueti et laetentur: hic quoque quodammodo, laetetur cor, quasi dicat,

VERS. 4.-- Faciem, etc. (ID.) Id est praesentiam, etc., usque ad malus timere potest praesentiam, quam bonus amat. (HIER.) A martyre Hyppolito, etc., usque ad ibi ex gentibus sumpturus Ecclesiam.

VERS. 5.-- Mementote et caetera. (AUG.) Quaerite 1019Bipsum, etc., usque ad si id quod Deus est, magnum est quaerere, vel quae fecit videte. Prodigia, etc. (ID.) Paulatim ascendit de prodigiis visibilibus ad judicia: inde ad aeternum testamentum, ubi et praeceptum et promissum.

VERS. 7.-- In universa terra. (ID.) Non putes filios Abrahae in una gente secundum carnem, quia in universa terra sunt Jacob et Israel, quibus judicia sua manifestat, sed non alii genti.

VERS. 8.-- In saeculum, (ID.) id est, in aeternum, unde post, in testamentum aeternum. Quod testamentum si Vetus accipitur propter terram Chanaam, de qua sequitur. Quomodo aeternum est, cum illa terrena haereditas non possit esse aeterna? Testamenti. Dicitur enim testamentum illud quod 1019Cpromittitur, et doctrina, in qua promissio declaratur, et pro qua servata redditur. (ID.) Promissum est quod accipere debemus: Mandatum quod facere. Haec est fides, ut justus ex fide vivat, et huic fidei promittitur haere ditas. Abraham, Isaac et Jacob. Ecce tres patriarchae, quorum specialiter se dicit Deum: Ego sum Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac, Deus Jacob. Ecce triplex auctoritas.

VERS. 10.-- In testamentum aeternum, (ID.) id est, quod ex ipso verbo impleto, etc., usque ad et manet filius in domo in aeternum.

VERS. 11.-- Terram Chanaan, (CASS.) id est, quod ab ea significatur: dedit enim etiam hanc terram in figuram aeternae haereditatis (I Joan. IV). (AUG.) Congrue haereditas aeterna dicitur terra Chanaam, 1019Dquia ab ea servi repelluntur et filii recipiuntur.

VERS. 12.-- Cum essent numero. (CASS.) Quae subsidia temporalis vitae praestitit patribus et filiis eorum tam carne, quam fide, non ut his haereant, sed ea ad bonum aeternum referant, quod est, ut his allecti, justificationes et legem Dei requirant.

VERS. 13.-- De regno. (AUG.) Non quod tunc esset, sed quod futurum esset regnum Israel.

VERS. 15.-- Nolite tangere. (ID.) Haec verba, licet in historia non sint, tamen vel latenter dixit ea Deus in cordibus hominum, vel per angelum. Christos, (ID.) quia jam tunc Christiani, etsi latenter, unde Abraham exsultavit, ut videret diem meum, vidit et 1020Agavisus est (Joan. VIII). Nullus enim praeter hanc fidem, vel ante, vel post, Deo reconciliatus est, unus enim mediator Christus (I Tim. II).

VERS. 16.-- Et vocavit. (AUG.) Quarta pars ubi incipit narrare, etc., usque ad jussit esse quae jam erat in dispositione. Ita vocavit, et omne firmamentum panis contritum (Gen. XXXVII).

VERS. 17.-- Virum. (ID.) Joseph venditus a fratribus, postea in Aegypto pro justitia sublimatus est. Joseph. (ID.) Si Joseph et humiliatus et exaltatus, etc., usque ad sed primum quaerite regnum Dei, et omnia adjicientur.

VERS. 18.-- In compedibus. (ID.) Non legimus de compedibus Joseph in Genesi, sed credendum est quod ibi praetermissum, dicit Spiritus in psalmo. 1020B(CASS.) Et si gratiam habuerit apud custodem carceris, tamen prius anxiatus. Sequitur. Ferrum pertransiit, etc. Quasi praeter mala corporis, ferrum, id est tribulatio durae necessitatis, quae in aestuante et sollicita anima erat, pertransiit, etc. Vel secundum aliam litteram, anima ejus pertransiit ferrum, id est tribulationem durae necessitatis. Idem sensus cum priore.

VERS. 23.-- In terra Cham, etc. (AUG.) Cham pater Chanaan, de quo Aegyptii trahunt originem.

VERS. 24.-- Et auxit populum suum, etc. (ID.) Quinta pars. Ecce quae in Aegypto gesta, breviter proponit, quae postea pleniter narrat. Dicit etiam, quomodo firmavit populum suum super inimicos suos.

1020CEt firmavit eum. Per signa Moysi scilicet, ante enim masculini fetus filiorum Israel necabantur, et ipsi in faciendis lateribus conterebantur. Sed postea in manu potenti, et per signa et portenta Domini, metuendi et honorandi facti sunt.

VERS. 25.-- Convertit. (ID.) Quomodo hoc factum sit narrare incipit. Convertit, non quod Deus sit auctor mali, sed malis bene utitur, dum auxit felicitatem Israel, illi ad invidendum conversi sunt, quia jam mali erant. Ut odirent. Invidia est odium felicitatis alienae.

VERS. 26.-- Misit. Qui omnia per se poterat ut doceret, qua moderatione haec egisset. Quem elegit ipsum. (ID.) Sufficeret dicere, quem elegit: sed nihil 1020Dquaerendum est in eo, quod addidit, ipsum, sed consuetudo divinae locutionis est ad explanationem.

VERS. 27.-- Verba signorum suorum. (ID.) Quibus ab eis praedicabatur, etc., usque ad verba ergo non vocum, sed signorum, vel prodigiorum per eos fecit.

VERS. 28.--(ID.) Vel: Exacerbaverunt sermones ejus, quod apertum est. Vel, non exacerbaverunt Moyses et Aaron sermones ejus, quia illos, scilicet Aegyptios, etiam durissimos, patienter tulerunt, propter mandatum Domini, donec omnia in eis, quae Dominus disposuit, fierent. Tenebras, etc. (CASS.) Inter plagas passi sunt. Sed hic dicit corda eorum obscurata, qui praecepta Dei spernebant. Competens 1021Ainitium plagarum caecitas, sine qua non incurrissent caetera.

VERS. 29.-- Convertit aquas. (AUG.) Secunda plaga, quae in Exodo prima, quae signabat, quod aquas maris Rubri verteret et eis in mortem.

VERS. 30.-- Edidit terra. (AUG.) Terram eorum convertit in ranas, quia tot fuerunt, ut hoc congrue per hyperbolen dicatur.

VERS. 31.-- Dixit, et venit cynomya, etc. (ID.) In verbo enim ejus erant sine tempore, antequam fierent in tempore per ipsum verbum: vel per angelos, vel per Moysen quodammodo dixit, ut fieret tunc, cum fuerat faciendum.

VERS. 32.-- Posuit pluvias eorum, etc. (ID.) Simile est illi, et dedit terra eorum ranas.

1021BVERS. 34.-- Locusta et bruchus. (ID.) Una plaga locusta et bruchus, quia altera est parens, altera fetus.

VERS. 36.-- Et percussit.(Id. ) Cum sint decem plagae, etc., usque ad qui non possent spernere laborum suorum mercedem, licet temporalem.

VERS. 37.-- Et eduxit eos, etc. Sexta pars secundum Cassiodorum et Augustinum. Superius, quae mala intulit inimicis Israelitarum justitia Dei dixit: nunc quae bona eis temporalia misericordia Dei dedit, supponit ut hic adjuti legem Dei quaerant. (AUG.) Et eduxit: Abrahae dixit Deus, etc., usque ad deinde sequitur secundum beneficium, Ft non erat infirmus, et caetera.

VERS. 38.-- Quia incubuit timor eorum super 1021Ceos. Timebat Israel, ne reliquias eorum consumeret.

(AUG.) Hic impletum est quod superius ait, et firmavit eum super inimicum ejus.

VERS. 39.-- Expandit nubem in protectione eorum. Et haec est secunda pars, secundum Augustinum, ubi supponit quae temporalia bona misericordia Dei eis dedit, dictis superius malis quae inimicis eorum justitia Dei intulit.

(AUG.) Jam incipit beneficia, quae iter agentibus in eremo facta sunt.

VERS. 40.-- Petierunt, (AUG.) boni ad sustentationem infirmorum. Coturnix: et pane coeli saturavit eos: quae est et caro, quia hic non de amaricatione iniquorum, sed de fide electorum loquitur: ipsi intelligendi 1021Dsunt petisse, unde amaricantium murmura premerentur.

VERS. 42.-- Quoniam memor fuit verbi sancti sui. (ID.) His omnibus beneficiis Deus commendat in Abraham meritum fidei, unde subdit: quoniam memor fuit.

VERS. 44.-- Et dedit illis. (AUG.) Non ut propter ista eum colant, sed ut ea ad bonum aeternum referant, id est, ut custodiant justificationes ejus. Possederunt, etc., non ut haec habenda sint pro summo bono, sed ut eis vacent unde summum et aeternum bonum possit acquiri, non ut in eis luxu defluant vel torpescant.

VERS. 45.-- Justificationes, etc. (CASS.) Sunt, ubi 1022Aest evidens et absoluta praeceptio, ut, Diligas Deum et proximum, quae custodienda. Lex de his, quae non corporaliter sed spiritualiter: et ideo quaerenda, quia umbra futurorum. Legem. Ut de circumcisione ejus et de aliis, quae diligenter investiganda sunt, quia mystice dicuntur.

PSALM CIV.

  • 1018D

VERS. 1.-- Alleluia. (CASS.) Here for the first time alleluia, nor was it set down before this by anyone; and no tongue has presumed to change it. Alleluia, praise ye. Ia is the name of the invisible God, which belongs to him alone. Through twenty psalms, which have this title, the great works of God are told, and great is the exultation in them. (CASS.) Here the prophet commends the good among that people of Israel, who together with other believers are the true seed of Abraham, the children of the promise.

Give glory to the Lord. (AUG.) The first psalm to which alleluia is prefixed, etc., as far as he subjoins what temporal things the mercy of God gave them.

VERS. 2.-- All things: (CASS.) all things; there is nothing that shame should 1019Akeep silent. Or, all the things which they shall tell are wonderful, for no one can relate them all.

VERS. 3.-- Be ye praised in the name, that is, rejoice that you are called Christians from Christ.

(AUG.) Be ye praised: he does not forbid being praised, if they are good; if they are not, then not save in the Lord, who makes men good. Be ye praised in the name. Which elsewhere is, In the Lord shall my soul be praised: what he adds there, let the meek hear and rejoice: here too in a manner, let the heart rejoice, as if he should say,

VERS. 4.-- The face, etc. (ID.) That is, the presence, etc., as far as the wicked man can fear the presence which the good man loves. (HIER.) From the martyr Hippolytus, etc., as far as there about to take his Church from among the Gentiles.

VERS. 5.-- Remember, and the rest. (AUG.) Seek 1019Bhim, etc., as far as if it is a great thing to seek what God is, at least behold the things which he has made. The wonders, etc. (ID.) Little by little he ascends from visible wonders to judgments: thence to the everlasting testament, where there is both precept and promise.

VERS. 7.-- In all the earth. (ID.) Think not that the sons of Abraham are in one nation according to the flesh, because in all the earth are Jacob and Israel, to whom he makes known his judgments, but not to another nation.

VERS. 8.-- For ever, (ID.) that is, unto eternity, whence afterwards, unto an everlasting testament. Which testament, if it be taken as the Old on account of the land of Chanaan, of which it follows. How is it everlasting, since that earthly inheritance cannot be everlasting? Of the testament. For that is called a testament which 1019Cis promised, and the teaching in which the promise is declared, and for the keeping of which it is rendered. (ID.) The promise is what we ought to receive: the commandment, what we ought to do. This is faith, that the just man live by faith, and to this faith an inheritance haere ditas is promised. Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Behold three patriarchs, whose God he calls himself in a special manner: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob. Behold a threefold authority.

VERS. 10.-- Unto an everlasting testament, (ID.) that is, that from the very word fulfilled, etc., as far as and the son abides in the house for ever.

VERS. 11.-- The land of Chanaan, (CASS.) that is, that which is signified by it: for he gave this land also as a figure of the eternal inheritance (I Joan. IV). (AUG.) Fittingly the eternal inheritance is called the land of Chanaan, 1019Dbecause from it servants are driven off and sons received.

VERS. 12.-- When they were in number. (CASS.) What supports of temporal life he bestowed upon the fathers and upon their sons, as well in flesh as in faith, not that they should cleave to these things, but should refer them to the eternal good, which is, that being drawn by them they should seek out the justifications and the law of God.

VERS. 13.-- From a kingdom. (AUG.) Not that the kingdom of Israel then was, but that it was to be.

VERS. 15.-- Touch ye not. (ID.) These words, although they are not in the history, God nevertheless spoke them either secretly in the hearts of men, or by an angel. The anointed, (ID.) because even then they were Christians, though secretly, whence Abraham rejoiced that he might see my day; he saw it and 1020Awas glad (Joan. VIII). For no one, either before or after, was reconciled to God apart from this faith, for there is one mediator, Christ (I Tim. II).

VERS. 16.-- And he called. (AUG.) The fourth part, where he begins to narrate, etc., as far as he commanded that to be which already was in his disposition. So he called, and all the staff of bread was broken (Gen. XXXVII).

VERS. 17.-- A man. (ID.) Joseph, sold by his brothers, was afterwards exalted in Egypt for his justice. Joseph. (ID.) If Joseph was both humbled and exalted, etc., as far as but seek ye first the kingdom of God, and all things shall be added.

VERS. 18.-- In fetters. (ID.) We do not read of Joseph's fetters in Genesis, but what was there passed over is to be believed, since the Spirit says it in the psalm. 1020B(CASS.) And although he found favour with the keeper of the prison, yet he was first in anguish. There follows. The iron pierced, etc. As if, besides the evils of the body, the iron, that is, the tribulation of hard necessity, which was in his burning and anxious soul, pierced through, etc. Or according to another reading, his soul passed through the iron, that is, the tribulation of hard necessity. The same sense as the former.

VERS. 23.-- In the land of Cham, etc. (AUG.) Cham the father of Chanaan, from whom the Egyptians draw their origin.

VERS. 24.-- And he increased his people, etc. (ID.) The fifth part. Behold, he sets forth briefly what was done in Egypt, which afterwards he relates more fully. He tells also how he strengthened his people over their enemies.

1020CAnd he strengthened him. By the signs of Moses, namely; for before this the male offspring of the children of Israel were being killed, and they themselves were worn down in the making of bricks. But afterwards, by a mighty hand and by the signs and portents of the Lord, they were made men to be feared and honoured.

VERS. 25.-- He turned. (ID.) He begins to relate how this was done. He turned: not that God is the author of evil, but he uses evils well; while he increased the prosperity of Israel, they were turned to envy, because they were already evil. That they should hate. Envy is the hatred of another's prosperity.

VERS. 26.-- He sent. He who could do all things by himself, that he might teach with what moderation he had done these things. Whom he chose, him. (ID.) It would have been enough to say, whom he chose: but nothing 1020Dis to be sought in this, that he added, him, but it is the custom of the divine manner of speech, for the sake of explanation.

VERS. 27.-- The words of his signs. (ID.) By which it was preached by them, etc., as far as he wrought therefore through them words not of voices, but of signs or of wonders.

VERS. 28.-- (ID.) Or: They provoked his words, which is plain. Or, Moses and Aaron did not provoke his words, because they bore patiently with those men, namely the Egyptians, even the hardest of them, on account of the commandment of the Lord, until all things which the Lord had appointed should be done upon them. Darkness, etc. (CASS.) They suffered it among the plagues. But here he says that their hearts were darkened, who despised the precepts of God. Blindness is a fitting 1021Abeginning of the plagues, without which they would not have incurred the rest.

VERS. 29.-- He turned their waters. (AUG.) The second plague, which in Exodus is the first, which signified that he would turn the waters of the Red Sea also, and that unto death for them.

VERS. 30.-- The earth brought forth. (AUG.) He turned their land into frogs, because they were so many that this is fitly said by way of hyperbole.

VERS. 31.-- He spoke, and there came the dog-fly, etc. (ID.) For in his word they were without time, before they came to be in time through that same word: or through angels, or through Moses he in a manner spoke, that it should be done then, when it was to be done.

VERS. 32.-- He made their rains, etc. (ID.) It is like to that: and their land gave forth frogs.

1021BVERS. 34.-- The locust and the bruchus. (ID.) The locust and the bruchus are one plague, because the one is the parent, the other the offspring.

VERS. 36.-- And he struck.(Id. ) Although there are ten plagues, etc., as far as who could not despise the wage of their labours, though a temporal one.

VERS. 37.-- And he brought them out, etc. The sixth part, according to Cassiodorus and Augustine. Above, the justice of God told what evils it brought upon the enemies of the Israelites: now he subjoins what temporal goods the mercy of God gave them, that being helped here they may seek the law of God. (AUG.) And he brought out: God said to Abraham, etc., as far as then there follows the second benefit, And Ft there was no one weak, and the rest.

VERS. 38.-- Because the fear of them fell upon 1021Cthem. They feared Israel, lest he should consume what was left of them.

(AUG.) Here was fulfilled what he said above, and he strengthened him over his enemy.

VERS. 39.-- He spread a cloud for their protection. And this is the second part, according to Augustine, where he subjoins what temporal goods the mercy of God gave them, the evils having been told above which the justice of God brought upon their enemies.

(AUG.) Now he begins the benefits which were done for them as they journeyed in the desert.

VERS. 40.-- They asked, (AUG.) the good, for the support of the weak. The quail: and he filled them with the bread of heaven: which is also flesh, because here he speaks not of the embittering of the wicked, but of the faith of the elect: they themselves are to be understood 1021Dto have asked, whereby the murmurs of the embittered might be held down.

VERS. 42.-- For he remembered his holy word. (ID.) By all these benefits God commends in Abraham the merit of faith, whence he adds: for he remembered.

VERS. 44.-- And he gave them. (AUG.) Not that they should worship him for the sake of these things, but that they should refer them to the eternal good, that is, that they may keep his justifications. They possessed, etc., not that these things are to be held for the highest good, but that they may be free for those things whereby the highest and eternal good may be acquired, not that in them they should melt away in luxury or grow torpid.

VERS. 45.-- The justifications, etc. (CASS.) They are where 1022Athere is a plain and absolute precept, as, Thou shalt love God and thy neighbour, which are to be kept. The law is of those things which are to be kept not bodily but spiritually: and therefore it is to be sought out, because it is a shadow of things to come. The law. As concerning its circumcision and the other matters, which are to be diligently investigated, because they are spoken mystically.

PSALMUS CV.

VERS. 1.-- Alleluia. Alleluia. Quidam dicunt, unum alleluia ad finem superioris psalmi pertinere, alterum esse sequentis. Hanc enim regulam Hieronymus tenendam esse tradit. Cujus assertioni Cassiodorus quoque consentit. Sed plures, ubicunque alleluia, sequenti dant: et aliquando semel, aliquando bis; ut Dominus in Evangelio, nunc dixit amen, nunc amen amen, pro majore certitudine 1022Brei. Istis consentit Augustinus, praesertim cum nulli Graecorum codices in fine psalmi habeant alleluia.

Confitemini Domino. (AUG.) Psalmus iste superiori conjunctus est, etc., usque ad monet ergo ad geminam confessionem laudis et peccatorum.

(CASS.) Hebraeus relicta patrum perfidia, ad misericordiam Dei conversus, suadet aliis ad eamdem misericordiam converti, orans ut populo beneplacito socientur, qui erat in adventu Christi congregandus.

VERS. 2.-- Quis loquetur. (CASS.) Iste, qui misericordiam petit, impletur consideratione divinorum operum, et admirans ait: Quis loquetur?

VERS. 3.-- Beati qui custodiunt. (AUG.) Vel quia 1022Csequitur, etc., usque ad judicium et justitiam, quia Beati sunt qui, etc.

VERS. 5.-- Ad videndum, etc. (AUG.), ut videamus te in ea bonitate, quam praestas electis, id est per gratiam tuam videamus, ne caeci remaneamus. Ut lauderis: mirum est in plerisque codicibus, etc., usque ad quia non laudatur nisi propter te.

VERS. 6.-- Peccavimus. Secunda pars, ubi enumerat peccata patrum, quae in Aegypto commiserunt, et tamen a Deo dicit liberatos.

Iniquitatem. (CASS.) Tertio idem dicit, ut pura confessio appareat; tanto citius solvitur, quanto vivacius se damnat homo.

VERS. 7.-- Non intellexerunt. (AUG.) Id est, quod per illa eis dare velles, id est, non temporale, sed 1022Daeternum bonum; quod per patientiam exspectatur, et ideo ipsi impatientes murmuraverunt, et temporalibus beati voluerunt. (CASS.) Duo sunt quae beneficia commendant, intellectus et memoria, quorum utrumque in eis redarguit. Et primo intellectum, cum ait: non intellexerunt mirabilia. Irritaverunt ascendentes. (AUG.) Timentes Deum et desperantes, etc., usque ad unde meruit inter alias regni privilegium vel principatum obtinere.

VERS. 9.-- Sicut in deserto. (ID.) Quia ubi fuerunt abyssi, factum est siccitate, ut desertum ubi non sunt aquae.

VERS. 10.-- Redemit eos de manu. (ID.) Quo praetio? quasi diceret, nullo; sed in figura baptismi 1023Afactum est, in quo redimimur de manu diaboli sanguine Christi; unde et mare Rubrum dixit, quod colore sanguis figurabatur.

VERS. 12.-- Et crediderunt in. (AUG.) Ecce dura corda Judaeorum, quae non ante, sed post miracula credunt: melius fuit promittenti credere.

VERS. 13.-- Cito fecerunt, obliti. Tertia pars, ubi exponit peccata, quae post exitum fecerunt: nec tamen defuit eis misericordia Dei per Moysen placati. Vel correptio, per justitiam Dei, in quosdam per Moysen vindicantis. (CASS.) Cito fecerunt. Summa celeritate mutati sunt, ete., usque ad distulit enim Deus dare, ut probaret eos.

VERS. 14.-- Concupierunt concupiscentiam in deserto. (AUG.) Talis locutio, ut laudaverunt, etc. (CASS.) 1023BNimietas desiderii, geminatione verbi ostenditur.

VERS. 15.-- Saturitatem. Non est haec saturitas de qua dicitur. Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt justitiam, quoniam ipsi saturabuntur (Matth. V).

In animas eorum. (AUG.) Animalitatem, quae sustentatur esca: Unde et in Evangelio: Nonne anima est plus quam esca? Vel, animas, ut voluntas, quae desperando petierat, copia vinceretur; saturitatem, sequitur seditio, unde subdit.

VERS. 16.-- Et irritaverunt. (CASS.) Honorem ambientes invidendo, Moysen in castris, et Aaron sanctum Domini: haec irritatio fuit pro sacerdotio, quod habebat Aaron, et filii ejus.

VERS. 17.-- Aperta est terra. (ID.) Laus Dei, qui suos vindicavit qualitas poenae facta indicat; a terra 1023Cvorantur, qui terrena sapuerunt.

VERS. 18.-- In synagoga. (ID.) Core namque et ducenti quinquaginta cum eo, volentes habere sacerdotium Aaron, acceperunt thuribula, ut adolerent incensum, ideoque divino igne consumpti sunt. Peccatores. (AUG.) Non ait peccantes, quod est boni: sed peccatores valde iniquos et gravibus sarcinis peccatorum oneratos.

VERS. 19.-- Et fecerunt. (CASS.) Absentiam Moysi non tolerantes, dum ipse in vertice montis Sinai moraretur, ut acciperet legem, fecerunt vitulum. Horeb. Interpretatur Calvaria, ubi crucifixio facta, etc., usque ad hoc impatientia levium fecit, sicut omnia mala ex ea nascuntur.

VERS. 20.-- In similitudine. (AUG.) Non ait in 1023Dsimilitudinem, sed in similitudine. Et est talis locutio, ut supra, et crediderunt in verbis ejus.

VERS. 21.-- Obliti sunt. (CASS.) Magna oblivio quidem in memoria, si non liberatio.

Terribilia. Quia adversarios afflixerunt, et istis, quem timere deberent, monstraverunt.

VERS 23.-- Stetisset in confractione. (AUG.) Dicens: Si non dimittis illis, dele me de libro tuo. Quantum valet intercessio sanctorum? Securus Moyses de justitia Dei, qua eum delere non posset, impetravit misericordiam iis qui juste perirent.

Ut averteret iram. De aqua contradictionis et immolatione filiorum, unde vehementius iratus Deus, et tamen postea misertus. Et pro nihilo. Quarta 1024Apars, ubi item et alia peccata enumerat, et per Phinees placatum Deum dicit.

Non crediderunt verbo ejus. (AUG.) Contempserunt quod per illam significabatur, etc., usque ad non sustinuerunt consilium ejus.

In tabernaculis ejus. (CASS.) Murmuraverunt, quia hoc non laborantibus, sed otiosis contingit, unde major invidia criminis crescit.

VERS. 26.-- Et elevavit manum suam super eos, etc. (CASS.) Haec justitia Dei praemittitur, ut secuta pietas magis glorificetur, quae pietas in sequenti ostenditur, ubi interventu Phinees Deus placatus dicitur.

VERS. 28.-- Et initiati sunt Beelphegor. (ID.) Vel, consecrati sunt, quasi modo ad tempus colentes: 1024Bgravior excessus et vehementior ira daemonibus devovebant filios. (AUG.) Et initiati sunt, antequam diceret, etc., usque ad cujus major interitus futurus erat, liberavit.

VERS. 30.-- Et stetit Phinees. (CASS.) Solida mente, etc., usque ad quia qui bene agit, orat.

VERS. 31.-- Et reputatum, etc. (AUG.) Deus, qui novit quanta charitate populi id factum sit, reputavit hoc sacerdoti suo in justitiam, non solum quandiu generatio est, sed usque in aeternum.

VERS. 32.-- Et irritaverunt, etc. (CASS.) Quinta pars, ubi agit de aqua contradictionis, et de immolatione filiorum, unde vehementius iratus est Deus, et tamen postea misertus. Quasi ita irritaverunt in adinventionibus suis, sicut supra dictum est; nunc 1024Citerum irritaverunt.

VERS. 33.-- Et distinxit in labiis suis, etc. (CASS.) Hoc miraculum, etc., usque ad non tenuit fiduciam qualem debuit. (AUG.) Et distinxit. Quasi, hoc non posset Deus facere, etc., usque ad non tamen alienatus est a regno gratiae Dei.

VERS. 35.-- Gentes. Septem illos populos, qui terram promissionis possidebant.

VERS. 36.-- Et factum est illis in scandalum. (CASS.) Terra promissionis data in praemium, versa est excedentibus in ruinam, quia gentium conformitate factae sunt idololatrae.

VERS. 37.-- Et immolaverunt. (AUG.) Haec etsi illa non narret historia, tamen hic propheta mentiri non potest. (CASS.) Si non in prima, in sequenti 1024Daetate factum est quod narrat David.

VERS. 38.-- Et interfecta. (AUG.) Tropica locutio, continens pro contento, id est homines; ipsi enim interficiebant animas suas immolando filios, et contaminati sunt in operibus.

VERS. 39.-- Adinventionibus suis. (ID.) Non quod primi invenissent, sed quia alios imitati sunt. Quod in Graeco apertius, et his et supra; unde et alii transferunt, studia, vel affectiones, vel voluptates.

VERS. 40.-- Abominatus est. (CASS.) Id est aversus est ab eis: quod averti est extremum omnium malorum, unde ruina sequitur, et tradidit.

VERS. 41.-- Et tradidit eos, etc. (ID.) Ecce, qui gloriabantur in idolis, opprobrio servitutis subsunt, 1025Aquia serviunt inimicis, quod difficile est. Qui oderunt. Grave est servire offenso, qui nullo placatur obsequio.

VERS. 43.-- Saepe liberavit, etc. (CASS.) Duplex misericordia, praemisit enim superius beneficia Dei, nec tamen cessat iniquitas eorum; intulit vindictam, et afflictis iterum miseretur.

In consilio suo. (AUG.) Consilium hominis malum est ipsi homini, qui quaerit quae sua sunt, non quae Dei.

VERS. 45.-- Testamenti. (CASS.) Causa est, ne Israel pro debito periret Testamentum Novum, ubi est adventus Domini, qui est Abrahae promissus. Poenituit. (AUG.) Quia mutavit, quod perdituros eos videbatur. (CASS.) Tunc poenitet, quando nos poenitere videt, et talis est nobis quales nos illi. (AUG.) Nihil quasi repentino 1025Bconsilio facit Deus, sed quod ab aeterno praescivit. Sed mutare dicitur, quod secundum rerum causas sequi videretur, aliis causis e contra intervenientibus. Sed et causas, et quid fieret, immutabiliter praevidit.

VERS. 46.-- In misericordias. (CASS.) Propter diversa dona: prophetae, apostoli, martyres et confessores de Judaeis fuerunt, quos dedit in misericordias: et hoc in conspectu omnium, caeperant eos, id est gentium, ut eos gentes mirarentur, quae prius eos despexerunt. Vel, coram daemonibus liberi facti, sub quibus fuere captivi.

VERS. 47.-- Salvos fac nos. (CASS.) Sexta pars. Jam copia laudis Dei expletus precatur quod futurum vidit, ut Ecclesia de omnibus gentibus congregetur, 1025Cet laudes aeternas cantet. (AUG.) Salvos fac nos, quasi: Dedisti misericordias in conspectu omnium, etc., usque ad sequitur. Et congrega nos de nationibus.

VERS. 48.-- Benedictus Dominus. (CASS.) Haec est laus, quam congregatos optat cantare, hoc nunc cantat Ecclesia de tanto bono laeta. A saeculo usque, etc., id est, ab aeterno in aeternum, quia sine fine laudabitur: haec est tertia consummatio corporis Christi in immortalitate, quod in principio psalmi oratum est: Memento nostri, Domine, in beneplacita populi tui ad videndum, ad laetandum, ut lauderis cum haereditate tua.

PSALM CV.

VERS. 1.-- Alleluia. Alleluia. Some say that one alleluia belongs to the end of the preceding psalm, and the other to the following. For Jerome hands down that this rule is to be held. To whose assertion Cassiodorus also agrees. But the greater number assign it, wherever alleluia stands, to the psalm that follows: and sometimes once, sometimes twice; as the Lord in the Gospel now said amen, now amen amen, for the greater certainty 1022Bof the matter. With these Augustine agrees, especially since no codices of the Greeks have alleluia at the end of a psalm.

Give glory to the Lord. (AUG.) This psalm is joined to the preceding, etc., as far as he admonishes therefore to a twofold confession, of praise and of sins.

(CASS.) The Hebrew, having left the perfidy of his fathers and being turned to the mercy of God, persuades others to be turned to the same mercy, praying that they may be joined to the well-pleasing people, which was to be gathered at the coming of Christ.
