VERS. 2.-- Who shall declare. (CASS.) He that asks for mercy is filled with the consideration of the divine works, and marvelling says: Who shall declare?

VERS. 3.-- Blessed are they that keep. (AUG.) Or because 1022Cthere follows, etc., as far as judgment and justice, because Blessed are they that, etc.

VERS. 5.-- To see, etc. (AUG.), that we may see thee in that goodness which thou bestowest upon the elect, that is, by thy grace let us see, lest we remain blind. That thou mayest be praised: it is strange that in very many codices, etc., as far as because he is not praised save on account of thee.

VERS. 6.-- We have sinned. The second part, where he enumerates the sins of the fathers which they committed in Egypt, and yet says that they were delivered by God.

Iniquity. (CASS.) A third time he says the same, that the confession may appear pure; a man is loosed the more quickly, the more keenly he condemns himself.

VERS. 7.-- They understood not. (AUG.) That is, what thou didst will to give them through those things, that is, not a temporal but 1022Dan eternal good; which is awaited through patience, and therefore they, being impatient, murmured, and wished to be happy in temporal things. (CASS.) There are two things which commend benefits, understanding and memory, and he reproves both of these in them. And first the understanding, when he says: they understood not the wonders. They provoked, going up. (AUG.) Fearing God and despairing, etc., as far as whence it deserved to obtain among the others the privilege or the princedom of the kingdom.

VERS. 9.-- As in the desert. (ID.) Because where there were depths, it was made by dryness like a desert where there are no waters.

VERS. 10.-- He redeemed them from the hand. (ID.) At what price? As if he should say, at none; but it was done as a figure of baptism, 1023Ain which we are redeemed from the hand of the devil by the blood of Christ; whence also he said the Red Sea, because by its colour blood was figured.

VERS. 12.-- And they believed in. (AUG.) Behold the hard hearts of the Jews, which believe not before but after miracles: it had been better to believe him who promised.

VERS. 13.-- They quickly did, forgetting. The third part, where he sets forth the sins which they committed after the going out: nor yet did the mercy of God fail them, he being appeased through Moses. Or rebuke, by the justice of God, taking vengeance upon certain of them through Moses. (CASS.) They quickly did. With the utmost speed they were changed, etc. ete., as far as for God put off giving, that he might prove them.

VERS. 14.-- They lusted a lust in the desert. (AUG.) Such a manner of speech, as they praised, etc. (CASS.) 1023BThe excess of the desire is shown by the doubling of the word.

VERS. 15.-- Fulness. This is not that fulness of which it is said. Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after justice, for they shall be filled (Matth. V).

Into their souls. (AUG.) The animal nature, which is sustained by food: whence also in the Gospel: Is not the soul more than the meat? Or, souls, that the will, which had asked in despair, might be overcome by abundance; after fulness there follows sedition, whence he adds.

VERS. 16.-- And they provoked. (CASS.) Canvassing for honour by envy, Moses in the camp, and Aaron the holy one of the Lord: this provoking was for the priesthood which Aaron had, and his sons.

VERS. 17.-- The earth was opened. (ID.) The quality of the punishment inflicted declares the praise of God, who has avenged his own; they are devoured by the earth 1023Cwho savoured of earthly things.

VERS. 18.-- In the synagogue. (ID.) For Core and two hundred and fifty with him, wishing to have the priesthood of Aaron, took censers, to burn incense, and therefore were consumed by divine fire. Sinners. (AUG.) He does not say sinning, which belongs to a good man too: but sinners, men exceedingly wicked and laden with heavy burdens of sins.

VERS. 19.-- And they made. (CASS.) Not enduring the absence of Moses, while he himself tarried on the top of mount Sinai to receive the law, they made a calf. Horeb. It is interpreted Calvary, where the crucifixion took place, etc., as far as this the impatience of the fickle did, as all evils are born of it.

VERS. 20.-- In the likeness. (AUG.) He does not say into 1023Da likeness, but in a likeness. And it is such a manner of speech as above, and they believed in his words.

VERS. 21.-- They forgot. (CASS.) Great forgetfulness indeed in the memory, if not the deliverance.

Terrible things. Because they afflicted their adversaries, and showed to these men whom they ought to fear.

VERS. 23.-- Had stood in the breach. (AUG.) Saying: If thou forgive them not, blot me out of thy book. How much avails the intercession of the saints? Moses, secure concerning the justice of God, by which he could not blot him out, obtained mercy for those who would justly have perished.

That he might turn away his wrath. Concerning the water of contradiction and the immolation of the sons, whereat God was the more vehemently angered, and yet afterwards had mercy. And for nothing. The fourth 1024Apart, where he likewise enumerates yet other sins, and says that God was appeased through Phinees.

They believed not his word. (AUG.) They despised that which was signified by her, etc., as far as they did not await his counsel.

In his tents. (CASS.) They murmured, because this befalls not them that labour but the idle, whence the greater odium of the crime grows.

VERS. 26.-- And he lifted up his hand over them, etc. (CASS.) This justice of God is set first, that the mercy which follows may be the more glorified, which mercy is shown in what follows, where God is said to be appeased by the intervention of Phinees.

VERS. 28.-- And they were initiated to Beelphegor. (ID.) Or, they were consecrated, as though worshipping only for a time: 1024Ba graver excess and a more vehement wrath: they devoted their sons to the demons. (AUG.) And they were initiated, before he should say, etc., as far as he delivered him whose destruction was to be the greater.

VERS. 30.-- And Phinees stood up. (CASS.) With a firm mind, etc., as far as because he who acts well, prays.

VERS. 31.-- And it was reputed, etc. (AUG.) God, who knew with how great charity for the people that was done, reputed this to his priest unto justice, not only so long as there is a generation, but even unto eternity.

VERS. 32.-- And they provoked, etc. (CASS.) The fifth part, where he treats of the water of contradiction and of the immolation of the sons, whereat God was the more vehemently angered, and yet afterwards had mercy. As if: they so provoked him in their own devices, as was said above; now 1024Cagain they have provoked him.

VERS. 33.-- And he made a distinction with his lips, etc. (CASS.) This miracle, etc., as far as he did not hold the confidence he ought to have held. (AUG.) And he made a distinction. As if: God could not do this, etc., as far as yet he was not estranged from the kingdom of the grace of God.

VERS. 35.-- The nations. Those seven peoples which possessed the land of promise.

VERS. 36.-- And it became to them a stumbling-block. (CASS.) The land of promise, given as a reward, was turned to ruin for those who transgressed, because by conformity with the nations they became idolaters.

VERS. 37.-- And they sacrificed. (AUG.) Although that history does not relate these things, yet this prophet cannot lie. (CASS.) If not in the first, then in the following 1024Dage was done what David relates.

VERS. 38.-- And slain. (AUG.) A figurative manner of speech, the container for the contained, that is, men; for they themselves were slaying their own souls by sacrificing their sons, and they were defiled in their works. [Vulg. Ps. 105:38 Et infecta est terra in sanguinibus, "and the land was defiled with blood"]

VERS. 39.-- In their own devices. (ID.) Not that they had invented them first, but because they imitated others. Which is plainer in the Greek, both in these places and above; whence others also render it, pursuits, or affections, or pleasures.

VERS. 40.-- He abhorred. (CASS.) That is, he turned away from them: and to be turned away from is the utmost of all evils, whence ruin follows, and he delivered.

VERS. 41.-- And he delivered them, etc. (ID.) Behold, they who gloried in idols lie under the reproach of servitude, 1025Abecause they serve their enemies, which is a hard thing. They that hated. It is grievous to serve one who has been offended, who is appeased by no compliance.

VERS. 43.-- Often he delivered, etc. (CASS.) A twofold mercy; for above he set out first the benefits of God, and yet their iniquity does not cease; he brought in vengeance, and again he has mercy on the afflicted.

In his own counsel. (AUG.) The counsel of man is evil to the man himself, who seeks the things that are his own, not the things that are God's.

VERS. 45.-- Of the testament. (CASS.) The cause that Israel did not perish for its debt is the New Testament, wherein is the coming of the Lord, who was promised to Abraham. It repented him. (AUG.) Because he changed what seemed about to destroy them. (CASS.) Then he repents, when he sees us repent, and he is such to us as we are to him. (AUG.) God does nothing as by a sudden 1025Bcounsel, but what he foreknew from eternity. But he is said to change that which, according to the causes of things, would seem to follow, when other causes intervene on the contrary part. But both the causes, and what should come to pass, he unchangeably foresaw.

VERS. 46.-- Unto mercies. (CASS.) Because of the diverse gifts: prophets, apostles, martyrs and confessors were of the Jews, whom he gave unto mercies: and this in the sight of all, they had taken them, [Vulg. Ps. 105:46 in conspectu omnium qui ceperant eos, "in the sight of all that had taken them captive"] that is, of the Gentiles, that the Gentiles might marvel at them, who before had despised them. Or, made free before the demons, under whom they had been captives.

VERS. 47.-- Save us. (CASS.) The sixth part. Now filled with the abundance of the praise of God, he prays for that which he saw was to come, that the Church may be gathered out of all nations, 1025Cand may sing eternal praises. (AUG.) Save us, as if: Thou hast given mercies in the sight of all, etc., as far as there follows. And gather us from among the nations.

VERS. 48.-- Blessed be the Lord. (CASS.) This is the praise which he desires that they, being gathered, should sing; this the Church now sings, glad for so great a good. From everlasting unto, etc., that is, from eternity unto eternity, because he shall be praised without end: this is the third consummation of the body of Christ in immortality, which was prayed at the beginning of the psalm: Remember us, O Lord, in the good pleasures of thy people, to see, to rejoice, that thou mayest be praised with thine inheritance.

PSALMUS CVI.

Alleluia, alleluia. (AUG.) Hic psalmus commendat 1025Dmisericordiam Dei, etc., usque ad quae Apostolus posuit, quamvis idem significantia.

VERS. 1.-- Confitemini Domino. (ID.) Docet hic psalmus quid simus per nos, etc., usque ad prius monet redemptos confiteri. Confitemini.

(CASS., AUG.) Cujus sunt septem partitiones, etc., usque ad septimo, agit de haereticis, ibi, Et pauci facti.

VERS. 3.-- Et mari. (CASS.) Pro austro, ponit mare, oceanum illius partis intelligens, hoc pro qualibet parte mundi potest accipi.

VERS. 4.-- Erraverunt. (ID.) Secunda pars, ubi prima tentatio, etc., usque ad quarto pro exauditione confessio, id est, laudatio.

1026AVERS. 5.-- Esurientes. (AUG.) Curiosos saeculi significat, qui veritatem diversis opinionibus exquirebant, nec inveniebant. Anima eorum, etc. Commendat se Deus, quod nobis expedit; deficimus ut rogemus, et subvenientem amemus.

VERS. 6.-- Et deduxit. (AUG.) Quasi, eripuit de ignorantia; ostendens viam, Christum. Ecce liberavit eos ab errore; de fame autem et siti quibus aestuabant, qualiter liberaverit, post dicet; sed praemittit de confessione.

VERS. 8.-- Mirabilia. (HIER.) Quasi mirabili modo redemptionis datae sunt misericordiae.

VERS. 9.-- Esurientem. (CASS.) Scire appetentem, vel non scire appetentem, sed inedia nimia deficientem, sicut contingere solet nimia fame vel infirmitate 1026Bconfecto, ut manducare non appetat, sed nimia inedia deficiat.

Sedentes. (AUG.) Tertia pars, ubi ponitur secunda tentatio, etc., usque ad et nos etiam hoc posse consideremus.

VERS. 11.-- Quia exacerbaverunt. (ID.) Hoc aliud iterum conantem, etc., usque ad unde eis erat iratus.

Consilium Altissimi. Ut qui superbierunt, in angustiis humiliarentur, quod erat salubre consilium, ut morbus saeculi contrario remedio curaretur.

VERS. 12.-- Nec fuit qui. (ID.) Deo enim desistente ab auxilio, laborare potes contra vitia, sed non vincere; et te presso tua prava consuetudine, humiliabitur cor, ut discas clamare, unde subdit: Et exclamaverunt.

1026CVERS. 13.-- Et exclamaverunt. (CASS.) Simili causa eadem sententia quae et supra.

VERS. 16.-- Portas aereas. (ID.) Portae aereae, hominum consuetudines vitiosae, quae clausos non sinunt exire.

Vectes. Spiritus immundi, qui portas obserant. Aereos, ferreos, pro fortitudine ponit, sed virtus Dei frangit.

VERS. 18.-- Omnem escam. (AUG.) Quarta pars, ubi ponitur tertia tentatio, quae est taedium. Qui supra fame languebant, item fastidio periclitantur ne ergo putes de satietate securos, quia et fastidio moriuntur. Et hoc est omnem escam, etc.

(AUG.) Postquam venit de ignorantia ad veritatem, de errore ad viam, de fame sapientiae ad verbum 1026Dfidei, et postquam difficultates malorum vicit, ut sine querela vivat, restat taedium, ut aliquando nec legere, nec orare delectet; evasit imperitiam et concupiscentiam, sed moritur taedio.

VERS. 23.-- Qui descendunt mare. Quinta pars, etc., usque ad si tota navis periclitatur.

VERS. 24, 25.-- Ipsi viderunt opera Domini. (AUG.) Vel viderunt, etc., usque ad exponit procellas eorum, dixit et stetit. In profundo. Dixit et stetit subdens, spiritus procellae. (ID.) Profundum cor hominum unde venti erumpunt, et fiunt tempestates seditionum et dissensionum.

VERS. 27.-- Sicut ebrius. (ID.) Titubant, quia prosperitas eorum vel adversitas, major est viribus. 1027AEt omnis sapientia eorum devorata est. Inquiete sapientes apparent, quando loquuntur, quando legunt; sed veniente tempestate, omnia humana consilia deficiunt; quid agendum sit, non videtur. Restat ergo clamare, ut cor eorum solidet Deus, ne tentationibus ventiletur.

VERS. 32.-- In Ecclesia. (AUG.) Ecce unde omnia dixerit, et ubi omnia praedicta aguntur.

VERS. 33.-- Posuit flumina. (CASS.) Sexta pars hactenus, quomodo et mala inimicorum prodesse facit. (AUG.) Posuit flumina. Consequenter Ecclesia conmendatur, etc., usque ad unde et erga Ecclesiam Dei beneficia aperte monstrantur.

VERS. 34.-- In salsugine. (CASS.) Salsus humor, ubi dominatur, fecunditatem tollit.

1027BA malitia habitantium. (AUG.) Propter malitiam eorum qui terram illam, id est tabernaculum Domini, dolosis mentibus inhabitabant.

VERS. 37.-- Et seminaverunt. (CASS.) Seminant agros, plantant vineas, qui corpora sua coelesti institutione purificant, ut fructus honorum operum ferant.

VERS. 38.-- Nimis: (CASS.) pro valde, vel quia multi vocati, pauci vero electi.

VERS. 39.-- Et pauci. (AUG.) Septima pars, ubi dicitur etiam aliquid de haereticis, etc., usque ad non erant de paucitate electorum. Vexati. (CASS.) Vel, persistentes per haereticos, vel haeretici insidiis diaboli. Dolor et tribulatio his qui auctorem salutis relinquunt.

1027CVERS. 40.-- Effusa est. (AUG.) Vel, effusus est contemptus, etc., usque ad et quid fecit etiam de illis seductis? Ecce.

VERS. 41.-- Adjuvit pauperem. Potuit illos pati Deus semper intus, sed nos de illis non proficeremus. Cum autem separati sunt, et per quaestiones nos inquietant, nascitur nobis inquisitionis studium et timoris exemplum, ut, Qui stat, videat ne cadat. Et quid in paupere adjuto fit de illis seductis? Et posuit sicut oves. Unum pauperem putabas; sed iste pauper est multae familiae, multae Ecclesiae: tamen et est una Ecclesia, una ovis. Haec tanta mysteria diu latentia, et ideo dulciter inventa.

VERS. 42.-- Videbunt recti et laetabuntur. (AUG.) 1027DEcce quo Psalmista tendat, ad hoc, scilicet ut ostendat quod boni per misericordiam Dei exaltantur, ut mali per superbiam conteruntur.

VERS. 43.-- Quis sapiens et custodiet haec? (ID.) Conclusio, quasi diceret, quia pauperem adjuvat Dominus, ergo: Quis est sapiens? Misericordias. Quod de errore liberat, etc., usque ad et iniquus os suum oppilat.

PSALM CVI.

Alleluia, alleluia. (AUG.) This psalm commends 1025Dthe mercy of God, etc., as far as the things which the Apostle set down, although they signify the same.

VERS. 1.-- Give praise to the Lord. (ID.) This psalm teaches what we are through ourselves, etc., as far as he first admonishes the redeemed to give praise. Give praise.

(CASS., AUG.) Of which there are seven divisions, etc., as far as in the seventh he treats of heretics, there, And they were made few.

VERS. 3.-- And from the sea. (CASS.) For the south he puts the sea, understanding thereby the ocean of that quarter; and this can be taken for any quarter of the world whatever.

VERS. 4.-- They wandered. (ID.) The second part, where is the first temptation, etc., as far as fourthly, confession for having been heard, that is, praise.

1026AVERS. 5.-- Hungry. (AUG.) He signifies the curious of the world, who sought out the truth by divers opinions, and found it not. Their soul, etc. God commends himself, because it is expedient for us; we fail that we may ask, and may love him who comes to our aid.

VERS. 6.-- And he led. (AUG.) As it were, he rescued them from ignorance, showing the way, Christ. Behold, he freed them from error; but in what manner he freed them from the hunger and thirst wherewith they burned, he will say afterwards; but he sets confession first.

VERS. 8.-- Wonderful things. (HIER.) As it were, in a wonderful manner of redemption were the mercies given.

VERS. 9.-- Him that is hungry. (CASS.) Him that desires to know, or him that desires not to know, but fails through too great fasting, as is wont to befall one worn out 1026Bby too great hunger or by infirmity, so that he desires not to eat, but fails through too great fasting.

Sitting. (AUG.) The third part, where the second temptation is set down, etc., as far as let us also consider that we can do this.

VERS. 11.-- Because they exasperated. (ID.) This is another thing, attempting yet again, etc., as far as whence he was wroth with them.

The counsel of the Most High. That they who were proud might be humbled in straits, which was a wholesome counsel, that the disease of the world might be cured by a contrary remedy.

VERS. 12.-- Nor was there any who. (ID.) For when God withdraws his aid, thou canst labour against vices, but not conquer; and when thou art pressed by thine own depraved habit, the heart will be humbled, that thou mayest learn to cry out, whence he subjoins: And they cried out.

1026CVERS. 13.-- And they cried out. (CASS.) From a like cause the same sentence as above.

VERS. 16.-- Brazen gates. (ID.) The brazen gates are the vicious customs of men, which suffer not those shut in to go out.

Bars. Unclean spirits, who bolt the gates. He puts brazen and iron for strength, but the power of God breaks them.

VERS. 18.-- All meat. (AUG.) The fourth part, where the third temptation is set down, which is weariness. They who above were languishing with hunger are in like manner endangered by loathing; lest therefore thou think men secure through satiety, since they die of loathing also. And this is all meat, etc.

(AUG.) After he has come from ignorance to truth, from error to the way, from the hunger of wisdom to the word 1026Dof faith, and after he has overcome the difficulties of evils, so as to live without complaint, there remains weariness, so that sometimes neither to read nor to pray delights him; he has escaped unskilfulness and concupiscence, but he dies of weariness.

VERS. 23.-- They that go down the sea. The fifth part, etc., as far as if the whole ship is in peril.

VERS. 24, 25.-- They have seen the works of the Lord. (AUG.) Or they saw, etc., as far as he expounds their storms, he spoke, and there stood. In the deep. He spoke, and there stood, subjoining, the spirit of the storm. (ID.) The deep is the heart of men, whence the winds break forth, and there arise tempests of seditions and dissensions.

VERS. 27.-- As a drunken man. (ID.) They stagger, because their prosperity or their adversity is greater than their strength. 1027AAnd all their wisdom was swallowed up. They appear restlessly wise when they speak, when they read; but when the tempest comes, all human counsels fail; what is to be done is not seen. It remains therefore to cry out, that God may make their heart firm, lest it be tossed about by temptations.

VERS. 32.-- In the Church. (AUG.) Behold whence he has spoken all these things, and where all that is foretold is done.

VERS. 33.-- He hath turned rivers. (CASS.) The sixth part, thus far: how he makes even the evils of enemies to profit. (AUG.) He hath turned rivers. Consequently the Church is commended, etc., as far as whence also the benefits of God toward the Church are openly shown.

VERS. 34.-- In saltness. (CASS.) Salt moisture, where it prevails, takes away fruitfulness.

1027BFrom the malice of them that dwell. (AUG.) Because of the malice of those who inhabited that land, that is, the tabernacle of the Lord, with deceitful minds.

VERS. 37.-- And they sowed. (CASS.) They sow fields and plant vineyards who purify their bodies by a heavenly institution, that they may bear the fruits of good honorum works.

VERS. 38.-- Exceedingly: (CASS.) for "greatly," or because many are called, but few chosen.

VERS. 39.-- And few. (AUG.) The seventh part, where somewhat is said also of heretics, etc., as far as they were not of the fewness of the elect. Afflicted. (CASS.) Either those who persevere under heretics, or heretics by the snares of the devil. Sorrow and tribulation to those who forsake the author of salvation.

1027CVERS. 40.-- It was poured out. (AUG.) Or, contempt was poured out, etc., as far as and what has he done even concerning those that were led astray? Behold.

VERS. 41.-- He helped the poor man. God could have suffered them always within, but we should not have profited by them. But when they are separated, and disquiet us with their questions, there is born in us a zeal of inquiry and an example of fear, so that, He that standeth, let him take heed lest he fall. And what is done concerning those led astray, in the poor man that is helped? And he set as sheep. Thou didst think him one poor man; but this poor man is many households, many churches: yet he is also one Church, one sheep. So great are these mysteries, long hidden, and therefore sweetly found.

VERS. 42.-- The upright shall see and shall rejoice. (AUG.) 1027DBehold whither the Psalmist tends: to this, namely, that he may show that the good are exalted through the mercy of God, as the wicked are crushed through pride.

VERS. 43.-- Who is wise, and will keep these things? (ID.) The conclusion, as if he should say: since the Lord helps the poor man, therefore: Who is wise? The mercies. That he delivers from error, etc., as far as and the unjust shall stop his mouth.

PSALMUS CVII.

VERS. 1.-- Canticum psalmi. (AUG.) Ex postremis partibus duorum, etc., usque ad ut complerentur eloquia prophetarum. (CASS.) Hic plura eadem quae supra, etc., usque ad et bene junguntur, quae nullatenus repugnant. (ID.) In primo agitur de fuga 1028ADavid, etc., usque ad Canticum ad divinas res, Psalmus ad actuales operas.

VERS. 2.-- Paratum. (CASS.) Sextus psalmus de duabus naturis in Christo. Paratum cor meum. Primo Christus gratias agit, quia suscipiens passionem surrexit in gloriam. Secundo, quae salus sit facta omni terrae, ibi, Ut liberentur.

VERS. 7.-- Ut liberentur. (ID.) Secunda pars, quae salus sit facta omni terrae super quam gloria, hic etiam humilitas humanitatis et potentia majestatis ostenditur.

Salvum fac. Ut liberentur in futuro, hic salva eos, ne cadant. Vel, se petit salvari in resurrectione, ut fideles liberentur, qui tali signo deitatem ejus senserunt. Quasi, ut cantem et psallam, Salvum 1028Bme fac in resurrectione dextera tua, id est per Verbum, qui est brachium Patris, ut sic liberentur dilecti tui. Ordo verborum conversus est. Dicit enim: Salvum me fac et exaudi, et salvum me fac.

VERS. 8.-- Exsultabo. (AUG.) Vel exaltabor, supra laetabor, hic vero exaltabor, quod satis convenit, quia de exaltatione est laetitia. Et loquitur hic Christus in persona Ecclesiae.

VERS. 9.-- Et Ephraim. (ID.) Ephraim meus est, id est, mea est fructificatio, quae est susceptio capitis mei. Haec fructificatio est ex eo quod caput suscepit me, vel ego caput. (CASS.) Vel Ephraim, id est, fructificatio, est susceptio capitis mei, quia dum spineam coronam caput meum suscepit, ultra omnes fructificavit: totum enim Christus lucratus est 1028Cmundum.

VERS. 11.-- Quis deducit me in civitatem munitam. (ID.) Sicut homo, quaerit Christus, ut respondeat; negat hoc ab homine posse fieri. Civitas, infernus quem nullus poterat aperire. Idumeae gentes, quibus post resurrectionem innotuit: haec a sola deitate poterant fieri.

VERS. 12.-- Repulisti nos, et non exibis. (ID.) Pluraliter dicit nos, quia hic Christus cum membris patitur supra, singulariter dicendo, deducet me. Horum omnium expositiones require in nono psalmo.

PSALM CVII.

VERS. 1.-- A canticle of a psalm. (AUG.) From the last parts of the two, etc., as far as that the words of the prophets might be fulfilled. (CASS.) Here are many of the same things as above, etc., as far as and they are well joined together, which in no wise disagree. (ID.) In the first there is treated the flight 1028Aof David, etc., as far as Canticle belongs to divine things, Psalm to actual works.

VERS. 2.-- Prepared. (CASS.) The sixth psalm concerning the two natures in Christ. My heart is ready. First Christ gives thanks, because, taking upon him the passion, he rose again into glory. Secondly, what salvation has been wrought for the whole earth, there, That they may be delivered.

VERS. 7.-- That they may be delivered. (ID.) The second part: what salvation has been wrought for the whole earth over which is the glory; here also the lowliness of the humanity and the power of the majesty are shown.

Save. That they may be delivered in the time to come, here save them, lest they fall. Or, he asks that he himself be saved in the resurrection, that the faithful may be delivered, who by such a sign perceived his Godhead. As it were: that I may sing and give praise, Save 1028Bme in the resurrection by thy right hand, that is, by the Word, who is the arm of the Father, that so thy beloved may be delivered. The order of the words is inverted. For he says: Save me and hear me, and save me.

VERS. 8.-- I will rejoice. (AUG.) Or, I shall be exalted: above, I shall be glad, but here, I shall be exalted, which agrees well enough, because gladness comes of exaltation. And here Christ speaks in the person of the Church.

VERS. 9.-- And Ephraim. (ID.) Ephraim is mine, that is, mine is the fruit-bearing, which is the taking up of my head. This fruit-bearing is from this, that the head took me up, or I the head. (CASS.) Or Ephraim, that is, fruit-bearing, is the taking up of my head, because when my head took up the crown of thorns, it bore fruit beyond all others: for Christ gained the whole 1028Cworld.

VERS. 11.-- Who bringeth me into the strong city. (ID.) As man, Christ asks, that he may answer; he denies that this can be done by man. The city. Hell, which none could open. The Idumeans are the Gentiles, to whom he became known after the resurrection: these things could be done by the Godhead alone.

VERS. 12.-- Thou hast cast us off, and thou wilt not go forth. (ID.) He says "us" in the plural, because here Christ suffers together with his members; above, speaking in the singular, "he will bring me." Seek the expositions of all these things in the ninth psalm.

PSALMUS CVIII.

VERS. 1.-- In finem, Psalmus. (AUG.) Prophetia de Christo, etc., usque ad et quae de Juda expressa sunt, ut illud: Et episcopatum ejus accipiat 1028Dalter.

(CASS.) Quintus eorum qui latius de passione agunt.

VERS. 2.-- Deus laudem. (CASS.) Monet Judae malitiam declinare, etc., usque ad Christus ergo secundum quod homo orans ad Patrem ait: Quia os peccatoris. (ID.) Decora diversitas, quia iniqui non tacent vituperium.

VERS. 3.-- Gratis. (AUG.) Sicut piis per se placet aequitas, sic impiis iniquitas.

VERS. 4.-- Pro eo ut me. (ID.) Plus nocent, in membris detrahentes Christo, quia animas crediturorum interficiunt, quam qui carnem ejus mox resurrecturam peremerunt.

1029AVERS. 5.-- Et posueruent adversum. (AUG.) Sex differentiae sunt, etc., usque ad quod est bonum pro malo, quod est Deus judex facit. (CASS.) Tribus modis omne peccatum contrahitur, etc., usque ad quod Christus orans pro Judaeis fecit.

VERS. 6.-- Constitue super. (AUG.) Secunda pars, ubi incipit prophetare, quae pro impietate recipiant. Supra de pluribus, etc., usque ad quorum personam Judas gessit. Constitue super eum peccatorem. Sicut de Juda, ita de eis.

VERS. 7.-- Cum judicatur exeat condemnatus. Quia in nequitia permanentes thesaurizant sibi iram. Oratio in peccatum: quia non fit per mediatorem.

VERS. 8.-- Dies pauci. Secundum regnum, quod 1029Bpost non diu stetit. Episcopatum, id est Christum (qui ad eos missus) accepit populus gentium.

VERS. 9.-- Filii orphani: amisso, quasi patre, regno; vel patre Deo. Uxor, id est plebs. Viduae, amisso regno.

VERS. 10.-- Transferatur, ut in captivitate factum est. Mendicent, regibus gentium.

VERS. 11.-- Omnem substantiam ejus, id est, vitam, singula peccati puniens; debita eorum non dimittuntur, quia in solo Christo dimittuntur. Et alieni, id est, diabolus et angeli ejus. Diripiant labores ejus, Quia thesaurizant in coelo.

VERS. 12.-- Et non sit illi, etc. Id est, adjutor non est ei, cui Christus deest. Nec sit qui misereatur. Non dico ad temporalia, habenda, sed aeterna.

1029CVERS. 13.-- Fiant nati ejus in interitum sempiternum. Ideo quia manserunt in generatione una, id est, quia non regenerati fuerunt. Et deleatur nomen. Id est, Jerusalem terrenae, quae servit cum filiis suis quae prophetas interfecit.

VERS. 15.-- Et dispereat de terra viventium, id est Ecclesia. Memoria eorum, quia cum essent rami naturales, facti sunt.

VERS. 16.-- Pro eo quod non est recordatus. Poenitendo.

Facere misericordiam. Supra membra Christi.

VERS. 18.-- Maledictionem, et veniet ei: et noluit benedictionem. (AUG.) Peccata modo delectant, sed dicuntur maledictio, quia tormenta parant.

VERS. 19.-- Quo operitur. Videtur dicere hic, 1029Detc., usque ad semper sit paratus, unde hic ait semper praecingitur.

VERS. 20.-- Apud Dominum. (ID.) Specialiter Christo detrahunt, qui dicunt non esse ex Patre, vel minorem Patre. Mala adversus animam. Dicentes, non potuisse surgere, cum vellet.

VERS. 21.-- Et tu, Domine. (CASS.) Tertia pars, ubi precatur, etc., usque ad adjuva me, secundum hominem. Propter nomen tuum. Nullis enim operum etc., usque ad quia suavis est misericordia tua.

VERS. 22.-- Quia egenus et pauper. (ID.) Egestas et paupertas Christi est infirmitas, ex qua crucifixus est.

1030AVERS. 23.-- Sicut umbra cum declinat ablatus sum. (CASS.) Sicut ex umbra declinante fit nox, sic ex mortali carne fit mors.

VERS. 24.-- Immutata est. (AUG.) Immutata est ergo caro Christi, etc., usque ad quia Jesus nondum fuit glorificatus. Propter oleum, id est, spiritualem gratiam, unde Christus dicitur.

VERS. 25.-- Moverunt capita. (CASS.) Furiosi commotione capitis minantur. (AUG.) Moverunt capita, quia viderunt pendere in cruce, sed nondum quando caro immutata.

VERS. 26.-- Adjuva me, Domine. (CASS.) Rogat ut homo, praestat ut Deus.

VERS. 27.-- Manus tua haec. (AUG.) Christus haec manus, et est Verbum apud Deum et fecit eam, dum Verbum caro factum est. Erat enim sine 1030Btempore secundum divinitatem, et facta est in tempore secundum carnem.

VERS. 28.-- Maledicent illi et tu benedices. Una est maledictio malorum Deus, cum benedicit, facit quod dicit.

VERS. 29.-- Sicut diploide, etc. Alii interpretantur pro diploide, duplex pallium, id est, confundantur intus et foris, id est, coram Deo, et hominibus.

VERS. 30.-- Nimis in ore meo. Solet poni nimis, pro plus quam debet, sed et pro valde. In medio. (AUG.) Id est, in communi, vel in corde.

VERS. 31.-- Quia astitit a dextris pauperis. Diabolus a dextris Judae, etc., usque ad sed ut animam 1030Csalvaret a persequentibus.

PSALM CVIII.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end, a psalm. (AUG.) A prophecy concerning Christ, etc., as far as and the things which are expressed concerning Judas, as that: And his bishopric let another 1028Dtake.

(CASS.) The fifth of those which treat more at large of the passion.

VERS. 2.-- O God, praise. (CASS.) He admonishes men to turn aside from the malice of Judas, etc., as far as Christ therefore, according as he is man, praying to the Father says: For the mouth of the sinner. (ID.) A comely diversity, because the wicked are not silent in their reviling.

VERS. 3.-- Without cause. (AUG.) As equity pleases the godly of itself, so does iniquity the ungodly.

VERS. 4.-- In return for this, that me. (ID.) They do more hurt who detract from Christ in his members, because they slay the souls of them that would believe, than they who slew his flesh, soon about to rise again.

1029AVERS. 5.-- And they set posueruent against. (AUG.) There are six differences, etc., as far as which is good for evil, which is, God the judge does. (CASS.) In three ways is every sin contracted, etc., as far as which Christ did when he prayed for the Jews.

VERS. 6.-- Set thou over. (AUG.) The second part, where he begins to prophesy what they shall receive for their impiety. Above, of many, etc., as far as whose person Judas bore. Set thou a sinner over him. As of Judas, so of them.

VERS. 7.-- When he is judged, may he go out condemned. Because, abiding in wickedness, they treasure up wrath to themselves. Prayer unto sin: because it is not made through the Mediator.

VERS. 8.-- Few days. According to the kingdom, which 1029Bdid not stand long after. The bishopric, that is, Christ (who was sent to them), the people of the Gentiles received.

VERS. 9.-- Children fatherless: the kingdom, as a father, being lost; or God the Father. The wife, that is, the people. Widows, the kingdom being lost.

VERS. 10.-- Let it be transferred, as was done in the captivity. Let them beg, of the kings of the Gentiles.

VERS. 11.-- All his substance, that is, his life, punishing each single thing of sin; their debts are not forgiven, because in Christ alone are they forgiven. And strangers, that is, the devil and his angels. Let them plunder his labours, Because they lay up treasure in heaven [thesaurizant; read non thesaurizant, "lay not up"].

VERS. 12.-- And let there not be for him, etc. That is, there is no helper for him to whom Christ is wanting. Nor let there be any to have mercy. I say not for the having of temporal things, but of eternal.

1029CVERS. 13.-- Let his children be given over to destruction everlasting. Therefore, because they remained in one generation, that is, because they were not regenerated. And let the name be blotted out. That is, of the earthly Jerusalem, which is in bondage with her children, which slew the prophets.

VERS. 15.-- And let it perish from the land of the living, that is, the Church. Their memory, because, though they were natural branches, so they became.

VERS. 16.-- Because he remembered not. By doing penance.

To shew mercy. Upon the members of Christ.

VERS. 18.-- Cursing, and it shall come to him: and he would not have blessing. (AUG.) Sins delight for a season, but they are called a cursing, because they prepare torments.

VERS. 19.-- Wherewith he is covered. He seems to say here, 1029Detc., as far as let him be always ready, whence here he says he is girded always.

VERS. 20.-- With the Lord. (ID.) They detract from Christ especially who say that he is not of the Father, or that he is less than the Father. Evils against the soul. Saying that he could not rise again when he would.

VERS. 21.-- And thou, O Lord. (CASS.) The third part, where he prays, etc., as far as help me, according to the man. For thy name's sake. For by no works, etc., as far as because thy mercy is sweet.

VERS. 22.-- Because needy and poor. (ID.) The neediness and poverty of Christ is the infirmity out of which he was crucified.

1030AVERS. 23.-- I am taken away as the shadow when it declineth. (CASS.) As night comes of the declining shadow, so death comes of mortal flesh.

VERS. 24.-- It hath been changed. (AUG.) The flesh of Christ therefore has been changed, etc., as far as because Jesus was not yet glorified. Because of the oil, that is, spiritual grace, whence Christ is named.

VERS. 25.-- They moved their heads. (CASS.) Madmen threaten by the shaking of the head. (AUG.) They moved their heads, because they saw him hanging on the cross, but not yet when the flesh was changed.

VERS. 26.-- Help me, O Lord. (CASS.) He asks as man, he grants as God.

VERS. 27.-- This is thy hand. (AUG.) Christ is this hand, and he is the Word with God, and he made it, when the Word was made flesh. For he was without 1030Btime according to the Godhead, and it was made in time according to the flesh.

VERS. 28.-- They shall curse, and thou wilt bless. One is the cursing of the wicked; God, when he blesses, does what he says.

VERS. 29.-- As with a diploide, etc. Others interpret, for diploide, a double cloak, that is, let them be confounded within and without, that is, before God and before men.

VERS. 30.-- Exceedingly in my mouth. Exceedingly is wont to be put for more than is due, but also for greatly. In the midst. (AUG.) That is, in common, or in the heart.

VERS. 31.-- Because he hath stood at the right hand of the poor. The devil at the right hand of Judas, etc., as far as but that he might save the soul 1030Cfrom them that persecute it.

PSALMUS CIX.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus David. (CASS.) Psalmus iste septimus, etc., usque ad quiquid in utroque Testamento continetur. (CASS.) Propheta hortatur Christo subjici. Primo refert propheta verba Patris de Filio, etc., usque ad hoc humanitatis.

Dixit Dominus. (CASS.) More nostro, ut homo instruatur. Dominus Domino. Personas discerne, et unam naturam, et potentiam accipe. Sede. Post laborem quiesce, et conregna, secundum quod homo. A dextris meis. In potioribus meis bonis et occultis, donec regnes manifestus. Et hoc est, donec ponam inimicos tuos, etc. (AUG.) Sede, non solum in alto, ut excelsis domineris, sed etiam in occulto, etc., 1030Dusque ad si non videt quod credit. Scabellum pedum tuorum: a similitudine, ubi et plena notatur subjectio. Per pedes stabilitas aeterna: hoc quotidie in conversis.

VERS. 2.-- Virgam virtutis. Incipit autem ex Sion, id est, ex Judaeis regnum Christi, unde subdit, Virgam virtutis, etc. Ex Sion. Non de illo regno Christi loquitur propheta, etc., usque ad et remissio peccatorum per omnes gentes, incipientibus a Jerosolyma.

VERS. 3.-- Tecum principium. (CASS.) Secundo indicat Pater naturam Divinitatis, etc., usque ad quando in resurrectione erunt splendidi, ut angeli Dei. (AUG.) 1031AJam dominatur, jam virtus; sed in die specialis virtutis, etc., usque ad qualiter Pater cum eo principium. Hoc tunc, sed nunc. Ex utero, id est, ut ex secreta et occulta substantia mea, etc., usque ad qui se offerat, unde sequitur, Juravit, etc. (CASS.) Vel Tecum principium: hoc Pater; quasi, hoc tibi tribuo plus quam alii, quia Filius per naturam. (AUG.) Vel ex persona prophetae potest accipi loquentis, etc., usque ad cum Spiritu sancto, qui sanctos splendificat.

VERS. 4.-- Juravit Dominus. (CASS.) Tertio agit propheta de humanitate Christi, etc., usque ad hinc constat transire victimas secundum ordinem Aaron. Non poenitebit eum: tu es sacerdos, in aeternum. (AUG.) In Deum nulla cadit poenitentia: scit enim 1031Bquid agat, nec mutat consilium, sed verbo poenitentiae mutatio rerum aliter quam sperabat evenientium significatur. Quomodo enim cum aliquid poenitet te fecisse, doles factum quod fecisti.

VERS. 5.-- Reges (AUG.) Qui volunt, vel volebant delere nomen Christi.

VERS. 6.-- Conquassabit, id est infirmos reddidit, etc., usque ad et nunc judicabit in gentibus, ut ruinas, non erectos impleat. Judicabit in nationibus. (CASS.) Quasi reges frangit pro superbia: populos judicat propter communia peccata: utrosque ut humilientur ad conversionem. Vel,

VERS. 7.-- De torrente. (CASS.) De transitoria passione et turbulenta. In via, qua itur ad aliam mansionem.

1031CExaltabit caput. Unde: Propter hoc exaltavit illum, et dedit Deus illi nomen, quod est super omne nomen, ut in nomine Jesu omne genu flectatur, coelestium, terrestrium et infernorum, et omnis lingua confiteatur quia Dominus Jesus Christus est in gloria Dei Patris.

PSALM CIX.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of David. (CASS.) This psalm is the seventh, etc., as far as whatsoever quiquid is contained in either Testament. (CASS.) The prophet exhorts men to be made subject to Christ. First the prophet relates the words of the Father concerning the Son, etc., as far as this belongs to the humanity.

The Lord said. (CASS.) After our manner, that man may be instructed. The Lord to the Lord. Distinguish the persons, and receive one nature and one power. Sit thou. After labour, rest, and reign together, according as thou art man. At my right hand. Among my better and hidden goods, until thou reign manifest. And this is, until I make thy enemies, etc. (AUG.) Sit thou, not only on high, that thou mayest have dominion over the exalted, but also in secret, etc., 1030Das far as if he sees not what he believes. A footstool for thy feet: from a similitude, wherein also full subjection is marked. By the feet, eternal stability: this daily in them that are converted.

VERS. 2.-- The rod of power. Now the kingdom of Christ begins out of Sion, that is, from the Jews, whence he subjoins, The rod of power, etc. Out of Sion. The prophet speaks not of that kingdom of Christ, etc., as far as and remission of sins throughout all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.

VERS. 3.-- With thee the beginning. (CASS.) Secondly the Father declares the nature of the Godhead, etc., as far as when in the resurrection they shall be resplendent, as the angels of God. (AUG.) 1031AAlready he has dominion, already there is power; but in the day of his special power, etc., as far as in what manner the Father is with him the beginning. This then, but now. From the womb, that is, as from my secret and hidden substance, etc., as far as one who may offer himself, whence there follows, He hath sworn, etc. (CASS.) Or With thee the beginning: this the Father says; as it were, this I grant to thee more than to another, because thou art the Son by nature. (AUG.) Or it can be taken as of the person of the prophet speaking, etc., as far as with the Holy Ghost, who makes the saints resplendent.

VERS. 4.-- The Lord hath sworn. (CASS.) Thirdly the prophet treats of the humanity of Christ, etc., as far as hence it is plain that the victims pass away according to the order of Aaron. It shall not repent him: thou art a priest, for ever. (AUG.) Upon God no repentance falls: for he knows 1031Bwhat he does, nor does he change his counsel; but by the word "repentance" is signified the change of things falling out otherwise than one hoped. For in what manner, when it repents thee to have done anything, thou grievest for the deed which thou hast done.

VERS. 5.-- Kings (AUG.) Who wish, or wished, to blot out the name of Christ.

VERS. 6.-- He shall crush, that is, he has rendered them weak, etc., as far as and now he shall judge among the Gentiles, that he may fill ruins, not the upright. He shall judge among nations. (CASS.) As it were, he breaks kings for their pride: he judges peoples for their common sins: both, that they may be humbled unto conversion. Or,

VERS. 7.-- Of the torrent. (CASS.) Of the passing and troubled passion. In the way, whereby men go to another dwelling.

1031CHe shall lift up the head. Whence: For this cause he exalted him, and God gave him a name which is above every name, that in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of them that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth, and that every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.

PSALMUS CX.

Alleluia. (CASS.) Primus psalmus per omnes litteras alphabeti, etc., usque ad tertio eosdem redemptos asserit, et Novum Testamentum mansurum, ibi Redemptionem.

VERS. 1.-- Confitebor. (AUG.) Non est hic confessio peccatorum, sed laudis: illa luget, haec gaudet: illa vulnus medico ostendit, haec de sanitate gratias agit. In concilio. Non temere, sed ex ratione, scilicet 1031Dpro aeternis, sicut omnes justi. (CASS.) In concilio justorum. Hic nunquam inter omnes justos ubi sunt misti mali, sed jam videntur in futura societate psallere spe rapti ad superna. In concilio, quod est, quando cum Domino judicant. In congregatione, quando de toto collecti.

VERS. 2.-- Magna opera. Haec est materia et causa confessionis. Magna sunt opera Domini, quod de impio facit pium. Exquisita. (AUG., CASS.) Cui nihil simile, dum sinit diabolum saevire, etc., usque ad non: Justitia enim ejus manet in saeculum saeculi. In omnes voluntates. (AUG.) Nihil superat voluntatem Dei, qui et si vult, ut non pecces, non tamen prohibet. Si vult parcere poenitenti, vult et impoenitentem punire; 1032Aita de homine semper Deus implet suam voluntatem, quia nihil facit homo, de quo non operetur Deus, quod vult.

VERS. 3.-- Confessio et magnificentia opus ejus. (CASS.) Quasi confitebor, quia magna sunt opera Domini. Quaelibet etiam opera sunt magna, si in eis videatur intentio et voluntas, quae est confessio peccatorum, et magnificentia bonorum operum: et justitia, id est, merces, quae juste datur.

VERS. 4.-- Memoriam fecit. (ID.) Secundo dicit fideles copioso munere satiatos, promittens adventum Domini, ut haereditas avide quaeratur. (AUG.) Memoriam fecit mirabilium suorum. Hunc humilians et hunc exaltans, etc., usque ad quid in futura glorificatur accipiet?

1032BVERS. 5.-- Escam dedit. (CASS.) Facit confessionem et magnificentiam, etc., usque ad ut omnia impleantur. Memor erit, etc. (AUG.) Nec totum dedit, qui pignus dedit, etc., usque ad per compungentes passionis angustias intrant.

VERS. 6.-- Virtutem operum. (CASS.) Virtus operum est, quod caeci vident, etc. Quae fecit nota Christiano populo. Ut det illis haereditatem, haec fuit intentio miraculorum, ut crederent.

VERS. 7.-- Ut det illis haereditatem gentium. (ID.) Quasi, licet illis det haereditatem, tamen multa patientur. Opera manuum ejus. (ID.) Id est, virtutis. Veritas, dum conversis promissa restituit: Judicium, quod impiis minatur. (AUG.) Veritas, quam sancti martyres tenent, pro qua et judicantur 1032Chic; et judicium, quo in futuro judicabunt eos a quibus hic judicantur. (ID.) Opera manuum ejus veritas et judicium. Teneatur veritas ab his qui judicantur, etc., usque ad hic est haereditas Novi Testamenti.

VERS. 8.-- Fidelia omnia mandata. (CASS.) Quia servant servantes se, non sunt mendacia. Confirmata. Non in cassum missa, ut verba humana: Facta non tantum dicta, in veritate, quia omnia complentur.

In aequitate. (AUG.) Quia omnia cum libra justitiae.

VERS. 9, 10.-- Redemptionem misit. (CASS.) Tertio, redemptos asserit, et Testamentum Novum aeterna gratia consecratum, vel. Nomen ejus: initium sapientiae. (ID.) Id est Filius, qui in humanitate sanctus, 1032Dpotentia deitatis terribilis. Ametur ergo advocatus, timeatur judex, ne sis negligens, ne desperes.

Timor Domini. (ID.) Metus judicii janua est conversionis, si addatur discretio dilectionis. Laudatio ejus manet. Intentio psalmi unde alleluia praescribitur, a laude incoepit, in laude finit, populus fidelis a diabolo liberatus gratias agens, expressit, quid et hic faciendum sit devotis, et in coelo peragendum, hic quia liberat, ibi quia coronat.

PSALM CX.

Alleluia. (CASS.) The first psalm through all the letters of the alphabet, etc., as far as thirdly he affirms the same men redeemed, and the New Testament abiding, there, Redemption.

VERS. 1.-- I will give praise. (AUG.) Here there is no confession of sins, but of praise: the one mourns, this rejoices: the one shows the wound to the physician, this gives thanks for health. In the council. Not rashly, but out of reason, namely 1031Dfor things eternal, as all the just do. (CASS.) In the council of the just. Here never among all the just, where the wicked are mingled with them, but they are seen already to sing in the fellowship to come, caught up by hope to the things above. In the council, which is, when they judge with the Lord. In the congregation, when they are gathered together out of the whole.

VERS. 2.-- Great works. This is the matter and the cause of the confession. Great are the works of the Lord, in that he makes a godly man out of an ungodly. Sought out. (AUG., CASS.) To which nothing is like, while he suffers the devil to rage, etc., as far as not: for his justice remaineth for ever and ever. Unto all the wills. (AUG.) Nothing surpasses the will of God, who, even if he wills that thou sin not, yet does not prevent it. If he wills to spare the penitent, he wills also to punish the impenitent; 1032Aso concerning man God always fulfils his own will, because man does nothing out of which God does not work what he wills.

VERS. 3.-- Confession and magnificence is his work. (CASS.) As it were: I will give praise, because great are the works of the Lord. Any works soever are also great, if in them there be seen the intention and the will, which is the confession of sins, and the magnificence of good works: and justice, that is, the reward which is justly given.

VERS. 4.-- He hath made a remembrance. (ID.) Secondly he says that the faithful are filled with a plentiful gift, promising the coming of the Lord, that the inheritance may be eagerly sought. (AUG.) He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works. Humbling this man and exalting that, etc., as far as what shall he receive, he is glorified [glorificatur; read glorificatus, "glorified"], in the things to come?

1032BVERS. 5.-- He hath given food. (CASS.) He makes confession and magnificence, etc., as far as that all things may be fulfilled. He will be mindful, etc. (AUG.) Nor did he give the whole who gave a pledge, etc., as far as they enter through the piercing straits of the passion.

VERS. 6.-- The power of the works. (CASS.) The power of the works is that the blind see, etc. Which things he made known to the Christian people. That he may give them the inheritance, this was the intent of the miracles, that they might believe.

VERS. 7.-- That he may give them the inheritance of the Gentiles. (ID.) As it were: although he gives them the inheritance, yet they shall suffer many things. The works of his hands. (ID.) That is, of his power. Truth, while he restores to the converted what was promised: Judgment, which he threatens to the ungodly. (AUG.) Truth, which the holy martyrs hold, and for which they are also judged 1032Chere; and judgment, whereby in time to come they shall judge those by whom they are here judged. (ID.) The works of his hands are truth and judgment. Let truth be held by those who are judged, etc., as far as this is the inheritance of the New Testament.

VERS. 8.-- All the commandments are faithful. (CASS.) Because they keep those who keep them, they are not lies. Confirmed. Not sent forth in vain, as human words are: Made, not only spoken, in truth, because all are fulfilled.

In equity. (AUG.) Because all things are done with the balance of justice.

VERS. 9, 10.-- He hath sent redemption. (CASS.) Thirdly he affirms the redeemed, and the New Testament consecrated by eternal grace; or. His name: the beginning of wisdom. (ID.) That is, the Son, who in his humanity is holy, 1032Din the power of the Godhead terrible. Let the advocate therefore be loved, let the judge be feared, lest thou be negligent, lest thou despair.

The fear of the Lord. (ID.) The dread of judgment is the gate of conversion, if the discernment of love be added to it. His praise continueth. The intent of the psalm, whence Alleluia is prefixed, began with praise and ends in praise: the faithful people, delivered from the devil and giving thanks, has expressed what is to be done here also by the devout, and to be accomplished in heaven: here because he delivers, there because he crowns.

PSALMUS CXI.

Alleluia reversionis. (AUG.) Aggaeus et Zacharias longe post David fuerunt, etc., usque ad aeternaliter solidetur. (CASS.) Perfectio hujus aedificii, etc., usque 1033Aad tanquam a captivitate liberavi et hilares de bonis quae habent.

VERS. 1.-- Beatus vir. (CASS.) Ostendit hic Psalmista post liberationem, etc., usque ad tertio impiis adversa provenire asserit. Qui timet Dominum. Timor mundi miseros facit, sed timor Dei ea appetere facit, per quae homo beatus est. In mandatis. Hoc timor Dei, ut velit. Et non ait faciet, etc., usque ad et terrena inhabitatio deprimit sensum multa cogitantem.

VERS. 2.-- Potens. (AUG., CASS.) Ecce praemia illius beati. Semen ejus. Id est, merces boni operis; Erit potens in terra, non hac, ubi derisui, sed coelesti. Vel etiam hic in isto tempore, quo minus videtur. Semen, opera misericordiae unde messis aeterna. Potens, quia re minima, etiam ut magna, regnum coelorum 1033Bemitur. Generatio. Non carnis sed imitationis. Vel opera rectorum. Recti sunt, qui non resistunt Patri emendanti, et credunt promittenti, non credunt perisse opera sua, cum non eis temporaliter retribuitur. Sunt enim qui bona illa agunt, mercedem hic a Deo sperantes, vel hominibus placere volentes, quod non beatus vir: et tamen,

VERS. 3.-- Gloria et divitiae in domo ejus. Id est, in cordis secreto, ubi habitat cum spe vitae aeternae, ubi divitiae sanctae, et gloria aeterna reponuntur. Justitia. Haec est gloria ejus, hae divitiae ejus, quam tamen habet a Deo. Manet in saeculum. Quasi non temporaliter beatus.

VERS. 4.-- Exortum est. (CASS.) Secundo agit de adventu Domini, etc., usque ad ut eam firmis allegationibus 1033Cet assertionibus in judicio praemuniat. Vel,

VERS. 5.-- Miseretur. (ID.) Qui dat egentibus, Commodat, qui mutuum praestat, post tantumdem recepturus.

VERS. 7, 8.-- Paratum cor ejus sperare in Domino, confirmatum est cor ejus, manet, etc. (AUG.) Patet itaque, quod hic non sua quaerit, sed quae sunt Christi, labores patienter sustinet, promissa fidenter exspectat. (CASS.) Vel, si quis mala minatur, non timet, sed paratum.

VERS. 9.-- Dispersit. Sperat non timere, quia dispersit. Dedit pauperibus. (AUG.) Ecce iste emebat quod non videbat, sed ille thesaurum in coelo servabat, qui esurire et sitire in pauperibus dignatur in terris. Justitia ejus manet in saeculum saeculi. (CASS.) 1033DSua dedit, et juste et pie vixit, vel, qui dat sua, justitiam operatur. Cornu ejus exaltabitur in gloria. Quia hic humilis, ibi potestatem habebit.

VERS. 10-- Peccator videbit. (ID.) Tertio contraria impiis provenire asserit. Bonis beatorum hortatur, malis inimicorum terret, et est iste psalmus institutorius fidelium.

Irascetur, dentibus suis fremet et tabescet, desiderium peccatorum peribit, dicens: Quid nobis profuit superbia et divitiarum jactantia? (Sap. V)

PSALM CXI.

Alleluia of the return. (AUG.) Aggeus and Zacharias were long after David, etc., as far as it may be made firm eternally. (CASS.) The perfection of this building, etc., as far 1033Aas as though men delivered liberavi from captivity and glad because of the good things which they have.

VERS. 1.-- Blessed is the man. (CASS.) Here the Psalmist shows, after the deliverance, etc., as far as thirdly he affirms that adverse things befall the ungodly. That feareth the Lord. The fear of the world makes men wretched, but the fear of God makes a man desire those things whereby he is blessed. In the commandments. This the fear of God does, that he should will. And he says not "he shall do," etc., as far as and the earthly habitation presseth down the mind that museth upon many things.

VERS. 2.-- Mighty. (AUG., CASS.) Behold the rewards of that blessed man. His seed. That is, the reward of a good work; Shall be mighty upon earth, not upon this earth, where he is a laughing-stock, but upon the heavenly. Or even here in this present time, wherein it is less seen. Seed, the works of mercy, whence comes the everlasting harvest. Mighty, because with a very small thing, even as with a great one, the kingdom of heaven 1033Bis bought. The generation. Not of the flesh, but of imitation. Or the works of the upright. The upright are they who resist not the Father when he corrects, and who believe him when he promises, and who believe not that their works have perished when no requital is made them in time. For there are those who do those good things while hoping here for a reward from God, or wishing to please men, which is not the blessed man: and yet,

VERS. 3.-- Glory and wealth in his house. That is, in the secret of the heart, where he dwells with the hope of eternal life, where holy riches and eternal glory are laid up. Justice. This is his glory, these are his riches, which nevertheless he has from God. It remaineth for ever. As it were, he is not blessed for a time.

VERS. 4.-- There hath risen up. (CASS.) Secondly he treats of the coming of the Lord, etc., as far as that he may fortify it beforehand with firm allegations 1033Cand assertions in the judgment. Or,

VERS. 5.-- He sheweth mercy. (ID.) He who gives to the needy; He lendeth, he who grants a loan, to receive afterwards as much again.

VERS. 7, 8.-- His heart is ready to hope in the Lord, his heart is strengthened, it remaineth, etc. (AUG.) It is plain therefore that this man seeks not his own things, but the things which are Christ's; he bears labours patiently, he awaits the promises with confidence. (CASS.) Or, if any man threatens evils, he fears not, but is ready.

VERS. 9.-- He hath distributed. He hopes not to fear, because he has distributed. He hath given to the poor. (AUG.) Behold, this man was buying what he did not see, but that other was keeping a treasure for him in heaven, who vouchsafes to hunger and to thirst in the poor upon earth. His justice remaineth for ever and ever. (CASS.) 1033DHe gave what was his own, and lived justly and godly; or, he who gives what is his own works justice. His horn shall be exalted in glory. Because he is humble here, there he shall have power.

VERS. 10.-- The sinner shall see. (ID.) Thirdly he affirms that contrary things befall the ungodly. By the good things of the blessed he exhorts, by the evils of the enemies he terrifies, and this psalm is an instructor of the faithful.

He shall be angry, he shall gnash with his teeth and pine away, the desire of the wicked shall perish, saying: What hath pride profited us, and the boasting of riches? (Sap. V)

PSALMUS CXII.

Alleluia (CASS.) Quia merito laudandus, qui merito humilitatis gentes assumit, titulum psalmi exponit. 1034AAlleluia enim, ut diximus, interpretatur laudate Dominum, qualiter et psalmus incipit.

VERS. 1.-- Laudate. (ID.) Primo monet Propheta devotos, ut laudent jugiter, et ubique praedicent. Secundo ipse facit, quod monet alios, id est, laudat Deum ibi: Quis sicut Dominus (I Cor. XIV)? Ad laudem ergo monens ostendit, qui et quem, et quandiu, et ubi, et quare laudent, dicit. Pueri. Non sensu, sed malitia, maxime superbia, id est, humiles, unde, Nolite pueri effici sensibus, sed malitia parvuli estote, ut mentibus perfecti sitis. (AUG., CASS.) Laudate Dominum, pueri, simplices et puri, qui debent laudare.

VERS. 2.-- Sit nomen. (CASS.) Ecce dixit, qui, et quem laudare debeant, deinde subdit: Quandiu laudamus sit, scilicet semper. Sit nomen Domini: 1034Bne ad horam putetis me imperare laudem, etc., usque ad per gentes carnales, per coelos spirituales.

VERS. 3.-- A solis ortu. (AUG.) Hic dicit quod ubique debeat laudari.

VERS. 4.-- Super coelos. (ID.) Apostolos, per quos regnat in gentibus, et est; ideo ad laudes invito, quia super omnes est regnaturus.

VERS. 5.-- Quis sicut. (CASS.) Secundo ipse facit, quod alios monet, ut et facto alios doceat. Quis? Nullus qui per se possit. In altis, etc. Angelis et sanctis: et licet altus, non despicit humiles.

VERS. 6.-- Humilia. Hi sunt qui dono ejus alti fiunt, et in eis sedet. Respicit, humiles singulos. In terra, sanctos quos ita respicit, sicut e converso odit superbos.

1034CVERS. 7.-- Suscitans a terra: de labore corporis. De stercore, erigitur cui carnis vitia non dominantur.

VERS. 9.-- Qui habitare. (CASS., AUG.) Exponit, ubi suscitat et erigit, etc., usque ad de mammona iniquitatis per opera misericordiae. Sterilem. (AUG.) Scilicet, Saram, id est, Ecclesiam gentilem, quae prius sterilis fuit, unde per Saram significatur. Eam, inquam, facit habitare in domo, id est, in Ecclesia Judaeorum, inter ipsos Judaeos, ut in lapide angulari duo parietes conjungantur, et fiat unum ovile. Filiorum. (ID.) Ex persona quorum haec dicuntur, etc., usque ad cum sciam me esse sine filiis, et viduam.

PSALM CXII.

Alleluia (CASS.) Because he is worthily to be praised who by the merit of humility takes up the Gentiles, he expounds the title of the psalm. 1034AFor Alleluia, as we have said, is interpreted "praise ye the Lord," in which manner the psalm also begins.

VERS. 1.-- Praise ye. (ID.) First the Prophet admonishes the devout to praise continually, and everywhere to preach. Secondly he himself does what he admonishes others to do, that is, he praises God there: Who is as the Lord (I Cor. XIV)? Admonishing therefore unto praise, he shows and says who and whom, and how long, and where, and why they should praise. Children. Not in sense, but in malice, and chiefly in pride, that is, the humble; whence, Be not children in sense, but in malice be children, that in mind ye may be perfect. (AUG., CASS.) Praise the Lord, ye children, the simple and the pure, who ought to praise.

VERS. 2.-- Let the name be. (CASS.) Behold, he has said who and whom they ought to praise; then he subjoins how long we praise [laudamus; read laudandus, "is to be praised"], namely always. Let the name of the Lord be: 1034Blest ye think that I command praise for an hour, etc., as far as by the Gentiles the carnal, by the heavens the spiritual.

VERS. 3.-- From the rising of the sun. (AUG.) Here he says that he ought to be praised everywhere.

VERS. 4.-- Above the heavens. (ID.) The Apostles, through whom he reigns among the Gentiles, and is; therefore I invite to praises, because he is to reign above all.

VERS. 5.-- Who is as. (CASS.) Secondly he himself does what he admonishes others to do, that by the deed also he may teach others. Who? None that can of himself. In the high places, etc. In the angels and the saints: and although he is high, he despises not the lowly.

VERS. 6.-- The lowly things. These are they who by his gift are made high, and in them he sits. He beholdeth, the lowly one by one. In the earth, the saints, whom he so beholds as, on the contrary, he hates the proud.

1034CVERS. 7.-- Raising up from the earth: from the labour of the body. Out of the dunghill, he is lifted up over whom the vices of the flesh have no dominion.

VERS. 9.-- Who maketh to dwell. (CASS., AUG.) He expounds where he raises up and lifts up, etc., as far as out of the mammon of iniquity by works of mercy. The barren woman. (AUG.) Namely Sara, that is, the Gentile Church, which was barren before, whereby she is signified by Sara. Her, I say, he makes to dwell in the house, that is, in the Church of the Jews, among the Jews themselves, that in the corner-stone the two walls may be joined together, and there may be made one fold. Of children. (ID.) In whose person these things are said, etc., as far as since I know myself to be without children, and a widow.

PSALMUS CXIII.

1034DAlleluia. (CASS.) Item hic alleluia ex alio negotio ponitur, etc., usque ad ut in psalmi expositione clarescit.

VERS. 1.-- In exitu. (AUG.) Hic non narrantur praeterita; sed futura praedicuntur, quia in illis gestis futura signabantur: et ideo non omnia hic dicuntur, quae ibi gesta, sed quaedam aliter, ne putetur praeterita recolere. (CASS.) Primo dicit Propheta, quae mira dederit Deus Hebraeis in figura, et Christianis in spiritu. Secundo interrogat quare haec facta sunt ibi, Quid est tibi mare? Tertio inania simulacra gentium reprobat, et religionem Dei commendat, ibi, Simulacra gentium.

In exitu. Quasi cum Israel, id est, domus Jacob, de Aegypto, id est populo barbaro exiret.

1035ABarbaro. (AUG.) Barbara lingua est, quae Deum non laudat.

VERS. 2.-- Facta est. (CASS.) Sicut ille populus, cum exiret de Aegypto, etc., usque ad possunt resistere vitiis, et hoc.

VERS. 3.-- Vidit mare, id est, peccatores saeculi. Jordanis, qui variis desideriis rapiunt homines in magnum mare, id est, hujus saeculi amaricantem malitiam; sed haec in adventu Domini cessant, quasi conversa retrorsum.

Mare vidit. (AUG.) Hoc hic aliter dicitur, quam factum est. Ibi legitur stetisse ab ea parte, qua aquae desuper fluebant, nec ibi quidquam dicitur de gestientibus montibus, sed tam ibi facta quam hic dicta figurae sunt.

1035BVERS. 4.-- Arietes. (ID.) Qui cornibus utriusque, etc., usque ad omnem scientiam adversus Christum se erigentem. Colles. (CASS.) A colendo, mediocres: non enim haec ad litteram; unde et per mare, et Jordanem, id est, per antiqua facta, haec signari non ambigas, quae hodie spiritualiter fiunt.

VERS. 5.-- Quid est tibi. (ID.) Secundo interrogat quare haec, ut excitet admirationem. Et solvit: A facie Domini.

VERS. 7.-- A facie. (ID.) Una duobus responsio, quia unus auctor, et saecula fecit obstupescere, et sua, id est, montes et colles gaudere: Christo enim apparente moti sunt homines a sua superstitione ad cultum Dei.

A facie Dei Jacob. Et quasi quaereret, quis est Dominus? 1035CDeus Jacob non recens; qui facit eos luctari.

VERS. 8.-- Qui convertit petram. (ID.) Dura corda Judaeorum, ad aquam baptismi.

Rupem. Gentiles, ut et ipsi emanent irriguos fontes praedicationis.

(AUG.) Id est, se prius durum, cum ignoraretur, etc., usque ad omnibus credentibus inundaret, dicens: Si quis sitit, veniat ad me, et bibat.

VERS. 1.-- Non nobis. (CASS.) Cum dixit Deum bona dare, etc., usque ad veritas, dum praemia restituit, vel impios punit. Ideo, Da.

VERS. 2.-- Nequando: hoc saepe impii imputant bonis afflictis.

Misericordia. (AUG.), id est, reparatione.

Veritate, id est, promissione impleta.

1035DUbi est Deus. (ID.) Hoc solent dicere gentes, quae habent visibiles deos: quia invisibilem Deum colimus.

VERS. 3.-- In coelo. (ID.), id est, Christo homine, secundum illud: Deus erat in Christo mundum sibi reconcilians. Vel, in coelo, (CASS.) id est, potens super omnes creaturas.

Omnia quaecunque voluit fecit. Per quod omnipotens apparet.

VERS. 4.-- Simulacra gentium. (ID.) Tertio, inania simulacra probat, et religio Dei quam sit utilis ostendit. Et est hic perfecta demonstratio in vituperatione et laude. (AUG.) Ostensa potentia veri Dei ex operibus, transit ad deos gentium visibiles. Argentum. (ID.) Sed quia Deus hoc fecit, inquit, Opera 1036Amanuum hominum, hoc venerantur quod inde fecerunt, materiam enim creavit Deus; sed stultitia hominum formam addidit.

VERS. 5.-- Os habent. (ID.) Manu sunt formata, etc., usque ad et servierunt creaturae potius quam creatori.

VERS. 7.-- Non clamabunt. (ID.) Post loqui (quod est hominis proprium) hoc commune addit, etc., usque ad et carens vita sensuque simulacrum.

VERS. 8.-- Similes illis. (ID.) Vide erubescibilem culturam, dum ait, similes, quod vere sunt; vel similes se eis intelligant.

VERS. 9.-- Domus Israel. (CASS.) Hic ostendit Christianae religionis utilitatem.

VERS. 10.-- Domus Aaron. (AUG.) Ne autem videatur majoribus jam res, quae inferioribus est 1036Bspes, addit, Domus Aaron.

VERS. 12.-- Memor. (CASS.) Ut converteret, et conversos per eumdem benedixit.

VERS. 14.-- Super vos. (AUG.) Quia crevit numerus magistrorum.

Super filios. Quia crevit etiam numerus sequacium. Ergo vos utrique, patres et filii, benedicti estis Domino, qui vos fecit coelum in majoribus, et terram in minoribus; vel fecit omnem creaturam.

VERS. 15.-- Benedicti vos a Domino. (CASS.) Qui optavit supra benedici, jam confisus dicit, Benedicti, quod ad Deum pertinet, ut ei serviatis. Vere Domino, quia etiam coelum coeli, id est, Christus est ad honorem Domini; vel,

VERS. 16.-- Coelum coeli, id est, empyreum, dedit 1036CDomino Christo, secundum quod homo. Terram autem. Istam inferiorem dedit. Filiis hominum. Ut in ea se purificent vel populum praedicatoribus; unde: Sicut misit me Pater, et ego mittam vos (Joan. VI).

Coelum coeli. (AUG.) Dicit eos quorum mentes, etc., usque ad quem infirmi sine adminiculo adhuc videre non possunt.

VERS. 17.-- Neque omnes qui descendunt. (CASS.) Vel non omnes qui descendunt; quia et sancti descenderunt, sed non in inferiori.

PSALM CXIII.

1034DAlleluia. (CASS.) Here again the Alleluia is set down from another occasion, etc., as far as as becomes clear in the exposition of the psalm.

VERS. 1.-- At the going out. (AUG.) Here things past are not related, but things to come are foretold, because in those deeds things to come were signified: and therefore not all the things which were done there are spoken of here, but certain of them otherwise, lest he be thought to be recounting things past. (CASS.) First the Prophet tells what wonders God gave to the Hebrews in figure, and to Christians in spirit. Secondly he asks why these things were done, there, What ailed thee, O sea? Thirdly he reproves the empty idols of the Gentiles, and commends the religion of God, there, the idols of the Gentiles.

At the going out. As it were, when Israel, that is, the house of Jacob, went out of Egypt, that is, from a barbarous people.

1035ABarbarous. (AUG.) That tongue is barbarous which praises not God.

VERS. 2.-- It was made. (CASS.) As that people, when it went out of Egypt, etc., as far as they are able to resist vices, and this.

VERS. 3.-- The sea saw, that is, the sinners of the world. Jordan, they who by divers desires snatch men into the great sea, that is, into the embittering malice of this world; but these things cease at the coming of the Lord, being as it were turned backward.

The sea saw. (AUG.) This is here said otherwise than it was done. There it is read to have stood on that side from which the waters were flowing down, nor is anything said there of the mountains skipping; but both the things done there and the things said here are figures.

1035BVERS. 4.-- Rams. (ID.) Who with the horns of both, etc., as far as every knowledge lifting itself up against Christ. The hills. (CASS.) From tilling, the middling sort: for these things are not according to the letter; whence also by the sea and by Jordan, that is, by the ancient deeds, doubt not that those things are signified which today are done spiritually.

VERS. 5.-- What ailed thee. (ID.) Secondly he asks why these things were, that he may stir up wonder. And he resolves it: At the face of the Lord.

VERS. 7.-- At the face. (ID.) One answer for two, because one author both made the ages to be astonished, and made his own, that is, the mountains and the hills, to rejoice: for at the appearing of Christ men were moved from their own superstition to the worship of God.

At the face of the God of Jacob. And as though one should ask, who is the Lord? 1035CThe God of Jacob, not a new one; who makes them wrestle.

VERS. 8.-- Who turned the rock. (ID.) The hard hearts of the Jews, unto the water of baptism.

The crag. The Gentiles, that they also may pour forth the watering fountains of preaching.

(AUG.) That is, himself, hard before, while he was not known, etc., as far as he might overflow upon all that believe, saying: If any man thirst, let him come to me and drink.

VERS. 1.-- Not to us. (CASS.) When he had said that God gives good things, etc., as far as truth, while he renders the rewards, or punishes the ungodly. Therefore, Give.

VERS. 2.-- Lest at any time: this the ungodly often lay to the charge of the good when they are afflicted.

Mercy. (AUG.), that is, by restoration.

Truth, that is, by the promise fulfilled.

1035DWhere is God. (ID.) This the Gentiles are wont to say, who have visible gods: because we worship an invisible God.

VERS. 3.-- In heaven. (ID.), that is, in Christ the man, according to that: God was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself. Or, in heaven, (CASS.) that is, mighty above all creatures.

He hath done all things whatsoever he would. Whereby he appears almighty.

VERS. 4.-- The idols of the Gentiles. (ID.) Thirdly he proves the idols empty, and shows how profitable the religion of God is. And here is a perfect demonstration in dispraise and in praise. (AUG.) The power of the true God having been shown from his works, he passes to the visible gods of the Gentiles. Silver. (ID.) But because God made this, he says, The works 1036Aof the hands of men: they venerate that which they made thereof, for God created the matter; but the folly of men added the form.

VERS. 5.-- They have mouths. (ID.) They were formed by hand, etc., as far as and they served the creature rather than the Creator.

VERS. 7.-- They shall not cry. (ID.) After speaking (which is proper to man) he adds this which is common, etc., as far as and an idol wanting life and sense.

VERS. 8.-- Like unto them. (ID.) See the worship that should shame them, when he says like, which indeed they are; or let them understand themselves to be like unto them.

VERS. 9.-- The house of Israel. (CASS.) Here he shows the profit of the Christian religion.

VERS. 10.-- The house of Aaron. (AUG.) But lest that should seem to be already a thing possessed by the greater which to the lesser is 1036Ba hope, he adds, The house of Aaron.

VERS. 12.-- Mindful. (CASS.) That he might convert them, and he blessed the converted through the same.

VERS. 14.-- Upon you. (AUG.) Because the number of teachers increased.

Upon the children. Because the number of followers also increased. Therefore ye both, fathers and sons, are blessed of the Lord, who made you heaven in the greater, and earth in the lesser; or who made every creature.

VERS. 15.-- Blessed be ye of the Lord. (CASS.) He who above wished to be blessed, now with confidence says, Blessed, which belongs to God, that ye may serve him. Truly of the Lord, because even the heaven of heaven, that is, Christ, is unto the honour of the Lord; or,

VERS. 16.-- The heaven of heaven, that is, the empyrean, he gave 1036Cto the Lord Christ, according as he is man. But the earth. This lower earth he gave. To the children of men. That in it they may purify themselves; or the people to the preachers; whence: As the Father hath sent me, and I will send you (Joan. VI).

The heaven of heaven. (AUG.) He speaks of those whose minds, etc., as far as whom the weak cannot yet see without a support.

VERS. 17.-- Nor all they that go down. (CASS.) Or, not all they that go down; because the saints also went down, but not into the lower place.

PSALMUS CXIV.

Alleluia. Hic titulus saepe iteratur, quia laudatio Dei, et dignitas est operum, et pretium laborum, id est, meritum est et praemium. (AUG.) Propheta de fovea peccatorum liberatus, et in petra constitutus, 1036Dprimo gratias agit quia exauditus est, et contra omnia pericula se invocasse dicit.

Psalmus iste est consolatio fidelium contra dolores saeculi.

VERS. 1.-- Dilexi. (ID.) Dicit hoc ovis quae erraverat, filius reversus, hujus saeculi peregrinus.

(CASS.) Dilexi. Non propter temporalia bona mihi data, ut infideles, sed quoniam, etc. Diligitur Deus et ab infidelibus quia bona dat; unde: Confitebor tibi cum benefeceris ei (Psal. XLVIII). Diligitur perfecte, eum animus adversis non movetur, sed spe accenditur: quem modum post exponit, dilexi. Non quia me regem fecit, prospera dedit, sed quia orationem audit in angustiis.

VERS. 2.-- Et in diebus meis. (AUG.) Scilicet meae miseriae, quos mihi feci peccando, qui sunt pleni laboris et doloris, id est, vetustae putredinis.

Invocabo. Quod non est sine fide; unde Apostolus: Quomodo invocabunt in quem non crediderunt? (Rom. X.) Dum ergo ait, invocabunt, nota quod non est otiosus dilector. In quibus, Circumdederunt me, etc. Vel, in diebus salutis, id est tempore plenitudinis; unde: Ecce nunc tempus acceptabile, etc. (II Cor. VI).

VERS. 3.-- Dolores. (CASS.) Peccata, unde dolor et mors animae; vel, aeterna, haec in inferno erit. Pericula inferni. (AUG.) Suffusus enim carnali voluptate, non animadverti mala me circumdantia.

VERS. 4.-- Tribulationem et dolorem. (ID.) Quasi, illa prius me circumdederunt, sed post inveni tribulationem 1037Bet dolorem, id est, afflictionem exteriorem esse utilem.

VERS. 5.-- O Domine, libera. (CASS.) Secundo item clamat, ut liberatus veniat ad requiem. Misericors Dominus. (AUG.) Quia primo inclinavit aurem mihi et me vocavit.

Justus. Quia flagellat iterum. Miseretur. Quia recipit ad beatitudinem. Nec tam amarum debet esse quod flagellat, quam dulce quod recipit, quia Dominus custodit parvulos, quos grandes quaerit haeredes.

VERS. 7.-- Convertere. (ID.) Non meritis vel viribus tuis, sed quia Dominus benefecit tibi.

VERS. 8.-- De morte oculos. (ID.) Mors est infidelitas; unde: Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos; et iterum: Non mortui laudabunt te, Domine (Psal. CIII).

1037CVERS. 9.-- Placebo. (ID.) Dixit, etc., usque ad et hoc in regione vivorum, qui vivunt aeternaliter.

PSALM CXIV.

Alleluia. This title is often repeated, because the praise of God is both the dignity of works and the price of labours, that is, it is both the merit and the reward. (AUG.) The Prophet, delivered from the pit of sins and set upon the rock, 1036Dfirst gives thanks because he was heard, and says that he has called upon him against all perils.

This psalm is the consolation of the faithful against the sorrows of the world.

VERS. 1.-- I have loved. (ID.) This the sheep says which had strayed, the son returned, the pilgrim of this world.

(CASS.) I have loved. Not for the temporal goods given to me, as the unbelievers do, but because, etc. God is loved even by unbelievers because he gives good things; whence: I will praise thee when thou shalt do well to him (Psal. XLVIII). [Vulg. Ps 48:19 confitebitur tibi, "he will praise thee," in the third person, which is what the gloss's argument requires] He is loved perfectly, him [eum; read cum, "when"] the mind is not moved by adverse things, but is kindled by hope: which manner he afterwards expounds, I have loved. Not because he made me a king, or gave me prosperity, but because he hears my prayer in straits.

VERS. 2.-- And in my days. (AUG.) Namely of my misery, which days I made for myself by sinning, which are full of labour and sorrow, that is, of the old rottenness.

I will call upon. Which is not without faith; whence the Apostle: How shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? (Rom. X.) When therefore he says, they shall call upon, note that the lover is not idle. In which, They have compassed me, etc. Or, in the days of salvation, that is, in the time of fulness; whence: Behold, now is the acceptable time, etc. (II Cor. VI).

VERS. 3.-- Sorrows. (CASS.) Sins, whence come the sorrow and the death of the soul; or eternal sorrows, and this shall be in hell. The perils of hell. (AUG.) For, steeped in carnal pleasure, I did not perceive the evils that compassed me about.
