VERS. 4.-- Trouble and sorrow. (ID.) As it were: those things first compassed me about, but afterwards I found trouble 1037Band sorrow, that is, outward affliction, to be profitable.

VERS. 5.-- O Lord, deliver. (CASS.) Secondly he cries again, that being delivered he may come to rest. The Lord is merciful. (AUG.) Because he first inclined his ear to me and called me.

Just. Because he scourges again. He hath mercy. Because he receives unto blessedness. Nor ought that to be so bitter which he scourges, as that is sweet which he receives, because the Lord keeps the little ones, whom, when they are grown, he seeks for heirs.

VERS. 7.-- Turn thee. (ID.) Not by thy merits or by thy strength, but because the Lord hath done well to thee.

VERS. 8.-- From death, the eyes. (ID.) Death is unbelief; whence: Let the dead bury their dead; and again: The dead shall not praise thee, O Lord (Psal. CIII).

1037CVERS. 9.-- I will please. (ID.) He said, etc., as far as and this in the land of the living, who live eternally.

PSALMUS CXV.

Alleluia. Voce laudis congrue praetitulatur hic psalmus, quia in hoc psalmo verba sunt martyrum, qui confessione viguerunt et praemia Dei consecuti sunt.

VERS. 10.-- Credidi, etc. (CASS.) Primo memorantur beneficia Dei, quibus quid dignum redderent cum dubitent, occurrit calix passionis, qui a Deo datur. Secundo, servos se dicunt, et filios ancillae, id est Ecclesiae, ibi: O Domine, quia ego, etc. Verus et congruus ordo, prius credere, post loqui: ne nondum credens audeat loqui, sed fidem sequatur confessio. Ne vero confessio viribus hominis detur, dicit 1037Dproprium hominis quod mendax: quod non facile sciret, nisi excessu mentis ad superna vectus esset. Magnum enim est si quis se imprudentem attendit. Et cum homo nihil boni proprium habeat, quid retribuendum? Credidi. (AUG.) Non ait: Credidi et locutus sum, quia non tantum credidit caetera quae fides exigit, sed et simul cum illis credidit, et quod praemium loquendo sperare, et quod poenam tacendo timere deberet; unde loquendi quidem amor ex praemio immittitur, et necessitas ex poena indicitur. Propter quod. Non enim perfecte credit, qui quod credit non loquitur; piger est ille servus, vel timidus, sed fidelis: quod accepit, impendit, et lucratur, et ideo intra in gaudium Domini sui, dicentis: Euge, 1038Aserve bone et fidelis, intra in gaudium Domini tui (Matth. XXV).

VERS. 11.-- In excessu meo. Vel, exstasi mea. (AUG.) Et dicitur hic exstasis, etc., usque ad quod est omnis homo mendax.

VERS. 12.-- Quid retribuam Domino. (ID.)? Territus iste respicit infirmitatem suam, et videt non esse praesumendum de se. Ex se enim homo mendax, ut et Petrus, dum praesumpsit, inventus est mendax: sed virtus Dei est, si non credit. Quod videns iste factum in se gratia Dei, subdit, quae retribuit mihi. Non ait, pro omnibus quae tribuit. Quae igitur praecesserunt hominis bona, ut omnium donorum Dei non tributio, sed retributio vocari possit? Quae praecesserant nisi peccata? Retribuit ergo Deus hominibus 1038Bbona pro malis, passus pro eis, cum homines retribuunt mala pro bonis.

VERS. 13.-- Calicem salutaris. (ID.) Passionem a simili, etc., usque ad quod post dicitur.

(CASS.) Calicem, quia sub mensura bibitur. Unde, Fidelis Deus, qui non patitur vos tentari supra id quod potestis (I Cor. X). Salutaris, quia in aeternam salutem propitiatur.

VERS. 15.-- Pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors sanctorum ejus. (AUG.) Qui prior passus est, dat imitari passiones suas; et ideo: Pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors sanctorum ejus. Emit eam sanguine quem pro eis fudit, ne dubitarent pro eo mori. Hoc ergo pretio comparatus, confitetur conditionem suam: O Domine, quia ego, etc.

1038CVERS. 16.-- O Domine, quia, etc. (CASS.) Secundo servos se dicunt, et filios Ecclesiae, quia non est locus veri sacrificii extra catholicam Ecclesiam, ne quis haereticorum martyrium Deo placere putet. O Domine. Admiratur se talia accepisse, qualia Dominus pro mundi redemptione. Et ut augeat admirationem repetit: Ego servus tuus. Filius ancillae. (AUG.) Jerusalem coelestis, liberae a peccatis, ancillae justitiae. Qui autem sunt praeter Ecclesiam, non sunt filii ancillae, etsi servos se dicunt (quia habent nomen Christi) et martyres, ut haeretici. Filius ancillae, Non schismaticus. Vel ut ancilla, non sibi, sed Domino; ita et ego in morte mea aliquos tibi parturiam, sicut et in vita.

VERS. 17.-- Dirupisti vincula mea. (CASS.) Virtute 1038Dmartyrii vincula peccatorum rumpuntur, quia omnia sanguine abluuntur. Hic versus tantae virtutis a quibusdam creditur, ut peccata homini dimittantur, si in fine vitae trina confessione dicatur.

(ID.) Qui pretiosa. O Domine, tibi sacrificabo; loquens Deo, affirmat, quod supra dixerat.

Sacrificabo. (AUG., CASS.) Et quia dirupisti, tibi sacrificabo, ut gratus, Hostiam laudis. Sic quod:

VERS. 18, 19.-- Vota mea reddum. Non ubique, sed, in atriis, id est, in catholica Ecclesia, non haereticorum. Domus Domini. Quae sit, ostendit.

In conspectu omnis populi. (CASS.) Publice debet laudari, qui pro omnibus pati voluit, ut plures aedificentur. Vota mea reddam. Meipsum, qui sum imago 1039ADei quae reddenda est Deo, etc., usque ad et apertius hic nominat Jerusalem. (AUG.) Sed ue quis putet per Jerusalem Judaeos solos significari, qui hoc nomine gloriantur, audiat sequentem Psalmus: Laudate Dominum, omnes gentes. Haec sunt atria Domini, ille enim populus.

PSALM CXV.

Alleluia. This psalm is fitly entitled with the voice of praise, because in this psalm are the words of the martyrs, who were strong in confession and obtained the rewards of God.

VERS. 10.-- I have believed, etc. (CASS.) First the benefits of God are recalled; and while they doubt what worthy thing they might render for them, the chalice of the passion presents itself, which is given by God. Secondly they call themselves servants, and sons of the handmaid, that is, of the Church, there: O Lord, for I, etc. It is a true and fitting order, first to believe, afterwards to speak: lest one not yet believing should dare to speak, but that confession should follow faith. But lest confession be ascribed to the strength of man, he says 1037Dthat this is proper to man, that he is a liar: which he would not easily know, unless he had been carried by an excess of mind to the things above. For it is a great thing if a man marks that he is unwise. And since man has nothing good of his own, what is there to be rendered again? I have believed. (AUG.) He says not: I have believed and I have spoken, because he did not only believe the other things which faith requires, but together with them he believed also both what reward he ought to hope for by speaking, and what punishment he ought to fear by keeping silence; whence the love of speaking is put in from the reward, and the necessity is laid on from the punishment. For which cause. For he believes not perfectly who speaks not what he believes; that other servant is slothful, or fearful, but this one is faithful: what he received, he lays out and gains withal, and therefore enter thou [intra; read intrat, "he enters"] into the joy of his Lord, who says: Well done, 1038Agood and faithful servant, enter into the joy of thy Lord (Matth. XXV).

VERS. 11.-- In my excess. Or, in my ecstasy. (AUG.) And ecstasy is here spoken of, etc., as far as that every man is a liar.

VERS. 12.-- What shall I render to the Lord. (ID.)? This man, affrighted, looks back upon his own infirmity, and sees that he must not presume of himself. For of himself man is a liar, as Peter also, when he presumed, was found a liar: but it is the power of God, if he does not believe. Seeing this wrought in himself by the grace of God, he subjoins, which he hath rendered to me. He says not, for all the things which he hath bestowed. What goods of man, therefore, went before, that of all the gifts of God it might be called not a bestowing, but a rendering again? What had gone before but sins? God therefore renders to men 1038Bgood things for evil, having suffered for them, whereas men render evil things for good.

VERS. 13.-- The chalice of salvation. (ID.) The passion, from a likeness, etc., as far as which is said afterwards.

(CASS.) The chalice, because it is drunk under measure. Whence, God is faithful, who suffereth you not to be tempted above that which ye are able (I Cor. X). Of salvation, because it is propitious unto eternal salvation.

VERS. 15.-- Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints. (AUG.) He who suffered first grants that his own sufferings be imitated; and therefore: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints. He bought it with the blood which he shed for them, that they might not doubt to die for him. Bought therefore at this price, he confesses his own condition: O Lord, for I, etc.

1038CVERS. 16.-- O Lord, for, etc. (CASS.) Secondly they call themselves servants, and sons of the Church, because there is no place of true sacrifice outside the Catholic Church, lest any of the heretics should think his martyrdom to be pleasing to God. O Lord. He wonders that he has received such things as the Lord received for the redemption of the world. And to increase the wonder he repeats: I am thy servant. The son of the handmaid. (AUG.) Of the heavenly Jerusalem, free from sins, the handmaid of justice. But they who are outside the Church are not sons of the handmaid, even though they call themselves servants (because they have the name of Christ) and martyrs, as the heretics do. The son of the handmaid, Not a schismatic. Or, as a handmaid brings forth not for herself, but for the Lord; so I too in my death shall bring forth some for thee, as also in my life.

VERS. 17.-- Thou hast broken my bonds. (CASS.) By the power 1038Dof martyrdom the bonds of sins are broken, because all things are washed away by the blood. This verse is believed by some to be of such power that a man's sins are forgiven, if at the end of his life it be said with a threefold confession.

(ID.) Who precious. O Lord, to thee will I sacrifice; speaking to God, he affirms what he had said above.

I will sacrifice. (AUG., CASS.) And because thou hast broken them, to thee will I sacrifice, as one that is thankful, The sacrifice of praise. So that:

VERS. 18, 19.-- I will pay reddum my vows. Not everywhere, but in the courts, that is, in the Catholic Church, not in that of the heretics. Of the house of the Lord. He shows which it is.

In the sight of all the people. (CASS.) He ought to be praised publicly who was willing to suffer for all, that the more may be edified. I will pay my vows. Myself, who am the image 1039Aof God, which must be rendered to God, etc., as far as and here he names Jerusalem more openly. (AUG.) But lest ue any think that by Jerusalem the Jews alone are signified, who glory in this name, let him hear the following psalm [Psalmus; read Psalmum, "the following psalm"]: Praise the Lord, all ye nations. These are the courts of the Lord, for that is the people.

PSALMUS CXVI.

Alleluia. (CASS.) Brevis psalmus, omnium primus atomus, id est sine divisione: pro sui enim brevitate non recipi divisionem, sed omnes compendio suae locutionis superat, et est quasi punctus psalmorum, unde diversae species formantur. Mira variatio contra taedium salutaria dicere, modo paucis, modo late.

VERS. 1.-- Laudate Dominum, omnes gentes. (CASS.) Ne qui praetereantur de toto orbe. (AUG.) Et 1039Bhaec sunt atria illa domus Domini, et ille omnis populus, unde in praecedenti psalmo egit. Non soli Judaei (qui sibi illud arrogare conantur) dico laudate eum. Et collaudate. (CASS.) ut sit in unum redacta omnium laudatio quod est catholicae Ecclesiae.

VERS. 2.-- Confirmata. (CASS.) Quia quod per prophetas promisit, adventu Christi complevit; et firmavit misericordiam, ut nunquam moveatur, quia qui dedit, custodit. Manet in aeternum. (AUG.) Sive in eis quae promisit piis, sive in eis quae minatur impiis.

PSALM CXVI.

Alleluia. (CASS.) A short psalm, the first of all that is an atom, that is, without division: for by reason of its brevity not to be received [recipi; read recipit, "it admits"] division, but it surpasses all others by the compendiousness of its utterance, and it is as it were the point of the psalms, out of which the divers kinds are formed. A wondrous variation against weariness, to speak wholesome things, now in few words, now at large.

VERS. 1.-- Praise the Lord, all ye nations. (CASS.) That none out of the whole world be passed over. (AUG.) And 1039Bthese are those courts of the house of the Lord, and that whole people, whereof he treated in the preceding psalm. Not the Jews alone (who attempt to arrogate it to themselves) do I say, praise ye him. And praise ye together. (CASS.) that the praise of all may be brought into one, which belongs to the Catholic Church.

VERS. 2.-- Confirmed. (CASS.) Because what he promised through the prophets he fulfilled by the coming of Christ; and he made his mercy firm, that it may never be moved, because he who gave it keeps it. It remaineth for ever. (AUG.) Whether in those things which he promised to the godly, or in those which he threatens to the ungodly.

PSALMUS CXVII.

Alleluia. (CASS.) Quintus psalmus de primo adventu, multis figuris decoratus, habet versus unifines, quosdam unius principii, quosdam intercalares et hujusmodi ornatus. Fidelis populus peccato 1039Csolutus, ete., usque ad Benedictus qui.

VERS. 2.-- Dicat nunc. (ID.) Ut ego vos, ita vos invicem monete; vel, dicat, id est, confiteatur.

Quoniam in saeculum. Ecce quatuor versus unifines.

VERS. 5.-- De tribulatione. (ID.) Exemplum de se ponit, ut alios ad misericordiam invitet.

VERS. 6.-- Dominus mihi adjutor. (ID.) Idem in duobus principium.

VERS. 7.-- Despiciam. Alias videbo. (ID.) Hic, ut tutior et cautior fiam. Inimicos meos. Damnandos.

VERS. 8.-- Bonum est. (ID.) Secundo, in solo Deo dicit confidendum, per quem inimicitias gentium evadit, et et ad veram vitam venit.

VERS. 9.-- In principibus. (AUG.) Angelis, etc., 1039Dusque ad qui eos pro modo eorum bonos facit.

VERS. 10.-- Omnes gentes. (CASS.) Ecce unde liberat de occulta vel aperta tribulatione, vel non permittendo cadere, vel, a casu revelando.

VERS. 11.-- Circumdantes, etc. (AUG.) Quasi reddens causam unde tanta potest superare, dicit quid primo in capite passus sit.

VERS. 12.-- Circumdederunt me, etc. (ID.) Quod ab ignorantibus gestum est, mystica subtilitate praedicit Spiritus sanctus. Nesciente Judae rem omnium fecerunt, et nobis dulciorem, passione Deum, sicut apes dum sibi putant reponere, aliis mel faciunt. Et exarserunt. Vel hoc melius de Ecclesia accipitur. Post passionem namque Domini contra Ecclesiam gentium et Judaei exarserunt sicut ignis in 1040Aspinis pecatorum. Ea enim, id est peccata, in fideli populo igne persecutionis cremaverunt, cui volentes officere, profecerunt. Quia ultus. Dum conversi, exstincta in eis malitia, populo Christiano sociati sunt; vel, cum in fine judicati, judicium veritatis sine misericordia sensuri sunt.

VERS. 13.-- Impulsus, etc. (CASS.) Ut quando boni dantur poenis, ut a fide cadant, et Dominus suscepit. (AUG.) Quia tam non cadit cui Dominus est fortitudo et laudatio quam non cadit Dominus: illi vero cadunt, qui sibi volunt esse fortitudo et laudatio.

Impulsus eversus sum, etc. Postquam ostendit quod liberat non permittendo cadere, ostendit etiam quod liberat a casu relevando.

VERS. 14.-- Factus est mihi in salutem. (ID.) 1040BNon fit, quod non erat sibi; sed illis salus est conversis, quod non erat aversis.

VERS. 17.-- Non moriar. (ID.) Dicit Ecclesia, ut putat persecutor strage funerum posse se delere nomen Christianum, cum potius augeat.

VERS. 18.-- Castigans. (CASS.) Cur autem tanta pertulit, indicat: Castigans, quidquid faciunt, castigatio est Domini. Nihil sibi vindicent, morti non datur, cujus vitia purgantur. (AUG.) Saepe pater per nequam servos emendat filios, cum illis poenam, his praeparet haereditatem. Quae sit autem haereditas, hinc potest cognosci: Aperite portas. Quid intus? Ingressus confitebor.

VERS. 19.-- Aperite. (CASS.) Tertio portas Jerusalem aperiri sibi cupit, ubi dicit et de angulari 1040Clapide. Aperite, o prophetae, qui portatis claves regni coelorum. Portas. (CASS., HIER.) Per has portas doctrinae ingressi vere laudant; extra Ecclesiam catholicam non est laus Dei. (CASS.) Hae omnes portae ducunt ad unam, quae est Christus, per quam justi intrant in coelum; unde: Ego sum ostium, per quod si quis introierit, salvus erit (Joan. X). Et alibi: Nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me (Joan. XIV). (AUG.) Ecce de utroque saeculo mentionem fecit: et quia haec porta Christus apparuit, confitebor tibi, laetus gratias agens, quia exaudisti in adventu Filii; priores enim justi adventum petebant. Portas justitiae. Id est, portas mortis, etc., usque ad id est, per eam ad vitam.

1040DVERS. 22.-- Aedificantes. (ID.) Soli Judaei Deum colentes aedificabant, aliis per idololatriam destructis; sed non perfecerunt, quia Christum contempserunt.

VERS. 23.-- A Domino factum. Vel, A Domino factum est ei, secundum aliam litteram. (ID.) Id est, ad honorem Patris.

VERS. 24.-- Haec est dies. Hic est annus jubilaeus, figuraliter sub lege observatus, qui dicitur remittens, vel initians, quia tunc servi manumittebantur, possessiones dominis restituebantur: et nos hac die a servitute peccati redempti sumus, quibus est haereditas restituta aeterna. (CASS.) Haec est dies. Etsi omnes fecit, hanc singulariter qua Dominus venit, in qua convenit laetari, quia diabolus jus perdidit, homo revixit; et quia hoc est,

1041AVERS. 25.-- O Domine, salvum, etc. Ecce desiderium magnae petitionis. Salvum, de clade saeculi. Prosperare, ut dolores isti vertantur in aeterna gaudia.

VERS. 26.-- Benedictus, etc. (CASS.) Quarto frequentari atria Dei suadet, de adventu Christi gaudens. (AUG.) Maledictus ergo qui venit in nomine suo, etc., usque ad qui erit maledictus. (CASS.) Benedictus. Laus de adventu, et o reliqui Christiani, nos majores quasi sacerdotes benediximus vobis, quod multum prodest, quia benediximus vobis de domo Domini.

De domo. (ID.) Id est, Ecclesia catholica, etc., usque ad quia laeta confessio post beneficia.

VERS. 27.-- Constituite diem. (AUG.) Magni, qui excedunt, qui mente verbum Deum apud Deum contingunt, etc., usque ad id est, ad aeterna gaudia attingat.

1041BDiem solemnem. In veteri lege (Deut. X.) Pascha, Pentecoste, scenophegia, tres praecipuae solemnitates, in quibus praeceptum ut nemo vacuus in conspectu Domini appareret. Vacuus est, qui in se Christum non habet, qui est fundamentum, quod nemo mutare valet. Inde est quod illis tribus solemnitatibus fidelis populus nummum offert manuali oblatione, interiorem significans. In nummo enim nomen et imago regis. Quisque ergo spiritualiter nummum offerat, ut nomen regis, id est Christi, in se habeat, a Christo Christianus dictus; et imaginem, id est animam, lumine vultus ejus insignitam Deo exibeat. Cornu altaris. (CASS.) Vel per altare intelligitur sacramentum corporis et sanguinis, etc., usque ad non habebit vitam aeternam.

1041CVel, altare intelligitur mens hominis; unde in lege praeceptum fuit (Exod. XXVII) fieri altare quadrangulum et concavum: ideo quadrangulum, quia mens humana quatuor virtutibus muniri debet, prudentia, justitia, fortitudine, temperantia; eadem debet esse concava ad recipiendum verbum Dei atque ignem dilectionis. Tumor enim infusa repellit; unde in Levitico praeceptum est (Levit. I) vesiculam gutturis et plumam projici, quando turtur vel columba offertur. Vesicula inflationem superbiae significat; plumae, inanes inquisitiones sublimium; haec ergo projice, ut sis altare concavum.

VERS. 28.-- Deus meus es tu. Et ut apertius dicamus, istorum verborum hic est sensus: Non sufficiat in terra iste dies festus, quo agnus occisus est: 1041Dsed constituatur in frequentationibus quousque perveniatur mentibus exaltatis ad interiorem ejus deitatem, ubi laudes cantabimus ita: Deus meus es tu, etc. Itaque, sicut coepit laudem, ita terminat.

VERS. 29.-- Confitemini Domino. Ab initio quod deseruimus, in finem quo redimus, non est salubrius aliquid, quod delectet, quam laus Dei

PSALM CXVII.

Alleluia. (CASS.) The fifth psalm concerning the first coming, adorned with many figures, has verses of one ending, some of one beginning, some intercalary, and ornaments of this kind. The faithful people, loosed from sin 1039C, etc., ete. as far as Blessed is he that.

VERS. 2.-- Let him now say. (ID.) As I admonish you, so do you admonish one another; or, let him say, that is, let him confess.

Because for ever. Behold four verses of one ending.

VERS. 5.-- Out of tribulation. (ID.) He sets an example from himself, that he may invite others to mercy.

VERS. 6.-- The Lord is my helper. (ID.) The same beginning in two.

VERS. 7.-- I shall look down. Elsewhere, I shall see. (ID.) Here, that I may become safer and more wary. My enemies. Those to be damned.

VERS. 8.-- It is good. (ID.) Secondly, he says that trust is to be placed in God alone, through whom he escapes the enmities of the Gentiles, and et comes to the true life.

VERS. 9.-- In princes. (AUG.) In the angels, etc., 1039Das far as he who makes them good according to their measure.

VERS. 10.-- All nations. (CASS.) Behold whence he delivers from hidden or from open tribulation: either by not suffering one to fall, or by revealing from the fall [revelando; read relevando, "by raising up"].

VERS. 11.-- They that compassed me about, etc. (AUG.) As it were rendering the reason whence he is able to overcome so many things, he tells what he first suffered in the head.

VERS. 12.-- They surrounded me, etc. (ID.) What was done by men who knew not, the Holy Spirit foretells with mystical subtlety. Judah not knowing, they made God, by his passion, the concern of all, and sweeter to us: as bees, while they think to lay up for themselves, make honey for others. And they were enkindled. Or this is better understood of the Church. For after the passion of the Lord the Jews also were enkindled against the Church of the Gentiles, like fire in 1040Athe thorns of sins pecatorum. For these, that is, sins, they burned up in the faithful people by the fire of persecution; and wishing to harm it, they profited it. Because I was avenged. While, being converted, malice being extinguished in them, they were joined to the Christian people; or, when, being judged in the end, they shall feel the judgment of truth without mercy.

VERS. 13.-- Being thrust at, etc. (CASS.) As when good men are given over to punishments, that they may fall from the faith, and the Lord upheld. (AUG.) Because he to whom the Lord is strength and praise falls as little as the Lord falls: but those fall who wish to be strength and praise to themselves.

I was thrust at and overthrown, etc. After he has shown that he delivers by not suffering one to fall, he shows also that he delivers by raising up from the fall.

VERS. 14.-- He is become my salvation. (ID.) 1040BHe is not made what he was not to himself; but he is salvation to them converted, which he was not to them turned away.

VERS. 17.-- I shall not die. (ID.) The Church says it, since the persecutor thinks that by a slaughter of funerals he can blot out the Christian name, whereas he rather increases it.

VERS. 18.-- Chastising. (CASS.) But why he bore so many things, he shows: Chastising, whatever they do is the chastisement of the Lord. Let them claim nothing to themselves; he is not given over to death whose vices are purged. (AUG.) Often a father amends his sons by worthless servants, when for those he prepares punishment, for these an inheritance. And what the inheritance is may be known from this: Open ye the gates. What within? Having entered I will confess.

VERS. 19.-- Open ye. (CASS.) In the third place he desires that the gates of Jerusalem be opened to him, where he speaks also of the corner 1040Cstone. Open, O prophets, who bear the keys of the kingdom of heaven. The gates. (CASS., HIER.) They who have entered through these gates of doctrine praise truly; outside the Catholic Church there is no praise of God. (CASS.) All these gates lead to one, which is Christ, through whom the just enter into heaven; whence: I am the door, through which if any man enter in, he shall be safe (Joan. X) [Vulg. per me si quis introierit, salvabitur, "by me, he shall be saved"]. And elsewhere: No man cometh to the Father, but by me (Joan. XIV). (AUG.) Behold, he has made mention of both worlds: and because this gate has appeared as Christ, I will confess to thee, giving thanks with gladness, because thou hast heard at the coming of the Son; for the just of former times were asking for the coming. The gates of justice. That is, the gates of death, etc., as far as that is, through it unto life.

1040DVERS. 22.-- They that build. (ID.) The Jews alone, worshipping God, were building, the rest being destroyed through idolatry; but they did not finish, because they despised Christ.

VERS. 23.-- This is done by the Lord. Or, This is done by the Lord for him, according to another reading. (ID.) That is, unto the honour of the Father.

VERS. 24.-- This is the day. This is the jubilee year, figuratively observed under the law, which is called remitting, or beginning, because then bondmen were set free, possessions were restored to their owners: and we on this day have been redeemed from the servitude of sin, to whom an eternal inheritance has been restored. (CASS.) This is the day. Although he made all days, this one singularly, on which the Lord came, on which it is fitting to rejoice, because the devil lost his right and man lived again; and because this is so,

1041AVERS. 25.-- O Lord, save, etc. Behold the desire of a great petition. Save, from the ruin of the world. Give prosperity, that these sorrows may be turned into eternal joys.

VERS. 26.-- Blessed, etc. (CASS.) Fourthly he urges that the courts of God be frequented, rejoicing in the coming of Christ. (AUG.) Cursed therefore is he that comes in his own name, etc., as far as he who shall be cursed. (CASS.) Blessed. Praise for the coming; and, O ye other Christians, we the elders, as it were priests, have blessed you, which profits much, because we have blessed you out of the house of the Lord.

Out of the house. (ID.) That is, the Catholic Church, etc., as far as because glad is the confession that follows benefits.

VERS. 27.-- Appoint a day. (AUG.) The great, who go beyond, who with the mind touch the Word, God with God, etc., as far as that is, that he may attain unto eternal joys.

1041BA solemn day. In the old law (Deut. X.) the Pasch, Pentecost, the feast of tabernacles, three chief solemnities, in which it was commanded that no man should appear empty in the sight of the Lord. He is empty who has not Christ in himself, who is the foundation, which no man is able to change. Hence it is that on those three solemnities the faithful people offers a coin by an offering of the hand, signifying the inward offering. For on a coin there is the name and image of the king. Let each one therefore offer a coin spiritually, that he may have in himself the name of the king, that is, of Christ, being called a Christian from Christ; and may show forth to God the image, that is, the soul, marked with the light of his countenance. The horn of the altar. (CASS.) Or by the altar is understood the sacrament of the body and blood, etc., as far as he shall not have life everlasting.

1041COr, the altar is understood to be the mind of man; whence in the law it was commanded (Exod. XXVII) that an altar be made four-cornered and hollow: four-cornered, because the human mind ought to be fortified with four virtues, prudence, justice, fortitude, temperance; and the same ought to be hollow to receive the word of God and the fire of love. For swelling drives back what is poured in; whence in Leviticus it is commanded (Levit. I) that the little bladder of the throat and the feathers be cast away, when a turtle-dove or a pigeon is offered. The bladder signifies the puffing up of pride; the feathers, empty searchings into lofty things; cast these away therefore, that thou mayest be a hollow altar.

VERS. 28.-- Thou art my God. And that we may speak more openly, this is the sense of these words: Let not this feast day upon earth, on which the lamb was slain, suffice: 1041Dbut let it be appointed in frequent celebrations, until with minds exalted we come to his inward Godhead, where we shall sing praises thus: Thou art my God, etc. And so, as he began with praise, so he ends with it.

VERS. 29.-- Give praise to the Lord. From the beginning which we forsook, unto the end to which we return, there is nothing more wholesome, which may delight, than the praise of God

PSALMUS CXVIII.

Expositionem hujus psalmi, ut valde prolixam, omittimus. Vide Ambrosii, Cassiodori, Augustini Enarrationes in psalmos, et quibus ad verbum expressa est glossa ordinaria in hunc locum.

PSALM CXVIII.

The exposition of this psalm, as being exceedingly long, we omit. See the Enarrationes on the psalms of Ambrose, Cassiodorus, Augustine, and from these the Glossa ordinaria on this place has been expressed word for word.

PSALMUS CXIX.

VERS. 1.-- Canticum graduum. (CASS.) Beatitudinem, 1042Aquam superior psalmus unita varietate cantavit, etc., usque ad his ergo gradibus inoffenso pede mentis ascenditur atque descenditur. (AUG.) Canticum graduum. Graduum nomen ambiguum apud nos, etc., usque ad et altitudinem deitatis ipsius. Primus gradus, a malis saeculi exire, et universae vanitati renuntiare. (CASS.) Initium profectus est carnalia vitia relinquere et Domino supplicare; unde in veteri lege, quando emebatur mancipium gentile, radebantur ungues ejus et capilli tondebantur (Deut. XII). Quia oportet vanitatem quaque exuere, ut Dei obsequio mancipetur. Hic ab renuntiatione saeculi quibusdam gradibus meritorum ad perfectam et aeternam pervenitur charitatem, quae in summo locata est.

Ad Dominum cum tribularer. (CASS.) Primo, ascendere 1042Bincipiens, quia multos invenit obsidentes, a linguis eorum petit liberari: secundo, de permistione malorum conqueritur, Hei mihi.

VERS. 2.-- Domine, libera, etc. Cum incipit homo ascendere, id est, cum cogitat proficere, contempto saeculo, soli haerens Deo, incipit pati linguas adversantium, id est detrahentium, et (quod gravius) quasi consulendo a salute avertentium: has qui non patitur, nondum proficere conatur. Ascensurus ergo primo contra eas precatur: Domine, libera animam meam a labiis iniquis.

VERS. 3.-- Quid detur tibi, etc. (CASS.) More nimis cogitantis haesitat, et quaerit remedium. Quid tibi detur, aut quid apponatur? Duo verba posuit, dari et apponi; sagittae dantur in arma, carbones 1042Capponuntur quasi in consolationem.

VERS. 4.-- Sagittae. (AUG.) Verbis Dei sagittatur cor, etc., usque ad ut sit purus locus aedificio Dei.

VERS. 5.-- Heu mihi. (CASS.) Secundo de incolatu, et permistione malorum conqueritur. Acceptis sagittis et carbonibus, factus triticum, nondum est in horreo, sed in area ubi multa palea premitur; videns ergo multa mala, quae ante non viderat clamat: Hei mihi. Nulli homini apparent mali, nisi factus sit bonus; Cum enim crevit herba, et fructum fecit, apparuerunt zizania. Prolongatus. Etsi breve tempus, desiderio nimis longum videtur. Cedar. (ID.) Filius Ismaelis, unde Saraceni descenderunt, qui verius ab Agar dicerentur Agareni: sed a Sara, digniori et libera sibi nomen vindicaverunt, quorum uterque in 1042Dtabernaculis legitur habitasse. Tabernacula Ismael recte Cedar dicta sunt: Cedar ad Ismael pertinet. (AUG.) Isaac ergo, etc., usque ad si nunc mali a bonis non possunt separari, ferendi sunt.

PSALM CXIX.

VERS. 1.-- A canticle of degrees. (CASS.) The beatitude 1042Awhich the foregoing psalm sang in a united variety, etc., as far as by these degrees therefore one ascends and descends with the unstumbling foot of the mind. (AUG.) A canticle of degrees. The name of degrees is ambiguous among us, etc., as far as and the height of his own Godhead. The first degree, to go out from the evils of the world, and to renounce all vanity. (CASS.) The beginning of advancement is to leave carnal vices and to make supplication to the Lord; whence in the old law, when a Gentile bondman was bought, his nails were pared and his hair was shorn (Deut. XII). Because vanity must be put off on every side, that a man may be made over to the service of God. Here, from the renunciation of the world, one comes by certain degrees of merits to that perfect and eternal charity which is set at the summit.

Unto the Lord when I was in trouble. (CASS.) First, beginning 1042Bto ascend, because he finds many besetting him, he asks to be delivered from their tongues: secondly, he complains of the mingling of the wicked, Woe is me.

VERS. 2.-- O Lord, deliver, etc. When a man begins to ascend, that is, when he purposes to advance, the world being despised, cleaving to God alone, he begins to suffer the tongues of adversaries, that is, of detractors, and (what is graver) of those who, as though counselling him, turn him away from salvation: he who does not suffer these does not yet endeavour to advance. Being about to ascend, therefore, he prays first against them: O Lord, deliver my soul from wicked lips.

VERS. 3.-- What shall be given to thee, etc. (CASS.) After the manner of one thinking overmuch he hesitates, and seeks a remedy. What shall be given to thee, or what shall be added? He has set down two words, to be given and to be added; arrows are given for arms, coals are 1042Cadded as it were for consolation.

VERS. 4.-- Arrows. (AUG.) The heart is shot through with the words of God, etc., as far as that there may be a clean place for the building of God.

VERS. 5.-- Woe is me. (CASS.) Secondly he complains of his sojourning and of the mingling of the wicked. Having received the arrows and the coals, being made wheat, he is not yet in the barn, but on the threshing-floor where much chaff is trodden; seeing therefore many evils which he had not seen before, he cries: Woe is me. To no man do the wicked appear, unless he has been made good; For when the blade was sprung up, and had brought forth fruit, the cockle appeared. Prolonged. Though the time be short, to desire it seems exceedingly long. Cedar. (ID.) The son of Ismael, from whom the Saracens are descended, who would more truly be called Agarenes from Agar: but from Sara, the worthier and the free woman, they have claimed a name for themselves, and both of these are read to have dwelt in 1042Dtents. The tents of Ismael are rightly called Cedar: Cedar belongs to Ismael. (AUG.) Isaac therefore, etc., as far as if now the evil cannot be separated from the good, they must be borne with.

PSALMUS CXX.

VERS. 1.-- Canticum graduum. (CASS.) Secundus gradus petere divinam defensionem, cui nihil posse obviare monstratur. (AUG.) Cui enim de mundo exeunti pericula occurrunt, exposcere debet divinum auxilium, etc., usque ad Talis est iste, qui oculos ad Deum levat. (CASS.) Primo levat oculos et orat: secundo quod oravit affirmat, ostendens virtutem auxilii impetrati.

Levavi oculos. (ID.) Qui quasi inclinatus clamavit, 1043Ajam respirans, oculos ad intercessores sanctos levat.

VERS. 3.-- Neque dormitet. (AUG.) Si dormit in te fides, dormit in te Christus.

(CASS.) Dicitur hoc humana consuetudine; ut quando fessus custos dormitat, furtum patitur.

VESS. 4.--(AUG.) Ecce non dormitabit. Dormitat Christus, etc., usque ad sed ne adhuc putes hoc de aliquo hominum, subdit, Dominus custodit.

Qui custodit Israel. (AUG.) Qui non potest videre faciem, etc., usque ad et huic non dormit Christus.

VERS. 5.-- Dominus custodit. (CASS.) Secunda pars, ubi quod oraverat affirmat. Et quasi quis quaereret, Quis est ille custos? subdit, Dominus custodit, etc. (AUG.) Non sine causa est, etc., usque ad dilectio Dei scilicet, et proximi.

1043BVERS. 6.-- Per diem sol non uret te, neque luna per noctem, etc. (ID.) Deus est sol, etc., usque ad vel luna, id est Ecclesia, non permittet uri nocte tribulationis. (HIER.) Vel per diem accipiuntur prospera, etc., usque ad ita nunc in prosperis et in adversis nos servat.

VERS. 7.-- Dominus custodiat introitum tuum. (CASS.) Cuncta concludit, bonis initiis bonos exitus adjungat. (AUG.) Dominus custodiat introitum tuum. Intrantes custodit, etc., usque ad jam in aeternum nihil nocebit.

PSALM CXX.

VERS. 1.-- A canticle of degrees. (CASS.) The second degree, to seek the divine defence, against which nothing is shown to be able to prevail. (AUG.) For he upon whom, as he goes out of the world, dangers press, ought to demand the divine help, etc., as far as Such is this man, who lifts his eyes to God. (CASS.) First he lifts his eyes and prays: secondly, he affirms what he prayed for, showing the power of the help obtained.

I have lifted up mine eyes. (ID.) He who cried out as one bowed down, 1043Anow taking breath, lifts his eyes to the holy intercessors.

VERS. 3.-- Neither let him slumber. (AUG.) If faith sleeps in thee, Christ sleeps in thee.

(CASS.) This is said after human custom; as when a weary watchman slumbers, he suffers theft.

VERS. 4.--(AUG.) Behold he shall not slumber. Christ slumbers, etc., as far as but lest thou still suppose this of some man, he subjoins, The Lord keepeth.

He that keepeth Israel. (AUG.) He who cannot see the face, etc., as far as and for this man Christ does not sleep.

VERS. 5.-- The Lord keepeth. (CASS.) The second part, where he affirms what he had prayed. And as if one should ask, Who is that keeper? he subjoins, The Lord keepeth, etc. (AUG.) It is not without cause, etc., as far as the love of God, namely, and of the neighbour.

1043BVERS. 6.-- By day the sun shall not burn thee, nor the moon by night, etc. (ID.) God is the sun, etc., as far as or the moon, that is, the Church, will not suffer thee to be burned in the night of tribulation. (HIER.) Or by day prosperity is understood, etc., as far as so now he keeps us both in prosperity and in adversity.

VERS. 7.-- May the Lord keep thy coming in. (CASS.) He concludes all: to good beginnings may he join good endings. (AUG.) May the Lord keep thy coming in. He keeps those who enter, etc., as far as now unto eternity nothing shall hurt.

PSALMUS CXXI.

VERS. 1.-- Canticum graduum. (CASS.) Tertius gradus. Magnum gaudium; in Ecclesia pura mente versari, atque digne Deo in hac peregrinatione militare: unde suspiramus ad coelestem Jerusalem, ad 1043Cquam duabus alis dilectionis levamur.

Laetatus sum in his, etc. Primo gaudet se monitum ire ad Jerusalem, ubi sancti securi et eum Domino judicabunt. Secundo, ascensurus optat abundantiam pacis: Rogate quae ad pacem, etc.

VERS. 4.-- Testimonium Israel. (AUG.) Id est, in quibus cognoscitur quod vere sunt Israel. Quando enim grana sunt cum paleis, totum palea putatur; sed cum separabuntur, tunc erit testimonium Israel.

VERS. 5.-- Sedes. (ID.) Id est justi, in quibus Deum sedet, etc., usque ad caveant ergo sibi omnes interrogandi.

VERS. 6.-- Rogate. (CASS.) Secunda pars, ubi loquitur ad judices, optans eis abundantiam pacis, quam amore fratrum praedicavit. Diligentibus. 1043D(AUG.) Qui amat in alio bonum, quod ipse non potest habere, imputatur ei quasi haberet; unde: Si charitas non habet quod det, det calicem aquae; et tantum imputatur ei quantum Zachaeo multa (Matth. X). Impar facultas, sed non impar charitas.

VERS. 7.-- Fiat pax. (ID.) Charitas est virtus fortis ut mors, etc., usque ad subdit: Propter fratres meos.

In turribus. (ID.) Id est in excelsis tuis. Pauci sunt judices, sed multi ad singulos pertinebunt, quos recipient in aeterna tabernacula, et tunc erit abundantia in turribus; Deus autem est tota eorum abundantia, tam recipientium quam receptorum.

VERS. 9.-- Propter domum Domini Dei. Vel sic legas 1044Aut hic versus sit expositio praecedentis. Quasi, loquebar pacem de te, propter proximos fratres, scilicet: Quaesivi bona tibi propter domum Domini Dei nostri. Sententia horum verborum non mutatur. Tibi. O tu, coelestis Jerusalem, quia domus Dei es, et ita in hoc hoc quod te diligo, Deum diligo.

PSALM CXXI.

VERS. 1.-- A canticle of degrees. (CASS.) The third degree. A great joy: to be conversant in the Church with a pure mind, and worthily to serve God as a soldier in this pilgrimage: whence we sigh for the heavenly Jerusalem, to 1043Cwhich we are lifted by the two wings of love.

I rejoiced at these things, etc. First he rejoices that he has been admonished to go to Jerusalem, where the saints, secure, shall judge him [eum; read cum, "with"] with the Lord. Secondly, being about to ascend, he wishes for an abundance of peace: Pray ye for the things that are for the peace, etc.

VERS. 4.-- A testimony to Israel. (AUG.) That is, in whom it is known that they are truly Israel. For when the grains are with the chaff, the whole is thought to be chaff; but when they shall be separated, then shall there be a testimony to Israel.

VERS. 5.-- Seats. (ID.) That is, the just, in whom God [Deum; read Deus, "God sits"] sits, etc., as far as let all therefore who are to be questioned beware for themselves.

VERS. 6.-- Pray ye. (CASS.) The second part, where he speaks to the judges, wishing them the abundance of peace which he proclaimed out of love of the brethren. To them that love. 1043D(AUG.) He who loves in another the good which he himself cannot have, it is reckoned to him as though he had it; whence: If charity has not what to give, let it give a cup of water; and as much is reckoned to him as to Zacchaeus his many gifts (Matth. X). The means are unequal, but the charity is not unequal.

VERS. 7.-- Let peace be made. (ID.) Charity is a virtue strong as death, etc., as far as he subjoins: Because of my brethren.

In the towers. (ID.) That is, in thy high places. The judges are few, but many shall pertain to each one of them, whom they shall receive into everlasting tabernacles, and then shall there be abundance in the towers; but God is their whole abundance, both of those who receive and of those who are received.

VERS. 9.-- Because of the house of the Lord God. Or thou mayest so read it 1044Athat this verse is the exposition of the preceding. As it were, I spoke peace of thee, for neighbours, brethren, namely: I have sought good things for thee, because of the house of the Lord our God. The sense of these words is not changed. For thee. O thou, heavenly Jerusalem, because thou art the house of God, and so in this hoc, that I love thee, I love God.

PSALMUS CXXII.

Canticum graduum. (CASS.) Quartus gradus, inter quaslibet angustias constanter de Domino esse praesumendum, donec misertus exaudiat. Qui supra ad montes, nunc ad Deum oculos levat.

VERS. 1.-- Ad te levavi. (ID.) Primo vox tribulatorum Deum respicientium, non ad alia patrocinia; secundo, precatur misericordiam contra insultantes. (AUG.) Ad te levavi. Quo levaret, nisi quo ascendens 1044Btendebat? non se attendit iste, ut superbus, qui sibi placet: nam qui sibi displicet, hic talis Deo placet; et cui Deus placet, ipse sibi displicet. Levavi. Ascensus ergo est in affectu, etc., usque ad sed qui peregrinatur et desiderat patriam.

VERS. 2.-- Ecce sicut oculi, etc. (CASS.) Servus levat oculos in manus Domini, quando eget vel quando vapulat, quia utrumque in Domini potestate. Sicut oculi ancillae. (AUG.) Servus est populus; Dominus, Christus; Ancilla, Ecclesia; domina, Dei virtus, et Dei sapientia. Et si jam filii et amici per gratiam, servi tamen sumus per creaturam, quia omnis creatura Deo servit. (CASS.) Dat similttudinem de servo et ancilla, domino et domina, ne femineus et debilior sexus se exceptum putet.

1044CVERS. 3.-- Miserere. (ID.) Secunda pars, ubi precatur misericordiam contra insultantes. Servus qui vapulat, levatis oculis ad Deum, erumpit in necessariam vocem: Miserere.

Repleti sumus. Ut cum dicitur. Quid credis, insane, vides quod credis? Reversus est ne aliquis ab inferis, et retulit tibi quid ibi agitur? Ecce, quod ego amo, video et fruor.

PSALM CXXII.

A canticle of degrees. (CASS.) The fourth degree, that amid whatsoever straits one must steadfastly presume upon the Lord, until he take pity and hear. He who above lifted his eyes to the mountains, now lifts them to God.

VERS. 1.-- To thee have I lifted up. (ID.) First the voice of the troubled looking to God, not to other patronages; secondly, he prays for mercy against those who insult him. (AUG.) To thee have I lifted up. Whither should he lift them, save whither he tended in ascending? 1044Bthis man does not regard himself, as the proud man does who pleases himself: for he who is displeasing to himself, such a one pleases God; and he to whom God is pleasing is himself displeasing to himself. I have lifted up. The ascent therefore is in the affection, etc., as far as but he who is a pilgrim and desires his country.

VERS. 2.-- Behold as the eyes, etc. (CASS.) The servant lifts his eyes to the hands of his master, when he is in want or when he is beaten, because both are in the master's power. As the eyes of the handmaid. (AUG.) The servant is the people; the Lord, Christ; the handmaid, the Church; the mistress, the power of God and the wisdom of God. And though we are now sons and friends by grace, yet we are servants by creation, because every creature serves God. (CASS.) He gives a similitude similttudinem from the manservant and the handmaid, the master and the mistress, lest the feminine and weaker sex suppose itself excepted.

1044CVERS. 3.-- Have mercy. (ID.) The second part, where he prays for mercy against those who insult him. The servant who is beaten, having lifted his eyes to God, breaks forth into the needful cry: Have mercy.

We are filled. As when it is said: What dost thou believe, madman; dost thou see what thou believest? Has anyone returned from the dead, and told thee what is done there? Behold, what I love, I see and enjoy.

PSALMUS CXXIII.

VERS. 1.-- Nisi quia. (CASS.) Primo sancti martyres memores quanta evaserunt, soli misericordiae ascribunt; secundo, gratias agunt, quod liberati.

VERS. 3.-- Forte vivos deglutissent nos. Vivunt qui sciunt idolum nihil esse. Mortui sunt, qui illud putant aliquid esse. Ergo mortui absorbentur, qui 1044Dputant malum faciendum quod faciunt; vivi autem, qui quidem sciunt malum esse quod faciunt, sed persecutione superati in societatem transeunt impiorum, et Deo hujus vitae dulcedinem praeferunt, sicut quidam qui timore mortis idolis sacrificaverunt. (AUG.) Attende etiam quod Petrus, id est Ecclesia, absorbet multos, sed non vivos. Cui dicitur: Macta et manduca. (Act. X.) Nullum enim manducat, id est, membris inserit, nisi mactatum, id est, renuntiantem diabolo. Mactatur ergo in malo, sed vivificatur in bono, qui manducatur a Petro. E contra accidit illi quem deglutit diabolus.

VERS. 4.-- Aqua. (AUG.) Peccator populus (et est a similitudine Aegyptiorum): quae aqua torrens fluit 1045Acum impetu, sed cito transit; unde subdit: torrentem. --Forsitan ponunt Latini, ut possunt, pro Graeco ἄρα dubitationis loco, quod intelligibilius dicitur: putas, pertransit anima nostra? id est, magnitudo periculi vix sinit hoc credi.

VERS. 5.-- Aquam intolerabilem. (AUG.) Sine substantia, ut sunt vitia, et peccata, et dulcedo hujus vitae, etc., usque ad prodigumque filium longa necessitate confectum ad patrem reduceret.

VERS. 6.-- Benedictus Dominus. (CASS.) Secunda pars, ubi sancti gratias agunt quod liberati et quod laqueus contritus.

VERS. 7.-- Anima nostra. (AUG.) Vel, sicut aliquo faciente strepitum magnum, etc., usque ad quae est quasi laqueus. Venantium. (ID.) Venantes sunt 1045Bpersequentes, esca in muscipula, dulcedo hujus vitae. Laqueus contritus. (CASS.) Occisis martyribus, non restat dulcedo vitae, qua possint iterum capi: sed ipsi non simul contriti sunt, imo liberati. Contritus. (ID.) Quasi diceret: quia ferreus erat; non ruptus, ut stupa, tanta fortitudo passionis, tanta potentia liberantis.

PSALM CXXIII.

VERS. 1.-- If it had not been that. (CASS.) First the holy martyrs, mindful of how great things they have escaped, ascribe them to mercy alone; secondly, they give thanks that they have been delivered.

VERS. 3.-- Perhaps they had swallowed us up alive. They live who know that an idol is nothing. They are dead who think it to be something. Therefore the dead are swallowed up, who 1044Dthink that the evil which they do is a thing to be done; but the living are they who indeed know that what they do is evil, but being overcome by persecution pass over into the fellowship of the ungodly, and prefer the sweetness of this life to God, as certain men did who for fear of death sacrificed to idols. (AUG.) Mark also that Peter, that is, the Church, swallows up many, but not alive. To whom it is said: Slay and eat. (Act. X.) [Vulg. occide, "kill"] For he eats none, that is, sets none among his members, save one slain, that is, one renouncing the devil. He therefore is slain as to evil, but quickened as to good, who is eaten by Peter. The contrary befalls him whom the devil swallows down.

VERS. 4.-- Water. (AUG.) The sinful people (and it is from the likeness of the Egyptians): which water flows as a torrent 1045Awith violence, but quickly passes; whence he subjoins: a torrent. --Perhaps the Latins set down, as best they can, for the Greek ἄρα in the place of doubting, which is more intelligibly said: thinkest thou, has our soul passed through? that is, the greatness of the peril scarcely suffers this to be believed.

VERS. 5.-- Water insupportable. (AUG.) Without substance, as are vices, and sins, and the sweetness of this life, etc., as far as and might bring back to the father the prodigal son worn out by long need.

VERS. 6.-- Blessed be the Lord. (CASS.) The second part, where the saints give thanks that they have been delivered and that the snare has been broken.

VERS. 7.-- Our soul. (AUG.) Or, as when someone makes a great noise, etc., as far as which is as it were a snare. Of them that hunt. (ID.) The hunters are 1045Bthe persecutors; the bait in the trap, the sweetness of this life. The snare is broken. (CASS.) The martyrs being slain, there remains no sweetness of life whereby they might be taken again: but they themselves were not broken along with it, nay rather delivered. Broken. (ID.) As if he should say: because it was of iron; not torn apart, like tow: so great was the fortitude of the passion, so great the power of him that delivered.

PSALMUS CXXIV.

VERS. 1.-- Canticum. (CASS.) Sextus gradus, confidentia fidelissimi Christiani solidissimis montibus comparatur, quam habet in Domino, ne zelet felices in hoc saeculo. Qui confidunt. (AUG.) Hic psalmus docet, etc., usque ad qui sunt isti? qualis est ista Jerusalem? breviter describit.

VERS. 2.-- Montes in circuitu, id est, angeli, prophetae, 1045Capostoli sunt murus ejus: unde Isaias: Et erit in ea murus, et antemurale (Isa. XXVI); sed ne in montibus remaneas, addit, et Dominus in circuitu. Ne ergo sit spes in montibus, sed in vertice montium: unde Isaias: Erit in novissimis diebus mons in vertice (Isa. XXI), etc. Qui confidunt. (CASS.) Primo asserit, etc., usque ad quia et multi sunt, et unum sunt. Mons Sion. (HIER.) Christus, in quo fundata est Ecclesia: Mons ille ad litteram, in fine saeculi commovebitur.

VERS. 3.-- Virgam peccatorum. (AUG.) Dominantur enim aliquando propter disciplinam bonorum, sed hoc non semper erit, ut hic aperte dicit propheta: et ideo non deficiunt justi, quia sciunt tempus futurum, quo Christus in claritate sua apparens, congregabit 1045Dante se omnes gentes, et dividet eas sicut pastor dividit haedos ab ovibus, ovesque ponet a dextris, haedos a sinistris. Sortem. (CASS.) Id est, justos sorte electos, vel qui sunt sors et haereditas Dei.

VERS. 4.-- Benefac, Domine. (ID.) Secunda pars, ubi confirmato populo, precatur quod scit futurum ut bonis prosperitas, malis vindicta veniat.

VERS. 5.-- Declinantes autem. (ID.) Pari etiam sententia pereunt, qui declinant jussa principis, et qui opera mala velle contendunt; deficientes, cum cogentibus deficere. Pax super Israel. (AUG.) Uno nomine patria haereditas dicitur quae est Christus. Ipse enim est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum, qui pacem supra pacem dabit nobis.

PSALM CXXIV.

VERS. 1.-- A canticle. (CASS.) The sixth degree: the confidence of the most faithful Christian, which he has in the Lord, is compared to the most solid mountains, that he may not be jealous of those who are happy in this world. They that trust. (AUG.) This psalm teaches, etc., as far as who are these? what manner of Jerusalem is that? he briefly describes it.

VERS. 2.-- The mountains round about, that is, the angels, the prophets, 1045Cthe apostles are its wall: whence Isaias: And there shall be in it a wall and a bulwark (Isa. XXVI); but lest thou remain among the mountains, he adds, and the Lord round about. Let there not then be hope in the mountains, but in the top of the mountains: whence Isaias: In the last days there shall be a mountain on the top (Isa. XXI), etc. They that trust. (CASS.) First he affirms, etc., as far as because they are both many and are one. Mount Sion. (HIER.) Christ, on whom the Church is founded: that mountain, according to the letter, shall be shaken at the end of the world.

VERS. 3.-- The rod of sinners. (AUG.) For they bear rule sometimes for the discipline of the good, but this shall not be always, as the prophet here plainly says: and therefore the just do not fail, because they know the time to come, in which Christ, appearing in his brightness, shall gather 1045Dbefore him all nations, and shall divide them as a shepherd divides the kids from the sheep, and shall set the sheep on the right hand, the kids on the left. The lot. (CASS.) That is, the just chosen by lot, or who are the lot and the inheritance of God.

VERS. 4.-- Do good, O Lord. (ID.) The second part, where, the people being confirmed, he prays for what he knows shall come to pass, that prosperity may come to the good, vengeance to the wicked.

VERS. 5.-- But such as turn aside. (ID.) By a like sentence also do they perish who turn aside from the commands of the prince, and they who strive to will evil works; those failing, together with those who compel them to fail. Peace upon Israel. (AUG.) By one name is called the paternal inheritance, which is Christ. For he is our peace, who has made both one, who shall give us peace above peace.

PSALMUS CXXV.

  • 1046A

VERS. 1.-- Canticum graduum. (CASS.) Septimus gradus in figura Veteris Testamenti per venturum Christum, reversionem de captivitate, quasi de Babylonia prophetat: unde jam consolatio, et seminatio ut plus metatur. (AUG.) Redempti sanguine Christi et conversi a captivitate, haec cantant, dum peregrini, gementes in via. Sion est Jerusalem in angelis aeterna, in hominibus captiva. In convertendo. (CASS.) Primum magnitudo facti, cum magnitudine gaudii ostenditur: secundo precatur conversionem a captivitate adhuc futura, ibi, Converte, Domine. In convertendo. (AUG.) Vel, cum converterit, etc., usque ad converte, Domine, captivitatem nostram. Sicut. (ID.) Non semper ad similitudinem ponitur, sed 1046Bad proprietatem, ut hic; unde etiam dicitur: Fecit ut justus, quod vere est, ita facti fiunt isti sicut consolati, id est, gavisi sunt, ut consolationem accipientes in resurrectione Christi, qui praecessit ut consequamur.

VERS. 2.-- Os nostrum. (CASS.) Cordis arcanum, ubi primum gaudia, quae post officio linguae erumpunt. (AUG.) Os nostrum. Cordis, inde procedit malum bonum, quod nos mundat, vel inquinat; unde non: Quod procedit de ore, inquinat (Marc. VII). Non de ore carnis, sed cordis. Non enim si nominas furta et alia mala, immundus es: sed dum cogitas, et si sileas. Inter gentes. (ID.) Non gentes, quia non omnes credunt. Magnificavit, quia vident eos etiam virtutes operari; firmum testimonium ab adversario. 1046C(CASS.) Et vere magnificavit, ne dubites de verbis gentium.

VERS. 4.-- Converte, Domine. (ID.) Secunda pars. Precatur conversionem, quae futura est, in qua fiet seminatio spe gaudii. (ID.) Adventus Domini redemptione praedicta, precantur iterum peccata sua dimitti. In generali remissione gaudent, et sibi veniam precantur. Converte, Domine, Captivitatem nostram. (ID.) Nulla ad litteram in diebus David, sed sub diabolo mundus captivus, etc., usque ad non ideo desistendum, quia qui seminat in lacrymis. (THEOD.) Austrum Hierosolymam vocat, etc., usque ad ut cogantur, et torrentis instar iter faciant.

VERS. 5.-- In lacrymis. (AUG.) Spiritualis seminatio semper in lacrymis, unde: Beati qui lugent. Qui 1046Dvero seminant in carne, cum laetitia seminant: sed post fletus: quia extrema gaudii luctus occupat. (ID.) Zachaeus, Ecce dimidium, etc., usque ad: Qui dederit calicem aquae frigidae, non perdet mercedem (Matth. X).

VERS. 6.-- Euntes. (CASS.) Provectu melioris vitae. Mittentes, ante se praemittentes in illo saeculo. Sua, non de rapina, sed de proprio labore; venientes, ad judicium. Hoc commune omnium, sed ad gaudium non nisi boni veniunt. Et flebant. (AUG.) Quia miseri erant, etc., usque ad optat multos esse aegros.

PSALM CXXV.

  • 1046A

VERS. 1.-- A canticle of degrees. (CASS.) The seventh degree, in a figure of the Old Testament, prophesies through Christ who is to come the return from captivity, as it were from Babylon: whence now consolation, and a sowing that more may be reaped. (AUG.) Those redeemed by the blood of Christ and turned back from captivity sing these things, while they are pilgrims, groaning by the way. Sion is Jerusalem, eternal in the angels, captive in men. In the turning. (CASS.) First the greatness of the deed is shown, with the greatness of the joy: secondly he prays for the turning from captivity still to come, there, Turn again, O Lord. In the turning. (AUG.) Or, when he shall have turned, etc., as far as turn again, O Lord, our captivity. As. (ID.) It is not always set for a likeness, but 1046Bfor a property, as here; whence it is also said: He did as a just man, which he truly is; so these are made as men comforted, that is, they rejoiced, as receiving consolation in the resurrection of Christ, who went before that we might follow.

VERS. 2.-- Our mouth. (CASS.) The secret of the heart, where joys first are, which afterwards break forth by the office of the tongue. (AUG.) Our mouth. Of the heart: thence proceeds the evil and the good which cleanses or defiles us; whence not: That which proceedeth out of the mouth, defileth (Marc. VII) [Vulg. Mc 7:15 quae de homine procedunt, illa communicant hominem; Migne's wording is that of Mt 15:11]. Not of the mouth of the flesh, but of the heart. For thou art not unclean if thou namest thefts and other evils: but while thou thinkest of them, even if thou keep silence. Among the Gentiles. (ID.) Not the Gentiles, because not all believe. He hath magnified, because they see them work miracles also; a firm testimony from an adversary. 1046C(CASS.) And he has truly magnified, lest thou doubt because of the words of the Gentiles.

VERS. 4.-- Turn again, O Lord. (ID.) The second part. He prays for the turning which is to come, in which there shall be a sowing in hope of joy. (ID.) The redemption of the coming of the Lord having been foretold, they pray again that their own sins be forgiven. In the general remission they rejoice, and they pray pardon for themselves. Turn again, O Lord, our captivity. (ID.) There was none according to the letter in the days of David, but under the devil the world was captive, etc., as far as it is not therefore to be given over, because he that soweth in tears. (THEOD.) He calls Jerusalem the south, etc., as far as that they may be constrained, and make their way after the manner of a torrent.

VERS. 5.-- In tears. (AUG.) Spiritual sowing is always in tears, whence: Blessed are they that mourn. But they 1046Dwho sow in the flesh, sow with gladness: but afterwards weeping: because mourning taketh hold of the end of joy. (ID.) Zacchaeus, Behold the half, etc., as far as: He that shall give a cup of cold water shall not lose his reward (Matth. X).

VERS. 6.-- Going. (CASS.) By the advancement of a better life. Casting, sending on before them into that world. Their own, not of rapine, but of their own labour; coming, to the judgment. This is common to all, but to joy none come but the good. And they wept. (AUG.) Because they were wretched, etc., as far as he wishes that many be sick.

PSALMUS CXXVI.

VERS. 1.-- Canticum graduum Salomonis. (CASS.) Octavus gradus, etc., usque ad et in se lapide angulari Ecclesiam de duobus parietibus Judaeorum et 1047Agentium construxit. (AUG.) Hic additur Salomonis, quia is aedificavit templum, in figura pacifici Christi, qui aedificavit Ecclesiam de duobus parietibus. Ne ergo acciperes illum Salomonem, ait, Nisi Dominus aedificaverit. In hoc spes ponenda, sed in nullo hominum: quia et ille Salomon cecidit qui templum aedificavit. (CASS.) Primo, monet quomodo ascendentes se habere debeant, scilicet discant quod aedificatio et custodia non nisi a Deo est. Et exaltatio in futuro non est nisi post humiliationem. Secundo, dicit quae sit haereditas, et quomodo collecta, ibi, Ecce haereditas. Nisi Dominus. (ID.) Quasi dieeret: jam venit Jesus, de captivitate reduxit: jam civitas aedificatur Jerusalem; sed discant ascendentes, quod aedificatio et custodia non nisi a Deo, et exaltatio 1047Bnon nisi post humiliationem in futuro; etsi enim laeti de gratia Novi Testamenti, tamen in tanto munere non est praesumendum alicui. Domum. (AUG.) Ad hanc ascendit omnis, qui proficit: cadit ab hac omnis, qui deficit; amando Deum ascendis, amando saeculum cadis. Sunt enim ista cantica amantium, et quodam desiderio sancto flagrantium. Laboraverunt. (ID.) Omnes in hac aedificatione laborant, qui in Ecclesia praedicant verbum Dei. Civitatem. (CASS.) De domo ad civitatem transit, ut nec in singulis, nec in minuta collectione fit praesumptio. Et quamvis domus et civitas secundum metaphoram, quae de diversis inducitur, sint diversa: una tamen est Ecclesia, quam utraque significat.

1047CVERS. 2.-- Ante lucem. (AUG.) Si surgitis antequam lux surgat; lux est Christus, post quem surgendum est, non ante; ut ille facit, qui se ei praeponit: volens hic esse altus, ubi ille humilis fuit: ut et filii Zebedaei: sed resurrectio, id est, exaltatio sequitur sessionem, id est humiliationem, ut lux nostra Christus post mortem surrexit altus. Sederitis. Sessio aliquando significat honorem judicandi, hic autem humiliationem. Manducatis panem doloris. (AUG.) Manducat panem doloris, qui gemit in hac peregrinatione, id est, in valle plorationis de afflictione se reficit, dicens: Factae sunt mihi lacrymae meae panes die ac nocte (Psal. XLI). Somnum. (CASS.) Mortem temporalem, in qua secura pausatio.

VERS. 3.-- Ecce haereditas. (ID.) Secundo, quae 1047Dhaereditas et quomodo collecta. Quasi diceret, dilecti post somnum surgent. Fructus ventris. (AUG.) Venter Ecclesiae, etc., usque ad quia omnes acquisivit per obedientiam passionis, unde postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes haereditatem tuam (Psal. II).

VERS. 4.-- Sicut sagittae. (ID.) Sed unde facta est tanta haereditas, quia potens Dominus, dum fortiter sagittas, apostolos, de arcu sacrae Scripturae excussit, usque ad fines terrae pervenerunt illae excussae, sic sunt autem filii excussorum, quomodo illi excussi. Filii excussorum. (ID.) Filii apostolorum; quibus dictum est, Excutite pulverem de pedibus vestris (Matth. XVIII). Sed ita videntur, etc., usque ad qui manu Dei missi sunt usque ad fines terrae.

PSALM CXXVI.

VERS. 1.-- A canticle of degrees of Solomon. (CASS.) The eighth degree, etc., as far as and in himself, as the corner stone, he built up the Church of two walls, of the Jews and 1047Aof the Gentiles. (AUG.) Here is added of Solomon, because it was he who built the temple, in a figure of Christ the peacemaker, who built the Church of two walls. Lest therefore thou shouldst understand that Solomon, he says, Unless the Lord build. In him is hope to be placed, but in no man: because even that Solomon fell who built the temple. (CASS.) First, he admonishes how they that ascend ought to bear themselves, namely that they learn that the building and the keeping are from none but God. And exaltation in the world to come is only after humiliation. Secondly, he tells what the inheritance is, and how it is gathered, there, Behold the inheritance. Unless the Lord. (ID.) As if he should say dieeret: now Jesus has come, he has brought back from captivity: now the city Jerusalem is being built; but let them that ascend learn that the building and the keeping are from none but God, and exaltation 1047Bonly after humiliation in the world to come; for although they are glad of the grace of the New Testament, yet in so great a gift no man ought to presume. The house. (AUG.) To this every man ascends who advances: from this every man falls who fails; by loving God thou ascendest, by loving the world thou fallest. For these are the songs of lovers, and of men burning with a certain holy desire. They have laboured. (ID.) All labour in this building who preach the word of God in the Church. The city. (CASS.) He passes from the house to the city, that presumption be made neither in individuals nor in a small gathering. And although house and city, according to the metaphor which is drawn from different things, are diverse: yet the Church is one, which both signify.

1047CVERS. 2.-- Before the light. (AUG.) If ye rise before the light rises; the light is Christ, after whom we must rise, not before; as he does who sets himself before him: wishing to be lofty here, where he was humble: as also the sons of Zebedee: but the resurrection, that is, the exaltation, follows the sitting, that is, the humiliation, as our light Christ rose lofty after death. Ye shall have sat. Sitting sometimes signifies the honour of judging, but here humiliation. Ye that eat the bread of sorrow. (AUG.) He eats the bread of sorrow who groans in this pilgrimage, that is, in the vale of weeping refreshes himself out of his affliction, saying: My tears have been made my bread day and night (Psal. XLI) [Vulg. Fuerunt mihi lacrimae meae panes, "my tears have been my bread"]. Sleep. (CASS.) Temporal death, in which is a secure rest.

VERS. 3.-- Behold the inheritance. (ID.) Secondly, what the 1047Dinheritance is and how it is gathered. As if he should say, the beloved shall rise after sleep. The fruit of the womb. (AUG.) The womb of the Church, etc., as far as because he acquired all men through the obedience of his passion, whence, ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance (Psal. II).

VERS. 4.-- As arrows. (ID.) But whence so great an inheritance was made: because the Lord is mighty: when he shot forth the arrows, the apostles, mightily from the bow of holy Scripture, those that were shot forth reached unto the ends of the earth; and such are the children of them that were shot forth, as were they that were shot forth. The children of them that were shot forth. (ID.) The children of the apostles; to whom it was said, Shake off the dust from your feet (Matth. XVIII). But they so appear, etc., as far as who were sent by the hand of God unto the ends of the earth.

PSALMUS CXXVII.

  • 1048A

VERS. 1.-- Canticum graduum. (CASS.) Nonus gradus est, ut pacificus caste timeatur, qui solus exaltat, custodit, aedificat. Primo bona timentis enumerat; secundo optat bona timentis. Beati omnes qui timent Dominum. Sciendum quatuor esse timores, etc., usque ad de quo hic dicit Propheta: Beati omnes qui timent Dominum.

VERS. 2.-- Labores manuum. (ID.) Et nota quod a pluribus coepit dicens: Beati: sed quia omnes unum sunt in Christo singulariter, sequitur, Labores manuum tuarum. (AUG.) Labores fructuum dicit, cum deberet dicere: Fructum laborum; sed quia et labore cum gaudio sumuntur propter spem, et ipsi jucundant, et modo sunt cibus; sed jucundior 1048Beorum fructus erit, quando sancti veniens cum exsultatione portantes manipulos suos.

VERS. 3.-- Uxor tua. (CASS.) Etsi hoc ad litteram accipi posset, etc., usque ad ad Novum Testamentum pertinet. (AUG.) Vel per uxorem intelligitur Ecclesia, et dirigitur sermo ad Christum, cum dicitur tua et tui; nec tamen mutatur vox, vel persona propter unitatem capitis et corporis. Unus enim homo Christus, caput est, et corpus, et in capite quisque fidelium hoc habet.

VERS. 4.-- Benedicetur. (CASS.) Ubi benedictio est, omnia bona confluunt ad gaudium suavitatis.

Benedicetur. (ID.) Secunda pars, ubi ex pietate postulat benedici timentes, optat hic bona timenti, quae, scilicet non sunt malis communia.

1048CVERS. 5.--Vel, Dominus. (AUG.) Judaeorum, Ex Sion, etc., usque ad quod non ita possunt.

PSALM CXXVII.

  • 1048A

VERS. 1.-- A canticle of degrees. (CASS.) The ninth degree is, that the peacemaker be chastely feared, who alone exalts, keeps, and builds. First he enumerates the good things of him that fears; secondly he wishes the good things of him that fears. Blessed are all they that fear the Lord. It is to be known that there are four fears, etc., as far as of which the Prophet here says: Blessed are all they that fear the Lord.

VERS. 2.-- The labours of the hands. (ID.) And note that he began from the plural, saying: Blessed: but because all are one in Christ, in the singular there follows, The labours of thy hands. (AUG.) He says the labours of the fruits, when he ought to say: The fruit of the labours; but because they are taken up with joy even in the labour, for the sake of hope, they themselves also give delight, and are even now food; but more delightful 1048Bshall their fruit be, when the saints, coming [veniens; read venient, "shall come"], carrying their sheaves with joyfulness.

VERS. 3.-- Thy wife. (CASS.) Although this might be taken according to the letter, etc., as far as it pertains to the New Testament. (AUG.) Or by wife the Church is understood, and the speech is directed to Christ, when thy and thine are said; nor yet is the voice or the person changed, because of the unity of the head and the body. For Christ is one man, both head and body, and in the head each one of the faithful has this.

VERS. 4.-- He shall be blessed. (CASS.) Where blessing is, all good things flow together unto the joy of sweetness.

He shall be blessed. (ID.) The second part, where out of piety he asks that they that fear be blessed; here he wishes good things for him that fears, which, namely, are not common to the wicked.

1048CVERS. 5.--Or, The Lord. (AUG.) Of the Jews, Out of Sion, etc., as far as which they cannot so do.

PSALMUS CXXVIII.

VERS. 1.-- Canticum graduum. (CASS.) Decimus gradus, ut qui caste timet, pro eo omnia ferat, quod nunc expedit Ecclesiae inter malos.

Saepe expugnaverunt. (AUG.) Mali, etsi audiunt verbum Dei, etc., usque ad quod tot malos ferant. (CASS.) Ostendens primo quae tulerit, consolatur infirmos. Secundo agit de reprobatione persequentium, ibi, Dominus justus. Saepe expugnaverunt. Quasi: O filii, nolite mirari ad ista, etc., usque ad quia crescit Ecclesia in adversis.

VERS. 2.-- Etenim non potuerunt mihi. (AUG.) 1048DScilicet praevalere, ut me traherent in consensum peccati.

VERS. 3.-- Supra dorsum. (CASS.) Quod mali nequeunt publice omnibus, occulte singulis tentant suadere, ut qui a facie venientes viderentur a tergo non sentiantur. Prolongaverunt iniquitatem. Alias, longe a me fecerunt injustitiam suam. (AUG.) Qui etsi mali cum bonis in saeculo, si etiam in Ecclesia sint: ne quis tamen putet iniquitatem juxta justitiam, etsi eos porto, tamen longe est a me eorum iniquitas, ne quis ergo timeat mistos sibi malos, qui longe sunt.

Dominus justus. (CASS.) Secunda pars, ubi agit de reprobatione persequentium.

VERS. 4.-- Qui oderunt Sion. (ID.) Quam non tantum manifesti persecutores, sed etiam qui ficte 1049Aintrant, oderunt. Qui enim nolunt observare verbum Dei, oderunt Ecclesiam.

Fiant sicut fenum tectorum. (CASS.) Feno tectorum mali comparantur, etc., usque ad sed in neutro fructus est malis.

(GREG.) Ante omnes herbas arescere scirpus dicitur, etc., usque ad quasi viriditatis speciem amittit, etc.

VERS. 6.-- Quod priusquam evellatur. (AUG.) Nondum finiti sunt in judicio Dei, et jam non habent succum viriditatis.

VERS. 8.-- Et non dixerunt. (CASS.) Mos inter Hebraeos erat ut viator operantibus benediceret: unde hic dicitur e contrario, quia inaniter operantibus benedictio nulla datur.

1049BEt non dixerunt. Quos non colligent angeli, quibus non praedicaverunt apostoli. Et hoc est quod ait:

(AUG.) Et non dixerunt, etc. Maxime Judaeis, mos erat quibuscunque operantibus dicere: Benedictio Domini super vos. Benediximus vobis in nomine, etc. (CASS.) Bonis benedicunt, non in suo, sed in nomine Domini: a quo omnia, non ab eis.

PSALM CXXVIII.

VERS. 1.-- A canticle of degrees. (CASS.) The tenth degree, that he who fears chastely may bear all things for his sake, which is now expedient for the Church among the wicked.

Often have they fought against me. (AUG.) The wicked, although they hear the word of God, etc., as far as that they bear so many wicked men. (CASS.) Showing first what things he has borne, he comforts the weak. Secondly he treats of the reprobation of the persecutors, there, The Lord is just. Often have they fought against me. As it were: O sons, do not marvel at these things, etc., as far as because the Church grows in adversities.

VERS. 2.-- For indeed they could not against me. (AUG.) 1048DNamely, prevail, so as to draw me into consent unto sin.

VERS. 3.-- Upon the back. (CASS.) What the wicked cannot do publicly to all, they attempt to urge secretly upon single persons, so that they who would be seen coming from the front may not be felt from behind. They have lengthened out iniquity. Elsewhere, they have put their injustice far from me. (AUG.) Who, although the wicked are with the good in the world, even if they be also in the Church: yet lest any suppose iniquity to stand beside justice, although I bear them, nevertheless their iniquity is far from me; let no one therefore fear the wicked mingled with him, who are far off.

The Lord is just. (CASS.) The second part, where he treats of the reprobation of the persecutors.

VERS. 4.-- They that hate Sion. (ID.) Whom not only open persecutors hate, but also they who enter 1049Afeignedly. For they who will not keep the word of God hate the Church.

Let them be as grass upon the housetops. (CASS.) The wicked are compared to grass upon the housetops, etc., as far as but in neither is there fruit for the wicked.

(GREG.) The bulrush is said to wither before all herbs, etc., as far as it loses, as it were, the appearance of greenness, etc.

VERS. 6.-- Which before it be plucked up. (AUG.) They are not yet finished in the judgment of God, and already they have not the sap of greenness.

VERS. 8.-- And they have not said. (CASS.) It was a custom among the Hebrews that a wayfarer should bless those at work: whence it is here said conversely, that to those who work in vain no blessing is given.

1049BAnd they have not said. Whom the angels shall not gather, to whom the apostles have not preached. And this is what he says:

(AUG.) And they have not said, etc. Chiefly among the Jews it was the custom to say to any whosoever were at work: The blessing of the Lord be upon you. We have blessed you in the name, etc. (CASS.) They bless the good, not in their own name, but in the name of the Lord: from whom are all things, not from them.

PSALMUS CXXIX.

VERS. 1.-- Canticum graduum. (ID.) Undecimus gradus, etc., usque ad ponitur laeta conclusio cum certitudine veniae, ibi, Speret Israel in Domino.

De profundis. (AUG.) Qui sentit se in profundo, etc., usque ad sicut dicit Scriptura: Peccator, cum venerit 1049Cin profundum vitiorum, contemnit.

VERS. 3.-- Quis sustinebit. (ID.) Quia prope omnis humana vita peccatis circumlatratur, omnisque conscientia suis cogitationibus accusatur. Non est castum cor, quod praesumit de justitia sua. Praesumat ergo de Dei misericordia, Quia apud eum propitiatio, unde subdit:

VERS. 4.-- Quia apud te propitiatio est. Quasi: Qua spe clamas? Quia est in te misericordia quod ita ait: Vel ita junge.

(AUG.) Nullus potest sustinere, etc., usque ad una ergo est spes: Quia apud te propitiatio est, etc., Propter legem tuam, (ID.) legem misericordiae sustinui, etc., usque ad et hanc legem dedisti in ipsa necessitate.

1049DVERS. 6.-- Matutina. (ID.) Speret vigilia matutina, qui non aliud a Deo quam immortalitatem speret. A custodia matutina, etc., usque ad inde in lege caput et cauda hostiae Domino offerebantur. Speret Israel in Domino. (CASS.) Secunda pars, ubi laeta conclusio: Securus de se, praedicat, ut semper sperent in Domino. Quasi sicut anima speravit, similiter speret Israel.

VERS. 8.-- Et ipse redimet Israel ex omnibus iniquitatibus ejus. (ID.) Hic dixit jam quid sit facturus ille, quem dixit misericordem et copiosum.

PSALM CXXIX.

VERS. 1.-- A canticle of degrees. (ID.) The eleventh degree, etc., as far as a glad conclusion is set down with the certainty of pardon, there, Let Israel hope in the Lord.

Out of the depths. (AUG.) He who feels himself in the deep, etc., as far as as the Scripture says: The sinner, when he shall have come 1049Cinto the depth of vices, contemneth. [Vulg. Prov. 18:3 impius, cum in profundum venerit peccatorum, contemnit, "the ungodly … the depth of sins"]

VERS. 3.-- Who shall abide it. (ID.) Because well nigh all human life is barked at round about by sins, and every conscience is accused by its own thoughts. That heart is not chaste which presumes upon its own justice. Let it therefore presume upon the mercy of God, For with him there is propitiation, whence he subjoins:

VERS. 4.-- For with thee there is propitiation. As it were: In what hope dost thou cry? Because there is mercy in thee, wherefore he speaks thus: Or join it thus.

(AUG.) No man can abide it, etc., as far as one hope therefore there is: For with thee there is propitiation, etc., For thy law's sake, (ID.) I have waited for the law of mercy, etc., as far as and thou hast given this law in the very necessity.

1049DVERS. 6.-- The morning. (ID.) Let him hope in the morning watch who hopes for nothing else from God than immortality. From the morning watch, etc., as far as thence in the law the head and the tail of the victim were offered to the Lord. Let Israel hope in the Lord. (CASS.) The second part, where is the glad conclusion: Secure concerning himself, he preaches that they should hope always in the Lord. As it were, as his soul has hoped, so let Israel hope.

VERS. 8.-- And he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities. (ID.) Here he has now said what that one shall do, whom he called merciful and plentiful.

PSALMUS CXXX.

VERS. 1.-- Canticum graduum. (CASS.) Duodecimus gradus est humilitas, quam intus et extra hic 1050Ase habere ostendit. Ad humilitatem ergo monet.

Domine, non est. (ID.) Primo proponens se humilem, poenam inducit non humili; secundo, suo exemplo ad spem monet. Ostendens ergo se humilem intus et extra, ait. Neque ambulavi. (AUG.) Non fui superbus, nolui quasi in mirabilibus, etc., usque ad: Quanto major es, humilia te in omnibus.

VERS. 2.-- Si non humiliter sentiebam. (ID.) Nutritus in lacte quod est Verbum caro factum ut sic crescerem ad panem angelorum, ad Verbum quod apud Deum, sed non.

Exaltavi, ut haeretici. Qui si utcunque aliquid coeperint, vel visi sunt capere, inde superbiunt; et cum adhuc teneri super matrem sint, et portentur manibus, ut crescant, qui portati fuerunt in utero 1050But nascerentur: a lacte ante tempus separantur, unde exstinguntur.

Ita retributio. (ID.) Obstringit se maledicto, etc., usque ad sic revelabit Deus quod aliter sapit, quia superbis resistit, humilibus dat gratiam.

Sicut ablactatus est. Sicut enim quinque tempora narrantur, etc., usque ad quia Deus erat homo; sed non mutatus in hominem.
