VERS. 3.-- Speret Israel. (CASS.) Secunda pars, ubi concludit suo exemplo caeteros monens.

PSALM CXXX.

VERS. 1.-- A canticle of degrees. (CASS.) The twelfth degree is humility, which he here 1050Ashows that he has within and without. To humility therefore he exhorts.

Lord, it is not. (ID.) First, setting himself forth as humble, he brings in punishment for the man that is not humble; secondly, by his own example he exhorts to hope. Showing therefore that he is humble within and without, he says. Neither have I walked. (AUG.) I was not proud, I would not, as it were, walk in wonderful things, etc., as far as: The greater thou art, humble thyself in all things. [Vulg. Sir. 3:20 Quanto magnus es, "howsoever great thou art"]

VERS. 2.-- If I was not humbly minded. (ID.) Nourished in milk, which is the Word made flesh, that so I might grow up to the bread of angels, to the Word which is with God, but not.

I have exalted, as the heretics do. Who, if they have in any way begun something, or have seemed to grasp it, thereupon grow proud; and while they are still tender upon their mother, and are carried in her hands that they may grow, they who were carried in the womb 1050Bthat they might be born: they are parted from the milk before the time, whence they are quenched.

So the reward. (ID.) He binds himself with a curse, etc., as far as so shall God reveal that wherein he is otherwise minded, because he resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.

As one is weaned. For as five ages are recounted, etc., as far as because God was man; but not changed into man.

VERS. 3.-- Let Israel hope. (CASS.) The second part, where he concludes, admonishing the rest by his own example.

PSALMUS CXXXI.

VERS. 1.-- Canticum graduum. (ID.) In tredecimo gradu jam humilis et mansuetus, etc., usque ad unde in Isaia: Super quem requiescet Spiritus meus, 1050Cnisi super humilem et quietum, et trementem sermones meos?

Memento, Domine, David et omnis. (ID.) Primo ostendens votum aedificandi domum, precatur ut impleat. Secundo, ostendit domum aedificatam, ibi, Ecce audi. Tertio, dicit promissiones Dei factas aedificatae Sion, ibi, Juravit Dominus. Volens ergo aedificare domum Domino, ait in persona totius Christi capitis: O Domine, etc. David. (AUG.) Ad litteram, mansuetus, ut Sauli malum pro malo non redderet.

Sicut juravit et votum vovit. Id est, ut impleat quod promisit: nemo praesumat viribus suis reddere quod vovit. Vovit autem Ecclesia in mansuetudine, ut sit domus Dei, quod nihil gratius potest Deo offerri. Domus autem est, si sua non quaerit, sed de 1050Dcommuni gaudet: de propriis fiunt mala, unde ait: Si introiero. Sciebat se proprio impediri, ne fiat locus Dei.

VERS. 3.-- Si introiero usque donec inveniam locum Domino. Littera suspenditur, et est aposiopesis, ac si diceret: Si hoc vel illud fecero, nunquam de caetero mihi credatur. Quasi juravit David Domino: Si introiero in tabernaculum domus meae, etc. (CASS.) Vel ex persona Christi ab illo loco: Si introiero in tabernaculum domus meae, scilicet, coelestis habitationis. Tabernaculum est coelestis habitatio. Si ascendero, etc., ad dexteram Patris, ubi lectus, id est requies et finis laborum.

VERS. 4.-- Sumnum, requies mortis triduanae, 1051ADeinde aliis verbis idem repetit. Et palpebris meis dormitationem. Et requiem temporibus meis donec Ecclesia sancta praedicatione sit fundata. Aposiopesis est quasi, non amplius credatur mihi.

Et palpebris. (AUG.) Est qui non dormit, sed dormitat: modo retrahitur a terrenis, modo illo revolvitur, crebro inclinat caput.

VERS. 5.-- Et requiem. A requie temporum somnus venit ad oculos quia dormituris tempora incipiunt. Cum ergo incipit delectare ad peccatum aliquid temporale, gravantur tempora, sed ne des te illi delectationi, et somnus non venit ad oculos, ista cogitatione, si quasi confricans frontem excutis somnum.

Inveniam: (ID.) dicit, quia diu quaesivit.

1051BLocum Domino: in se quaerebat, qui super humilem et quietum requiescit. Locus autem Dei est, si suas deserit res; vel saltem, si se non amat, sed Deum.

Tabernaculum. (ID.) Adhuc gemimus. In domo laudabimus, quia gemitus est peregrinantium; laudatio jam in patria commorantium. Deo Jacob. Dicit solvisse, sicut supra dixit promisisse.

VERS. 6.-- Ecce audivimus. (CASS. Secunda pars ubi ostenditur aedificata domus, et ubi et precatur qui exaltentur, et ne Judaei sint penitus alieni. Eam in Ephrata, (AUG.) vel eam, etc., usque ad ubi erant vepres idololatriae.

(CASS.) Ecce audi, scilicet Dominum nasciturum in Ephrata Bethlehem, ubi natus est Dominus: auditum 1051Cest nasci in Bethlehem, sed propter fidem gentium in campis sylvae compertus est.

VERS. 7.-- Introibimus. (AUG.) Nos quoque perseverando in militia nostra tamen introivimus (vel introibimus) in tabernaculum ejus, Dei Jacob: ad hanc domum pertinet, qui aliis tanquam vivis lapidibus charitate compaginatus est. Intrat ergo qui diligit, et qui intrat, domus Dei efficitur. In loco. Domus Dei est, ubi debet adorari: praeter quam non audit Deus ad vitam aeternam. Ille ad domum pertinet, qui est charitate compaginatus aliis. Vel locus in quo stant pedes domus Domini, Christus est, in quo perseverant.

VERS. 8.-- Surge. (ID.) Et dicitur, qui dicit, Dormivi conturbatus: Surge a morte, in requiem 1051Dtuam, ut jam non conturberis, quia mors ultra non dominabitur.

VERS. 9.-- Sacerdotes. (ID.) Accipit eosdem sacerdotes et sanctos, scilicet omnes fideles. Vel, per sacerdotes, significat praelatos Ecclesiae; per sanctos, subjectos fideles. Arcam ergo, quam surgere precatus erat, per partes Ecclesiae distinguit.

Sacerdotes, ut in Veteri Testamento sacerdotes diversis ornamentis, ita evangelici sacerdotes diversis virtutibus adornantur: haec sunt ornamenta, quae Deus exigit. Quae enim legales pontifices in vestibus gestabant, illa evangelici sacerdotes in cordibus habere debent.

VERS. 10.-- Propter David servum. (CASS.) Memento: 1052AEt bene dico propter David, quia juravit Dominus David.

Propter: deinde ex persona ipsius David rogantis Deum Patrem.

(AUG.) Quia enim Christus a Judaeis faciem avertit ad gentes, rogatur Pater propter reliquias, ut salvae fiant, quod in apostolis et in aliis multis impletum est. Et ait: propter David, ac si diceret: Mei etiam memento, ut propter me Judaeos funditus non repellas.

VERS. 11.-- Juravit. (CASS.) Tertia pars, ubi dicit promissiones Dei factas aedificatae Sion, id est Ecclesiae. Et loquitur David in sua vel in totius Christi persona. Et non frustrabitur (alias) non poenitebit. (AUG.) Poeniteri dicitur Deus, etc., usque ad tu 1052Benim facis quia erraveras: ille facit, et liberat. De fructu ventris tui. Poterat dicere ex fructu femoris tui, etc., usque ad quia quos David temporaliter rexit, Christus spiritualiter.

VERS. 12.-- Si custodierint. (ID.) Meritum videntur facere, etc., usque ad hoc non mutatur. Et filii eorum. (CASS.) Si custodierint testamentum. Sedebunt super sedem tuam, id est, participes erunt tuae beatitudinis: Ut sicut es regiae potestatis, ita et ipsi, pro modo suo, et hoc, Usque in saeculum saeculi, id est in aeternum.

VERS. 14.-- Haec requies mea. (ID.) Sic amat nos Deus, ut dicat se requiescere, si nos requiescimus in illo.

VERS. 15.-- Viduam. (ID.) Vidua est anima, 1052Cquae se intelligit desertam omni auxilio, nisi solius Dei. Panibus. Deus est panis, qui in carne se lac fecit.

VERS. 16.-- Sacerdotes ejus. Vel distinguendum inter sacerdotes et sanctos, sicut supra. Et est, Sacerdotes ejus, id est, praelatos, Induam salutari, id est Christo, id est, ut honesti sint ad docendum. Et sancti, id est subditi. Exsultatione exsultabunt de Christo.

Exsultatione exsultabunt. (ID.) Quia induti sunt salutari, etc., usque ad qui habitat in eo, ergo, secure exaltaxit.

VERS. 17.-- Cornu David, paravi lucernam Christo. (ID.) Ecclesiae altitudo spiritualis, etc., usque ad ante Christi mortem et resurrectionem.

1052DVERS. 18.-- Induam confusione, etc. (CASS.) Hoc faciet Filius, cui omne judicium datum. Sed nota Patrem, qui hic loquitur, facere quod Filius facit.

PSALM CXXXI.

VERS. 1.-- A canticle of degrees. (ID.) In the thirteenth degree, now humble and meek, etc., as far as whence in Isaias: Upon whom shall my Spirit rest, 1050Cbut upon the humble and the quiet, and him that trembleth at my words? [Vulg. Is 66:2 ad quem autem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum, et contritum spiritu, et trementem sermones meos, "but to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little, and of a contrite spirit"]

Remember, O Lord, David, and all. (ID.) First, showing the vow of building a house, he prays that he may fulfil it. Secondly, he shows the house built, there, Behold, hear. Thirdly, he tells the promises of God made to Sion when built, there, The Lord hath sworn. Willing therefore to build a house for the Lord, he says in the person of the whole Christ, the head: O Lord, etc. David. (AUG.) According to the letter, meek, in that he rendered not evil for evil to Saul.

As he swore and vowed a vow. That is, that he may fulfil what he promised: let no man presume to render by his own strength what he has vowed. And the Church has vowed in meekness that she may be the house of God, because nothing more pleasing can be offered to God. And it is a house if it seeks not its own, but rejoices in 1050Dwhat is common: from things of one's own come evils, whence he says: If I shall enter. He knew that he was hindered by what was his own, lest a place for God should be made.

VERS. 3.-- If I shall enter as far as till I find out a place for the Lord. The letter is left hanging, and it is an aposiopesis, as if he said: If I shall do this or that, let me never hereafter be believed. As it were, David swore to the Lord: If I shall enter into the tabernacle of my house, etc. (CASS.) Or, in the person of Christ, from that place: If I shall enter into the tabernacle of my house, namely of the heavenly habitation. The tabernacle is the heavenly habitation. If I shall go up, etc., to the right hand of the Father, where is the bed, that is, rest and the end of labours.

VERS. 4.-- Sleep Sumnum, the rest of the three days' death. 1051AThen in other words he repeats the same. And to my eyelids slumber. And rest to my temples until the holy Church be founded by preaching. It is an aposiopesis, as it were, let me be believed no more.

And to my eyelids. (AUG.) There is he who sleeps not, but slumbers: now he is drawn back from earthly things, now he is rolled back into them, often he nods his head.

VERS. 5.-- And rest. From the rest of the temples sleep comes to the eyes, because for them that are about to sleep the temples begin. When therefore something temporal begins to give delight unto sin, the temples are weighed down; but give not thyself to that delight, and sleep comes not to the eyes, by this thought, if, as though rubbing thy forehead, thou shakest off sleep.

I shall find: (ID.) he says it, because he sought long.

1051BA place for the Lord: he sought it in himself, who rests upon the humble and the quiet. And a man is a place of God if he forsakes his own things; or at the least, if he loves not himself, but God.

A tabernacle. (ID.) As yet we groan. In the house we shall praise, because groaning belongs to them that are on pilgrimage; praise to them that already abide in the fatherland. To the God of Jacob. He says that he has paid, as above he said that he had promised.

VERS. 6.-- Behold we have heard. (CAS.) The second part, where the house is shown built, and where he also prays for those who are to be exalted, and that the Jews be not utterly strangers. It in Ephrata, (AUG.) or it, etc., as far as where were the brambles of idolatry.

(CASS.) Behold, hear, namely that the Lord was to be born in Ephrata Bethlehem, where the Lord was born: it was heard 1051Cthat he should be born in Bethlehem, but for the faith of the Gentiles he was found in the fields of the wood.

VERS. 7.-- We will go in. (AUG.) We too, by persevering in our warfare, have nevertheless gone in (or shall go in) into his tabernacle, the tabernacle of the God of Jacob: to this house belongs he who is framed together with others in charity as with living stones. He therefore enters who loves, and he who enters is made the house of God. In the place. The house of God is where he ought to be adored: apart from which God hears not unto life eternal. He belongs to the house who is framed together with others in charity. Or the place in which the feet of the house of the Lord stand is Christ, in whom they persevere.

VERS. 8.-- Arise. (ID.) And it is said to him who says, I have slept troubled: Arise from death, into thy rest, 1051Dthat thou be troubled no more, because death shall no more have dominion.

VERS. 9.-- Priests. (ID.) He takes the same men for priests and for saints, namely all the faithful. Or, by priests he signifies the prelates of the Church; by saints, the faithful that are subject. The ark therefore, which he had prayed might arise, he distinguishes by the parts of the Church.

Priests, as in the Old Testament the priests are adorned with divers ornaments, so the priests of the Gospel with divers virtues: these are the ornaments which God requires. For what the pontiffs of the law bore upon their garments, the priests of the Gospel ought to have in their hearts.

VERS. 10.-- For David the servant's sake. (CASS.) Remember: 1052AAnd well do I say for David's sake, because the Lord hath sworn to David.

For the sake of: then in the person of David himself entreating God the Father.

(AUG.) For because Christ turned away his face from the Jews unto the Gentiles, the Father is entreated for the remnant, that they may be saved, which was fulfilled in the apostles and in many others. And he says: for David's sake, as if he said: Remember me also, that for my sake thou cast not off the Jews utterly.

VERS. 11.-- He hath sworn. (CASS.) The third part, where he tells the promises of God made to Sion when built, that is, to the Church. And David speaks in his own person or in the person of the whole Christ. And he will not make it void (otherwise) he will not repent. (AUG.) God is said to repent, etc., as far as 1052Bfor thou doest it because thou hadst erred: he does it, and delivers. Of the fruit of thy womb. He could have said, of the fruit of thy loins, etc., as far as because those whom David ruled temporally, Christ rules spiritually.

VERS. 12.-- If they shall keep. (ID.) They seem to earn merit, etc., as far as this is not changed. And their children. (CASS.) If they shall keep the testament. They shall sit upon thy seat, that is, they shall be partakers of thy blessedness: that as thou art of kingly power, so they also, according to their measure, and this, Unto the age of the age, that is, unto eternity.

VERS. 14.-- This is my rest. (ID.) So does God love us, that he says that he himself rests, if we rest in him.

VERS. 15.-- The widow. (ID.) The soul is a widow 1052Cwhich understands itself forsaken of all help save of God alone. With bread. God is the bread, who in the flesh made himself milk.

VERS. 16.-- Her priests. Or a distinction is to be made between priests and saints, as above. And it is, Her priests, that is, the prelates, I will clothe with salvation, that is, with Christ, that is, that they may be honourable for teaching. And the saints, that is, those subject. They shall rejoice with exceeding great joy over Christ.

They shall rejoice with exceeding great joy. (ID.) Because they are clothed with salvation, etc., as far as who dwells in him; therefore he has exalted exaltaxit securely.

VERS. 17.-- The horn of David, I have prepared a lamp for Christ. (ID.) The spiritual height of the Church, etc., as far as before the death and resurrection of Christ.

1052DVERS. 18.-- I will clothe with confusion, etc. (CASS.) This the Son will do, to whom all judgment is given. But note that the Father, who here speaks, does what the Son does.

PSALMUS CXXXII.

VERS. 1.-- Canticum graduum. (ID.) Quartus decimus gradus: Charitas quae facit fratres habitare in unum, unde benedictio et vita. Ecce quam bonum. Et est hic psalmus atomus, etc., usque ad hic ergo vir justus de cohabitatione fratrum exsultans ait: Ecce quam. Ecce quam. (AUG.) Iste versus toto orbe notissimus, ut tuba Spiritus Sancti divisos congregavit: monasteria plurima peperit. (CASS.) Ecce. Quasi plus ostensione, quam lingua explicetur. Habitare in 1053Aunum. (AUG.) Hoc de omnibus Christianis, sed proprie convenit monasteriis, a quibus tamen ad caeteros benedictio descendit, ut etiam illis fratribus de Judaea, de quibus dicitur. Erat illis cor unum, et anima una.

VERS. 2.-- Sicut unguentum. (THEOD.) Oleum sacerdotale, etc., usque ad perfectae virtutis odorem perficit. Barbam. (AUG.) Ecce determinatio, id est in apostolos et alios primitivos sanctos, qui primo fide certaverunt, sed vinci non potuerunt, quia jam caput passum praecesserunt. Aaron. Sacerdos, qui se ipsum obtulit, etc., usque ad sed vinci non potuerunt. Ab illis. In oram. (CASS.) Vel per oram, quae est finis vestis, etc., usque ad subditos usque concordiae utilitas pervenit.

VERS. 3.-- Sicut ros. (ID.) Ros tenuis aqua, unde terra germinat, et significat gratiam, qua peccatores convertuntur. Hermon. (AUG.) ad litteram mons trans Jordanem, etc., usque ad caeteri assumuntur, qui in unum corde sunt.

PSALM CXXXII.

VERS. 1.-- A canticle of degrees. (ID.) The fourteenth degree: charity, which makes brethren to dwell in one, whence blessing and life. Behold how good. And this psalm is an atom, etc., as far as here therefore the just man, rejoicing over the dwelling together of brethren, says: Behold how. Behold how. (AUG.) That verse, most famous in the whole world, has as the trumpet of the Holy Ghost gathered together them that were divided: it has brought forth very many monasteries. (CASS.) Behold. As though more were set forth by the showing than could be unfolded by the tongue. To dwell in 1053Aone. (AUG.) This concerning all Christians, but it properly befits monasteries, from which nevertheless the blessing comes down to the rest, as also to those brethren of Judaea, of whom it is said: They had one heart, and one soul.

VERS. 2.-- As the ointment. (THEOD.) The priestly oil, etc., as far as it perfects the odour of perfect virtue. The beard. (AUG.) Behold the determination, that is, upon the apostles and the other primitive saints, who first strove in faith, but could not be overcome, because they had already gone before the head that had suffered [praecesserunt; read praecesserat, "the head had gone before"]. Aaron. The priest who offered up himself, etc., as far as but they could not be overcome. From them. To the skirt. (CASS.) Or by the skirt, which is the edge of the garment, etc., as far as the profit of concord reaches even to them that are subject.

VERS. 3.-- As the dew. (ID.) Dew is thin water, whence the earth brings forth, and it signifies grace, whereby sinners are converted. Hermon. (AUG.) According to the letter a mountain beyond Jordan, etc., as far as the rest are taken up, who are in one in heart.

PSALMUS CXXXIII.

VERS. 1.-- Canticum graduum. (CASS.) Quintus decimus gradus: Charitas saeculi. Et est hic tertius psalmus de charitate Dei, de qua hic agit, sicut supra de charitate proximi. Non alia gratia sit qua diligitur Deus, et alia qua proximus. Sed quia diversos actus habet gratia, et diversa diliguntur ea. Monet ergo ad diligendum Deum. Primo, invitat pluraliter benedicere Deum; secundo, optat benedici, ibi, Benedicat.

Ecce, demonstrantis est. Et quibus faciat hanc demonstrationem, determinat, vos servi Domini.

Statis. Servorum est, non sedere in domo domini. Vel, de eisdem intelligitur: Et per domum, intelligitur Ecclesia, per atria, latitudo charitatis. In charitate enim, quae extenditur usque ad inimicos, latitudo est, in odio angustia. Quasi diceret, vos benedicite, qui statis, id est perseveratis, In domo Domini, id est in Ecclesiis; et qui statis, In atriis domus Dei nostri, id est iu latitudine charitatis, ubi nullus angustiatur.

VERS. 2.-- Extollite manus vestras. Sicut Moyses manus suas levavit pugnante populo Israel contra Amalec, Extollite dico, in sancta: ut intentione aeternum bonum operemini, aliter enim non valet.

1053DBenedicat te Dominus. Secunda pars, ubi optat benedici fideles. Quasi diceret, benedicite, et ut hoc possitis, Benedicat te Dominus, benedictione quae est ex Sion. Qui potest, quia ipse est, qui fecit coelum et terram. (CASS.) Benedicat. Supra hortatur plures benedicere Deum, ipse vero unum benedicit tantum, quia, etsi plures sint, tamen in unum sunt, et unitati convenit benedictio. Unde unus in piscina sanabatur, qui prior descendebat. Esto ergo in uno, et ad te perveniet benedictio.

PSALM CXXXIII.

VERS. 1.-- A canticle of degrees. (CASS.) The fifteenth degree: the charity of the world. And this is the third psalm concerning the charity of God, of which he here treats, as above of the charity of the neighbour. There is not one grace whereby God is loved, and another whereby the neighbour. But because grace has divers acts, and by it divers things are loved. He admonishes therefore unto the loving of God. First, he invites in the plural to bless God; secondly, he wishes them to be blessed, there, May he bless.

Behold, is the word of one pointing out. And to whom he makes this pointing out he determines: you, ye servants of the Lord.

Ye stand. It belongs to servants not to sit in the house of their lord. Or, it is understood of the same men: and by the house the Church is understood, by the courts, the breadth of charity. For in charity, which extends even to enemies, there is breadth; in hatred, narrowness. As though he said: do ye bless, who stand, that is, who persevere, In the house of the Lord, that is, in the churches; and who stand, In the courts of the house of our God, that is, in iu the breadth of charity, where no man is straitened.

VERS. 2.-- Lift up your hands. As Moses lifted up his hands while the people of Israel fought against Amalec, Lift up, I say, unto the holy places: that with such intention ye may work the eternal good, for otherwise it avails not.

1053DMay the Lord bless thee. The second part, where he wishes the faithful to be blessed. As though he said, bless ye, and that ye may be able to do this, May the Lord bless thee, with the blessing which is out of Sion. Who is able, because he it is who made heaven and earth. (CASS.) May he bless. Above he exhorts many to bless God, but he himself blesses one only, because, though they be many, yet they are in one, and to unity blessing belongs. Whence one was healed in the pool, he who went down first. Be thou therefore in one, and the blessing shall come unto thee.

PSALMUS CXXXIV.

VERS. 1.-- Alleluia. (CASS.) Post gradus, qui ducunt ad aeternitatem componitur alleluia, ut Ecclesia fruatur laudibus Dei cui tale munus paratum est. 1054ALaudate. Primo demonstrativa oratione monet, etc., usque ad qui et quare laudare debeant subdit: Laudate, servi.

VERS. 3.-- Laudate Dominum, etc. (AUG.) Si omnia laudantur, quia bona, etc., usque ad in quibus totum semen Israel intelligitur, tota Ecclesia cogitatur.

Psallite nomini ejus, id est, laudate eum, eo quod id fecit, quod res sui nominis exigit, cum se incarnatum dedit hominibus gustari.

VERS. 4.-- Jacob. (ID.) Luctator interpretatur, et significat illos qui contra spirituales nequitias luctantur. Israel in possessionem. Ad litteram. Caeteras gentes sub angelis custodiendas Dominus posuit: Jacob sibi elegit, quem ut agrum coleret, seminaret, possideret, servaret.

1054BVERS. 6.-- Omnia quaecunque. (ID.) Quasi diceret: Magnus est in essentia, magnus in operibus, etc., usque ad sed spiritus hominis ignoratur, unde ecce dicitur.

VERS. 7.-- Qui producit ventos de thesauris suis. Qui percussit primogenita. (ID.) Fides unde incipimus, qua viva proficit homo in melius, Aegyptus afflictio: quicunque ergo affligit Ecclesiam, et scandala facit, etsi Christianus dicitur, perdit fidem.

Ab extremo. Sive ab imo terrae, sive a circumdatione finium terrae. Fulgura et pluviam. Fulgur terrorem, pluvia gaudium facit. Qui ergo terruit fulgure, reficit pluvia.

VERS. 8.-- Qui percussit. (ID.) Hoc in hominibus fecit propter poculum suum. Si dixit quae amares, 1054Caudi et quae timeas. Ab homine usque ad pecus. (CASS.) Hoc saepe repetit, etc., usque ad quae destruit in prudentibus et idiotis.

VERS. 10.-- Reges fortes. (ID.) Mundi spiritus: qui sunt occisi, dum nequeunt in nobis quod volunt.

VERS. 11.-- Sehon regem Amorrhaeorum, etc. Hoc sub Moyse factum: de hoc in libro Numeri legitur, quod cum prohiberent filios Israel per fines suos transire, percussi sunt ab eo, et possedit populus Israel terram eorum.

Chanaan. (ID.) Humiliatio, mala, scilicet, quando ab honore sancti decidunt.

VERS. 12.-- Et dedit terram eorum haereditatem. (ID.) Id est, coelestem beatitudinem, quam 1054Ddaemones per superbiam deseruerunt, dedit fidelibus. Haec est vera terra promissionis, quae verius dicitur haereditas, quae in pace est, quam illa actualis, quam saepe amiserunt filii Israel. Haereditatem Israel. (AUG.) Haereditas, sunt gentes Israel, fidelis scilicet populi, quem pascunt tribulatione, docentes patientiam, vel quas Israel excolit conformando sibi.

VERS. 13.-- In generationem et generationem. (ID.) Generatio una est, qua renascimur per baptismum, altera qua resurgemus: non est oblitus Deus in hac vocare, in illa coronare.

VERS. 14.-- Quia judicabit. (CASS.) Causa laudis, quia vidit Dominus populum cui tot fecit, prophetas 1055Amisit, post et Filium. Sed quia duri fuerunt, judicabit eos in futuro, et in servis, id est, fidelibus, consolabitur, cum praemia aeterna restituet. Ecce gradatio laudis ad judicium perducta est. (AUG.) Vel, ita. Ideo de praesenti, etc., usque ad videant, et qui vident, caeci fiant.

VERS. 15.-- Simulacra. (CASS.) Secunda pars: postquam laudibus se Dei explevit, idolorum cultores irridendo redarguit, quia perfecta laus veritatis est destruere falsitatem, supra fuerunt eadem dicta, sed repetita verecundiam augent.

VERS. 16.-- Os habent et non loquentur. (AUG.) Illa exteriora artifex potuit facere; sed non spiritum dare, nec auditum auribus, nec lucem oculis, nec vocem ori.

1055BVERS. -- Similes illis fiant. (ID.) Haec scientes irrident idola, etc., usque ad nec sentiunt bonum odorem Christi.

VERS. 19.-- Domus Israel benedicite. (CASS.) Haec est tertia pars, ubi post irrisa idola, laudes Dei celebrare monet omnes ordines: quasi : Cultores idolorum similes illis fiant. Sed vos, qui estis domus Israel. Domus Aaron benedicite. (AUG.) Praepositi sunt domus Aaron: ministri, domus Levi, populi omnes qui timent; omnes generaliter sunt domus Israel, omnes una voce dicamus: Benedictus.

VERS. 21.-- Benedictus Dominus. (ID.) Vel juxta interpretationem nominum, etc., usque ad ubi videbimus eum in aeterna pace.

PSALM CXXXIV.

VERS. 1.-- Alleluia. (CASS.) After the degrees, which lead unto eternity, the alleluia is set, that the Church may enjoy the praises of God, for whom such a gift is prepared. 1054APraise ye. First, by a demonstrative address he admonishes, etc., as far as he subjoins who ought to praise and why: Praise ye, servants.

VERS. 3.-- Praise ye the Lord, etc. (AUG.) If all things are praised because they are good, etc., as far as in whom the whole seed of Israel is understood, the whole Church is thought of.

Sing ye to his name, that is, praise him for this, that he did what the reality of his name requires, when, being incarnate, he gave himself to men to be tasted.

VERS. 4.-- Jacob. (ID.) He is interpreted "wrestler," and signifies those who wrestle against spiritual wickednesses. Israel for a possession. According to the letter. The other nations the Lord set under angels to be guarded: Jacob he chose for himself, that he might till him as a field, sow him, possess him, keep him.

1054BVERS. 6.-- All things whatsoever. (ID.) As though he said: He is great in essence, great in works, etc., as far as but the spirit of man is unknown, whence, behold, it is said.

VERS. 7.-- Who bringeth forth winds out of his treasures. Who slew the firstborn. (ID.) Faith, whence we begin, by which, when it is living, a man advances unto better things; Egypt, affliction: whosoever therefore afflicts the Church and makes scandals, though he be called a Christian, loses faith.

From the end. Either from the lowest part of the earth, or from the compass of the ends of the earth. Lightnings and rain. [Vulg. Ps 134:7 fulgura in pluviam fecit, "he hath made lightnings for the rain"] The lightning works terror, the rain gladness. He therefore who terrified with the lightning refreshes with the rain.

VERS. 8.-- Who slew. (ID.) This he did among men for his own cup's sake. If he has told what things thou shouldst love, 1054Chear also what things thou shouldst fear. From man even to beast. (CASS.) This he often repeats, etc., as far as which he destroys in the prudent and in the simple.

VERS. 10.-- Mighty kings. (ID.) The spirits of the world: who are slain, while they cannot do in us what they will.

VERS. 11.-- Sehon king of the Amorrhites, etc. This was done under Moses: of this it is read in the book of Numbers, that when they forbade the children of Israel to pass through their borders, they were smitten by him, and the people of Israel possessed their land.

Chanaan. (ID.) Humiliation, an evil one, namely, when the holy fall away from honour.

VERS. 12.-- And he gave their land for an inheritance. (ID.) That is, the heavenly blessedness, which 1054Dthe demons forsook through pride, he gave to the faithful. This is the true land of promise, which is more truly called an inheritance, which is in peace, than that actual land, which the children of Israel often lost. The inheritance of Israel. (AUG.) The inheritance: they are the nations of Israel, that is, of the faithful people, whom they feed with tribulation, teaching patience; or which Israel cultivates by conforming them to himself.

VERS. 13.-- Unto generation and generation. (ID.) One generation there is, whereby we are born again through baptism, another whereby we shall rise again: God has not forgotten to call in the one, to crown in the other.

VERS. 14.-- For he will judge. (CASS.) The cause of praise, because the Lord saw the people for whom he did so much, to whom he sent prophets, 1055Aand afterward the Son also. But because they were hard, he will judge them in the time to come, and in the servants, that is, in the faithful, he will comfort, [Vulg. Ps 134:14 et in servis suis deprecabitur, "and he will be entreated in favour of his servants"] when he shall render the eternal rewards. Behold, the gradation of praise is brought through unto judgment. (AUG.) Or, thus. Therefore concerning the present, etc., as far as they may see, and they who see may become blind.

VERS. 15.-- The idols. (CASS.) The second part: after he had filled himself with the praises of God, he refutes the worshippers of idols by mocking them, because the perfect praise of truth is to destroy falsehood; above the same things were said, but repeated they increase shame.

VERS. 16.-- They have a mouth, and they shall not speak. (AUG.) Those outward things the craftsman could make; but he could not give a spirit, nor hearing to the ears, nor light to the eyes, nor voice to the mouth.

1055BVERS. 18.-- Let them become like unto them. (ID.) Knowing these things they mock the idols, etc., as far as neither do they perceive the good odour of Christ.

VERS. 19.-- House of Israel, bless ye. (CASS.) This is the third part, where, after the idols have been mocked, he admonishes all orders to celebrate the praises of God: as it were: Let the worshippers of idols become like unto them. But you, who are the house of Israel. House of Aaron, bless ye. (AUG.) The prelates are the house of Aaron: the ministers, the house of Levi; the peoples, all that fear; all generally are the house of Israel: let us all with one voice say: Blessed.

VERS. 21.-- Blessed be the Lord. (ID.) Or according to the interpretation of the names, etc., as far as where we shall see him in eternal peace.

PSALMUS CXXXV.

VERS. 1.-- Alleluia. (AUG.) Psalmus iste laudem Dei continet, ubi etsi multa in laude Dei dicantur, maxime tamen hic misericordia Dei commendatur. (CASS.) Diversa initia versuum, etc., usque ad ita praesto est divina praesentia si pure cantatur. Confitemini Domino. (ID.) Primo, magnificentiam Dei et totius orbi conditionem exponit. Secundo dicit quae in Aegypto et gente Judaeorum fecit in figuram nostri, ibi, Qui percussit. Tertio, agit de Christianis, ibi, et dedit terram eorum haereditatem. Confitemini Domino. (AUG.) Modo laudemus, etc., usque ad per misericordiam beatitudo aeterna est.

VERS. 2.-- Confitemini Deo deorum. Deos dicit homines, ad quos sermo Dei factus est in alio psalmo, ubi ait, Ego dixi, Dii estis et filii Excelsi, 1055Detc. Et non ideo dicuntur dii, quod omnes sint boni: si enim omnes boni essent, non diceret in eodem psalmo: in medio autem deos dijudicat, id est discernit, de quibus etiam subdit: Confitemini Domino dominorum.

VERS. 3.-- Qui facit mirabilia. (ID.) Sicut in fine ubique ponitur, etc., usque ad ideo confitemini, quoniam in aeternum misericordia ejus.

VERS. 4.-- Mirabilia magna solus. (ID.) Quia et quaedam per homines vel angelos facit, et quaedam magna ipse solus, quae et prius exsequitur.

VERS. 5.-- Qui fecit coelos. (ID.) Universam ergo creaturam per se fecit, etc., usque ad unde, Omnia in sapientia fecisti, Deus.

1056AVel typice, Coelos in intellectu, id est spirituales sanctos, cui non modo credere, sed intelligere divina dedit. Simplices autem qui solam fidem firmam tenent, quasi infra coelos, terra dicuntur, qui quia in baptismo, quem acceperunt, quasi super aquas firma fide consistunt, quasi super aquas terram firmavit.

VERS. 6.-- Terram super aquas. (ID.) Sed quo terra gravior ab aquis levioribus portatur, etc., usque ad sic Dominus super puteum sedit, id est juxta.

VERS. 7.-- Qui fecit luminaria magna. (ID.) id est dona gratiarum fidelibus suis contulit.

VERS. 9.-- Lunam et stellas in potestatem noctis. (CASS.) Aliter etiam dici potest mystice, etc., usque 1056Bad ut per haec quaeque minores luceant.

VERS. 10.-- Qui percussit Aegyptum. (ID.) Secunda pars, ubi dicit, quae in Aegypto facit et gente Judaeorum sub figura nostri. Jam incipit, quae per homines, vel per angelos fecit. Cum primogenitis eorum. Primogenita Aegypti percussit, etc., usque ad sed Deus a se excludit.

VERS. 12.-- In manu potenti. (ID.) Manus Dei invincibilis actio, quae a brachio venit, id est ab omni potentia singulari.

VERS. 13.-- Divisit mare Rubrum in divisiones. (ID.) Ad litteram in divisiones duodecim pro numero tribuum, ut singulae tribus suas vias eundi haberent; typice, sic per vias varias ad Deum de mundo transitur. Per mare Rubrum saeculum accipitur.

1056CVERS. 15.-- Et excussit Pharaonem. (ID.) Diabolum, cum ministris excussit, ut pulverem, qui celeriter excutitur. In hac celeritate, et virtus Dei ostenditur, et illae terrenae sordes indicantur, quas solemus excutere. Pharaonem. (ID.) Congrue per Pharaonem diabolus intelligitur: Pharao masculos necat, feminas servat; ita diabolus virtutes praefocat, concupiscentiam nutrit.

VERS. 21.-- Et dedit terram eorum haereditatem. (CASS.) Tertia pars, ubi descendit ad Christianos, exponens beneficia eis data, ut sic unum auctorem omnium scias.

VERS. 22.-- Israel servo suo. Accipit per Israel servum, Christum, etc., usque ad nullum dedit pretium 1056DAegyptiis.

VERS. 25.-- Dat escam. (THEOD.) A singulari Providentia, etc., usque ad in Evangeliis inquit: Respicite volatilia coeli, quae neque serunt, neque congregant in horrea, et Pater vester coelestis pascit illa. Omni carni. (AUG.) Omni generi hominum, Israel et gentium, non sicut manna soli Judaeo.

PSALM CXXXV.

VERS. 1.-- Alleluia. (AUG.) This psalm contains the praise of God, where, although many things are said in the praise of God, yet chiefly here the mercy of God is commended. (CASS.) The divers beginnings of the verses, etc., as far as so is the divine presence at hand if it be sung purely. Give praise to the Lord. (ID.) First, he sets forth the magnificence of God and the founding of the whole world [orbi; read orbis, "of the whole world"]. Secondly he tells what things he did in Egypt and in the nation of the Jews as a figure of us, there, Who smote. Thirdly, he treats of Christians, there, and he gave their land for an inheritance. Give praise to the Lord. (AUG.) Let us now praise, etc., as far as through mercy is eternal blessedness.

VERS. 2.-- Give praise to the God of gods. He calls men gods, to whom the word of God came in another psalm, where he says, I have said, You are gods and sons of the Most High, 1055Detc. And they are not therefore called gods because all are good: for if all were good, he would not say in the same psalm: but in the midst he judgeth gods, that is, he distinguishes them; of whom also he subjoins: Give praise to the Lord of lords.

VERS. 3.-- Who doth wonders. (ID.) As it is everywhere set at the end, etc., as far as therefore give praise, for his mercy endureth for ever.

VERS. 4.-- Great wonders alone. (ID.) Because he does certain things through men or angels, and certain great things he himself alone, which also he sets forth first.

VERS. 5.-- Who made the heavens. (ID.) The whole creation therefore he made by himself, etc., as far as whence, Thou hast made all things in wisdom, O God.

1056AOr typically, The heavens in understanding, that is, the spiritual saints, to whom he granted not only to believe, but to understand divine things. But the simple, who hold fast only a firm faith, as though beneath the heavens, are called earth; who, because in the baptism which they received they stand fast as it were upon the waters by a firm faith, as it were upon the waters he established the earth.

VERS. 6.-- The earth above the waters. (ID.) But whereby the heavier earth is borne by the lighter waters, etc., as far as so the Lord sat above the well, that is, beside it.

VERS. 7.-- Who made the great lights. (ID.) that is, he conferred the gifts of graces upon his faithful.

VERS. 9.-- The moon and the stars for the power of the night. (CASS.) It can also be said otherwise, mystically, etc., as far 1056Bas that through these each of the lesser may give light.

VERS. 10.-- Who smote Egypt. (ID.) The second part, where he tells what things he does in Egypt and in the nation of the Jews under a figure of us. Now he begins upon the things which he did through men or through angels. With their firstborn. He smote the firstborn of Egypt, etc., as far as but God shuts them out from himself.

VERS. 12.-- With a mighty hand. (ID.) The hand of God is his invincible action, which comes from the arm, that is, from his whole singular power.

VERS. 13.-- He divided the Red Sea into parts. (ID.) According to the letter into parts twelve, for the number of the tribes, that each tribe might have its own ways to go by; typically, thus by divers ways there is a passing out of the world unto God. By the Red Sea the world is understood.

1056CVERS. 15.-- And he shook off Pharao. (ID.) He shook off the devil, with his ministers, as dust, which is quickly shaken off. In this quickness both the power of God is shown, and those earthly defilements are pointed out which we are wont to shake off. Pharao. (ID.) Fitly by Pharao the devil is understood: Pharao kills the males, keeps the females alive; so the devil stifles the virtues, nourishes concupiscence.

VERS. 21.-- And he gave their land for an inheritance. (CASS.) The third part, where he comes down to Christians, setting forth the benefits given to them, that thus thou mayest know one author of all things.

VERS. 22.-- To Israel his servant. He takes by Israel the servant Christ, etc., as far as he gave no price 1056Dto the Egyptians.

VERS. 25.-- He giveth food. (THEOD.) From his singular Providence, etc., as far as in the Gospels he says: Behold the birds of the air, which neither sow, nor gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feedeth them. To all flesh. [Vulg. Mt 6:26 Respicite volatilia caeli, quoniam non serunt, neque metunt, neque congregant in horrea, "behold the birds of the air, for they neither sow, nor do they reap, nor gather into barns"] (AUG.) To every kind of men, of Israel and of the Gentiles, not as the manna to the Jew alone.

PSALMUS CXXXVI.

Psalmus David. (CASS.) Tertius psalmus de lamentatione Jerusalem, etc, usque ad hic autem de captivitate facta a Nabuchodonosor. (AUG.) Duae civitates sunt permistae corpore, etc., usque ad qui mente desiderio sunt cives Jerusalem.

VERS. 1.-- Super flumina. (CASS.) Primo, captivandos 1057Alonge post, etc., usque ad incipit desiderio patriae, dicens: Super flumina, etc. Dum recordaremur, (AUG.) In hostili terra dulcis recordatio patriae, etc., usque ad utrumque de Babylonia est.

VERS. 2.-- In salicibus. (ID.) Quae rigantur fluminibus Babylonis, etc., usque ad sed differendo suspendimus. (CASS.) Vis doloris exaggeratur, quando delectatio, qua se solebant consolari, suspenditur.

Quia illic interrogaverunt nos. (BASIL.) Et hinc haud parum emolumenti coeperunt, etc., usque ad ut et cantica nostra audire voluerint.

VERS. 3.-- Verba cantionum. (AUG.) Vel, canticorum, ut quid prodest Christus? vel, quae est alia vita? Sed, hic qui pleni sunt malis, non debemus 1057Bpercutere organum, ut sonet, sed suspendere. (ID.) Diabolus astute quaerit ut irrideat, etc., usque ad et constrinxit se juramento, dicens: Si oblitus fuero, etc.

VERS. 4.-- Quomodo cantabimus. (ID.) Cavendum est, ne quis timens talibus displicere, affectet amicitias eorum, et incipiat delectari in Babylonia.

VERS. 5.-- Dextera mea. (ID.) Quidquid facis pro aeternis, dextera operatur; si et alio intenderis, sinistra se immiscuit; et in ea delectatus quasi in dextera perdis aeterna.

VERS. 6.-- Adhaereat. (CASS.) Mutus fiam in laudibus Dei, quod est consolatio fletus et miseriarum. Lingua mea. (AUG.) Canticum Jerusalem, lingua nostra, canticum saeculi, lingua barbara. Mutus est 1057CDeo, qui oblitus est Jerusalem.

VERS. 7.-- Memor esto. (CASS.) Secunda pars, ubi contra hostes ad Deum fit conversio. Memor esto, in die sequestrationis, ut puniantur. Filiorum Edom. (AUG.) Filii Edom, id est Idumaei, impedimento fuerunt reaedificantibus Jerusalem; vel, in destructione conjuncti Babylonis, unde dicit, Filia Babylonis misera. Edom moraliter est carnalitas, quae ad illicitos motus nos seducit. Edom. (ID.) Esau omnes carnales; Jacob spirituales; major carnalis homo, minor spiritualis, quia prius quidem animale, postea quod spirituale. Omnes carnales inimici sunt spiritualibus, unde ait: Memor esto, libera nos ab illis. Exinanite. (CASS.) A similitudine 1057Dcisternae, unde si aqua hauritur, ad fundamentum pervenitur. Sed quid prodest et vitam talibus tollere, quibus in fundamento (qui est Christus) vita aeterna est? dum putant nocere mali, coronas dant.

VERS. 8.-- Filia. (AUG.) Per successionem facta est filia Babylonis civitas malorum, sicut Ecclesia; Jerusalem scilicet, civitas bonorum per successionem filia Sion. (CASS.) Filia Babylonis moraliter. Caro est, quae confusionem, etc., usque ad allidunt ad petram Christum, ut confracti dispereant.

VERS. 9.-- Beatus qui tenebit. (AUG.) Quam retributionem? ut Babylonia natos in mundo, dum parvi sunt, parentum et saeculi suffocat erroribus: ita qui jam juvenes, data agnitione Dei, parvulos Babylonis 1058Aelidunt, id est nascentes cupiditates, antequam robur accipiant, sic facilius vincuntur, sed et majores ad petram occidendae sunt.

PSALM CXXXVI.

A psalm of David. (CASS.) The third psalm concerning the lamentation of Jerusalem, etc, as far as but this one concerning the captivity brought about by Nabuchodonosor. (AUG.) Two cities there are, mingled together in body, etc., as far as who in mind, in desire are citizens of Jerusalem.

VERS. 1.-- Upon the rivers. (CASS.) First, that they should be led captive 1057Along afterward, etc., as far as he begins with the desire of the fatherland, saying: Upon the rivers, etc. While we remembered, (AUG.) In a hostile land sweet is the remembrance of the fatherland, etc., as far as both are of Babylon.

VERS. 2.-- On the willows. (ID.) Which are watered by the rivers of Babylon, etc., as far as but by deferring we hang them up. (CASS.) The force of grief is heightened when the delight wherewith they were wont to console themselves is hung up.

For there they asked us. (BASIL.) And hence they began no small profit [coeperunt; read ceperunt, "they took"], etc., as far as so that they were even willing to hear our songs.

VERS. 3.-- The words of the songs. (AUG.) Or, of the canticles, as, what does Christ profit? or, what is that other life? But here, among those who are full of evils, we ought not 1057Bto strike the instrument, that it should sound, but to hang it up. (ID.) The devil craftily seeks occasion to mock, etc., as far as and he bound himself with an oath, saying: If I forget thee, etc.

VERS. 4.-- How shall we sing. (ID.) Care must be taken lest any man, fearing to displease such men, court their friendships, and begin to take delight in Babylon.

VERS. 5.-- My right hand. (ID.) Whatever thou doest for eternal things, the right hand works; if thou aim also at another thing, the left hand has mingled itself in; and delighting in it as in the right hand thou losest eternal things.

VERS. 6.-- Let it cleave. (CASS.) Let me become dumb in the praises of God, which is the consolation of weeping and of miseries. My tongue. (AUG.) The canticle of Jerusalem is our tongue, the canticle of the world a barbarous tongue. He is dumb 1057Cto God who has forgotten Jerusalem.

VERS. 7.-- Remember. (CASS.) The second part, where the turning to God is made against the enemies. Remember, in the day of the separation, that they may be punished. Of the children of Edom. (AUG.) The children of Edom, that is, the Idumeans, were a hindrance to them that rebuilt Jerusalem; or, in the destruction they were joined with Babylon, whence he says, The daughter of Babylon, miserable. Edom morally is carnality, which seduces us unto unlawful motions. Edom. (ID.) Esau, all the carnal; Jacob, the spiritual; the elder, the carnal man, the younger, the spiritual, because first indeed that which is animal, afterward that which is spiritual. All the carnal are enemies to the spiritual, whence he says: Remember, deliver us from them. Empty it out. (CASS.) From the likeness 1057Dof a cistern, out of which, if the water be drawn, the bottom is reached. But what does it profit even to take away the life of such men, for whom, in the foundation (which is Christ), there is life eternal? while the wicked think to hurt, they give crowns.

VERS. 8.-- The daughter. (AUG.) By succession the city of the wicked is made the daughter of Babylon, as the Church, that is, Jerusalem, the city of the good, is by succession the daughter of Sion. (CASS.) The daughter of Babylon morally. It is the flesh, which confusion, etc., as far as they dash them against the rock, Christ, that being broken they may perish.

VERS. 9.-- Blessed is he that shall take. (AUG.) What retribution? that as Babylon smothers those born in the world, while they are little, with the errors of their parents and of the world: so they who are now grown up, the knowledge of God being given them, dash the little ones of Babylon 1058Ato pieces, that is, the desires as they are being born, before they receive strength; thus they are more easily overcome, but the greater ones also must be slain against the rock.

PSALMUS CXXXVII.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus ipsi David. (CASS.) Captivus, qui fleverat, quasi reaedificata Jerusalem et templo, et quasi concivis illi parti Jerusalem, quae non fuit captiva, id est, angelis, exsultat et laudat primo beneficia sibi data. Ex persona igitur Ecclesiae, quae in superioribus est spe, exspectans ibi esse in re, ait, confitebor.

Confitebor tibi, Domine. Primo, commendat beneficia sibi data: secundo, dicit quomodo haec ad omnes dilatentur, ibi, Confiteantur tibi, Domine, etc. In conspectu. 1058B(AUG.) In laudando propono mihi angelos, quibus aequari sicut nunc, ita post, dignitate expecto. Hi autem in laude Dei nihil aliud proponunt, quam ipsum. In conspectu ergo angelorum, in ea puritate, qua te conspiciunt angeli, ut in te solo sibi acquiescant, ego Psallam tibi.

VERS. 2.-- Super misericordia. (ID.) Universae viae Domini misericordia et veritas: Non sunt aliae viae, quibus ad nos venit, Non sunt aliae, quibus ad eum veniamus: has Deo reddamus, misericordiam in subveniendo, veritatem in judicando. Super omne nomen sanctum tuum. (CASS.) Vel super nomen sanctum tuum, cum nobis cultura tua innotuit.

VERS. 3.-- In anima. Et quia in anima potest fieri carnalis multiplicatio, addit, virtutem quasi non 1058Caliud in anima peto, nisi virtutem.

VERS. 4.-- Confiteantur. (ID.) Secunda pars, ubi dici quomodo haec bona ad omnes sint dilatanda. Quasi meo exemplo: Confiteantur, etc. Omnia verba oris tui. (AUG.) Quae modo ubique revelata sunt, et ad omnes gentes missa, etc., usque ad et ita vellere siccato, audierunt omnia verba, etc.

VERS. 5.-- Magna est gloria. (ID.) Si humiles sunt, hoc amant et cantant, nam si se extulerint, timeant quod sequitur. Quoniam excelsus Dominus. Humilia respicit. (CASS.) Non est hic humana conditio, ubi humilis despicitur, superbus respicitur; sed Dominus humiles respicit.

Alta a longe cognoscit. (AUG.) Non hoc agit superbus, etc., usque ad lugentes hunc incolatum, unde 1058Dsubditur.

VERS. 7.-- Si ambulavero in medio tribulationis. Aliter non vivificat, nisi in medio tribulationis, unde, Beati qui lugent, vae ridentibus.

Super iram. (ID.) Hoc ipsum, quod irascuntur mihi, tua est in illos animadversio, id est punitio. Est enim eis irasci poena, noc tantum culpa. Dum ergo hoc permittis, super omnes vindictae manum extendis.

Dextera tua. Non habet Deus dexteram vel sinistram, sed dextera Dei dicitur felicitas aeterna, sinistra felicitas temporalis. Aliquando ergo non salvat in sinistra sanctos suos, sed semper salvat eos in dextera.

1059AVERS. 8.-- Retribuet. (AUG.) Quod ego non possum, etc., usque ad in quo principes mundi peccatum non invenit, quare occideret.

PSALM CXXXVII.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm to David himself. (CASS.) The captive, who had wept, as though Jerusalem and the temple were rebuilt, and as a fellow-citizen with that part of Jerusalem which was not captive, that is, with the angels, rejoices and praises first the benefits given him. In the person therefore of the Church, which is in the things above in hope, awaiting to be there in reality, he says, I will confess.

I will confess to thee, O Lord. First, he commends the benefits given him: secondly, he tells how these are spread abroad unto all, there, Let them confess to thee, O Lord, etc. In the sight. 1058B(AUG.) In praising I set before myself the angels, to whom I look to be made equal in dignity hereafter, as I am now. But these in the praise of God set before themselves nothing else but himself. In the sight therefore of the angels, in that purity wherein the angels behold thee, that in thee alone they may rest, I will sing to thee.

VERS. 2.-- For thy mercy. (ID.) All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth: There are no other ways by which he came to us, there are no others by which we may come to him: let us render these to God, mercy in succouring, truth in judging. Above every holy name of thine. (CASS.) Or above thy holy name, when thy worship became known to us.

VERS. 3.-- In the soul. And because in the soul a carnal multiplication can take place, he adds, strength, as though: I seek nothing 1058Celse in the soul but strength.

VERS. 4.-- Let them confess. (ID.) The second part, where it is said [dici; read dicit, "he tells"] how these good things are to be spread abroad unto all. As it were, after my example: Let them confess, etc. All the words of thy mouth. (AUG.) Which have now been revealed everywhere, and sent unto all nations, etc., as far as and thus, the fleece being dried, they heard all the words, etc.

VERS. 5.-- Great is the glory. (ID.) If they are humble, they love and sing this; for if they exalt themselves, let them fear what follows. For the Lord is high. He looketh on the low things. (CASS.) Here is not the human condition, where the humble man is despised and the proud man regarded; but the Lord regards the humble.

The high he knoweth afar off. (AUG.) The proud man does not this, etc., as far as mourning this sojourning, whence 1058Dit is subjoined.

VERS. 7.-- If I shall walk in the midst of tribulation. Otherwise he does not quicken, save in the midst of tribulation, whence, Blessed are they that mourn, woe to them that laugh.

Upon the wrath. (ID.) This very thing, that they are angry with me, is thy chastisement upon them, that is, thy punishment. For to be angry is to them a punishment, not noc only a fault. While therefore thou permittest this, thou stretchest forth the hand of vengeance upon them all.

Thy right hand. God has not a right hand or a left, but the right hand of God is called eternal happiness, the left, temporal happiness. Sometimes therefore he does not save his saints in the left hand, but he always saves them in the right.

1059AVERS. 8.-- He will repay. (AUG.) What I cannot do, etc., as far as in whom the princes of the world found no sin, wherefore they should kill him.

PSALMUS CXXXVIII.

VERS. 1.-- In finem psalmus Ddvid. (CASS.) Psalmus profunditate mysteriorum plenus, etc., usque ad in prophetis velatus, in Evangelio manifestus. (AUG.) Loquitur totus Christus, tanquam unus et integer vir, etc., usque ad sicut duo in carne una. Domine, probasti me. (CASS.) Primo, de notitia Dei, etc., usque ad quarto, quomodo mali ei non noceant, ibi, Si occideris, Deus, etc. Domine, probasti. (AUG.) Jam in Jerusalem restitutus, etc., usque ad haec est persona totius humanae naturae revertentis.

1059BVERS. 3.-- Intellexisti. (CASS.) Praescientia deitatis hic ostenditur, etc., usque ad quia homo assumptus divinae substantiae non potest aequari. De longe. (AUG.) Cum adhuc in peregrinatione sum, antequam ad patriam veniam, ut filio minori redeunti occurrit pater, quia intellexit ejus cogitationes de longinquo, quia apud se dixerat egestare confectus: Surgam et ibo ad patrem meum.

Semitam meum, scilicet malam, qua ivi, patrem deserens.

Et funiculum. (Alias) limitem, quousque perveni: longe quidem ieram, sed tu ibi. Ut deprehensus fugitivus loquitur, sequente se vindicta Dei.

VERS. 4.-- Et omnes vias meas: antequam irem eas, et permisisti me in labore ire, ut redirem si 1059Cnollem laborare, hoc fateor. Quia non est dolus in lingua mea: jam in tua gratia justificaui.

VERS. 5.-- Novissima mea, quando porcos pavi, Antiqua, quando partem substantiae petii, hoc secundum parabolam. Sed mystice, Antiqua, quando per antiquum pecatum lapsi sumus: Novissima, poena, quando in hanc mortalitatem venimus, quae est ultima, si redire volumus alioquin restat aeterna. Formasti me, ad labores, ad quos omnes nati sumus. Posuisti. (Alias) Gravasti manum, vindicem, gravantem superbum salubriter, ut erigat humilem, in gravata manu.

VERS. 6.-- Mirabilis, et incomprehensibllis mihi. Facta est scientia. Non est mihi facile contemplari te, quem superbus reliqui, ut prius erat cum essem apud te, quando dixi, da mihi partem substantiae. 1059DEx me, id est ex peccato meo.

Confortata est, (alias) invaluit. Et non potero attingere ex me. (AUG.) In Exodo legitur Dominum, etc., usque ad te non lateo, cujus limitem vides.

VERS. 7.-- Quo ibo spiritu tuo? (CASS.) Secunda pars, ubi jam deliberat non esse ab eo fungiendum, sed ad eum, ab irato ad placatum, quod erit per ipsum, quo plenus est mundus: Spiritus enim Domini replet omnia. Quo a facie tua fugiam? vertit se hac et illac, quasi quaerens locum fugae.

VERS. 8.-- Si ascendero in coelum, tu illic es, etc. (AUG.) Si me extulero, invenio repressorem; si de justitia mea superbiero, Tu ibi es, cujus vere est justitia. Si descendero, peccando venero, Ad infernum, 1060Avel in profundum, et nolens confiteri: dicam, quis me videt? Ades, ut vindices. Invenit consilium, sed sic potero fugere iratum.

VERS. 9.-- Si sumpsero pennas, duas alas charitatis, quas perdideram.

Pennas. (CASS.) Quae meae potestatis, in est efficaciam deitatis, qua corpus de sepulcro levavit. Has sumpsit diluculo, ante lucem, id est, tempore resurrectionis: et habitavit in extremis maris, hoc est, super saeculi amplissimum finem. Et habitavero in extremis. (AUG.) Mente, in fine saeculi, ut non saeculum amem, sed ejus finem, in quo sit mihi requies. Sed et ipse illuc ducit, unde subdit:

VERS. 10.-- Etenim illuc manus tua. Considerans autem longinquitatem viae, subdit:

1060BVERS. 11.-- Et dixit forsitan tenebrae conculcabunt, etc. Abundat iniquitas saeculi, qua pennae charitatis refrigescere possunt. Et quia in nocte desperavi transire mare, nox mihi facta est illuminatio: Venit mulier, sapientia Dei, quae drachmam, ubi est imago regis, id est hominem, perdiderat: accendit de se lucernam, quae de luto est, id est carnem, et nocte illuminata invenit drachmam.

Et dixit. (AUG.) Deliberavi.

Forsitan te. Tenebras dicit illam inferiorem partem rationalis creaturae, contrariam insistentem, scilicet iniquos homines vel carnem, unde timet: Et est, Tenebrae, id est inferior rationalis creatura sinistram tenens viam.

Conculcaverunt me. (ID.) Ita timebam, sed nox 1060Cfacta est illuminatio, in deliciis meis, id est illis qui, prius nox, illuminati erunt in deliciis. Quia te. Peccatores.

VERS. 12.-- Non obscurabuntur, etc., et nox, a peccatoribus degentibus. Sicut dies, id est sancti de Judaeis. Sicut tenebrae ejus, ita et lumen, quia quatenus agnoscit, eatenus ignoscit. Sed unde hoc mihi? quia tu possedisti renes meos. Quia tenebrae. (AUG.) Qui non confitetur peccata, suas tenebrat tenebras; sed si confitetur, Deus illuminat. Sicut tenebrae ejus. Nostrae noctis, id est, humanae vitae miseriae, etc., usque ad quem lumen non extollit.

VERS. 13.-- Quia tu possedisti renes meos. (ID.) Unde haec differentia tibi? quia interior possessor 1060Dnon solum cor, id est cogitationes tenet, sed et renes, id est delectationes: ut non delectet lux noctis, sed lux sapientiae suae.

VERS. 14.-- Confitebor tibi. (CASS.) Tertia pars, ubi dicit, revolanti ad Deum, Deo illuminante, renes possidente, quanta est exsultatio et multiplicatio. Anima mea cognoscet nimis. (AUG.) Jam cognoscit anima mea valde: ante erat mira scientia tua ex me, nec poteram ad eam; sed modo possum, quia noctem illuminasti, renes possedisti, de utero suscepisti, id est, quia venit mihi gratia tua, et illuminavit me.

VERS. 15.-- Non est occultatum os meum a te quod fecisti in occulto. (ID.) Os ab osse, non ab ore, etc., usque ad unde Apostolus: Quasi tristes, semper autem 1061Agaudentes. (BASIL.) Iterum de praescientia Dei loquitur, aut omnia illius arcana esse dicit, aut aliud quod dicit, opificium videlicet et figurationem. Substantia mea in inferioribus terrae. (AUG.) In carne et tamen os non cedit malis hujus inferioris, etc., usque ad non ergo desperent.

VERS. 16.-- Imperfectum meum viderunt oculi tui, et in libro tuo omnes, etc. (ID.) Qui hucusque locutus est ex persona corporis, hic jam loquitur ex persona capitis. Dies formabuntur. (Alias) Per diem errabunt. Dies hic manens adhuc erat Christus, etc., usque ad quia facti apostoli duces et pastores Ecclesiae. Quasi merito ego illos confortavi, etc., usque ad in promissione dictum est Abrahae: Multiplicabo semen tuum sicut stellas coeli et sicut arenam maris.

1061BVERS. 18.-- Adhuc sum tecum, etc. Sicut ante mortem, quod putaverunt se tulisse Judaei. Vel, adhuc, id est, ipsa morte, quod non videtur de mortuo. Vel, etsi resurrectio sit signum deitatis, tamen adhuc sum occultus pluribus, tecum, id est, ut tu.

(AUG.) Adhuc sum tecum. Nondum cum ipsis per notitiam, quia nondum agnoscunt, quia non mox post resurrectionem Christum agnoverunt. Vel, toto hoc tempore tecum sum in occulto ad dexteram Patris, antequam reveletur in ea claritate qua venturus est.

VERS. 19.-- Si occideris, Deus, peccatores, etc. (CASS.) Quarta pars quomodo a malis non noceatur ei. (AUG.) Si occideris. Subdit quid interea patitur, 1061Cetc., usque ad in judicio dicet aperte: Amen dico vobis, non novi vos, discedite a me.

VERS. 21.-- Nonne qui oderunt te, Domine. Quasi, Si occideris, Nonne qui oderunt te oderam? Illos, et ego occidam.

(AUG.) Quasi haeretici non intelligentes, etc., usque ad quomodo ergo permistione eorum contaminor?

Proba me, Domine. (ID.) Hucusque de haereticis et aliis eos sequentibus ab Ecclesia separatis, nunc etiam agit de malis, vel fictis sibi conjunctis, quos patitur Ecclesia, et gemit. Quasi haeretici se, et alios separant, etc., usque ad tu vero Deus, Proba me et scito.

PSALM CXXXVIII.

VERS. 1.-- Unto the end, a psalm of David Ddvid. (CASS.) A psalm full of the depth of mysteries, etc., as far as veiled in the prophets, manifest in the Gospel. (AUG.) The whole Christ speaks, as one entire man, etc., as far as as two in one flesh. Lord, thou hast proved me. (CASS.) First, concerning the knowledge of God, etc., as far as fourthly, how the wicked do him no hurt, there, If thou wilt kill, O God, etc. Lord, thou hast proved. (AUG.) Now restored in Jerusalem, etc., as far as this is the person of the whole of human nature returning.

1059BVERS. 3.-- Thou hast understood. (CASS.) The foreknowledge of the Godhead is here shown, etc., as far as because the manhood assumed cannot be made equal to the divine substance. From afar off. (AUG.) While I am still on pilgrimage, before I come to the fatherland, as the father ran to meet the younger son returning, because he understood his thoughts from afar off, because he had said within himself, worn out with want egestare: I will arise and go to my father.

My path, namely the evil one, by which I went, forsaking my father.

And the line. (Otherwise) the boundary, how far I came: far indeed had I gone, but thou wast there. He speaks as a fugitive caught, the vengeance of God following after him.

VERS. 4.-- And all my ways: before I went in them; and thou didst permit me to go in labour, that I might return if 1059CI would not labour: this I confess. For there is no guile in my tongue: [Vulg. Ps 138:4 quia non est sermo in lingua mea, "for there is no speech in my tongue"] now I have justified in thy grace.

VERS. 5.-- My last things, when I fed the swine, The old things, when I asked for the portion of the substance: this according to the parable. But mystically, The old things, when through the ancient sin pecatum we fell: The last things, the penalty, when we came into this mortality, which is the last, if we are willing to return; otherwise the eternal remains. Thou hast formed me, unto labours, unto which we are all born. Thou hast laid. (Otherwise) Thou hast made heavy the hand, the avenging hand, weighing down the proud man wholesomely, that it may raise up the humble man, in the hand made heavy.

VERS. 6.-- Wonderful, and incomprehensible incomprehensibllis to me. Thy knowledge is become. It is not easy for me to contemplate thee, whom in my pride I forsook, as it was before, when I was with thee, when I said, give me the portion of the substance. 1059DFrom me, that is, from my sin.

It is strengthened, (otherwise) it has prevailed. And I shall not be able to attain to it of myself. (AUG.) In Exodus it is read that the Lord, etc., as far as I am not hidden from thee, whose boundary thou seest.

VERS. 7.-- Whither shall I go by thy spirit? (CASS.) The second part, where he now determines that he must not flee fungiendum from him, but to him, from him angered to him appeased, which shall be through him with whom the world is full: For the Spirit of the Lord filleth all things. Whither shall I flee from thy face? [Vulg. Wisd. 1:7 Spiritus Domini replevit orbem terrarum, "the Spirit of the Lord hath filled the whole world"] he turns himself this way and that, as though seeking a place of flight.

VERS. 8.-- If I shall ascend into heaven, thou art there, etc. (AUG.) If I shall lift myself up, I find one to repress me; if I shall be proud of my own justice, Thou art there, whose justice it truly is. If I shall descend, if by sinning I shall come, Into hell, 1060Aor into the deep, and unwilling to confess: I shall say, who sees me? Thou art present, to avenge. He found a counsel, but thus shall I be able to flee from him angered.

VERS. 9.-- If I shall take wings, the two wings of charity, which I had lost.

Wings. (CASS.) Which are of my own power, in [in; read id, "that is"] is the efficacy of the Godhead, whereby he raised the body out of the sepulchre. These he took at daybreak, before the light, that is, at the time of the resurrection: and he dwelt in the uttermost parts of the sea, that is, above the widest end of the world. And if I shall dwell in the uttermost parts. (AUG.) In mind, at the end of the world, that I may not love the world, but its end, in which there may be rest for me. But he himself also leads thither, whence he subjoins:

VERS. 10.-- For even there shall thy hand. But considering the length of the way, he subjoins:

1060BVERS. 11.-- And he said, perhaps darkness shall tread down, etc. The iniquity of the world abounds, whereby the wings of charity can grow cold. And because in the night I despaired of crossing the sea, the night was made a light to me: There came a woman, the wisdom of God, who had lost the groat wherein is the image of the king, that is, man: she lighted from herself a lamp, which is of clay, that is, flesh, and the night being lit up she found the groat.

And he said. (AUG.) I deliberated.

Perhaps thee. By darkness he means that lower part of the rational creature, pressing upon him as an adversary, namely wicked men or the flesh, whence he fears: And it is, Darkness, that is, the lower rational creature holding the left-hand way.

They have trodden me down. (ID.) So I feared, but the night 1060Cwas made a light, in my delights, [Vulg. Ps 138:11 et nox illuminatio mea in deliciis meis, "and night shall be my light in my pleasures"] that is, to those who, being before night, shall be enlightened in delights. Because thee. Sinners.

VERS. 12.-- They shall not be darkened, etc., and the night, by the sinners that dwell there. As the day, that is, the saints out of the Jews. As his darkness, so also his light, because in so far as he acknowledges, in so far he pardons. But whence is this to me? because thou hast possessed my reins. Because darkness. (AUG.) He who confesses not his sins darkens his own darkness; but if he confesses, God enlightens. As his darkness. Of our night, that is, the miseries of human life, etc., as far as whom the light does not lift up.

VERS. 13.-- Because thou hast possessed my reins. (ID.) Whence is this difference in thee? because the inward possessor 1060Dholds not only the heart, that is, the thoughts, but the reins also, that is, the delights: that the light of night may not delight, but the light of his own wisdom.

VERS. 14.-- I will confess to thee. (CASS.) The third part, where he tells how great is the exultation and the multiplication for him that flies back to God, God enlightening him and possessing his reins. My soul shall know exceedingly. [Vulg. Ps 138:14 anima mea cognoscit nimis, "my soul knoweth right well," in the present tense] (AUG.) Now my soul knows greatly: before, wonderful was thy knowledge from me, and I could not attain unto it; but now I can, because thou hast enlightened the night, hast possessed the reins, hast received me out of the womb, that is, because thy grace came to me and enlightened me.

VERS. 15.-- My bone is not hidden from thee, which thou hast made in secret. (ID.) Os from osse, not from ore, etc., as far as whence the Apostle: As sorrowful, yet always 1061Arejoicing. (BASIL.) Again he speaks of the foreknowledge of God, and either says that all things are his secrets, or that other thing which he says, namely the workmanship and the fashioning. My substance in the lower parts of the earth. (AUG.) In the flesh, and yet the bone yields not to the evils of this lower place, etc., as far as let them not therefore despair.

VERS. 16.-- Thy eyes did see my imperfect being, and in thy book all, etc. (ID.) He who has hitherto spoken in the person of the body, here now speaks in the person of the head. Days shall be formed. (Otherwise) They shall wander through the day. The day here abiding was still Christ, etc., as far as because the apostles were made leaders and shepherds of the Church. As it were, deservedly I strengthened them, etc., as far as in the promise it was said to Abraham: I will multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven and as the sand of the sea.

1061BVERS. 18.-- I am still with thee, etc. As before death, which the Jews thought they had taken away. Or, still, that is, in death itself, which is not seen of a dead man. Or, though the resurrection be a sign of the Godhead, yet I am still hidden from the many, with thee, that is, as thou art.

(AUG.) I am still with thee. Not yet with them by knowledge, because they do not yet acknowledge him, because they did not acknowledge Christ soon after the resurrection. Or, through all this time I am with thee in secret at the right hand of the Father, before he be revealed in that brightness wherein he is to come.

VERS. 19.-- If thou wilt kill, O God, the sinners, etc. (CASS.) The fourth part, how he is not hurt by the wicked. (AUG.) If thou wilt kill. He subjoins what he suffers meanwhile, 1061Cetc., as far as in the judgment he will say openly: Amen I say to you, I know you not, depart from me. [Vulg. Mt 7:23 numquam novi vos : discedite a me, "I never knew you: depart from me"; the opening words are those of Mt 25:12 Amen dico vobis, nescio vos]

VERS. 21.-- Have not they that hate thee, O Lord. As it were, If thou wilt kill, Have I not hated them that hate thee? Them will I also slay.

(AUG.) As it were, heretics not understanding, etc., as far as how then am I defiled by being mingled with them?

Prove me, O Lord. (ID.) Hitherto concerning heretics and others following them, separated from the Church; now he treats also of the wicked, or of feigned men joined to himself, whom the Church suffers, and groans over. As it were, heretics separate themselves and others, etc., as far as but thou, O God, Prove me and know.

PSALMUS CXXXIX.

1061DVERS. 1.-- In finem Psalmus David. (ID.) Conquestio, gemitus, oratio corporis Christi inter malos constituti, nondum habentis in re, sed in spe bonum, ubi est plena exsultatio. Monet ut contra mala saeculi Deum oremus.

VERS. 2.-- Eripe me, Domine, ab homine. (CASS.) Prius proponit, qui hostes, quae mala movent, opponens eis preces. Secundo, dicit quod auxilium habeat contra mala, ibi, Dixi Domino: Tertio, quae sint mala inimicorum aperit, ibi, Caput. Ecclesia ergo inter malos laborans, clamat. A viro iniquo. (AUG.) Iniquus est qui nocet, unde cum dixisset, Ab homine malo, quasi exponens, subjunxit, A viro iniquo.

1062AVERS. 3.-- Qui cogitaverunt. (CASS.) Qualiter mali persequuntur exsequitur, impugnant enim bonos tribus modis, scilicet lingua, manu et corde: et de corde praemittit, dicens, Qui cogitaverunt, quasi diceret, Eripe me a populo malorum. (AUG.) Qui etsi in labiis plerumque bona praetendant, tamen cogitaverunt iniquitatem in corde.

VERS. 4.-- Acuerunt. Qualiter in lingua persequuntur, ostendit.

Sicut serpentis. (ID.) In serpente est astutia et dolus nocendi: ideo et serpit, non habens pedes, ut non audiatur, cum venit; lenis est ejus tractus, sed non rectus: sic mali serpunt ad nocendum, sub levi tractu habentes occultum venenum, unde subdit, Venenum aspidum sub labiis eorum.

1062BVERS. 5.-- Custodi me, Domine. (CASS.) De persecutione, quae fit manu, id est, opere, subdit. Custodi me, quia per multa fallit, quae nequit praecavere.

VERS. 9.-- Superbi. (AUG.) Hoc nomine breviter totum corpus diaboli explicavit: inde est quod et justos se dicunt et nolunt confiteri; omnis superbus etiam invidus est, sicut diabolus, qui invidit homini, quod perdidit. Et funes extenderunt in laqueum, etc. Unde Isaias: Vae his qui trahunt peccata sicut vestem longam, quia addunt peccata peccatis, etc., usque ad et mittatur in tenebras exteriores.

VERS. 7.-- Dixi Domino. (ID.) Diapsalma. Secunda pars, quod auxilium contra mala, quasi dicat, tot modis mali impugnant, et quod est remedium inter 1062Ctot et tanta mala?

Dixi Domino: Deus meus. Magna fiducia, etsi omnium Deus, proprie tamen eorum qui eo fruuntur.

Exaudi, Domine, vocem deprecationis meae. (ID.) Vox hominum et anima eorum, etc., usque ad non ut homines Domini, qui emunt saccello, tu sanguine.

VERS. 8.-- Virtus salutis meae obumbrasti super caput meum. (ID.) Qui das vires salutis meae, etc., usque ad quantumcunque saeviat hostis.

VERS. 9.-- Non tradas me, Domine, a desiderio. (ID.) Diabolus proponit lucrum, etc., usque ad nisi ex tuo desiderio.

VERS. 10.-- Caput circuitus. (CASS.) Diapsalma. Tertia pars, ubi dicit, quae sint mala inimicorum. 1062D(AUG.) Quasi dicat, Me tegit umbra tua, etc., usque ad vel de assertione superantur. Labor labiorum ipsorum operiet eos. (CASS.) Id est, falsa et mendax assertio eorum, operiet eos, quia de sua falsa assertione superantur.

VERS. 11.-- Cadent super eos. (AUG.) Vel carbones ignis in terra, etc., usque ad unde Apostolus: Aliis sumus odor vitae in vitam, aliis odor mortis in mortem (II Cor. II.)

VERS. 12.-- Vir linguosus. (ID.) Quisquis vult dirigi, etc., usque ad de exterioribus necessitas, non voluntas. Injustum, etc., in interitu. Quod non fit inopi, qui, si capitur malis, non tamen in interitum; flagellat Deus omnem filium quem recipit. Et licet 1063Aboni modo sint afflicti, tamen confitebuntur inter gravia, quod laudabilius: Et habitabunt, ideo nil timetur in mundo.

VERS. 14.-- Verumtamen. (CASS.) Conclusio psalmi ubi dicit quod si boni liberati sint, et de inimicis vindicati, non tamen sibi dant, sed Deo, unde, et habitabunt cum eo.

Habitabunt cum vultu tuo. Quia Deum, sicut est, videbunt.

PSALM CXXXIX.

1061DVERS. 1.-- Unto the end. A psalm of David. (ID.) A complaint, a groaning, the prayer of the body of Christ set among the wicked, not yet having the good in fact, but in hope, where there is full exultation. He admonishes us to pray to God against the evils of the world.

VERS. 2.-- Deliver me, O Lord, from the man. (CASS.) First he sets forth who the enemies are, what evils they stir up, setting prayers against them. Secondly, he says what help he has against evils, there: I said to the Lord: Thirdly, he discloses what the evils of his enemies are, there: The head. The Church therefore, labouring among the wicked, cries out. From the unjust man. (AUG.) He is unjust who does harm; whence, when he had said, From the evil man, as though expounding it, he added, From the unjust man.

1062AVERS. 3.-- Who have devised. (CASS.) He pursues in what manner the wicked persecute, for they assail the good in three ways, namely with the tongue, the hand and the heart: and he puts the heart first, saying, Who have devised, as if he were to say, Deliver me from the people of the wicked. (AUG.) Who, although for the most part they put forward good things upon their lips, have nevertheless devised iniquity in the heart.

VERS. 4.-- They have sharpened. He shows in what manner they persecute with the tongue.

Like that of a serpent. (ID.) In the serpent there is cunning and the guile of doing harm: therefore also it creeps, having no feet, that it may not be heard when it comes; its motion is smooth, but not straight: so the wicked creep to do harm, having a hidden venom beneath a smooth motion, whence he adds, The venom of asps is under their lips.

1062BVERS. 5.-- Keep me, O Lord. (CASS.) He adds concerning the persecution which is done by the hand, that is, by deed. Keep me, because he deceives through many things which he cannot guard against beforehand.

VERS. 9.-- The proud. (AUG.) By this name he has briefly set forth the whole body of the devil: hence it is that they both call themselves just and are unwilling to confess; every proud man is also envious, as the devil is, who envied man that which he himself had lost. And they have stretched out cords for a snare, etc. Whence Isaias: Woe to them that draw sins as a long garment, [Vulg. Isa. 5:18 Vae qui trahitis iniquitatem in funiculis vanitatis, et quasi vinculum plaustri peccatum, "that draw iniquity with cords of vanity"] because they add sins to sins, etc., as far as and he be cast into the exterior darkness.

VERS. 7.-- I said to the Lord. (ID.) Diapsalma. The second part, what help there is against evils, as if he should say, In so many ways do the wicked assail, and what is the remedy amid 1062Cso many and so great evils?

I said to the Lord: My God. Great confidence: though he is the God of all, yet he is properly the God of those who enjoy him.

Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication. (ID.) The voice of men and their soul, etc., as far as not as the men of the Lord, who buy with a purse, thou with blood.

VERS. 8.-- O strength of my salvation, thou hast overshadowed my head. (ID.) Thou who givest the strength of my salvation, etc., as far as however much the enemy may rage.

VERS. 9.-- Deliver me not, O Lord, from desire. [Vulg. Ps. 139:9 Ne tradas, a prohibitive subjunctive] (ID.) The devil sets forth gain, etc., as far as save out of thy desire.

VERS. 10.-- The head of the compassing. (CASS.) Diapsalma. The third part, where he says what the evils of his enemies are. 1062D(AUG.) As if he should say, Thy shadow covers me, etc., as far as or they are overcome out of their own assertion. The labour of their lips shall overwhelm them. (CASS.) That is, their false and lying assertion shall overwhelm them, because they are overcome out of their own false assertion.

VERS. 11.-- They shall fall upon them. (AUG.) Or coals of fire upon the earth, etc., as far as whence the Apostle: To some we are the odour of life unto life, to others the odour of death unto death (II Cor. II.)

VERS. 12.-- A man full of tongue. (ID.) Whosoever wills to be directed, etc., as far as in outward things there is necessity, not will. The unjust man, etc., unto destruction. Which does not befall the needy man, who, if he is taken by evils, is yet not taken unto destruction; God scourges every son whom he receives. And although 1063Athe good be for the present afflicted, yet they shall confess amid grievous things, which is the more praiseworthy: And they shall dwell, therefore nothing is feared in the world.

VERS. 14.-- But yet. (CASS.) The conclusion of the psalm, where he says that if the good have been delivered, and avenged of their enemies, they do not nevertheless give it to themselves, but to God, whence, and they shall dwell with him.

They shall dwell with thy countenance. Because they shall see God as he is.

PSALMUS CXL.

VERS. 2.-- Dirigatur oratio. (CAS.) Oratio sit incensum, etc., usque ad qui in fine poenitet.

Elevatio manuum mearum, etc. (AUG.) Hoc de capite omnes intelligant, etc., usque ad subdit ex voce corporis.

1063BVERS. 3.-- Pone, Domine, custodiam. Nota, quod et cordi et ori petit apponit custodiam: duplici munimine opus est, ut nec cogitatio iniqua sapiat, nec prava voluntas in fatua verba erumpat.

Ostium. (AUG.) A similitudine illius qui circumstat ostium, ne intret, vel exeat, cui non licet.

VERS. 4.-- Non declines. (CASS.) Quasi: Ad hoc pone ostium ut non excusetur: quod summum vitium dominatur hominibus, unde tardius poenitent; unde in libro regum: Quasi peccatum hariolandi est repugnare, et quasi scelus idololatriae est nolle acquiescere (I Reg. XV).
