Ad excusandas excusationes. (ID.) Consuetudo impudentium, ut deprehensi, primum per aliqua falsa excusent, et inde convicti alia quaerunt, tempori 1063Cvel necessitati vitia imputantes, ne quando veritati cedant.

Non communicabo. (ID.) Vel, combinabor. Combinati dicuntur, quando duo simul ligantur, ut alter alterum impediat, ne sit fuga libera. Non combinabor ad similitudinem carnis. Cum electis. (AUG.) Electi sunt, qui se justificant, caeteros despiciunt, ut Pharisaeus (Luc. XVIII); et peccata defendunt quibusque modis. Cum talibus non vult iste combinari, id est sociari, ne impediatur ab eis.

VERS. 5.-- Corripiet me. (CASS.) Secunda pars, ubi fidelis iste jam e contra a justo correctus, spernit falsos laudatores, malis verbo et moribus profuturus, in quo et petit custodiri.

Oleum autem peccatoris, etc. (ID.) Dilectio simulata, 1063Dquae mentes a rigore veritatis emollit ad noxia.

VERS. 6.-- Judices. (AUG.) Potentes, docti, qui de moribus judicant, etc., usque ad quem omnes colunt.

VERS. 7.-- Audient. (ID.) Aure obedientiae, non sicut Adam, etc., usque ad maledictioni proximos.

Crassitudo terrae. (ID.) Sunt quae dam contemptibilia unde tamen terra accipit pinguedinem, etc., usque ad qui sunt ossa et firmamentum fidelium vel fidei.

VERS. 8.-- Secus infernum. (ID.) Secus infernum dicit, non, in inferno: quia etsi communi sorte moriuntur, non tamen descendunt in infernum ut mali, sed vita aeterna datur illis. Quia ad te, Domine. 1064A(CASS.) Dicta fragilitate hominis, ad divina remedia confugit.

Ne auferas a bonis tuis, sed spes mea semper sit in te: et oculi mei semper ad te intendant. Non enim petit iste contra hoc quod sancti volunt, scilicet de saeculo eripi et esse cum Christo.

VERS. 9.-- Custodi me a laqueo. Per laqueos et scandala, totius mundi mala breviter notat. Laquei sunt blandi nexus, carnis desideria; sed dum per hos diabolus non proficit, nititur scandalis, quae per inquietos movet.

Vel aliter. Et dicit, statuentes laqueum, persecutores manifestos: operantes autem iniquitatem, consentientes illis dicit, qui timore persecutionis deficiunt. Et est: Ne auferas animam meam, sed 1064Bpotius, Custodi me a laqueo persecutionis, quem statuerunt mihi. (AUG.) Hoc faciunt persecutores, qui escam vitae hujus quasi in muscipula ponunt. Si amat avis hanc escam, in muscipulam cadit: quia timore mortis persecutioni succumbit. Custodi me.

A scandalis operantium iniquitatem. Id est, scandalo eorum qui, consentiendo illis, labuntur, et ita iniquitatem operantur. Quasi dicat: Custodi me a persecutoribus, qui terrent, et lapsis.

VERS. 10.-- Cadent in retiaculo. Apta verba comparationi, cum istis non vult combinari.

Cadent de vitio in vitium, sed

Singulariter sum ego donec transeam. Singulariter, id est quia cum pessimis non ambulat. Singulariter. (AUG.) Idem quod dicit, etc., usque ad sic et alii antiqui.

1064CTranseam. Ut viator hujus mundi, qui nulla voluptate capitur.

PSALM CXL.

VERS. 2.-- Let prayer be directed. (CAS.) Let prayer be incense, etc., as far as he who repents at the end.

The lifting up of my hands, etc. (AUG.) Let all understand this of the Head, etc., as far as he adds it from the voice of the body.

1063BVERS. 3.-- Set, O Lord, a watch. Note that he asks, he sets [apponit; read apponi, "to be set"] a watch upon the heart as well as upon the mouth: there is need of a twofold defence, that neither may an unjust thought have savour, nor may a depraved will break out into foolish words.

A door. (AUG.) From the likeness of him who stands about the door, that he may not enter or go out to whom it is not lawful.

VERS. 4.-- Incline not. (CASS.) As if: Set a door to this end, that he may not be excused: for this greatest vice has dominion over men, whence they repent the more slowly; whence in the book of Kings: As the sin of soothsaying is it to rebel, and as the crime of idolatry to be unwilling to acquiesce (I Reg. XV).

To make excuses for excuses. (ID.) It is the custom of the shameless that, when caught, they first excuse themselves by certain falsehoods, and then, convicted of these, they seek others, imputing their vices to the time 1063Cor to necessity, lest at any time they should yield to the truth.

I will not communicate. (ID.) Or, I shall be coupled. Men are said to be coupled when two are bound together, so that the one hinders the other, that flight may not be free. I shall not be coupled after the likeness of the flesh. With the elect. (AUG.) The elect are those who justify themselves, despise the rest, as the Pharisee did (Luc. XVIII); and defend their sins by whatever means. With such men this man does not wish to be coupled, that is, associated, lest he be hindered by them.

VERS. 5.-- He shall correct me. (CASS.) The second part, where this faithful man, now on the contrary corrected by the just man, spurns false praisers, being about to profit the wicked by word and by manners, wherein also he asks to be kept.

But the oil of the sinner, etc. (ID.) A feigned love, 1063Dwhich softens minds away from the rigour of truth toward hurtful things.

VERS. 6.-- Judges. (AUG.) The powerful, the learned, who judge concerning manners, etc., as far as whom all worship.

VERS. 7.-- They shall hear. (ID.) With the ear of obedience, not like Adam, etc., as far as those nearest to a curse.

The fatness of the earth. (ID.) There are quae dam contemptible things from which nevertheless the earth receives its fatness, etc., as far as who are the bones and the firmament of the faithful or of the faith.

VERS. 8.-- Near hell. (ID.) He says near hell, not, in hell: because although they die by the common lot, they do not nevertheless go down into hell as the wicked do, but eternal life is given them. For unto thee, O Lord. 1064A(CASS.) The frailty of man having been spoken of, he takes refuge in the divine remedies.

Take not away from thy good things, but let my hope be always in thee: and let my eyes ever be intent upon thee. For this man does not ask against that which the saints will, namely to be snatched from the world and to be with Christ.

VERS. 9.-- Keep me from the snare. By snares and scandals he briefly notes the evils of the whole world. Snares are the flattering bonds, the desires of the flesh; but while the devil does not prevail through these, he strives with scandals, which he stirs up by means of the restless.

Or otherwise. And by those setting the snare he means open persecutors: but by those working iniquity he means those consenting to them, who fail through fear of persecution. And the sense is: Take not away my soul, but 1064Brather, Keep me from the snare of persecution, which they have set for me. (AUG.) This the persecutors do, who set the bait of this life as it were in a trap. If the bird loves this bait, it falls into the trap: because through fear of death it succumbs to persecution. Keep me.

From the scandals of them that work iniquity. That is, from the scandal of those who, by consenting to them, fall, and so work iniquity. As if he should say: Keep me from the persecutors, who terrify, and from those who have fallen.

VERS. 10.-- They shall fall in the net. Words fitted to the comparison, since he does not wish to be coupled with these.

They shall fall from vice into vice, but

I am alone until I pass. Alone, that is, because he does not walk with the worst. Alone. (AUG.) The same that he says, etc., as far as so also other ancients.

1064CI pass. As a wayfarer of this world, who is taken by no pleasure.

PSALMUS CXLI.

VERS. 1.-- Intellectus David. (CASS.) Psalmus iste quintus est eorum qui nomine orationis intitulantur, ubi non alia dicuntur quam quae in aliis dicta sunt psalmis, sed eadem. (AUG.) Quia autem repetitione hujusmodi communi consulitur infirmitati, non supervacue iterantur, ut repetita melius memoriae commendentur; unde scriptum est in Proverbiis: Thesaurus desiderabilis requiescit in ore sapientis (Prov. XII), quia sapiens, quae audierit, cogitat; retractando ruminat; vir autem stultus glutit illum, 1064Did est non cogitat, oblivioni dat; et haec sunt illa munda animalia in lege quae ruminant; ista immunda. David fugiens Saulem in spelunca latuit, de quo tamen hic non agitur, sed de significato. David enim significat Christum. Spelunca vero carnem, vel saeculum, vel sepulcrum. David ergo, Christus, cum membris in saeculo, vel Christus in carne, vel in sepulcro.

VERS. 2.-- Voce mea ad Dominum clamavi. Primo ponitur oratio contra mala, secundo agit de fine malorum, ibi: Clamavi ad te, Domine. Monet ergo nos orare. Et in persona totius Christi, quasi de spelunca ad Deum clamantis, ait: Deprecatus sum. (AUG.) Quod dicit clamavi, exponit, deprecatus sum. Quasi dicat: Clamor 1065Ameus deprecatio est, non murmur, non blasphemia.

VERS. 3.-- In conspectu ejus. (AUG.) Dominus redditurus est, in occulto ora; unde in Evangelio: Tu autem cum oraveris, intra in cubiculum tuum, et clauso ostio ora Patrem tuum qui videt in abscondito, etc. (Matth. VI.)

VERS. 4.-- Et tu cognovisti. (ID.) Hoc addit, ne audientes, defecit spiritus meus, putarent eum dejectum. Ac si diceret: Si illi putant me dejectum, quia spiritus meus defecit, tu me stantem vides, cujus Spiritus me vivificat.

Semitas. Justitiae, quas illi non vident.

In via. Multae viae, quia multa praecepta: una via, quia omnia ad unum, id est charitatem, rediguntur.

1065BAUG.) In via, secundum votum eorum; juxta viam, secundum veritatem. Christus enim est via, qui non sinit eos laqueum ponere in via, ut non sit nobis quo eamus; sinit tamen ponere juxta viam, ne a via declinemus.

VERS. 5.-- Considerabam ad dexteram. (AUG.) Quam mali non videbant; et hoc est, et non erat qui cognosceret. (CASS.) Cum enim pateris omnia, quis novit quid attendas? (AUG.) Qui in dexteram attendit, videt; qui in sinistram, excaecatur. Vel, apostoli non stabant ad dexteram, quia carnali timore dispersi sunt, sed ego perstiti.

Periit fuga. Tam corporis quam mentis. Et non est qui requirat. (CAS.) Quia nulla est consolatio, sed solus ad passionem relictus est. Periit fuga. 1065C(AUG.) Circumclusum se dicit. Periit fuga, quia non fugit animo, corpore licet aliquando. Circumclusus non fugit corpore, quia non potest. Fortius non fugit mente, qui non vult. Periit fuga concluso vel forti; fuga quidem, unde dicitur in Evangelio: Videt lupum venientem et fugit (Joan. X). Ubi Dominus mercenarium vituperat. Sed alia est fuga corporis, quam Dominus permittit dicens: Si vos persecuti fuerint in una civitate, fugite in aliam (Matth. X).

Et non est qui requirat animam. Quaeritur anima aut a persecutoribus, aut a dilectoribus. Sic fuga perit duobus modis, et a capto et a forti.

VERS. 6.-- Clamavi. (CAS.) Secunda pars ubi agit de fine malorum. Spes mea. Quia te ex omnibus eligo. Portio. Humiliter dicit et communiter portionem 1065Dsibi esse in terra viventium, cum tota sit sua. Hoc patet ex hoc quod latroni dixit: Hodie mecum eris in paradiso: qui est terra viventium aeternaliter.

VERS. 7.-- A persequentibus me. Diabolus enim per vasa sua, id est per filios diffidentiae, agit persecutionem corporis, ut intus fiat cordis ruina.

VERS. 8.-- Educ de custodia, etc. (AUG.) Ex persona Ecclesiae loquens, exponit unde liberandus. Alias de carcere. Quia in corruptione (quae est poena corporis) angustiatur: post quas angustias in domo Dei tota vita erit confessio, id est laus Dei; modo impedit carcer confiteri. Hic carcer vel spelunca mundus potest dici, ubi omnia vana: unde rogat 1066Aeduci animam, quae inde multa patitur, etc., usque ad sed corruptio ejus, et tentatio, carcer est.

PSALM CXLI.

VERS. 1.-- The understanding of David. (CASS.) This psalm is the fifth of those which are entitled by the name of a prayer, where no other things are said than those which have been said in other psalms, but the same. (AUG.) But because by a repetition of this kind provision is made for the common infirmity, they are not repeated to no purpose, that things repeated may the better be committed to memory; whence it is written in the Proverbs: A desirable treasure rests in the mouth of the wise man (Prov. XII), [Vulg. Prov. 21:20 Thesaurus desiderabilis, et oleum in habitaculo justi, "a desirable treasure, and oil in the dwelling of the just"] because the wise man ponders what he has heard; he ruminates upon it by going over it again; but the foolish man swallows it down, 1064Dthat is, he does not ponder it, he gives it over to forgetfulness; and these are those clean animals in the law which chew the cud; those are the unclean. David, fleeing from Saul, lay hid in a cave, of which nevertheless there is no question here, but of the thing signified. For David signifies Christ. The cave, the flesh, or the world, or the sepulchre. David therefore, that is, Christ, with his members in the world, or Christ in the flesh, or in the sepulchre.

VERS. 2.-- With my voice I have cried to the Lord. First the prayer against evils is set down, secondly he treats of the end of evils, there: I have cried to thee, O Lord. He admonishes us therefore to pray. And in the person of the whole Christ, as of one crying to God out of a cave, he says: I have made supplication. (AUG.) That which he says, I have cried, he expounds, I have made supplication. As if he should say: My cry 1065Ais a supplication, not a murmur, not a blasphemy.

VERS. 3.-- In his sight. (AUG.) The Lord is about to repay, pray in secret; whence in the Gospel: But thou when thou shalt pray, enter into thy chamber, and having shut the door, pray to thy Father who sees in secret, etc. (Matth. VI.)

VERS. 4.-- And thou hast known. (ID.) This he adds, lest those hearing, my spirit hath failed, should suppose him cast down. As if he were to say: If they suppose me cast down, because my spirit has failed, thou seest me standing, whose Spirit gives me life.

Paths. Of justice, which they do not see.

In the way. Many are the ways, because many are the precepts: one is the way, because all are brought back to one, that is, to charity.

1065BAUG.) In the way, according to their desire; beside the way, according to the truth. For Christ is the way, who does not suffer them to set a snare in the way, so that we should have nowhere to go; yet he suffers them to set it beside the way, lest we turn aside from the way.

VERS. 5.-- I looked to the right hand. (AUG.) Which the wicked did not see; and this is, and there was none that knew. (CASS.) For when thou sufferest all things, who knows what thou art regarding? (AUG.) He who attends to the right hand, sees; he who attends to the left, is blinded. Or, the apostles were not standing at the right hand, because they were scattered by a carnal fear, but I stood fast.

Flight hath perished. As much of the body as of the mind. And there is none that seeks. (CAS.) Because there is no consolation, but he was left alone to the passion. Flight hath perished. 1065C(AUG.) He says that he is shut in on every side. Flight hath perished, because he does not flee in mind, though sometimes in body. He who is shut in does not flee in body, because he cannot. More strongly [Fortius; read Fortis, "the strong man"] does he not flee in mind, who does not will it. Flight hath perished for the man shut in or for the strong man; flight indeed, whence it is said in the Gospel: He sees the wolf coming and flees (Joan. X). Where the Lord reproves the hireling. But there is another flight, of the body, which the Lord permits, saying: If they shall have persecuted you in one city, flee into another (Matth. X). [Vulg. Mt 10:23 Cum autem persequentur vos in civitate ista, fugite in aliam, "when they shall persecute you in this city"]

And there is none that seeks the soul. The soul is sought either by persecutors or by those who love it. So flight perishes in two ways, both for the man taken captive and for the strong man.

VERS. 6.-- I have cried. (CAS.) The second part, where he treats of the end of evils. My hope. Because I choose thee out of all. Portion. Humbly and in common with others he says that a portion 1065Dis his in the land of the living, whereas the whole is his. This appears from the fact that he said to the thief: This day thou shalt be with me in paradise: which is the land of the living everlastingly.

VERS. 7.-- From them that persecute me. For the devil through his vessels, that is, through the children of unbelief, works persecution of the body, that within there may come about the ruin of the heart.

VERS. 8.-- Bring forth out of custody, etc. (AUG.) Speaking in the person of the Church, he sets forth from what he is to be delivered. Otherwise, out of the prison. Because in corruption (which is the punishment of the body) he is straitened: after which straits in the house of God the whole life shall be confession, that is, the praise of God; now the prison hinders him from confessing. This prison or cave may be called the world, where all things are vain: whence he asks 1066Athat the soul be led forth, which suffers many things there, etc., as far as but its corruption, and temptation, is the prison.

PSALMUS CXLII.

Psalmus David. Psalmus iste septimus poenitentialium, qui ideo sunt septem, ut eodem numero quo peccavimus, peccata diluamus. (CAS.) Sicut enim in hebdomada mundi hujus peccamus, ita hoc numero psalmorum remedium poenitentiae peccatis opponitur. In quibus psalmis talis est forma, quia a lacrymis incipitur, et in gaudio finis est, ne quis de venia desperet. (AUG.) Sicut Absalom David, sic Judas Christum, falsi fratres corpus ejus; vel illiciti motus et operatio.

VERS. 1.-- Domine, exaudi, etc. (CAS.) Primo 1066Bcaptat exordium; secundo narrat mala sua, et quid contra egerit, ibi, quia persecutus est; tertio ponitur deprecatio causis confirmata, ibi, velociter exaudi; quarto ponitur laeta conclusio, ibi, spiritus tuus. Monet ad poenitentiam, et orationem, ad orandum. In persona totius Christi dicit: O Domine, etc. In veritate tua. (CAS.) Non est hoc contra humilitatem, quae petebat audiri: sed veritas et justitia Dei est, ne cum rogante disceptet, ne eum qui se damnat judicet; unde subditur: et non intres, non petivit justitiam judicii. (AUG., CAS.) In veritate tua, in tua justitia. Vel justitiam et veritatem dicit, quae parcit poenitentibus, et se damnantes absolvit, et accipit pro eodem veritatem et justitiam. Et est, in veritate tua, et tua justitia, id est secundum justitiam et 1066Cveritatem quam poenitentibus et se accusantibus indulges.

VERS. 2.-- Et non intres in judicium. (AUG.) Intrant in judicium cum Domino, qui suam justitiam constituunt, quod non iste humilis; unde propheta: Quid vultis mecum in judicio contendere? Omnes dereliquistis me, dicit Dominus. Cum servo tuo. Indignum est cum servo, ne dicam cum amico: et si tu dicis amicum, ego servum, fugitivus redeo, pacem quaero, non sum dignus vocari filius tuus.

VERS. 3.-- Quia persecutis. (CAS.) Secunda pars, ubi est narratio malorum quae patitur, et quid contra egerit.

VERS. 6.-- Memor fui. (AUG.) Hoc dicunt membra, etc., usque ad sed non esse coepisti. Meditatus 1066Dsum. Quia utique omnia bona sunt, in quo percipit, quia quidquid in se boni est, a Deo est. In factis manuum. Ac si dicat: Quaesivi in opere artificem, et in conditis omnibus conditorem: creatura tua facta est mihi spectaculum.

Memor fui dierum. (CAS.) Recolens iste quod fecit coelum et terram, et quod benefecit antiquis, obliviscitur miseriarum mundi. Et ex his quae Deus fecit se consolatur.

VERS. 7.-- Velociter. (CAS.) Tertia pars, ubi ponitur deprecatio causis confirmata. Defecit spiritus. (AUG.) Impleat me tuus Spiritus, quia defecit meus: jam sum pauper spiritu. In quo enim vivit spiritus suus, ille superbus est spiritu suo, et extollitur 1067Acontra Deum. Unde alibi: Auferes spiritus eorum, et deficient (Psal. CIII). In lacum. Ille descendit in profundum, quia etiam perdit confessionem, ut qui proponit sibi licentiam peccandi sine spe veniae, habenis iniquitatis effusis. Talis non audit Deum dicentem: Convertimini ad me, et ego convertar ad vos (Zach. I).

VERS. 8.-- Mane. (CAS.) Post noctem peccatorum. (AUG.) Mane est, cum peccata laxantur. Notam fac mihi viam. Hoc fecit Deus, etc., usque ad perveniemus ad lumen purum, ad Verbum in principio apud Deum. Animam. (CAS.) Ut vas ad fontem attuli: imple ergo.

VERS. 10.-- Spiritus tuus bonus. (CAS.) Quarta pars, ubi est laeta conclusio. Propter nomen tuum, 1067BDomine, vivificabis me in aequitate tua. Gratia Dei hic commendatur: quia non ex meritis, sed ex nomine, quod est Jesus, se vivificatum dicit, sed cum hoc gratia aequitatis miseretur, quia licet Deus omnia gratis faciat, justitiae tamen ejus est supplices justificare, quos daemones videt impetere.

PSALM CXLII.

A psalm of David. This psalm is the seventh of the penitential psalms, which are therefore seven, that by the same number by which we have sinned we may wash away our sins. (CAS.) For as we sin in the week of this world, so by this number of psalms the remedy of penance is set against our sins. In which psalms the form is such, that it is begun from tears, and the end is in joy, lest any despair of pardon. (AUG.) As Absalom did to David, so Judas to Christ, false brethren to his body; or unlawful motions and action.

VERS. 1.-- O Lord, hear, etc. (CAS.) First 1066Bhe takes his exordium; secondly he narrates his own evils, and what he has done against them, there, because he has persecuted; thirdly the supplication is set down, confirmed by reasons, there, hear speedily; fourthly the joyful conclusion is set down, there, thy spirit. He admonishes to penance, and to prayer, that we should pray. In the person of the whole Christ he says: O Lord, etc. In thy truth. (CAS.) This is not against the humility which was asking to be heard: but it is the truth and justice of God, that he should not dispute with the one asking, that he should not judge him who condemns himself; whence it is added: and enter not, he did not ask for the justice of judgment. (AUG., CAS.) In thy truth, in thy justice. Or he calls justice and truth that which spares the penitent, and absolves those who condemn themselves, and he takes truth and justice for the same thing. And the sense is, in thy truth, and thy justice, that is, according to the justice and 1066Ctruth which thou grantest to the penitent and to those who accuse themselves.

VERS. 2.-- And enter not into judgment. (AUG.) They enter into judgment with the Lord who establish their own justice, which this humble man does not do; whence the prophet: Why will you contend with me in judgment? You have all forsaken me, says the Lord. With thy servant. It is unworthy to contend with a servant, not to say with a friend: and if thou sayest 'friend', and I 'servant', a fugitive I return, I seek peace, I am not worthy to be called thy son.

VERS. 3.-- Because he has persecuted. (CAS.) The second part, where there is the narration of the evils which he suffers, and what he has done against them.

VERS. 6.-- I have been mindful. (AUG.) This the members say, etc., as far as but thou hast begun not to be. I have 1066Dmeditated. Because assuredly all things are good, wherein he perceives that whatsoever of good is in him, is from God. In the works of the hands. As if he should say: I have sought the craftsman in the work, and in all created things the creator: thy creature has been made a spectacle for me.

I have been mindful of the days. (CAS.) This man, calling to mind that he made heaven and earth, and that he did good to the ancients, forgets the miseries of the world. And out of those things which God has made he consoles himself.

VERS. 7.-- Speedily. (CAS.) The third part, where the supplication confirmed by reasons is set down. The spirit hath failed. (AUG.) Let thy Spirit fill me, because mine has failed: already I am poor in spirit. For in whom his own spirit lives, he is proud in his own spirit, and is lifted up 1067Aagainst God. Whence elsewhere: Thou shalt take away their spirits, and they shall fail (Psal. CIII). Into the pit. He goes down into the deep who loses even confession, as one who sets before himself licence to sin without hope of pardon, the reins of iniquity let loose. Such a man does not hear God saying: Turn to me, and I will turn to you (Zach. I).

VERS. 8.-- In the morning. (CAS.) After the night of sins. (AUG.) It is morning, when sins are loosed. Make the way known to me. This God has done, etc., as far as we shall come to the pure light, to the Word in the beginning with God. The soul. (CAS.) As a vessel I have brought it to the fountain: fill it therefore.

VERS. 10.-- Thy good spirit. (CAS.) The fourth part, where the joyful conclusion is. For thy name's sake, 1067BO Lord, thou wilt quicken me in thy equity. The grace of God is here commended: because he says that he is quickened not out of merits, but out of the name, which is Jesus; yet along with this the grace of equity shows mercy, because although God does all things freely, it belongs nevertheless to his justice to justify the suppliants whom he sees the demons assail.

PSALMUS CXLIII.

VERS. 1.-- Psalmus David ad Goliam. (CAS.) David, Christus totus, etc., usque ad et sic caput ejus gladio suo inciditur.--David Goliam, Christus occidit diabolum, etc., usque ad unde spiritualiter sequens psalmus, laudatio intitulatur.

Benedictus. (CAS.) Triumphalis psalmus, etc., usque ad precans per eum liberari, ibi, Deus canticum.

1067CQui docet manus meas. (AUG.) Id est qui per Spiritum sanctum, etc., usque ad quod sequitur. Misericordia mea. (CAS.) Quia prolixum est multis causas explicare, breviter singulis verbis tangit, etc., usque ad quia cum despectu et sub admiratione subditur, Domine, quid est homo quia, etc. (AUG.) Misericordia mea. Quia tu das mihi ut misericors sim, etc., usque ad dimitte ergo, et dimitto; da, et do.

VERS. 3.-- Quia reputas eum? (AUG.) Magnum est quod Deus aestimat, et tanti facit, ut pro eo Filium dederit, cui etiam fit panis, qui est panis angelorum: non enim sic aestimat hominem Deus, ut homo, qui charius emit equum quam hominem.

VERS. 4.-- Vanitati similis factus est: dies ejus 1067Dsicut umbra. (ID.) Quando homo conditus est, veriteti simlis factus est, vanitati peccando. Vana sunt omnia transitoria, comparatione semper manentis veritatis. (CAS.) Vanum est, quod de sua substantia cadens vanescit: ut fumus, ut umbra. Ita et ipse homo tabescit, unde subdit, Dies ejus, id est vita ejus notoria, id est transitoria, sic praeterit sicut umbra.

VERS. 5.-- Domine, inclina. (AUG.) Humilis David ex persona Ecclesiae, plenus gratia praesumens de Deo, pugnans hic invocat adjutorium Dei. Quasi, in lucta sumus, sed ne deficiamus. Domine, inclina. (CAS.) Domine. Idem aperit, etc., usque ad et forma Dei formam servi suscepit.

1068AVERS. 7.-- Emitte manum. (CAS.) Ad Patrem verba convertit: Emitte manum, id est Christum; de alto ubi cum Patre, ut carnem induat. (AUG.) Vel de secundo adventu agit in persona Ecclesiae. Quasi dicat: Ita fac modo. Emitte manum tuam de alto, id est Christum de caelo ad judicium. Veniet enim Dominus in voce angeli, et in tuba Dei descendet de coelo. Deinde ex persona Ecclesiae subdit: Eripe me, scilicet, per eam manum. Et libera, etc., ut in littera.

VERS. 9.-- Deus, canticum novum cantabo tibi. (CAS.) Secunda pars, ubi quasi ille quem precabatur, victor et liberator venerit, ei se cantare in Novo Testamento et Veteri promittit: et ab eo precatur liberari ab his qui beatitudinem putant in terrenis. 1068BCanticum. (AUG.) Hoc alio nomine significat legem, quam per quinque lapides significavit.

VERS. 10.-- Gladio. (AUG.) Quas superius dixit aquas, ipsum hic dicit gladium; unde et hic subdit quod ibi: Et erue me de manu filiorum alienorum. Maligno. De quo: Lingua eorum gladius acutus (Psal. LVI). Est et benignus gladius, de quo Dominus ait: Non veni pacem mittere, sed gladium (Matth. X). Hic est gladius bis actus (Apoc. XIX), utroque acumine praepotens, scilicet Veteris et Novi Testamenti, quo omnis putredo a membris Christi abscinditur.

VERS. 12.-- Quorum filii. Hic, qui sint alieni, et quae illorum dextera iniquitatis, et qualiter locuti sunt vanitatem, exponit. (AUG.) Felicitatem eorum 1068Cenumerat, haec est dextera eorum, haec est vanitas, quam loquuntur, dum haec dicunt beatitudinem. (CASS.) Quorum filii. Vel, mystice haec possunt intelligi ab illo loco, etc., usque ad sed novis erroribus pullulaverunt.

Filiae. (CASS.) Quae non habent vires constantiae.

Compositae. Non natura pulchrae, sed ab hominibus compositae. Hae filiae sunt cogitationes vel praedicationes eorum qui non habent veram Ecclesiam, sed similitudinem.

VERS. 13.-- Promptuaria. Corda diversis rebus facta: unde pessimas eructationes exhalant, quae fetent.

Ex hoc in illud. Instabiles, quia non habent radicem 1068Dveritatis.

VERS. 14.-- Oves eorum fetosae. Ad litteram, quia vult eos ostendere caducis rebus haerere. Quasi dicat: Peculium eorum fetosum, cum ipsi fide steriles; unde mystice discipuli eorum, hae oves sunt fetosae, quia ipsi alios plures in errore generant. In egressibus. Non in ingressibus, quia totum bonum quod habere videntur, ab eis egreditur cito perituris. Boves. Non laboro macri, sed otio pingues, ut his qui affluunt divitiis, eum ipsi sint a veritate jejuni. Vel mystice, boves, magistri terrenis affluunt. Maceriae. Quae de solis saxis in hortis sed vel vineis; nec ipsa ruit illis, ideo prosperi.

(CAS.) Neque transitus, neque clamor, turbidus 1069Ainterrumpit quietem eorum, etc., usque ad quae ducit ad mortem.

VERS. 15.-- Beatum. Non inde reprehendit quia his abundant, sed quia pro dextera habent, id est, pro beatitudine: et haec est vanitas quam locuti sunt. His et Abraham, et Isaac, et Jacob, abundavit. Felicitas est sinistra, id est temporalis, mortalis.

PSALM CXLIII.

VERS. 1.-- A psalm of David to Goliath. [Vulg. Ps. 143:1 Psalmus David. Adversus Goliath] (CAS.) David, the whole Christ, etc., as far as and so his head is cut off with his own sword.--David slew Goliath, Christ the devil, etc., as far as whence spiritually the following psalm is entitled praise.

Blessed. (CAS.) A triumphal psalm, etc., as far as praying to be delivered through him, there, O God, a canticle.

1067CWho teaches my hands. (AUG.) That is, who through the Holy Spirit, etc., as far as that which follows. My mercy. (CAS.) Because it is tedious to explain the causes of many things, he touches them briefly in single words, etc., as far as because with contempt and under wonder it is added, O Lord, what is man, that, etc. (AUG.) My mercy. Because thou grantest me to be merciful, etc., as far as forgive therefore, and I forgive; give, and I give.

VERS. 3.-- That thou makest account of him? (AUG.) Great is that which God esteems, and holds of such worth that for it he gave his Son, for whom he even becomes bread, who is the bread of angels: for God does not so esteem man as man does, who buys a horse more dearly than a man.

VERS. 4.-- He is become like to vanity: his days 1067Das a shadow. (ID.) When man was created, he was made like simlis to truth veriteti; like to vanity by sinning. All transitory things are vain, in comparison with the truth that ever abides. (CAS.) That is vain which, falling away from its own substance, vanishes: as smoke, as a shadow. So man himself also wastes away, whence he adds, His days, that is, his notorious life, that is, his transitory life, so passes away as a shadow.

VERS. 5.-- O Lord, bow down. (AUG.) The humble David, in the person of the Church, full of grace, presuming upon God, fighting here calls upon the help of God. As if: we are in a wrestling, but let us not fail. O Lord, bow down. (CAS.) O Lord. He discloses the same thing, etc., as far as and the form of God took upon it the form of a servant.

1068AVERS. 7.-- Send forth the hand. (CAS.) He turns his words to the Father: Send forth the hand, that is, Christ; from on high where he is with the Father, that he may put on flesh. (AUG.) Or he treats of the second coming in the person of the Church. As if he should say: So do now. Send forth thy hand from on high, that is, Christ from heaven unto judgment. For the Lord shall come in the voice of an angel, and in the trumpet of God he shall descend from heaven. Then in the person of the Church he adds: Take me out, namely, by that hand. And deliver, etc., as in the letter.

VERS. 9.-- O God, I will sing to thee a new canticle. (CAS.) The second part, where, as though he whom he was entreating had come as victor and deliverer, he promises to sing to him in the New Testament and in the Old: and he prays to be delivered by him from those who think beatitude to lie in earthly things. 1068BA canticle. (AUG.) By this other name he signifies the law, which he signified by the five stones.

VERS. 10.-- With the sword. (AUG.) Those which above he called waters, the same he here calls a sword; whence here also he adds what he added there: And rescue me from the hand of strange children. Malignant. Of which: Their tongue is a sharp sword (Psal. LVI). There is also a kindly sword, of which the Lord says: I came not to send peace, but the sword (Matth. X). This is the sword twice driven [actus; read acutus, "sharpened"] (Apoc. XIX), mighty with either edge, namely of the Old and of the New Testament, by which all rottenness is cut away from the members of Christ.

VERS. 12.-- Whose sons. Here he sets forth who the strangers are, and what their right hand of iniquity is, and in what manner they have spoken vanity. (AUG.) He enumerates their felicity: 1068Cthis is their right hand, this is the vanity which they speak, while they call these things beatitude. (CASS.) Whose sons. Or, mystically these things can be understood from that place, etc., as far as but they have sprouted with new errors.

Daughters. (CASS.) Which have not the strength of constancy.

Decked out. Not beautiful by nature, but decked out by men. These daughters are the thoughts or the preachings of those who have not the true Church, but a likeness of it.

VERS. 13.-- Storehouses. Hearts made for divers things: whence they breathe out the worst belchings, which stink.

From this into that. Unstable, because they have not the root 1068Dof truth.

VERS. 14.-- Their sheep fruitful. According to the letter, because he wishes to show that they cleave to perishable things. As if he should say: Their flock is fruitful, while they themselves are barren in faith; whence mystically their disciples, these are the fruitful sheep, because they themselves beget many others in error. In the goings out. Not in the goings in, because all the good which they seem to have goes out from them, who are soon to perish. Oxen. Not I labour [laboro; read labore, "with labour"] lean, but fat with idleness, like those who abound in riches, him [eum; read cum, "whereas"] they themselves are fasting from truth. Or mystically, oxen, the masters, abound in earthly things. The fence. Which are of stones alone in gardens but or in vineyards; nor does it itself fall down for them, therefore they are prosperous.

(CAS.) Neither passage, nor cry, turbulent, 1069Ainterrupts their quiet, etc., as far as which leads to death.

VERS. 15.-- Blessed. He does not blame them on this account, because they abound in these things, but because they hold them for a right hand, that is, for beatitude: and this is the vanity which they have spoken. In these Abraham also, and Isaac, and Jacob abounded. Happiness is a left hand, that is, temporal, mortal.

PSALMUS CXLIV.

VERS. 1.-- Laudatio ipsi David. (CAS.) Breviter continet hic psalmus quae in Scripturis divinis late diffunduntur, etc., usque ad ne quis in ejus laude errare posset:

(AUG.) Spiritu sancto implet Deus sanctos, etc., 1069Busque ad ideoque spiritus ejus in servis suis laudet eum, quia laudari se facit.

(CAS.) Ut septem psalmi poenitentiae, sic et septem spiritus, juxta illud sacramentum quod praecepit Dominus Moysi in tabernaculo septem lucernas ponere, perpetuo lumine lucentes.

Exaltabo te. (CAS.) Primo propheta promittit infinitam laudem; secundo, omnes perfecturos Dei laudem novem modis dicit, ibi, Generatio et generatio; tertio, eadem latius explicat, ibi, miserator.

In saeculum saeculi. (CAS.) Qui hic non incipit, in futuro mutus erit.

VERS. 2.-- Per singulos dies, etc. (ID.) Qui hic per singulos dies, in aeterno die merebitur laudare continua exsultatione.

1069C(AUG.) Benedicit nunc per singulos dies, ut, cum venerit unus sine fines dies, eat ex laude in laudem, sicut ex virtute in virtutem. In saeculum et in saeculum saeculi. (CAS.) De qua laude alibi: In saecula saeculorum laudabunt (Psal. XXXVIII), quia semper amabunt quem semper videbunt, quia visione nihil delectabilius.

VERS. 3.-- Nimis. (CAS.) Uno verbo dedit cogitare quod non potest capi plene: et ideo nunquam cesses a laudibus.

VERS. 4.-- Generatio et generatio. (CAS.) Secundo, omnes perfecturos laudem Dei novem modis promittit. Opera tua. (AUG.) Si in magnitudine deficimus, vel de operibus laudemus operantem, de conditis conditorem, de creaturis creatorem. (CAS.) 1069DNovem sunt opera: potentia, magnificentia, sanctitas, mirabilia, virtus, terribilium magnitudo, memoria, justitia, quae post explicabuntur: ex his quasi locis et seminibus omnis laus trahitur, ad quem modum omnia argumenta de paucitate locorum sumuntur. Et potentiam tuam. (AUG.) Non enim opera laudant, nisi ut virtutem operantis annuntient. Sed quidam eloquentes creaturam laudant, creatoris obliti. Sancti vero laudatores, si opera amant, et laudant magis operatorem: et propter haec illum amant. Si in rebus factis sentitur aliqua species, utilitas, virtus, et laudatur magis in illo qui fecit. Si opera laudas, et te qui es Dei opus. Et occurrit illud: Non te laudet os tuum, ne arrogans 1070Avidearis (Prov. XXVII). Sed non est arrogantia, quia Deum in te, non te laudas.

VERS. 6.-- Et virtutem. Si non minaretur, nulla esset corectio; si vero non blandiretur, nulla esset exhortatio. Est itaque amabilis et terribilis. Dicent ergo virtutem disciplinantis et punientis, si praedicant regnum aeternum, non tacent ignem aeternum.

VERS. 7.-- Memoriam abundantiae suavitatis tuae eructabunt. (AUG.) Ipse per abundantem suavitatem suam prius memor nostri est, nos vocando, gratia sua nos praeveniendo, inde nos ejus.

Eructabunt dicit, non manducabunt.

(AUG.) Manducat qui discit, eructat qui docet: hoc tamen eructat quod manducat. Haec memoria, quia valde dulcis manducanda est et eructanda. Sic ergo 1070Bmanduca ut eructes.

VERS. 8.-- Miserator et misericors. (CAS.) Tertio latius explicat quae secundo breviter proposuit. Quasi: Merito in his laudabunt, quia miserator, etc. Partes laudis ponuntur hic, quae superius, sed non singulae possunt explicari: quis enim opera vel potentiam ejus plene explicaret? (AUG.) Miserator et misericors. Quibus eam veniam dedit. Patiens. His quibus nondum dedit, sed exspectat ut det.

VERS. 9.--(CAS.) Miserationes. Ab operibus incipit, ut miserator dicatur dum cadentes restituit. Misericors, natura, etiam dum creat. Patiens, hoc sumit de secundo loco laudis, scilicet de potentia, quam laudat, non quod terras suspendit, maria coercuit, stellis coelos depinxit, etc., sed quia tolerat 1070Cpeccantes, ut convertantur. Et miserationes ejus. (AUG.) Si enim tollas opera tua mala, et non in te remaneant nisi opera ejus, non te dimittet miseratio ejus: si autem tu non dimittas opera tua, erit ejus severitas in opera tua, cum dicet: Ite, maledicti, in ignem aeternum (Matth. XXV).

VERS. 10.-- Confiteantur tibi, Domine, omnia opera tua. (AUG.) Laudent sicut ea quae non habent sensum laudandi, qui sunt materia laudis: quia dum inquiris, invenis magnam vim in eis, quae a Deo.

Et sancti tui. (CAS.) Omne quod est confitetur vel per se, vel per rationales creaturas. Vel sancti, id est, angeli et homines. Hoc de sanctitate: ipsa est enim sanctitas Dei, ut ei sancti debeant confiteri.

1070DVERS. 11.-- Gloriam regni. (ID.) De mirabilibus ergo sumitur. Quasi: Quam mirabilis enim qui fecit coelum et terram, et diversis bonis implevit.

VERS. 12.-- Ut notam. (ID.) De virtute terribilium hoc sumitur, etc., usque ad cui magnifico nil comparatur.

VERS. 13.-- Regnum tuum, etc. (ID.) Laudat de perpetuitate et dominationis effectu. Et sumitur hoc de magnitudine: si magnum est ad tempus imperare, majus est dominationis terminum non habere.

Fidelis Dominus in omnibus. (ID.) De abundanti suavitate hoc sumitur; unde supra: Memoriam abundantiae suavitatis tuae. Fidelis, quia adventus dona complevit. Ad abundantiam quoque pertinet 1071Aquod allevat ruentes, erigit elisos; unde recordatio suavitatis habetur, et in laudibus ejus eructatur.

VERS. 14.-- Qui corruunt. (CAS.) A malis suis, quos omnes allevat Deus. Vel, ab his temporalibus, sicut sancti, ut Job, qui in saeculo aliquid perdunt et abjecti fiunt, decidentes sunt: sed hos omnes confirmat, quia septies cadit justus et resurgit; impii autem infirmantur in malis (Prov. XXIV).

Et erigit omnes elisos. (AUG.) Ad se pertinentes, quia superbis resistit.

VERS. 15.-- Oculi omnium in te sperant, Domine. (ID.) De justitia latius agit, ut qui misericordem audit, justum timeat: et justitiae est ut sperantes satiet corporaliter vel spiritualiter. Non semper enim danda est esca, sed in tempore opportuno: 1071Bmultis enim petentibus salubriter differtur. Et tu das escam illorum in tempore opportuno. (ID.) Dat ergo medicus aegro quod convenit, etc., usque ad benedicens Deum in omni tempore.

VERS. 16.-- Aperis tu manum. (ID.) Etsi non das aliquando, das tamen opportune: differs quidem, non aufers.

VERS. 17.-- Justus. (CAS.) Ipso nomine justitiam aperit, ut manifeste ostendatur hic laus de justitia esse. Viae sunt dispositiones et voluntates, quae omnes justae, etiam si verberat.

Viis suis, et sanctus in omnibns operibus suis. Sciendum quod Viae ad dispositionem pertinent, opera ad effectum: haec secundum nos dividuntur. Sed apud illum, hoc est velle, quod facere: quia 1071Cex ejus voluntate res habent esse.

VERS. 18.-- Prope est omnibus invocantibus eum. (CAS.) Propitius, qui ubique, et hoc de justitia.

VERS. 19.-- Voluntatem timentium se faciet. (ID.) Concludit de justitia: aequum est enim et diligentes custodire et peccatores perdere.

VERS. 21.-- Laudationem. (CAS.) Expositis omnibus, sequitur brevis conclusio, qua concludit quod non potest explicari.

PSALM CXLIV.

VERS. 1.-- Praise, for David himself. (CAS.) This psalm contains briefly the things which in the divine Scriptures are spread abroad at large, etc., as far as lest any should be able to err in his praise:

(AUG.) God fills the saints with the Holy Spirit, etc., 1069Bas far as and therefore let his spirit in his servants praise him, because he makes himself to be praised.

(CAS.) As there are seven psalms of penance, so also seven spirits, according to that sacrament wherein the Lord commanded Moses to set seven lamps in the tabernacle, shining with perpetual light.

I will extol thee. (CAS.) First the prophet promises endless praise; secondly, he says that all shall accomplish the praise of God in nine ways, there, Generation and generation; thirdly, he explains the same at greater length, there, compassionate.

For ever and ever. (CAS.) He who does not begin here shall be dumb in the world to come.

VERS. 2.-- Every day, etc. (ID.) He who here every day does so, shall deserve in the eternal day to praise with continual exultation.

1069C(AUG.) He blesses now every day, that, when the one day without ends [fines; read fine, "without end"] shall have come, he may go from praise to praise, as from virtue to virtue. For ever, and for ever and ever. (CAS.) Of which praise elsewhere: They shall praise for ever and ever (Psal. XXXVIII), because they will always love him whom they will always see, since nothing is more delightful than that vision.

VERS. 3.-- Exceedingly. (CAS.) In one word he has given us to consider that which cannot be fully grasped: and therefore never cease from praises.

VERS. 4.-- Generation and generation. (CAS.) Secondly, he promises that all shall accomplish the praise of God in nine ways. Thy works. (AUG.) If we fail in his greatness, let us at least praise the worker from his works, the founder from the things founded, the creator from his creatures. (CAS.) 1069DNine are the works: power, magnificence, holiness, wonders, strength, the greatness of terrible things, memory, justice, which shall be explained hereafter: from these, as from topics and seeds, all praise is drawn, in the manner in which all arguments are taken from a small number of topics. And thy power. (AUG.) For works do not praise, save that they may announce the strength of the worker. But certain eloquent men praise the creature, forgetful of the Creator. But holy praisers, if they love the works, praise the worker the more: and on account of these they love him. If in things made there is felt any beauty, usefulness, strength, it is the more praised in him who made it. If thou praisest the works, thou praisest thyself also, who art the work of God. And this occurs: Let not thy own mouth praise thee, lest thou 1070Aseem arrogant (Prov. XXVII). [Vulg. Prov. 27:2 Laudet te alienus, et non os tuum ; extraneus, et non labia tua, "Let another praise thee, and not thy own mouth"] But it is not arrogance, because thou praisest God in thee, not thyself.

VERS. 6.-- And the power. If he did not threaten, there would be no correction corectio; but if he did not allure, there would be no exhortation. He is therefore both lovable and terrible. They shall declare therefore the power of him that disciplines and punishes, if they preach the eternal kingdom, they do not keep silent concerning the eternal fire.

VERS. 7.-- They shall belch forth the memory of the abundance of thy sweetness. (AUG.) He himself through his abundant sweetness is first mindful of us, by calling us, by preventing us with his grace, and thence we of him.

They shall belch forth, he says, not, they shall eat.

(AUG.) He eats who learns, he belches forth who teaches: yet he belches forth that which he eats. This memory, because it is exceeding sweet, is to be eaten and to be belched forth. So then 1070Beat, that thou mayest belch forth.

VERS. 8.-- Compassionate and merciful. (CAS.) Thirdly he explains at greater length the things which in the second place he set forth briefly. As if: Deservedly in these things they shall praise, because compassionate, etc. The parts of praise are set down here which were set down above, but they cannot be explained one by one: for who could fully explain his works or his power? (AUG.) Compassionate and merciful. To those to whom he has given that pardon. Patient. To those to whom he has not yet given it, but waits that he may give it.

VERS. 9.--(CAS.) Tender mercies. He begins from the works, that he may be called compassionate while he restores the fallen. Merciful, by nature, even while he creates. Patient, this he takes from the second topic of praise, namely from power, which he praises, not because he has hung the lands, restrained the seas, painted the heavens with stars, etc., but because he bears with 1070Csinners, that they may be converted. And his tender mercies. (AUG.) For if thou takest away thy evil works, and there remain in thee nothing but his works, his mercy will not let thee go: but if thou dost not let go thy own works, his severity will be upon thy works, when he shall say: Go, ye cursed, into everlasting fire (Matth. XXV). [Vulg. Mt 25:41 Discedite a me maledicti in ignem aeternum, "Depart from me, ye cursed"]

VERS. 10.-- Let all thy works confess to thee, O Lord. (AUG.) Let them praise as do those things which have not the sense of praising, which are the matter of praise: because while thou inquirest, thou findest a great power in them, which is from God.

And thy saints. (CAS.) Everything that is confesses either by itself, or through rational creatures. Or the saints, that is, angels and men. This concerning holiness: for this is the holiness of God, that the saints should owe him confession.

1070DVERS. 11.-- The glory of the kingdom. (ID.) It is taken therefore from the wonders. As if: How wonderful is he who made heaven and earth, and filled them with divers good things.

VERS. 12.-- That known. (ID.) This is taken from the power of terrible things, etc., as far as to whom, being magnificent, nothing is compared.

VERS. 13.-- Thy kingdom, etc. (ID.) He praises from the perpetuity and the effect of dominion. And this is taken from greatness: if it is great to rule for a time, it is greater to have no term of dominion.

The Lord is faithful in all. (ID.) This is taken from the abundant sweetness; whence above: The memory of the abundance of thy sweetness. Faithful, because his coming fulfilled the gifts. To abundance also belongs 1071Athat he lifts up those who fall, raises up the crushed; whence the remembrance of sweetness is had, and is belched forth in his praises.

VERS. 14.-- Who fall down. (CAS.) From their own evils, all of whom God lifts up. Or, from these temporal things, as the saints do, like Job, who lose something in the world and are made abject, and are falling: but all these he confirms, because seven times the just man falls and rises again; but the wicked are weakened in evils (Prov. XXIV).

And he lifts up all that are cast down. (AUG.) Those belonging to him, because he resists the proud.

VERS. 15.-- The eyes of all hope in thee, O Lord. (ID.) He treats of justice at greater length, that he who hears of the merciful one may fear the just one: and it belongs to justice that he should satisfy those who hope, bodily or spiritually. For food is not always to be given, but in due season: 1071Bfor to many who ask it is wholesomely deferred. And thou givest them their food in due season. (ID.) The physician therefore gives the sick man what is fitting, etc., as far as blessing God at all times.

VERS. 16.-- Thou openest the hand. (ID.) Although sometimes thou dost not give, yet thou givest opportunely: thou deferrest indeed, thou dost not take away.

VERS. 17.-- Just. (CAS.) By the very name he discloses justice, that it may be manifestly shown that this praise is concerning justice. Ways are dispositions and wills, which are all just, even if he scourges.

In his ways, and holy in all omnibns his works. It is to be known that Ways pertain to disposition, works to effect: these are divided according to us. But with him, to will is the same as to do: because 1071Cfrom his will things have their being.

VERS. 18.-- He is near to all that call upon him. (CAS.) Propitious, who is everywhere, and this concerning justice.

VERS. 19.-- He will do the will of them that fear him. (ID.) He concludes concerning justice: for it is just both to keep those who love him and to destroy sinners.

VERS. 21.-- Praise. (CAS.) All things having been expounded, there follows a brief conclusion, in which he concludes that which cannot be explained.

PSALMUS CXLV.

VERS. 1.-- Alleluia. (CAS.) Vox ista, quasi musicas salutaris, tanquam harmonia coelestis, quae non solum homines, sed etiam angelos delectat, laudem Dei exprimens. Quae congrue huic psalmo praescribitur, 1071Dubi vir justus exhortatur animam ad laudem Dei: quia in adversis aliquando, velit nolit, perturbatur anima. Unde supra: Quare tristis es, anima mea, et quare conturbas me? Sed ut auferat ei perturbationem, suggerit gaudium de spe, si non in re: Spera in Deo, etc. (AUG.) Haec spe erecta anima Deum laudat hic. (CAS.) Primo, sibi quasi omnibus consulit laudare, ne in vanis oretur; et quasi acquiescens consilio, asserit se laudaturum ibi ubi poterit plene. Secundo, alios monet non sperare in homine, ibi: Nolite confidere. Tertio, docet omnem spem in Omnipotente ponendam, ibi: Beatus, etc.

VERS. 2.-- Lauda, anima mea, Dominum. Sed 1072Aquaeritur, a quo, cui hoc consulitur? Si dicitur caro consulere animae, non videtur hoc esse verum, cum a meliori et a digniori soleat inferiori dari consilium: caro autem inferior est anima. Anima enim, licet vituperata quia peccatrix, tamen melior dicitur per naturam corpore laudato in suo genere, quia spiritualis natura praestat corpore, quam movet, regit, sensificat, capit: et ipsa infinita, vicina est substantiae Dei. Sic aurum, vituperatum quia sordidum, praeest plumbo in puritate laudatio: sic et malus homo optimo equo. Non datur ergo consilium animae a carne, quamvis domita valde et pacata: quae tamen mortua est propter peccatum. Nec etiam caro mortalis immortali consulit animae, quia semper infra animam est; sed superior pars animae, 1072Bscilicet mens, quae cogitat sapientiam divinam, illi inhaerens et in illam suspirans, videt quasdam sui partes perturbari motibus saeculi, cupiditate terrenorum ad exteriora rapi: unde ad interiora et superiora revocat eam. Se ergo secundum sensualitatem exhortans dicit: Lauda, anima mea, Dominum. Quid enim tibi placet in hoc saeculo? Divisa per tot saeculorum rerum amores, collige te ad auctorem: hic tibi pax et securitas. Deinde respondet anima menti, quasi hic praegravata non valens desistere, ut dignum est. Laudabo in vita. Hic in morte laudabo tenuiter, quia corpus aggravat animam, et terrena inhabitatio sensum deprimit multa cogitantem (Sap. IX); hic spes pascit, vita in futuro.

In vita mea. (CAS.) Cum ei perfecte inhaesero, a 1072Cquo separari, ut modo fit, mors est: sed spes consolatur, in qua quodammodo vivens laudat.

Quandiu. Non quod aliquando non sit, quia in aeternum erit, et ideo vere diu.

VERS. 3.-- Nolite confidere, etc. (CAS.) Secunda pars. Dato consilio et affirmato, ubi plene laudare poterit, quasi longe remotos, et interim dum mala sunt (quibus turbatur anima), monet non sperare in homine, sed in Deo. (AUG.) Vel quasi in fine saeculi mente positus: cito finienda docet non amare pro aeternis; quasi et meo exemplo, nolite confidere, etc. In filiis hominum. (ID.) In uno filio hominis est salus, et in ipso sperate. Non quia filius hominis est, sed quia Filius Dei est. Non propter illud quod suscepit ex te, sed propter illud quod servavit in se.

1072DVERS. 4.-- Exibit spiritus ejus, etc. (CAS.) Prius mundat corda prohibendo a noxiis, ut post salutaria intendat monendo salubria.

VERS. 5.-- Beatus cujus Deus Jacob. (CAS.) Tertia pars, ubi docet totam spem in Omnipotenti ponendam, quem ex factis describit ut gentilitas tam frequenter convicta quiescat. (AUG.) Remotis noxiis, docet quod salutis est, scilicet in quo sperandum sit. Adjutor ejus spes ejus. (CAS.) Ipsius Jacob sic fuit adjutor, etc., usque ad id est, hujus veri Jacob, sicut illius.

VERS. 6.-- Qui fecit coelum et terram. (ID.) Quia et cultoribus daemonum spes est in deo suo, determinat in quo debet esse spes, id est in Christo, et hoc 1073Ausque in finem psalmi ostendit, describendo eum per omnia. Omnia quae in eis sunt. Ne quem alium putes creatorem, vel minutissimarum rerum existere creatorem.

VERS. 7.-- Qui custodit veritatem in saeculum. (CAS.) Christus, qui est veritas, omnis homo mendax. Facit judicium. Haec duo ad justitiam pertinent. Christus judex vindicat patientes propter nomen suum, et dat escam diligentibus se. Injuriam patientibus. (AUG.) Non omnis molestia est injuria. Quod jure pateris non est injuria, ut quod patitur latro et scelerati alii. Aliud ergo est pati injuriam, aliud supplicium. Supplicium enim jure quis patitur, injuria autem juri contraria est.

VERS. 8.-- Dominus solvit compeditos. (CAS.) Hoc 1073Bad abundantiam suavitatis.

Dominus erigit elisos. Quos diabolus elidit, Dominus erigit.

Diligit justos. (CAS.) Quos locat in aeterna beatitudine.

VERS. 9.-- Pupillum et viduam suseipiet. (AUG.) Omnis Ecclesia gentium adventitia est ad patres, non carne, sed imitando, filia.

Pupilli sunt omnes in peregrinatione, quibus est absens pater; et omnis fidelis anima est vidua sponso absente: unde et magis patrem et sponsum desiderant, et hos protegit Deus non visus, sed desideratus.

VERS. 10.-- Regnabit Dominus in saecula. (CAS.) Hoc est de magnificentia.

1073CRegnabit in nobis, cum corda nostra erunt in eo firma, quod non modo.

PSALM CXLV.

VERS. 1.-- Alleluia. (CAS.) This voice, as it were saving musics [musicas; read musica, "a saving music"], like a heavenly harmony, which delights not men only but angels also, setting forth the praise of God. And it is fitly prefixed to this psalm, 1071Dwhere the just man exhorts his soul to the praise of God: because in adversities the soul is sometimes troubled, whether it will or no. Whence above: Why art thou sad, O my soul, and why dost thou disquiet me? But that he may take away her disquiet, he suggests joy out of hope, if not out of the thing itself: Hope in God, etc. (AUG.) This soul, lifted up by hope, praises God here. (CAS.) First, he counsels himself, as it were all men, to praise, lest prayer be made among vain things; and as though acquiescing in the counsel, he affirms that he will praise there where he shall be able to praise fully. Secondly, he admonishes others not to hope in man, there: Trust not. Thirdly, he teaches that all hope is to be placed in the Almighty, there: Blessed, etc.

VERS. 2.-- Praise the Lord, O my soul. But 1072Ait is asked, by whom, and to whom, is this counsel given? If it be said that the flesh counsels the soul, this does not seem to be true, since counsel is wont to be given by the better and the worthier to the inferior: but the flesh is inferior to the soul. For the soul, although it be blamed because it is a sinner, is nevertheless called better by nature than the body that is praised in its own kind, because a spiritual nature excels the body, which it moves, rules, endows with sense, and apprehends: and being itself unbounded, it is near to the substance of God. So gold, blamed because it is foul, surpasses lead in purity, praise [laudatio; read laudato, "that is praised"]: so too a bad man surpasses the best of horses. Counsel therefore is not given to the soul by the flesh, however greatly it be subdued and made peaceable: which nevertheless is dead because of sin. Nor yet does the mortal flesh counsel the immortal soul, because it is always beneath the soul; but the higher part of the soul, 1072Bthat is, the mind, which thinks upon the divine wisdom, cleaving to it and sighing after it, sees certain of its own parts troubled by the motions of the world, and hurried away to outward things by the desire of earthly goods: whence it calls it back to things inward and higher. Exhorting itself therefore according to its sensuality, it says: Praise the Lord, O my soul. For what pleases thee in this world? Divided among so many loves of the things of the ages, gather thyself to thy Author: here is peace and security for thee. Then the soul answers the mind, as one weighed down here and not able to leave off, as is meet. I will praise in life. Here in death I shall praise but thinly, because the body is a load upon the soul, and the earthly habitation presseth down the sense that thinketh upon many things (Sap. IX); here hope feeds us, life is in the world to come.

In my life. (CAS.) When I shall have cleaved to him perfectly, from 1072Cwhom to be parted, as now befalls, is death: but hope consoles, in which, living after a sort, it praises.

As long as. Not that at some time he shall not be, because he shall be for ever, and therefore truly long.

VERS. 3.-- Trust not, etc. (CAS.) The second part. The counsel being given and confirmed, where he shall be able to praise fully, he admonishes them, as though set far off, and in the meantime while evils last (by which the soul is troubled), not to hope in man, but in God. (AUG.) Or, as one set in mind at the end of the world: he teaches them not to love things soon to end in place of things eternal; as if by my example also, trust not, etc. In the children of men. (ID.) In one son of man is salvation, and in him do ye hope. Not because he is a son of man, but because he is the Son of God. Not for that which he took from thee, but for that which he kept in himself.

1072DVERS. 4.-- His spirit shall go forth, etc. (CAS.) First he cleanses hearts by forbidding what is hurtful, that afterward he may aim at what is saving by admonishing to wholesome things.

VERS. 5.-- Blessed is he whose God is the God of Jacob. (CAS.) The third part, where he teaches that the whole hope is to be placed in the Almighty, whom he describes from his works, that the Gentile world, so often confuted, may be still. (AUG.) Hurtful things being removed, he teaches what belongs to salvation, namely, in whom hope is to be placed. His helper is his hope. (CAS.) Of that Jacob himself he was so the helper, etc., as far as that is, of this true Jacob, as of that one.

VERS. 6.-- Who made heaven and earth. (ID.) Because the worshippers of demons also have hope in their god, he determines in whom hope ought to be, that is, in Christ, and this 1073Ahe shows even to the end of the psalm, describing him through all things. All things that are in them. Lest thou think any other to be the creator, or that there exists a creator even of the smallest things.

VERS. 7.-- Who keepeth truth for ever. (CAS.) Christ, who is the truth; every man is a liar. He executeth judgment. These two pertain to justice. Christ the judge avenges those who suffer for his name, and gives food to them that love him. For them that suffer wrong. (AUG.) Not every trouble is a wrong. What thou sufferest by right is not a wrong, as is that which the robber and other wicked men suffer. It is one thing therefore to suffer wrong, another to suffer punishment. For a man suffers punishment by right, but wrong is contrary to right.

VERS. 8.-- The Lord looseth them that are fettered. (CAS.) This 1073Bbelongs to the abundance of his sweetness.

The Lord lifteth up them that are cast down. Whom the devil casts down, the Lord lifts up.

He loveth the just. (CAS.) Whom he sets in eternal blessedness.

VERS. 9.-- The fatherless and the widow he will receive. suseipiet (AUG.) The whole Church of the Gentiles is come as a stranger to the fathers, a daughter not by flesh but by imitation.

The fatherless are all who are in pilgrimage, whose father is absent; and every faithful soul is a widow while the bridegroom is absent: whence they desire the more both the father and the bridegroom, and God protects them, not seen but desired.

VERS. 10.-- The Lord shall reign for ever. (CAS.) This is of his magnificence.

1073CHe shall reign in us when our hearts shall be firm in him, which is not yet.

PSALMUS CXLVI.

VERS. 1.-- Alleluia. (AUG.) Hic item ait de laude Dei, ubi propheta monet laudare colligentem Israel.

Laudate Dominum. (CAS.) Primo ostendit quos colligat, et quomodo. Secundo, post praedicta, quasi adhuc haerentes et dubios increpat, ostendens unde possint laudare Deum, scilicet si fuerint humiles, ibi, Praecinite.--Laudate Dominum. (AUG.) Hoc dicitur omnibus gentibus. Et quasi quaereremus qualiter laudabimus, laudis causam attulit, quoniam bonus est psalmus. (CAS.) In laude Dei ipse actus est merces quae in futuro erit; ideo laudandus, quia 1073Daedificat, sic, quia disper iones Israel, id est fidelium, de toto mundo in fine saeculi congregabit ad regnum. Et est hic laus de factis mirabilibus. (AUG.) Haec est tota merces laudantium, etc., usque ad modo exerceamur in hac laude bonorum operum.

Deo nostro sit jucunda, etc. Non est satis psallere ad hoc ut laus Deo placeat, sed opus est ut per vitae quoque munditiem illi placeamus.

VERS. 2.-- Aedificans Jerusalem Dominus. (AUG.) Vel, accepit Jerusalem generalem Ecclesiam, etc., usque ad quem Pater misit ad captivitatem nostram redimendam pretio sanguinis.

VERS. 3.-- Et alligat. A similitudine medici, etc., usque ad et Dominus alligat contritiones. (HIER.) 1074AQualiter Samaritanus ille qui descendebat a Jerusalem in Jericho (Luc. X), quando vidit vulneratum jacentem in itinere, colligavit vulnera ejus. Caeterum de his qui non obtriverunt cor, dicitur per Isaiam: Non est malagma imponere, neque oleum, neque alligaturas (Isa. I, secundum LXX). Alligamenta Dei sunt temporalia sacramenta, quibus interim consolationem habemus; quae tunc detrahentur cum erit perfecta sanitas.

VERS. 4.-- Qui numerat multitudinem stellarum, et omnibus eis nomina vocat. (CAS.) Non aliena ut astrologi qui Jovem et Venerem nominant. Vel, typice, de sanctis, quia cuique proprium donum dat; vel, omnes sunt in familiaritate, a similitudine Domini, qui famulorum suorum nomina novit.

1074BVERS. 5.-- Sapientiae ejus, etc., (AUG.) Ipsam mensuram, et numerum et pondus, etc., usque ad vide quid sequitur, humilians autem peccat.

VERS. 6.-- Humilians autem peccatores. (AUG.) Qui enim reprehendunt intelligibilia, ideo sentiunt terrena, de Deo incorporeo corporaliter cogitantes. Haec facit his qui volunt irridere legem antequam noscant. Quia ergo magnum est proficere ad intelligibilia et spiritualia, simus mansueti, pulsemus et faciamus quod sequitur.

VERS. 7.-- Praecinite. Sic pervenietur ad intelligentiam, sic imago Deo reformabitur. Praecinite. (CAS.) Secundo, ex praedictis quasi adhuc haerentes increpat et impellit, ostendens unde possint intelligere, si humiles et non superbi. Quasi: Et ut intelligere 1074Cvaleatis, praecinite, etc.

VERS. 8.-- Qui operit coelum. (CAS.) Memorat opera per quae potestas ostenditur. Ad hoc enim quaedam obscura in Scripturis voluit esse, ut haberent servi Dei quid interpretando influerent super aures et corda hominum, excipientium de nubibus Dei saginem laetitiae spiritualis.

Servituti hominum. Praedicatoribus, qui hominibus serviunt. Unde Apostolus ait: Nos autem servos vestros per Jesum Christum (II Cor. IV). Hi seminant spiritualia et recipiunt ab excelsis saeculi fenum et herbam, id est temporalia.

VERS. 9.-- Et pullis corvorum. (AUG.) Omnia enim, quae dantur Ecclesiae a divitibus, fenum sunt.

1074D(ID.) Judaei, qui se solos justos, omnes gentes dicebant peccatores. Et vere patres nostri corvi, nos autem non sic remanemus: tamen recte pulli corvorum dicimur et sumus. Corvus non invocat, nos vero dimissi invocamus. (CAS.) Pulli corvorum dicuntur rore vesci et beneficio aetatis, ignorant paternas escas, id est fetores cadaverum: sic filii paganorum innocentes, qui invocant.

VERS. 10.-- In tibiis viri. In composito habitu praesumptuosi et audacis. Per virum enim audacem praesumptorem notat. In tibiis notatur incessus incompositus, in tibiis viri. Vel, secundum aliam litteram, in tabernaculis viri, id est in conventiculis haereticorum, beneplacitum erit ei. Nota quod non 1075Aait in tabernaculis Dei, sed viri, per hoc designans audaciam haereticorum.

VERS. 11.-- Super timentes, etc. (AUG.) Timori spem conjunxit, quia non valet timor sine spe veniae: Judas enim timens, sed desperans, laqueo se suspendit. Qui ergo timet Deum, speret et in eo. Placabis autem si speres in misericordia ejus, atque de caetero ita peccare caveas, ut de praeteritis depreceris ut tibi dimittantur.

PSALM CXLVI.

VERS. 1.-- Alleluia. (AUG.) Here likewise he speaks of the praise of God, where the prophet admonishes men to praise him that gathers Israel.

Praise ye the Lord. (CAS.) First he shows whom he gathers, and in what manner. Secondly, after these things, he rebukes them as still doubting and wavering, showing whence they may be able to praise God, namely if they shall have been humble, there, Sing praise.--Praise ye the Lord. (AUG.) This is said to all the Gentiles. And as though we should ask in what manner we shall praise, he brought forward the cause of praise, for a psalm is good. (CAS.) In the praise of God the act itself is the reward which shall be in time to come; therefore is he to be praised, because 1073Dhe builds up, and thus, because the dispersions disper iones of Israel, that is, of the faithful, out of the whole world at the end of the age he shall gather into his kingdom. And here is praise from his wonderful works. (AUG.) This is the whole reward of them that praise, etc., as far as let us for the present be exercised in this praise of good works.

Let it be pleasant to our God, etc. It is not enough to sing psalms unto this end, that praise may please God, but there is need that we please him also by cleanness of life.

VERS. 2.-- The Lord buildeth up Jerusalem. (AUG.) Or, he has taken Jerusalem for the Church universal, etc., as far as whom the Father sent to redeem our captivity by the price of his blood.

VERS. 3.-- And he bindeth up. From the likeness of a physician, etc., as far as and the Lord binds up their bruises. (HIER.) 1074AEven as that Samaritan who was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho (Luc. X), when he saw the wounded man lying in the way, bound up his wounds. But concerning those who have not bruised their heart it is said by Isaias: There is no plaster to lay on, nor oil, nor bandages (Isa. I, secundum LXX). The bandages of God are the sacraments of time, by which for the present we have consolation; and these shall then be taken away when health shall be perfect.

VERS. 4.-- Who numbereth the multitude of the stars, and calleth them all by their names. (CAS.) Not strange names, as the astrologers who name Jupiter and Venus. Or, figuratively, of the saints, because to each he gives his proper gift; or, all are in his familiarity, from the likeness of a lord who knows the names of his own household servants.

1074BVERS. 5.-- Of his wisdom, etc., (AUG.) The measure itself, and the number and the weight, etc., as far as see what follows, but humbling sinners.

VERS. 6.-- But humbling sinners. (AUG.) For they who find fault with things intelligible, therefore savour of earthly things, thinking bodily concerning the incorporeal God. These things he does to those who wish to mock the law before they know it. Because therefore it is a great thing to advance to things intelligible and spiritual, let us be meek, let us knock and do that which follows.

VERS. 7.-- Sing praise. So shall a man come to understanding, so shall the image be reformed unto God. Sing praise. (CAS.) Secondly, out of the things aforesaid he rebukes and urges them as still wavering, showing whence they may be able to understand, if they be humble and not proud. As if to say: And that ye may be able 1074Cto understand, sing praise, etc.

VERS. 8.-- Who covereth the heaven. (CAS.) He calls to mind the works through which his power is shown. For unto this end he willed certain things in the Scriptures to be obscure, that the servants of God might have somewhat which by interpreting they should pour upon the ears and hearts of men, who receive from the clouds of God the fatness of spiritual gladness.

To the service of men. To the preachers, who serve men. Whence the Apostle says: But we ourselves your servants through Jesus Christ (II Cor. IV). [Vulg. 2 Cor. 4:5 nos autem servos vestros per Jesum, "your servants through Jesus"] These sow spiritual things and receive from the high ones of the world hay and grass, that is, temporal things.

VERS. 9.-- And to the young of the ravens. (AUG.) For all things that are given to the Church by the rich are hay.

1074D(ID.) The Jews, who called themselves alone just and all the Gentiles sinners. And truly our fathers were ravens, but we do not so remain: yet rightly are we called, and are, the young of ravens. The raven calls not upon God, but we being let go do call. (CAS.) The young of ravens are said to feed upon dew, and by the benefit of their age they know not their fathers' food, that is, the stench of carcasses: so the innocent children of the pagans, who call upon God.

VERS. 10.-- In the legs of a man. In the composed bearing [In composito; read Incomposito, "in the uncomposed bearing"] of the presumptuous and bold. For by a bold man he denotes a presumptuous one. In the legs is noted an uncomposed gait, in the legs of a man. Or, according to another reading, in the tabernacles of a man, that is, in the conventicles of heretics, shall it be well pleasing to him. Note that he says not 1075Ain the tabernacles of God, but of a man, thereby designating the boldness of heretics.

VERS. 11.-- Upon them that fear him, etc. (AUG.) He joined hope to fear, because fear avails not without hope of pardon: for Judas, fearing but despairing, hanged himself with a halter. He therefore that fears God, let him hope also in him. And thou shalt appease him if thou hope in his mercy, and for the rest so beware of sinning that for things past thou entreat that they may be forgiven thee.

PSALMUS CXLVII.

VERS. 12.-- Alleluia. Psalmus iste facit amorem futurae Jerusalem. Aggaei et Zachariae dicitur, qui in captivitate reparationem Jerusalem prophetaverunt, quae, ut Jeremias praedixit, post septuaginta annos 1075Bfacta est, id est, post volubilitatem totius temporis, quod septem diebus agitur.

Lauda, Jerusalem. (CASS.) Totus hic psalmus potentiam Dei praedicat. Primo, dicit bona futurae Jerusalem, secundo, dicit quae bona hic dantur sanctis, ibi: Qui emittit. (AUG.) In captivitate adhuc constitutus propheta, etc., usque ad qui audivimus sic ructantem.

VERS. 13.-- Confortavit seras portarum tuarum. (AUG.) Nota clausam esse januam admissis prudentibus, et exclusis fatuis virginibus, ut nemo jam exeat vel intret. Et congrue post laudis admonitionem subdit de clausis januis: clausa enim janua Jerusalem secure laudat, quia nemo exiit unde doleat; nemo intrat quem timeat, unde sint scandala.

VERS. 14.-- Adipe frumenti. (ID.) Pane qui de coelo 1075Cdescendit: in mundo carne clausus est, sola fide cognitus, tunc videbitur sicut est.

VERS. 15.-- Qui emittit eloquium suum. Secunda pars subdit quae munera hic dantur electis, per quae veritas futuri potest agnosci.

Terrae. (AUG.) Ut in terra cognoscatur. Nisi enim mittere verbum terrae, qua gravamur et impedimur a reditu, ad adipem frumenti satiantem non levaremur. In terra enim, ubi laboramus fessi, languidi, pigri, frigidi, scilicet in eremo, non deserit, sed manna qui emittit eloquium, etc.

Velociter currit. (AUG., CASS.) Vel usque in velocitatem, id est, a Deo, ut sit ipsa velocitas quo electius vel expressius dici non potuit.

Non ait velox verbum, velox sit velocitate, qua 1075Dplus vel minus participat: sed ipsa velocitate, qua caetera dicuntur velocia, nihil est velocius. Et item quod velox est, ut equus alicui est, non ubique: velocitas vero ipsa ubique est, non est in parte. Ad verbum Dei pertinet non esse in parte, ubique esse per seipsum. Haec est sapientia, quae attingit a fine usque ad finem fortiter, non tamen motu locali, sed immobilitate. Sed et de sapientiae spiritu dicitur, actus mobilis, certus, incoinquinatus; hoc facit velocitas, ut et ubique semper sit, et nusquam inclausa teneatur. Sed quis ista sufficit cogitare? Est tamen spes ad capiendum verbum, quia praedestinavit nos.

VERS. 16.-- Qui dat nivem, etc. (AUG.) Terrae. Frigescente enim charitate, etc., usque ad et hos 1076Adum vocat ad poenitentiam, nebulam sicut cinerem spargit.

(ID.) Nebulam sicut cinerem spargit, etc. Cinis ad poenitentiam pertinet, etc., usque ad et qui praedestinavit et ad poenitentiam vocavit. Ad litteram: Spargit Deus nivem quasi lanam, nebulam ut cinerem, crystallum facit ut frusta candidi panis. Est enim crystallum species quaedam in modum vitri, sed candida est: dicitur autem esse nix glacie indurata per multos annos, ut resolvi non possit.

Crystallum suam, etc. Id est obstinatos, qui non facile ut nix solvuntur.

VERS. 17.-- Mittit sicut buccellas, etc. Alias, ut frusta panis, ut pascant alios, ut praedicent veritatem, quam impugnant. Omnes, unus panis; singuli, 1076Bfrusta; unde: Multi unus panis sumus in Christo (I Cor. X). Paulus crystallum fuit, durus et nitidus: durus, quia persecutus Ecclesiam; nitidus, quia in lege peritus. Hanc autem Deus solvit, et factus est panis, qui veritatem docuit. Sed nisi solvat,

Ante faciem ejus Dei quis sustinebit? Alias, subsistet. (AUG.) Frigus est, qui deserit, non vocat, non infundit gratiam: et quis alius solvet? Nullus. Unde Apostolus: Quis me liberabit de corpore mortis hujus? (Rom. VII.) Quasi dicat: Frigesco, nullus solvit, nisi gratia Dei emittat verbum suum.

VERS. 18.-- Emittet verbum suum, et liquefaciet eam. (CASS.) Verbo namque Dei veniente, nec frigus, nec obscuritas, nec duritia desperare potest. Salubriter enim liquefiunt, et fluenta spiritualis beneficii 1076Cprofundunt aliis unde bibant, juxta illud: Omnes sitientes, venite ad aquas (Isa. LV).

VERS. 16.-- Jacob . . . Israel. (AUG.) Vel idem significatur per Israel, etc., usque ad quia non fuit missus nisi ad oves quae perierunt Israel (Matth. XV).

Judicia sua. (ID.) Judicium incipit a domo Dei, etc., usque ad tres alios psalmos laudis subjungens, ut in hoc opere gratias Trinitatis eluceat.

PSALM CXLVII.

VERS. 12.-- Alleluia. This psalm works the love of the Jerusalem to come. It is said to be of Aggeus and Zacharias, who in the captivity prophesied the restoring of Jerusalem, which, as Jeremias foretold, was accomplished after seventy years, 1075Bthat is, after the rolling round of the whole of time, which is carried on in seven days.

Praise, O Jerusalem. (CASS.) This whole psalm proclaims the power of God. First, it tells the good things of the Jerusalem to come; secondly, it tells what good things are given here to the saints, there: Who sendeth forth. (AUG.) The prophet, being as yet set in captivity, etc., as far as we who have heard him thus pouring it forth.

VERS. 13.-- He hath strengthened the bolts of thy gates. (AUG.) Note that the door is shut, the prudent virgins being admitted and the foolish shut out, so that now none may go out or come in. And fitly after the admonition to praise he subjoins concerning the shut gates: for with the gate of Jerusalem shut she praises securely, because none has gone out for whom she should grieve; none comes in whom she should fear, whence scandals should be.

VERS. 14.-- With the fat of corn. (ID.) With the bread that came down from heaven: 1075Cin the world he is shut up in flesh, known by faith alone; then shall he be seen as he is.

VERS. 15.-- Who sendeth forth his speech. The second part subjoins what gifts are given here to the elect, through which the truth of that which is to come may be known.

To the earth. (AUG.) That he may be known on earth. For unless to send [mittere; read mitteret, "he were to send"] his word to the earth, by which we are weighed down and hindered from our returning, we should not be lifted up to the fat of corn that satisfies. For in the earth, where we labour weary, faint, sluggish, cold, that is, in the desert, he forsakes us not, but manna: who sendeth forth his speech, etc.

Swiftly runneth. (AUG., CASS.) Or even unto swiftness, that is, from God, so that it is swiftness itself, than which nothing could be said more choicely or more expressly.

He says not that the word is swift, that it be swift with a swiftness 1075Dof which it partakes more or less: but than swiftness itself, whereby all other things are called swift, nothing is swifter. And again, that which is swift, as a horse is swift to a man, is not so everywhere: but swiftness itself is everywhere, it is not in a part. To the Word of God it belongs not to be in a part, but to be everywhere through himself. This is that wisdom which reacheth from end to end mightily, yet not by motion of place, but by immobility. And of the spirit of wisdom also it is said, driven, moveable, sure, undefiled; this swiftness effects, that it be both always everywhere, and nowhere held shut in. But who is sufficient to think upon these things? Yet there is hope of laying hold of the Word, because he has predestinated us.

VERS. 16.-- Who giveth snow, etc. (AUG.) To the earth. For charity growing cold, etc., as far as and while he calls these 1076Ato penance, he scattereth mist like ashes.

(ID.) He scattereth mist like ashes, etc. Ashes pertain to penance, etc., as far as and who has predestinated and has called to penance.
