According to the letter: God scatters snow like wool, mist like ashes, he makes crystal like morsels of white bread. For crystal is a certain kind of thing after the manner of glass, but it is white: and it is said to be snow hardened by ice through many years, so that it cannot be dissolved.

His crystal, etc. That is, the obstinate, who are not dissolved easily as snow is.

VERS. 17.-- He sendeth as morsels, etc. Otherwise, as crumbs of bread, that they may feed others, that they may preach the truth which they assail. All together, one bread; singly, 1076Bmorsels; whence: Being many, we are one bread in Christ (I Cor. X). [Vulg. 1 Cor. 10:17 unus panis, unum corpus multi sumus, "one bread, one body, we being many"] Paul was crystal, hard and shining: hard, because he persecuted the Church; shining, because he was skilled in the law. But God dissolved him, and he was made bread, who taught the truth. But unless he dissolve,

Before the face of him, of God, who shall stand? Otherwise, shall subsist. [Vulg. Ps. 147:6 ante faciem frigoris ejus quis sustinebit, "before the face of his cold who shall stand?"] (AUG.) It is cold when he forsakes, calls not, pours not in grace: and who else shall dissolve it? None. Whence the Apostle: Who shall deliver me from the body of this death? (Rom. VII.) As if he said: I grow cold, none dissolves me, unless the grace of God send forth his word.

VERS. 18.-- He shall send out his word, and shall melt it. (CASS.) For when the word of God comes, neither cold, nor darkness, nor hardness can despair. For they are melted healthfully, and pour out streams of spiritual benefit 1076Cto others whereof they may drink, according to that saying: All you that thirst, come to the waters (Isa. LV).

VERS. 16.-- Jacob . . . Israel. (AUG.) Or the same thing is signified by Israel, etc., as far as because he was not sent but to the sheep that were lost of Israel (Matth. XV). [Vulg. Mt 15:24 domus Israel, "of the house of Israel"]

His judgments. (ID.) Judgment begins at the house of God, etc., as far as subjoining three other psalms of praise, that in this work the graces of the Trinity may shine forth.

PSALMUS CXLVIII.

VERS. 1.-- Laudate Dominum de coelis. (CASS.) Per paucorum commemorationem universam creaturam hortatur laudare Deum. Sunt quaedam quae 1076Dhabent spiritum laudandi Deum in eo affectu quo placet eis Deus: quaedam non habent intellectum, sed quia ipsa bona sunt in ordine suo, et ad pulchritudinem universalitatis referuntur, per se non laudant, sed ab ipsis per attendentes ea laudatur Deus: et ita quodammodo laudant, quia de illis nascitur in nobis laus Dei, ad quam nos hic monet propheta.

VERS. 5.-- Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt. (CASS.) Hoc contra illos qui dicunt mundum Deo coaeternum; sequitur: Ipse mandavit. Verbo suo, et creata sunt. Prius dixit, facta, postea creata. Facere enim et nos possumus, sed non creare. Ipse ergo solus creat, quod est proprium Deitatis. Laus ex operibus

1077AVERS. 6.-- Statuit. Ex potentia omnipotens est, cujus opera non mutantur.

In saeculum et in saeculum saeculi. (CAS.) Et si coelum novum, Deo tamen bene statuta dicuntur, quae novantur per Christum et meliorata permanent. Et est hic laus a potentia.

VERS. 7.-- Laudate Dominam. Secunda pars, ubi, enumeratis coelestibus, descendit ad terrestria. Conversus ergo ad illa, tanquam exhortans nos ut eorum consideratione laudemus Deum, quae considerata aperiunt laudem Dei, ait: O vos qui de terra. Omnes ubyssi. (AUG.) Profunditas aquarum, etc., usque ad ipsa ergo, id est, nos consideratione eorum hortatur laudare.

VERS. 8.-- Quae faciunt verbum ejus. Hoc ideo 1077Bquia visum fuit quibusdam quod Deus superiora regeret, sed haec inferiora despiceret, sed a casibus regerentur; sed et haec agit Deus, et in his minimis laudatur, et alleluia cantatur.

VERS. 13.-- Confessio. (CAS.) Supra dixit prius de coelo, postea de terra; hic de omnibus simul. Et accipit per coelum omnia superiora, et per terram omnia inferiora. (AUG.) Confessio ejus super coelum et terram. Illum omnia confitentur in se vel in aliis; pulchritudo omnium vox est confitentium in attendentibus ea, id est, attendentes laudent eum, et de terrenis et de coelestibus, quo non est aliquid melius.

VERS. 14.-- Exaltavit cornu populi sui. (ID.) Ecce quod prophetavit Aggaeus et Zacharias. Modo humile 1077Cest in tribulationibus cornu populi sui, sed cum venerit Dominus, exaltabitur.

PSALM CXLVIII.

VERS. 1.-- Praise ye the Lord from the heavens. (CASS.) By the mention of a few he exhorts the whole creation to praise God. There are certain things which 1076Dhave a spirit of praising God in that affection wherewith God pleases them: certain have no understanding, but because they themselves are good in their own order, and are referred to the beauty of the whole, they praise not of themselves, but by them God is praised through those that consider them: and so after a sort they praise, because from them the praise of God is born in us, whereto the prophet here admonishes us.

VERS. 5.-- For he spoke, and they were made. (CASS.) This against those who say that the world is coeternal with God; there follows: He commanded. By his word, and they were created. First he said, made, afterward created. For make we also can, but not create. He therefore alone creates, which is proper to the Godhead. Praise from his works

1077AVERS. 6.-- He hath established. From his power he is almighty, whose works are not changed.

Unto the age, and unto the age of the age. [Vulg. Ps. 148:6 Statuit ea in aeternum, et in saeculum saeculi, "he hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages"] (CAS.) And though the heaven be new, yet they are said to be well established by God, which are made new through Christ and remain bettered. And here is praise from his power.

VERS. 7.-- Praise ye the Lady [Dominam; read Dominum, "the Lord"]. The second part, where, the heavenly things being enumerated, he descends to earthly things. Turning therefore to them, as exhorting us that by the consideration of them we may praise God, which things considered lay open the praise of God, he says: O ye that are of the earth. All ye deeps. ubyssi (AUG.) The depth of the waters, etc., as far as these therefore, that is, he exhorts us to praise by the consideration of them.

VERS. 8.-- Which do his word. This therefore 1077Bbecause it seemed to certain men that God ruled the higher things, but despised these lower ones, and that they were ruled by chance; but these also God does, and in these least things he is praised, and alleluia is sung.

VERS. 13.-- Confession. (CAS.) Above he spoke first of heaven, afterward of earth; here of all together. And he takes by heaven all higher things, and by earth all lower things. (AUG.) His confession above heaven and earth. All things confess him in themselves or in others; the beauty of all things is the voice of them that confess, in those who consider them, that is, let those who consider praise him, both from earthly and from heavenly things, than which there is nothing better.

VERS. 14.-- He hath exalted the horn of his people. (ID.) Behold what Aggeus and Zacharias prophesied. Now the horn of his people is lowly 1077Cin tribulations, but when the Lord shall come, it shall be exalted.

PSALMUS CXLIX.

VERS. 1.-- Alleluia. (CAS.) Post omnes creaturas quas in praecedenti psalmo monuit laudare Deum, eo quod ab ipso creatae sunt, hic proprius et specialius Israel invitat ad novum canticum pro novitate sibi facta, quae mirabilior est Dei operatio: haec est sanctificatio Israel, per quam de veteri factus est novus.

Cantate Domino, etc. (CAS.) Primo multis modis monet laudare regem qui eis benevolus et benficus. Secunda agit de gaudiis sanctorum, ibi, Exsultabunt. (AUG.) Qui vult cantare hoc canticum, diligat aeterna, 1077Dut fiat novus. Vetus enim homo vetus canticum cantat de terrenis. Novus homo novum cantat de spiritualibus; canticum scilicet pacis, eanticcum charitatis et jucunditatis. Quisquis enim sequitur veterem animositatem, non novam charitatem, novum canticum non cantat.

Laus ejus in Ecclesia. (CAS.) Hic ubi et a quibus cantari debat hoc canticum determinat.

VERS. 2.-- In rege suo. (ID.) Id est, in Christo, qui est rex et sacerdos. (AUG.) Ut rex pugnavit pro nobis de cruce, diabolum vincens: ut sacerdos, se pro nobis obtulit, nihil inveniens in hominibus quod pro eis offerret.

VERS. 3.-- In choro. (ID.) Quia nulla dispersio, 1078Ased charissima unitas; tunc exsultatio erit de tympano et psalterio, non ipsius actus.

VERS. 4.-- Quia beneplacitum est Domino. (ID.) In prima conditione rerum legimus omnia placuisse Deo, etc., usque ad vel cum parem angelis faciet.

VERS. 5.-- Exsultabunt sancti. (ID.) Secunda pars, ubi agit de gaudiis sanctorum et potestate. Gloria. Est bonorum actuum frequens laudatio, de quibus justi laetantur in cubilibus, id est in conscientia, ideo quia habent tam bonum Dominum, qui dat peccantibus gratiam et in meritis vitam aeternam. Fatuus extra in fabulis hominum laetatur; sanctis hic modus gaudii est, ut ad illum referantur bona qui dedit.

VERS. 6.-- Exaltationes. (ID.) Virtus Dei et potentia praedicatur in gloria sanctorum. In cubilibus, 1078Bin diversis mansionibus est gloria sanctorum. De quibus Dominus. In domo Patris mei mahsiones multae sunt. (Joan. XIV.)

In gutture. Qui in corde et in lingua non desinunt laudare eum, a quo aeterna habent.

Gladii. Potestatem verbi Dei accipientes, cum Domino judicabunt, sedentes super duodecim sedes; et tunc vere fiet vindicta et increpatio in populis, tunc reges terrae ligabuntur: unde nos sit liberum exire. Et nobiles ferent ferrea vincula, ut gravia ad portandum, et quae non possunt rumpi: et sic fiet judicium conscriptum, id est ab angelis comprobatum. De quo Apostolus: Neseitis quia angelos judicabimus? (I Cor. VI.) Et ne putes solos apostolos judicare, addit, gloria haec, scilicet potestas judicii, est omnibus 1078Csanctis ejus, id est perfectis, qui pro Christo omnia terrena reliquerunt.

(AUG.) Exaltationes Dei in gutture. Sic enim laetantur in cubilibus et faucibus, id est in corde et lingua, ut non sibi tribuant quod boni sunt, sed Deo, a quo acceperunt quod sunt, et sperant id quod nondum sunt.

VERS. 8.-- Ad alligandos. His vinculis mandatorum et praeceptorum Dei ligantur gentium reges, nobiles saeculi, ab infirmis et contemptibilibus hujus mundi, quos elegit Dominus ut fortia quaeque confunderet; ipsosque implevit Spiritu sancto, et dedit eis frameas bis acutas, ut ad Christi timorem nobilium corda converterent, et saeculari nobilitate 1078Dcontempta, paupertatem eligerent et nobilitatem in Christo. Voluit enim prodesse imperatori de piscatore, non piscatori de imperatore.

(AUG.) Per hos ligat reges et nobiles in vinculis ferrcis, ne progrederentur ad illicita.

PSALM CXLIX.

VERS. 1.-- Alleluia. (CAS.) After all the creatures which in the foregoing psalm he admonished to praise God, for that they were created by him, here more properly and more especially he invites Israel to a new canticle for the newness wrought in it, which is the more wonderful working of God: this is the sanctification of Israel, whereby out of the old it was made new.

Sing ye to the Lord, etc. (CAS.) First in many ways he admonishes them to praise the King who is kind and bountiful benficus to them. Secondly he treats of the joys of the saints, there, They shall rejoice. (AUG.) He that would sing this canticle, let him love things eternal, 1077Dthat he may be made new. For the old man sings an old canticle of earthly things. The new man sings a new one of spiritual things; a canticle, namely, of peace, a canticle eanticcum of charity and of gladness. For whosoever follows the old animosity, and not the new charity, sings not a new canticle.

His praise in the Church. (CAS.) Here he determines where and by whom this canticle ought debat to be sung.

VERS. 2.-- In their king. (ID.) That is, in Christ, who is king and priest. (AUG.) As king he fought for us from the cross, overcoming the devil: as priest, he offered himself for us, finding nothing in men that he might offer for them.

VERS. 3.-- In choir. (ID.) Because there is no dispersion, 1078Abut a most dear unity; then shall the rejoicing be of the timbrel and the psaltery, not the act of the thing itself.

VERS. 4.-- For the Lord is well pleased. (ID.) In the first framing of things we read that all things pleased God, etc., as far as or when he shall make them equal to the angels.

VERS. 5.-- The saints shall rejoice. (ID.) The second part, where he treats of the joys of the saints and of their power. In glory. It is the frequent praise of good deeds, wherein the just rejoice in their beds, that is, in their conscience, therefore because they have so good a Lord, who gives grace to sinners and eternal life upon their merits. The fool rejoices without, in the tales of men; to the saints this is the manner of joy, that good things be referred to him who gave them.

VERS. 6.-- Exaltations. (ID.) The strength and power of God is preached in the glory of the saints. In their beds, 1078Bin the divers mansions, is the glory of the saints. Whereof the Lord says: In my Father's house there are many mansions mahsiones. (Joan. XIV.)

In the throat. They who in heart and in tongue cease not to praise him from whom they have things eternal.

Swords. Receiving the power of the word of God, they shall judge with the Lord, sitting upon twelve seats; and then shall truly be wrought vengeance and rebuke among the peoples, then shall the kings of the earth be bound: whence it is free for us to go out [nos; read non, "not"]. And the nobles shall bear iron fetters, as heavy to carry, and such as cannot be broken: and so shall be wrought the judgment written, that is, approved by the angels. Whereof the Apostle: Know you not Neseitis that we shall judge angels? (I Cor. VI.) And lest thou think that the apostles alone judge, he adds, this glory, that is, the power of judgment, is to all 1078Chis saints, that is, to the perfect, who for Christ left all earthly things.

(AUG.) The exaltations of God in the throat. For so do they rejoice in their beds and in their throats, that is, in heart and tongue, that they ascribe not to themselves that they are good, but to God, from whom they received what they are, and hope for that which they are not yet.

VERS. 8.-- To bind. With these bonds of the commandments and precepts of God are bound the kings of the Gentiles, the nobles of the world, by the weak and contemptible of this world, whom the Lord chose that he might confound all the strong things; and he filled these same with the Holy Ghost, and gave them two-edged swords, that they might turn the hearts of nobles to the fear of Christ, and that, worldly nobility 1078Dbeing despised, they might choose poverty and nobility in Christ. For he willed to profit the emperor by a fisherman, not the fisherman by an emperor.

(AUG.) By these he binds kings and nobles in iron ferrcis fetters, that they should not go forward to unlawful things.

PSALMUS CL.

VERS. 1.-- Laudate Dominum. (CAS.) De laude Dei in sanctis ejus, qui glorificati sine fine laudant. Monetur civitas Dei, scilicet unitas omnium sanctorum, ore et animo cantare. In hoc culmen omnis psalmodia perducitur, quae nuptiali dulcedine cantatur.

Laudate eum in firmamento. (AUG.) Virtus est in 1079Afirmamento, etc., usque ad qui invicem se honorantes, dant laudem Deo.

(CAS.) Quibus propheta in principio formam conversationis ostendit, jam in illa Jerusalem receptis, dicit in eis laudandum esse Deum, qui omnia dedit. In firmamento, quia morte sua diabolum vicit, et credentes ad coelum perduxit. In virtutibus vel potentatibus, quia omnia subjecta pedibus ejus.

VERS. 2.-- Secundum multitudinem magnitudinis ejus. Quomodo hoc, cum magnitudinis ejus non est finis? sed spiritualibus et sanctis dicitur hoc. Et cum non sit finis magnitudinis, secundum eam laudatur. Deus, cum sine fine laudetur. Quomodo autem debeat laudari, per similitudines mysticas usque ad finem psalmi dicit: Tuba concrepet regi, psalterium canat 1079BDeo: cithara cum reliquis sponso. Tuba enim terribilis, vel in bello sumitur, vel, in adventibus regum apparatur; psalterium a summo, cithara ab imo sonat: haec omnia, humanis actibus comparata, figuraliter ibi dicuntur laudes Dei personare.

VERS. 4.-- In chordis et organo. (CAS.) Chordas ponit pro omni instrumento musico, quod chordarum tensione sonat. Organum est quasi turris fistulis diversis fabricata, flatu follium sonans; et ut haec 1080Aomnia de hominibus acciperes, ad hominis os venit: et exponens quid sit laudare in chordis et organo subdit.

Laudate eum in cymbalis, etc. Cymbala bene sonantia labia nostra sunt quae cordi concinna in laudibus Dei bene sonant, in quibus est similitudo cymbalorum, et harmoniam reddunt, et ideo bene inter musica instrumenta sunt. (CAS.) Cymbala bene tinnientia sunt ex permistis metallis parvissimae phialae, quae acutum sonum reddunt. Sed quia omnia spiritualiter intelligi vult, apto fine concludit:

VERS. 6.-- Omnis spiritus, angelicus et humanus, laudet Dominum. Non caro et sanguis, non habitus saeculi: sed quod est in natura rerum sublimius, 1080Bquod coelestia sapit, aeterna capit. Brevis et perfecta scientia, ut Deum spiritualiter omnia laudent, in his totius musicae perfectio est. Est enim flatus in tuba, pulsus in cithara et in cymbalis, vox in choro. Quibus musicis instrumentis significatur spiritualis harmonia, quae non auribus, sed pura mente advertitur.

(AUG.) Tria sunt genera, etc., usque ad vitae aeternae vox est: Omnis spiritus laudet Dominum.

PSALM CL.

VERS. 1.-- Praise ye the Lord. (CAS.) Of the praise of God in his saints, who being glorified praise him without end. The city of God is admonished, that is, the unity of all the saints, to sing with mouth and with mind. In this is all psalmody brought to its summit, which is sung with nuptial sweetness.

Praise ye him in his firmament. (AUG.) There is power in 1079Athe firmament, etc., as far as who, honouring one another, give praise to God.

(CAS.) To whom the prophet in the beginning showed the form of their conversation, now, being received into that Jerusalem, he says that in them God is to be praised, who gave all things. In the firmament, because by his own death he overcame the devil, and led believers to heaven. In his powers or mighty acts, because all things are subject under his feet.

VERS. 2.-- According to the multitude of his greatness. How is this, since of his greatness there is no end? but this is said to the spiritual and to the saints. And since there is no end of his greatness, he is praised according to it. God, since he is praised without end. But in what manner he ought to be praised, he tells by mystical similitudes even to the end of the psalm: let the trumpet sound loud to the King, let the psaltery sing 1079Bto God: the harp with the rest to the Bridegroom. For the trumpet is terrible, and is either taken up in war, or made ready at the coming of kings; the psaltery sounds from above, the harp from below: all these things, being compared to human acts, are there said figuratively to sound forth the praises of God.

VERS. 4.-- On strings and organ. (CAS.) Strings he puts for every musical instrument which sounds by the stretching of strings. The organ is as it were a tower framed of divers pipes, sounding by the blast of bellows; and that thou mightest take all these 1080Athings of men, he comes to the mouth of man: and expounding what it is to praise on strings and organ he subjoins.

Praise ye him on cymbals, etc. Cymbals well sounding are our lips, which being tuned to the heart sound well in the praises of God, wherein is the likeness of cymbals, and they render a harmony, and therefore are they rightly among musical instruments. (CAS.) Cymbals well tinkling are very small bowls of mingled metals, which render a shrill sound. But because he would have all things understood spiritually, he concludes with a fitting end:

VERS. 6.-- Let every spirit, angelic and human, praise the Lord. Not flesh and blood, not the habit of the world: but that which is more sublime in the nature of things, 1080Bwhich savours of heavenly things, which lays hold of things eternal. A brief and perfect knowledge, that all things should praise God spiritually; in these is the perfection of all music. For there is breath in the trumpet, striking in the harp and in the cymbals, voice in the choir. By which musical instruments is signified the spiritual harmony, which is perceived not by the ears, but by a pure mind.

(AUG.) There are three kinds, etc., as far as it is the voice of life eternal: Let every spirit praise the Lord.
